[Berakhot 2:4.14] Temple service (precedes) Thanksgiving: ( Ps. 50:23 ) “He who brings a sacrifice of thanksgiving honors Me and shows a path; I shall make him see God’s help.” One finishes with Peace, since all benedictions end with peace. {NAME} said: There is no vessel that contains more blessing than peace. What is the reason? ( Ps. 29:11 ) “The Eternal gives strength to His people, the Eternal blesses His people with peace.”
[Berakhot 2:4.15] “If he recited and made a mistake then he should return to the place of the mistake.” If he made a mistake between the first and second mention of “writing” he must return to the first “writing”. If he made a mistake and does not know where he made the mistake, he returns to the start, to any place that he is sure about. An explanation: {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} were preparing the wedding canopy for {NAME}. They heard the voice of {NAME} when he explained something new. They said: Who is going down to hear that from him? They said, let {NAME} go down since he is very careful. He descended, ascended, and said to them: So says {NAME}, if he recited and found himself at למען one can be sure that he had the right intention.
[Berakhot 2:4.16] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of the great {NAME}: If he prayed and he found himself in “He Who hears prayer”, he may assume that he prayed with intent. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If he prayed without intent and he knows that the second time he will pray with intent, he may pray a second time; otherwise he should not pray. {NAME} said: I never managed to pray with intent, but one time I made an effort to concentrate and I started to think and said to myself, who enters first before the king, the ἀργαπέτης or the Resh Galuta ? {NAME} said: I counted chicks. {NAME} said: I counted stone rows. {NAME} said: I an thankful to my head that when I come to modim it bends down by itself.
[Berakhot 2:5.1] MISHNAH: Professional workers read on top of a tree or on top of a wall in construction; they are not permitted to do this for prayer.
[Berakhot 2:5.2] HALAKHAH: So is the Mishnah: The hourly workers read on top of a tree and the professionals on top of a wall in construction.
[Berakhot 2:5.3] It was stated: “They pray on top of an olive tree or on top of a fig tree.” Hence, on all other trees he descends and prays on the ground. “The owner descends in all cases and prays on the ground.” And why on top of an olive tree or on top of a fig tree? {NAME} and {NAME} say both, because those are very laborious.
[Berakhot 2:5.4] It was stated: “The porter may recite the Shema‘ even with his load on his shoulders but he should start neither when he unloads nor when he loads because he cannot then concentrate. In any case he may not pray until he unloads, but if he was carrying a load of 4 qab it is permitted.” {NAME} said: only if he is in equilibrium. What means that he is in equilibrium? Two parts on his back and one part in front.
[Berakhot 2:5.5] It was stated: “Nobody should give messages with his eyes while reciting.”
[Berakhot 2:5.6] It was stated: “The hourly workers who worked for an employer have to recite the first benediction of Grace and subsume that of Jerusalem in the benediction for the Land and close with the benediction for the Land. But if they were working for him for their meals or if the employer was eating with them, then they recite all four benedictions.” {NAME} said: This means that one may not work while reciting Grace. Otherwise, why do we have to say this? Let him work and recite the benedictions!
[Berakhot 2:5.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One should not stand and pray while he keeps a coin in his hand; (having the coin) in front of him is forbidden, at his back it is allowed. {NAME} used to bind them together and grab them in his hand. And for money matters, ( Deut. 14:25 ) “you shall bind the money together in your hand”, only in your hand. {NAME} thus taught his son-in-law {NAME}.
[Berakhot 2:5.8] {NAME} and {NAME} were sitting at one place and {NAME} had coins on him. There came the time for prayer, he unbound them and gave them to {NAME}. He bound them together little by little. They became untied and lost. He asked: What have you left?
[Berakhot 2:5.9] {NAME} said: Also one who has his water on his shoulder may recite Shema‘ and pray. {NAME} said: So the reciting of Shema‘ and praying do not require concentration? {NAME} said: I pointed out the difficulty before {NAME} that even if you say that the recitation of Shema‘ does not need concentration, does prayer not need concentration? {NAME} said: I confirmed it following what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: You got it, the completion of the works of water that are not clear from the words of the Torah.
[Berakhot 2:6.1] MISHNAH: The bridegroom is free from reciting the Shema‘ in the first night; until the end of Sabbath if he did not do the act. An action: {NAME} married and recited in the first night. His students said to him: Our teacher, did you not teach us that the bridegroom is free? He said to them: I will not listen to you to lift from me the Kingdom of Heaven even for one hour.
[Berakhot 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This means that it is permitted to start sexual relations on the Sabbath. {NAME} said before {NAME}: Explain it for a widow where he does not make a wound. He answered him: Did we not formulate “Four nights?” Can you say four nights for a widow?
[Berakhot 2:6.3] {NAME} said: I asked the question before {NAME}: What is the difference between her and him who breaks a clay amphora in order to eat a dried fig from it? He said to me: But it says afterwards, “only he should have no intent to make it into a usable vessel.” And here when he has the intention of making her a married woman it is as if he had the intention of making her into a vessel. {NAME} said similarly: What is the difference between her and him who opens a boil on the Sabbath? He said to him, but it says afterwards: “only he should have no intention of making a permanent opening.” And here when he has the intention of making her a married woman it is as if he had the intention of making her into a vessel.
[Berakhot 2:6.4] It was stated: “A man should not have first sexual relations on the Sabbath because he makes a wound; but others allow it.” {NAME} said: The reason of the others is that he is intent on his job; the wound results automatically. {NAME} said, it is forbidden. {NAME} went out and said in the name of Rab, it is allowed. {NAME} heard it and resented it, he [Benjamin] died, he [{NAME}] recited for him: praised be He Who smote him. About Rav, he [{NAME}] recited: ( Prov. 12:21 ) “The just will cause no wrong.”
[Berakhot 2:6.5] {NAME} said: All the rules spelled out at the start of the last chapter of Niddah are theoretical and not for practical application. {NAME} fled even from married pre-puberty girls. They asked before {NAME}: What about a second sex act? They said, he did not teach to take all for blood of the wound, how could he rule for a second sex act? What we are asking about is the case when there were days of interruption, days of purity, in between. {NAME} said: I was the best man of {NAME} and I asked {NAME}: is it possible to have the second sex act? He permitted it, since he holds like {NAME}, and {NAME} said: One may enter a narrow gap on the Sabbath, even if one rubs off some pebbles. {NAME} said: I was the best man of {NAME}; I asked {NAME} and he shrank from it. I asked {NAME}; he said: now, what is blood of a period and what is blood of virginity? It was stated: “The bride is forbidden for her house all seven days and he may not take from her the cup of blessings, the words of {NAME}.” What is the reason of {NAME}? It is impossible that not some menstrual blood be mixed in the blood of virginity.
[Berakhot 2:7.1] MISHNAH: He took a bath in the first night after his wife died. His students said to him: Did you, our teacher, not teach us that the mourner may not take a bath. He said to them: I am not like most other people, I am asthenic.
[Berakhot 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: Who stated that the mourner is forbidden to take a bath during the entire seven days? {NAME}. Something happened to {NAME}, he asked {NAME} who instructed him “all seven days following {NAME}”. Something happened to {NAME}; he sent {NAME} to {NAME}; he said to him: Rebbi, did you not so teach us that something happened to {NAME}, he asked {NAME} who instructed him “all seven days following {NAME}”. He said to him, maybe these were two separate incidents, we say it in the name of {NAME}, you say it in the name of {NAME}. And also from the following: Something happened to {NAME}, {NAME}, he asked the rabbis and they forbade it.
[Berakhot 2:7.3] {NAME} asked, which rabbis? The rabbis here or the rabbis in the South? If you say the rabbis of here, it is fine. If you would say the rabbis from the South, would he have asked minor authorities when greater ones were before him? If you say the rabbis of the South, some of them would allow and some of them would forbid, as we have stated: “At a place where it is customary to bathe after a funeral, one may bathe; in the South one bathes.” {NAME} said: He who permits that bath makes it like eating and drinking.
[Berakhot 2:7.4] That means, about a bath for pleasure. But a bath that is not for pleasure is permitted. An example is the case of {NAME} who developed scab. They came and asked {NAME}, what is the rule, may he bathe? He said to them: If he does not bathe, would he not die? If he needs it, even on the Ninth of Av. If he needs it, even on Yom Kippur.
[Berakhot 2:7.5] They saw {NAME}, immersing himself. They did not know whether it was for his emission, they did not know whether it was to cool down because bathing in cold water is not called bathing.
[Berakhot 2:7.6] {NAME} taught like that which was stated. {NAME} taught about him who comes from the road and his feet ache that he is permitted to wash them with water.
[Berakhot 2:7.7] It has been stated: “A mourner and one banned on a trip are permitted to wear sandals. When they come to town they should remove them. The same holds for the Ninth of Av and public fasts.”
[Berakhot 2:7.8] It is stated: “In a place where one is used to greet mourners on the Sabbath one may do so. In the South one does greet.” The great {NAME} went to some place, saw there mourners on the Sabbath and greeted them. He said to them: “I do not know the custom of your place, but be greeted according the custom of our place.” {NAME}, praised {NAME} before {NAME}: A great, holy, and meek man. At some time, he saw mourners on the Sabbath and greeted them. They said to him: Is that the one whose praise you proclaim? He said to them, what are his works? They said to him, he saw mourners on the Sabbath and greeted them. He said to them: you have to recognize his strength; he comes to make you aware that there is no mourning on the Sabbath. That is what is written ( Prov. 10:22 ): “The blessing of the Lord makes rich,” that is the blessing of Sabbath, “He will not add grief to it,” that is mourning, as it is said ( 2Sam. 19:3 ): “The king is grieving about his son.”
[Berakhot 2:8.1] MISHNAH: And when his slave Tevi died, he received condolences about him. They said to him: Our teacher, did you not teach us that one does not accept condolences for slaves? He said to them: My slave Tevi was not like other slaves, he was honest.
[Berakhot 2:8.2] HALAKHAH: Hence, about unrelated freed men one accepts condolences? So is the Mishnah: one does not accept condolences for slaves.
[Berakhot 2:8.3] It happened that {NAME} maidservant died and his students came to him for condolences but he did not accept. He entered the courtyard, they followed him there. He entered the house, they followed him there. He told them: I was thinking that you would be burned by lukewarm water but you are not burned even by boiling water. Did they not say that one does not accept condolences for slaves because slaves are in this like animals? If one does not accept condolences for unrelated free persons, so much more for slaves. If one’s slave or animal died, people say to him: The Omnipresent may replace your loss.
[Berakhot 2:8.4] When {NAME}, the nephew of {NAME}, died did {NAME} accept for him since he was his teacher and a student is beloved as a son. He went and eulogized him: ( Song of Songs 6:2) “My friend descended to his garden, to the spice patch, to shepherd in the gardens.” It would have been necessary only to say “ “My friend descended to shepherd in the gardens.” But “my friend” is the Holy One, praise to Him. “He descended to His garden”, that is the world. “To the spice patch”, that is Israel. “To shepherd in the gardens”, these are the peoples of the world. “And to collect lilies”, these are the just ones whom He removes from their midst. They gave a parable, to what can this be compared? To a king who had a son whom he loved very much. What did the king do? He planted a garden for him. When the son did the will of his father, the father searched in the entire world for a nice plant and planted it in his garden. When the son was making him angry, he cut down all his plants. So when Israel does the will of the Holy One, praise to Him, he searches the entire world and observes the just person, brings him and attaches him to Israel, like Jethro and Rahab. And when they are making him angry he removes the just ones from amongst them.
[Berakhot 2:8.5] A clarification. {NAME} and his group, some say {NAME} and his group, and some say {NAME} and his group, were sitting to study Torah under a fig tree. The owner of the fig tree was coming every morning at sunrise and collected figs. They said, maybe he mistrusts us, let us change place. The next day, the owner of the fig tree came to them; he said to them: the one miẓwah that you used to do with me you are withholding from me. They said to him: We thought that maybe you mistrust us. During the morning he came and informed them that if the sun shines on ripe figs they get wormy. At that time they said, the owner of the fig tree knows the best time to collect figs and he collects them. Likewise, the Holy One, praise to Him, knows the time of the just ones to be removed from the world and He removes them.
[Berakhot 2:8.6] When {NAME} died, {NAME} ascended his pulpit and eulogized him: ( Eccl. 5:11 ) “Sweet is the year of the worker.” It does not say here “sleeps” but “whether he eats little or much.” To what can {NAME} be likened? To a king who hired many workers and there was one worker who was exceptionally productive in his work. What did the king do? He took him and walked with him the long and the short. In the evening, the workers came to receive their wages and he gave him his total wages with them. The workers complained and said: we were toiling the entire day and this one did toil only for two hours and he gave him his total wages with us! The king told them: This one produced in two hours more than what you produced all day long. So {NAME} produced in Torah in 28 years what an outstanding student cannot learn in a hundred years.
[Berakhot 2:8.7] When {NAME} died, {NAME} ascended and eulogized him: Four things are used in the world and if they are lost, they have replacement, ( Job 28:1 , 2 ) “But silver has a source, and a place is where gold is refined; iron is taken from dust, and stone is smelted into copper.” Those, if they are lost, have replacement. But a scholar who died, who can bring us his replacement, who can bring us his substitute? ( Job 28:12 ,21) “Wisdom, where can it be found, where is the place of understanding? It is hidden from the eyes of all living!” {NAME} said: If the brothers of Joseph lost their spirit because they found something, as it is written ( Gen. 42:28 ) “they lost their spirit”, we, who lost {NAME}, so much more!
[Berakhot 2:8.8] When {NAME} died, {NAME} came and eulogized him: ( Eccl. 12:13 ) “Final word: Everything has been heard, fear God.” To what can {NAME} be compared? To a king who had a vineyard with a hundred vines which gave him every year a hundred barrels of wine. He reduced them to 50, to 40, to 30, to 20, to ten, to one, and this one gave him a hundred barrels of wine. This one vine was as dear to him as the entire vineyard. So {NAME} was beloved before the Holy One, praise to Him, like all mankind. This is what is written ( loc. cit. ) “Because that is all of man,” that one is like all of mankind.
[Berakhot 2:8.9] {NAME} was very young when he came up here. A person in rags saw him and asked him, what is new in Heaven? He answered: The judgment over this man has been sealed. This happened to him and he was stricken. Another one in rags saw him and asked, what is new in Heaven? He answered: The judgment over this man has been sealed. This happened to him. He said: Did I not go up to gain merit, but I am sinning! Did I come up to kill the people of the Land of Israel? I shall go and step down the way I came up. He came to {NAME} and said to him: A man whose mother wishes him well and whose step mother honors him, should he go there? He said to him, he should go there where he is honored. {NAME} descended the way he came up. They came and told {NAME} that {NAME} had descended to Babylonia. He said, how could he go without asking permission? They told him: that question, that he asked of you, was his request for permission.
[Berakhot 2:8.10] {NAME} went to have himself bled when he ascended here. He went and wanted to buy a pound of red meat from a butcher. He asked him: How much is that pound? He said to him, 50 minas and one slap. He said to him: Take 60, but he did not accept. Take 70, but he did not accept. Take 80, take 90, until he came to 100 and he did not accept. Then he said: Do what is your routine. The next morning he went to the Academy and said to them: Rabbis, what is this bad practice here that nobody can eat a pound of red meat unless they slap him! They said to him: Who is that? He said, the butcher so-and-so. They sent to him to bring him but they found that his coffin was being carried out. They said to him: Our teacher, all that? He said to them: That should happen to me, but I was not angry about him; did I not think that this was general practice?
[Berakhot 2:8.11] When {NAME} ascended here, he went to a barber. He wanted to bathe in a public bath of Tiberias. He met a scoffer who hit him once on his neck and said: The noose of this man is loose. There was an admistrator sitting who was interrogating a robber. He went and stood there all laughing opposite him. The administrator asked him: Who was with you? He looked around and said: The one who is laughing here was with me. He fetched him, interrogated him, and he confessed about one murder. When they both went out, carrying two beams, {NAME} passed by going to the bath. He said to him: That noose which was loose you already tightened. He answered him: That is the bad luck of this man, is it not written ( Is. 28:22 ): “Now do not scoff, that your fetters should not be tightened.” {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: Scoffing is hard since its start is pain and its end destruction. Its start is pain since it is written “Now do not scoff, that your fetters should not be tightened,” and its end is destruction as it is written ( loc. cit. ) “For destruction and finality I heard from the Lord of Hosts over the entire earth.”
[Berakhot 2:9.1] MISHNAH: The bridegroom may recite the Shema‘ in his first night if he wishes. {NAME} says, not everyone who wants to grab a reputation can do so.
[Berakhot 2:9.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: In anything that gives pain, everyone who wants to distinguish himself may do so. A scholar does and may blessing come to him. In anything that gives praise, not everyone who wants to distinguish himself may do so. A scholar does except if he has been appointed to a position of public authority.
[Berakhot 2:9.3] It was stated: One may step to one side because of obstacles on the road. And when one sinks, even into a field full of saffron. {NAME} said: It happened that {NAME} and {NAME} were on the road and stepped on the side because of obstacles on the road when they saw {NAME}, who was sinking, coming towards them. {NAME} said to {NAME}: Who is this one who makes an exhibition of himself? He answered: This is {NAME}, all whose deeds are done for Heaven’s sake. He said to him: Did we not formulate “In anything that gives praise, not everyone who wants to distinguish himself may do so. A scholar does except if he has been appointed to a position of public authority.” He answered him: Did we not also formulate, “In anything that gives pain, everyone who wants to distinguish himself may do so. A scholar does and may blessing come to him.” {NAME} said, but only if he does not shame others.
[Berakhot 2:9.4] Clarification. {NAME} and {NAME} were sitting and eating in one of the upper synagogues. There came the time of prayer and {NAME} got up to pray. {NAME} said to him: Teacher, did you not teach us that once one started one does not interrupt. And Ḥizkiah stated: Every one who is free from an obligation and does it anyway is called uneducated. He answered him: Did we not state: “The bridegroom is free?” The bridegroom, if he wants. He answered him: Is that not from {NAME}? He said to him, I can free myself as {NAME} did; {NAME} said: I shall not listen to you to lift from me the Kingdom of Heaven.
[Berakhot 3:1.1] MISHNAH: Anyone whose dead is lying before him is free from reciting Shema‘ and from tefillin . The carriers of the bier, their substitutes, and the substitutes of their substitutes, in front of the bier or behind the bier, those that are needed by the bier are free, those that are not needed by the bier are obligated. All of them are free from the obligation to pray.
[Berakhot 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: “And from tefillin .”A mourner may not put on tefillin on the first day; on the second day he puts on tefillin and when new faces appear during the seven days of mourning he takes them off; these are the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says: On the first and second days he does not put on tefillin ; on the third day he puts on tefillin and if new faces come he does not take them off. If he does not put on tefillin even on the second day, why is it necessary to mention “anyone whose dead is lying before him”? Because he stated the one he stated the other.
[Berakhot 3:1.3] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: Practice follows {NAME} in putting on and {NAME} in taking off. {NAME} inquired: If he put them on on the second day, following {NAME}, would {NAME} act like {NAME}, not to take them off? {NAME} said: Is it so that {NAME} would act like {NAME}, not to take them off? If it were so, we should say “practice follows {NAME}.”
[Berakhot 3:1.4] {NAME} said: It is written ( Deut. 16:3 ) “So that you should remember the day of your exodus from Egypt the totality of the days of your living;” the days when you are occupied with the living, not the days that you are occupied with the dead.
[Berakhot 3:1.5] It was stated: If he wants to be more stringent with himself one does not listen to him. Why? Because of the honor of the deceased or because he has nobody to carry his load? What is the difference between them? If he has someone who is carrying his load; if you say because of the honor of the deceased it is forbidden, but if you say because he has nobody to carry his load, here he has somebody to carry his load. Has it not been stated: he is free from taking the lulab ? Explain that it refers to weekdays. But has it not been stated: he is free from blowing the shofar . Can you say on weekday? No, on holiday. {NAME} said: Because he is obliged to bring him a casket and burial shrouds as we have stated ( Šabbat 23:4): “One waits for nightfall at the borders of the Šabbat domain to oversee matters for a bride and matters for a deceased to bring for him a casket, burial shrouds, fifes, and women mourners;” it is as if someone was carrying his load.
[Berakhot 3:1.6] When does one overturn the couches? From the moment when the dead left the gate of the courtyard, the words of {NAME}. But {NAME} says, from when the cover plate was laid on the grave. And when {NAME} died, after he left the gate of the courtyard, {NAME} said to his students: Overturn the couches. And when the cover plate was laid on the grave, {NAME} said: Overturn the couches. They said to him: We already did turn them over on the orders of the old man. Friday evening he rights his couch, at the end of Sabbat he overturns them.
[Berakhot 3:1.7] It was stated: “A dargesh is put upright and is not turned over. {NAME} says, he removes its qlbnṭryn and that is enough.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, a couch whose posts are upright and removed together with it, he takes them off and that is enough.
[Berakhot 3:1.8] What is a couch and what is a dargesh ? {NAME} said, one that one plaits on its body is a couch and one that one does not plait on its body is a dargesh . But have we not stated ( Kelim 16:1 ) “Bed and crib after he rubs them with fish skin.” If he plaits on its body, why does he rub? {NAME} said, explain it with those Caesarean cribs that have holes.
[Berakhot 3:1.9] From where the overturning of beds? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: ( Job 2:13 ) “They sat with him towards the ground.” It does not say here “on the ground” but “they sat with him towards the ground,” on something close to the ground. It follows that they were sleeping on overturned couches. {NAME} said: A beautiful form I had in your house and you caused me to overturn it, you also overturn your bed! Some quote it by the expression “let him overturn; overturn the agent!” {NAME} and {NAME}, both in the name of {NAME}. One said, why does he sleep on an overturned coach? So that he should wake up in the night and realize that he is a mourner. The other one said, since he sleeps on an overturned bed he wakes up in the night and realizes that he is a mourner.
[Berakhot 3:1.10] All the time that his deceased in lying before him, he eats at his neighbor’s, and if he has no neighbor, he eats in another room. If he has no other room, he makes a wall of separation and eats. If he is unable to make a wall of separation, he turns his face towards the wall and eats. He does not eat reclining; he does neither eat nor drink his fill. He eats neither meat nor drinks wine. One does not allow him to participate in a group to say Grace. If he recited Grace, one does not answer “amen” after him. If others recited Grace, he does not anwer “amen”. That is meant on weekdays. But on the Sabbath, he does eat reclining; he eats meat and drinks wine, eats and drinks his fill. One lets him participate in a group to say Grace. If he recited Grace, one does answer “amen” after him. If others recited Grace, he answers “amen”. {NAME} said: Because I allowed all of these, oblige him for all other obligations of the Torah. If I permitted him temporary life, so much more eternal life. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}.
[Berakhot 3:1.11] If he was handed over to the public, he may eat meat and drink wine. If he was handed over to the carriers it is as if he was handed to the public.
[Berakhot 3:1.12] When {NAME} died, {NAME} received his mourners and gave them meat to eat and wine to drink. When {NAME} died, {NAME} received his mourners and gave them meat to eat and wine to drink. When {NAME} died, {NAME} received his mourners and gave them lentils to eat, saying that this was the tradition. When {NAME} was dying he commanded and said: “You should not accept mourning for me this day, tomorrow consolers.”
[Berakhot 3:1.13] {NAME} suffered an accident. Rebbis Mana and Yudan went to him. There was good wine, they drank a lot and laughed. The next day they wanted to visit him again. He said to them: Rabbis, is that what a man does to his friend? Yesterday, the only thing that was missing for us was that we would get up and dance!
[Berakhot 3:1.14] It is stated: Ten cups one drinks in the house of a mourner: two before the meal, five during the meal, and three after the meal. These are the three after the meal: one for Grace, one for those who exercise charity, one for those who console mourners. And when {NAME} died, they added another three: One for the Ḥazzan of the community, one for the head of the community, and one for {NAME}. But when the Rabbinical authorities saw that they regularly got drunk they decreed and returned it to the original status.
[Berakhot 3:1.15] May a Cohen defile himself for the honor of his teacher? {NAME} died. He was both his father-in-law and his teacher. He asked {NAME} who forbade it. {NAME} heard it and said: His students should defile themselves for him. The students of {NAME} defiled themselves for him but ate meat and drank wine. {NAME} told them: One of two things you cannot escape. If you are mourners, why did you eat meat and drink wine; if you are not mourners, why did you defile yourselves?
[Berakhot 3:1.16] May a Cohen defile himself for the honor of Torah? {NAME} was sitting and teaching when a dead body was brought in. He did not say anything either to those who left or to those who remained sitting.
[Berakhot 3:1.17] {NAME} said: My father did not walk under the arch of Caesarea. {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} and {NAME} went walking on those streets of Sepphoris. They came to the arch and {NAME} left. They reached a place of purity and he returned to them. He asked them: “What were you discussing?” {NAME} said to {NAME}: “Do not tell him anything!” We do not know whether it was because he was angry that he left since one defiles oneself for words of Torah or whether it was because he was haughty.
[Berakhot 3:1.18] It is stated: A Cohen may defile himself by leaving the Land for civil and criminal suits, for the consecration of the New Moon and intercalation of a year, to save a field from a Gentile, and he even may leave and lodge a complaint about it, to study Torah and to marry a wife. {NAME} says, if he has a place to study, he should not defile himself. {NAME} says, even if he has a place to study, he may defile himself, since a man may not have the luck to learn from every teacher. They said about Joseph the Cohen that he defiled himself and followed his teacher to Sidon. In truth, they said a priest should not go abroad unless one promised him a wife.
[Berakhot 3:1.19] May a Cohen defile himself for the lifting of hands? I never told him anything. Bring him in and I will cause him to be flogged!
[Berakhot 3:1.20] {NAME} was sitting teaching in the fortified synagogue in Caesarea; there was a coffin there. There came the time for lifting the hands and they did not ask him. [Berakhot 3:1.24] May a Cohen defile himself in honor of the public? That refers to impurity by their words; also for impurity that is from the words of the Torah? From what {NAME} said, so great is the honor of the public that it temporarily pushes aside a prohibition, that means even impurity that is from the words of the Torah.

[Berakhot 3:2.1] MISHNAH: When they buried the deceased and returned, if they are able to start and finish before they form the row they should start, otherwise they should not start. Those who stand in the row, the innermost are exempt and the outer ones are obliged.
[Berakhot 3:2.2] HALAKHAH: It is stated: “One does not take the dead for burial close to the recitation of the Shema‘ unless one does it one hour in advance or one hour afterwards, so that they may recite and pray.” But did we not formulate: “When they buried the deceased and returned”? Explain it for those who thought that they have a free period but they did not have a free period.
[Berakhot 3:2.3] It is stated: The eulogizer and all who participate in a eulogy interrupt for the recitation of Shema‘ and do not interrupt for prayer. It happened that our teachers interrupted for the recitation of Shema‘ and prayer. Did we not formulate: “If they are able to start and finish”? Our Mishnah speaks of the first day, what is stated for the second day.
[Berakhot 3:2.4] {NAME} said: He who enters the synagogue and finds them standing and praying, if he knows that he could start and finish before the reader starts, so that he may answer “Amen”, he may pray, otherwise he should not pray. About which “Amen” did they talk? Two Amoraïm, one says the Amen of “the holy King” and the other says the Amen of “He Who listens to prayer”. {NAME} said, they do not disagree. He who said: the Amen of “the holy King”, on the Sabbath, and he who said: the Amen of “He Who listens to prayer” on weekdays.
[Berakhot 3:2.5] It is stated ( Tosephta Berakhot 2:11 ): “{NAME} says, if they all are standing in one row, those who are standing because of honor are obliged, those because of mourning are exempt. When they descend for a eulogy, those who see inside are exempt, those who do not see inside are obliged.” It would be that what we stated: “Those who stand in the row, the innermost are exempt and the outer ones are obliged” is the last teaching, and what is stated: “Those who are standing because of honor are obliged, those because of mourning are exempt”, is the first teaching. And what we have stated there ( Mishnah Sanhedrin 2:2 ): “When he consoles others, all the people stand one behind the other and the executive officer becomes a partition between himself and the people”, the last teaching. (Another opinion: the first.) {NAME} said: Originally, all families were standing still and the mourners passed between them. When competition increased in Sepphoris, {NAME} decreed that the families should pass by and the mourners stand still. {NAME} Tosephta said: Matters returned to their original state.
[Berakhot 3:3.1] MISHNAH: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from reciting the Shema‘ and from phylacteries but are obliged for prayer, mezuzah , and Grace for food.
[Berakhot 3:3.2] HALAKHAH: Women from where? ( Deut. 11:19 ) “You must teach them to your sons.” To your sons but not to your daughters.
[Berakhot 3:3.3] Slaves from where? ( Deut. 6:4 ): “Hear, o Israel, the Eternal, our Power, the Eternal is unique.” He who has only one Lord, this excludes the slave who has another lord.
[Berakhot 3:3.4] Minors from where? ( Ex. 13:9 ) “So that the Torah of the Eternal should stay in your mouth”, at a time when he is permanent in it.
[Berakhot 3:3.5] They are obliged to pray so that everybody ask mercy for himself.
[Berakhot 3:3.6] And for mezuzah , as it is written ( Deut. 6:9 ): “You shall write them on the doorpost of your house and your gates.
[Berakhot 3:3.7] And grace after meals, as it is written ( Deut. 8:10 ): “You will eat and be satiated; then you must praise the Eternal, your God.”
[Berakhot 3:3.8] There ( Mishnah Qiddushin 1:7 ) we have stated: “Every positive commandment that is activated by time, men are obliged by it but women are exempt. Every positive commandment that is not activated by time, both men and women are obliged by it.” ( Tosephta Qiddushin 1:10 ): “What is a positive commandment that is activated by time? For example sukkah , lulab , shofar , and tefillin . What is a positive commandment that is not activated by time? For example lost articles, sending away the nest, railing, and ẓiẓit . {NAME} exempts women from ẓiẓit because it is a positive commandment activated by time.” Because a nightgown is exempt from ẓiẓit . {NAME} said: The reason of the rebbbis is that, if a garment is designated both for daytime and for night, it needs ẓiẓit .
[Berakhot 3:3.9] It is stated: “For every obligation that a man is free of, he may help the congregation to fulfill their obligation, except for Grace.” But have we not stated: “Anybody who is not obligated may not help the congregation to fulfill their obligation”? If he were obligated, he could help them to fulfill even if he himself already fulfilled it! {NAME} said: There is a difference about Grace since it is written ( Deut. 8:10 ): “You will eat and be satiated, then you must praise the Eternal, your God;” he who ate must give praise. {NAME} and {NAME} were sitting together and saying: It would be reasonable for reciting the Shema‘ that every single person should repeat it aloud. It would be reasonable for prayer that every single person should pray for mercy by himself.
[Berakhot 3:3.10] What is the difference between sukkah and lulab? Sukkah does not need a benediction after the first night of the holiday, lulab needs a benediction all seven days. {NAME} and {NAME} were sitting and saying, what is the difference between sukkah and lulab? Sukkah applies both nights and days, lulab applies only during daytime. {NAME} objected: But the study of Torah applies by night as by day? How is this? Sukkah will end; the study of Torah, it is impossible that it should ever end.
[Berakhot 3:3.11] It is stated: In truth, they said a woman may say Grace for her husband, a slave for his master, and a minor for his father. In truth, they said there should be a curse on the man of twenty years who needs the child of ten.”

[Berakhot 3:5.1] MISHNAH: If someone was standing and praying when he remembered that he had qeri , he should not stop but shorten his prayer. He should cover himself neither with stinking water nor with steeping water unless he diluted them with water. How much does one have to remove oneself from these and excrement? Four cubits.

[Berakhot 3:5.5] New Section. “Otherwise, he should cover himself with water and recite.” The Mishnah deals with opaque water, but in clear water it is forbidden. And if he is able to make it opaque by stirring with his feet he may make it opaque.

[Berakhot 3:6.1] MISHNAH: The person with gonorrhea who had an emission of semen, as well as a menstruating woman who lost semen, and the woman who started menstruating while having intercourse, need immersion, but {NAME} frees them
[Berakhot 3:6.2] HALAKHAH: So far the person with gonorrhea who had an emission of semen; is it good for anything if the person immerses himself who had an emission and afterwards has an episode of gonorrhea? We hear it from this: “The woman who started menstruating while having intercourse needs immersion, but {NAME} frees her.”
[Berakhot 3:6.3] What is {NAME} reason? Is it because what would one profit if he immersed himself or whether there is a name for light impurity in the presence of severe impurity? What is the difference between these possibilities? If he saw qeri , if you say what would one profit if he immersed himself, he would profit! Hence, the only reason is that there is no name for light impurity in the presence of severe impurity!
[Berakhot 3:6.4] That is if the light impurity came at the end. Is it even if the severe impurity came at the end? We may understand it from this: “The woman who started menstruating while having intercourse needs immersion, but {NAME} frees her.” That means, one case is like the other case.
[Berakhot 4:1.1] MISHNAH: Morning prayers are until noon; {NAME} says, until four hours. Afternoon prayers are until evening, {NAME} says until half ofʹ Minḥah . Evening prayers have no fixed time. Musaph prayers have all day.
[Berakhot 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: It is written ( Deut. 11:13 ) “To love the Eternal, your God, and to work for Him with all yor heart and all your soul,” does there exist work in the heart? This refers to prayer. And so it says ( Dan. 6:17 ): “Your God, whom you serve permanently, may rescue you.” Is there any service in Babylonia? This refers to prayer.
[Berakhot 4:1.3] One might think that one may pray all three together - it is explained in Daniel ( Dan. 6:11 ): “Three times a day he fell on his knees, etc.” One might think that one may pray in any direction one wants - the verse says “slits were open for him in the direction of Jerusalem.” One might think that he started after he went into captivity - the verse says “as was his wont from before that.” One might think that one may pray all three at any time he wishes - already David did explain ( Ps. 55:18 ): “Morning, evening, and afternoon.” One might think that one may pray aloud - it was explained about Hannah ( 1Sam. 1:13 ): “Hannah was speaking to herself.” One might assume that he might simply think - the verse says “only her lips moved.” How is that? One whispers with one’s lips.
[Berakhot 4:1.4] {NAME} said: From this verse ( 1Sam. 1:13 ) you may learn four things. “Hannah was speaking to her heart,” from here that prayer needs attention. “Only her lips moved,” from here that one must whisper with one’s lips. “Her voice was not heard,” from here that nobody should pray at high voice. “And Eli thought that she was drunk,” from here that a drunk is forbidden to pray.
[Berakhot 4:1.5] The word of {NAME} disagrees since {NAME} said to the colleagues: I shall tell you one of the good things that I saw Rav do and, when I told it before {NAME} he got up and kissed me on my mouth. At “praised are You”, he bows down. When he comes to mention Hashem , he straightens up. {NAME} said: I shall give the reason ( Ps. 35:10 ): “The Lord straightens the bent ones.” {NAME} said: It is not reasonable, but ( Mal. 2:5 ): “Before My Name he is low.” {NAME} said: If it were written “at My Name he is low” then you would be right, but it is written “before My Name he is low”, before he mentions Hashem he is low.
[Berakhot 4:1.6] {NAME} prayed aloud. {NAME} prayed whispering in the synagogue; he prayed aloud in his house so that the people in his house should learn prayer from him. {NAME} said: Really, the people in my father’s house learned prayer from him.
[Berakhot 4:1.7] From where did they learn the three prayers? {NAME} said: According to the three times that the day changes for man. In the morning, one must say: I thank you, o Eternal, my God and God of my fathers, that you led me from darkness to light. At Minḥah , one must say: I thank you, o Eternal, my God and God of my fathers, that just as You let me see the sun in the East, so I could see it in the West. In the evening, one must say: May it be Your pleasure, o Eternal, my God and God of my fathers, that just as I was in darkness and You led me into light, so may You lead me from darkness into light.
[Berakhot 4:1.8] {NAME} said: They learned prayers from the patriarchs. Morning prayer from our father Abraham ( Gen. 19:27 ): “Abraham got up early to the place where he had stood there in the presence of the Eternal.” Standing means praying, as it says ( Ps. 106:30 ) “Phineas stood and prayed.” Minḥah prayers from our father Isaac. ( Gen. 24:63 ) “Isaac went out to speak on the field.” Speaking means praying, as it says ( Ps. 102:1 ) “A prayer of the deprived one when he faints and pours out his speech before the Eternal.” Evening prayer from our father Jacob. ( Gen. 28:11 ) “He entreated at the Place.” Entreaty means prayer, as it is said ( Jer. 27:18 ) “Please, let them entreat the Eternal of hosts.” And it says ( Jer. 7:16 ): “Do not lift for them (your voice in) a cry and do not entreat me.”
[Berakhot 4:1.9] The rabbis said, they inferred prayers from daily sacrifices. The morning prayer from the perpetual sacrifice of the morning ( Num. 28:4 ): “The first lamb you should present in the morning.” Minḥah prayer from the perpetual sacrifice of the evening: “And the second lamb you should present in the evening.” They did not find anything to peg evening prayers onto it and simply stated it; that is what we have stated: Evening prayers have no fixed time. Musaph prayers are all day. {NAME} said: In fact, they fixed it corresponding to the consumption of limbs and fat which were consumed on the altar during the entire night.
[Berakhot 4:1.10] {NAME} learned from words of the Torah, since {NAME} stated: ( Ex. 16:21 ) “The sun was hot and it melted,” four hours into the day. You say four hours or should it be six hours? When it says ( Gen. 18:1 ): “In the heat of the day”, that means at six hours. Therefore, how can I interpret: “The sun was hot and it melted,” four hours into the day! You derive it from ( Ex. 17:21 ): “In the morning,” ( Num. 28:4 ) “in the morning.” Since the first “morning” meant “four hours”, “morning” mentioned there also means “four hours.” At four hours the sun is warm and the shadow is cool. At six hours both sun and shadow are hot. {NAME} said ( Gen. 18:1 ): “In the heat of the day”, at an hour when there is no shadow for any creature.
[Berakhot 4:1.11] {NAME} prayed at three hours. {NAME} prayed at three hours. They saw {NAME} that he recited Shema‘ and prayed after three hours. But did we not formulate ( Berakhot 1:5 ): “He who reads after that did not lose, he is like a man reading in the Torah.” We may say that he accepted the yoke of heaven in its time.
[Berakhot 4:1.12] Or {NAME} learned from testimony since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: In the time of the hellenistic government they lowered them two boxes with gold and they gave them two lambs to pull up. Once they lowered them two boxes with gold and they gave them two kid goats to pull up. At that moment the Holy One, praise to Him, enlightened their eyes and they found two certified lambs in the hall of lambs. About that time did {NAME} testify that the perpetual morning sacrifice was brought at four hours.
[Berakhot 4:1.13] {NAME} said: Also in the days of the present evil government they lowered them two boxes with gold and they gave them two sheep to pull up. Once they lowered them two boxes with gold and they let them pull up two swine. They did not manage to get to half the height of the wall when the swine clawed the wall; the wall trembled, and [the swine] jumped 40 parasangs from the Land of Israel. At that time the sins caused that the perpetual sacrifice was stopped and the Temple destroyed.
[Berakhot 4:1.14] What is the reason of the rabbis? ( Num. 28:3 ) “Two for the day”, split the day in two. The reason of {NAME}: “two for the day”, two advocates per day; “two for the day” that they should be slaughtered expressly for the day.
[Berakhot 4:1.15] “Two for the day”, that their slaughtering should be facing the day. That is what we have stated: The perpetual morning sacrifice was slaughtered at the Northwest corner at the second ring, facing the day, and the evening one was slaughtered at the Northeast corner at the second ring, facing the day. And that he should know which one was to be slaughtered in the morning and which one in the evening.
[Berakhot 4:1.16] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Minḥah and Musaph prayers, the Minḥah prayer has precedence. They wanted to say, that is if there is no time in the day to pray both of them; but if there is time in the day to pray both of them then the Musaph prayer has precedence. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even if there is time in the day to pray both of them, the Minḥah prayer has precedence. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even if there is time in the day to pray both of them, the Minḥah prayer has precedence. But did we not state: “If somebody made Minḥah prayer precede Musaph prayer, he has done his duty.” Retrospectively, but from the start, not so. Explain it if the time for prayer has not yet arrived, as in the following: {NAME} commanded his students: If you have lunch and the day progressed to six hours before you entered, then pray Minḥah before you enter.
[Berakhot 4:1.17] ( Tosephta Berakhot 3:1 ) How much is half of Minḥah ? Eleven hours minus a quarter.
[Berakhot 4:1.18] There ( Pesaḥim 5:1) we have stated: “The perpetual sacrifice is slaughtered at 8:30 hours and brought at 9:30 hours. On Passover Eve days it is sacrificed at 7:30 hours and brought at 8:30 hours, whether it be weekday or Sabbath.” {NAME} asked: Here you make Minḥah at two and a half hours and here you make Minḥah at three and a half hours? {NAME} said, Minḥah prayer was not bound to the perpetual sacrifice of evening but to incense burning. What is the reason? ( Ps. 141:2 ): “May my prayer be prepared as incense before You, the lifting up of my hands as the gift of evening.” Take one hour for its preparation and you make Minḥah at two and one half hours.
[Berakhot 4:1.19] {NAME} used to pray when the sun set so that the fear of Heaven should be on him the entire day long. {NAME} said: May my lot be with those who pray at sunset. What is the reason? ( Ps. 32:6 ) “For that, every pious person should pray to You at the time of מצא”, at the time when the day is pushed out.

And when the sun is on top of the date palms it is daytime. As {NAME} said ( Is. 44:27 ): “He Who said to the deep: dry up!”, that is Babylonia, the filth of the world. {NAME} said: Why is it called “the deep”, because there the dead of the Deluge were submerged, ( Jer. 51:49 ) “Also in Babylonia the slain of Israel will fall, also in Babylonia the corpses of all the earth did fall.” It is written ( Gen. 11:2 ) “They found a valley in the land Shinear and dwelt there.” {NAME} said, why is it called Shinear? Another explanation: Shinear, because they are stripped of miẓwot, without terumah and without tithes. Another explanation: Shinear, because its rulers die as youths. Another explanation: Shinear, because it produced a hater and enemy of the Holy One, praise to Him. Who is that? That is Nebuchadnezzar the evil one.

[Berakhot 4:4.11] {NAME}, {NAME}. {NAME}, {NAME} comes to it in the name of {NAME}: A person has to turn his face to the wall in order to pray. What is the reason? [That is what is written ( Jos. 6:23 ): “The youths came, etc.” {NAME} said, even if her family was 200 persons strong and they furthermore were related to another 200 families, all of these were saved by her merit.] My forefathers who brought to You all these proselytes, so much more. {NAME} said, he lifted his eyes to the wall of the Temple. My fathers who built for You all this glory, so much more. {NAME} said, he lifted his eyes to the wall of the woman from Sunem, as it was said ( 2Kings 4:10 ): “Let us make a small upper storey on the wall”. ( Jer. 4:19 ) “My innards, my innards I make tremble, the walls of my heart are in uproar.” He said before Him: Master of the world, I checked all my 248 limbs that You gave me and I did not find one of them I offended You with; so much more that You should give me my life.
[Berakhot 4:5.1] MISHNAH: If one was riding on a donkey, he should descend. If he cannot descend, he should turn his head; if he cannot even turn his head, he should focus his intent towards the Holiest of Holies. If he was riding in a ship or on a raft, he should focus his intent towards the Holiest of Holies.
[Berakhot 4:5.2] HALAKHAH: It has been stated: One who was riding on a donkey, if he has somebody to hold his donkey, he should descend and pray on the ground, otherwise he should pray where he is. Rebbi says, in any case he should pray where he is because then his mind will be at peace. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows Rebbi.
[Berakhot 4:5.3] {NAME}: It has been stated there, in all directions one does not stop him except in the Eastern direction. {NAME} said, as of old ( Ez. 8:16 ): “Their backs to the Temple of the Eternal and their faces turned East, they were prostrating themselves Eastwards before the sun.”
[Berakhot 4:5.4] It has been stated: One who is blind and one who cannot determine directions should have in mind to pray to Heaven as it is said ( 1Kings 8:44 ) “They shall pray to the Eternal”. Those who are praying outside the Land turn their faces towards the Land of Israel. What is the reason? ( 1Kings 8:48 ) “They will pray to You through their Land that You gave to their forefathers.” Those who are praying in the Land of Israel turn their faces towards Jerusalem. What is the reason? ( 2Chr. 6:34 ) “They shall pray to You by way of this city that You chose.” Those who are praying in Jerusalem turn their faces towards the Temple Mount, as it is said ( 1Kings 8:48 ): “And the Temple that I built for Your Name.” Those who are praying on the Temple Mount turn their faces towards the Holiest of Holies. What is the reason? ( 1Kings 8:30 ) “They will pray to this place and You will hear at Your dwelling place in Heaven, You will hear and forgive.” Those who stand North will be facing South, those who stand South will be facing North, those who stand East will be facing West, those who stand West will be facing East. It turns out that all of Israel pray towards one place. That is what is written ( Is. 56:7 ) “For My house will be called a house of prayer for all people.”
[Berakhot 4:5.5] {NAME} said: ( 1Kings 6:17 ) “That is the Temple לִפְנָי”, Inside. A Temple towards which all turn. So far when it is standing. In its destruction, from where? {NAME} said ( Cant. 4:4 ): “Built for talpiot ”, a mound (תל) on which all mouths (פיות) pray, in Grace, recitation of Shema , and Amidah . In Grace, “Builder of Jerusalem”. In Amidah , “God of David Who builds Jerusalem”. In the recitation of Shema‘ , “He Who spreads a hut of peace over us and His people Israel, Consoler of Zion and Builder of Jerusalem.”
[Berakhot 4:5.6] One verse says ( Hosea 5:19) “I shall go, I shall return to My place”. Another verse says ( 1Kings 9:3 ) “My eyes and attention shall be there forever.” How is that? One’s face upwards, one’s eyes and attention downwards.

The Great {NAME}: towards the Heavenly Holiest of Holies. {NAME} said, towards the earthly Holiest of Holies. {NAME} said, they do not disagree, the earthly Holiest of Holies corresponds to the Heavenly Holiest of Holies. ( Ex. 15:16 ) “A base for Your throne”, corresponding to Your throne.

[Berakhot 5:1.1] MISHNAH: One starts to pray only in a serious frame of mind. The first Ḥasidim waited one hour before praying in order to be able to concentrate. Even if the king greets one, he should not respond. Even if a snake is wound around one’s heel, he should not interrupt.
[Berakhot 5:1.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Prayer is forbidden to him who comes from a trip. What is the reason? ( Is. 51:21 ) “Listen to that, poor woman, drunk and not from wine.” {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Prayer is forbidden to one in pain; is that not our verse: “Listen to that, poor woman, drunk and not from wine”?
[Berakhot 5:1.3] It is stated: “One should pray neither out of conversation, nor out of jokes, nor out of frivolities, nor out of idle occupations, but out of words of Torah. Similarly, one should not take leave from one’s friend either out of conversation, or out of jokes, or out of frivolities, or out of idle occupations, but out of words of Torah, since we find that the earlier prophets were closing their words with expressions of praise and consolation.” {NAME} said, except for Jeremiah who closed with words of reprobation. {NAME} said to him, still he closed with words of consolation and said ( Jer. 51:64 ) “So Babylon shall sink.” Because Jeremiah continued to prophesy about the Temple. One could think that he closed with the destruction of the Temple, but the verse states ( Jer. 51:64 ) “So far the words of Jeremiah,” he finished with the downfall of its destroyers, he did not close with words of reprobation. But is it not written ( Is. 66:24 ): “They will be a horror for all flesh?” That verse deals with Gentiles. But is it not written ( Lament. 5:22 ): “But You much despised us”? ( Lament. 5:21 ) “Make us return” replaces “But You much despised us”. Also Elijah did take leave from Elisha only out of words of Torah, ( 2Kings 2:11 ) “they walked talking.” What did they talk of? {NAME} said, they discussed the recitation of Shema‘ , ( Deut. 6:7 ) “you should talk about them.” {NAME} said, they were discussing Creation, ( Ps. 33:6 ) “through the word of the Eternal the heavens were made.” {NAME}, said, they were occupied with the consolations of Jerusalem, as you say ( Is. 40:2 ) “Speak to Jerusalem’s heart.” But the rabbis say, they were occupied with the Divine Chariot, as you say ( 2Kings 2:11 ) “behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire, etc.”
[Berakhot 5:1.4] {NAME} said, one should start to pray only from a practical rule. {NAME} said, he who deals with public needs is like him who studies Torah. {NAME} said: a woman who saw a spot like a mustard seed sits and watches seven days of purification because of it; then he stood up and prayed. {NAME} said: He who draws blood from a dedicated animal committed larceny; that is one of the decided practices. {NAME} stated: Eleven days between periods is a practice taught to Moses at Sinai. {NAME} stated: One may add produce on the stalk and be tricky in order to free it from tithes. {NAME} asked Rebbi: How many levels are there for dedicated things? He answered him: four. And how many levels for Terumah ? He answered: three, then he stood up and prayed.

[Berakhot 6:1.23] Why does one finish with “the Land”? It is similar to Grace for day laborers. As has been stated: “Workers who were doing work with the owner shall recite the first benediction, include Jerusalem in the benediction for the Land and finish with ‘the Land.’ But if they were working for their food or if the employer was eating with them, then they recite four benedictions.” In the school of {NAME} they treated it as a formula of benediction.
[Berakhot 6:1.24] Does one have to mention in it the occasion? {NAME} said that {NAME} used to mention the occasion in it. {NAME} said: Since {NAME} took notice of it, so we have to take notice.
[Berakhot 6:1.25] It has been stated: “One recites the benediction on the better kind of flour. Rolls and a full home baked loaf, one recites over a roll. A broken roll and a full home baked loaf, one recites on the full home baked loaf. Wheat bread and barley bread, one recites on wheat bread. A broken loaf of wheat bread and a full loaf of barley bread, one recites on the broken wheat bread. Barley bread and spelt bread, one recites on barley bread. But is not spelt bread better? But this is from one of the Seven Kinds, that one is not of the Seven Kinds.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This is from {NAME}, since {NAME} said ( Mishnah 4 ), “if there is among them a fruit of the Seven Kinds, on it he recites the benediction.” Impure bread and pure bread, {NAME} said, he recites on the pure one. Impure white bread and pure coarse bread, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He may recite on the one that he prefers.

[Berakhot 6:2.1] MISHNAH: If he pronounced the benediction “Creator of the fruit of the soil” on fruits of the tree, he has fulfilled his obligation, on fruits of the soil “Creator of the fruit of the tree”, he has not fulfilled his obligation. On all of them if he pronounced “everything was created”, he has fulfilled his obligation.
[Berakhot 6:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This is {NAME} since {NAME} makes trees like straws. {NAME} said, it is everybody’s opinion since fruits of a tree are also fruits of the soil but fruits of the soil are not fruits of the tree. {NAME} said, except for bread and wine. The Mishnah (6:1 ) says so: Except for wine because on wine one says “Creator of the fruit of the vine;” except for bread because on bread one says “He Who produces bread from the earth.”
[Berakhot 6:2.3] It has been stated: {NAME} says, anyone who changes the formula established by the Sages did not fulfill his duty. {NAME} says, everything that has been changed from the way it was created but one did not change its benediction, he did not fulfill his duty. {NAME} says, even if he says: “Praised be He Who created this property, how beautiful it is,” he has fulfilled his duty. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: practice follows {NAME}. The words of Rav also say so. A Persian came before Rav: “Since I am eating my piece of bread, but I do not know how to recite the benediction over it, I use to say: ‘Praise to Him Who created this piece of bread,’ did I fulfill my duty?” He said to him: yes.
[Berakhot 6:2.4] {NAME} in the name of Abba bar {NAME}: {NAME} and two of his students were with the innkeeper at the “inn of blessings”. He brought before them partridge, orach, and leeks. They said, if we recite the benediction on leeks, it will serve also for orach but not for the partridge. If we recite on orach, it will not serve for anything else. One of them jumped the gun and recited “by Whose word everything was created” on the partridge. His colleague laughed at him. {NAME} said to that one, not about that glutton but about you scoffer. This one acted in his gluttony, why did you laugh? And to the other one he said, is there no rabbi here, is there no old man here? They said, within a year they both died. {NAME} said, there two are gone and we did not learn anything from the incident. What is it? It is reasonable that one recites the benediction on leeks because “By Whose word everything was created” is secondary for vegetables.
[Berakhot 6:3.1] MISHNAH: On food that is not grown on the soil one recites “that all was by His word.” On vinegar, on locusts, and on wind-fall fruit one recites “that all was by His word.” {NAME} says, one does not recite a benediction on a kind that comes from a curse.

When he consumes it, he recites “that all was by His word.” If he sees fallen fruit, he recites “praise to the True Judge”. When he consumes it, he recites “that all was by His word.”

[Berakhot 6:6.1] MISHNAH: If they were sitting, every one makes the benediction for himself. If they were lying on couches, one would make the benediction for everybody. [Berakhot 6:6.3] It was stated: The order of a formal meal: Guests enter and sit on low benches or on chairs until all of them are assembled. They are served wine; everyone makes the benediction for himself. They bringthem water, everyone washes one hand. They bring them snacks, everyone makes the benediction for himself. When they entered and lie down on couches they are served wine; even though one made the benediction on the first one, he must now make the benediction on the second one; one of them makes the benediction for all of them. They bring them water; even though one had washed one hand, he now has to wash both hands. When they are served snacks, one makes the benediction for all of them. No guest may enter after three servings of snacks.

[Berakhot 6:7.1] MISHNAH: If salted fish was brought before him with bread, one recites the benediction over the salted fish and frees the bread because the bread is accessory. [Berakhot 7:1.1] MISHNAH: Three persons who ate together are required to “invite”. If one ate demai , or first tithe of which the heave was taken, or second tithe or dedicated foods that were redeemed, or the waiter who ate the volume of an olive, or a Samaritan, these can be invited. But if one ate untithed produce, or first tithe of which the heave was not taken, or the second tithe or dedicated foods that were not redeemed, or the waiter who ate less than the volume of an olive, or a Gentile, these cannot be invited.
[Berakhot 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: Here it has been said “they are not allowed to split” and here it has been said “they are required to ‘invite’ ”. {NAME} said, one is at the start and one is at the end. What means “beginning” and what means “end”? Two Amoraïm; one said if they decided to eat together that is the start, when they ate the volume of an olive that is the end. But the other one said, if they ate the volume of an olive that is the start, when they finished their meal that is the end.
[Berakhot 7:1.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Three are required, two have permission. {NAME} said this before {NAME}. [Berakhot 7:1.4] {NAME} said, three who ate each one by himself and then came together do “invite”. {NAME} said, only if they came from three groups. According to the opinion of {NAME} and his group, only if all three ate together. {NAME} on that of {NAME}: If he dipped three stalks of hyssop each one by himself and then took them together, he may sprinkle with it. {NAME} said, only if they came from three bundles. According to the opinion of {NAME} and his group, only if all three were dipped together. [Berakhot 7:1.5] Three who ate together and one wants to leave, Rav said he should recite the first benediction, then he may leave. What is the first benediction? In the Yeshivah of Rav they said, the benediction of invitation. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: that is “He Who feeds all.” {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: that is “He Who feeds all.” {NAME} objected, but a baraita disagrees: “Two, three are obliged to recite Grace.” If you want to say the benediction of invitation is the first one, one should state “four.” They found stated “four.” If you want to say this is “He Who feeds all”, it is difficult. If you want to say that it is “He Who is good and does good”, you cannot do that, there is a difference because {NAME} said that “He Who is good and does good” was fixed after permission was received to bury the slain of Betar, “He Who is good” because the dead did not decompose and “He Who does good” that they could be buried. {NAME} said, you may explain it following {NAME} since {NAME} said, “He Who is good and does good” is an obligation from the Torah as it is written ( Deut. 8:10 ): You will eat and be satiated, then you must praise , that is the benediction of invitation; t he Eternal, your God , that is “He Who feeds all”; for the Land , that is the benediction over the Land; the good one , that is the benediction “builder of Jerusalem” [and so it says ( Deut. 3:25 ) “this good mountain and the Lebanon”]; that He gave you , that is “He Who is good and does good”.
[Berakhot 7:1.6] For Torah there is written a benediction before, but no benediction is written after. What is written before it? ( Deut. 32:3 ) “For I am invoking the name of the Eternal, attribute greatness to our God.” For food there is written a benediction after, but no benediction is written before. What is written after it? ( Deut. 8:10 ): “You will eat and be satiated, then you must praise”. From where that which is said about one on the other and vice-versa? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Name is mentioned in both verses as parallel expressions. Just as the Name that is mentioned concerning Torah implies a benediction before, so the Name that is mentioned concerning food implies a benediction before. And just as the Name that is mentioned concerning food implies a benediction after, so the Name that is mentioned concerning Torah implies a benediction after. That follows {NAME}. What following {NAME}? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, an inference from the lesser to the greater. If food that needs no explicit benediction before, needs a benediction afterwards, regarding Torah that needs a benediction before, it is only logical that it should need a benediction afterwards. That works for Torah; what about food? If Torah that needs no benediction afterwards, needs a benediction before, regarding food that needs a benediction afterwards, it is only logical that it should need a benediction before. {NAME} and {NAME} say, ( 1Sam. 9:13 ): “For he will recite the benediction over the sacrifice and after that the invited guests will eat.” {NAME} said, ( Ex. 23:24 ) “you shall serve the Eternal, your God and give praise for your bread and your water”; when is it called your bread and your water, before you eat. Rebbi said, if he has to give praise when he ate and is satiated, somuch more at a time when he is hungry for food. That is for food, what about Torah? If food, which sustains only temporary life, needs a benediction before and after, Torah, which sustains eternal life, so much more.
