But today when olive trees are everywhere, they are under the law of the forgotten sheaf.
[Peah 7:1.4] Šofkānī drips oil. But did we not state “dripping,” so it must be that it yields much oil. But did we not state: “By its production, if it yields a lot.” So, Šofkānī yields much oil. Nĕṭūfah drips oil. Its production, it yields a lot, viz., it produces a lot of olives. Bês̄ānī , some say, really from Beth She’an; some say, it puts the other trees to shame by producing fourfold, similar to what we have stated: If all sheaves of the field are of one qab , except one which is of four qab and was forgotten. Since it produces more than others, it is considered marked. On condition that it produces every year? Since it produces most years it is considered marked.

[Peah 7:3.1] MISHNAH: What are dropped berries? Anything that drops during vintage. If he was gathering grapes, cut off the bunch, it got mixed up in the leaves, fell to the ground and scattered, that belongs to the proprietor. He who puts a basket under the vine while he is gathering grapes robs the poor, and about him it was said ( Prov. 22:28 , 23:10 ): “Do not displace an eternal boundary.” What is a gleaning of grapes? Anything that has no shoulder and no dropping. If it has either shoulder or dropping it belongs to the proprietor, in case of doubt it belongs to the poor. A gleaning on a cut branch, if it can be cut off together with a bunch it belongs to the proprietor, otherwise to the poor. An isolated berry, {NAME} says, it is considered a bunch, but the sages say, a gleaning.
[Peah 7:3.2] HALAKHAH: This means that dropped berries become sanctified in the act of falling down. Does this not simply answer Hilfai’s question, since Hilfai asked: Do gleanings become sanctified in the act of falling down? {NAME} said: There is a difference, because he prevented them from reaching the ground.
[Peah 7:3.3] ( Tosephta Peah 3:11 ): “What are gleanings? Anything that has no shoulder and no dropping. If it has shoulder but no dropping, dropping but no shoulder, it belongs to the proprietor, if it is doubtful it belongs to the poor. What is a shoulder? Spread out one on top of the other. What is a dropping? They hand downward on the spine.”

[Peah 8:1.6] And before that, is it not forbidden because of robbery? They received their answer according to their reasoning: You who say that because of the cold only young people will go out, for you, since he knows that he will not bring home enough for his upkeep, he will not go out.
[Peah 8:2.1] MISHNAH: They can be trusted about gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and peah at harvest time, and about the tithe of the poor its entire year; the Levite can always be trusted. But they can be trusted only about things that people are in the habit of doing.
[Peah 8:2.2] HALAKHAH: How far? {NAME} said, to a place where he usually goes and returns the same day. It happened that Rebbi trusted five brothers about five kor of wheat. Is that not impossible? A little here and a little there adds up to a kor .
[Peah 8:2.3] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does our Mishnah follow {NAME}, since {NAME} said, if he can be trusted for the Second, he can be trusted for the First? {NAME} said, it is everybody’s opinion. Here it is different since nobody fools around with deadly sins. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Just as Jews are not suspected in matters of the great heave, so Levites are not suspected in matters of the heave of tithes. {NAME} said, our Mishnah says so: The Levite can always be trusted.
[Peah 8:2.4] {NAME} asked, can the Levite always be trusted, even in the Sabbatical year?
[Peah 8:2.5] {NAME} said, the Levite may be trusted if he says, this is certainly tithe, to free it from Second Tithe. But if he says: It was given to me, or if he says that it is from his own crop, they cannot be trusted. That is the Mishnah: But they can be trusted only about things that people are in the habit of doing. So is the Mishnah: But they can be trusted only about things that people are in the habit of giving.
[Peah 8:3.1] MISHNAH: They are trustworthy about wheat but not flour or bread. They are trustworthy about panicles of rice but not if it is either raw or cooked. They are trustworthy about beans but not bean groats, either raw or cooked. They are trustworthy about oil if they say it is from the tithe of the poor, but not if they say it is made from picked olives. They are trustworthy in regard to fresh vegetables but not for cooked ones except if it was a small amount, since it is the way of householders to bring out from their pans.
[Peah 8:3.2] HALAKHAH: Should the poor be trustworthy if they say: It was given me as grain and I turned it into flour, it was given me as grain and I turned it into bread? It is clear to him that he is trustworthy. Even if everybody knew that most people store gleanings, he is not trustworthy. It was stated: “{NAME} says, at a place where one presses gleanings of grapes, the poor shall be trusted when they say, this wine is from gleanings of grapes.” Similarly, at a place where one presses picked olives, the poor should be trusted when they say, this oil is from picked olives.
[Peah 8:3.3] In {NAME} they cooked vegetables but had forgotten to put them in order. Gamliel the twin came and fixed them in the pot.
[Peah 8:4.1] MISHNAH: One may not give to the poor from the threshing floor less than half a qab of wheat or a qab of barley; {NAME} says, half a qab . One and a half qab of spelt, a qab of dried figs or a mina of fig cake; {NAME} says, half. Half a log of wine; {NAME} says, a quarter. A quarter of a log of olive oil; {NAME} says, an eighth. About all other produce, {NAME} says enough so he may sell it and buy food for two meals from the proceeds.
[Peah 8:4.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: A quarter of rice, an ukla of spices, a pound of vegetables, three qab carob, half a log of wine, a quarter of a log of olive oil, ten nuts, five peaches, two pomegranates, one etrog . What is the reason? ( Deut . 26:12 ) “They shall eat in your gates and be satiated,” give him to satisfy him. {NAME} asked his father: From where do we get all these amounts? He said to them, a pebble supports a tower. {NAME} was sitting before {NAME}, the latter was giving a reason and the former destroyed it, the latter was giving a reason and the former destroyed it, until he said to him, is it not depraved to destroy instead of building up?
[Peah 8:4.3] {NAME} said, one should state “four pounds.”
[Peah 8:4.4] {NAME} said, the same is valid for an eruv . {NAME} said, this is for wine, but oil for an eruv must be enough for two meals. It was stated: One may use for eruv vinegar enough for two meals. It was stated: One may use for eruv oil enough for two meals. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: For dipping in it bundled vegetables for two meals. {NAME} Aṭoshaya said before {NAME} in the name of the House of {NAME}: One may use for eruv raw peas enough for two meals. For whom is this statement necessary? For {NAME}, that one should not say because they produce bad mouth odor one may not use them for eruv . One may use salted fish for eruv . One may use salted meat for eruv . Fresh meat, as we have stated: The Babylonians eat it raw because their taste is strange. {NAME} asked: May one use χαλκίς for eruv since the Samaritans eat it raw? {NAME} in the name of Rav: One may use for eruv pa‘apu‘in , gudganiot , and ḥaluglugot . They asked him: what are these? He said to them, καυκαλίς, melilot, and purslain.
[Peah 8:5.1] MISHNAH: These measures apply to priests, Levites, and Israel. If he wanted to save, he gives half and takes half. If it was little, he puts it before them and they divide it up among themselves.
[Peah 8:5.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} refers the Mishnah to the case when he has more than the measure: If he wanted to save, he takes away half and gives half, but if he has only the measure, he puts it before them and they divide it up among themselves. {NAME} refers the Mishnah to the case when he has the exact measure: If he wants to save, he takes away one half and gives one half; since if he takes away one half and gives one half it becomes less, he puts it before them and they divide it up among themselves.
[Peah 8:5.3] It was stated: “One does not bother at all with those who beg at doors.” {NAME} said, only if he would not get less than his collection.
[Peah 8:5.4] Here you say, one may not give to the poor less than this from the threshing floor. And there you say, one may not give to the poor who is travelling from one place to another less than that. {NAME} said, deduct one third for expenses. {NAME} gave to the bakers according to the statement of {NAME}, but only for these measures.
[Peah 8:5.5] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: What if they saw him leave the town and enter it again? He said to him, he who gives shall give and he who takes should be afraid for himself.
[Peah 8:6.1] MISHNAH: One does not give to the poor who is travelling from one place to another less than a loaf that costs a dupondius at a time when four seah cost a sela ‘. If he stays overnight, one provides him with a bed for sleeping. If he stays over the Sabbath, one gives him food for three meals. He who has food for two meals should not take from the tamḥui , if for fourteen meals, he should not take from the charity chest. The chest is collected by two people and distributed by three.
[Peah 8:6.2] HALAKHAH: Tamḥui is collected every day, the chest every Friday. Tamḥui is for everybody, the chest is only for local people.
[Peah 8:6.3] {NAME} said, the tamḥui is collected by three people, because it it given out on the spot. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, one does not appoint less than three providers. Come and look, money matters are judged by three, matters of life and death not so much more? But then they should be 23. Until one assembles them, he is in danger.
[Peah 8:6.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not appoint two brothers as providers. {NAME} removed one of two brothers. He came and said before them: There was not anything wrong with Mr. X, only one does not appoint two brothers as providers.
[Peah 8:6.5] {NAME} went up to Kufra and wanted to appoint providers there, but they did not accept. He came and said before them: “{NAME} over the oakum.” If this one had been appointed over the wicks and therefore merited to be counted with the leaders of his generation, you who are being appointed over the lives of people, so much more. {NAME}, when he inducted providers, let them carry the Torah, to indicate that every public office is given by the Torah ( Prov . 8:15–16 ): “Through me, kings rule, through me, princes become princes.” {NAME} appointed magistrates.
[Peah 8:6.6] {NAME} was provider. Once, he returned to his house and said to them: What happened? He said to him, there came a group, they ate and drank and prayed for you. He said to them, that does not give much reward. Another time, he came to his house and said to them: What happened? They said to him, there came another group, they ate and drank and cursed you. He said to them, that gives much reward.
[Peah 8:6.7] They wanted to appoint {NAME} as provider. He said that he had to take counsel with his house. They followed him and heard him say: In order to be cursed, in order to be insulted.
[Peah 8:6.8] {NAME} said: Rav and {NAME} disagreed. One said, one checks out before giving clothing but one does not check out for necessities of life. The other said, even before giving clothing one does not check out, because of the covenant of the patriarch Abraham. A baraita disagrees with him who says that even before giving clothing one does not check out. He explains it for giving him according to his status, as we have stated: “When has this been said? If they do not know him. But if they know him, they also clothe him, everything befitting his status.” But was it not stated: “For food thirty days, for clothing six months.” Explain it, to contribute. But was it not stated: “For food thirty days, for assessments and charity twelve months?” This means to contribute, the earlier must mean to receive. It still means to contribute; what does it mean, for assessments and charity twelve months? For the salaries of scribes and teachers.
[Peah 8:7.1] MISHNAH: He who owns 200 zuz should not take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, peah , and tithes of the poor. If he had 199, even if a thousand people gave him at the same time, he should take. If they were mortgaged for his wife’s ketubah or for a creditor, he may take. One does not require him to sell his house or the vessels of daily use.
[Peah 8:7.2] HALAKHAH: A student of Rebbi had 199 denar; Rebbi used to let him receive the tithe of the poor once every three years. His students cast an evil eye on him and completed for him. The next time, when he wanted to let him receive, he said: My teacher, I have the measure. He said, this one was hit by a beast of prey. He gave a hint to his student who took him to a store, made him spend a carat, then he (Rebbi) let him receive as he was used to do.
[Peah 8:7.3] A family from Nevallat in Jerusalem traced its descent from Oman the Yebusite. Once the Sages alotted them six hundred talents of gold to avoid causing them to leave Jerusalem, since they interpreted “in your gates, in your gates,” to include Jerusalem.
[Peah 8:7.4] Also, we have stated: It happened that Hillel took for a poor son of a prominent family a horse for his exercise and a slave to serve him. Also, it happened that the people of Galilee brought a Sepphoris pound of meat to an old man every day. Is this not impossible? It was because he did not eat except in company.
[Peah 8:7.5] It was stated: “If he was used to golden vessels, one gives him silver vessels, silver vessels one gives him brass vessels, brass vessels one gives him glass vessels.” {NAME} said, silver vessels and glass vessels of personal use. But was it not stated: If he was used to silk clothes, one gives him silk clothes. Here it is on his body, there it is not on his body.
[Peah 8:7.6] One from the family of the Patriarch lost his possessions; they provided for him in pottery vessels, he ate and threw up. The doctor told him, is not the main preparation of food in the cooking pan? Eat out of the pan!
[Peah 8:7.7] So far a creditor who pushes for payment. Also for a creditor who does not push for payment? Let us hear from the following: “If they were mortgaged for his wife’s ketubah or for a creditor.” Is the wife not like a creditor who does not push for payment? “One does not require him to sell.”
[Peah 8:7.8] {NAME} said: A person has to have two outer garments, one for weekdays and one for the Sabbath. What is the reason ( Ruth 3:3 ): “Wash, rub yourself with oil, and put on your clothes.” Was she naked? But that refers to her Sabbath clothes. When {NAME} preached this in public, the companions cried and said to him, our teacher, as our garments are on weekdays so our garments are on the Sabbath. He said to them, nevertheless, you have to change, from this: “Wash, rub yourself with oil, and put your clothes on yourself and descend to the threshing floor.” (It is written “I will decend,” she said to her, my merits will go down with you. Was she naked? No, she said to her: put on your Sabbath garments.)
[Peah 8:8.1] MISHNAH: He who has 50 zuz and uses them for trade should not take. One who has no need to take but takes will not die of old age until he needs the creatures. One who has need to take but does not take will not die of old age until he can provide for others from what is his; for him is was said ( Jer . 17:7 ): “Blessed be the man who will be confident in the Eternal, the Eternal will be his trust.” The same applies to a judge who delivers strictly true judgment. But one who is neither lame nor blind nor limping and presents himself as such will not die from old age until he will be one of them, as it is said ( Deut . 16:20 ): “Justice, justice you shall pursue.” But every judge who takes bribes and bends the law will not die from old age until his eyes are dimmed, as it is said ( Ex . 23:8 ): “Do not take bribes, for bribes blind the eyes of the seeing.”
[Peah 8:8.2] HALAKHAH: This means that 50 at work are better than 200 not at work.
[Peah 8:8.3] He who blinds his eye or swells his legs or blows up his belly does not leave this world until it really happens to him.
[Peah 8:8.4] {NAME} ran away from his father and stayed between two huts of the poor. He heard their voices saying, on which silver will we eat today, on golden silverplate or silver silverplate? He returned and told his father about it. He said to him, we have to give thanks to the dishonest among them.
[Peah 8:8.5] Clarification. {NAME} and {NAME} went to bathe in the public baths of Tiberias. A poor man met them and said to them: acquire merit by me. They said to him, when we return, when we return. When they returned, they found him dead. They said, since we did not acquire merit during his lifetime, let us care for him in his death. While they were occupied with him, they found a pouch of denars hanging on him. They said, that is what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: We have to give thanks to the dishonest among them, because if there were no dishonest persons among them, if one of them was requesting alms from a man and he would not give him, he would be punished immediately.
[Peah 8:8.6] {NAME} gave coins to his son {NAME} to distribute to the poor. He found one poor who ate red meat and drank wine. He returned and told his father about it. The latter said to him, give him more since his soul is bitter.
[Peah 8:8.7] {NAME} and {NAME} were providers and gave a denar to {NAME}, but he gave it away to others. All were saying evil things about {NAME}, the son-in-law of {NAME}; they said that he was taking while he did not need it. When he died, they checked and found that he was splitting it up for others.
[Peah 8:8.8] {NAME} used to distribute his charity in the night. Once the prince of spirits encountered him. He said to him, did not our teacher teach us ( Deut 19:14 ): “Do not displace your neighbor’s boundaries.” He said to him, but is it not written ( Prov . 21:14 ): “A gift in secret appeases anger.” He was afraid of him and fled from him.
[Peah 8:8.9] {NAME} said, it is not written, “hail to him who gives to the needy,” but ( Ps . 41:2 ): “Hail to him who is considerate to the needy;” this refers to him who fulfills this commandment intelligently. How did {NAME} do it? When he saw a son of a prominent family who had lost his property, he used to say to him: My son, since I heard that an inheritance fell to you at another place, take and you will pay back. When he had taken it, he said to him, it is a gift.
[Peah 8:8.10] {NAME} said, in our days there were old people who used to take if somebody gave to them between New Year’s Day and the Great Fastday. After that, they were not taking. They said, there is permission for us.
[Peah 8:8.11] Neḥemiah from Shiḥin met a Jerusalemite who said to him, acquire merit by giving me that chicken. He said to him, here is its value, go buy red meat; he ate and died. He said, come and eulogize him whom Neḥemiah killed.
[Peah 8:8.12] Naḥum from Gimzo was carrying a gift to the house of his father-in-law when he met a person afflicted with boils who asked him, acquire merit from what you have on you. He said to him, when I shall return. He returned and found him dead. He said before him, his eyes which saw you and did not give to you shall go blind, his hands which did not stretch out to give to you shall be cut off, his feet which did not run to give to you shall be broken. This happened to him. {NAME} came to visit him and said, woe to me that I see you in this state. He answered, woe to me that I do not see you in this state. He asked, why do you curse me? He answered, why are you contemptuous of suffering?
[Peah 8:8.13] The teacher of the great {NAME} son was blind and he used to invite him to eat with him every day. One day there were guests and he did not ask him to eat with him. In the evening, he went to him and said: Please, Sir, do not be angry with me. Since I had guests, I did not want risking injuring the Sir’s honor, therefore I did not eat with you today. He said to him, you assuaged him who is seen but does not see; may He be appeased by you Who sees but is not seen. He asked him, from where do you have this? He said, from {NAME}. For there came a blind man to {NAME} town; {NAME} sat below him so that they should say if he were not a great person, {NAME} would not sit below him. They provided for him in honor. He asked them, what is this? They told him, because {NAME} sat below you. He prayed for him the following prayer: You did a good deed for one who is seen but does not see; He Who sees but is not seen may be appeased by you and do good for you.
[Peah 8:8.14] Clarification. {NAME} and {NAME} were strolling through the synagogue of Lod. {NAME} said to {NAME}: How much money did my forefathers invest here! He answered him: How many souls did your forefathers invest here, there is no one in here who studies Torah!
[Peah 8:8.15] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, so is the Mishnah: Everybody who needs to take and does not take commits suicide and one may not have mercy on him. If he does not care for himself, would he care for others? Everybody who has no need to take but takes will not die of old age until he needs the creatures. Everybody who needs to take but does not take will not die of old age until he can provide for others from what is his; on him is was said ( Jer . 17:7 ): “Blessed be the man who will be confident in the Eternal; the Eternal will be his trust.”

[Demai 1:1.1] MISHNAH: The easy ones for demay are shitin , lotus fruit, the fruit of the service tree, white figs, and sycamore figs, fallen dates, fennel, and capers. Also in Judea sumac, vinegar, and coriander. {NAME} says, all shitin are free except those from a tree bearing fruit twice a year, all lotus fruit are free except lotus fruit from Shiqmanah, and all sycamore fruits are free except those cracked open.
[Demai 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, the Sages enumerated them because the majority of these kinds are collected only from abandoned property.
[Demai 1:1.3] {NAME} said, only demay is mentioned, hence one is obligated if they are certain. {NAME} said, they are free whether demay or certain. It is difficult for {NAME}, didn’t they mention only demay? Hence if it is certain, is it not obligated? {NAME} said, since at every place he considers only demay , here he quotes only demay .
[Demai 1:1.4] The Mishnah supports {NAME}: “From Akhzib and further on it is free from demay .” Is not from Akhzib and further on no difference between demay and certainty? Here also there is no difference between demay and certainty.
[Demai 1:1.5] A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: “If they were kept in storage they are obligated.” Did they not essentially come from abandoned property? He explains it, if most people keep them in storage. Come and see, if most people keep them in storage, it is everybody’s opinion that they are obligated, be it demay or certain. If most people do not keep them in storage, it is everybody’s opinion that they are free, be it demay or certain. Half and half you cannot consider since we have stated: “Half and half is demay .” {NAME} said, not only the easy ones for demay but even demay itself.
[Demai 1:1.6] It was stated: If one enters a town inhabited mostly by Gentiles, if there is a doubt whether the majority keep them in storage or not, everybody agrees that they are obligated, be it demay or certain. If one enters a town inhabited mostly by Jews, if there is a doubt whether the majority keep them in storage or not, everybody agrees that they are free, be it demay or certain. If there is any doubt whether there is a majority of Gentiles or a majority of Jews, that is the disagreement between {NAME} and {NAME}.
[Demai 1:1.7] These are the shitim : {NAME}: Those appearing under the leaves.
[Demai 1:1.8] “ Early and late fruits are exempt. These are the early fruits, before one appoints a watchman.” But does this depend on the watchman? {NAME} said, if they are not worth the attention of a watchman. “These are the late fruits, after they folded up the mats. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, the early ones are obligated because of an assumption that they are being watched.” {NAME} said, shitin in Sepphoris are obligated because of an assumption that they are watched.
[Demai 1:1.9] If the fig harvest was finished and he watches his field because of grapes, grape harvest and he watches his field because of vegetables, if a worker enters there and the owner is offended, they are forbidden because of robbery.
[Demai 1:1.10] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Rebbi and {NAME} entered to eat of late fruits; the watchman shouted at them, and {NAME} stopped. Rebbi told him: eat, because the owners already gave up their expectations for them! {NAME} asked: He shouted, and you say so? {NAME} said, he objects rightfully. But does not a Mishnah disagree: “ Calamint, hyssop, and thyme in the courtyard are obligated if they are tended.” Hence, in the garden they are free even if they are watched. There, he may say, the entire world is before you, but here, there is one basketful and I am watching it for my employer.
[Demai 1:1.11] It was stated: “{NAME} says, fallen dates sold with regular dates are free.” Is it about two boxes, one beside the other or one on top of the other? No, here we deal with a mixed bunch. Did they start to ferment or did they not start to ferment? {NAME} said, we deal with fermenting ones. If they started to ferment, they should be obligated for themselves! You cannot say that, since {NAME} said, the Sages detailed them because the majority of these kinds are collected only from abandoned property. {NAME} said, we deal with nonfermenting ones. If we deal with nonfermenting ones they should be free even when mixed. You cannot say that, since it was stated: “{NAME} said in his father’s name that a bunch of grapes of which one berry ripened, is all connected for tithes.” {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME}, one adopted the first opinion, the other the second opinion. But the Sages say one does not follow either of them; those fermenting are obligated, those not fermenting are free.
[Demai 1:1.12] Gufnān is šāmērāh . What is the difference between Judea and Galilee? Since one has a popular saying in Galilee: šāmērāh , šĕmar mārāh (its owner should watch it), would anybody compare it to spices? That means, in Galilee it is free but in Judea it is obligated.
[Demai 1:1.13] Coriander is kusbārātā . What is the difference between Judea and Galilee? Since one has a popular saying in the South: Coriander is kusbārātā , would anybody compare it to spices? That means, in Galilee it is obligated but in Judea it is free.
[Demai 1:1.14] It was stated: “{NAME} said, in earlier times, vinegar in Judea was exempt from tithes. Since they made all their wine in purity for Temple offerings, it never got sour; they made vinegar from the skins of grapes. But now, since wine turns sour, it is obligated.” The argument of {NAME} is inverted since we stated there: “If one makes after-wine and puts in a given volume of water, if he finds exactly the same volume it is free, but {NAME} obligates him.” And here he says so! {NAME} said, in earlier times when grapes were plentiful, their skins were not counted as anything, but now that grapes are not plentiful, the skins are important.
[Demai 1:1.15] {NAME} said: {NAME} asked, does this not contradict {NAME}? Should not all lotus fruit be more than the lotus fruit of Shiqmana, should they not be free? {NAME} said, explain it at a place where most people store it. {NAME} asked: Is not the entire world before him, should not all lotus fruit be more than the lotus fruit of this place and be free?
[Demai 1:2.1] MISHNAH: Demay is not subject to a fifth or to elimination, it may be eaten by a strict mourner, it may enter Jerusalem and leave it, and one may destroy a small part of it on the road; he may give it to the am haäreẓ if he eats correspondingly, he may redeem silver for silver, copper for copper, silver for copper, and copper for produce if he again redeems the produce, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, produce should be brought up and eaten in Jerusalem.
[Demai 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: Not following the High Priest Joḥanan who abolished the declaration of tithes. He abolished the declaration but one still has to eliminate, i. e., eliminate the sure tithes. But demay one does not have to eliminate.
[Demai 1:2.3] It was stated: It may be eaten in strict mourning but not in impurity. What is the difference between strict mourning and impurity? {NAME} said, impurity is frequent, strict mourning is infrequent. They made a decree for a frequent situation, they did not decree for an infrequent situation. {NAME} said, they did not even make it similar to a doubt of ṭevel . Since for a doubt of ṭevel , whether Second Tithe was given in order, or maybe Second Tithe was not given in order, is that not forbidden for the strict mourner? But here, it is permitted to the mourner.
[Demai 1:2.4] There, we have stated: “Heave, the heave of the tithe, and the heave of the tithe of demay .” And here you say so! {NAME} said, there we have stated heave of the tithe of demay but here Second Tithe of demay . {NAME} said, the Mishnah does not stop to deal with the heave of the tithe of demay . What is that? There it is {NAME}, but here the rabbis. {NAME} said in the name of the rabbis: It would have been logical that for the heave of the tithe of demay one would not have to add a fifth; why did they say that one has to add a fifth? Because of a fence for it, for if you tell him that he does not have to add, he will not treat it as holy. It would have been logical that for the Second Tithe of demay one would have to add a fifth; why did they say that one does not have to add a fifth? Because of a fence for it, for if you tell him that he has to add, he will not separate it at all.
[Demai 1:2.5] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Why demay and not also what is certain, why a little bit, maybe the greater part? Did we not state: One does not bring the heave from the threshing floor to town, nor from the prairie to cultivated land, except in a place where [an animal] would drag it away; in that case he brings it and takes money from the tribe. He said to him, is it not a commandment to return a find? {NAME} said, it is a commandment to return a find in small matters; it is not a commandment to return in large matters, except if it is certain; it is not a commandment to return demay since we have stated: “one may destroy a small part of it on the road”. So far, if he had no money in hand. If he had money in hand? {NAME}, said, my father had money in a double sack and he did not redeem. [Demai 1:2.6] In {NAME} Yannai they said, if it is in crumbs one is permitted to waste in amounts less than a meal, but whole foods only up to the volume of a dried fig. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If it is whole, up to the volume of a dried fig, in crumbs any amount. [Demai 1:3.1] MISHNAH: He who buys as seeds or animal fodder, flour for tanning, oil for lighting, or oil to rub on vessels, is free from demay . From Akhzib and further he is free from demay . Ḥallah of the am haäreẓ , food containing heave, food bought with money of the Second Tithe, and the remainders of flour sacrifices are free from demay . Sweet oil, the House of Shammai declare it obligated but the House of Hillel declare it free.
[Demai 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: Since he bought it as seeds there is no difference whether it is something of which the seed disappears or something of which the seed does not disappear. {NAME} said, we have stated this: “If he bought as seeds and then changed his mind to use them for consumption, they enter by thought. If he bought for consumption and then changed his mind to use them as seeds, not all is from him.”
[Demai 1:3.3] It was stated: One does not sow ṭevel , one may not cover ṭevel , but one covers ṭevel with a Gentile. If one forgot and sowed ṭevel , he is free, for it is already lost if it is something that usually is not collected; but for something that usually is collected, he is fined to collect it before it sprouts. But if it sprouted, it turns into something that usually is not collected.

[Demai 1:3.6] Thieves stole the she-ass of {NAME} at night. She was hidden with them for three days during which she did not eat anything. After three days, they took counsel to return her to her master. They said, let us send her to her master lest she die with us and foul up the cave. They let her out; she stood at her master’s door and started braying. He said to them, open to that poor creature because for three days now she did not taste anything. They opened for her and she entered. He said to them, give her something to eat. They put oats before her but she did not eat. They said to him, rabbi, she does not want to eat. He asked them, did you put it in order? They said: Yes. He asked them, did you remove its demay ? They said, did the rabbi not teach us: “He who buys for seeds or animals, flour for tanning, oil for lighting, or oil to rub vessels, is free from demay .” He said to them, what can we do with this poor creature since she is very restrictive for herself? They removed the demay and she ate.

[Demai 1:3.16] “ Wine for brine, wine for perfume, legumes to make into powder are subject to demay , not to mention if they are certain. They themselves are free from demay .” Where are we standing? According to Rebbi, they should be subject to demay , according to {NAME}, even if certain they should be free. But we follow Rebbi, we say we are dealing with the easy ones, for which they eased the rules of demay .
[Demai 1:3.17] “Wine for eye medication, flour to make into wound dressing, are obligated if they are certain and one does not have to mention that they are under the rules of demay . They themselves are free if certain.” Here you say, free if certain, and there you say, free from demay . Here it disappears by itself, there it disappears when used.
[Demai 1:3.18] Did we not state: “Eye medication from a pagan temple is forbidden to use?” There is a difference, since it is written ( Deut . 13:16 ): “Nothing banned should stick to your hands.” What is the difference between this and grape skins from Gentiles? Are these not also forbidden to use? But dried skins are not forbidden because of idolatrous use.
[Demai 1:3.19] “ From Akhzib and further on it is free from demay .” What is the status of Akhzib itself? It was stated ( Tosephta Demay 1:4 ): “Akhzib itself is free from demay .”
[Demai 1:3.20] “He who buys from a donkey caravan at Tyre and from the chest at Sidon is obligated.” Hence, from the donkey caravan at Sidon and from the chest at Tyre it is free. From a single donkey at Tyre. A donkey caravan that entered Tyre through Akhzib? Come and see, if it were standing at Akhziv it would be free, now that it entered Tyre would it be obligated?

[Demai 4:1.1] MISHNAH: He who buys produce from a person who is not trustworthy for tithes and forgot to tithe them may ask the seller on the Sabbath and eats on the seller’s information. [Demai 4:1.3] It was stated only for someone acting in error, not intentionally, as we have stated: If he forgot to tithe, if he had made no previous stipulation. But with a stipulation, one eats even on the stipulation by a friend.
[Demai 4:1.4] May one eat on the question of another person? How is that understood? If two persons bought at the same time from him, if one of them asked him, the other may not eat until he tithed or also asked; I say he tithed one batch, but not the other. If one person bought from him two fig cakes and asked him about one of them, he may not eat from the second cake until he tithed or asked him; I say that he tithed one but not the other. At nightfall when Sabbath ends, he tithes from one on the other. According to him who says that it is because of the glory of the Sabbath, this is fine. According to him who says that the fear of the Sabbath is on him, why should he be able to tithe from one on the other?
[Demai 4:1.5] So far, if he has nothing of the same kind. Even if he has of the same kind, that is a matter of preference.
[Demai 4:1.6] A holiday next to the Sabbath, be it before the Sabbath or after the Sabbath, and likewise the two holidays of the diaspora, according to him who says they are one sanctity, he may eat; according to him who says that they are two sanctities, he may not eat. Even according to him who says that they are two sanctities, he may eat as long as there was no possibility to tithe between them. It was stated: “If he asks him on the holiday, he eats on the Sabbath; if he asks him on the Sabbath, he eats on the holiday.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, explain it regarding produce he had intended to use on Sabbath eve. But produce he had not intended on Sabbath eve (to use during the Sabbath) is not included. {NAME} said, the words of the rabbis support {NAME}, my father, since we have stated there: “He who takes a vow regarding his friend that he will eat at his place but he does not trust him with the tithes.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: On the Sabbath of the preliminary marriage they permitted because of hatred. Is the Sabbath of the preliminary marriage not comparable to produce that on Sabbath eve he intended to use (later on the Sabbath)? Nevertheless, he only said “because of hatred.”
[Demai 4:1.7] If he invited him the first Sabbath but he did not come, the second time he should not eat unless he tithes or asks him. Did he not already ask him? {NAME} said, there he asked for himself. But here a third party asked about it.
[Demai 4:1.8] {NAME} asked: May he ask him in a roundabout way? {NAME} asks in this way. {NAME} bought wheat from {NAME}. He went to him and said, not that I suspect you, but since I bought wheat from you and I saw a multitude with you, I said maybe you forgot to put them in order. Were they put in order? He complained strongly about him and said: Why do you suspect me?
[Demai 4:1.9] It was stated: “Heave of the tithe from demay that returned to its origin makes dema ‘, not to its origin does not make dema ‘. {NAME} said, both at its origin and not at its origin it does not make dema ‘.” {NAME} asked before {NAME}: For one who says, it makes dema ‘, it makes dema ‘; for one who says, it does not make dema ‘, it does not make dema ‘; this is reasonable. But if one says, in its origin it makes dema ‘, not in its origin it does not make dema ‘; what is the difference between in its origin and not in its origin? {NAME} came up. They said, this one will say, “by Moses, I shall explain the reason.” He said, by Moses, I shall explain the reason: He who says, it makes dema ‘, because it permits the rest to be eaten. He who says, it does not make dema ‘, because it does not permit the rest to be eaten. {NAME} taught according to that of {NAME}. {NAME} said: A case came before {NAME} and he taught according to {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice does not follow {NAME}.

On the second Sabbath, even though he makes a vow to refuse any benefit from him, he shall not eat until he tithed.”

[Demai 4:3.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, nobody has to give a name to the tithe of the poor from demay . But the Sages say, he has to give a name but does not have to separate. He who gave a name to his heave of the tithe of demay , or to the certain tithe of the poor, should not separate them on the Sabbath. But if a Cohen or a poor person were used to eat from his food at his table, they may come and eat it on condition that he inform them.
[Demai 4:3.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of Rav: He who eats his produce without having separated the tithe of the poor commits a deadly sin. What is the reason of {NAME}? Because he knows that it would be a deadly sin, he will separate it. What is the reason of the rabbis? He only has to give a name but does not have to separate it.
[Demai 4:3.3] It was stated: He is trustworthy if they saw him separate the Second Tithe. It was stated: For the Second, he is trustworthy for the First, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, if he trustworthy for the First, he is trustworthy for the Second. He who is trustworthy for the Second is not trustworthy for the First. What is the reason of {NAME}? Is it because he is not suspected of advancing the tithe, or because if he separated the Second it is a standing presumption that he separated the First? But did we not state: “{NAME} says, nobody has to give a name to the tithe of the poor from demay. ” Hence, for the Second it is needed. Since he has to separate the Second, on which the owner earns no goodwill he certainly will separate the First, on which he earns goodwill!
[Demai 4:3.4] “If somebody brought out Second Tithe from his house to somebody and said: ‘It is redeemed,’ he is trustworthy; ‘redeem for me and yourself,’ he is not trustworthy.” The baraita is {NAME}, since {NAME} said, he who is trustworthy for the Second is trustworthy for the First. {NAME} said, everybody agrees, they made it like additions to First Fruits. Just as additions to First Fruits are eaten in purity and are free from demay , so this is eaten as Second Tithe and is free from the First. {NAME} confirmed in the name of {NAME}: it is {NAME}.
[Demai 4:3.5] This is the Mishnah: He should not hand them over on the Sabbath, since we have stated there: “The House of Shammai say that one does not bring ḥallah and gifts to the Cohen on a holiday, whether they were separated the day before or on the day itself, but the House of Hillel do permit this.” The first statement implies the second, the second implies the first. The first statement implies the second; there is no difference between holiday and Sabbath. The second implies the first; that is, if they are used to. But if they are not used to, no person comes to eat his piece of bread at another’s house.
[Demai 4:3.6] It was stated: “One should not importune anybody to be his guest if he knows that the other person will not accept. He should not offer many gifts of closeness if he knows that the other person will not accept.” What are gifts of closeness? He knows that the other person expects that he would exert himself for him. In Jerusalem one turned his clasp from left to right.

[Demai 4:5.1] MISHNAH: If someone enters a town, does not know anybody there, and asks: Who is trustworthy here, who tithes? [Demai 5:2.7] If somebody had 100 figs, 50 large ones and 50 small ones. If he takes from the large ones, should he take nine? If he takes from the small ones, should he take eleven? If he takes ten large ones, there might be one profane among them and we would worry lest perhaps he use that one to make it heave of the tithe for another place, but it is written ( Num. 18:26 ): “The heave of the Eternal, tithe from tithe,” not profane from tithe. {NAME} said, he stipulates and says, the tithe due from this produce should be fixed from the tip of each stem und continue until it reaches; in each of the ten there is heave of the tithe and a tiny bit of profane.
[Demai 5:2.8] That takes care of large quantities. If there was little, if he had ten figs, five large ones and five small ones? If he takes from the large ones, he has to take one minus a little. From the little ones, he has to take one plus a little. It would turn out that either he diminishes or increases the heave. Since he says, what is here on this side is profane ṭevel , whether he diminishes or increases the heave does not matter.

[Demai 6:1.1] MISHNAH: He who receives a field as sharecropper from a Jew, a Gentile, or a Samaritan, distributes in their presence. He who leases a field from a Jew separates heave and delivers to him. {NAME} says, when is that? When he gives from that field and from that kind. But if he gives from another field or from another kind, he must tithe and give him. He who leases a field from a Gentile tithes and delivers to him. {NAME} says, also he who is a sharecropper for a Gentile on a field that used to belong to his family tithes and delivers to him.
[Demai 6:1.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, these are the words of {NAME}. But the words of the Sages are: From a Jew, he splits; from a Gentile, he gives heave. We have stated: “He who leases a field from a Gentile separates heave and then gives to him. {NAME} said: If the Gentile does not wish to give heave, I have no right to it, but he distributes and puts it before him.”

[Demai 6:1.5] So far a Gentile; a Samaritan? [Demai 6:1.6] “If he received a field to harvest for wheat, grapes to harvest for wine, olives to harvest for oil, he tithes before he delivers.” Come and see: Before he sows, he separates heave; after it was sown, he tithes? {NAME} said, they made a special decree for the sharecropper, so that the Land of Israel should not lie fallow. But here it is already sown.
[Demai 6:1.7] “If he received a field to harvest for early ears, grapes to harvest for baskets of grapes, olives to harvest for baskets of olives, he delivers as is.” That means, if (he is paid) in the same kind; but from another field, or from that field but not from the same kind, he must tithe before he delivers. {NAME} stated: “From the same field, whether it be the same kind or another kind, he separates heave and delivers. From another field, whether it be the same kind or another kind, he tithes and delivers.” The Mishnah follows {NAME}; what {NAME} stated follows the Sages, and they disagree. We also may come and state that the Mishnah deals with some place where barley usually does not yield twice as much as wheat; what {NAME} stated refers to a place where barley usually yields twice as much as wheat.
[Demai 6:1.8] There you say, he separates heave and delivers to him. Here you say, he tithes and delivers to him. Can anybody make such a statement? But so it is, the Sages fined him who leases from a Gentile but they did not fine him who leases from a Jew. {NAME} said, the Sages did not fine him who leases from a Gentile; hence, if the Gentile converted or sold to another Jew, it is permitted.

[Demai 6:2.1] MISHNAH: A Cohen or a Levite who received a field (as sharecroppers) share in the tithe in the same proportion as they share in a profane yield. {NAME} says, the tithe is theirs because they came because of it.
[Demai 6:2.2] HALAKHAH: The rabbis object to {NAME}: How did they acquire? He said to them, do you not agree with me that if they agreed among themselves, tithes go to the workers? Even if they made a condition, how did they acquire? If there is nothing said, it is as if somebody said: Harvest from this land so that its tithes should be yours. They said to him, there is no stipulation here; if nothing is said there is no stipulation. It is as if he said, harvest this land on condition that you take one tenth for yourselves.
[Demai 6:2.3] It was stated: “A Cohen from a Cohen, a Levite from a Levite, an Israel from an Israel, split the tithes.” Who needs this statement? {NAME}; even though {NAME} says that the tithe is theirs because they came because of it, here he agrees that they divide up the tithes.
[Demai 6:2.4] “An Israel who received a field (as sharecropper) from a Cohen, if he said to him, on condition that the tithes be mine, or yours, or mine and yours; this is permitted. A Cohen who received a field (as sharecropper) from a Cohen, if he said to him, on condition that the tithes be mine, that is permitted. That they be yours, that is forbidden. That they be mine and yours, that is forbidden. If he received it under the standard sharecropping contract, it is permitted, otherwise it is forbidden.” Even without that, do not the tithes belong to them? But so it must read: “My part is mine, your part is mine and yours, if he received it under the standard sharecropping contract, it is permitted, otherwise it is forbidden.”
[Demai 6:2.5] “If an Israel received (as sharecropper) a field from another Israel on condition that the tithes go to a certain person, that clause is forbidden; on condition that I shall take them and deliver them to a certain person, that clause is permitted.” Is the second version not identical with the first? {NAME} said, “if you agree” makes the difference. {NAME} said, you say it is permitted if it follows the standard sharecropper’s contract. You say it is forbidden if it does not follow the standard sharecropper’s contract. It turns out that {NAME} holds with {NAME} and {NAME} with {NAME}. As {NAME} said, a person gives his tithes for the benefit of goodwill. {NAME} said, a person may not give his tithes for the benefit of goodwill. What is the reason of {NAME}? ( Num. 5:10 ) “Everybody shall be the owner of his holy things.” What does {NAME} with this? He may give them to whomever he likes.
[Demai 6:2.6] A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “A vow that no Cohanim or Levites should have any advantage from me, they should take against his will.” He explains it about a person who says, I cannot possibly give them any gifts. You should know that this is so, since we have stated: “ These Cohanim and Levites, let others take.” A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: “An Israel can say to another Israel, here you have a tetradrachma and give this first born to my daughter’s son, a Cohen.” He explains, if he already wanted to give it to two Cohanim and that daughter’s son was one of them; then one said, here you have a tetradrachma and give all of it to my daughter’s son, a Cohen.
[Demai 6:2.7] They asked before {NAME}, in that situation, a Cohen to an Israel, what is the rule? Because of the following, as it was stated: “Cohanim and Levites who help at the threshing floor have no right either to heave or to tithe, and if the farmer gave, it is desecrated, as it is said ( Lev. 22:15 ): ‘They should not desecrate the sanctified things of the Children of Israel,’ but they desecrate them! In addition, they said that their heave is no heave, their tithes are no tithes, their dedications are no dedications, and about them the verse says ( Micha 3:11 ): ‘Their heads judge for bribes and their priests come for a price.’ The Omnipresent brings over them three catastrophies; that is what is written ( Micha 3:12 ): ‘Therefore, because of you Zion will be ploughed over as a field, etc.’”
[Demai 6:2.8] A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If somebody marries giving heave, tithes, ‘gifts’, water for sprinkling, or ashes of the red heifer, she is married, even if the groom is Israel.” He explains it with heave he inherited from his maternal grandfather, a Cohen.
[Demai 6:2.9] “ If a Cohen sold a field to an Israel and made the condition that the tithes should be his, the tithes are his.” May he sell them to a Cohen? Let us hear from the following. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: He who sells the tithes of his field to another person did not do anything, the future children of his slave girl to another person, he did not do anything, the fetus of his animal to another person, he did not do anything, the airspace of his dry land to another person, he did not do anything. But he may sell him a field and reserve the tithes for himself, a slave girl and reserve her children for himself, an animal and reserve her fetus for himself. Is it not impossible for a person to sell the airspace of his dry land to another person? Explain it if he tells him, tear out some grasses in that dry land to acquire its airspace. And here there is real estate before him and he says, pluck something from the ground so that you acquire one tenth of it.
[Demai 6:2.10] “ If a Cohen sold a field to an Israel on condition that the tithes should be his, the tithes are his. Even for heirs whose claim is not from the Torah!
[Demai 6:2.11] “ That all tithes should be mine as long as you own it, he gets its tithes as long as the buyer owns it.” When he sold it to a third party, he has no tithes. If the buyer then bought it back from the third party, {NAME} states that he has no tithes, {NAME} states that the tithes are his. This disagreement turns out like the other disagreement, as we have stated there “that he who divorces his wife and then remarries her, remarries her on the basis of the first ketubah .” {NAME} stated before {NAME}: Two Amoraïm, one says for ketubah but not for individual stipulations, and the other says, both for ketubah and individual stipulations. For him who says, for ketubah but not for individual stipulations, he has the tithes. For him who says, both for ketubah and for individual stipulations, he has no tithes. But did we not state: “If somebody received (as sharecropper) from the daughter of a Cohen, she has the tithes. If she married an Israel, they split the tithes. If she was widowed or divorced, she returns to her prior status.” There when he sold, here when he received. But did not {NAME} state: “When she sold?” {NAME} said, there it left the power of both parties; here, it left the power of the seller but not that of the buyer.
[Demai 6:2.12] “A Cohen who sold a field to an Israel on condition that the tithes be his for four or five years can oppose the buyer’s planting it as a vineyard, sowing woad, or turning it into a field of reeds. [Demai 6:2.13] “If an Israel sold a field to a Cohen on condition that the tithes be his for four or five years, it is permitted. Forever, it is forbidden, since no Cohen can make a Cohen. [Demai 6:3.1] MISHNAH: If an Israel received (as sharecropper) from a Cohen or a Levite, the tithes are for the owners. {NAME} says, if a villager received a field from a Jerusalemite, the Second Tithe is the Jerusalemite’s. [Demai 6:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody receives olives to make oil, they split heave just as they split the profane. {NAME} says, if an Israel received olives from a Cohen or a Levite for oil or for half the yield as his wages, the tithes are for the landlords.

Now it seems that {NAME} is thinking like {NAME}, as {NAME} says, “the tithe is theirs because they came because of it.” So here, if a Cohen or a Levite received a field (as sharecroppers), the tithes are theirs because they came because of them.
[Demai 6:4.3] “ A cow of a Cohen that was put in an Israel’s care and gave birth to a firstborn calf, the firstborn calf is the Cohen’s, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, the firstborn is their common property. {NAME} said to them, do you not agree with me that the tithes of his field are his? They said to him, because the body of the field is his property, but the body of the cow is joint property. If the body of the cow were sole property of the Cohen, the firstborn would be the Cohen’s.” We have stated accordingly, “ put in care means joint responsibility, selling is the sole responsibility of him who gives.”
[Demai 6:4.4] “If a Cohen gave money to an Israel to buy produce for half the profit and he (the Cohen) said to him: If they go up or down in price, it is on my account, and the tithes are yours, this is permitted. If an Israel gave money to a Cohen to buy produce for half the profit and he (the Israel) said to him: If they go up or down in price, it is on my account, and the tithes are yours, if he had paid the wages, it is permitted, otherwise it is forbidden. An Israel who sold olives against 60 log of ṭevel . If one said to him, sell them to me and I shall give you 60 log that are in order, that is permitted. 60 log ṭevel , and both of us will share in the tithes, that is forbiden.” If he gives him everything, it is permitted, if he gives him half, it is forbidden? {NAME} said, if he extends credit to him. We also have stated in this respect: If he extends credit to him it is forbidden because of interest and because of degradation of holy things.
[Demai 6:5.1] MISHNAH: The House of Shammai say, one should sell one’s olives only to a ḥaver . The House of Hillel say, also to one who tithes. But the modest ones of the House of Hillel used to follow the words of the House of Shammai. If two people put the yield of their vineyards into one wine press and one tithes but the other does not, then he who tithes must tithe his own and what could be his at any place.
[Demai 6:5.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, the reason of the House of Hillel is that people eat from their olives while they are being loaded into the oil vat, as a subterfuge. The House of Hillel follow their own opinion, as we have stated: “One should not sell him a ploughing cow in the Sabbatical year, but the House of Hillel permit this because he may slaughter it.” Do people really slaughter their cattle? As a subterfuge. They agree that one may sell ears of grain for dough even though one knows that the buyer will not prepare the dough in purity.
[Demai 6:5.3] It was stated: “They agree that one does not sell a wheat stack, a grape vat, or an olive vat to anybody but a ḥaver or to somebody who is known to process in purity.” Is the grape vat not from the Torah? This does not disagree with {NAME}; just as {NAME} said, the little one is a restriction, so “vat of olives” is a restriction. {NAME} said to {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They disagree about connections. Because everywhere “biting” is a connection, squeezing is not a connection. Then the olive vat should be from the Torah! What about this? Explain it following {NAME}, since {NAME} said, sap is counted as a fluid.
[Demai 6:5.4] {NAME} said, the reason of the House of Shammai is that a ḥaver should never sell olives to anybody but one who tithes.
[Demai 6:5.5] Who are the modest ones? Those of noble conduct. {NAME} said, here we have taught that those of noble conduct are called modest.
