[Demai 6:6.1] MISHNAH: If two people received a field as sharecroppers or inherited it or bought it as partners, one can say to his partner, take your wheat on this side and I shall take on that side, take your wine from this side and I shall take from the other side. But he should not say to him, take the wheat and I shall take the barley, take the wine and I shall take the oil. If a ḥaver and an am haäreẓ inherited from their am haäreẓ father, the ḥaver may say, take your wheat on this side and I shall take on that side, take wine from this side and I shall take from the other side. But he should not say to him, take wheat and I shall take barley, take the moist produce and I shall take the dry.
[Demai 6:6.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: “If a Jew and a Gentile bought a field in Syria, it is as if ṭevel and tithed produce were mixed together, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} says, the Jew’s part is obligated, the Gentile’s part is free.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: When do they disagree? If they split the field while the grain was standing. But if they split grain stacks, even {NAME} will agree with Rebbi that every single stalk belongs to the partnership. {NAME} said, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: When do they disagree? If they split the field while the grain was standing. But if they split sheaves, even {NAME} will agree with Rebbi that every single stalk belongs to the partnership. According to {NAME}, what is the difference between stacks and sheaves? If he harvests a small amount and shares with his partner. {NAME} said, that is, if they bought with the idea that they would not split. But if they bought with the idea that they always would split, Rebbi will agree with {NAME} that his part already belonged to him from the first moment. {NAME} said, the words of the rabbis disagree since {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said that partners are the subject of the disagreement between Rebbi and {NAME}. Are brothers who split not like these partners?
[Demai 6:7.1] MISHNAH: If a proselyte and a Gentile inherited from their Gentile father, the proselyte may say, take the idols and I shall take money, take the wine for libations and I shall take produce. After they came into the proselyte’s possession, this is forbidden. He who sells produce in Syria and says: ‘They are from the Land of Israel,’ must tithe them. ‘They are tithed,’ one believes him because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permits. ‘They are from my field,’ he must tithe them. ‘They are tithed,’ one believes him because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permits. If it is known that he has a field in Syria, he must tithe.
[Demai 6:7.2] HALAKHAH: a Jew and a Gentile bought a Gentile’s house and found there idols, libation wine, and coins, he should not tell him, take the idols and libation wine, and I shall take the coins.” {NAME} said, not only idols, libation wine, and coins, but even if there were two idols, one shaped as a tripod and one not shaped as a tripod, he should not tell him, take the one that is not shaped as a tripod and I shall take the one shaped like a tripod. {NAME} said, that is correct, since even in the case of a ḥaver and an am haäreẓ who inherited from their am haäreẓ father and found there produce which might become impure and produce which might not, may he say to him, you take the produce which might become impure and I shall take that which might not? But our Mishnah disagrees: “Take the idols and I shall take money, take the wine for libations and I shall take produce.” But the end shows that there is no disagreement: “After they came into the possession of the proselyte, this is forbidden;” here, from the moment he acquired it it is as if it entered into his possession.
[Demai 6:7.3] “Aquila the Proselyte split with his brothers; he restricted himself and brought his gain to the Dead Sea.” Three Amoraïm; one said that he brought the price of the idols to the Dead Sea, another said that he brought the price of his part in the idols to the Dead Sea, and another said that he brought the idols themselves to the Dead Sea, in order to remove them from his father’s house.
[Demai 6:8.1] MISHNAH: An am haäreẓ who said to a ḥaver , buy for me a bunch of vegetables, buy for me a loaf, if he buys anonymously, he is free. If he says, this one is for me and that one is for my friend, if they became mixed up he has to tithe, even if there are a hundred.
[Demai 6:8.2] HALAKHAH: : There, we have stated: “They can be trusted about gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and peah at harvest time.” And here you say so? There, his assertion is for exemption, but here his assertion is for obligation. And we have stated so: “If his assertion is for exemption, he may be trusted in restrictions.” But here, he can be trusted even if his explanation is to make it easier.
[Demai 6:8.3] It was stated: “A Gentile who was calling out, ‘come and buy fruits from me, they are from an orlah tree, they are from a vineyard in its fourth year,’ cannot be believed. If he says, ‘I brought them from a certain Gentile,’ he may be trusted for restrictions, the words of Rebbi. The Sages say, the words of a Gentile are irrelevant.” {NAME} asked, what if he calls out when he is uninformed? {NAME} asked, what if one holds that a Samaritan is like a Gentile, since they disagreed: “A Samaritan is like a Gentile, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} says, a Samaritan is like a Jew in all respects”?
[Demai 6:8.4] {NAME} said, that is only if most of what he takes in comes from his own.
[Demai 6:8.5] If a Jew had a sharecropper in Syria who sent him fruits and said that they were tithed; I say that he bought them on the market, if that kind is found on the market. Not only if he does not grow that kind on his field, but even if he does grow that kind on his field; since that kind is found on the market it is permitted.
[Demai 6:8.6] Our Mishnah follows {NAME}, as we have stated: “He who buys anonymously has to tithe.” What are we talking about? If he said to him, go and buy for me, he is his agent; go and buy for yourself, they are his property. But in our case nothing was spelled out. {NAME} says that the seller wants the person who buys to get the property rights, {NAME} says that the seller wants the owner of the money to get the property rights. Therefore, if he added a piece, {NAME} says, it belongs to the buyer, {NAME} says, it belongs to both of them. The argument of {NAME} seems to be inverted. There he says that the seller wants the owner of the money to get the property rights, and here you say so? Here the transaction is through the money of one and the feet of the other, therefore they split.
[Demai 6:8.7] It was stated: “{NAME} says, if he exchanged the coin he has to tithe.” {NAME} said, this means that if somebody gives coins to another person to exchange them, when they are lost the recipient is answerable for their alienation.
[Demai 6:8.8] {NAME} says, if he distributes it himself. {NAME} said, only if he took his share last. {NAME} said, both statements are necessary. If he distributes it himself and took his share first he only has to tithe his share. If he did not distribute it but took his share last, he only has to tithe his share.
[Demai 6:8.9] It was stated: “One may say to his worker: Here you have a denar, use it for food, here you have a denar, use it for drink, and not be worried about either the Sabbatical year, tithes, or wine for libations. But if he told him, go and buy yourself a loaf and I shall give you the money, go and buy yourself a reviït of wine and I shall give you the money, he has to worry because of the Sabbatical year, tithes, and wine used for libations.” {NAME} said, the grocer becomes the plenipotentiary of the employer to let the worker acquire. {NAME} said, the worker acquired for the employer from the grocer and then acquires it himself. What is the difference between them? If the grocer was deaf-mute. According to {NAME}, he does not have to worry because a deaf-mute cannot become a plenipotentiary; according to {NAME}, he has to worry.
[Demai 6:8.10] It was stated: “A person should not say to his friend, here you have 200 zuz and pay for me to the treasury, but he says to him, free me from the treasury. Similarly, a person should not say to his friend, here you have 200 zuz and pay the leiturgia , but he says to him, free me from the leiturgia .”
[Demai 7:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody invites his friend for a meal but the latter does not trust him with tithes, the friend should say on Friday eve: That which I will separate in the future shall be tithe, the rest of tithe near to it. That which I made tithe shall be the heave of the tithe for everything, and the Second Tithe shall be to the North (or South) and be redeemed by coins.
[Demai 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said: The Mishnah deals with demay . Hence, not with certain produce? A Mishnah says, even for certain produce, as we have stated there: “If he had ṭevel figs in his house and he was in the House of Study or on the field.” If you want to say that we deal with demay , you cannot do so, since it is stated: “If it was demay .” What {NAME} said was that it deals with demay . He did not say, not with certain produce, but that this Mishnah deals with demay . What is the difference between demay and certain produce? For demay , a person may make a proviso for something that is not in his possession; for certain produce, he may only make a proviso for something that is in his possession.
[Demai 7:1.3] {NAME} had made a proviso for certain produce. He asked the Great {NAME}, may one fix this on the Sabbath? He said to him ( Deut . 14:23 ): “That you should learn to fear the Eternal, your God, all the days,” including the Sabbath. How did you see a way to be so lenient, my initiative depends on me! He said to him, in the future you will carry leadership in Israel.
[Demai 7:1.4] {NAME} had made a proviso for certain produce. One woman cooked vegetables she had forgotten to put in order. She came to {NAME} who sent {NAME} to put it in order for him and for her. {NAME} asked, would {NAME} not have to give {NAME} property rights on these vegetables? {NAME} asked, where do we hold? If his proviso was meant for him and for others, he does not have to give him property rights on the vegetable. If his proviso was not meant for him and for others, he has to give him property rights on the vegetable. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It was answered, {NAME} did not give {NAME} property rights on the vegetable.
[Demai 7:1.5] {NAME} said, he must remember his proviso. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, he must whisper with his lips.
[Demai 7:1.6] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is he not like somebody who makes repairs on the Sabbath? He said to him, because of his proviso. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is it not forbidden because of destruction of edibles? He said to him, he crumbles a small amount and eats. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is it not forbidden because of robbery? He said to him, the host desires the satisfaction of his guest.
[Demai 7:1.7] The words of the rabbis disagree since {NAME} said: Rebbi and {NAME} were guests of a private person. Evil rumors told the latter, watch out, they are suspecting you! He sat near them and was watching them. They pretended to throw food against each other and in that way were putting the food in order. Does he not desire their satisfaction? He does, but he does not want to be suspected.
[Demai 7:1.8] It was stated: “{NAME} forbids.” What is the reason of {NAME}? Can a person make a proviso about something not in his possession? “But {NAME} agrees that he may go, buy from the place from which his host bought, and tithe.” Can a person give for something that is not his? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: they considered him as one who sold ṭevel produce to another person, as was stated: “He who sells ṭevel produce to another person has to run after him and put the produce in order. If he does not find him, if it is known that the produce still exists, he has to tithe for him; if not, he does not have to tithe for him. If it is doubtful whether the produce exists or not, he tithes for it and gives a name to the tithes.”
[Demai 7:2.1] MISHNAH: When they mixed him a cup, he says: What I shall leave at the rim of the cup shall be tithe, the rest of tithe near to it. What I made tithe shall be the heave of the tithe for everything, and the Second Tithe shall be on its top and be redeemed by coins.
[Demai 7:2.2] HALAKHAH: So is the Mishnah: Concerning the mixing of the cup.
[Demai 7:2.3] Where are we at? If he says it beforehand, the drink is mixed. If he says, when I shall have drunk, before that he drank ṭevel . What we are dealing with is that he says beforehand: When I shall have drunk. But does he then not move impure heave on the Sabbath? {NAME} said, he leaves some profane, as what we have stated there: “One moves pure heave with impure one and with profane food.” But that does not compare. There, the impure is for the needs of the pure, but here the profane is for the needs of the impure. {NAME} said, when he sets down the cup it will be holy.
[Demai 7:2.4] There, we have stated: “Is somebody buys wine from the Samaritans.” It was stated: “{NAME} and {NAME} forbid it, for the wine bag may spring a leak and it will turn out retroactively that he drank ṭevel .” Is our Mishnah not following {NAME} and {NAME}? {NAME} said, all agree that the cup is at its place.
[Demai 7:3.1] MISHNAH: A worker who does not believe his employer takes one dried fig and says: This one and the next nine shall be tithe for ninety that I shall eat. This one is made heave of the tithe for them. The Second Tithe is at the end and it is redeemed by a coin. He saves one fig. {NAME} says, he should not save because he reduces the work he will be able to do for his employer. But {NAME} said, he should not save because that is a stipulation of the Court.
[Demai 7:3.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They considered him a worker who does not trust his employer. The following is obvious: If the produce was burned, the heave is ṭevel . If the heave is burned, when the produce is eaten the heave will have been sanctified retroactively.
[Demai 7:3.3] What did he save? From his food he separates the heave of the tithe.
[Demai 7:3.4] It was stated: “A man should not plough with his cow at night and rent her out during the day, he should not work for himself at night and rent himself out during the day, he should not starve himself and not torment himself because he reduces the work he will be able to do for his employer.”
[Demai 7:3.5] {NAME} went to some place where he found the schoolteacher weak. He asked them, what has happened? They said to him, he is fasting. He said to him, that is forbidden to you. If one says that it is forbidden for the work one does for flesh and blood, so much more for the work of the Holy One, praise to Him!
[Demai 7:3.6] {NAME} in the name of Rav: It is a stipulation of the Court that the heave of the tithe should be from the worker and the Second Tithe from the employer.
[Demai 7:4.1] MISHNAH: If someone buys wine from Samaritans he may say: Two log that I shall separate in the future are heave, ten tithe, and nine Second Tithe; then he redeems and drinks.
[Demai 7:4.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: “{NAME} and {NAME} prohibit to do so, maybe the wine bag will spring a leak and it turns out retroactively that he drank ṭevel .” But the reason of one is not the reason of the other. The reason of {NAME} is that maybe he will pour. The reason of {NAME} is that maybe he will forget and drink the remainder. As it was stated: “The Second Tithe in this container should be redeemed by the tetradrachma in that wallet, it is redeemed. {NAME} says, it is not redeemed.” What is the reason of {NAME}? “ If he said, the old tetradrachma or the old denar, he did redeem. The Sages admit to {NAME} that if he said, the tetradrachma I shall take from my son’s hand, or the denar I shall take from my son’s hand, it is not redeemed since it was not in his hand at that time.”
[Demai 7:4.3] There, we have stated: “If somebody puts aside produce … to serve for Second Tithe.” Does that Mishnah disagree with {NAME} and {NAME}? {NAME} said, there they become spoiled retroactively, but here they become spoiled only starting from the moment of loss.
[Demai 7:4.4] There, we have stated: “If a peruṭah of Temple property fell into somebody’s wallet, or if somebody said, a peruṭah in this wallet shall be Temple property,” it was stated that “with the first coin he committed probable larceny, with the second one certain larceny, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, with any of them he committed probable larceny, except that with the last one he committed certain larceny.” {NAME}, {NAME} said, that is, if there were ten coins. But if there were only two, with the first coin he committed probable larceny, with the second one certain larceny. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: What is the difference between him who says “in the wallet” and him who says “from the wallet?” {NAME} said, even if he spent the entire wallet he would not have committed larceny; just as you say ‘that he drank ṭevel retroactively,’ here also ‘retroactively he spent profane money.’ But here it depends on the act of separation. {NAME} said, in both cases it depends on the act of separation; it is as if he said, this wallet should not be freed from a peruṭah of Temple property. {NAME} argument is inverted. There, he says that one commits larceny with a peruṭah corresponding to the computation of three log . And here, he says so? After he asked, he returned and gave the simple answer.
[Demai 7:4.5] {NAME} said, a person can say on Friday, this shall be heave tomorrow, but nobody can say on the Sabbath, this shall be heave tomorrow. {NAME} said, nobody can say on Friday, this shall be heave tomorrow. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If a vessel was immersed that day and somebody filled it from an amphora with ṭevel tithe, if he said, its contents should be heave of the tithe tomorrow, i. e., after nightfall, then this is heave. If he said, that should be eruv , he did not say anything.” Explain it if he transgressed. But {NAME} stated: “He says,” and you say, if he transgressed? {NAME} retracted that.
[Demai 7:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody had ṭevel figs in his house but was in the House of Study or on the field, he says: Two figs that I shall separate in the future shall be heave, ten tithe, and nine heave of the tithe. If they were demay , he says: That which I shall separate in the future shall be tithe tomorrow, the rest of tithe near to it. That which I made tithe shall be heave of the tithe for all, and the Second Tithe shall be to the North (or to the South) and be redeemed by coins.
[Demai 7:5.2] HALAKHAH: What is done? ‘From before I shall separate it.’ Think about it, if it was pure heave, ‘from before I shall eat it.’ Think about it, if it was impure heave, ‘from before I shall deposit it in a corner.’
[Demai 7:5.3] We have stated: “One may move both pure and impure heave.” {NAME} said, it means that one is permitted to move ṭevel that has a condition on it on the Sabbath. What does he do? He thinks about a part of it and eats the rest.
[Demai 7:6.1] MISHNAH: If he had before him two baskets of ṭevel and he said, the tithes of one are in the other and those of the other in the one, the first one is tithed; (if he said) their tithes are tithes of each basket in the other one, he gave it a name.
[Demai 7:6.2] HALAKHAH: 8: We have stated for this: “He takes from the second one two figs and two tenths and a tenth of a tenth.” {NAME} says, you cannot state that; when he takes one in ten he has to take one in a hundred, when he takes one in a hundred he has to take one in a thousand, when he takes one in a thousand he has to take one in ten thousand.
[Demai 7:6.3] {NAME} said, for the first basket he transgresses a commandment, for the second a commandment and a prohibition. For the first basket he transgresses a commandment since he gave both names simultaneously, and for the second a commandment and a prohibition since he gave both names simultaneously and he put the Second Tithe of the first basket before the First Tithe of the second basket.
[Demai 7:6.4] {NAME} said, this is from {NAME} since {NAME} says that you accept only the very first version. There, we have stated: “This one shall be a substitute for a burnt offering and for an offering of well-being, then it is a substitute for a burnt offering, the words of {NAME}.” {NAME} said, we were of the opinion that {NAME} and the Sages disagree only after the time for speech, but not within the time for speech. Since {NAME} said, the Mishnah is {NAME}, it means that even within the time of speech he cannot retract.
[Demai 7:6.5] This is the Mishnah: “Their tithes are tithes for each basket in the other one, he gave it a name,” because he declared both names at the same time. One after the other you accept only the very first version. {NAME} said, the Sages agree with {NAME} about him who says “this heave substitutes for Second” (that he is guilty). “This animal instead of well-being offerings,” he is obligated for two since he declared two names at the same time; hence, one after the other you accept only the very first version. Not so, said {NAME} who said in the name of {NAME}: “This one shall be a substitute for a burnt offering,” he may retract that within the time for speech. That is, if he wants to retract, there if he wants to add. If one said, “this is heave,” even within the time of speech he cannot retract. A person can be asked about his dedication but nobody can be asked about his heave.
[Demai 7:6.6] How does one act? “One takes 20 figs from any basket one chooses.” And in any 10 one takes there is one of heave of the tithe. That is, if they were equal. “If in one basket there were 100 and in the other 200, if he takes for the one with a hundred, he takes 11. If for the one with 200 he takes 30. “If in one basket there were 100 and in the other 1000, if he takes for the one with a hundred, he takes 15. If for the one with a thousand, even if he takes the entire basket he does not complete taking.”
[Demai 7:6.7] “ If someone has a basket and wants to tithe it, he takes two ninths and a ninth of a ninth, corresponding to ten tithe and nine Second Tithe.” Why does he not say 19? {NAME} said, the words of the Sages and their riddles. He who wants to bring a hundred figs in order into his house takes for ever single fig two ninths and a ninth of a ninth, 23 figs in all, four called ninth of a ninth.
[Demai 7:7.1] MISHNAH: A hundred ṭevel in a hundred profane, he removes 101. A hundred ṭevel in a hundred tithe, he removes 101. A hundred profane fully in order and a hundred tithe, he removes 110. A hundred ṭevel and ninety tithe, ninety ṭevel and eighty tithe, he did not lose anything. That is the rule: Anytime that ṭevel is more, he did not lose anything.
[Demai 7:7.2] HALAKHAH: : {NAME} said, one has to specify a stipulation and say: If ṭevel is in my hands, it shall be tithe, but if tithe is in my hands, it shall be heave of the tithe. {NAME} said, one has to add the converse stipulation and say, otherwise I did not do anything. {NAME} said, one does not have to add the converse stipulation. Either one of them follows his own opinion, since they disagreed: Two heaps of grain, in one of them. {NAME} said, they are both forbidden as dema‘ , but {NAME} said, they are not forbidden.
[Demai 7:7.3] {NAME} said, they differ with {NAME}. As he stated: “ Ṭevel mixed with profane produce, if it can be provided from another place, one takes it out in proportion. Otherwise, {NAME} says, he gives a name to the heave of the tithe and takes it out by 101.” {NAME} said, explain it with kinds one cannot take out. {NAME} asked: Why can he not crack them? {NAME} said, is one permitted to crack them? Did we not state: “If the nuts were cracked,” in the past. That means, not to start out with.
[Demai 7:7.4] {NAME} said, so is the Mishnah: Anytime that ṭevel is more than the tithe, tithe does not lose anything.
[Demai 7:7.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Any ṭevel mentioned here is ṭevel for first and second tithes.
[Demai 7:7.6] {NAME} said, Rebbi and {NAME} disagree. One says, he takes the second tithe from another place, but the other one says, he makes all of it second tithe and takes the first tithe from another place. What are we talking about? “A hundred ṭevel and ninety tithe, he takes 92 minus one tenth. A hundred ṭevel and eighty tithe, he takes 83 minus two tenths. Other quantities proportionally.”
[Demai 7:8.1] MISHNAH: If somebody had ten rows of ten wine jugs each, and he said that one from an outer row was tithe but he does no longer know which one, he takes two diagonally opposite amphoras. One of half an outer row was tithe but he does no longer know which one, then he takes the four amphoras at the four corners. One row was tithe but he does no longer know which one, then he takes one diagonal row. Half a row was tithe but he does no longer know which one, then he takes from the two diagonal rows. One amphora was tithe but he does no longer know which one, then he takes from each amphora.
[Demai 7:8.2] HALAKHAH: Why does he not take two? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: When he separated half of the heave from another place.
[Demai 7:8.3] It was stated: “If there were two amphoras before him, one of pure tithe which was ṭevel and one of impure tithe which was ṭevel , he brings two vessels and takes from each of them heave of the tithe for both of them. He then turns and lifts one vessel and says: If this one is pure, I am making it heave of the tithe; else I did not do anything. Then he turns, does the same for the second vessel, immerses himself and drinks, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} says, he takes it only at the end.” What is the reason of Rebbi? I say, maybe he started drinking the impure one first. And what is the reason of {NAME}? Maybe he drank the impure one at the end. Everybody agrees that he who drinks impure liquids may not even eat heave that is in doubt. If the liquids were possibly impure, everybody agrees that he may eat what certainly is heave. But here we deal with another Mishnah. What is the reason of {NAME}? Since according to both the impurity is certain, he needs immersion. What is the reason of Rebbi? That he should not be led into drinking a reviït . According to the reason of {NAME}, he drinks less than a reviït . Is {NAME} not afraid that he would be led into drinking a reviït ? {NAME} said, the only explanation you have is our first one. Rebbi is afraid that he drank the impure liquid first and {NAME} is afraid that he drank the impure liquid at the end.

[Kilayim 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Wheat and zěwānîn are not kilaim one with the other. Barley and fox tail, spelt and oats, beans and Indian peas and grass peas and chick peas and fava beans and green beans are not kilaim one with the other.
[Kilayim 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: It is written: ( Lev . 19:19 ) “you should not sow your field kilaim ;” I could think, even two kinds of wheat or two kinds of barley. “You should not breed your animals kilaim ;” I could think, even black on white cattle, or white on black cattle. “And kilaim cloth, שעטנז, should not be worn by you;” I could think, even two kinds of wool or two kinds of linen. It was made explicit about garments, ( Deut . 22:11 ) “do not wear שעטנז, wool and linen together.” Just as for garments where I forbade you two kinds, neither one is of the genus of the other, so kilaim that I forbade you at any place, neither one is of the genus of the other.
[Kilayim 1:1.3] “Wheat and zĕwānîn are not kilaim one with the other.” Hence, with barley they would constitute kilaim . “Wheat and zĕwānîn are not kilaim one with the other;” could anybody err about something that is not food and state it as kilaim ? {NAME} said, because there are places where they are collected as food for pigeons. {NAME} said, this follows {NAME}, as we have stated there: “If somebody lets thorns grow in his vineyard, they become ‘sanctified’, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, they do not become ‘sanctified’.” {NAME} said, the reason of {NAME} is that at some places in Arabia one stores them for camels. Does this imply that the Sages think that there are no places in Arabia where one stores them for the camels? Let them check it out! The Sages say, where one stores them they are forbidden, but at places where one does not store them they are permitted. But {NAME} cannot follow {NAME}! There, people do not transport horns from place to place. But here, people do transport zewānîn from place to place.
[Kilayim 1:1.4] If so, should they not be kilaim with wheat? {NAME} said, they are a kind of wheat but the fruits went astray. As it was stated: ( Lev . 19:29 ) “The Land should not go whoring,” from here that produce may go astray.
[Kilayim 1:1.5] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is our Mishnah from {NAME}? As it was stated: “{NAME} says in the name of his father that one may take heave from wine on vinegar but not from vinegar on wine. If somebody transgressed, his heave is heave. Rebbi says that wine and vinegar are two distinct kinds and one does not give heave nor does one tithe from one on the other.” He was looking at him. He said to him, what are you staring at me? Bring a lash for yourself; there it is for tithing, here it is for kilaim . {NAME} said, he should not have stared at him since the earlier rabbis wanted to understand this matter and understood that there it refers to tithing but here to kilaim .
[Kilayim 1:1.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: All of these form pairs. Has that been said for the entire Chapter, or only for this Halakhah? From what Rav said, that the five vegetables with which one may satisfy one’s obligation at Passover time can all be sown in one vegetable bed, and one says that the statement of Rav disagrees with {NAME}, it follows that it has been said for the entire Chapter. {NAME} in the name of Rav: All have been stated in pairs. The reasoning of Rav is inverted; there he says that they all constitute one kind, and here, he says so? No, Rav did not say that they all constitute one kind, but rather that they all are kinds of vegetables that may be sown in one vegetable bed.
[Kilayim 1:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, they found written in the notebook of {NAME}; {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, they found written on the wall of {NAME}: Beans, πίσον, chick peas, mlwt’ , krpwnh , climbing beans.
[Kilayim 1:1.8] So is the Mishnah: Fava beans and string beans. {NAME} said, why is it called שעוּעית? Because if makes the heart happy and the intestines going.
[Kilayim 1:2.1] MISHNAH: Green melon and sweet melon are not kilaim one with the other. {NAME} says, they are kilaim . Lettuce and garden lettuce, endives and field endives, leeks and field leeks, coriander and field coriander, mustard and Egyptian mustard, Egyptian pumpkin and ash-gourd, Egyptian beans and carob beans are not kilaim one with the other.
[Kilayim 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said: The opinion of the Sages is that one takes a small piece from the pericarp of a green melon and plants it and it grows to a water melon. One takes a small piece from the pericarp of a water melon and plants it and it grows to a sweet melon. {NAME} says, it in itself is kilaim . One takes a small piece from the pericarp of a water melon and a small piece from the pericarp of an apple and puts them into one cavity where they unite and become kilaim . Therefore it is called “apple melon” in the Greek language.
[Kilayim 1:2.3] What does {NAME} say about green melon and water melon? Let us hear from the following: “Green melon, water melon, and sweet melon are not kilaim [if combined] one with the other; {NAME} says, they are kilaim .” It has been said that green melon and water melon are not kilaim one with the other, and water melon and sweet melon are not kilaim one with the other; {NAME} says they are kilaim . Green melon and water melon are questionable.
[Kilayim 1:2.4] “Lettuce and garden lettuce.” {NAME} said, roof lettuce. Simeon, {NAME}, said, Antiochian (lettuce.) {NAME} said, sweet yase . Endives may be eaten raw, field endives are ‘ ulthin . Leeks. Fields leeks are κεφαλωτόν.
[Kilayim 1:2.5] “Egyptian gourd.” Our Mishnah does not follow {NAME}. In the name of {NAME}: Aramean gourd is Egyptian gourd; it is kilaim with Greek gourd, kilaim with ash-gourd.
[Kilayim 1:2.6] “Ash gourd.” {NAME} said, it is a kind of bitter gourd and they sweeten it in hot ashes.
[Kilayim 1:2.7] “And carob beans.” {NAME} said, they are a kind of Egyptian - Persian beans and their pods look like carob.
[Kilayim 1:3.1] MISHNAH: Turnips and naphew, cabbage and cauliflower, beets and orach, are not kilaim one with the other. {NAME} added that garlic and dwarf garlic, onion and dwarf onion, lupine and wild lupine are not kilaim one with the other.
[Kilayim 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Turnips and naphew, cabbage and cauliflower,” thin cabbage. “Beets and orach,” orach. “{NAME} added garlic and dwarf garlic,” little garlic. “Onion and dwarf onion,” little “radish.” “Lupine and wild lupine,” pdmw‘h , are not kilaim one with the other
[Kilayim 1:4.1] MISHNAH: Among trees, pears and golden apples, quince and sorbs are not kilaim one with the other. Apple and ḥizrar , peaches and almonds, jujubes and lotus fruit, even though they resemble one another, they are kilaim one with the other.
[Kilayim 1:4.2] HALAKHAH: “Quince.” {NAME} said, quince. Why are they called “prepared”, because there is no tree only producing for the pot except that kind.
[Kilayim 1:4.3] Salman the Levite, the brother of Zavdi the Levite, in the name of {NAME}: All statements are pair by pair. Rav said, all are one kind. A baraitha disagrees with Rav, for we have stated: also the baka-bush. {NAME} objected, did we not also state oregano?
[Kilayim 1:4.4] “ They used to graft quince onto pears in the markets of Sepphoris. A student saw them and said to them, you are forbidden [to do so.] They went and cut them down. Then they went and asked at Jabneh. They said to them, the one who hit you was from the students of the House of Shammai.” It says only, quince on a pear tree. Hence, not a pear tree on a ḥizrar .
[Kilayim 1:4.5] “ In the region of Ariaḥ they grafted apple on ḥizrar . A student came and told them, this is forbidden to you. They went, cut them down, and came to ask at Jabneh. They said to them, that student said correctly.” He said only, apple on ḥizrar . Hence, not about ḥizrar on pear? What the occasions were, they were.
[Kilayim 1:4.6] It was stated: If a Gentile grafted walnut on a peach stump, a Jew, even though he is not permitted to do this, may take a shoot and go and plant it at another location. What results from them? Persian qdryh . If he crosses beet and purslain, a Jew, even though he is not permitted to do this, may take a seed and go and plant it at another location. What results from them? Groundsel. Zargun and turnips, what results from them? Parsley. Almonds and terebinths, what results from them? Pistachios. Olive trees and pomegranate trees, what results from them? Zizyphus .
[Kilayim 1:5.1] MISHNAH: Radish and naphew, mustard and hoar-hound; Greek gourd with the Egyptian and ash ones, even though they look similar, are kilaim one with the other.
[Kilayim 1:5.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, there are some where they considered the fruit, and there are some where they considered the leaves. Turnips and radish, they went in their regard after the fruit. Turnips and naphew, they considered after the leaves. They objected: But radish and naphew have similar fruits and similar leaves, and you say, they are kilaim ? {NAME} said, in that case, they considered the taste of the produce.
[Kilayim 1:6.1] MISHNAH: Wolf and dog, rural dog and fox, goat and deer, mountain goats and sheep, horse and mule, mule and donkey, donkey and wild donkey, even though they look similar, they are kilaim one with the other.

Even though {NAME} says that the dog is a domesticated animal, he agrees that the rural dog is a wild animal. Hence, according to {NAME}, dog and rural dog are kilaim .

[Kilayim 1:7.1] MISHNAH: One does not bring a tree on a tree, a vegetable on a vegetable, and neither a tree on a vegetable nor a vegetable on a tree. {NAME} permits vegetable on tree.
[Kilayim 1:7.2] HALAKHAH: The opinion of {NAME} seems inverted. There, he says that a man takes a small piece from the pericarp of a water melonand a small piece from the pericarp of an apple, places them into one cavity where they unite and become kilaim , and here he says so? There, because he places them so that they touch one another, unite and become kilaim , but here it is vegetable on tree.
[Kilayim 1:7.3] It was stated: From where that one may not graft a tree bearing no edible fruit onto a fruit-bearing tree, or a fruit-bearing tree onto another fruit-bearing tree of a kind that is not his own kind, from where? If it is so, is should be forbidden to graft a black fig tree on a white fig tree. {NAME} said, did you not infer the rules from kilaim of textiles? Just as for kilaim of textiles two kinds, not one from this kind and the other from the other kind, also any other kilaim that I forbade you, not one from this kind and the other from the other kind.
[Kilayim 1:7.4] It was stated in the name of {NAME}: “The Gentile may sow and wear kilaim , but he may not mate his animals as kilaim or graft his tree kilaim .” Why? Because about these, it is written “by their kinds.” But is it not also written for grasses “by their kinds?” It is not written for the commandment, only at the realization. If this is so, why was Earth cursed? {NAME} said, because it transgressed the orders of the Holy One, praise to Him! ( Gen . 1:11 ) “The earth should produce lawns, grasses producing seed,” but it produced only ( Gen . 1:12 ) “lawns, grasses producing seed by their kinds.” {NAME} said, it enjoyed the commandment and added shade trees. In the opinion of {NAME}, Earth was justly cursed. In the opinion of {NAME}, why was Earth cursed? Like a man who said: The breastnipples should be cursed that this one suckled from. This follows {NAME}: Three stood in judgment and four went out cursed, ( Gen . 3:17 ) “Earth is cursed because of you.”
[Kilayim 1:7.5] So far it only is written, “do not mate your animals kilaim .” Birds from where? Some Tannaim state from ( Lev . 19:19 ): “You must keep My basic Laws,” some state from: “your animals you shall not mate kilaim .” If somebody grafted a tree and mated birds, following him who says “you must keep My basic Laws,” he is guilty of two offenses, according to him who says, “your animals you shall not mate kilaim ,” he is guilty only of one offense. When he mated animals and birds, following him who says “you must keep My basic Laws,” he is guilty only of one offense; according to him who says, “your animals you shall not mate kilaim ,” he is guilty of two offenses.
[Kilayim 1:7.6] It was stated: “One does not graft olives on the stem of a date palm because that would be tree on tree.” {NAME} asked, does that not disagree with {NAME}? “( Ps . 128:3 ) ‘Your wife be like a fruitful vine on the sides of your house, your sons like saplings of olive trees around your table.’ Just as olive trees are not subject to grafting, thus in your sons shall not be found any flaws.” But here it follows that there are flaws in them. There is a difference here, because in the end it will sweeten its fruit. Similar to that, {NAME}, {NAME}, used to water his peach tree with cooked wine in order to sweeten its fruit.
[Kilayim 1:8.1] MISHNAH: One does not plant vegetables in the stump of a Sycamore tree, one does not graft rue on white cassia, because that would be vegetable on tree. One does not put a pumpkin seed into a mallow so that it should protect it, because that would be vegetable on vegetable.

[Kilayim 2:1.1] MISHNAH: Every seah that contains a quarter of seeds from another kind should be diminished; {NAME} says, he must pick it out, whether it be from one kind or from two kinds. {NAME} said, they said it only for one kind, but the Sages say, everything that is kilaim with the seah counts together for a quarter. If there was a quarter composed of two kinds, does he pick out one kind and that is sufficient, or does he have to pick out everything?
[Kilayim 2:1.8] “{NAME} said, they said it only for one kind,” not two kinds. How far? Up to the greater part of the seah . If he added afterwards, the grain returned to its permitted status. If there were twenty-three and one half quarters of wheat and half a quarter of barley, and into that fell less than a quarter of lentils, even so the two kinds would not combine for permission.

[Kilayim 2:2.1] MISHNAH: If his field was sown with wheat and he changes his mind to sow it with barley, he should wait until it gets wormy, then he turns it over and after that he may sow. Like furrows for the rainy season. {NAME} says, so that there should not remain a quarter for a bet seah .

[Kilayim 2:3.1] MISHNAH: [If the field was] sown and he decided to plant, he should not say, I shall plant and then I shall turn over, but he shall turn over and then plant. [If it was] planted and he decided to sow, he should not say, I shall sow and then I shall uproot, but he should uproot and then sow. If he wishes, he cuts down to less than a hand-breadth, plants, and then takes out the roots. If his field was sown with hemp or arum, one should not sow on it because they produce all of three years. One is not required to weed grain in which there appeared aftergrowth of indigo, or the threshing floor on which many kinds are appearing, or fenugreek in which grasses appeared. But if he weeded or cut, one says to him, uproot everything except one kind.

But did we not state: “One is not required to weed … fenugreek in which grasses appeared?” If he intends to use the grasses, one should oblige him to weed! {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He would be happy if they were torn out and lying before him. {NAME} did not say so, but in the end he approves that they should be torn out and lying before him. [Kilayim 2:4.1] MISHNAH: If someone wants to make his field into separate garden beds of different kinds, the House of Shammai say, three furrows of the ploughshare, and the House of Hillel say, the width of a Sharon yoke. Both criteria are close to one another.

[Kilayim 2:6.1] MISHNAH: One does not sow mustard or saffron close to a grain field, but one may sow mustard or saffron close to a vegetable field. [Kilayim 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: What is חריע? Yellow dye.
[Kilayim 2:6.3] So is the Mishnah: “One does not surround,” hence one may sow close up. Our Mishnah is {NAME}, as it was stated: “One may surround by mustard or saffron only bulbous vegetables, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} said, any field one may surround by mustard or saffron except a grain field. {NAME} said, any field one may surround by mustard or saffron. {NAME} said, one may surround small vegetable beds by mustard or saffron.”
[Kilayim 2:6.4] It was stated: “One may sow a row of mustard or saffron in the middle of one’s field on condition to make the row long, a length of 10.5 cubits the entire width.” {NAME} said, that applies only to a small field, not to a large one. What is large and what is small? If there is between the two ends a bet rova‘ , that is large, otherwise it is small. Does this not disagree with {NAME}, for {NAME} said that a vertex that comes from a dry spot is forbidden? There it is for grain, here for vegetables. Even though {NAME} disagrees for grain, he will agree here with respect to vegetables.
[Kilayim 2:6.5] On dry soil one may sow any kind he desires. {NAME} said, only if he uses three of six [hand-breadths]. Three that are close to a fence are like dry land. If there were three inside six and one outside six, since the former ones were saved, that one also is saved. If only two were inside six and one outside six, since the first ones were not saved, neither is that one. If there was one row dry, one row fence, and another row, one jails the row by the fence on fields. Two fields, one above the other, the upper one is close to a ditch, the lower one close to a fence.
[Kilayim 2:6.6] The House of Yannai said, on the fence one may sow all kinds of mixtures. A fence implies leniencies and stringencies. How is this? Less than a bet rova‘ shaven in a grain field may not be sown; if surrounded with a fence it may be sown. A bet rova‘ in open country may be sown with two kinds; if surrounded with a fence this is forbidden.
[Kilayim 2:6.7] Does a fence save grains? Does sown dry land save vegetables? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} understood it from the following: “One sows close to dried-up tree roots.” This mentions only dry ones; hence, if they are moist, it is forbidden. {NAME} understood it from the following: “One does sow close to a fallow field, a ploughed field, a closure, a foot path, a fence ten hand-breadths high.” That implies that a sown fence saves grains! Even if you accept “fence ten hand-breadths high,” a sown fence does not have to save grains. There is a difference here because the fence is sown and no sown fence saves grains.
[Kilayim 2:6.8] {NAME} asked: Do dry land and length add together? How is that? If there was space ten and a half cubits long and six hand-breadths wide, one does not have to have dry land. If dry land was added on both sides, one may sow close on both sides.
[Kilayim 2:6.9] It was stated: {NAME} said, one may sow close to a rock ten hand-breadths long and four hand-breadths wide on both of its sides. If it was ten by ten hand-breadths, one may sow close to it on all four sides.
[Kilayim 2:7.1] MISHNAH: He who wants to turn his field into patches for all different kinds makes 24 patches per bet seah , each patch one bet rova‘ , and sows in each one any kind that he desires. If there were one or two patches, he may sow them with mustard; three he should not sow because that would look like a mustard field, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, nine patches are permitted, ten are forbidden. {NAME} says, even if its field is a bet kor , he should not make in it more than one patch.
[Kilayim 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: For the first part, {NAME} says, even jailed, even adjacent, but the rabbis say, on condition that they were neither jailed nor adjacent. How is that done? 3,2,1,2,l.
[Kilayim 2:8.1] MISHNAH: Anything that is inside the bet rova‘ counts for the measurement of bet rova‘ . The surroundings of a vine, a grave, or a rock count for the measurement of bet rova‘ . Grain and grain need a bet rova‘ , vegetable and vegetable six hand-breadths. Grain and vegetables, vegetables and grain need a bet rova‘ . {NAME} says, vegetable and grain six hand-breadths. Grain leaning over grain, vegetable over vegetable, grain over vegetable, vegetable over grain, all is permitted except Greek gourd. Rebbi says, also green melon and Egyptian beans, but I prefer their words over my words.
[Kilayim 2:8.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They taught only the surroundings of the vine, hence, not the vine itself. Why? Because it is forbidden for usufruct. But is not the grave also forbidden for usufruct? A grave is not recognizable as forbidden. And is the working space of a vine forbidden for usufruct? This follows {NAME}, since {NAME} said that a single vine does not have working space. But is not the grave forbidden for usufruct? A grave is not recognizable as forbidden.
[Kilayim 2:8.3] “Grain and grain need a bet rova ‘.” But only if it is not jailed on all four sides. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does this mean that we say that in the ravine of Simonia one may sow only one kind?
[Kilayim 2:8.4] {NAME} objected to the rabbis: Are you not lenient for one row and restrictive for rectangles? It is so, we find that the rabbis are lenient for one row and restrictive for rectangles, as it was stated: He who wants to make one row of vegetables in a grain field makes a row 10½ cubits long and six hand-breadths wide. {NAME} said, therein he sows only one kind. {NAME} said, {NAME} agrees that if it is seven wide he sows one hand-breadth on one side, one on the other side, and the remaining five count for both sides, just as {NAME} had explained {NAME} opinion there.
[Kilayim 2:8.5] Somebody planted half a row, stopped, and wanted to start a second row. {NAME} said, this is forbidden. One tells him, either tear out that row or finish it.
[Kilayim 2:8.6] {NAME} said: {NAME} and {NAME} disagree. One says, even three in a width of six, the other said, one on one side, the other on the other side, and the third in the middle. We do not know who said what. Since {NAME} said, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, only if there is no dry patch, that means that {NAME} said: One on one side, the other on the other side, and the third in the middle. If the sides were more than the dry patch, it is permitted.
[Kilayim 2:8.7] It was stated: “Five things were said about Greek gourd: One may not allow it to cover grains, it brings impurity and stops impurity, its stalk is one hand-breadth, the tiniest amount of it makes forbidden, and to him who makes a vow not to use pumpkins, only Greek gourd is forbidden.” {NAME} asked, why do we not count “it brings impurity and stops impurity” as two? {NAME} stated seven: “One may not allow it to cover grains, it brings impurity, it stops impurity, its stalk is one hand-breadth, one gives it its working space, it is kilaim with Aramean [pumpkin], and kilaim with ash pumpkin.” He did not state that it makes forbidden or anything about making a vow.
[Kilayim 2:8.8] {NAME} said, {NAME}, {NAME}, went to the market. They came and asked him whether the roofing they mentioned referred to touching. He went and asked his father, who told him that the roofing they mentioned referred to touching. {NAME} said, {NAME} went to the market. They came and asked him whether the roofing they mentioned referred to touching. He went and asked his father, who told him that the roofing they mentioned referred to touching.
[Kilayim 2:8.9] What means “but I prefer their words over my words?” {NAME} said, if Egyptian pumpkin whose leaves form roofs is permitted, green melon and Egyptian beans so much more. {NAME} said, {NAME} did not say so. Rebbi said, all those about which we did state “green melon and Egyptian beans,” also include Egyptian pumpkin. What means “but I prefer their words over my words?” That none of these form roofs like Greek gourd.
[Kilayim 3:1.1] MISHNAH: In a garden bed that is six by six hand-breadths one may sow five kinds of seeds, four at its four sides and one in the middle
[Kilayim 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: ( Is. 61:11 ) “Its sown seeds,” the minimum of seeds are two. {NAME} said, from two you infer four. Just as for two you start at the beginning of six and reduce continuously, so for four you start at the beginning of six and reduce continuously. It is impossible that there should not be a free space to plant in the middle
[Kilayim 3:1.3] {NAME} and {NAME} were sitting and asking, did we not state: “If it had a wall around it at least one hand-breadth high, one may sow in it thirteen kinds: three at each of the three sides of the wall, and one in the middle.” Should we not state, ‘six in the middle?’ Explain it if the walls diminish six. If the walls diminish six, is it that about which we stated: “{NAME} says, six kinds may be in the middle?” We upheld it, but we do not know whether the colleagues upheld it or {NAME} did; it refers to the beginning. And if it refers to the beginning, it is that about which {NAME} stated: {NAME} says, 18.
[Kilayim 3:1.4] May one raze a bet rova‘ and sow in it five different kinds of grain? If about a six-by-six, for whose infringement one is whipped by Biblical decree, you say it is permitted, then so much more here where you are not whipped by Biblical decree. May one raze at the corners of a six-by-six to make a continously narrowing patch? If in a case where working space does meet working space, you say that it is permitted, then so much more in this case where working space does not meet working space. That was unnecessary. May one raze at the corners of a bet rova‘ to make a continously narrowing patch? If about a six-by-six, for whose infringement one is whipped by Biblical decree, you say it is permitted, then so much more here where you are not whipped by Biblical decree.
[Kilayim 3:1.5] {NAME} asked: Is it not reasonable that, if the top of the surrounding wall is two hand-breadths wide, one is permitted to sow on it two kinds? {NAME} asked: If he drew a string in the middle, sowed in half of it, how far can he draw it? From what {NAME} and {NAME} said, “explain it if the walls diminish six,” that means that it may be even less than that. Let us hear from the following: “In depressions that are one hand-breadth deep one may sow three seeds, one on each side and one in the middle.” That means, down to one hand-breadth. {NAME}, Simeon from Nerash in the name of {NAME}: They taught “leaning towards a dry spot”.
[Kilayim 3:1.6] {NAME} said, they made every single hand-breadth on the border wall a domain for itself. Then there should be 25, six on each side of the border wall and one in the middle! Is that so? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} objected: Did we not state that “in a furrow or a water canal one hand-breadth deep one may sow (two) kinds of seeds, one on each side and one in the middle.” Should one not state five, two on each side and one in the middle? That is impossible; the two sides jail the middle one.
[Kilayim 3:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME} asked: Does the border wall save vegetables from melons? If the border wall does not save different kinds of grains that are saved by 10.5 cubits, does this not apply a fortiori to melons that are saved only by twelve cubits? Does planting melon save on top of the border wall? If different kinds of grains that are saved by 10.5 cubits are not saved on top of the border wall, does this not apply a fortiori to melons that are saved by eight cubits? {NAME}, {NAME}, said, is that a reasoning a fortiori ? It must be as follows: If different kinds of grains that are saved by 12.5 cubits are not saved on top of the border wall, does this not apply a fortiori to melons that are saved only by twelve cubits?
[Kilayim 3:2.1] MISHNAH: One does not sow any kind of seed-plants in a garden bed; but one may sow any kind of vegetables in a garden bed. Mustard and smooth peas are counted as seed-plants, large peas are vegetables. A border wall that was one hand-breadth high and shrank is in order because it was in order at the start. In a furrow or a water canal one hand-breadth deep one may sow three kinds of seeds, one on each side and one in the middle.
[Kilayim 3:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Any kind of seeds, etc.” Mustard and smooth peas are counted as seed-plants; if one sowed them for use as vegetables he may not put them in a garden bed. Large peas and Egyptian beans sown to produce seeds one may not put in a garden bed. If one sowed them for use as vegetables he may put them in a garden bed. All other garden seeds that are not eaten, even though one sowed to produce seeds, he may put them in a garden bed.
[Kilayim 3:2.3] “If it shrank it is in order.” {NAME} said, that means for the seeds that were already on it; hence, it is forbidden to sow anew. If one transgressed and sowed, since the earlier ones are permitted, so are the new ones. {NAME} asked: It is acceptable that if the later ones were uprooted, the earlier ones are permitted. If the earlier ones were uprooted, what is the status of the later ones? Let us hear from the following: “If the two long boards of a bed were removed and one made two new ones in their stead but did not change the holes, if the new boards were broken, it is impure, if the old ones, it is pure, since all goes after the prior status.” That means, if the later ones were uprooted, the earlier ones are permitted. If the earlier ones were uprooted, the later ones are forbidden.
[Kilayim 3:2.4] {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME}, both in the name of {NAME}, one said one plants near a fence but not near a border wall, and the other said, a border wall which lost height is in order, hence a fence which lost height is invalid. But we do not know who said what. Since {NAME} said, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One plants near a fence but not near a border wall, this means {NAME} is the one who said that a border wall that lost height is in order, hence a fence which lost height is invalid. {NAME} said, we also did make both statements, that a border wall that lost height is in order, hence a fence that lost height is invalid. One plants near a fence, as we have stated ( Mishnah 2:8 ): “One does sow close to a fallow field, a plowed field, a stone wall, a foot path, a fence ten hand-breadths high.” One does not plant near a border wall, as we have stated ( Mishnah 3:2 ): “In a furrow or a water canal that are one hand-breadth deep one may sow three kinds of seeds, one on each side and one in the middle.” If you say that one may sow close to a border wall, he should sow several rows down in the ditch. The colleagues said before {NAME}: Explain it if the top of the border wall was sown. He said to them, if it is so, let him uproot that stem and sow several rows down in the ditch. Is it not better to uproot one stem and sow several rows down in the ditch?
[Kilayim 3:3.1] MISHNAH: It is permitted that a vertex of vegetables enter a field of other vegetables, since it is visibly the end of its field. If one’s field was sown with vegetables and he wants to plant in it a row of a different vegetable, {NAME} says, not unless he has an open furrow from one end of the field to the other. {NAME} says, a length of six hand-breadths for a full width. {NAME} says, the width must be the width of the sole of a foot.
[Kilayim 3:3.2] HALAKHAH: “A vertex, etc.” {NAME} stated: He sows in it only one kind.
[Kilayim 3:3.3] What did {NAME} say about the width? Now if {NAME}, who encloses it from three sides, requires a full width, {NAME} who encloses it by two rows, not so much more? What does {NAME} say about a row of vegetables in a grain field? Now if {NAME}, who is more lenient here, is restrictive there, {NAME}, who is more restrictive here, certainly will be restrictive there! No, this is not necessarily so. What does {NAME} say there about width? As we say there, there is no difference between {NAME} and {NAME} in matters of width.
[Kilayim 3:3.4] {NAME} said, they taught only one row, hence two are forbidden. {NAME} and {NAME} both say that there is no difference between one and two rows.
[Kilayim 3:3.5] {NAME} said, it is permitted to split four rows in an open field. {NAME} said, only if the two outer rows be treated as garden beds. {NAME} said, only if three are within six.
[Kilayim 3:3.6] {NAME} said, what is the reason of {NAME}? ( Deut. 11:10 ) “That you irrigated with your feet as in a vegetable garden.” What is the measure of a foot sole? A hand-breadth.
[Kilayim 3:3.7] We have stated the opinion of {NAME} here, and we have stated it there. If it had been stated here but not there, we would have said that just as {NAME} who is restrictive here is permissive there, the rabbis who are permissive here certainly will be permissive there. Hence, it is necessary to state there. Or if it was stated there but not here, we would have said that just as the rabbis who are restrictive there are permissive here, {NAME} who is permissive there certainly will be permissive here. Hence, it is necessary to state both here and there.
[Kilayim 3:4.1] MISHNAH: If someone plants two rows of green melons, two rows of pumpkin, two rows of Egyptian beans, this is permitted. One row of melons, one row of pumpkin, one row of Egyptian beans is forbidden. One row each of melons, pumpkin, Egyptian beans, and one row of melons, {NAME} permits but the Sages forbid. One may plant melon and pumpkin in the same hole on condition that one of them points to one side, the other to the other side. (One plants so that the hair of one be here, the hair of the other one there, for what the Sages forbade is only because of the misleading impression.)
[Kilayim 3:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If one plants two rows”, etc. {NAME} said, there is disagreement. He who says there 12 [cubits], here also 12 [cubits]. He who says there eight, here also eight. {NAME} said, this Mishnah is according to everybody. A strip of melon is good enough among strips of melons to be saved by eight.
[Kilayim 3:4.3] How long does it have to be to jail? {NAME} said, let us infer it from a vineyard. Just as you say in regard to a vineyard that there is no difference between length and separation, so here also there is no difference between length and separation. That is fine according to the opinion of {NAME}; there eight and here also eight. According to {NAME}, with how much will it jail? If you say with eight, is there an argument a fortiori that a strip of melons among onions will jail only with twelve? But a melon strip, which you empowered among melon strips to save by a mere eight, will be jailed by eight, melon strips among onions, which you weakened to save only by twelve, certainly will be jailed only by eight. If you say that a melon strip among onions will be jailed only by twelve, then an argument a fortiori shows that a melon strip among melons should be jailed only by twelve.
[Kilayim 3:4.4] So far if [the planting] is covering [the entire area]. What about producing single stalks? Just as you say of a vineyard that there is no difference between covering or producing [single stalks], so here also there is no difference between continuous planting or producing single stalks.
[Kilayim 3:4.5] {NAME} said, it is a controversy whether two kinds join together to save but do not join together to prohibit. Rav said, it is everybody’s opinion that just as two kinds join together to save so they do join together to prohibit. Our Mishnah supports {NAME}, as we have stated: “{NAME} permits it.” Our Mishnah differs with Rav: “One row of melons, one row of pumpkin, one row of Egyptian beans, and one row of melons.” Before he started the fourth one, was it not already forbidden? Explain it that he planted the four rows simultaneously.
[Kilayim 3:4.6] “One may plant melon”, etc. It was stated: “One may make a small hole in one’s field, one hand-breadth deep, sow in it four seeds, and turn them to the four directions of the compass.” {NAME}, Simeon of Nerash in the name of {NAME}: That was taught regarding those which lean towards a dry spot. {NAME} asked, if we deal with those that lean towards a dry spot, should we not state “eight,” two on each of the edges?
[Kilayim 3:5.1] MISHNAH: If one’s field was sown with onions and he desired to plant there rows of pumpkin, {NAME} says, he uproots two rows, plants one row, and leaves two rows of onion standing, uproots two rows, plants one row. {NAME} says, he uproots two rows, plants two rows, and leaves two rows of onion standing, uproots two rows, plants two rows. But the Sages say, if between one row and the next is less than twelve [cubits], he should not keep the seeds in between.
[Kilayim 3:5.2] HALAKHAH: (He who plants his vineyard, etc.). {NAME} said, according to the words of {NAME} sometimes there are 16, sometimes 12, sometimes 8. When he gives all the working space in the interior, 16. Part interior and part exterior, 12. All exterior, 8. {NAME} says, it always must be 12. We have stated thus: “It is determined according to the statements of both of them: {NAME} says 12, {NAME} says 8.” Now, {NAME} says 12, and the rabbis say 12; in what do they disagree? Closing up! In the opinion of {NAME} one may not close up, but the rabbis say he may.
[Kilayim 3:6.1] MISHNAH: Pumpkin in the middle of vegetables goes by the rules of vegetables, in the middle of grain it needs a bet rova‘. If one’s field was sown with grain and he desired to plant there one row of pumpkin, he must allow six hand-breadths to tend it. If it grows, he has to uproot before it. {NAME} said, he allows four cubits to tend it. They said to him, are you making this more restrictive than for a vine? He said to them, we find that this case is more restrictive than that of a vine. For a single vine one allows six hand-breadths to tend it, but for a single pumpkin a bet rova‘. {NAME} says in the name of {NAME}, if there are three pumpkin plants in a bet seah one should not sow in that bet seah. {NAME}, the son of the Snatcher from Efrat, says in the name of {NAME}, if there are three pumpkin plants in a bet kor one should not sow in that bet kor .
[Kilayim 3:6.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said: The words of {NAME} imply that one allows space for tending even for a single row.
[Kilayim 3:6.3] Does one allow space for tending the first plant? Just as you say in regard of a vineyard that one gives space for tending the first plant, so here also one allows space for tending the first plant. May one sow between the holes? Just as you say in regard of a vineyard that one may not sow between the vines, so here also one may not sow between the holes.
[Kilayim 3:6.4] {NAME} asked: If somebody planted five pumpkins and trained them to grow on a fence, does one give it the rules of a trellis?
[Kilayim 3:6.5] Does one estimate so for all kinds of pumpkins? Every place at which you made green melon and Egyptian beans equal to Greek gourd, you make Egyptian pumpkin equal to Greek gourd. Here, where you did not make melon and Egyptian beans equal to Greek gourd, you do not make Egyptian pumpkin equal to Greek gourd.
[Kilayim 3:6.6] Why did they not object to him: If someone keeps single fresh stalks growing to produce seeds, must he not clear around them a bet rova‘ or fence them in by a fence of ten hand-breadths? For a row one is more lenient. Since they did not object to him, it follows that {NAME} thinks that row and square are the same. For {NAME} and {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: He who keeps a single fresh stalk growing to produce seeds must clear around it a bet rova‘ or fence it in by a fence of ten hand-breadths, even if it is the same kind. {NAME} objected before {NAME}, did we not state: “If coriander was sown for its seeds, its greens are exempt?” He answered him, coriander is a special case since both the plant and its seeds are eaten.

[Kilayim 4:1.1] MISHNAH: A bald spot in a vineyard: the House of Shammai say 24 cubits but the House of Hillel say 16 cubits. The circumference of a vineyard: the House of Shammai say 16 cubits but the House of Hillel say 12 cubits. What is a bald spot in a vineyard? A vineyard that dried up in the middle; if there are less than 16 cubits one should not bring seeds there. If there are 16 cubits, one allows it space to be tended and the rest one may sow. What is the circumference of a vineyard? Between the vineyard and the fence. If less than 12 cubits are there, one should not introduce seeds there. If 12 cubits are there, one gives it space for tending and sows the remaining area. {NAME} says, that is only the fence of a vineyard. What is the circumference of a vineyard? A vineyard between two Vineyards. What is a fence? If it is ten hand-breadths high, and a ditch is ten deep and four wide.
[Kilayim 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: “A bald spot in a vineyard.” {NAME} said that the rules for a bald spot in a vineyard and a dried-up vineyard are the same. A bald spot is cleared in its middle, a dried-up vineyard is cleared on all four sides. {NAME} said, this applies to a large vineyard but if it comes from the plants of a small vineyard, the rules of a bald spot in a vineyard do not apply. Also, we have stated: “What is a bald spot in a vineyard? A vineyard that dried up in its middle but enough for a vineyard remained, whether it be from all four sides, or from three, or from two opposite sides.” How is that? Five rows of seven each, one took out one row of vineyard, that leaves four vineyards and three intervals. One takes out another one, that leaves three vineyards and two intervals. One takes out another one, that leaves two vineyards and one interval.
[Kilayim 4:1.3] {NAME} said, they made it like the start of its planting. The House of Shammai say, 24 at the start of planting, 24 at its destruction. {NAME} said, the House of Shammai are more restrictive in its destruction than at the start of its planting. At the start of its planting 16, at its destruction 24. In every case, the House of Shammai add one third: The circumference of a vineyard, according to the House of Shammai 18, according to the House of Hillel 12. But did we not state: “The circumference of a vineyard, the House of Shammai say 16 cubits, the House of Hillel say 12 cubits.” Some want to say, deduct from this four cubits for tending, there remain 12 cubits according to the House of Shammai and 8 following the House of Hillel.
[Kilayim 4:1.4] But for tending a vineyard, according to the House of Shammai 8 cubits, according to the House of Hillel 6 cubits. But did we not state: “Therefore, he who sows four cubits in a vineyard, the House of Shammai say that he sanctified one row, but the House of Hillel say that he sanctified two rows.” Let us say that it was stated because of the House of Hillel. But did we not state: “What is a trellis? He who plants a row of five vines.” There is a difference, since {NAME} said, this was taught about a curved trellis. By its curving, two are absorbed.
[Kilayim 4:1.5] Not only a fence, but even if he puts up laths, if between one lath and the next there is less that three hand-breadths it is considered a fence. Even standing grain and straw? Or does it agree with what {NAME} said: Nothing forbidden may form a separation to save? They are of the opinion that what is forbidden does form a separation to forbid.
[Kilayim 4:1.6] In the opinion of {NAME}, it is as in the interior of a vineyard. Then 16 should be forbidden! {NAME} said, it means that the trunks are not aligned. But if the trunks are aligned, they forbid 16.
[Kilayim 4:1.7] Only if it is surrounded by a fence on all four sides? From what we have stated: “Between two vineyards,” that means even from one side only. Only if the fence encloses all of that side? Let us hear from the following that {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of {NAME}: There is no tail for a large vineyard and no circumference for a small vineyard. There is no tail for a large vineyard because one does not need it. Neither a circumference for a small vineyard to forbid more outside than inside; inside eight and outside twelve. What is a small vineyard? Three parallel three. Hence, three parallel three parallel three, [the vineyard] has a circumference. {NAME} said, that means that if he made laths along three vines then [the vineyard] has a circumference.
[Kilayim 4:1.8] {NAME} asked: What if he made a fence inside a fence? He said, if there are three hand-breadths one may sow there, otherwise one may not sow there. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If there was a place of twelve cubits there, the circumference would be eliminated. {NAME} said, only if it is twelve by twelve. {NAME} said, even if it continuously narrows.
[Kilayim 4:2.1] MISHNAH: If there are less than three hand-breadths of distance between the sticks of a partition fence made from sticks, so that a kid goat cannot enter, then that is a valid partition wall. Also, if a wall was torn down up to a length of ten cubits, that acts as a gate. If more than that, it is forbidden along the torn-down part. If it is torn down in many places, if what is standing is more than what is torn down, it is permitted, but if the torn-down part is more than the standing one, it is forbidden at the torn-down places.
[Kilayim 4:2.2] HALAKHAH: Ten laths at the in-betweens and what is standing is four hand-breadths wide, and what is standing is more than what is torn down: where it is standing it is permitted, where it is torn down it is forbidden. If one made laths in front of the vines, and what is standing is less than four hand-breadths, and what is torn down is more than what is standing, it is obvious that where it is standing it is permitted, where it is torn down it is forbidden.
[Kilayim 4:2.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If one put in four poles at the four corners of a vineyard and connected them with a bast string on top, this saves as a symbolic fence. {NAME} said, the rules of separation walls for the Sabbath are the rules for kilaim . {NAME} said, it happened that {NAME} went to {NAME} at Nagnigar; he showed him a field called bet ḥaverata whose wall had parts torn down more than ten wide. He took wood to insert, forked poles to insert, until he reduced to less than ten. He said, just like that is a dividing wall for the Sabbath. {NAME} said, {NAME} agrees that on the Sabbath, a symbolic fence does not save more than ten. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says so: “One surrounds it with three ropes, one above the other.” If you say that the string saves, one rope would be sufficient.
[Kilayim 4:2.4] {NAME} said: {NAME} asked, what do you say about that symbolic fence, on top or at the sides? If you say on top, so much more on the sides. If you say on the sides, then not on the top. If you say on the top, {NAME} said it correctly. If you say from the sides, {NAME} did not say anything. What do you want to say, if on top, it must be on top. Or from the sides, it is on the sides. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it if they were strung on forked poles.
[Kilayim 4:2.5] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: In height even one hundred cubits. {NAME} said, that is, for kilaim , but as regards the Sabbath, a symbolic fence should not be better than a beam. {NAME} said, it is the same for kilaim and Sabbath. [Kilayim 4:2.7] {NAME} and the rabbis asked before {NAME}, does a symbolic fence save in a sukkah ? He said to them, a symbolic fence saves in a sukkah . Does the end of the roofing save in a sukkah ? He said to them, the end of the roofing does not save in a sukkah . What is the difference between them? One is made for the purpose, the other one is not made for the purpose. {NAME} said, all these things are for discussion’s sake, but as far as teaching, it is forbidden to teach it. [Kilayim 4:2.9] “ It turns out that concerning kilaim everything less than three hand-breadths is considered closed. From three to four, if what is standing is more than what is torn down it is permitted, but if what is torn down is more than what is standing, it is forbidden. From four hand-breadths to ten cubits, if what is standing is more than what is torn down, it is permitted; but if what is torn down is more than what is standing it is permitted where it is standing, forbidden where it is torn down. Concerning the Sabbath, everything less than three hand-breadths is considered closed. From three to four, and from four hand-breadths to ten cubits, it is permitted if what is standing is more than what is torn down, but forbidden if what is torn down is more than what is standing. More than ten, it is forbidden even though what is standing is more than what is torn down.” {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: There is no “from three to four.” There is a hole of three and no place of four! {NAME} objected: Did we not state: “One surrounds with reeds,” does a reed form a place? He said to him, do not object to me from a breach less than three hand-breadths, since anything less than three is considered closed! {NAME} in the name of Rav: In any case, since what is standing is more than what is torn down, it is permitted.
[Kilayim 4:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody plants one row of five vines, the House of Shammai say that this is a vineyard. But the House of Hillel say, [a planting] is not a vineyard unless it has two rows. Therefore, if somebody sows within four cubits of a vineyard, the House of Shammai say that he sanctifies one row, but the House of Hillel say, two rows.
[Kilayim 4:3.2] HALAKHAH: That is, if sown in the middle. If he sowed in front of a middle vine, in the opinion of the House of Shammai he makes the entire row forbidden. In the opinion of the House of Hillel, he forbids three parallel three. If he sowed in front of an interval in the middle, in the opinion of the House of Shammai, he forbids two on each side. What is said about the fifth? If the seeds were close to one vine, those are forbidden; if not, they are permitted. In the opinion of the House of Hillel, four parallel two are forbidden. If he sowed opposite the corner, which row is forbidden in the opinion of the House of Shammai? Both of them! In the opinion of the House of Hillel, two parallel two and one forming a tail on each side are forbidden. If one sowed in an interval at the corner, in the opinion of the House of Shammai he makes the entire row forbidden. In the opinion of the House of Hillel, two parallel two and one forming a tail are forbidden. What is the sixth? The third in the first row, the second in the third row.

No, the terrace has to be higher. {NAME} said, they declared the entire ten hand-breadths of the terrace a domain by itself.
[Kilayim 6:2.4] We have stated there: “If somebody throws from four cubits [distance] to a wall, if [the projectile hits] higher than ten hand-breadths, he is like one throwing into the air, if lower than ten hand-breadths, he is like one throwing onto the ground.” {NAME} said, if it extends slanting. But will it not finally descend? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, explain it that it was a soft fig cake and it stuck. {NAME} asked before {NAME}, does this not imply that the declivity of a terrace belongs to the level below? He said to him, there the vegetables profit from the terrace but here people rub it and it falls down. If it would say, if there is a hole [in the wall] and it profits from the hole just as vegetables profit from the terrace, you would be justified.
[Kilayim 6:2.5] “Two gardens, one above the other, the lower one is made into a vineyard, the upper one is not made into a vineyard. He said to him, because plants will bend into the airspace of the vineyard. “If the upper one is made into a vineyard but the lower one is not made into a vineyard, one may sow the lower one and the declivity until one reaches the roots of the vines.” {NAME} said, one does not have here “the roots of the vines” but “below three [hand-breadths],” following that which was stated: “roots of madder that enter within four cubits of a vineyard are permitted below three hand-breadths.”
[Kilayim 6:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody trains a vine over part of a papyrus , he should not sow under the rest, but if he did, it does not become sanctified. If the new growth expands it becomes forbidden. The same applies to one who trains over parts of a futile tree. If somebody trains a vine over part of a fruit tree he may sow under the rest. If new grows expands, he must move it. It happened that {NAME} visited {NAME} Aziz. He showed him a vine trained over parts of a fig tree and asked, may I sow under the rest? He told him, it is permitted. He took him from there to the armory and showed him a vine trained over part of a beam and a sycamore stump on which were many beams. He said to him, under that one beam it is forbidden, the rest is permitted. What is a futile tree? One which does not bear fruit. {NAME} says, every tree is futile except olive and fig trees. {NAME} says, a futile tree is one of which one does not plant entire orchards.
