[Kilayim 6:4.1] MISHNAH: An interrupted trellis is more than eight cubits. No linear measurement stated by the Sages requires “more than” except an interrupted trellis. What is an interrupted trellis? A trellis [whose vines are] dried up in its middle, but there remained five vines on each side. If between them are eight cubits, one should not sow there. If there are more than eight cubits, one gives each side its working space and he may sow the rest. A trellis which starts from a wall in a corner and ends there, one gives it its working space and he may sow the rest. {NAME} said, if there are less than four cubits one should not bring seeds there. Sticks that stand out from the trellis, if he worries whether to remove them, then under them it is permitted, but if he made them so that the new growth can expand on them, it is forbidden. One looks at a blossom that comes out from the trellis as if a plumb-line were hanging down from it; under it it is forbidden. The same holds for a branch. Under a shoot of vine drawn from one tree to another, it is forbidden. If he binds them together with a rope or bast, under the binding it is permitted. But if he did that to accomodate future growth, it is forbidden.

But is it not written ( 1K . 1:33 ): “Let my son Solomon ride on my she-mule”? That was a creature from Creation.
[Kilayim 8:2.4] {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, he who leads kilaim by voice will be whipped. We have stated so: “If he led it, if he made it draw, if he called it and it came, he is responsible to pay like a borrower.” But did not {NAME} state: “If it was standing outside the Sabbath domain, he called it and it came after him, he is free.” There it comes of its own volition, here it is forced to walk But did we not state: “If he clapped before his [a slave’s] eye and blinded it, before his [a slave’s] ear and made it deaf, he [the slave] does not attain freedom.” {NAME} said before {NAME}, there is a difference because he [the slave] could have fled. Know that it is so because we have stated: “If he grabbed him he is guilty.”
[Kilayim 8:2.5] : He who sits in a cart, the rabbis say he is a weight, {NAME} says, he is no weight.

[Kilayim 8:3.1] MISHNAH: One does not tie a horse to the sides or the back of a cart, or a Libyan donkey to camels. {NAME} says, all animals born from a horse are permitted one with the other even if their father was a donkey, all animals born from a donkey are permitted one with the other even if their father was a horse, but those born from a horse are forbidden with those from a donkey.
[Kilayim 8:3.2] HALAKHAH: : “One does not tie a horse to the sides or the back of a cart.” It is stated: {NAME} frees from prosecution. If it supported, whether in ascent or in descent, everybody agrees that it is forbidden. {NAME} said, because either one carries the laziness of the other. Rav says, because the rope is carried between them.
[Kilayim 8:3.3] {NAME} asked: If he bound them by their hair? Where do we hold? In case he bound them together by their hair, should we say that it is forbidden to let one animal ride on another? If he tied them by a rope, we say because they carry the rope between them. {NAME} said, Rav and {NAME} disagree, {NAME} said, because either one carries the laziness of the other. Rav says, because they carry the rope between them. What is the difference? Both according to Rav as also according to {NAME}, if he bound them by their hair he is not punishable!

A mounting donkey. {NAME}: {NAME} asked: Do proselytes from Libya have to wait three generations? {NAME} said, from what we see that they call a green Egyptian bean Libyan but a dry one Egyptian, that means a proselyte from Libya has to wait three generations, it means that Libya is identical with Egypt.

[Kilayim 9:1.1] MISHNAH: Only wool and linen are forbidden as kilaim . Only wool and linen can become impure by mold disease. Only wool and linen are worn by priests for their service in the temple. If one mixed camel wool and sheep wool, if most is camel wool it is permitted, if most is sheep wool it is forbidden, half and half is forbidden. The same applies if hemp and linen are mixed. Raw silk and kalak silk are not subject to kilaim but are forbidden because of the bad impression. Mattresses and pillows are not subject to kilaim but one’s skin should not touch them. There is no provisional kilaim . One may not wear kilaim over ten other garments, not even to trick the customs.
[Kilayim 9:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Only [wool and linen] are forbidden as kilaim ”. It is written ( Deut . 22:11 ): “Do not wear ša‘aṭnez , wool and linen together.” I would say one is only forbidden to wear it; the verse says ( Lev . 19:19 ): “It shall not come on you.” If it shall not come on you I would say one may not carry a chest on his back; the verse says “do not wear.” Since a garment is specifically useful to the body, [included are] only things useful to the body. Why was it said that “it shall not come on you?” {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, if there was a large piece of cloth, in a part of which was kilaim and that part was lying on the ground, one cannot cover himself with the other part. I would say, it includes even sea flax, even hemp; the verse says “wool and linen”; just as wool cannot have an epithet so nothing else can have an epithet. From where that [wool] has no epithet? {NAME} said, it is written ( 2K . 3:4 ) “Mesha‘, the king of Moab, was a nôqēd ;” what is a nôqēd ? A shepherd! “He delivered to the king of Israel 100’000 lambs and 100’000 wool rams.” Only ram’s wool is called “wool”.
[Kilayim 9:1.3] “Only wool and linen can become impure by mold disease,” for it is written ( Lev . 13:47 ) “on woolen cloth or on linen cloth.” I could think they can become impure whether dyed or natural; the verse says “woolen cloth or linen cloth.” Just as linen is in its natural state so wool must also be in its natural state. I might exclude what was dyed by humans but not what was dyed by nature; the verse says ( Lev . 13:48 ): “For the linen and for the wool”, just as linen is white so wool has to be white.
[Kilayim 9:1.4] We have stated two rules and they do not resemble one another. We have stated: Only wool and linen are forbidden as kilaim , whether dyed or white. We have stated: Only wool and linen can become impure by mold disease, but only white. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: There, you say “whether dyed or white”, but here you say “but only white”? He said to him, there is a difference because the verse repeated twice “wool, wool”; just as linen is in its natural state so also wool must be in its natural state.
[Kilayim 9:1.5] {NAME} said: It is written ( Lev . 16:4 ) “He shall wear a garment of holy bad ,” growing singly. But wool also grows in single strands. It is explained in tradition ( Ez . 44:17 ): “There should be no wool on them when they officiate inside the inner doors.” Therefore, on the outside wool may be on them. From where that they may wear kilaim ? As it says ( Ex . 39:28 ): “The cap of byssus, the hat-turbans of byssus, the cloth trousers of spun byssus, and the belt of spun byssus, blue, purple, and crimson.” And it is written ( Ez . 44:18 ): “Linen turbans shall be on their heads, linen trousers shall be on their hips, they shall not belt with sweat.” You infer “byssus” from “byssus”, “byssus” from “turbans”, “turbans” from “turbans”. Just as crimson is made from a living being, so the rest is made from a living being. Just as wool cannot have an epithet so linen cannot have an epithet.

Rav speaks about the case when he made the material itself into a garment, {NAME} speaks about the case where he wants to mix it with other things.

A baraita contradicts Rav: “One should not make a visible fringe of linen dyed with soot, but for mattresses and pillows it is permitted.” A baraita contradicts Rav: “If one’s coins were strewn before an idol he should not bow down to collect them lest he look as if he was prostrating himself before the idol. If aquaeduct pipes spout it is forbidden. {NAME} stated that if it occurred at a hidden place it is permitted. All these statements contradict Rav and he cannot explain them.

He [Solomon] saw the Angel of Death looking at them and grinding his teeth. He said a word and put them into space. He [the Angel of Death] went and took them from there, then he came laughing before him [Solomon]. He said to him, just before you were grinding your teeth and now you are laughing at us? He said to him, the Merciful told me to take Eliḥoref and Aḥiah from space and I was wondering who would put them there where I was sent to take them; He put it into your mind to do so that I could complete my mission. I went and dealt with them there. The two sons of {NAME} were students of Rebbi. He [Rebbi] saw the Angel of Death looking at them and grinding his teeth and said, let us exile them to the South, maybe the exile atones. He [the angel of death] went and took them from there.
[Kilayim 9:3.15] {NAME} was an emigrant. He was dying there and started to cry. They said to him, why are you crying? We shall bring you to the Land of Israel. He said to them, how does this help me? I am losing my pearl in an impure land. One cannot compare one who expires in the bosom of his mother to one who expires in the bosom of a strange woman. {NAME} was dying in Assos. He said, tell the people of the Land of Israel, there is your Messiah. With all that, he said to put his bier on the sea-cape since it is written ( Ps . 24:2 ): “For He founded it on seas, based it on rivers.”
[Kilayim 9:3.16] “Seven seas surround the Land of Israel: The ocean, lake Tiberias, lake Samkho , the salt sea, lake Ḥolata, lake Sheliat, lake Apamea.” But does there not also exist the lake of Ḥomṣ? Diocletian dammed up rivers and created it. It is written ( Num . 21:20 ): “Looking down on the desert.” {NAME} said, if one ascends the desert mountain one finds the likeness of a sieve in lake Tiberias, that is the well of Miryam. {NAME} said, the rabbis estimated it and it is assessed opposite the middle gate of the old synagogue of Sarongin .
[Kilayim 9:3.17] {NAME} and {NAME} were talking a walk on the road when they saw coffins being brought into the Land from abroad. {NAME} said to {NAME}: What good is that going to do them? [Kilayim 9:4.1] MISHNAH: Birsīm , Burdesīm , and Dalmatian garb as well as pinon shoes one should not wear unless one checks them. {NAME} says, those coming from the sea shore in maritime countries do not have to be checked because usually they are made from hemp. Padded shoes have no problem with kilaim .
[Kilayim 9:4.2] HALAKHAH: Bursīn are birri . Burdesīn are delma . Dalmatian garb are short sleeved tunics and overcoats. Pinon shoes are socks.
[Kilayim 9:4.3] “{NAME} says, those coming from the sea shore in maritime countries.” Does this mean “from the sea shore and from overseas countries” or “from the seashore of maritime countries”? Since it was stated: For example, Tyre and its surroundings, Caesarea (maritima) and its surroundings, it means “from the seashore of maritime countries”.
[Kilayim 9:4.4] “They do not have to be checked.” That means in earlier times when flax was not found everywhere. But today, when flax is found everywhere, they need to be checked.
[Kilayim 9:4.5] “Padded shoes”. There are places where they are padded from the outside. As {NAME} said to {NAME} to tell {NAME} not to sew his shoes with flax but with [leather] strips. {NAME} agrees that if one bound a woolen belt over a linen garment that would be permitted, for if he makes himself thin, it will fall down.

[Kilayim 9:5.1] MISHNAH: Only spun and woven cloth is forbidden because of kilaim since it is said ( Deut . 22:11 ): “Do not wear šaʻaṭnez ”, anything carded, spun, or woven. {NAME} said, he has turned aside and turned his Father in Heaven against him. Felt is forbidden because it is carded. A woolen border on a linen garment is forbidden because it goes around like the woven part. {NAME} says, woven ropes are forbidden because he stitches them before he ties them. One should not bind a strip of wool on one of linen to gird his hips even if a leather belt is in between.
[Kilayim 9:5.2] HALAKHAH: It could have stated שעו and not טוי. If it had stated שעז but not טוי we would have said that spinning is permitted. But the Mishnah does not say so, but “only spun and woven cloth is forbidden because of kilaim .” It could have stated שעט and not נוז. If it had stated שעט but not נוז we would have said that weaving is permitted. But the Mishnah does not say so, but “a woolen border on a linen garment is forbidden because it goes around like the woven part.” It could have stated טנז and not שע. If it had stated טנז but not שע we would have said that carding is permitted. But the Mishnah does not say so, but “felt is forbidden because it is carded.”
[Kilayim 9:5.3] Ropes of purple wool are forbidden. Some Tannaïm state, they are permitted. He who says they are forbidden, for example those of embroiderers who tie them on. He who says they are permitted, for if he makes himself thin, it will fall down.
[Kilayim 9:6.1] MISHNAH: Tags of weavers and washermen are forbidden because of kilaim . If one stiches one pin-stitch there is no connection, it does not fall under kilaim , and if he removes it on the Sabbath he is not prosecutable. If the two ends appear on the same side it is a connection, it falls under kilaim , and if he removes it on the Sabbath he is guilty. {NAME} says, only if there are three pin-stitches. A sack or a chest bring together for kilaim .
[Kilayim 9:6.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, not until it comes down an entire side. {NAME} said, they said to {NAME}, get out and read! Did we not state, “if the two ends appear on the same side?” That means, only if it goes down and up. And did we not state, “{NAME} says, only if there are three needle-stitches.” That means [the thread] goes down, up, and down. But so and so.
[Kilayim 9:6.3] A thread drawn through by means of a needle, even it if has a knot on each side, is no connection for cloth. The thread is a connection for cloth but not for the needle. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, only if it is knotted on both sides. The words of the rabbis disagree since {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of Rav: He who straightens out the sides on the Sabbath is guilty because of sewing. He should have said “because of sewing and making knots.”
[Kilayim 9:6.4] {NAME} said, the reason of {NAME} is that by the third his work becomes permanent. Does {NAME} hold with {NAME}? But here, might less than that be undone?
[Kilayim 9:6.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They stated only “sack”. Hence not a basket. It was found stated: The basket, the sack, and the chest bring together for kilaim . Tents have nothing to do with kilaim .
[Kilayim 9:6.6] {NAME} asked, can he and his son combine for kilaim ? How may this be? He wears woolen clothes but his son wears linen clothes. [Sheviit 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Until when may one plough an orchard in the year preceding the Sabbatical? The House of Shammai say, as long as it helps the fruits, the House of Hillel say, until Pentecost. Their words do not differ by much.
[Sheviit 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Until when may one plough, etc.” It is written ( Ex . 23:12 ): “Six days you shall do your work but on the Seventh Day you shall rest.” And it is written ( Ex . 34:21 ): “You shall rest from ploughing and harvesting.” Where do we hold? If one speaks about the Sabbath of Creation, was it not already said ( Ex . 20:9 ): “Six days you shall labor and do all your work?” If one speaks about Sabbatical years, was it not already said ( Lev . 25:3 ): “Six years you shall sow your field and six years you shall prune your vineyard?” If it cannot refer to the Sabbath of Creation nor to Sabbatical years, let it refer to the prohibition of the first two terms. “You shall rest from ploughing and harvesting,” from ploughing when harvesting is forbidden; what is this? This is ploughing in the year preceding the Sabbatical in preparation of the Sabbatical. And from harvesting when ploughing is forbidden, what is this? That is the harvest of Sabbatical growth after the Sabbatical.
[Sheviit 1:1.3] If it is so, why was it said: One ploughs until the New Year? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} and his court abolished the prohibition of the first two terms. {NAME} asked: Did we not state: No court may annul the words of another court unless it is greater in wisdom and numbers? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If they wanted to plough, they may plough. Then it should have been eliminated from the Mishnah! {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If they wanted to re-establish it, they may do so.
[Sheviit 1:1.4] {NAME} objected: There is the chapter on the induction and the chapter on the generation of the deluge which will have no future use. Should they have been eliminated from what is studied? They are there to inform you. So here also to inform you. {NAME} said, as we stated there: “If a person says, so is my tradition, one will say to him, you heard the opinion of Rebbi X.” And so, if somebody should say, I heard that it is forbidden to plough until the New Year, they will say to him, you heard the prohibition of the first two terms.
[Sheviit 1:1.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: When they forbade it, they were inspired by Scripture, and when they permitted it, they were inspired by Scripture. When they forbade it, they were inspired by Scripture, ( Lev . 25:3 ): “You shall rest from ploughing and harvesting,” from ploughing when harvesting is forbidden; what is this? This is ploughing in the year preceding the Sabbatical in preparation of the Sabbatical. And from harvesting when ploughing is forbidden, what is this? That is the harvest of Sabbatical growth after the Sabbatical. When they permitted it, they were inspired by Scripture, ( Ex . 20:9 ): “Six days you shall labor and do all your work,” just as on the eve of the Sabbath of Creation one may do work until sundown, also before the start of the Sabbatical year one may work until sundown.
[Sheviit 1:1.6] Why until Pentecost? Until then it is good for the fruits, from there on he degrades his fruits. But did we not state: Both for a useless tree and a fruit tree, until then it fortifies the stem, from there on it weakens its force. Let him plough! Because he knows that he will weaken the tree, he does not intend to work the ground.
[Sheviit 1:1.7] Why did we not state this with the leniencies of the House of Shammai and the stringencies of the House of Hillel? Sometimes there is no rain and no moisture and he would plough only before Pentecost following the House of Shammai. The House of Hillel say, until Pentecost.
[Sheviit 1:2.1] MISHNAH: What is an orchard? Any three trees on a bet seah ; if they may produce a fig cake in the weight of a talent of 60 Italic minas one ploughs the entire bet seah because of them. If it is less, one ploughs for them only to accomodate the harvester and his basket beside him.
[Sheviit 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody buys three trees on another person’s property, spaced so that ten trees could be planted in a bet seah and that the ox and its harness could pass between them, then he acquired the ground under them, the ground between them, and outside the space for the harvester and his basket. Rav said, if they form a group. {NAME} says, also if they are in a straight line. {NAME} said, this refers to there but not to here. {NAME} said, it refers even to here, if they are close. {NAME} said to him, did we not state “that the ox and its harness could pass between them”? Come and see, if the ox and its harness can pass between them, the roots can expand laterally, but if the ox and its harness cannot pass between them, the roots cannot expand laterally.
[Sheviit 1:2.3] {NAME} asked, from one to the other sixteen and on the sides twenty five? {NAME} asked: If they were next to a fence, does one plough the entire bet seah because of them? {NAME} said, if you want that, we should give them their four bate seah , two bate seah here, two bate seah there. {NAME} asked, if there was one vine drawn over two seah , do you plough the ground under it and outside it for the harvester and his basket?
[Sheviit 1:2.4] Regarding the prohibition of the first two terms, those above plough downwards and those below plough upwards. It seems reasonable that those above plough downwards but not that those below plough upwards. Let us hear from the following: “One removes a tree 25 cubits from a cistern.” We have stated on that: Both higher and lower. Or let us say both if the tree is higher and the cistern lower or if tree and cistern are on the same level. In this sense, we stated: “Whether the tree is higher and the cistern lower or the tree lower and the cistern higher”; is that reasonable? If the tree is higher and the cistern lower; but the tree lower and the cistern higher, do roots climb? {NAME} said not because of the roots [climbing], but they loosen the earth and damage the bottom of the cistern. A case came before {NAME}; he said that is a single opinion and we do not rely on it, for we have stated on this: “{NAME} says, just as they said higher so they said lower.”
[Sheviit 1:3.1] MISHNAH: Any useless or fruit trees are considered as if they were fig trees. If they would produce a fig cake in the weight of a talent of 60 Italic minas one ploughs the entire bet seah because of them. If less, one ploughs for them only as necessary. If one tree yields a “fig cake” but two do not, or two do and one does not, one only ploughs for them as necessary, unless there are three, and so from three to nine. If there are ten or more than ten one ploughs the entire bet seah because of them, whether they produce or not, since it is said ( Ex . 34:21 ): : “You shall rest from ploughing and harvesting.” One does not have to mention ploughing and harvesting of the Sabbatical, but it refers to ploughing in the year preceding the Sabbatical in preparation of the Sabbatical, and harvesting of Sabbatical growth after the Sabbatical. {NAME} says, just as ploughing is voluntary so harvesting is voluntary; this excludes the harvest of the ‘ omer .
[Sheviit 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Any useless tree, etc.” Why did they mention fig trees? Because their fruits are large and they produce many. The Etrog tree has large fruits but it produces few of them. Olive trees produce much but its fruits are not large. But these produce much and its fruits are large. {NAME} said, all trees produce one year less than another year but the fig tree produces every year.
[Sheviit 1:3.3] “If one tree yields, etc.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Only he should not diminish from the computation of triads. {NAME} said, only he should not diminish from the computation of nonads.
[Sheviit 1:3.4] If there were four and the ox may pass between them with its harness and two where the ox cannot pass with its harness, you consider it as if there were five. If there are five, we have the disagreement of {NAME} and the rabbis, as we have stated there: “A vineyard planted less that four cubits apart, {NAME} says that it is no vineyard. But the Sages say that it is a vineyard and one disregards the ones in the middle as if nonexistent.”
[Sheviit 1:3.5] “One ploughs the entire bet seah because of them since it is said ( Ex . 34:21 ): ‘You shall rest from ploughing and harvesting.’ ” That refers only to the first part, “one ploughs for them only as necessary because it is said ‘you shall rest from ploughing and harvesting.’ ”.
[Sheviit 1:3.6] “One does not have to mention, etc.” {NAME} is consistent since {NAME} said the ‘ omer may not come from Syria; the harvesting of the ‘ omer is different, it is a commandment.
[Sheviit 1:4.1] MISHNAH: Three trees belonging to three different owners are counted together and one may plough the entire bet seah for them. How much space must be between them? {NAME} says, so that the ox and its harness can pass.
[Sheviit 1:4.2] HALAKHAH: “Three trees, etc.” {NAME} stated: Trees belonging to one owner and ground belonging to a second owner are counted together and one may plough the entire bet seah for them. {NAME} said, we have stated more: Three trees belonging to three different owners are counted together and one may plough the entire bet seah until the New Year.
[Sheviit 1:5.1] MISHNAH: Ten saplings distributed on a bet seah , one ploughs the entire bet seah for them until the new year. If they formed a row or were surrounded by a grate one ploughs only what is necessary for them.
[Sheviit 1:5.2] HALAKHAH: “Ten saplings, etc.“{NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The “willow” is practice going back to Moses on Mount Sinai. This is against {NAME}, since {NAME} said the willow is a word of the Torah ( Lev . 23:40 ): “Brook willows,” two. One willow for the lulab , the other willow for the Temple. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, willow and pouring of water are practice going back to Moses on Mount Sinai. This is against {NAME}, since {NAME} said the pouring of water is a word of the Torah. On the second day, ( Num . 29:19 ) “and their libations.” On the sixth day, ( Num . 29:31 ) “and its libations.” On the seventh day, ( Num . 29:33 ) “and its rules.” מ י מ spells “water”. {NAME} asked before {NAME}, why does one now plough because of old trees? He said to him, when the practice was established it was given so that when they desired to plough they might plough.
[Sheviit 1:5.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Willow, water libation, and ten saplings are institutions of the early prophets. Do they disagree? {NAME} in the name of Levi: That was the current practice; they forgot it, but the later ones got up and agreed to the opinion of the earlier ones to teach you that everything the Court insists on will come to be in the end just as Moses was told on Sinai; as {NAME} said ( Deut . 32:47 ): “For it is not an empty word, from you,” if it is empty it is from you because you do not exert yourself about it. “Because it is your life,” when is it your life? At the time that you exert yourself!
[Sheviit 1:5.4] {NAME} said to {NAME}: Babylonian, two things came from you, prostrating oneself on fast days and the willow of the seventh day. {NAME} say, and the moving.
[Sheviit 1:5.5] It was stated: “A sapling by the rule of ten and an old tree by the rule of three.” Come and see, a sapling appearing like an old tree you consider as an old tree; and you say a sapling by the rule of ten? {NAME} said, what means “by the rule of ten”? That a sapling does not follow the rule of three. That you should not say, three producing saplings are like ten non-producing ones and, similarly, three producing old ones are like ten non-producing ones. [Sheviit 1:6.4] {NAME} and {NAME} said the same thing since {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of {NAME}: He who prunes his vineyard down to less than a hand-breadth is subject to the rules of orlah because of the bad appearance. The Sages say, only if he prunes down to the ground.
[Sheviit 2:1.1] MISHNAH: Until when may one plough a shadeless field in the year preceding the Sabbatical? [Sheviit 2:1.3] Not only a field planted with melons and gourds but even when people intend to plant melons and gourds in the future it is permitted.

[Sheviit 2:1.5] What explains the difference between a shadeless field and an orchard? Since a shadeless field will be newly sown it needs existing superficial moisture but an orchard which already is planted does not need superficial moisture.
[Sheviit 2:2.1] MISHNAH: One fertilizes and hoes in melon and gourd fields until the New Year; the same applies to irrigated fields. [Sheviit 2:3.1] MISHNAH: One dirties saplings, ties them, clips them, builds them shelter, and waters them until the New Year. {NAME} says, one may water the leaves in the Sabbatical year but not the stem. One rubs unripe figs and pricks them until the New Year. One may not rub or prick unripe figs entering the Sabbatical year, or those of the Sabbatical year leaving it. {NAME} says, at a place where people usually rub them, one may not rub them because that is agricultural work, but in a place where one does not usually rub, he may do so. {NAME} permits it for a tree since one may work a tree.
[Sheviit 2:3.2] HALAKHAH: “One dirties saplings” etc. The Mishnah follows Rebbi, but according to the rabbis one dirties, one removes worms in the Sabbatical year but not on [the intermediate days of] holidays. In neither case does one cup but one may remove what one sees.
[Sheviit 2:3.3] {NAME} said that {NAME} asked: What is the difference between dirtying and making a shelter? Dirtying is like appointing a watchman, a shelter creates shadow [for the plant] and it grows because of that.
[Sheviit 2:3.4] There (Mishnah 4:5), we have stated: “He who breaks off [branches] from an olive tree should not cover with dust but he may cover with stones or straw.” {NAME} said that {NAME} asked: What is the difference between straw and dust? Straw may only be compared to appointing a watchman, dust creates clay and [the plant] grows because of that.
[Sheviit 2:3.5] It was stated: “{NAME} said in the name of {NAME} that the House of Shammai say, one waters the leaves and it trickles down to the root, but the House of Hillel say, one waters both on the leaves and on the root.” In the House of {NAME} one watered with a basket. {NAME} said: {NAME} watered with a basket. {NAME}: {NAME} watered with a basket and hoed. Did he intend to work the land? In the days of {NAME} they watered date palms with new brooms and dried branches
[Sheviit 2:3.6] “One rubs unripe figs,” etc. We have stated: “One rubs unripe figs.” In the House of Rebbi they stated: “These are the unripe figs from the year before the Sabbatical which enter the Sabbatical.” {NAME} follows our Mishnah. {NAME} follows those who stated in the House of Rebbi. In the opinion of {NAME}, {NAME} comes only to make things easy. In the opinion of {NAME}, {NAME} comes only to make things harder.
[Sheviit 2:4.1] MISHNAH: One does not plant, sink, or graft in the year preceding a Sabbatical year later than thirty days before the New Year; if he planted, sank, or grafted he has to uproot it. {NAME} said, any graft that does not take hold within three days will never take hold; {NAME} and {NAME} say, within two weeks.
[Sheviit 2:4.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not plant … or graft”, etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Our Mishnah [deals with the] unadvertised [case], but if it is clear [e. g. when] he ploughed, it is permitted.
[Sheviit 2:4.3] “One does not plant, sink, or graft in the year preceding a Sabbatical year later than thirty days before the New Year; if he planted, sank, or grafted he has to uproot it.” If one did not uproot, what is with its yield? {NAME} and {NAME} were sitting in Tyre when a case came before them. {NAME} taught that the fruits should be thrown away. {NAME} said, I was not counted with them on the upper floor. They said, let us go out and study. They went out and heard {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not make a new restriction. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not add to a restriction.
[Sheviit 2:4.4] If he planted and died, may his son keep it? {NAME} stated from {NAME}: If he planted and died, his son may not keep it. This follows the one who says because of the suspicion, but because of the building of the father, his son may build.
[Sheviit 2:4.5] It was stated: “If somebody planted, sank, or grafted 30 days before the New Year, it counts for him as a full year and he is permitted to keep it in the Sabbatical year. Less than 30 days before the New Year, it does not count for him as a full year and he is not permitted to keep it in the Sabbatical year. Truly, they said, the fruits from this planting are forbidden until the fifteenth of Shevaṭ.” What is the reason? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} ( Lev . 19:24 ): “And in the year.” How do you understand this? {NAME} said ( Lev . 19:23 ): “Three years they shall be uncircumcised for you, and in the [fourth] year.”
[Sheviit 2:4.6] {NAME} said before {NAME}: It is understandable if they were planted thirty days before the New Year. But if they were not planted thirty days before the New Year? Come and see: A full year is counted for him, and you say so? He said to him: If it is so, even if they were planted thirty days before the New Year, should it not be forbidden until thirty days before the New Year? What about it? {NAME} said, since it stands in the middle of its year, it has to finish its year.
[Sheviit 2:5.1] MISHNAH: Rice, millet, poppies, and sesame that took root before the New Year are tithed for the past year and are permitted in the Sabbatical year. Otherwise they are forbidden in the Sabbatical and tithed for the coming year. {NAME} says, Egyptian bean which one sowed originally for its beans has the same rules. {NAME} says, large peas have the same rules. {NAME} says, [only] large peas when they formed pods before the New Year.
[Sheviit 2:5.2] HALAKHAH: “Rice, millet,” etc. For produce they went after its being a third [ripe], for rice after roots taking hold, and for vegetables the collection is the time of its tithing. From where that they could go after its being a third [ripe] for produce? ( Deut . 16:16 ) “From your threshing-floor and from your wine-press.” “From your threshing-floor”, not all your threshing-floor, “from your wine-press”, not all your wine-press. Then also if it is less than a third [ripe]? {NAME} said, it is written ( Deut . 14:22 ): “Tithe! You should tithe all produce of your seed,” something which may be sown and will sprout; this excludes produce less than a third [ripe] which when sown will not sprout. Then one should tithe the first third for the past and the other two thirds for the future! {NAME} said, from the holiday of Tabernacles. Just as Tabernacles belongs to the next year but you celebrate it for the past, so this one is for the future and you celebrate it for the past.
[Sheviit 2:5.3] One might say, this similarly applies to rice, millet, poppy seeds, and sesame! {NAME} said, there it is impossible to recognize. They objected to {NAME}, was it not stated: He collects it together with his threshing, it turns out that he tithes from his seeds for his vegetable and from his vegetable for his fruits? {NAME} said, {NAME} confirmed it; {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is written ( Deut . 14:22 ): “Tithe! You should tithe all produce of your seed,” you give one tithe in one year but not two tithes in one year. They objected, does not Egyptian bean require two tithes in one year? Was it not stated: He collects it together with his threshing, it turns out that he tithes from his seeds for his vegetable and from his vegetable for his fruits? {NAME} said, it is written ( Lev . 25:3 ): “Six years you shall sow your field and harvest.” Six sowings and six harvests, not six sowings and seven harvests. {NAME} said, we cannot hold with six but instead hold with seven; so it is: Six sowings and seven harvests, not six sowings and five harvests. They objected, does not Egyptian bean have six sowings and five harvests? As it was stated: He collects it together with his threshing, it turns out that he tithes from his seeds for his vegetable and from his vegetable for his fruits.
[Sheviit 2:5.4] On which basis did they rule that for vegetables their collection is the time of tithing? ( Deut . 16:16 ) “From your threshing-floor and from your wine-press.” Threshing-floor and wine-press are sustained by the waters of the preceding year, you go for them after the past. These live from the waters of the coming year, you go for them to the future. They objected, but Egyptian beans, if one sowed them for the beans, are tithed for the past, but if he sowed for vegetable, they are tithed for the future. Does it hold a charm [to know that] if one sowed them for the beans, they drink from the past year, but if he sowed them as vegetable, they drink from the future year?
[Sheviit 2:5.5] What means תרמילו? They produced pockets.
[Sheviit 2:5.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} said, {NAME} instructed {NAME} Zadoq’s, following {NAME}.
[Sheviit 2:5.7] It was stated: The Sages enumerated six cases for Egyptian bean. If one sowed it for seeds it is tithed for the past; if he sowed it as vegetable it is tithed for the future. If he sowed it for both seeds and vegetable, or if he sowed for seeds and then wanted it as vegetable, one may tithe from its seed on vegetable and from vegetable on seeds, on condition that it was one-third ripe before the New Year. But if it was only ripe one-third after the New Year, its seed is tithed for the past and its vegetable is tithed at the moment of its being plucked if it was collected before the New Year. But if some of it was collected after the New Year, both seed and vegetable are tithed for the future.
[Sheviit 2:5.8] If he sowed it for seeds and then thought about it for vegetable, it follows his thought. If he sowed it as vegetable, the thought of seeds cannot take hold on it unless he withheld three morbiot . That is, if it was one-third ripe before the New Year, but if it was not one-third ripe before the New Year, even if he did not withhold three morbiot . If he sowed for seeds and all [plants] formed complete pods before the New Year, its seeds are tithed for the past year, its greens are tithed at the time of their harvest. If some [plants] had formed complete pods but some did not, that is the case of: “He collects it together with his threshing, it turns out that he tithes from his seeds for his vegetable and from his vegetable for his fruits”. {NAME} stated: Even if not all [plants] formed complete pods before the New Year, its seeds are tithed for the past year, its greens are tithed at the time of their harvest. {NAME} said, that is if it was one-third ripe for the intention of seeds. But if it was one-third ripe for the intention of vegetables, it is impossible to say that its seeds are tithed for the past year and its greens are tithed at the time of their harvest, since you say that “he collects it together with his threshing; it turns out that he tithes from his seeds for his vegetable and from his vegetable for his seeds”.
[Sheviit 2:5.9] If one sowed it for seeds before the Sabbatical New Year, then in the Sabbatical year both seeds and vegetables are permitted. If one sowed it as vegetable before the Sabbatical New Year, then in the Sabbatical year both seeds and vegetables are forbidden. If one sowed it both for seeds and vegetable before the Sabbatical New Year, then in the Sabbatical year clearly seeds are permitted. What is the status of vegetables? {NAME} stated “forbidden”, {NAME} stated “permitted”. He who says “permitted” follows the word of the orah. He who says “forbidden”, because of the bad impression. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Then it should be forbidden even to use it to feed one’s animals, because of the bad impression. He said to him, one should not give to his son or to his agent, nor should he harvest in a row. {NAME} said, if a hole was torn out it is permitted. Even according to him who says it is forbidden, if he harvested and found vegetable in it, it is permitted. Similarly, when a man came carrying ten bundles of Lybian [beans] as tithe to {NAME}, he said that this should not be done; do not harvest more than what is needed for the pan.
[Sheviit 2:5.10] If one sowed it [for seeds] before the New Year of the eighth year, then in the eighth year both seeds and vegetables are forbidden. If one sowed it as vegetable before the New Year of the eighth year, then in the eighth year both seeds and vegetables are permitted. If one sowed it both for seeds and vegetable before the New Year of the eighth year, then in the eighth year seeds are forbidden and the vegetable is permitted.
[Sheviit 2:6.1] MISHNAH: Sterile onions and Egyptian beans from which water was withheld thirty days before the New Year are tithed for the past [year] and may be kept in the Sabbatical year; otherwise they are forbidden in the Sabbatical year and are tithed for the coming year. For those from a ba‘al field, if one withheld water for two periods, the words of {NAME}, but the Sages say three.
[Sheviit 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: What are sterile onions? Those rural onions which do not form seeds.
[Sheviit 2:6.3] {NAME} said, since he withheld water for thirty days before New Year’s Day, they are as on a ba‘al [field].
[Sheviit 2:6.4] {NAME} asked: Do they become seed-plants retroactively [or are] they seed-plants for the future? What would be the difference? If he took some within the thirty days and some afterwards, if you say that they become seed-plants retroactively, he tithes from one for the other; if you say, only in the future, he may not tithe from one for the other.
[Sheviit 2:7.1] MISHNAH: If gourds kept for seeds became hard before the New Year and unusable as food, one may keep them in the Sabbatical year; otherwise, it is forbidden to keep them in the Sabbatical year. Their buds are forbidden in the Sabbatical year. One may sprinkle with water on white dust, the words of {NAME}; {NAME} forbids it. One may tear off rice in the Sabbatical year; the words of {NAME} are that one may not trim.
[Sheviit 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: Why do I need that they became hard? Even if they did not become hard! If they became hard they fall under the rules of kitchen seed plants that are not eaten.
[Sheviit 2:7.3] How does one check? He pricks it; if it heals, it is forbidden, otherwise it is permitted.
[Sheviit 2:7.4] {NAME} said: qarmals are free from tithes. That is, as long as they did not form gourds; but when they formed gourds they are like vegetables.
[Sheviit 2:7.5] {NAME} taught that it is forbidden to sip water from colocasia leaves because they are food for deer.
[Sheviit 2:7.6] “One may sprinkle with water on white dust, the words of {NAME}; {NAME} forbids it.” {NAME} follows the rabbis and {NAME} is consistent, as we have stated there: “One may continue [to draw] water from tree to tree on condition not to water the entire field.” {NAME} said it anonymously, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They disagree anonymously. Where are we holding? If they are widely spaced, it is forbidden according to everybody, if they are tightly planted, it is permitted according to everybody. But we deal with the case that they are planted ten to a bet seah . {NAME} makes them widely spaced, the rabbis make them tightly planted. So the rabbis said, if they are widely spaced, it is forbidden to irrigate. May one continue? Let us learn the opinion of the rabbis from that of {NAME}. Just as {NAME} says, it is forbidden to irrigate but permitted to continue, so the rabbis say it is permitted to continue but forbidden to irrigate. Did we not think that according to everybody if they are widely spaced, it is forbidden; but is white dust not when they are widely spaced? But here it is the Sabbatical, there the holiday.
[Sheviit 2:7.7] What is the difference between Sabbatical and holiday? In the Sabbatical year, because work is permitted they permitted work needing effort as well was work not needing much effort. On a holiday, because work is forbidden they only permitted work to prevent loss and only if it does not need much effort. Some want to understand it from this: During the Sabbatical year, which lasts for a long time, they permitted; during holiday, which is a short time, they forbade. But would it not be reasonable to make these other seven days equal to the seven days of the holiday, and should they not be forbidden? It was found stated: “One may sprinkle with water on white dust during the Sabbatical year but not during the holiday, the words of {NAME}; {NAME} forbids it.”
[Sheviit 3:1.1] MISHNAH: When may one bring out manure to form dungheaps? From the moment the agricultural workers stop, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, when the colocynth dried up. {NAME} says, when it forms its fruit. How much manure may one use? Up to three dungheaps for a bet seah , each one containing ten boxes of a letekh each. One may add boxes but not dungheaps; {NAME} says, also dungheaps.
[Sheviit 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: “When may one bring out,” etc. Is it permitted to assemble a dungheap at the door of one’s courtyard before the agricultural workers stop? Silanus asked {NAME} and he forbade it to him. {NAME} said, he permitted it, and they were gossipping about him that he was taking the tithe. He instructed himself to leave the Land, so that he could not take the tithe. Then should it be forbidden even after the agricultural workers did stop because of the bad impression, that they would not say, he brings it out to his irrigated field? The people of one’s town know whether he has an irrigated field or not. {NAME} said, this means that they did not worry about a bad impression on passers-by.
[Sheviit 3:1.3] May one do that during the prohibition of the first two terms? Let us hear from the following: “One may sell and transport manure with those who work during the Sabbatical year until the New Year, with a Gentile and a Samaritan even during the Sabbatical year on condition that he not unload the boxes.” It said only, “on condition that he not unload the boxes,” hence he is permitted to transport. That means it is permitted. If you say it is forbidden, he should be forbidden to transport.
[Sheviit 3:1.4] “When the colocynth dried up.” Citrullus colocynthis . {NAME} said, that means the colocynth of the open field.
[Sheviit 3:1.5] “When it forms its fruit.” When it forms many fruits. {NAME} said, when its uppermost fruit is fully formed, it immediately dries up. About this we have stated: Their statements are close to each other.
[Sheviit 3:1.6] {NAME} said, if he uses fewer boxes; hence, two are permitted. {NAME} questioned, if he uses fewer boxes, then two should be forbidden. But where do we hold? If he exceeds the measure, as we have stated: “{NAME} says, one may not add boxes or dungheaps, but the Sages say, one may add boxes but not dungheaps.” If one adds boxes, are they not of full measure? Similarly, one brings out to the dungheap even full measures.
[Sheviit 3:2.1] MISHNAH: A person may fill his entire field with dungheaps, three each per bet seah ; more is forbidden, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, only if he raises or lowers it by three [hand-breadths]. A person may store his entire manure together; {NAME} says only if he raises or lowers it by three [hand-breadths]. If he had little, he may continuously add to it; {NAME} says only if he raises or lowers it by three [hand-breadths] or puts it on a rock.
[Sheviit 3:2.2] HALAKHAH: Why is this stated twice? {NAME} said, there if he used fewer boxes, but here if he makes it according to the measure. We have stated thus about {NAME}: “On condition that he use no less than three boxes per dungheap.”
[Sheviit 3:2.3] “But the Sages forbid.” When he brings more than the measure. But if the full measure is permitted in three places, so much more in one place.
[Sheviit 3:2.4] One may give two explanations: If he had little [manure] on his field, he may continuously add to it after the agricultural workers stopped; {NAME} forbids it. What is the reason of {NAME}? Maybe there will be manure and it will turn out that he fertilizes that place. One may give another explanation: If he had little [manure] in his house before the Sabbatical year and he wants to transport it to his field during the Sabbatical, he may continuously add to it after the agricultural workers stopped; {NAME} forbids it. What is the reason of {NAME}? Maybe there will be no more manure and it will turn out that he fertilizes that place. Has it not been fertilized before the Sabbatical year? {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because of the bad impression [it is forbidden] unless he transports ten boxes together. Do the rabbis not care for a bad impression? {NAME} said his stick, his basket, and his shovel prove that he intends to make a dungheap.
[Sheviit 3:2.5] {NAME} applied these traditions from here, as we have stated: “{NAME} said, one does not build a new water canal during the intermediate days of holidays or during the Sabbatical year.” {NAME} said, because he would prepare its banks to be sown. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because of the bad impression. They wanted to say, the one who says there “because of the bad impression” says here “because of the bad impression”; the one who says “because he would prepare its banks to be sown”, what can he say here? The only answer would be “maybe there will be no more manure and it will turn out that he fertilizes that place.” What would be the difference between them? If he dug to build a water canal for a building. They wanted to say, the one who says there “because of the bad impression” will say in this case “because of the bad impression,” but the one who says there "because he would prepare its banks to be sown,” here its banks will not be prepared to be sown. Everybody agrees that if he built there with lime, pebbles, stones, or cement it would be permitted.
[Sheviit 3:3.1] MISHNAH: He who wants his field to be fertilized makes a corral enclosing two bet seah . He may remove the walls in three directions and leave the middle one; then he may fertilize four bet seah ; {NAME} says eight bet seah
[Sheviit 3:3.2] HALAKHAH: There, we have stated: “A field cleared of thistles may be sown after the Sabbatical year. If it was improved or manured, it may not be sown after the Sabbatical year.” {NAME} said, so is the Mishnah: He who wants to put his flock on his field makes a corral enclosing two ḅet seah.
[Sheviit 3:3.3] With everything one makes [walls of] corrals, with bast mats, straw, or stones, or even three ropes one above the other.
[Sheviit 3:3.4] On condition that between one corral and the next there be less than a full corral. In that place he milks, shears, and through it leads his flock in and out.
[Sheviit 3:3.5] It was stated: “{NAME} says, if he wishes he sticks a peg into the ground and makes four corrals in the four cardinal directions for a total of eight bet seah .”
[Sheviit 3:3.6] “ One does not fertilize on the Sabbath, on holidays, or on the intermediate days of holidays, even if only for goodwill. One is not permitted to put a watchman there, nor to have the flock relieve themselves, and if they came by themselves one may not help them. But if they were working with him over the Sabbaths and holidays, he is permitted to put a watchman there, to have the flock relieve themselves, and if they came by themselves he may help them.” It was stated: “{NAME} says, on the Sabbath [workers] fertilize for goodwill, on the holidays for meals, and on the intermediate days of holidays even for wages.”
[Sheviit 3:3.7] It was stated: “He who rents a flock may not help them to relieve themselves.” What means to help them to relieve themselves? He moves the animals from place to place. That is, if he rented them for a short time. But if he rented it for a longer period it is permitted; only the last day is forbidden.
[Sheviit 3:3.8] {NAME} in the name of Rab {NAME}: He who goes to do his needs and cannot relieve himself should walk around and he will be able to relieve himself. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Ḥafrita root is good for the intestines.
[Sheviit 3:3.9] {NAME} asked: Before the agricultural workers stopped, may one be permitted to take from the corral and put on his field in the way people treat dung?
[Sheviit 3:4.1] MISHNAH: Nobody should start a quarry inside his field unless there were three heaps of three by three standard stones, 27 stones in all. A stone wall containing ten stones, each a load for two carriers, may be taken away. The measure of a stone wall is ten hand-breadths. Less than that is a quarry; he may cut it down to a distance of less than a hand-breadth from the soil. That is, from his own. But from another person’s, he may take what he wants. That is, if he did not start it before the Sabbatical year. But if he started it before the Sabbatical year, he may take what he wants.
[Sheviit 3:4.2] HALAKHAH: How is this? Three times nine, nine times three, 27.
[Sheviit 3:4.3] It was stated: If there was a quarry between him and his neighbor and the neighbor had started to quarry it when it was permitted, this is permitted. But if it was empty of stones it is forbidden.
[Sheviit 3:4.4] There, we have stated: “Any moulding brings impurity, the frieze [and] the Giblean frieze [only] when they are open one hand-breadth.” {NAME} sayd, that means that anybody who receives a row of building stones from another person must prepare for it a space of four hand-breadths. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says so: “When did they say that any moulding brings impurity? For a moulding higher than the door by three rows of stones which is twelve hand-breadths.” Why did they state “rows of stones?” For the legal standard.
[Sheviit 3:4.5] {NAME} asked, are these standards like those standards? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: These standards are like those standards. Here you say “the measure of a stone wall is ten hand-breadths, less than that is a quarry;” and there you say so? Where do we stand? If there were two rows of stones, one should state “eight hand-breadths”; if there were three one should state “twelve hand-breadths!” {NAME} said, deduct half a hand-breadth for hewing top and bottom and so for the next row, one finds three rows of ten hand-breadths. Less than that is neither a stone wall nor a quarry.
[Sheviit 3:4.6] We have stated: “{NAME} said that is if he did not intend to improve his field; but if he intended to improve his field even more is permitted. {NAME} said, that is if he did not intend to improve his field; but if he intended to improve his field even less is forbidden.” {NAME} said, {NAME} taught following the Tanna who is lenient.
[Sheviit 3:5.1] MISHNAH: Stones which the plough displaced or which were hidden and became uncovered may be taken if among them there are two which are a load for two carriers. He who clears his field from stones takes the upper ones and leaves those which touch the soil. And so from a round heap of pebbles or a stone heap, he takes the upper ones and leaves those which touch the soil; if beneath them is rock or straw they may be taken.
[Sheviit 3:5.2] HALAKHAH: Not only if the plough displaced them, but even if the plough might displace them in the future. {NAME} said, a baraita says so: “They may be taken if among all of them there are two which are a two-person load”.
[Sheviit 3:5.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This means that it is forbidden to collect pebbles from another person’s field, for if he weeds, he will put his grasses there. That is, in an agricultural area, but on mountains and rocks it is permitted and he will think of it a kindness.
[Sheviit 3:6.1] MISHNAH: One does not build steps out of ravines before the Sabbatical year after the rains stopped because that is preparation for the Sabbatical. But he may build during the Sabbatical year after the rains stopped because that is preparation for the year after the Sabbatical. One should not fill with earth but he may use it for a divider. Any stone may be taken if he can stretch out his hand and take it.
[Sheviit 3:6.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME}: The Mishnah refers to the prohibition of the two terms. It was stated: “{NAME} and {NAME} forbid it.” Does this not refer to the prohibition of the two terms, so here also about the prohibition of the two terms. {NAME} inquired: If this is about the prohibition of the two terms, did we state that one is permitted to plough but forbidden to build? So it must refer to the permission of the two terms. If it refers to the permission of the two terms, we have stated: “But he may build during the Sabbatical year after the rains stopped because that is preparation for the year after the Sabbatical.” {NAME} said, is {NAME} correct? In the first case, one is permitted to plough because that prepares for the year after the Sabbatical. It is forbidden to build since that prepares for the Sabbatical. The Mishnah does not say so, “but he may build during the Sabbatical year after the rains stopped because that is preparation for the year after the Sabbatical.”
[Sheviit 3:6.3] “He should not cover it with earth but he may use it for a divider.” What is a divider? It divides, as it is said ( Ez. 13:10 ): “He is building a dividing wall.”
[Sheviit 3:7.1] MISHNAH: Shoulder stones come from anywhere. The contractor may bring them from anywhere. These are shoulder stones: Any which cannot be taken up with one hand, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says shoulder stones are what their name indicates; all that can be carried on the shoulder by three’s or two’s. Somebody building a fence between his property and the public domain may dig down to the bedrock. What should he do with the soil? He makes heaps in the public domain and then uses it to improve [the public domain], the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, just as one may not damage the public domain, so one may not improve it. What should he do with the soil? He makes heaps on his own property in the way of those who manure. The same rule applies to somebody digging a cistern, a ditch, or a cave.
[Sheviit 3:7.2] HALAKHAH: “Shoulder stones come from anywhere,” even from his own [property] and “the contractor may bring from anywhere,” even smaller than shoulder stones.
[Sheviit 3:7.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They stated only “between his property and the public domain”; hence, between his own and his neighbor’s properties [building] is forbidden in the Sabbatical year. [Sheviit 5:2.6] {NAME} explains the Mishnah before the New Year of the Sabbatical: If one planted before the New Year of the Sabbatical, it formed a bulb before the Sabbatical; he pressed [the leaves] down during the Sabbatical and tore them out after the Sabbatical. If you say that pressing down is like tearing out, everything is for the poor. If you say that pressing down is not like tearing out, not everything is for the poor. Because of this doubt, he should settle with the poor.
[Sheviit 5:2.7] {NAME} explains the Mishnah as referring to the eve of New Year’s Day of the Sabbatical. If he planted on the eve of New Year’s Day of the Sabbatical, it grew a bulb at the start of the Sabbatical; then he pressed [the leaves] down during the Sabbatical and tore them out after the Sabbatical. If you say that pressing down is like tearing out, everything belongs to the farmer. If you say that pressing down is not like tearing out, not everything belongs to the farmer; therefore, the poor have no settlement with the farmer.
[Sheviit 5:2.8] “If it was in the ground three years, he gives one quarter to the poor. Two years, he gives one half to the poor.” {NAME} explains the baraita before New Year’s Day of the Sabbatical, {NAME} explains the Mishnah [as dealing with] the eve of New Year’s Day of the Sabbatical.

[Sheviit 5:3.1] MISHNAH: These are the implements which the professional may not sell during the Sabbatical: A plough and all its implements, a yoke, a winnowing fork and an axe. But he may sell a hand sickle, a grain sickle, a carriage and all its implements. This is the principle: Everything that is used only for its work is forbidden; [if it is usable] for both forbidden and permitted [work] it is permitted. The seller may sell five oil amphoras and fifteen wine amphoras because so much one brings from ownerless property. If he brought more than that amount, it is permitted. He may sell to Gentiles in the Land and to Jews outside of the Land. The House of Shammai say, one may not sell to him a ploughing cow during the Sabbatical but the House of Hillel permit it because he might slaughter it. One may sell him produce even during the sowing season and lend him one's measuring device even though one knows that he has workers, and one may exchange coins for him even though one knows that he has workers. In all cases it is forbidden if specified.
[Sheviit 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: “These are the implements”, etc. {NAME} said: So is the Mishnah: “These are the implements which the professional may not sell during the Sabbatical to a person suspected of violating the Sabbatical.” If one does not know, what is the rule? Since it was stated “[if it is usable] for both forbidden and permitted [work] it is permitted”, that means that it is permitted if one does not know.
[Sheviit 5:3.3] “The potter may sell”. Should we not worry and say, maybe he will switch? {NAME} said, one recognizes, these are for wine and those for oil. {NAME} said, the material of these is known and the material of those is known.
[Sheviit 5:3.4] “He may sell to Gentiles in the Land” even a larger quantity “and to Jews outside of the Land” even for what was bought in the Land.
[Sheviit 5:3.5] “The House of Shammai say”, etc. It was stated: If somebody sells an ox and it turns out be a goring one, Rav said it is an erroneous transaction but {NAME} says, he can tell him: I sold it to you for slaughtering. What are we talking about? If he sold it to a sharecropper, he sold it for ploughing. If he sold it to a butcher, he sold it for slaughter. But we are considering that he sold it to a broker. Rav said it is an erroneous transaction but {NAME} says, he can tell him I sold it to you for slaughtering. The reasoning of Rav is inverted, the reasoning of {NAME} is inverted. For they disagreed: If he sold it during the Jubilee year itself, Rav said he acquired it and it leaves his hand in the Jubilee year; {NAME} says he did not acquire. The reasoning of Rav is inverted: there he said he acquired and here he said he did not acquire. There the Jubilee is public knowledge but here there is an erroneous transaction. The reasoning of {NAME} is inverted: there he said he did not acquire and here he said he acquired. For what purpose did he sell it to him if not for sowing? But here he can tell him I sold it to you for slaughtering.

Rav follows the House of Shammai, but even if he would follow the thinking of the House of Hillel, people do not usually keep for thirty days. If he keeps it for thirty days would it not be an erroneous transaction? {NAME} follows the House of Hillel, but even if he would follow the thinking of the House of Shammai, people do not usually slaughter ploughing cattle.

The wife of a fellow may lend to the wife of a vulgar a coarse sieve and a fine sieve, she may cull, grind and sift with her, but she may not touch hers once water has been put in because one does not support transgressors. All this has only been said for communal peace. One encourages Gentiles in the Sabbatical year but not Jews. One greets them for communal peace.

I can say a coarse sieve to count coins, a sieve to sift sand, grindstones to grind spices, a stove to put in flax bundles.

If one saw him buying from Saracens. [Sheviit 5:4.6] “All this has only been said for communal peace.” {NAME}, {NAME}. One said: “Plough it well then I will rent it from you after the Sabbatical.” The other one said: “May you succed” For him who says plough it well, what means “one greets them”? “May you succed.” For him who says may you succed, what means “one greets them”? Jewish greeting, “Peace upon you.”
[Sheviit 5:4.7] Explanation: {NAME} and {NAME} passed by one of the ploughmen in the Sabbatical. {NAME} said to him, may you succed. {NAME} said to him, did not Rebbi teach us ( Ps . 129:8 ): “The passers-by did not say, the blessing of the Eternal be on you,” that it is forbidden to say “may you succeed” to one who ploughs in the Sabbatical. He told him, you know to read but you do not know to make a homily. “The passers-by did not say,” these are the nations of the world who pass out of the world, they did not say to Israel “the blessing of the Eternal is on you.” What does Israel say to them, “we bless you in the Name of the Eternal.” All blessings that come into the world because of us are not enough for you, you do not say, come and take from these blessings for yourselves, but you roll over us pro-rated contributions and fines, head taxes and annonae .
[Sheviit 6:1.1] MISHNAH: There are three territories regarding the Sabbatical. Every place held by the immigrants from Babylonia from Akhzib inside the Land of Israel cannot be eaten from or worked. Every place held by the immigrants from Egypt between Akhzib and Euphrates and Amanus can be eaten from but not worked. From Euphrates or Amanus to their side they can be eaten from and worked.
[Sheviit 6:1.2] HALAKHAH: It is written ( Deut . 12:1 ): “These are the statutes and the rules of law which you will be required to follow in the Land.” In the Land you are required to follow them but not outside the Land. Still we say obligations depending on the Land apply only in the Land, but we might think that obligations not depending on the Land also should apply only in the Land. The verse says ( Deut . 11:16–18 ) “Guard yourselves, lest your heart be seduced … And the Eternal’s rage be inflamed against you, etc. Put these words on your hearts, etc.” Even if you are exiled. ( Deut . 11:18 ) “Put these words on your hearts and your persons.” You have to say, for example tefillin and the study of Torah. Just as tefillin and the study of Torah do not depend on the Land and apply both in the Land and outside the Land, so everything not depending on the Land applies both in the Land and outside the Land.
[Sheviit 6:1.3] If it is so, they should have been freed once they were exiled. It is written ( Neh . 8:17 ): “All the congregation coming from captivity made Sukkot and sat in tabernacles … something nobody had done since the days of Joshua bin Nun.” Why Joshua? {NAME}, {NAME}: The verse damaged the reputation of the just person in his grave for the reputation of the just person in his time; it compares their coming in the days of Ezra to the coming in the days of Joshua. As at the coming in the days of Joshua they had been free and became obligated, also at the coming in the days of Ezra they had been free and became obligated. How did they become obligated? {NAME} said, they became obligated by the words of the Torah; that is what is written ( Deut . 30:5 ): “The Eternal, your God, will bring you to the Land that your fathers had inherited and you will inherit it.” Just as the inheritance of your fathers was by the words of the Torah, so your inheritance is by the words of the Torah. “He will be good to you and give increase to you more than to your forefathers.” Your fathers had been free and became obligated, also you had been free and became obligated. On your fathers was no yoke of government, but you even though there is on you the yoke of government. Your fathers did become obligated only after 14 years, seven they conquered and seven they distributed, but you became obligated immediately when you entered. Your fathers did become obligated only after they had acquired all, you become obligated for every single piece at the moment you acquire it.
[Sheviit 6:1.4] {NAME} said, they accepted the tithes voluntarily. What is the reason? ( Neh . 10:1 ) “In view of all this, we execute a contract and write, signed by our princes, Levites, and priests.” How does {NAME} uphold (10:37): “The first-born of our cattle and flock”? Since they accepted upon themselves matters they were not obligated for, even matters they were obligated for are credited to them as if they were accepted voluntarily.
[Sheviit 6:1.5] How does {NAME} explain “In view of all this”? Since they accepted [the obligations] with good grace, the verse credits it to them as if they had accepted it voluntarily. How does {NAME} explain “more than your forefathers?” He explains it for the future since {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Your forefathers inherited the land of seven peoples, but you will in the future inherit the land of ten peoples. The three others are ( Gen . 15:19 ) “the Qenites, the Qenizites and the Qadmonites.” {NAME} said, [these are] Arabia, Salmaia and Nabataea. {NAME} says, Asia, Spain, and Damascus. {NAME} says, Asia, Cartagena, and Thrace. Rebbi says, Edom, Moab, and the best of Ammon. “More than your forefathers”: Your forefathers, even though they were redeemed, were later subjugated again. But you when you are redeemed will not be subjugated again. What is the reason? ( Jer . 30:6 ) “Inquire and see whether a male gives birth.” Just as a male cannot give birth so you, after you are redeemed, will not be subjugated again.
[Sheviit 6:1.6] If one walks from Acco to Akhzib, to one’s right hand side and the East the road is pure regarding the land of Gentiles and is subject to tithes and the Sabbatical unless it was known to you to be exempt. To one’s left and the West, the road is impure regarding the land of Gentiles and is free from tithes and the Sabbatical unless it was known to you to be obligated, until one arrives at Akhzib; {NAME} said in his father’s name, as far as Lablab. What is the status of Acco itself? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: From two actions of Rebbi we learn that Acco is partly of the Land of Israel and partly outside the Land. Rebbi was in Acco when he saw them eating clean bread; he asked them, how did you wash [the grains]? They said to him, a student came here and instructed us that egg water is in order. They thought, we will cook eggs and wash with the cooking water [because] they thought he was talking about cooking water of eggs when he spoke only of egg fluid. {NAME} said, at that moment they decreed that a student may not render decisions. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If a student gives instructions even according to practice, his instructions are no instructions.
[Sheviit 6:1.7] It was stated: A student who gave instructions about practice in front of his teacher has committed a deadly sin. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: Nadab and Abihu died only because they determined practice in the presence of their teacher Moses. It happened that a student gave instructions about practice in front of his teacher {NAME}. The latter said to his wife {NAME}: That one will not live out his week. The week was not completed when he died. His students said to him: Rebbi, you are a prophet. He said to them ( Amos 7:14 ) “I am neither a prophet nor the disciple of a prophet” but I have received a tradition that any student who gives instructions about practice in front of his teacher has committed a deadly sin. It was stated: A student is forbidden to give instructions about practice during the lifetime of his teacher unless he be at a distance of at least 12 mil from him, [the breadth of] the camp of Israel. What is the reason? ( Num . 33:49 ) “They encamped along the Jordan from Bet Hayyešimot to Abel Haššiṭṭim”; how far is this? Twelve mil . Like this: {NAME} was in Ḥefer; they asked him repeatedly and he gave instructions about practice. When you mention the Sabbatical, its produce is forbidden in the minutest amount only after it must be destroyed, but for food if it can be tasted.” What do they do with it? {NAME} and {NAME} explain it in mixtures, but as far as growing plants are concerned, this is more severe since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: An onion of kilaim in a vineyard, taken out of the ground and replanted, stays forbidden even if it grows enormously because growth of something forbidden cannot neutralize the prohibition. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME} as we have stated ( Terumot 9:4): “A growth from heave is heave but the growth from its growth is profane. But the growth from ṭevel , First Tithe, aftergrowth of the Sabbatical, heave of the tithe, dema‘ , and First Fruits is profane.” We have stated on this: “When is this true? If the seed disappears. But if the seed does not disappear even growth from growth is forbidden.” How does {NAME} deal with this? He explains it that the sanctity of the Sabbatical applies when it must be destroyed, but for food once the new growth is the majority it is permitted.
[Sheviit 6:3.5] {NAME} went up to Arbel and was received by {NAME}. They came and asked him about these onions; he taught them the statement of {NAME} “once the new growth is the majority it is permitted.” He saw them relying on him; then he said to them: I was referring only to those that are bent down {NAME} said, I know beginning and end; when he heard that {NAME} and {NAME} disagreed, he shrank from it.
[Sheviit 6:4.1] MISHNAH: When may one buy vegetables in the year following the Sabbatical? After similar ones are ready. When the early ripe one is ready, the late is permitted. Rebbi permitted to buy vegetables immediately after the end of the Sabbatical. One does not export oil to be burned and produce of the Sabbatical from the Land to outside the Land. Rebbi said, I heard explicitely that one exports to Syria but not to outside the Land. One does not bring heave from outside the Land into the Land. Rebbi said, I heard explicitly that one may bring from Syria but not from outside the Land.
[Sheviit 6:4.2] HALAKHAH: Originally, vegetable was forbidden at border settlements of the Land of Israel. They decreed that vegetable should be permitted at border settlements of the Land of Israel but it would still be forbidden to import vegetables from outside into the Land. Then they decreed that it was permitted to import vegetables from outside into the Land but it would still be forbidden to buy vegetables immediately after the end of the Sabbatical. Rebbi permitted to buy vegetables immediately after the end of the Sabbatical except for leeks. What did the Sepphorians do? They clothed one specimen in sack and ashes and brought it before Rebbi, saying what sin did this one commit among all vegetables? He permitted it to them.

[Sheviit 7:1.1] MISHNAH: They established a comprehensive principle for the Sabbatical: Everything that is food for humans or animals or material for dye and cannot be preserved in the ground is subject to the Sabbatical and its proceeds are subject to the Sabbatical; it is subject to removal and its proceeds are subject to removal. What are these? This is the leaf of wild arum, mint, endives, leeks, purslain and milk bud . Animal feed, thistles and thorns. Dyestuffs, the wild growth of isatis and safflower. These are subject to the Sabbatical and their proceeds are subject to the Sabbatical; both they and their proceeds are subject to removal. They established another principle for the Sabbatical: Everything that is food for humans or animals or dyestuff and is preserved in the ground is subject to the Sabbatical; its proceeds are subject to the Sabbatical; it is not subject to removal nor are its proceeds subject to removal. What are these? These are the root of wild arum, the root of mint, ceterach, ḥalbiẓin , and wild nard. Kinds of dyestuffs: madder and campeachy-wood. These and their proceeds are subject to the Sabbatical; these and their proceeds are not subject to removal. {NAME} says, their proceeds have to be removed before New Year’s Day. They said to him, they do not have to be removed, a fortiori their proceeds. Pomegranate skins and its peduncles, nut shells, and pits are subject to the Sabbatical and so are their proceeds. The dyer dyes for himself; he should not dye for payment because one does not treat the produce of the Sabbatical as merchandise, nor firstlings or heaves, carcasses, torn animals, abominations, and crawling things. One may not buy vegetables to sell them on the market but he may collect and his son sells for him. If he bought for himself and has leftovers, it is permitted to sell them. If somebody bought a first-born animal for his son’s wedding or for a holiday and now does not need it, he may sell it. Catchers of wild animals, birds, or fish who accidentally caught impure species may sell them. {NAME} says, even one who incidentally has such an opportunity may take and sell them on condition that this not be his profession, but the Sages prohibit it.
[Sheviit 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: Does the sanctity of the Sabbatical fall on dyes for humans? Let us hear from the following ( Lev . 25:6 ): “For you”, all that is needed by you. We have stated on that: For example eating, drinking, anointing, and coloring. This excludes wound dressing which is only for the sick. This excludes olentia which are only for the malodorous. {NAME} asked: Why does one exclude wound dressing because the sanctity of the Sabbatical cannot fall on it? But did we not state: “Sanctity of the Sabbatical falls on din , sad , and indigo seed that one sows after the end of the Sabbatical.” What is that? “For you”, for all of you equally. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} understood it from the following ( Lev . 25:7 ): “Shall be”, even to kindle the light and to dye. Does this not destroy animal feed? {NAME} said, explain it if animal feed is used for human needs and you cannot infer anything from it.
[Sheviit 7:1.3] Does the sanctity of the Sabbatical fall on dyes for animals? Let us hear from the following: “Roots of rose, thornbush, and sumac have no sanctity of the Sabbatical.” Does the sanctity of the Sabbatical fall on cleansing materials? Let us hear from the following: Asphodel, potash, and aloë fall under the sanctity of the Sabbatical. Does the sanctity of the Sabbatical fall on perfumes? Let us hear from the following: Parḥalabin and laurel trees have no sanctity of the Sabbatical. The colleagues: This is by {NAME}, since {NAME} said: Balsamum has no sanctity of the Sabbatical since it is no fruit. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it according to everybody referring to jonquil. What about fuel, for example oakum?
[Sheviit 7:1.4] About roses, three things were stated: Their leaves are subject to the Sabbatical and so are their proceeds; they are subject to removal and so are their proceeds. Their spine is subject to the Sabbatical and so are its proceeds; it is not subject to removal, neither are its proceeds. Its root is not subject to the Sabbatical nor are its proceeds; it is not subject to removal, neither are its proceeds. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: May one make preserves from roses? He said to him, do they have any other use? {NAME} stated that it is human food.

[Sheviit 7:1.6] The Sepphoreans asked {NAME}: May one keep moist with thistles?
