[Sheviit 7:1.7] It was stated: “Green grass and any other vegetables he took to moisturize may be used to moisturize. When he thought about them as human food it is forbidden to use them to moisturize.” {NAME} stated: One may use them to moisturize but he may not squeeze out from them because the holiness of the Sabbatical is on them. But there is no Sabbatical holiness on animal feed since you say one may use them to make wound dressing for humans. {NAME} said, we understand that one may use them to make wound dressing for humans, and we understand that one may press them to prepare medication for humans.
[Sheviit 7:1.8] There, we have stated: “Sprouts of new shoots, [of nasturtium,] and the leaves of wild arum cannot receive impurity of food until they become sweet.” Why? Because they are bitter. But are lupines not also bitter? It is different with lupines since they are human food from the start. It is different for these; we would not know that the sanctity of the Sabbatical would not fall on them unless they become sweet.
[Sheviit 7:1.9] Did not {NAME} say: Endives are important enough in the Sabbatical to become susceptible to impurity of food? The reason was spelled out: This is, before Rebbi permitted the importation of vegetables from outside the Land into the Land. But after Rebbi permitted the importation of vegetables from outside the Land into the Land, there is no difference between the Sabbatical and the other years of the sabbatical cycle. Then they should not be important unless somebody thinks about them! Do we find anything on which from the start the sanctity of the Sabbatical (falls) [does not fall] but in the end the sanctity of the Sabbatical (does not fall) [may fall] on them? They objected: “The sanctity of the Sabbatical does not fall on calamint, hyssop, and thyme if one collected them as wood. If he considered them as food, the sanctity of the Sabbatical falls on them.” {NAME} said, if he collected them first as food, the sanctity of the Sabbatical falls on them immediately.
[Sheviit 7:1.10] Calamint is ṣatra , hyssop is esoba , thyme is qornita . What are ḥalbiẓin ? Eggs of milk bud.

[Sheviit 7:1.18] There, we have stated: “{NAME} said, when is that? If he has no other, different profession. But if he has another, different profession it is permitted.” How is this implemented? [Sheviit 7:2.1] MISHNAH: Bundles of new sprouts and carobs are subject to the Sabbatical and so are their proceeds; they are subject to removal and so are their proceeds. Branches of terebinth, pistachio, and thornbushes are subject to the Sabbatical and so are their proceeds; they are not subject to removal nor are their proceeds. But the leaves are subject to removal since they fall from their stems. Roses, henna, balsamum, and chestnut are subject to the Sabbatical and so are their proceeds. {NAME} says, balsamum is not subject to the Sabbatical because it is not a fruit. If new roses were preserved in old oil, the roses should be taken out. Old in new are subject to removal. New carobs preserved in old wine and old ones in new are subject to removal. This is the principle: Anything that gives flavor to another kind is subject to removal, in its own kind in the minutest amount. The Sabbatical makes forbidden in the minutest amount in its own kind, and by giving taste in another kind.
[Sheviit 7:2.2] HALAKHAH: At the beginning of the chapter you said that one does not eat because of the roots and here you say one does eat because of the roots? {NAME} said, there they will not ultimately harden; here they will ultimately harden; after they hardened they become part of the stem.
[Sheviit 7:2.3] It was stated: “And all those which remained from the sixth year into the Sabbatical belong to the sixth except for nasturtium which is like a vegetable.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: There is no [rule that] “from the sixth year into the Sabbatical they belong to the sixth” but [they belong] to the Sabbatical. But did we not state: “Calamint, hyssop, and thyme he brought to the courtyard, (but) if it was from the second year into the third they belong to the third; from the sixth year into the Sabbatical they belong to the sixth?” Here, you count the past [year], there the coming! {NAME} said, in the third and sixth years, even though there is no second tithe, there are tithes; in the Sabbatical there is no tithe whatsoever. But did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: There is no “from the sixth year into the Sabbatical they belong to the sixth” but they belong to the Sabbatical? There it is in the possession of the landowners, here it is in the possession of the poor. He prefers one which is certain to two which are possible.
[Sheviit 7:2.4] About leaves preserved with sprouts, some Tannaïm state: both of them are subject to removal. Some Tannaïm state: neither of them is subject to removal. Leaves are subject to removal, sprouts are not subject to removal. He who says [both] are not subject to removal is {NAME}; he who says [leaves] are subject to removal but sprouts are not subject to removal is {NAME}.

If you say that unripe fruits are fruit, if he did it with heave it is permitted. Why? Because usufruct of heave is permitted but usufruct of orlah is forbidden.

[Sheviit 8:1.1] MISHNAH: They established a comprehensive principle for the Sabbatical: Nothing that is exclusively food for humans may be used for a wound dressing for humans or, it goes without saying, for animals. Anything that is not exclusively food for humans may be used for a wound dressing for humans but not for animals. Anything that is not exclusively food, for humans or for animals, if intended as food for humans or animals one puts on it all restrictions regarding humans or animals; if intended as wood then it is wood. Examples are calamint, hyssop, and thyme.
[Sheviit 8:1.2] HALAKHAH: “They established a comprehensive principle for the Sabbatical,” etc. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Human and animal food is mentioned in the paragraph. What reason do you have to say that from human food one cannot make a wound dressing but from animal feed one may make a wound dressing? He said to him ( Lev . 25:6 ): “The Land’s Sabbath shall be for you as food”, an exclusion. It excludes human food that cannot be made into wound dressing. It also excludes animal feed! {NAME} said, any interpretation you give which contradicts the prior interpretation is not valid. {NAME} did not say so, but ( Lev . 25:6 ): “The Land’s Sabbath shall be for you as food”, an exclusion, “for you, your slave, and your handmaid”, an exclusion after an exclusion, to add that human food cannot be made into wound dressing. He added animal feed! As {NAME} said, any interpretation you give which contradicts the prior interpretation is not valid. {NAME} said, when you did exclude, you excluded from human food; when you included, you included animal feed.
[Sheviit 8:1.3] May one make dyes for humans from animal feed? Since one may make dyes for humans from human food even though one may not use human food for a wound dressing, one certainly may make dyes for humans from animal feed since one may use animal feed for a wound dressing. May one make dyes for humans from materials for wound dressings? Since one may make dyes for humans from human food even though one may not use human food for a wound dressing, one certainly may make dyes for humans from wound dressing materials since one may use wound dressing materials for a wound dressing. The only question is: May one make animal dyes from human food? Just as you say for human food that one may use it to make human dyes even though one may not use it for wound dressing, similarly animal feed, though one may not use it for animal wound dressing, should be usable for animal dyes. {NAME} said, why may one make dyes from human food? Because human dyes have holiness. Should one be able to make animal dyes from animal feed when animal dyes have no holiness?
[Sheviit 8:1.4] We understand “one puts on it all restrictions regarding humans and animals” that it is forbidden to boil them to a pulp. We have stated: If the seller sells as food and the buyer buys as wood, the latter is not determining. If the seller sells as food and the buyer buys as food and then thinks of them as wood, the latter is not determining. If the seller sells as wood and the buyer buys as food and then thinks of them as wood? Where do we hold? If he gave him the money and afterwards took it up, he paid for wood. If he took it up and afterwards gave him the money, he paid for food. We must hold that he gave him the money and afterwards took it up; this is the disagreement between {NAME} and {NAME}. According to {NAME}, who said that [transfer of] money does not mean acquisition by Torah law, he paid for food. According to {NAME} who said that [transfer of] money does mean acquisition by Torah law, he paid for wood.
[Sheviit 8:1.5] If each one keeps to his word, it should be treated as follows: “If the seller sues the buyer one follows the buyer, if the buyer sues the seller, one follows the seller.” And here [one follows] the same [rule].
[Sheviit 8:2.1] MISHNAH: Sabbatical produce is to be used for food, drink, and anointing; to eat everything commonly eaten, to anoint with what commonly is used for anointing. One should not anoint with wine or vinegar, but with olive oil. The same rules apply for heave and second tithe, except that the Sabbatical admits the additional leniency that its [oil] may be used for lighting.
[Sheviit 8:2.2] HALAKHAH: What means “to eat everything commonly eaten”? “One does not oblige anybody to eat mouldy bread, or discarded leaves of vegetables, or spoiled food.” On the other hand, if somebody wants to eat raw beets or chew raw wheat kernels one does not listen to him.What means “to drink everything one commonly drinks”? “ One does not oblige anybody to drink oily fish sauce, or sour fish sauce, or wine with yeast. He who has a throat ache should not gargle with oil but he may load fish sauce with oil and sip it.”
[Sheviit 8:2.3] “One should not anoint with wine or vinegar, but with olive oil.” “If somebody has a headache or he has a scab, he may rub with oil but not with wine or vinegar.” One does not use Sabbatical oil as base for perfumes but one may buy sweet oil before the Sabbatical without worry. {NAME} thought, even from one who is suspect. {NAME} told him, they said that only if one does not know whether he is suspect or not. Impure heave may be used for lighting; even pure Sabbatical oil may be used for lighting. {NAME} went to the bath. [Sheviit 8:3.1] MISHNAH: Sabbatical produce should not be sold by measure, weight, or count. Figs may not be sold by count nor vegetables by weight. [Sheviit 8:4.1] MISHNAH: Is somebody says to a day-laborer: “Here you have an as and collect vegetables for me today”, these wages are permitted. “For its value collect vegetables for me today”, these wages are forbidden. [Sheviit 8:4.3] Their bread. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This also belongs to the practices of obfuscation. {NAME} said, I objected before {NAME}: Why should it belong to the practices of obfuscation? I say that at a place where no Jewish bread is available it is logical that Gentile bread should be permitted, but they obfuscated the matter and forbade it. {NAME} said: Does there exist obfuscation for prohibition? Is bread not like Gentile cooking? So we say: At a place where no Jewish cooking is to be found it is logical that Gentile cooking should be permitted, but they obfuscated the matter and forbade it. But so it was: At a place where no Jewish bread is available it is logical that Gentile bread should be forbidden, but they obfuscated the matter and permitted it as a necessity of life. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} [hold] with the one who permits, but only from a store. But one does not follow this.
[Sheviit 8:4.4] {NAME} said, if he shows him the stump; then he pays him only the wages of his feet. {NAME} said, even if he did not show it to him it is as if he had. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}, as it was stated: “If somebody hires a worker to bring wine for a sick person, or an apple for a sick person, if he delivered it, he must pay, otherwise he does not have to pay. But if he said to him, wine for a sick person from place X, or an apple for a sick person from place X, he has to pay him whether he delivered or not because he pays him the wages of his feet.” What does {NAME} do with this? He explains that he showed him. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}, as it was stated: “Nobody should say to his neighbor, here you have a denar and bring me gleanings today, bring me peah today. But he may say to him, for gleanings you will bring today, for peah you will bring today. The same rules apply to a Levite.” Here, he did not show him; is it considered as if he showed him? What does {NAME} dowith this? They were particularly lenient with the Sabbatical because it is rabbinical.
[Sheviit 8:4.5] “If somebody bought from the baker a loaf in the value of a dupondius [and says], when I collect vegetables from the field I shall bring to you, that is permitted.” It was stated: “{NAME} and {NAME} forbid it.” What are we talking about? About one who says, give it to me and it is clear to me [where to find it], I shall bring it to you; {NAME} and {NAME} forbid it because vegetables on the field are rare; but the Sages permit it because vegetables on the field are abundant.

There he says, washing oneself is not a necessity of life. [Sheviit 8:6.1] MISHNAH: One does not cut Sabbatical figs with the fig-knife but he may cut with a dagger. One does not tread grapes in the wine press but he may tread in a trough. One does not work olives in the oil press and with a roller but he pounds them and puts them into a hand press. {NAME} says, one may grind them in the oil press house and put them into the hand press.
[Sheviit 8:6.2] HALAKHAH: It is written ( Lev . 25:5 ) “The aftergrowth of your harvest you should not reap.” That means, not in the way of reapers. {NAME} said, if it cannot refer to forbidden aftergrowth, take it to refer to permitted aftergrowth. {NAME} said, it is needed for itself when it grew by itself. You should not say that since it grew by itself it is permitted; therefore it was necessary to say that it is forbidden. “The aftergrowth of your harvest you should not reap and the grapes of your wild growth you should not process into wine.” You may not harvest grapes from what is being watched over on the land, but you may gather grapes from what is abandoned. “You should not process into wine,” not in the way of vintners. From here, they said that “one does not cut Sabbatical figs with the fig-knife but he may cut with a dagger. One does not tread grapes in the wine press but he may tread in a trough. One does not work olives in the oil press and with a roller.” Our teachers permitted to use a roller.

[Sheviit 8:7.3] “Always the last substitute is caught and the fruit remains forbidden”. How is this? If he took meat in exchange for Sabbatical fruits, both are subject to removal in the Sabbatical. If he exchanged the meat for fish, the meat is released and the fish are obligated. If he exchanged fish for oil, the fish are released and the oil enters [into the obligation.] Always the last substitute is obligated and the fruit remains forbidden.

[Sheviit 9:2.1] MISHNAH: There are three regions for removals, Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee. Each of them has three subregions: Upper Galilee, Lower Galilee, and the Valley. From Kefar Ḥananiah upwards, everywhere no sycamores can grow, is Upper Galilee. From Kefar Ḥananiah downwards, everwhere sycamores do grow, is Lower Galilee. And the district of Tiberias and the Valley. In Jehudah the hills, the lowland, and the Southland. The lowlands of Lydda are like the Southern lowlands, its hills are like King’s Mountain. From Bet Ḥoron to the Sea is one domain. Why did they mention three regions? That in each one may eat until the last produce has vanished. {NAME} says, they mentioned three regions only for Judea; all other regions follow King’s Mountain. All regions are one for olives and dates.
[Sheviit 9:2.2] HALAKHAH: ( Lev . 25:7 ): “For your domesticated animals and the wildlife in your land, etc.” Any time a wild animal finds food on the field, your domesticated animal can eat from the house. If it is finished for wildlife on the field, it is finished for the domesticated animal from the house.
[Sheviit 9:2.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They were of the opinion that mountain wildlife does not develop in the valley, nor does valley wildlife develop on the mountains. If you want to check, bring deer and send them to a distant land; in the end they will return to their places. He did so, brought deer, covered their antlers with silver, and sent them to Africa. At the end of thirteen years they returned to their places.

[Sheviit 9:5.9] Does one not destry animal feed? Explain it that animal feed is used for humans. {NAME} said, explain it about the sanctity by removal of the Sabbatical, and it does not imply anything.
[Sheviit 9:6.1] MISHNAH: If somebody had Sabbatical produce when the time of removal came, he distributes food for three meals to everybody. The poor may eat after removal but not rich persons, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, both poor and rich persons may eat after removal. If somebody had Sabbatical produce which fell to him as inheritance or was given to him as a gift, {NAME} says it should be given to those who eat it. But the Sages say, a sinner should not be rewarded, but it should be sold to those who eat it and the payment distributed to anybody. He who eats from Sabbatical dough of which ḥallah was not taken commits a deadly sin.
[Sheviit 9:6.2] HALAKHAH: What is the reason of {NAME}: ( Ex . 23:11 ) “The destitute of your people should eat including the remainder.” What is the reason of {NAME}: ( Ex . 23:11 ) “The destitute of your people should eat with the remainder.” It was stated: {NAME} says, richpersons may eat from storage. What is the reason of {NAME}: ( Ex . 23:11 ) “The destitute of your people should eat, and the remainder.”
[Sheviit 9:6.3] {NAME} said, the Mishnah deals with unlawful produce. But was it not stated: He who finds unlawful produce may not touch it. There is a difference between a find and something that fell to him automatically.
[Sheviit 9:6.4] {NAME} said, the Mishnah deals with permitted produce. For that we stated: {NAME} said, it should be given to those who eat it. Since {NAME} is a Shammaiite, did we state: One does eat Sabbatical produce in reciprocity and without reciprocity, following the House of Shammai? For that, the rabbis answer him that the sinner should not be rewarded? They answered him according to his argument: Against your argument, when you say that it should be given to those who eat it, a sinner should not be rewarded.
[Sheviit 9:6.5] {NAME} said, {NAME} instructed regarding qwndsy ’ that their proceeds should be thrown into the Dead Sea. {NAME} asked {NAME}, may one eat kafan -dates of Ascalon? He said, it is forbidden. {NAME} stood in the market place of Caesarea when he saw a person carrying forbidden produce. He turned away his face in order not to see him and stated: take down! Why all that? That his place should be one of rebuke. {NAME} heard and said, the mother of this one gave birth to a son!
[Sheviit 9:6.6] {NAME} commanded his student: Do not buy me vegetables except from Sisera’s garden. He, may he be remembered for the good, stood nearby and said to him: Go tell your teacher that this is not Sisera’s garden; it did belong to a Jew but he killed him and took it away from him. If you want to be restrictive for yourself, be made equal to your friend.
[Sheviit 9:6.7] A man was suspected of [trading in] Sabbatical [produce]. He said to his wife, take ḥallah . She said to him, that man is suspected of Sabbatical [trading], and you say, take ḥallah ? He said to her, ḥallah is [an obligation] from the Torah, the Sabbatical is from {NAME} and his colleagues.
[Sheviit 10:1.1] MISHNAH: The Sabbatical remits any loan, with or without a document. Store credit is not remitted; if it is transformed into a loan it is remitted. {NAME} says, any preceding one is remitted. Wages of a hired hand are not remitted; if they are transformed into a loan they are remitted; {NAME} says, for any work that stops in the Sabbatical they are remitted; if it does not stop they are not remitted. If somebody slaughters a cow and divides it up on New Year’s Day, if the month was long it is subject to remission, otherwise it is not subject to remission. The rapist, the seducer, the calumniator, and all court documents are not subject to remission. If somebody gives loans on pledge, or deposits his documents with the court, they are not subject to remission.
[Sheviit 10:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The Sabbatical remits any loan, etc.” We can understand if it is without a document. With a document it should be treated similar to a loan on a pledge and not be remitted. {NAME} said, explain it for a document from which alienation of property is missing, following {NAME}. A case came before {NAME} of a document without alienation of property and he instructed that it was remitted. Because we are interpreting the Mishnah, should we act on this?
[Sheviit 10:1.3] {NAME} said, it is only if he has no real estate. Hence, if he has real estate it is not remitted. {NAME} said, even if he has real estate it is remitted. {NAME} parallels Rav, since {NAME} said in the name of Rav if he singled out real estate it is remitted. They said only “if he singled out”; therefore, if he did not single out it is not remitted.
[Sheviit 10:1.4] “If somebody established a lien on a field for his wife but then went and sold it, if she wishes she collects from this field or she collects from any other property.” {NAME} said, {NAME} instructed following this baraita . The colleagues asked: Should she not collect only from the properties that are under the lien? {NAME} said to them, there are unencumbered properties and you say, those under the lien? The baraita [applies] if he did not say you shall be paid only from this. But when he said, you shall be paid only from this, she may collect only from this.
[Sheviit 10:1.5] If somebody established a lien for another person on his field and then went and sold it; {NAME} said, it is temporarily sold. {NAME} said, even temporarily it is not sold. The strength of {NAME} is from the following: He may induce his ox to flee; he cannot induce his field to flee. Think about it, if [the field] was sold to a violent person! {NAME}, {NAME}, said: Violent persons are apt to fall.
[Sheviit 10:1.6] It was stated: “If somebody mortgages a field to a woman for her ketubah or a creditor for his claim and then sells it, that is sold and the buyer should beware for himself” This baraita if he said to her: you should be paid from this. They disagree if he says, you should only be paid from this.
[Sheviit 10:1.7] Rav said, if she compromised [her ketubah ], even if she did not extend credit, if she extended credit even though she did not compromise. {NAME} stated: Unless she would compromise it and extend credit.
[Sheviit 10:1.8] Because he extends him credit a second time, is the first turned into a loan? {NAME} said, this follows {NAME}. But can he require payment on New Year’s Day? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: About money for which he can believe him. And since he could ask him for payment, he should be able to give him money. And here, because he should have been able to give him money and he did not give, the first [debt] is turned into a loan.
[Sheviit 10:1.9] {NAME} says, for ploughing. {NAME} said, for building. In the opinion of {NAME}, any work that stops because of the Sabbatical. In the opinion of {NAME}, any work that stops in any way. Does {NAME} hold with {NAME}; does not {NAME} say, for any work that stops in the Sabbatical they are remitted, if it does not stop they are not remitted? But {NAME} does not hold with {NAME}; while “{NAME} says that it is not the way of a banker to give an as unless he has received a denar ,” he agrees that the wages of the hired man are due only at the end.
[Sheviit 10:1.10] Rebbi says, Nisan never was lengthened. But did we not state: “If the New Moon appeared in time”? If it would appear, it did not appear. Rav said, Tishre was never lengthened. But did we not state: “If the month was long”? If it would be, it never was.
[Sheviit 10:1.11] “When they sanctified the year at Usha, on the first day {NAME} led and recited following the opinion of {NAME}. {NAME} said, we did not follow this at Jabneh. On the second day, {NAME} led and recited following the opinion of {NAME}. {NAME} said, this we did follow at Jabneh.” But does this not mean that they sanctified it on the first and the second day? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: That year was disorganized. What is “the first, the second”? {NAME} in the name of Rav: The first year, the second year! But was it not stated: the first day, the second day?
[Sheviit 10:1.12] If they sanctified it before its time or after its lengthening, should I assume it was lengthened? The verse says ( Lev . 23:2 ) “them”, you, “these are My holidays.” Before its time is not “My holidays.” Before its time, the 29 day, after its lengthening, the 32 day. From where that one intercalates the year because of the [men of the] diaspora that set out but did not yet arrive? The verse says ( Lev . 23:2 ), “the Children of Israel, my holidays”. Make the holidays so they can be observed by all of Israel. {NAME} said, only if they had reached the river Euphrates.
[Sheviit 10:1.13] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: If they sanctified it and afterwards the witnesses turned out to be perjured, it still is sanctified. {NAME} stayed with {NAME} and asked him: Did you hear this from your father? He said, yes. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: One does not cross-examine the witnesses of the New Moon.
[Sheviit 10:1.14] {NAME} said, this follows {NAME} since he could ask him for payment on New Years’s Day. {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: If somebody makes a loan to another person stipulating that he will not press for repayment, the Sabbatical will remit it. We did state: “If somebody slaughters a cow and divides it up on New Year’s Day,” and {NAME} said, this follows {NAME}. But can he require payment on New Year’s Day? As {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Since he could ask him for payment, he can believe him. And since he could believe him, he could pay him. And here, because he could have given him but did not give, the first [debt] is turned into a loan.
[Sheviit 10:1.15] {NAME} in the name of Rav: If somebody gives a loan to a person on condition that the Sabbatical not remit it, the Sabbatical does not remit, as we have stated: “Whether he gives it after thirty days or after ten years.” Are there ten years without a Sabbatical? {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} disagreed. One of them said, if the loan was given on a pledge, but the other said, if he writes him a prozbol .
[Sheviit 10:1.16] It was stated: “For thirty days he will not come.” What means “for thirty days he will not come”? {NAME} said, if somebody gives a loan to a person without specifying details, he has no right to ask for payment until after 30 days. {NAME} came and explained ( Deut . 15:9 ): “The Sabbatical year, the remitting year, is close.” Is not the Sabbatical year the remitting year? Why does the verse say: “The Sabbatical year, the remitting year, is close”? That you should not say, I am not permitted to ask for payment until after 30 days; after 30 days the debt will be remitted and I will not collect; therefore, it must say that “the Sabbatical year, the remitting year, is close.” Did not {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} say in the name of Rav: If somebody makes a loan to another person stipulating that he will not press for repayment, the Sabbatical will remit it? It was found stated in the name of {NAME} ( Deut . 15:9 ): “The Sabbatical year, the remitting year, is close.” Is not the Sabbatical year the remitting year? Why does it have to say, “the Sabbatical year, the remitting year, is close”? That you should not say, all six years long his field is before me, his vineyard is before me, but after six years the debt is remitted and I cannot collect; therefore, it has to say “the Sabbatical year, the remitting year, is close.”
[Sheviit 10:1.17] “The rapist, the seducer, the calumniator.” {NAME} said, Rav [said]: This follows {NAME}, since {NAME} said, it depends on the one extending credit.
[Sheviit 10:1.18] “And all court judgments,” these are court decisions.
[Sheviit 10:1.19] This is obvious: A loan that is disputed is not remitted. A loan that was disputed but is now a [confirmed] loan, is remitted. {NAME} asked: Is this also true for judgments? It is not necessary to say that a loan that was disputed can be collected. A disputed loan turned into a [confirmed] loan is collected from property of average quality.
[Sheviit 10:1.20] “If somebody makes a loan on a pledge”, {NAME} says, even on a needle. ( Deut . 15:3 ): “What you have on your brother you shall release;” that excludes your brother’s [property] in your hand. “What you have on your brother you shall release,” which excludes one who hands over his documents to the court.
[Sheviit 10:2.1] MISHNAH: A prozbol does not remit. This is one of the ordinances of Hillel the elder. When he saw that the people refrained from giving loans to one another and transgressed what is written in the Torah, as it is said ( Deut . 15:9 ): “Guard yourself, lest there be in your heart an unworthy thought saying, etc.”, he instituted the prozbol . This is the essence of prozbol : I declare before you, judges X and Y at place Z, that I shall collect any debt due me any time I wish. The judges sign at the bottom or the witnesses.
[Sheviit 10:2.2] HALAKHAH: From here they supported the notion that prozbol is from the Torah. But is prozbol from the Torah? When Hillel instituted it, they supported it from words of the Torah.
[Sheviit 10:2.3] {NAME} said, I asked before {NAME}: Following him who says tithes [are from their words, it is understandable that Hillel instituted prozbol . But following him who says tithes] are from the Torah, does Hillel institute anything against the words of the Torah? {NAME} said, from the moment that Israel was exiled to Babylonia, did they not become free from all commandments connected with the Land, but the remission of debts applies both in the Land and outside the Land from the words of the Torah [because it is an obligation of the person]? {NAME} turned and said, ( Deut . 15:2 ) “this is the word of the abandonment, remit” as long as abandonment is followed as a word of the Torah, remission of debts applies both in the Land and outside the Land from the words of the Torah, but when abandonment is followed as their word, remission of debts applies both in the Land and outside the Land from their word. There, they say that even one who holds that tithes are from the Torah will hold that the Sabbatical is from their word. As we have stated ( Deut . 15:2 ): “this is the word of the remission, remit!” Rebbi says, these two remissions are the Sabbatical and the Jubilee. As long as the Jubilee is operative, the Sabbatical is from words of the Torah. If the Jubilees are abolished, the Sabbatical is operative from their words. When were the Jubilees abolished? ( Lev . 25:10 ) “[All its] inhabitants.” In the time when its inhabitants lived on it, not when they went into exile. If they lived on it but intermingled, the tribe of Judah in Benjamin, and the tribe of Benjamin in Judah, I could think that the Jubilee is operative. The verse mentions its inhabitants, “All its inhabitants;” you find that when the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh went into exile, the Jubilees were disestablished.
[Sheviit 10:2.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even if they are in Rome.
[Sheviit 10:2.5] {NAME} in the name of the rabbis there: If three sat in judgment and one of them died, two sign and note: Even though we are two who sign, we were three in judging. {NAME} said, our Mishnah implies this: “The judges sign at the bottom or the witnesses.” Does one learn court documents from prozbol ? It was found stated: This about court documents was learned from the rules of prozbol .
[Sheviit 10:2.6] If he has no real estate but his debtors have real estate, one writes a prozbol for him. How is that done? Ruben owes Simeon and Levi owes Ruben. Ruben has no real estate, Levi has real estate. One writes for Simeon on the properties of Levi.
[Sheviit 10:3.1] MISHNAH: A predated prozbol is valid, postdated it is invalid. Predated documents of indebtedness are invalid, postdated they are valid. If one person borrows from five, one writes a prozbol for each single [creditor]. If five persons borrow from one, he writes only one prozbol for all of them. One writes prozbol only on the basis of real estate. If he has none, [the other party] gives him the right to a minute area of their field. If he had a field mortgaged in town, one writes a prozbol on it. {NAME} says, one writes for a man on his wife’s properties and for orphans on those of the guardians. A bee hive. {NAME} says, it is like real estate: one may write a prozbol on it, it is not subject to impurity in its place, and somebody who takes honey from it on the Sabbath is guilty. But the Sages say, it is not like real estate, one may not write a prozbol on it, it is subject to impurity in its place, and somebody who takes honey from it on the Sabbath is not sanctionable. If somebody returns a debt in the Sabbatical, he [the lender] says to him: “I am remitting.” If he [the borrower] says “anyway”, he [the lender] should accept it, for it is said ( Deut . 15:2 ): “This is the word of remission”. Similarly, a homicide exiled to a city of refuge whom the citizens of the town wanted to honor, should say to them: I am a homicide. If they tell him, anyway, he should accept it, for it is said ( Deut . 19:4 ): “This is the word of a homicide.”
[Sheviit 10:3.2] HALAKHAH: “A predated prozbol is valid” because he diminishes its power, but “postdated it is invalid” because he increases its power. “Predated documents of indebtedness are invalid” because he increases their power, but “postdated they are valid” because he diminishes their power.
[Sheviit 10:3.3] Who notifies? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: the signatories of the document. But did not {NAME} say, they treated the statement of the signatories of a document as if their testimony had been cross-examined by the court? There, it is about those who would say: We did not sign at all. But here they say, on this we signed, on that we did not sign.
[Sheviit 10:3.4] {NAME} said, they are really invalid. {NAME} said, he only counts from the time of writing. But did we not state: “A prozbol is valid, whether predated or postdated, but it only counts from the time of writing”? If you assert this for financial documents, what is the difference between a prozbol and a financial document?
[Sheviit 10:3.5] “A document dated on a Sabbath or on the Tenth of Tishrē, {NAME} declares it valid and {NAME} invalid. {NAME} said to him, a case came before you in Sepphoris and you declared it valid. He said to him, I did not declare it valid, but if I did it, I did it.” They wanted to say that he who holds it invalid [does so] because it might be later, and he who holds it valid [does so] because it might be earlier; but he who holds it invalid [does so] because it might be forged.
[Sheviit 10:3.6] Rav said, only if both lender and borrower have real estate. But {NAME} says, if the creditor does but not the borrower, or the borrower but not the lender. If he has no real estate but one who owes him has real estate then one writes him a prozbol . {NAME} in the name of Rav: Even if he has only one stalk in a field, one writes him a prozbol . But did we not state: Partners, sharecroppers, and guardians have no prozbol ? They say, there each single stalk is property of the partnership but here it is his.
[Sheviit 10:3.7] May one write for a guardian based on the orphans’ real estate? Let us hear it from the following: “One writes for a husband on his wife’s properties”. May one write for a woman on her husband’s properties? Let us hear it from the following: “And for orphans on those of the guardians”.
[Sheviit 10:3.8] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The reason of {NAME} ( 1S . 14:26 ): “The people came to the forest and behold, there was a flow of honey.” What do you understand from this? {NAME} said, the thicket produced honey. If he had said from ( 1S . 14:27 ): “He dipped it into the forest of honey”, it would have been better. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: He really understood it from ( 1S . 14:27 ): “He dipped it into the forest of honey.”
[Sheviit 10:3.9] Where do we hold? If it is connected to the ground, everybody agrees that it belongs to the ground. If it is on two bars, everybody agrees that it is not like ground. But where we hold is if it rests on the ground. It compares to what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: One writes a prozbol on the space for an oven, also on the space for a hearth. {NAME} said, also on the space for a lamp.
[Sheviit 10:3.10] Is it also the same for the space for bread, is that the disagreement between {NAME} and the Sages? Honey is a product of the bee hive, bread is not a product of the oven.
[Sheviit 10:3.11] If somebody repays a debt in the Sabbatical even though he [the lender] says to him: “I am remitting,” the Sages are pleased with him. {NAME} said, he says it in a soft voice and his right hand is stretched out to receive.
[Sheviit 10:3.12] {NAME} said, this means that if a person who knows one collection goes to a place and they honor him for two, he has to tell them: “I know one collection.”
[Sheviit 10:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody repays a debt in the Sabbatical, the Sages are pleased with him. If somebody borrows from a convert whose sons converted with him, he does not have to repay the sons but if he repaid, the Sages are pleased with him. Movables are acquired only by being drawn close, but the Sages are pleased with everybody who keeps his word.
[Sheviit 10:4.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, only to his sons. {NAME} asked, what means “only to his sons?” If he has sons, one should return it to his sons. If he has no sons, one should return it to his daughters. That you should not say, since the inheritance of the convert is not settled in the Torah, he should return it to the children. Similarly, if somebody died who was the last of his family and he has no heir except his mother one does not have to repay, but if the debtor repaid the Sages are pleased with him.
[Sheviit 10:4.3] The robber who repents and wants to return what he robbed, if somebody accepts it from him, the Sages are displeased with him.
[Sheviit 10:4.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody trades in promises, there you say the Sages are displeased with him. But sometimes you say only that one gives him up to “Him who made pay”.
[Sheviit 10:4.5] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He who gives a ring as surety and wants to get out of the deal, may get out of the deal. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: A gold coin? He said to him, a ring. What is the difference between a gold coin and a ring? Gold coins are exchanged, a ring remains as it is.
[Sheviit 10:4.6] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody wanted to change his mind after he had promised a gift to another person, he may change his mind. {NAME} was with {NAME}; he said to him: Is that just no ( Lev . 19:36 ) “and just yes?” He said, when he said it, it was a just yes. Rav disagrees since Rav said, when I tell my family to give a gift to somebody, I never change my mind. A baraita disagrees with Rav: “ Where did they say that movables are acquired by being drawn close? In the public domain or in a courtyard which is not their joint property. In the domain of the buyer, when the deal was accepted; in the domain of the seller one never acquires until either he lift it up or he draw and remove everything from the prior owner’s property. In the domain of a depositary he cannot acquire unless he gave permission or rented their place out to him.” What does Rav do with this? One is if he was standing with him, the other if he was not standing with him. Rav disagrees since Rav said, when I tell my family to give a gift to somebody, I never change my mind. You should know because somebody had given surety on salt; it rose in price. He came before Rav who said, either he should give corresponding to the surety or he should be given up to “Him who made pay”. The arguments of Rav are contradictory. There he says, when I tell my family to give a gift to somebody, I never change my mind and here he says so? There it is for a legal rule; what Rav did himself was a measure of piety.

[Terumot 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Five [persons] cannot give heave and if they gave it is not heave: the deaf and dumb, the insane, the minor, and one who gives heave from what is not his. The Gentile who gave heave for a Jew’s property, even with the latter’s authorization his heave is not heave. A deaf person who speaks but cannot hear should not give heave, but if he did, his heave is heave. A “deaf person” mentioned anywhere by the Sages is a deaf-mute. {NAME} says, the heave given by a minor who has not yet grown two pubic hairs is heave. {NAME} says, before he came to the time of vows, his heave is not heave. After he has reached the time of vows, his heave is heave.
[Terumot 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Five [persons] cannot give heave,” etc. {NAME} understood all of these from here ( Ex . 25:2–3 ): “Speak to the Children of Israel that they should give heave for Me”, excluding the Gentile, “from every man”, excluding the minor, “whose intention is to volunteer”, excluding the deaf-mute and the insane. “The following is the heave you shall accept from them ”, except from one who gives heave for what is not his.
[Terumot 1:1.3] Should not their action be proof of their intentions? As we have stated there: “If a deaf-mute, insane, or minor person brought them up, they are not under the category of ‘when given’ because they have action but no intention.” What is their action? {NAME} said, when he grabs it while full of dew. We also have stated there: “If a deaf-mute, insane, or minor person brought them down, even if he thought that [his animals’] feet should be doused, it is not under the category of ‘when given’ because they have action but no intention.” What is their action? {NAME} said, when he rubs them with water. We should also say here, let their action be proof of their intentions! {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}; {NAME} in the name of the rabbis ( Num . 18:27 ): “Your heave will be credited to you.” When thought is mentioned in the verse, his action cannot prove his intentions; when thought is not mentioned in the verse, his action can prove his intentions. Since here thought is mentioned in the verse, his action cannot prove his intentions.
[Terumot 1:1.4] {NAME} said, I questioned before {NAME}: But with bills of divorce, thought is not written and his action cannot prove his intention! As we have stated: “Everybody is permitted to write a bill of divorce, even an insane person, a deaf-mute, and a minor.” {NAME} said, if a sane person directs him. {NAME} asked, is that ( Deut . 24:1 , 3 ): “he writes for her”, for her personally? {NAME} came back and said, there one person writes and another person divorces. But here, the same person thinks and takes heave. {NAME} said, there, if he would write himself and divorce, would that not be a divorce? But here, he thinks and takes heave.
[Terumot 1:1.5] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: One disagrees with this Mishnah teacher. How is that? It turns out that {NAME} concerning heaves parallels {NAME} concerning sanctification, and {NAME} concerning divorces parallels the rabbis concerning sanctification, as we have stated: “The sanctifications of a deaf-mute person, an insane, and a minor who sanctified are no sanctifications. {NAME} says, if they are alone, their sanctifications are no sanctifications. Together with others, their sanctifications are sanctifications.”
[Terumot 1:1.6] It was stated: “If a deaf-mute person gave heave, it is not heave. {NAME} said, when was this said? If he was born deaf-mute. But if he was normal and became deaf and dumb, he writes and others confirm his signature. If he hears but cannot speak, he is like a normal person.”
[Terumot 1:1.7] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: One disagrees with this Tanna. They say, does not a Mishnah disagree: “If he became deaf-mute or insane, he may never divorce.” Why can he not write and have others fulfill his written instructions? They upheld it, if he is illiterate. {NAME} objected, does not a baraita disagree: “If he wrote himself, or he told the scribe to write and the witnesses to sign, even though the scribe wrote, the witnesses signed, they gave him [the document] and he in turn gave it to her, it is no divorce.” {NAME} said, complete the sentence and there is no disgreement: “it is no divorce unless they hear his voice.” But even if he gave a sign with his head you say it is invalid, here also it is invalid. {NAME} said, it is valid: hearing the voice has the same status as seeing him nod his head!
[Terumot 1:1.8] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Just as you say that three times he must give a sign with his head, must one equally hear his voice three times? He said to him, hearing his voice once, giving a sign with his head three times.
[Terumot 1:1.9] {NAME} said, there, if he said I did such and such, here, if he says do such and such. {NAME} inquired: If he has understanding for the past, he should have understanding for the future; ifhe has no understanding for the past, he would not have understanding for the future! {NAME} said, here we deal with a mute; there is no agency for a mute. {NAME} said, we deal with a sane person. Why is there no divorce? Because I say, he was occupied with his documents. We also stated so: “When was this said? When he explained it in his regular state. But if he was paralyzed by sickness, once is enough.”

[Terumot 1:1.11] The signs of an insane: One who goes out in the night, stays overnight in a graveyard, tears his clothing, and destroys what one gives to him. {NAME} said, only if all of that is in him since otherwise I say that one who goes out in the night is a man-dog; he who stays overnight in a graveyard burns incense to spirits, he who tears up his clothing is a choleric person, and he who destroys what one gives to him is a cynic. {NAME} said, even only one of these is proof. {NAME} said, what {NAME} said, even only one of these is reasonable only for him who destroys what one gives to him; even the greatest idiot does not destroy all one gives to him. [Terumot 1:1.13] Who stated “a minor”? This does not follow {NAME}, as we have stated: “A minor whom his father put in a melon field where he was giving heave and his father sold on that basis, his heave is heave. But if he collected and gave to him, in no case does he have to worry about robbery.” Can you say it became heave retroactively? No, from now into the future! Here also, it will be made heave from now on into the future.
[Terumot 1:1.14] ( Num . 18:28 ) “you” excludes partners, “you” excludes guardians, “you” excludes one who gives heave from what is not his. [Terumot 1:1.15] “ ‘You’ excludes one who gives heave from what is not his.” What is the interpretation, one who gives heave from what is not his own, or one who gives heave from what is somebody else’s? Let us hear the following: If he declared his heap as ownerless and then smoothed it and took possession again, if you refer to one who gives heave from what is not his own, his heave is not heave, if you refer to one who gives heave from what is somebody else’s, his heave is heave. Let us hear from the following: “If he stole Temple heave and ate it, he pays two fifths and the principal because there is no double payment for Temple property.” Who gave the heave if not the administrator? Is he not giving heave from what is not his? And you say his heave is heave! The reason must be that he does not give heave from another person’s property. Or should we say, who gave the heave if not a Levite who dedicated his heave? This does not follow {NAME}, since {NAME} said the administrator is like any other person.

[Terumot 1:1.17] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: An Israel who said to a Levite: “You have a kor of tithe in my hand”, and this Levite went and made it heave of the tithe for other produce but the Israel went and gave it to another Levite, [the first one] has only a complaint on him. [Terumot 1:3.1] MISHNAH: One may not give heave from gleanings, abandoned sheaves, peah , and ownerless property; not from First Tithe of which its heave was taken; not from Second Tithe and dedicated produce which were redeemed; not from what is obligated on what is free from obligation or from what is free on what is obligated; not from harvested produce for what is standing or from what is standing for what was harvested; not from new produce for old or from old for new; not from produce of the Land for that of foreign countries or from foreign countries for produce of the Land. [Terumot 1:4.1] MISHNAH: Five categories of persons should not give heave but if they gave, their heave is heave. The mute, the drunk, the naked person, the blind, and a man who had an emission of semen should not give heave but if they gave, their heave is heave. One gives heave neither by measure, nor by weight, nor by count. But one may give heave from what was measured, weighed, or counted. One does not give heave in a measuring basket or box, but one may give in them a half or a third. One should not give half a seah of heave in a seah vessel because half of it is a [standard] measure.
[Terumot 1:4.2] HALAKHAH: “Some of these [rules] are because of the benediction, some because the [persons] are unable to give from the best. The mute, the naked person, and the man who had an emission because of the benediction, the blind and the drunk because they cannot give from the best.”
[Terumot 1:4.3] {NAME} said, one who drank [wine] should not pray but if he did pray, his prayer is a supplication. A drunk should not pray but if he did pray, his prayer is blasphemy. [Terumot 1:5.1] MISHNAH: One does not give oil as heave on crushed olives, nor wine on pressed grapes. If one did, it is heave and he has to give another heave. [Terumot 2:1.1] MISHNAH: One does not give heave from pure produce for impure, but if heave was given it is heave. One may not give heave from impure produce for pure, but if he gave in error, his heave is heave, if intentionally, he did not do anything. Similarly, a Levite who has ṭevel tithe which he continually uses to give, if he is in error, what he did is done, if intentionally, he did nothing. {NAME} says, if he had known of it earlier, even if he did it in error, he did not do anything. He who immerses vessels on the Sabbath, if unintentionally he may use them, if intentionally he may not use them. He who tithes or cooks on the Sabbath, if in error it may be eaten, if intentionally it may not be eaten. He who plants on the Sabbath, if unintentionally he may keep it, if intentionally it must be uprooted. In the Sabbatical year it must be uprooted, whether in error or intentionally.

[Terumot 2:1.4] Heave of the tithe is taken from pure produce for pure, from impure for impure, from pure for impure, but not from impure for pure. {NAME} says, just as it may not be taken from impure for pure, so it may not be taken from impure for impure. {NAME} agrees in the case of demay . That is, if he has from the same kind. If he does not have anything from the same kind, let us hear from the following: {NAME} Eyntanaya went with {NAME} to Ḥammat Gader. He bought him a roll and wanted to put it in order from one day to the next. He said to him: We do not have to worry about a single opinion! Can you say that he had from the same kind?
[Terumot 2:1.5] “In truth;” {NAME} said that every place where they stated “in truth,” it is practice going back to Moses on Mount Sinai.
[Terumot 2:1.6] “If a cake of dried figs became partially impure one may give heave from its pure part for its impure part;” but if part of it becomes impure is not all of it impure? The Mishnah deals with the case that they are connected only by fruit juice. But will it not be cut into two parts in the end? Explain it if he gave it a name when it still was connected.
[Terumot 2:1.7] “And similarly for a bunch of vegetable.” The Mishnah deals with the case that it became impure as a bunch but when the single stalks were impure and he bound them together, this does not apply. But will it not be split and made into two parts in the end? Explain it if he gave it a name when it still was connected. What is the situation if a bundle became impure, he unbound it and bound it again?
[Terumot 2:1.8] Should we have stated only fig cake and neither bunch nor heap? If we had stated about fig cake and not bunch we would have said he may give heave for the fig cake which is all one body but not for the bunch which is not one body. So it is necessary to state also “bunch”. If we had stated bunch not heap, we would have said he may give heave for the bunch because it is all held together but not for the heap which is not held together in one piece. So it is necessary to state fig-cake, necessary to state bunch, and necessary to state heap.
[Terumot 2:1.9] Since we stated: “If there were two fig-cakes, two bunches, and two heaps,” why do we need this since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME} ( Num . 18:27 ): “Your heave will be counted as if it were grain,” etc.? {NAME} said, the Mishnah speaks about heaps of green melons or squash.
[Terumot 2:1.10] If there were two fig cakes, one partially impure and one partially pure, may one give heave from one for the other? If he had two heaps, and from both of them he had given part of heaves and tithes, may he give heave from one for the other? The students of the elder {NAME} asked the elder {NAME} and he said to them ( Eccl . 4:5 ): “The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh.” {NAME} in the name of the elder {NAME}: He may not give heave from one for the other.
[Terumot 2:1.11] “If somebody brought many kinds in a box, cabbage on top and cabbage on the bottom but something else in between, he may not give heave or tithe from one for the other.” That means, if there is no empty space. But if there is empty space he may give heave or tithe from one for the other. “The entire house of the wine press is one.” The entire threshing house is one. It was stated: {NAME} said, only if the main threshing place is in the middle. So far this is for wheat; [it is] the same even for stubbles, even for straw.

He said to them, that is the case of the five sacks, as it was stated: “Five sacks on the threshing floor, one does not give heave and tithes from one for the other.”
[Terumot 2:1.13] It was stated: “{NAME} says in the name of {NAME}: For food in fluids, one gives heave from pure for impure. How is this? If somebody pickled olives in impurity and wants to give heave in purity, he brings a funnel whose opening is less than [the width of] an egg, fills it with eggs and puts it on top of the amphora; it turns out that he gives heave from what is earmarked.” Why does it have to be less than [the width of] an egg? Are these not single pieces? It is only that not many olives should become impure. “ They said to him, the only food fluid called fluid is wine and olive oil.” How is that? One beam for two pits or two beams for one pit. One understands one beam for two pits, but two beams for one pit? Is it not that if it is partially impure it is totally impure? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it, if he had intended to process it in one batch, and he changed his mind to make it in two batches. {NAME} said, this applies if it became impure after he syphoned off [the froth] and [the seeds] formed lumps. [Terumot 2:1.17] Our Mishnah is about large vessels, but with small vessels one may use a ruse and immerse them, as {NAME} had stated: “A person may fill an impure vessel from the cistern as a ruse and immerse it.” Also, we have stated: “If his pail or garment fell into the cistern, one may use this as a ruse and immerse them.” Two Amoraïm, one says [one may use a ruse] for vessels impure in original impurity; but the other one says [only] for vessels impure in derivative impurity. The one who said in derivative impurity objected to the one who said in original impurity: Even on weekdays, would it not need sundown? He said to him, if he wants to use them in purity for profane food.
[Terumot 2:1.18] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: An intelligent woman washes a cup here, a bowl there, a dish there; it turns out that her entire house was wetted on the Sabbath.
[Terumot 2:1.19] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “Unintentionally”, when it is forbidden, “intentionally” when it is forbidden. {NAME} said, the Mishnah states this: “He who tithes or cooks on the Sabbath, if unintentionally it may be eaten, if intentionally it may not be eaten”; “unintentionally”, when it is forbidden, “intentionally”, when it is [equally] forbidden. It was stated: “What was cooked on the Sabbath, if it was done unintentionally it may be eaten, intentionally it may not be eaten, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} said, unintentionally it may be eaten at the end of the Sabbath, intentionally never. {NAME} said, unintentionally it may be eaten at the end of the Sabbath by others but not by himself, intentionally neither by him nor by others.” {NAME} followed {NAME}. Rav in his own group instructed following {NAME}, in public following {NAME}. {NAME} said, he instructed us following {NAME}. As it was stated: “{NAME} said, in any case where an intentional sin is punished by extirpation and an unintentional sin by an expiatory offering, if the sin was committed on the Sabbath unintentionally or intentionally, the result is forbidden both for him and for others; it may not be eaten. In any case an intentional sin is not punished by extirpation and for the unintentional sin no expiatory offering is due; if it was done on the Sabbath unintentionally the result may be eaten by others after the end of the Sabbath but not by him, intentionally neither by him nor by others.” They asked before {NAME}: What do you say? He said, I have only the Mishnah: “He who tithes or cooks on the Sabbath, if in error it may be eaten, if intentionally it may not be eaten”. {NAME} heard this and said, the Sabbaths have been permitted! Did not {NAME} say in the name of Rav and did not {NAME} state: “In earlier times they said, one who forgets some dish on his stove on the Sabbath, unintentionally it may be eaten, intentionally it may not be eaten. People were suspected that they left it intentionally and said, it was forgotten; they forbade it to them when it was forgotten.” And here, you say so? {NAME} said, they were suspected to leave it on, they were not suspected to cook. They imposed a fine for forgetting but not for cooking.
[Terumot 2:1.20] “ They came back to say, a dish which will improve the more it shrinks is forbidden, deteriorate the more it shrinks is permitted. What is a dish better the more it shrinks? Cabbage, peas, and chopped meat.” {NAME} said, they also considered heads of turnips and leeks as dishes better the more they shrink. What about eggs? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: My father came home and found eggs and forbade them, hot water and permitted it. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: I went with my father to Ḥammat Gader where they brought before us eggs small like ḥizrar apples and they tasted delicious like sweet bread.
[Terumot 2:1.21] It was stated: “A woman should not fill a pot with ‘assasiot and lupines and put them into the oven at the start of the Sabbath, at nightfall. If she did, they are forbidden after the end of the Sabbath until the time they could have been done.” {NAME} said: intentionally, following {NAME}; {NAME} said: unintentionally, following {NAME}. {NAME} said, that is correct, did not {NAME} say, “ He who is planting on the Sabbath, if unintentional, he may keep it, if intentional, he must tear it out. In the Sabbatical year, he must tear it out whether [planting was] unintentional or intentional. {NAME} says, it is the other way around. In the Sabbatical, if unintentional, he may keep it, if intentional, he must tear it out, on the Sabbath he must tear it out whether [planting was] unintentional or intentional because the profit of the Sabbath [is forbidden] to him.” And here, since you say that after the end of the Sabbath he has to wait until the time it could have been done, he did not gain anything from the Sabbath. What is the reason of the rabbis? People are suspected about the Sabbatical but not about the Sabbath. Another explanation: One counts Sabbaticals, one does not count Sabbaths. What is this about? If somebody planted less than thirty days before the Sabbatical and now it is the Sabbatical, if it is because of suspicion, there is no suspicion; if it is for counting, it is counted. Less than thirty days before the eighth year and now it is the eighth year, if it is because of suspicion, there is suspicion; can it be explained for counting? But you have to say because of suspicion; they fined for the unintentional because of the intentional.
[Terumot 2:2.1] MISHNAH: One does not give heave from one species for another species; if he gave, his heave is no heave. All kinds of wheat are one. All kinds of figs, dried figs, and fig cakes are one; he may give heave from one for the other. At a place where there is a Cohen one gives from the best, but where there is no Cohen he gives from what is durable. {NAME} says, one always gives from the best. One gives a small whole onion as heave but not half a large onion. {NAME} says it is not so, one rather gives half a large onion. Similarly, {NAME} said one gives onions of town people as heave for rural ones but not rural ones for those of town people because they are city-dwellers’ food.
[Terumot 2:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This is one of three obvious inferences in the Torah. ( Num . 18:12 ): “All the best of olive oil, all the best of cider and grain.” Where do we hold? Is it to conclude that one may give heave from cider for grain and from grain for cider? One must object that cider and olive oil come from two different species of tree and one may not give heave or tithe from one for the other! This means that cider and olive oil are paradigms for two species of trees, in which case one may not give heave or tithe from one for the other. Then I have to add two species of grain, two kinds of produce of which one may not give heave or tithe from one for the other.
[Terumot 2:2.3] “All kinds of wheat are one.” It is needed [since it applies] even from white wheat on brown wheat and vice-versa.
[Terumot 2:2.4] “All kinds of figs, dried figs, and fig cakes are one; he may give heave from one for the other.” It was stated: “One gives as heave fresh figs for dried figs; dried figs go by count. Dried figs for fresh figs by volume, but fresh figs for dry figs do not go by volume, nor dry figs for fresh figs by count. {NAME} said, baskets of fresh and dried figs are all one kind and one gives heave and tithes from one for the other. {NAME} said, my father used to take ten dried figs from the drying place for ninety fresh figs in the container.” {NAME} wanted to say, you consider the shriveled ones as if they had swelled and you take the baskets as they are. {NAME} and {NAME} both say that swollen shrinks but shrunk does not swell; one would have to take large baskets for fresh figs.. {NAME} said to them, that is what your teacher {NAME} thought about it.

There, we have stated: “They said to him, that will make it deficient or redundant.” Who said this to him? {NAME}! Sometimes the sour dough will be of high quality and it rises; if it were fine flour it would have shrunk but now, since the sour dough is of high quality it rose; you have to look at the risen [dough] as if it had shrunk; it looks deficient. Sometimes the sour dough is bad and it shrinks; if it were fine flour it would have risen but now, since the sour dough is bad, it shrinks; you have to look at the shrunken [dough] as if it had risen; it looks redundant. According to {NAME}, the Southerners, {NAME}, and {NAME}, all three say the same thing in case it is redundant. According to {NAME} and {NAME}, all three say the same thing in case it is deficient. Those of {NAME} cooked rice and had forgotten to put it in order. The colleagues wanted to say, he should take raw [rice] corresponding to the cooked. {NAME} said to them, I also am saying so because regularly it increases in volume.

[Terumot 3:1.1] MISHNAH: If one gives a green melon as heave and it turns out to be bitter, a water melon and it turns out rotten, it is heave and he should give heave a second time. If one gives an amphora of wine as heave and it turns out to be vinegar; if it was known that it turned into vinegar before he gave heave it is not heave, but if it turned into vinegar after he had made it heave, it is heave. In case of doubt it is heave and heave should be given a second time. Neither the first nor the second [heaves] do create dema‘ by themselves nor does one have to pay the fifth. If one of them fell into profane [food] it does not create dema‘ . If the other one fell into another place it does not create dema‘ . If both together fell into one place they create dema‘ relative to the smaller one.
[Terumot 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If one gives a green melon”, etc. We understand a water melon and it turned out rotten, but a green melon and it turned out bitter, was it not always bitter? {NAME} said, they made it doubtful whether it is food. {NAME} inquired: Is it doubtful as food in all respects, to become impure as food, that one burns it if impure, one owes a fifth for it, and one whips for it outside the walls, if one made an ‘eruv with it does he become a donkey-camel driver? [Terumot 3:2.1] MISHNAH: Partners who gave heave one after the other, {NAME} says both of their heaves are heave. One statement for wine, the other for oil. But are not wine and oil the same? Wine is frequently impure, oil is not.

Wine is frequently impure, oil is not frequently impure. {NAME} said, both are frequently impure but impurity is found with wine more often than with oil.

[Terumot 4:1.3] What is the difference between taking from itself for itself and taking from itself for another place? When it is from itself for itself, what comes into his hand is all ṭevel . If he separates from it for another place, both together come into his hand. That is difficult: If he took [produce] with the intention of taking from itself for itself, what comes into his hand is all ṭevel . If he changed his mind to use it for another place, both together come into his hand! If he took [produce] with the intention to use for another place, both together come into his hand. If he changed his mind to take from itself for itself, all that came into his hand is ṭevel ! If he gave too little, all that came into his hand is ṭevel . If he added, both together came into his hand.

[Terumot 4:8.4] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If two boxes were before him, in each one 50 seah , and one seah of heave fell into one of them but it is not known into which of them, if he wants to lift from any one of them he may do so, or he may lift half from this one and half from the other. [Terumot 4:8.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “If before him there were two boxes of fifty seah each; one seah of heave fell into one of them and it is known into which one it fell, then a second [ seah ] fell and it is not known into which it fell, one says that the second fell into the place of the first.” Why? Because one attaches the damage to the damaged. If in error he added to the known one and made [the heave] disappear, he lifts and makes it permitted. The second [ seah ] returns to be proven. It turns out that two seot may be lifted from 150 seah . “If there were two boxes of fifty seah each; one seah of heave fell into one of them and it is not known into which one it fell, then a second [ seah ] fell and it is known into which it fell, one does not say that the first fell into the place of the second.” If in error he added to one and made [the heave] disappear, he lifts and makes it permitted, but the second one remains forbidden until he would add to it in error.
[Terumot 4:8.6] If he said, what is below is heave, above all is profane, or what is below is all profane, above is heave, it depends on his opinion. Also for a miqweh it is the same: If he said, all water below is usable, above is unusable, or all water below is unusable, above is usable, it depends on his opinion.
[Terumot 4:8.7] You say, one may lift from boxes but not from storage bins. How is this? Two storage bins in two attics and a seah of heave fell into one of them, both are forbidden. If he added to one of them and made [heave] disappear in error, he lifts and makes permitted; the second bin, once he would accidentally add to it, will be permitted and does not need lifting since heave was already lifted.
[Terumot 4:8.8] It was stated: “If it is mixed, if may be lifted, unmixed it may not be lifted.” But did we not state: “{NAME} said: There came a case before {NAME} about 50 bundles of vegetables into which one [bundle] fell half of which was heave, and I said before him that it should be lifted,” in that case it is unmixed and may be lifted! We want to say that if he resents the admixture, it cannot be lifted but if he does not resent the admixture, it may be lifted. How is that? An impure green melon which fell into 100 pure ones, since he does not resent the admixture, may be lifted, but in case they were prepared for impurity, because then he resents the admixture, it may not be lifted.
[Terumot 5:1.1] MISHNAH: One seah of impure heave that fell into less than 100 [ seah ] of profane produce, or First Tithe, or Second Tithe, or dedicated produce, be it pure or impure, must be left to rot. If that seah was pure, all should be sold to Cohanim for the price of terumah except for the value of that seah . If it fell into First Tithe, heave of the tithe must be given its name; if it fell into Second Tithe or dedicated produce, they should be redeemed. If it was impure and profane, it should be eaten as crackers, or dry roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice, or split into pieces of dough so that no volume of an egg should be together. But the Sages say, it should be taken out and eaten as crackers, or dry roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice, or split into pieces of dough so that no volume of an egg should be together,. [Terumot 5:2.1] MISHNAH: One seah of impure heave which fell into 100 seah of pure heave, the House of Shammai forbid and the House of Hillel permit. The House of Shammai answered them no, if simple profane produce which is permitted to outsiders lets pure [heave] be lifted, can one infer that heave, operating under stringent rules, may let the impure be lifted? After they conceded, {NAME} said it should be lifted and burned but the Sages say, it was lost in its minority. One seah of heave which fell into one hundred, was taken out, and fell into another place: {NAME} says it creates dema‘ like certain heave but the Sages say, it creates heave only in proportion. One seah of heave which fell into less than one hundred and made it dema‘ and from the dema‘ fell into another place; {NAME} says it creates dema‘ like certain heave but the Sages say, dema‘ creates heave only in proportion; sour agent makes sour only in proportion, and drawn water invalidates a ritual bath only in proportion. One seah of heave which fell into one hundred, was taken out, and another one fell in: the latter is permitted until there will be more heave than profane. A seah of heave fell into 100 [profane] and before he managed to lift it, another one fell in: that is forbidden but {NAME} permits it.

[Terumot 5:3.1] MISHNAH: A seah of heave which fell into 100, if he milled it and it lost volume, in proportion to what the profane lost, the heave lost, and it is permitted. A seah of heave which fell into less than 100, if he milled it and it increased in volume, in proportion to the increase of the profane is the increase of heave, and it is forbidden. If it is known that the profane wheat was of better quality than the heave, it might be permitted. If a seah of heave fell into less than 100 and more profane fell into it later, if it was in error, it is permitted, if intentional, it is forbidden.
[Terumot 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: Not only if the heave lost volume but even if only the profane grain lost but the heave remains as it was, he mills and permits. It was stated: “The waste of heave does not combine with heave to forbid the profane, but the waste of profane combines with the profane to lift the heave.” {NAME} asked: Does the waste of heave combine with profane to lift the heave? Since {NAME} said, the husks of what is forbidden combine to permit, that means waste of heave combines with profane to lift the heave. {NAME} said, the shells of what is forbidden lift what is permitted. A seah of heave which fell into 100, one does not remove zewanin in it, into less than 100, one does remove the zewanin in it. Similarly, if one log of clear wine fell into 100 log of cloudy wine, one would not remove the latter’s dregs; if one log of cloudy wine fell into 100 log of clear wine, one would remove the former’s dregs.

[Terumot 6:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody eats heave in error, he pays principal and fifth; whether he eats, drinks, or anoints, whether the heave be pure or impure, he pays. [Terumot 7:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody eats heave intentionally, he pays the principal but not the fifth. His payment is profane and if the Cohen wants to forgive this, he may forgive.
[Terumot 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody eats heave intentionally,” etc. There, we have stated: “The following are flogged,” and we have stated: “These are the girls.” Here you say, he is flogged, and there you say, he pays. {NAME} said, the Mishnah is two-sided: If he was cautioned, he is flogged; if he was not cautioned, he pays. {NAME} is of the opinion that in a case where there is flogging or restitution, when he pays he is not flogged. [Terumot 7:1.3] {NAME} said, even if he was not cautioned should he not pay since when cautioned he would be flogged? A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “These are the girls for which one incurs a fine,” but if he was cautioned, will he not be flogged? {NAME} holds with {NAME} since {NAME} said, he is flogged and pays. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} learned from the calumniator. ( Deut . 22:19 ) “And they shall fine him”, money; ( Deut . 22:18 ) “they shall punish him,” flogging. But the rabbis say, [the law of] the calumniator is separate because of its novelty; one cannot learn from a novelty! Because nowhere else will a person become guilty by speech, but here he becomes guilty by speech. Since one cannot transfer this feature, one cannot transfer the rules of either payment or flogging. Did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: If he [eats] fat intentionally but is in error about the sacrifice, if he was cautioned he will be flogged and has to bring a sacrifice! {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, ( Deut . 25:2 ) “Because of his guilt.” If two possibilities are given to the court, one chooses one of them. This excludes matters in the power of Heaven.
[Terumot 7:1.4] Everybody agrees that there is no money payment in capital cases, as it is written ( Lev . 24:21 ): “The slayer of a living animal must pay for it but the slayer of a human shall be put to death.” Just as you did not make a difference between unintentional and intentional action of a slayer of an animal to force him to pay money, so you should not make a difference between unintentional and intentional action of a slayer of a human to free him [from paying]. Where do they differ? About money in a flogging case. {NAME} said, there is no money in a capital case but there is money in a flogging case, but {NAME} said, just as there is no money in a capital case so there is no money in a flogging case.
[Terumot 7:1.5] {NAME} in the name of the rabbis from there: The reason of {NAME} is “criminal, criminal.” “Criminal” is mentioned in capital cases, “criminal” is mentioned in cases of flogging. Just as for the criminal in capital cases there is no monetary fine, so for the criminal mentioned in flogging cases there is no monetary fine.
[Terumot 7:1.6] {NAME} said, one speaks about a girl, the other about an adult woman. Why should he pay and not have to be flogged? From perjured witnesses. Just as perjured witnesses pay and are not flogged, here also he pays and is not flogged. {NAME} said, the reason of {NAME}: ( Deut . 25:2 ): “The judge shall have him laid down and flogged in his presence.” It refers to one whose flogging frees him from his guilt, excluding one who is told: get up and pay.

[Terumot 8:3.9] {NAME} understands it from this occurrence: A woman loved very much doing good deeds. One time, a poor man came to her and she served him food. While he was eating, she noticed that her husband was coming. She put him [the poor] on the upper floor. She put food before her husband who ate, took a nap, and slept. A snake came and ate from what was before him; he [the poor] saw it. When he awoke and got up he wanted to continue eating what was before him. The one on the upper floor started to talk to him. That means, if he was sleeping, it is permitted. It was familiar with it. Is she not forbidden for being alone [with another man?] Since he is not suspected in one thing, he is not suspected in the other, ( Ez . 23:37 ) “For they committed adultery, blood is on their hands.”

[Terumot 8:3.23] There are three kinds of poison. Poison which sinks down, poison which floats on top, and poison remaining on the surface like a net. In the days of {NAME}, the barrels of the great assembly were uncovered. The first ones drank and did not die but the last ones died. I say that was sinking poison. Workers were on the field when the water pitcher was uncovered. The first ones drank from it and did not die but the last ones died. I say that was sinking poison. We have stated so: An uncovered amphora or a water melon with pecking marks, even if the first ones ate or drank [from it], the later ones should not eat or drink; I say that there is sinking poison. Uncovered wine from which ten persons drank is forbidden for others to (eat or) drink after them; I say that there is sinking poison.
