[Terumot 9:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody sows heave in error it should be ploughed under; if intentionally it must be kept. If it is one third ripe it must be kept, whether in error or intentionally. But flax must be ploughed under when [sown] intentionally. But it is subject to gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and peah . Israel poor and poor Cohanim collect; the Israel poor must sell to the Cohanim poor for the value of heave but the proceeds are theirs. {NAME} says, only Cohanim poor may collect; maybe they would forget and put some in their mouths. {NAME} said to him, if that is so, then only pure persons should collect. Also, it is subject to tithe and the tithe of the poor. Poor Israel and poor Cohanim may take; the poor Israel must sell to Cohanim for the value of heave but the proceeds are theirs. He who flails is praiseworthy; he who threshes, what shall he do? He hangs baskets over the neck of the animal and fills it from the same kind. In that way, he will not muzzle the animal or feed it heave.
[Terumot 9:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If someone sows heave in error it should be ploughed under;” etc. Would it not be reasonable to switch? They fined him that his field should be worthless under the heave.
[Terumot 9:1.3] {NAME} asked: Can he be trusted if he says, I did it intentionally? They said to him, if other people knew, it is not on his [word]; otherwise, the mouth which forbade is the mouth that permitted.
[Terumot 9:1.4] {NAME} asked: If he had sown vetch? If he had sown heave from outside the Land? They said to him, it is a “fence”, and there is no “fence” for a “fence”.
[Terumot 9:1.5] That means that sanctity falls on it when it is still standing. That means, if he separated before it was one third ripe it did not become holy.
[Terumot 9:1.6] “[It] must be ploughed under when [sown] intentionally.” They fined him lest he profit from the wooden parts.
[Terumot 9:1.7] {NAME} asked: If he dedicated sheaves of his [harvest] and they were switched, do even so poor Israel and poor Cohanim collect?
[Terumot 9:1.8] It was stated: “The wife of a vulgar may grind with the wife of a Fellow when she is impure. But when she is pure she should not grind, for she will hold herself more pure that the other.” Following the words of {NAME} she should not grind even when she is impure lest she forget and put some into her mouth!
[Terumot 9:1.9] So is the Mishnah: “If that is so, then only pure persons should collect.”
[Terumot 9:1.10] So is the Mishnah: “It is subject to heaves, tithes, and the tithe of the poor.”
[Terumot 9:1.11] If he planted one pound of onions of First Tithe and it became ten pounds, these are subject to tithes. Its First Tithe is given for the heave of the tithe and for what he planted. If he planted one pound of onions of Second Tithe and it became ten pounds, these are subject to tithes and he still has to redeem the second tithe from what he planted.
[Terumot 9:1.12] “ “He who flails is praiseworthy.” Praiseworthy in relation to whom? To him who threshes. “He who threshes, what shall he do?” It was stated in the name of {NAME}: “He hangs vetch for her and she likes it better than anything.” {NAME} said, this implies that if he did this with profane [grain] he does not transgress “do not muzzle.”
[Terumot 9:1.13] “ One does not transgress ‘do not muzzle’ while softening legumes or fenugreek, but it is forbidden because of the bad impression.” Some Tannaїm state: “Threshing which is permitted to you.” But some Tannaїm state: “Threshing which is not permitted to you.”
[Terumot 9:1.14] {NAME} said, our Mishnah after the lentils lost their sap; [then] the lentils shrink it that it will not give [any taste]. But if he gave it before the lentils gave their sap; it does not deal with that case. And just as you say, the lentils shrink it that it will not give, so the lentils shrink that it will not absorb. How is that? If he put a profane onion into lentils of heave, the lentils shrink it that it will not absorb. That means, if it is dry, but if it is moist it is forbidden. Onions and leeks are forbidden moist or dry, whole or cut up. If he removed the top it is as if cut up. If they are two or three they are as if cut up.
[Terumot 9:1.15] This all is if the outer skin does not impart taste. But if it does, there are Tannaïm who state: “Threshing which is permitted to you.” The Mishnah there implies also threshing which is not permitted to you, since we have stated: “He hangs baskets over the neck of the animal.”
[Terumot 9:1.16] “When it threshes,” not when it tramples on it. {NAME} says, even if it tramples on it.
[Terumot 9:1.17] {NAME} said: {NAME} asked {NAME} in order to examine him: If somebody muzzled outside and then brought [the animal] inside? He said to him ( Lev . 10:9 ): “When you come to the tent of meeting;” from when you come to the tent of meeting. {NAME} said, ( Deut . 25:4 ) “Do not muzzle an ox at his threshing;” do not thresh using a muzzled ox.
[Terumot 9:2.1] MISHNAH: The growth from heave is heave; the growth from their growth is profane. But the growths from ṭevel , First Tithe, aftergrowth of the Sabbatical, heave from outside the Land, demaʻ , and First Fruits are profane. Growths from dedicated [seeds] and Second Tithe are profane; one redeems them corresponding to the time of sowing. One hundred lagenae of heave and one profane are all permitted for produce whose seeds desappear; but for produce whose seeds do not disappear, even if there are one hundred profane and one of heave they all are forbidden. Growth from ṭevel is permitted for anything whose seeds disappear, but if the seeds do not disappear even the growth from the growth is forbidden. What is one whose seeds do not disappear? For example arum, garlic, and onions. {NAME} says, garlic is like barley.
[Terumot 9:2.2] HALAKHAH: We have stated on this: When has this been said? Anything whose seeds disappear. But in produce whose seeds do not disappear, the growth from their growth is forbidden. But ṭevel is mostly profane, First Tithe is mostly profane, aftergrowth of the Sabbatical is infrequent, heave from outside the Land is infrequent, most of dema‘ is profane, First Fruits are infrequent.
[Terumot 9:2.3] “Growths from dedicated [seeds] and Second Tithe are profane; one redeems them corresponding to the time he sowed.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He redeems the entire storage for the value of that seah . The difference between dedicated [produce] and Second Tithe: Second Tithe, whether produce whose seeds disappear or whose seeds do not disappear, is redeemed by the wholesale price; only that produce whose seeds disappear is redeemed by current prices, produce whose seeds do not disappear is redeemed following the early price. Dedicated [produce], whether produce whose seeds disappear or whose seeds do not disappear, is treated in its place and time; only that one redeems the entire storage of produce whose seeds disappear for the value of that seah , but for produce whose seeds do not disappear he has to redeem the [contents of] the entire storage.
[Terumot 9:2.4] {NAME} said: This implies that if there were 100 seah , each one lifted from 100 seah , and one profane was switched with one of them, all would be permitted.
[Terumot 9:2.5] There, {NAME} said if a seah of heave was lifted from 100 of profane produce, anything will cause it to become insignificant. And here, if he collected and some profane produce fell into it, should it not be permitted? As {NAME} said there, he mills and it is permitted, so also here. There, both kinds came into his hands. But here, only ṭevel came into his hands if he collected from one [ lagena ]. But if he collected from two, both kinds came into his hands.
[Terumot 9:2.6] How far? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is forbidden for three harvests; it is forbidden up to the fourth harvest, but the fourth is permitted. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: How far for heave? He said to him, they made the fourth harvest like the first harvest. Just as the first harvest of growth whose seeds disappear is forbidden for heave and permitted for ṭevel , so the fourth harvest of growth whose seeds do not disappear is forbidden for heave and permitted for ṭevel .
[Terumot 9:2.7] What do you have? {NAME} said, e. g., bulb plants.
[Terumot 9:2.8] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Garlic up to the size of a barley corn is a plant whose seeds disappear. Larger than that, it is a plant whose seeds do not disappear. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Garlic is like barley in every respect.
[Terumot 9:3.1] MISHNAH: He who weeds with a Non-Jew among bulb plants, even though his vegetables are ṭevel one may eat a snack from them. Saplings of heave that became impure if planted become pure not to transmit impurity but they remain forbidden to be eaten until he removes what is edible. {NAME} says, until he removes a second time.
[Terumot 9:3.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This follows {NAME}. If it follows {NAME}, even a full meal! But since {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} agrees that nevertheless he must separate tithes as a matter of practice; therefore we have to say that this follows {NAME}.
[Terumot 9:3.3] It was stated: Demay is permitted to him who weeds with a Samaritan. Therefore, not if it is certain! Why? For demay disappears when it is in the ground but the growth of forbidden produce cannot lift it.
[Terumot 9:3.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Saplings of heave that had become impure he may plant and make them heave but if they were heave from before they already were pushed aside. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Water that became impure is made to touch and may be used as water for Tabernacles but if it was water for Tabernacles from before it already is pushed aside. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Figs and grapes that had become impure one may squeeze and make them heave but if they were heave from before they already were pushed aside. {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}, one squeezes less than the volume of olives and his wine is good even for libations. They said, {NAME} disagrees. Both about leniency and restriction? If you say about leniency, this is understandable. If you say about restriction, did we not state: “Until he removes what is edible?”
[Terumot 9:3.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: so is the Mishnah, “until he removes the leaves a second time. 105”
[Terumot 10:1.1] MISHNAH: An onion which one added to lentils, if whole it is permitted, if cut up it depends on transferring taste. Any other cooked food, whether whole or cut up, depends on transferring taste. {NAME} permits in anchovies where it only serves to remove pollutants. If a mashed apple is added to dough and it soured, [the dough] is forbidden. But if barley grains fell into a cistern of water, even though they made it stink, [the water] is permitted.
[Terumot 10:1.2] HALAKHAH: “An onion which one added to lentils,” etc. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, our Mishnah [in case] after the lentils lost their sap; [then] the lentils shrink it so it will not absorb [any taste]. (As you say, lentils shrink it so it will not absorb.) Similarly, lentils shrink it so it will not give.
[Terumot 10:1.3] The Mishnah speaks about a profane onion which he put into heave lentils; but not the case of a heave onion put into profane lentils. If it is dry, but moist is forbidden. An onion, but leeks are forbidden moist or dry, entire or cut up.
[Terumot 10:1.4] If he removed the tip it is as if cut up. If there were two or three small ones, they are as if cut up. Only if the outer shell does not transmit taste. But if the outer shell transmits taste, it is forbidden.
[Terumot 10:1.5] There, we have stated: “If fish improved in value when cooked with leeks of second tithe, the increase is proportional.” {NAME} said, that Mishnah does not follow {NAME}, since we have stated: “{NAME} permits in anchovies where it only serves to remove pollutants.”
[Terumot 10:1.6] {NAME} asked: The saying of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, that all forbidden [food] is estimated as if it were onion, as if it were leeks, does this contradict {NAME}? {NAME} will agree regarding an onion of the Temple or an onion of idol worship.
[Terumot 10:1.7] “If a mashed apple is added to dough which soured, [the dough] is forbidden” It was stated: {NAME} permits it. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They disagree when it becomes sour from the juice [of the apple]. But if it becomes sour from its solid substance it is permitted. Just as {NAME} says there, its souring is not clearly souring, so he says here, its cooking is not clearly cooking.
[Terumot 10:1.8] “Everything that can be smelled is forbidden, whether it improves or spoils, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, if it improves it is forbidden, if it spoils it is permitted.” {NAME} said, in what do they disagree? If it first improved but then spoiled. But if it spoiled and later improved, even {NAME} will agree. {NAME} said, there is no difference whether it spoiled and improved or improved and spoiled, it is a disagreement. There, we have stated: “If barley grains fell into a cistern of water, even though they made it stink, the water is permitted.” What is the status of that Mishnah? {NAME} said it is a disagreement; {NAME} said it is the opinion of everybody. {NAME} said this tradition here: {NAME} said it is a disagreement; {NAME} said it is the opinion of everybody.
[Terumot 10:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody takes hot pitta bread out of the oven and deposits it on the mouth of an amphora of heave wine, {NAME} forbids and {NAME} permits. {NAME} permits in the case of wheat and forbids in the case of barley because barley absorbs. If an oven was heated with heave cumin and one baked bread in it, the bread is permitted since it absorbs not the taste of cumin but the smell of cumin.
[Terumot 10:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, they asked before {NAME}: What [are the rules] if he put it on the plug of the amphora? He said to them ( Job 36:33 ): “Its neighbor will inform about it.” What means, “its neighbor will inform about it”? {NAME} said, that which we have stated there: “An amphora full of fruits added to fluids, or one full of fluids added to fruits.” As you say there, only if the fluids touch the amphora; so here only if the loaf touches the plug. {NAME} said, from this it follows as you say there, only if the fluids touch the amphora itself; so here only if the loaf touches the plug itself. His opinion implies, even [if the pitta] is cold. {NAME} said, the problem was about a cold one. But did we not state “hot”? {NAME} said, that one should not say since the vapor absorbs it should be permitted.
[Terumot 10:2.3] Following {NAME}, water acts on fruits, [other] fluids do not act on fruits, against {NAME}! But {NAME} says, water acts on fruits and loses fluid volume, [other] fluids act on fruits and do not lose volume. {NAME} says, [other] fluids do not act on fruits at all.
[Terumot 10:2.4] And what {NAME} said, when we went to Caesarea to study Torah with the Great {NAME}, we put our flat-cake on boxes of fish sauce and we tasted there the taste of fish sauce. Is this against {NAME}? They put it into the brine. Is that not forbidden because they rob the owner? They had obtained the owner’s permission.
[Terumot 10:2.5] Wheat below and barley above; just as wheat does not absorb so the barley will not absorb. Barley below and wheat above, just as barley absorbs so wheat will absorb.

[Terumot 10:3.1] MISHNAH: Fenugreek that fell into a water cistern, for heave and second tithe if the seeds are enough to impart taste, disregarding the wood. But for the Sabbatical, kilaim in a vineyard, and dedicated seeds, if seeds and wood together impart taste. If somebody had bundles of fenugreek of kilaim from a vineyard, they should be burned. If he had bundles of fenugreek from ṭevel , he pounds them and computes how much seed this contains and separates the seeds but not the wood. If he separated, he should not say I shall pound, take the wood, and give the seeds but he gives seeds with the wood.
[Terumot 10:3.2] HALAKHAH: Does not the wood spoil repeatedly? Our Mishnah follows him who says that anything that spoils is forbidden. But even according to him who says anything that spoils is permitted, he agrees here that it is forbidden. Why? Fenugreek improves anything into which it falls.
[Terumot 10:3.3] How much is a bundle? 25 plants. {NAME} said, four to a bed.
[Terumot 10:3.4] It implies that they become ṭevel in bundles. Why not single ears? One never gathers for that. But may grains be gathered thus? One does not grow for that. But these, one gathers for this, one grows for this.

[Terumot 11:1.1] MISHNAH: One does not put a fig cake or figs into muries because he would destroy them but one may add wine to muries . One does not use olive oil as base for perfume but one may use wine as base for ὀινόμελι. One may not cook heave wine because he diminishes it; {NAME} permits it because he improves it.
[Terumot 11:1.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not put fig cake or figs into muries ”, etc. It was stated: “One puts fig cake or figs into muries in the way one uses spices on condition he not squeeze them to extract their juice. But spices are permitted, for that is what they are used for. A bundle of spices put into one pot and then transferred to another, if their taste is lost they are permitted, otherwise forbidden.”
[Terumot 11:1.3] What is the difference between this and dill? From biblical law it should not accept the impurity of foodstuffs; they said that it should accept the impurity of foodstuffs and they said that after it transferred its taste it is disregarded.

[Maasrot 1:1.1] MISHNAH: They declared a principle for tithes: Anything that is food, is guarded, and grows from the earth, is subject to tithes. They declared another principle: Anything that is food from start to end, even though it was kept to grow, is subject to tithes small or large. But anything that is not food from the start but at the end is food, is not subject to tithes until it becomes food.
[Maasrot 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “They declared a principle for tithes, etc.” It is written ( Deut . 14:22 ): “You should certainly tithe all produce of your seed.” I would say, everything is subject to tithes. The verse says, “ all produce of your seed,” this includes. Does it include garden seeds that are not eaten? It is written: “produce of your seed,” and it is written: “which your field produces every year.” How is that? Take from among them anything that is food and is guarded.
[Maasrot 1:1.3] Some want to understand it from the following: ( Deut . 14:22 ): “You should certainly tithe,” a general statement. “All grain of your seed,” a detail. For every general statement followed by a detail, the general statement only implies the detail. That means, only grain. From where legumes? The verse says ( Lev . 27:30 ): “All tithe from the earth, from seeds of the earth, from the fruit of the tree, belongs to the Eternal.” This includes seeds of garlic, cress and rocket. I might think to add the upper part of arum and the seeds of vetch, the seeds of onions, the seeds of turnips and radishes, and all other garden seeds that are not eaten; the verse says, “from seeds of the earth,” and not all seeds of the earth. ( Lev . 27:30 ) “From fruits of trees,” to include all fruits of trees. I might think to add acacia and ṣalmona pods, and carobs from dry land; the verse says, “from fruits of trees,” not all fruits of trees.
[Maasrot 1:1.4] Vegetables from where? {NAME} says, tithes of vegetables are from their words.
[Maasrot 1:1.5] {NAME} said, if somebody declared his standing grain ownerless, came back and retook possession, and illegally gave heave, that is heave. What is the difference between standing grain and ears of grain? Standing grain, if he illegally gave heave before he declared it ownerless, that is not heave. Ears, if he illegally gave heave before he declared them ownerless, that is heave. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, the same applies to a dedicated crop. The words of the rabbis disagree, since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: ( Deut . 14:29 ) “The Levite shall come, because he has neither part nor inheritance with you.” You are obliged to give him from what you have but he has not. This excludes gleanings for which your and his hands are equal. Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, peah , and abandoned property are all equal. {NAME} said, the company did ask: But dedications, where your and his hands are not equal, are treated as if your and his hands were equal. Said {NAME}, what are we talking about? If the heap was made when it was ownerless or dedicated, the Torah said ( Deut . 18:4 ) “the first of your grain”, not the ownerless, “the first of your grain”, not Temple property. But we must be talking about ears that he declared ownerless and of which he retook possession. If they were ownerless, he would be free, if dedicated, he would be obligated. If they were ownerless, he would be free, since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: ( Deut . 14:29 ) “The Levite shall come, because he has neither part nor inheritance with you.” You are obligated to give him from what you have but he has not. This excludes gleanings for which your and his hands are equal. If dedicated, he would be obligated, from the following: “If somebody dedicated standing produce and redeemed it standing, it is obligated.” What is the difference between ownerless and dedicated? Ownerless [property] is outside the power of everybody, dedicated [property] is not outside the power of the Temple treasurer. {NAME} said, it did not even go outside the power of its owners since he must say to him you redeem first.
[Maasrot 1:1.6] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody sowed an ownerless field, the crop is subject to tithes. {NAME} offers the language: Because he acquired the ownerless field and its growth.
[Maasrot 1:1.7] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Are truffles and mushrooms obligated for tithes? {NAME} said to him in the name of {NAME}, it is written ( Deut . 14:22 ): “You should certainly tithe all produce of your seed.” Anything which is sown and grows. This excludes truffles and mushrooms which grow but are not sown. {NAME} offers the language: Because the earth extrudes them.
[Maasrot 1:1.8] “Even though it was kept to grow it is subject to tithes small or large.” Does this imply that if it was not kept to grow it is not subject to tithes small or large? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: To exclude the words of {NAME} as we have stated there: “{NAME} says, flower buds of fenugreek, mustard, and white beans are subject to tithes.” {NAME} said, did {NAME} obligate them because of food? If it were so, what about their greenery? But {NAME} says, they are important as food, but the rabbis say, they are not important as food. In addition, from what we are stating: “{NAME} said, I never wanted to tell anybody go, collect flower buds of fenugreek, mustard, and white beans and cook them, to free them from tithes.”
[Maasrot 1:1.9] It was stated: “Everything that is food at the start but not at the end.” What is this? As we stated: “He who keeps the castor plant for seeds, his opinion is inoperative; for single stalks it is not inoperative.” {NAME} said, only if he collected greens. But if he did not collect greens, do we say that wood is subject to tithes?
[Maasrot 1:1.10] “But anything that is not food from the start but at the end is food, is not subject to tithes until it becomes food.” What is that? That is what we have stated next: “From when are fruits subject to tithes? Figs from the moment they start to ripen.”
[Maasrot 1:2.1] MISHNAH: From when are fruits subject to tithes? Figs from the moment they start to ripen, grapes and wild grapes when they start to produce sap. [Maasrot 1:4.1] MISHNAH: What is their threshing floor for tithes? Green melon and pumpkins from when they are cleaned; if they are not cleaned, when one makes a heap. Water melons, when they are cleaned; if they are not cleaned, when he puts them in storage. Vegetables sold in bundles, when they are bundled. When he makes no bundles, when he is finished filling the vessel; if he does not fill the vessel, when he is finished harvesting. A fig basket when he covers it; if he does not cover it when the vessel is completely filled; if he does not completely fill the vessel, when he has collected all he wants. When has this been said? When he brings it to market. But if he brings it to his house, he may eat snacks from it until he reaches his house. Dried pomegranate cells, raisins, and carob when he makes them into a pile. Onions when they are cleaned, if he does not clean when he makes them into a pile. Grain when it is in smooth piles, if he does not smoothe when he makes it into a pile. Legumes when they are sifted, if he does not sift when he makes smooth piles. Even though he made smooth piles, he may take from the broken ones, from the sides, and from what is in the chaff and eat. Wine after he cleaned it. Even after he cleaned it he may collect from the upper part of the winepress or the pipe and drink. Oil after it descended into the barrel. Even after it descended, he may take from the press, the weight, and between the beams and put it on a pizza or into a bowl but he should not add it to a hot pan or pot. {NAME} says, he may put it anywhere except into anything containing vinegar or fish sauce.
[Maasrot 1:4.2] HALAKHAH: When its peksos is removed, when its šelqoq is removed. “ When he continued removing peksos or šelqoq , it becomes ṭevel only when he finished with all he needs.” When he removed peksos or šelqoq when it was property of the Temple and redeemed it, if he made a large bundle in the field. But if he made a small bundle for the market, it became ṭevel .” {NAME} asked: The work on the field is not yet finished and you say so? But so it must be: If he made a large bundle in the field and he intends later to make it into small bundles for the market, it became ṭevel .
[Maasrot 1:4.3] “If he had one basket and he intended to fill half of it, it became ṭevel once it was half filled. If he intended to fill it completely, it does not become ṭevel until it is completely filled. If there were two and he intended to fill both of them, they do not become ṭevel until he filled both of them. When has this been said? When he brings it to market. But if be brings it to his house, he may eat snacks from it until he reaches his house.” What is the difference between him who brings to market and him who brings to his house? When he brings to his house, it depends on his intention. But if he brings to market, it does not depend on his intention but on that of his customers. Maybe he will find a customer; therefore, it becomes ṭevel immediately.
[Maasrot 1:4.4] It was stated: When he makes a pile on his roof top. {NAME} asked: Therefore, not on his field? {NAME} said, it tells you something additional: even if he makes a pile on his roof top.
[Maasrot 1:4.5] “Onions when they are cleaned,” when he removes what is clinging to them.
[Maasrot 1:4.6] “Grain when it is in smooth piles.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: When he straightens his heap. But did not {NAME} state: “When does he start to give heave from his threshing floor? When he removes the pitchfork.” Here, when he intends to smoothe, there if he did not intend to smoothe. It was stated: “He sifts part and gives heave from the sifted part for what is not sifted.” {NAME} said, for this is the way of householders to bring it into their houses. What is the reason? ( Is . 30:24 ) “The bulls and young donkeys which work the soil will eat sour mix.” If he sifted [grain] dedicated to the Temple and then redeemed it; since he was able to eat from it as a snack and now he cannot eat, it is as if he did it with the permission of the Temple and he is obligated. {NAME} objected: Did we not state, “if he took out and cleaned what was dedicated to the Temple, he is free?” {NAME} said, there it is not impossible for him not to preserve or not to cook a long time. But here it is impossible for him not to smooth it, as {NAME} said, the bulls and young donkeys, etc.

[Maasrot 2:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody passed by the market place and said: “take some figs,” one may eat without tithing. Therefore, if they brought to their houses, they have to put in order only as demay . [Maasrot 2:1.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, this is {NAME} opinion since {NAME} says a gift is not like a sale. {NAME} said, it is the opinion of everybody. [Maasrot 2:1.3] Our Mishnah [deals with] the case that most people bring to their houses but in case most people bring directly to market one has to put in order only as demay . If we were dealing with the case that most people bring to their houses, is that not what we have stated: “ ‘Take some figs and bring them home,’ one should not eat them as a snack?” Since he said, “take some figs and bring them home,” it is as if he said, “take, I am taking care of the tithes for you.” But if most people bring directly to market he is not trusted if he says to somebody, I did tithe, nor is he trusted if he says to him, I am bringing mine to my house.
[Maasrot 2:1.4] If he gave much, even if he said, take and eat, it is as if he said, take and store. If he gave him anything that usually is not eaten raw, even if he said, take and eat, it is as if he said, take and store. If [the recipient] was an important personality who does not usually eat in public, if he said, take and eat, it is as if he said, take and store. If there were two people; to one he said, take and eat; to the other he said, take and store. The one to whom he said, take and eat, is free; the one to whom he said, take and store, is obligated. {NAME} said, is that not a Mishnah (2:2): “They eat and are free but the owners of the gate or the store are obligated?” {NAME} said, it is everybody’s opinion; here for demay , there for certain.

[Maasrot 2:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody brings fruits from Galilee to Judea or if he is on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem, he may eat until he reaches his destination; the same holds for the return journey. {NAME} says, until he reaches the place where he stays for the Sabbath. [Maasrot 2:2.2] HALAKHAH: When fruits were collected not for use on the Sabbath and the Sabbath started, {NAME} said, the Sabbath makes it ṭevel , {NAME} said, the Sabbath does not make it ṭevel . {NAME} objected to {NAME}, since you say the Sabbath makes it ṭevel , did we not state: “If somebody brings fruits from Galilee to Judea or if he is on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem, he may eat until he reaches his destination; the same holds for the return journey?” We stated about this: Even if he stayed overnight, even if he stayed over the Sabbath! [Maasrot 2:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody says to another person, here take this as for twenty figs that I shall choose, he chooses and eats; for the bunch of grapes that I shall choose, he selects single grape berries and eats; for the pomegranate that I shall choose, he picks single kernels and eats; for the watermelon that I shall choose, he bites off and eats. But if he said, for these twenty figs, for these two bunches, for these two pomegranates, for these two watermelon, he eats as he is used to and he is free since he bought when it was still connected to the ground. If somebody hires a worker to slice figs; if that one told him, on condition that I may eat from the figs, he eats and is free; on condition that I and my son will eat, or that my son may eat in lieu of my wages, he may eat and is free, and his son may eat but is obligated; on condition that I may eat while cutting and after cutting, while cutting he eats and is free, after cutting he eats and is obligated since he does not eat because of the Torah. That is the principle: He who eats because of the Torah is free; if he does not eat because of the Torah he is obligated. If he was working with lĕbāsîm he should not eat benôt ševa ‘ and vice-versa. But he may hold back until he reaches the place of good ones and eat there. If somebody switches with another person so that each one eats directly, or each one cuts, or one eats and one cuts, he is obligated. {NAME} says, he who exchanges to eat is obligated, to cut is free.
[Maasrot 2:4.2] HALAKHAH: ‘ {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He plucks single berries and eats. {NAME} said, that is what my teacher did. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: If he bit off the minutest amount from a watermelon, he acquired it. {NAME} asked, does this also hold for a pomegranate?
[Maasrot 2:4.3] Why do I need “on condition”? Even without “on condition”! {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is necessary, even if he says “on condition”!
[Maasrot 2:4.4] There, we have stated: “If he worked with his hands but not with his feet, with his feet but not with his hands, even on his shoulder, he eats.” We have stated about this, with his hands he makes bundles, with his feet he creates support, even on his shoulder he carries. “{NAME} says, only if he works with his hands, feet, and body,” as in threshing where he works with his hands, feet, and body, so for anything he works with his hands, feet, and body. Threshing, just as threshing is particular in that it applies to plucked [grain], so for anything plucked. This excludes him who thins among garlic and onions, makes supports for vines, and weeds under an olive tree. Threshing, just as threshing is particular in that it applies to growth from the earth, so for anything growing from the earth. This excludes him who milks, makes cheese, or churns milk. Threshing, just as threshing is particular in that it does not apply after processing, so for anything not after processing. This excludes him who separates dates or dried figs, wine after it is fermented and olive oil when it descends into the vat. Threshing, just as threshing is particular in that it applies before the obligation of tithes, so for anything before the obligation of tithes. This excludes him who kneads dough, separates, or bakes.
[Maasrot 2:4.5] It is written ( Deut . 23:26 ): “If you come into your neighbor’s standing grain.” I could think that this means everybody; the verse says “do not swing a sickle over your neighbor’s standing grain,” he who has permission to swing a sickle, that means the laborer. {NAME} says, the verse speaks about everybody. Why does the verse say, “do not swing a sickle over your neighbor’s standing grain?” He has no right except at the time of swinging the sickle. It was stated: {NAME} says, how far was the Torah careful about robbery that it judged between a human and his neighbor about a swing of the sickle! How great is labor, since the generation of the Flood was destroyed only because of robbery, but the laborer does his work, eats, and is free of any robbery!
[Maasrot 2:4.6] It is written ( Deut . 25:4 ): “Do not muzzle an ox while he is threshing.” Is there only an ox in the cut and a human in the standing? May a human eat from the cut? If an ox which does not eat from the standing may eat from the cut, a human who may eat from the standing should a fortiori be able to eat from the cut. The verse says, “do not muzzle an ox while he is threshing.” To an ox applies “do not muzzle”; to a human “do not muzzle” does not apply. May an ox eat from the standing? If a human who does not eat from the cut may eat from the standing, an ox which may eat from the cut should a fortiori be able to eat from the standing. This means, if “do not muzzle” applies to one case, it also should apply to the other. The verse says, “do not muzzle an ox while he is threshing.” You may not muzzle him when he is threshing but you may muzzle him for what is standing on the ground.
[Maasrot 2:4.7] From here they said, “a person may renounce for himself, his adult son or daughter, or his adult male or female slave, or his wife, because they have a mind. But he may not renounce for his minor son or daughter, or his minor male or female slave, or his animal, because they have no mind.”
[Maasrot 2:4.8] He who eats by biblical decree, should he not be obligated? {NAME} said, the Torah freed him.
[Maasrot 2:4.9] There, we have stated: “When he is working on figs he should not eat grapes, on grapes he should not eat figs.” On that, we stated: If he is working on one branch, he should not eat from another branch. Also, we have stated: “When he is working with lĕbāsîm he should not eat benôt ševa‘ and vice-versa.” This is needed, even if both are on the same branch.
[Maasrot 2:4.10] It is written ( Deut . 23:25 ): “If you come into your neighbor’s vineyard.” I could think that this means everybody; the verse says: “Do not put into your own vessel,” but you may put into somebody else’s vessel. Who is this? This is the laborer. “You may eat grapes.” Do we not know that in a vineyard there is nothing to eat but grapes? Why does the verse say, you may eat grapes ? From here [it follows] that if he works fig trees he cannot eat grapes, vines he cannot eat figs. “All your soul’s desire,” all that your inclination may be. “All your soul’s desire,” anything that is free from tithes. What you eat without obligation also the laborer may eat without obligation. “All your soul’s desire,” from here that the laborer should not eat more than the value of his wages. From here did {NAME} Ḥisma deduce that the laborer should not eat more than the value of his wages, but the Sages permit it. From where that his wages are called his soul? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, it says here “his soul” and it says at another place “his soul” as it is written ( Deut . 24:15 ): “For that he carries his soul.” Just as “his soul” there means his wages, so here “his soul” means his wages. “Until you are satiated,” that he should not eat and vomit. “Until you are satiated,” that he should not peel figs or suck out grapes.
[Maasrot 2:4.11] “The laborers are permitted to dip their bread in sauce so they should eat more grapes. The employer is permitted to give them wine to drink so they should eat less grapes. The owner of a cow is permitted to starve her through the night so she should eat much while threshing. The employer is permitted to feed her bundles of straw so she should not eat much while threshing.” {NAME} said, give citrus to the animals! {NAME} fed them fig cake. {NAME} fed them carrots.
[Maasrot 2:4.12] {NAME} stated: The laborer may eat the first bunch of grapes. It was stated, the last bunch. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If he put it in the basket it is forbidden. {NAME} said, that needs to be said if he harvests and another transports. But if he harvests and transports originally he eats because of local usage. At the end he eats because of “ the laborers eat when they go from one row to the next and when they return to the winepress, and the donkey until it is unloaded.”
[Maasrot 2:4.13] It was stated: A person may use a trick so his workers will eat ten and cut one. Some Tannaïm stated: That they will cut ten and eat one. We understand “that they will eat ten and cut one.” But “that they will cut ten and eat one”? {NAME} said, that you should not say it is as if done after the end of their work, and it should be obligated.
[Maasrot 2:4.14] We understand that eating may be obligated, but should cutting be obligated? {NAME} said, this is {NAME} since {NAME} says trade induces ṭevel in produce not completely processed. {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} both said the same. As {NAME} said, heave induces ṭevel in produce not completely processed so {NAME} said trade induces ṭevel in produce not completely processed.
[Maasrot 3:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody transports figs through his courtyard to cut them into pieces, his children and companions may eat and they are free; the same holds for laborers who work for him as long as they cannot claim their meals from him. But those who can claim their meals from him may not eat. If somebody takes his workers out to the field, if they have no claim to meals from him, they eat and are free. But if they can claim meals from him they may eat single fruits from the fig tree but not from the basket or the box or the muqẓeh . If somebody hires a laborer to work with him on olive trees and said to him “on condition to be able to eat olives,” he eats one by one and if he takes them together he is obligated. To thin out onions, if he said to him “on condition to be able to eat vegetables” he snips off leaf by leaf and eats but if he takes them together he is obligated.

[Maasrot 3:1.3] According to Rav, what is the difference between himself and his children? He is forbidden because he depends on muqẓeh . His children who do not depend on muqẓeh are permitted. We understand his children, but his wife? Does she not have a claim for food against him? Following him who says, the wife’s food is not from the Torah. Following what we have stated: “The court will not determine food for a wife from Sabbatical money, but she may be given Sabbatical produce to eat at her husband’s.” Can she not be considered like a worker whose work is not worth a peruṭah ? It implies that she is not considered like a worker whose work is not worth a peruṭah . Even according to him who says, the wife’s food is not from the Torah, does she not have a claim to a dwelling? Following what we stated: “If men participate with food without the knowledge of their wives, the participation is valid. But if wives participate without the knowledge of their husbands, the participation is invalid”.
[Maasrot 3:1.4] It was stated: All that was brought from the field to town became ṭevel . Who stated this? Rebbi! As it was stated: “ If somebody brought figs from the field to eat them on his roof, Rebbi obligates, {NAME} frees.” It is as it was stated, “if somebody transports figs through his courtyard to cut them into pieces;” therefore, if it is not to cut into pieces he is obligated.

[Maasrot 3:1.9] The house of Rebbi stated: He eats normally and is free. {NAME} asked, where do we hold? If he hired him to work with him on the olives, everybody agrees that he eats normally and is free. [Maasrot 3:1.10] {NAME} asked the colleagues: What is the reason we stated here that “he is free”? They said to him, because he is eating a snack in the field and is free. It is subject to tithes since the owners still have it in mind. How far, that he could give heave from abandoned property? He cannot give heave from abandoned property! “He turns it into money’s worth and eats.”

He who pounds olives to remove the resin is free. He who squeezes olives on his skin is free but if he squeezed and put into his hand he is obligated. [Maasrot 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: Fire creates ṭevel , buying creates ṭevel , salt creates ṭevel , heave creates ṭevel , the Sabbath creates ṭevel , a secure courtyard creates ṭevel , but {NAME} said that buying and Sabbath are not biblical. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, the most reasonable of these is the secure courtyard.
[Maasrot 4:1.3] He who pickles, only if he pickles completely? He who cooks, only if he cooks thoroughly? Let us hear from the following: If one singes ears of grain in the fire they become ṭevel . Without that, would they not need to be worked over by fire? There is a difference here, because that is the end of their processing. Where has this been said? If one plucks out kernels from ears destined for dough, if it is to eat them rolled they are ṭevel , but to make a dough they are not ṭevel .
[Maasrot 4:1.4] If he pickled or cooked without the owners’ knowledge, there is a difference between {NAME} and {NAME} since these differ: If somebody made a heap [of somebody’s grain] without the latter’s knowledge, {NAME} said, it is ṭevel , {NAME} said, it is not ṭevel . {NAME} said, there it is impossible for him not to make a heap, here it is possible for him not to pickle.
[Maasrot 4:1.5] If he cooked it while it was property of the Temple, redeemed it, and brought it into a secure courtyard, what is its status? In the opinion of {NAME} it became ṭevel ; this is biblical, that is not biblical. If he brought it into a secure courtyard, redeemed and then cooked it, everybody agrees that it became ṭevel , what did he process while it was property of the Temple? If he dedicated it, cooked it, brought it into a secure courtyard, redeemed it, and cooked it again, everybody agrees that it became ṭevel . If he redeemed it and put it out to dry, what is its status? If you say that fire creates ṭevel , fire frees from ṭevel ; if you say that fire does not create ṭevel , fire does not free from ṭevel .
[Maasrot 4:1.6] {NAME} asked: If he fried in the field, what is its status? Does not the fire create ṭevel anyhow? Is it impossible not to use oil?
[Maasrot 4:1.7] {NAME} used to asked in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} said, {NAME} stated: If someone organized a meal in a circle in the field he created ṭevel . If one did not organize a meal a circle he did not create ṭevel . What organizing in a circle creates ṭevel ? Any meal in a circle with wine. If people prepared to eat in a circle but then did not?
[Maasrot 4:1.8] It was stated: “Garlic, garden cress, and mustard seed which were prepared in the field became ṭevel ” That means, ṭevel garlic with profane oil. Profane garlic with ṭevel oil?
[Maasrot 4:1.9] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: A bunch of grapes which he squeezed into a cup became ṭevel ; into a tamḥui it did not become ṭevel .
[Maasrot 4:1.10] Does not the fire induce ṭevel anyhow? Explain it if the dish was cold. “In a pot it is obligated;” {NAME} said, that refers to an empty pot. The Mishnah does not say so, but “he who prepares wine sauce for a dish is free but in a pot it is obligated for it is like a small cistern.”
[Maasrot 4:2.1] MISHNAH: If children hid figs for the Sabbath and he forgot to tithe them they may not be eaten after the Sabbath until they are tithed. One may drink from the winepress both warm or cold and is free, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} declares him obligated. But the Sages say, for warm drink he is obligated, cold he is free.
[Maasrot 4:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, if a child covered a harvesting basket for transport to the market, it became ṭevel ; in any situation in which the intent of an adult has an effect, the action of a minor has an effect. {NAME} asked: Since the intent of an adult does not have an effect until he opens on the market, the action of a minor should not have an effect until he opens on the market! The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If children hid figs for the Sabbath and he forgot to tithe them they may not be eaten after the Sabbath until they are tithed.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain if it they collected close to sundown when their action was proof of their intent!

It does not even disagree with {NAME}. [Maasrot 4:2.7] Where do we hold? If there are two vats, everybody agrees that it is forbidden. If there is only one vat, everybody agrees that it is permitted. Where do we hold? If he has a pure vat and his friend an impure one. {NAME} says, a person may return to his friend’s vat but the rabbis say, a person does not return to his friend’s vat.

[Maasrot 4:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody peels barley, he may peel one by one and eat but if he peeled and collected in his hand he is obligated. [Maasrot 4:4.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, the budding fruits of fenugreek, mustard, and white beans are subject to tithes. {NAME} says, the caper tree is subject to tithes for its budding fruits and capers. {NAME} says, only the berries are subject because they are fruit.
[Maasrot 4:4.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, if he collected two or three modii from it, it comes under the category of vegetable. If one sowed it for seeds it is tithed for the past; if he sowed it as vegetable it is tithed for the future. If he sowed it for both seeds and vegetable, or if he sowed for seeds and then wanted it as vegetable, one may tithe from its seed on vegetable and from vegetable on seeds, on condition that it was collected before the New Year; but if some of it was collected after the New Year, its seed is tithed for the past and its vegetable is tithed at the moment of its being harvested if it was one-third ripe before the New Year. But if it was only ripe one-third after the New Year, both seed and vegetable are tithed for the future.
[Maasrot 4:4.3] It was stated: “Dill sown for its seeds is tithed for seeds but not vegetable. If sown as vegetable, it is tithed for seeds and vegetable but not perianths. If sown it for periants, it is tithed for seeds, vegetable, and perianths.” But we have stated: “Only cress and wild rocket are tithed for seeds and vegetable!” So is the Mishnah: The only things sown for seeds which are tithed for seeds and vegetable are cress and wild rocket.

On the ripe fruits one applies the stringencies of both trees and vegetables. In which respect? If it is after the second year going into the third, he separates, redeems, and gives it to the poor.
[Maasrot 4:4.8] The caper bush. The House of Shammai say, it is kilaim in a vineyard but not with grains. The House of Hillel say, it is never kilaim , neither in a vineyard nor with grains. [Maasrot 5:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody lifts out plants from his own property and replants them in his own property, it is free. If somebody bought standing produce, it is free. Onions which developed roots in storage became pure and cannot become impure again. If a mudslide fell on them and they are uncovered they are as if planted in the field.

The Sages agree with {NAME} in the matter of young plants. What is the difference between wheat and young plants? For wheat, it was the end of processing; for plants it is not the end of processing. {NAME} agrees with the Sages in the matter of turnips and radishes because they spoil. Does wheat not also spoil? Wheat admits another threshing floor, these have no other threshing floor.

But did we not state “outside the Land?” There is a difference, outside the Land both for the stem and future growth; is here not a difference between the stem and future growth?

[Maasrot 5:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If a heap of onions produced roots, if one takes from them on the Sabbath he is free since he does not want their growing roots. {NAME} said to him: What is the worry of Sabbath compared to tithes? [Maasrot 5:2.1] MISHNAH: A person should not sell his produce after it reached the period of tithing to anybody not trustworthy in matters of tithe, or in the Sabbatical year to anybody suspect in matters of the Sabbatical.
