[Maaser Sheni 1:1.1] MISHNAH: One does not sell Second Tithe, one does not take it as a pledge, one does not barter it, and one does not weigh corresponding to it. One should not say to his neighbor in Jerusalem, here you have wine, give me its value in oil, but they may give free gifts to one another. One may not sell animal tithe unblemished alive, or blemished alive or slaughtered, and one may not use it for preliminarily marrying a woman. One may sell a firstling unblemished alive, blemished alive or slaughtered, and one may use it for preliminarily marrying a woman. One does not exchange Second Tithe by a blank, or by a coin not in circulation, or on money not in his possession.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not sell Second Tithe.” One does not sell it because holiness is written for it. One does not use it as a pledge because blessing is written about it. “ How may one not sell it? A person should not say to his neighbor, here you have this mina’s worth of Second Tithe, give me 50 zuz profane for it.”
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.3] Who is the Tanna of “one does not sell it”? {NAME}! But for {NAME} it should be logical that it be permitted to be sold, by an argument a minore ad majus : If it is permitted to sell heave which is forbidden to lay people, since Second Tithe is permitted to lay people, one should certainly be permitted to sell it. No, if you assert this for heave which does not need an enclosure, what can you imply for Second Tithe which needs an enclosure? First Fruits shall prove it which need an enclosure and one may sell them! No, if you assert this for First Fruits which do not implicate their monetary substitute, what can you imply for Second Heave which implicates its monetary substitute! The Sabbatical shall prove it which implicates its monetary substitute and it is permitted to sell it! {NAME} said, from this? The sale of Sabbatical produce is its redemption.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.4] {NAME} said, who is the Tanna of “one does not sell it”? {NAME}! But for {NAME} it should be logical that it be permitted to be sold, by an argument a minore ad majus : If it is permitted to sell Sabbatical produce with which one may not liquidate one’s debts, it is logical that it should be permitted to sell Second Tithe since with it one may liquidate one’s debts. We find that one may liquidate one’s debts with Second Tithe, following what we stated: “If he took from him tithe worth one tetradrachma and did not come to exchange it until it was worth two.” {NAME} said, there is a difference since from the start the value of Second Tithe was due. If he had owed before, it would be an argument. {NAME} said, a Mishnah said that it is forbidden to sell it, as we stated there: “If intentional, he married, if in error, he did not marry.” If you say that he may sell it, he should be able to use it for marriage but anything he may not sell he may not use for marriage. But did we not state: “One does not buy slaves, real estate, and unclean animals from Sabbatical money. If he bought them, he has to eat their worth.” {NAME} said, this means that it is forbidden to acquire a wife with Sabbatical money. Otherwise, what is the difference between one who acquires a wife and one who acquires a slave girl? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, everybody agrees because of these arguments. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, everybody agrees that all should need the enclosures.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.5] “ How does one not take it as a pledge? He who enters another’s house to take a pledge should not take his debtor’s Second Tithe as pledge.” It was stated: “One does not give it as a deposit and he should not give it to a grocer to receive food in its value.” If one transgressed and took as pledge, trangressed and gave as deposit? It shall be as the following: “If somebody eats his Second Tithe, whether in error or intentionally, he shall cry out to Heaven, the words of {NAME}. Rebbi says, in error he shall cry out to Heaven, intentionally the money’s worth shall be restituted. If it was money, in error he shall cry out to Heaven, intentionally the money’s worth shall be restituted, the words of {NAME}. Rebbi says, whether in error or intentionally, the money’s worth shall be restituted.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows Rebbi for money and {NAME} for produce. {NAME} said, there was a case about money and they instructed following Rebbi.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.6] Or it may follow this: “One does not plant, sink, or graft in the year preceding a Sabbatical year later than thirty days before the New Year; if he planted, grafted, or sank he has to uproot it.” If one did not uproot, what is with its yield? {NAME} [and] {NAME} were sitting in Tyre when a case came before them. {NAME} taught that the fruits should be thrown away. {NAME} said, I was not counted with them on the upper floor. They said, let us go out and study. They went out and heard {NAME} and {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not make a new restriction. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not add to an established practice.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Since it was stated, “one does not take it as a pledge nor give it as a deposit”, this means that if one transgressed and took it as a pledge, trangressed and gave as a deposit, one fines him for it.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.8] “ One does not use it to weigh coins, not even a profane tetradrachma to turn it into a tetradrachma of Second Tithe.” If he had a tetradrachma of Second Tithe whose weight was known to him, may he use it to weigh another tetradrachma of Second Tithe so that its weight should be known to him? May brothers who split [an inheritance] weigh one against the other?
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.9] We have stated: “One should not say to his neighbor in Jerusalem, here you have wine, give me its value in oil, here you have oil, give me its value in wine. But he may say to him, here you have wine since you have no wine, here you have oil since you have no oil.” Here you have wine since I have no oil, they wanted to say that this is forbidden. They found stated: “It is permitted.” Is it not forbidden because of barter? Since he cannot enforce it in a court, this is not barter. Why could he have said: Here you have wine since I have no oil? If I had oil, I would give you that also.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.10] “But they may give free gifts to one another.” Our Mishnah is {NAME} since {NAME} says a gift is not like a sale. {NAME} said, here it is everybody’s opinion, following what was stated: A person says to his neighbor [in Jerusalem]: What did you eat today? If that one says summer figs, he knows that it was firstling. Just as summer figs are sold cheaply, so firstlings are sold cheaply. If that one said manna, he knows that it was Second Tithe. Just as manna was given as a gift, so Second Tithe may be given as a gift. They objected: Everybody agrees that animal tithe cannot be sold; do you say it can be given as a gift? This also can be given as a gift. {NAME} did not say so but was following {NAME} since {NAME} said He made it one’s property. They objected: Everybody agrees that animal tithe is not one’s property; do you say it can be given as a gift? This also can be given as a gift.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.11] Therefore, once it was slaughtered, is it permitted? It was stated by the House of {NAME}: There is no difference between alive and slaughtered, unblemished and blemished. For what did we state then “live but not slaughtered?” For example, what was stated after this: “One may sell a firstling unblemished alive, blemished alive or slaughtered.”
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.12] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is said here ( Lev . 27:33 ): “It may not be redeemed.” It has been said about Cohanim‘s bans ( Lev . 27:28 ) “It may not be sold or redeemed.” Since “it may not be redeemed” for Cohanim’s bans includes sale, so “it may not be redeemed” here includes sale. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is it not written about a firstling ( Num . 18:17 ) “it should not be redeemed?” About a blemished animal. For animal tithe, the Torah made no difference between living and slaughtered, unblemished and blemished.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.13] “One may not use it for preliminarily marrying a woman.” But one may use its sinews, bones, horns, and hooves for preliminary marriage. {NAME} said, because a blessing is mentioned for it. Why can one not use its meat for preliminary marriage? {NAME} said, they learned tithe only from Cohanim’s bans. Since one may not use Cohanim’s bans for preliminary marriage, one may not use any sacrifices for preliminary marriage. Then one should not be able to use its sinews, bones, horns, and hooves for preliminary marriage. One needs what {NAME} said, because a blessing is mentioned for it.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.14] {NAME} asked: If somebody said to a woman, draw this animal tithe to you from me and be preliminarily married to me by it after slaughtering. Since it is in his hand to slaughter, is she immediately preliminarily married or only after slaughtering?
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.15] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If someone steals someone else’s animal tithe, if it still exists he returns it as is, if he ate it, he ate what he ate. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He cannot ask him to give anything; if it is worth less than a peruṭah one cannot say that he should give. {NAME} said, that is, if it was worth less than a peruṭah from the start. But if it was worth a peruṭah from the start, one tells him to pay.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.16] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Alive, but not slaughtered. There, we have stated: “If somebody betrothes a woman with his share in most holy or simple holy sacrifices, she is not betrothed.” {NAME} said, {NAME} learns all dedicated things from the firstling. Just as one may betrothe a woman with a firstling, so all sacrifices may be used to betrothe a woman. {NAME} learns all sacrifices from animal tithe. Just as one may not betrothe a woman with animal tithe, so no sacrifices may be used to betrothe a woman. The opinion of {NAME} is inverted. There, he says, alive or slaughtered. But here, he says alive, but not slaughtered. There in his own name, here in the name of {NAME}. Even if you say there and here in his own name; if he betrothes while it is still alive and with what is scheduled to fall to him. After slaughter, what is the reason of {NAME}? ( Num . 18:18 ): “Their meat shall be for you, like the breast of weaving.” And what is the reason of {NAME}? “ Shall be for you ”, even after slaughtering. How does {NAME} uphold “ shall be for you ”? He added another being that it should be eaten during two days and one night.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.17] Our Mishnah does not follow {NAME}, as it was stated: “One may exchange Second Tithe for a blank, the words of {NAME}, but the Sages forbid it.” What is {NAME} reason? ( Deut . 14:25 ) “You should bundle the money;” something which is bundled together, or which has a form and is current because of its form. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The word of {NAME} that one exchanges [Second] Tithe for a pound of silver. If he had [only] said “silver”, we would have said just as he said silver, so he said gold. If he had [only] said “silver”, we would have taught to exclude broken pots and baskets from which one could get a pound of silver.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.18] “For a blank”. Everybody agrees that one does not exchange for the coins given to the olearius . That is, the way they are used for the olearius . But the way they are used by the tremissarius one may exchange.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.19] A coin out of circulation which the government will accept, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is like a blank. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A coin of the earlier kings, if it is currently accepted because of its coinage one exchanges, otherwise one does not exchange. A revolutionary coin like that of {NAME} one does not exchange. If he had dangerous coins: such a case came before {NAME}. He said, one should carry its yield to the Dead Sea. If one had coins difficult to determine: {NAME}: One exchanges at the value given by the tremissarius . If he wants to spend the coins, he exchanges in his usual way.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.20] “ One does not exchange it for money in Babylonia nor for Babylonian money here.” Not for money from here in Babylonia if he is in Babylonia; nor for Babylonian money here when he is here. If he had Babylonian money in Babylonia but he is here, let us say that he may exchange if the road was open; but otherwise he cannot exchange and put in order here.
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.21] {NAME} said, all coins were current in Jerusalem in old times, following ( Ps . 48:3 ) “beautiful region, enjoyment of all the earth.”
[Maaser Sheni 1:1.22] I could think that if someone had money on King’s Mountain or in a castle he might exchange based on it. The verse says ( Deut . 14:25 ): “take the silver in your hand;” what means “in your hand”? In your possession! {NAME} asked, if his wallet with 1’000’000 [denars] fell into a cistern and he could spend 500’000 to get them out, is that as if 500’000 were in his possession?
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody buys a domestic animal for a well-being offering or a wild animal for meat of desire, the hide becomes profane even though it may be worth more than the meat. [If he buys] sealed wine jugs at a place where jugs usually are sold sealed, the pitcher becomes profane. The shells of walnuts and almonds become profane. Afterwine before it fermented cannot be bought with tithe money; after it fermented it may be bought with tithe money. If somebody buys a wild animal for a well-being offering or a domestic animal for meat of desire, the hide does not become profane. [If he buys] open wine jugs or sealed ones at a place where wine usually is sold from the barrel, the pitcher does not become profane. [If he buys] baskets of figs and baskets of grapes sold with the vessel, the price money of the vessel does not become profane.
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: “{NAME} Bag says ( Deut. 14:26 ): ‘You shall spend the money for anything you desire.’ It was stated: A person may buy a cow because of its hide, a sheep because of its fleece, and wine because of its pitcher.” {NAME} said, that is, if the seller was a private person. But if the seller was a professional it is as if he sold this separately and that separately. {NAME} said, the Mishnah said this: “In a place where wine jugs usually are sold sealed, the pitcher becomes profane.” {NAME} said, from this [you conclude that] just as you say there, if the seller was a professional it is as if he sold this separately and that separately, so if the buyer was a professional it is as if he bought this separately and that separately.
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.3] Palm-leaf baskets of dates, plates of dates became profane. Some Tannaїm state that boxes of dates did become, some Tannaïm state that they did not become. {NAME} said, he who said they did become, when they were pressed. He who said they did not become, [meant] when not pressed.
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.4] “Afterwine before it fermented cannot be bought with tithe money and invalidates a miqweh ; after it fermented it may be bought with tithe money and does not invalidate a miqweh .” Our Mishnah follows {NAME} as we have stated there: “If someone makes after-wine and pours in a measured amount of water, if he found the same amount he is free. {NAME} declares him obligated.” {NAME} said, sometimes in the name of {NAME}, sometimes in the name of {NAME}: Only if it fermented. {NAME} said, it is the opinion of everybody since even salt water may be bought with tithe money.
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.5] {NAME} said, the tithe [money] did not acquire. {NAME} said, first we said that if somebody bought a domestic animal for meat of desire, against his will it gets the name of well-being offering but we said nothing since {NAME} said, the tithe [money] did not acquire.
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: An animal of Second Tithe in Jerusalem following {NAME} is free from the rules of firstlings; following {NAME} it is under the rules of firstlings. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If it gave birth to a firstling, must its sacred parts be brought onto the altar? Did not its sacred parts fall under the rules of Second Tithe and you would hide it from being eaten? He said to him, if somebody bought meat as meat of desire, would not [the holiness of] Second Tithe have fallen on its sacred parts, would you not hide it from being eaten? He said to him, when it was bought, the holiness of tithe left it. {NAME} said, we were not saying so but the Torah did permit to buy from tithe money only well-being sacrifices exclusively. What is the difference between them? If it gave birth to a firstling and he dedicated it as well-being sacrifice. For him who says, the Torah did permit to buy from tithe money only well-being sacrifices exclusively, it is offered. For him who says, when it was bought, the holiness of tithe left it, and it is not offered.
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.7] {NAME} said, we teach all these words but a Mishnah supports {NAME}: “He should not bring from wheat of Second Tithe but from money of Second Tithe.” What is the difference between wheat and money? It must be that when it was bought, the holiness of tithe left it. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Why should he not bring wheat, the heave to the Cohen and the rest for the owners, why does he not bring? He said to him, think of it, if the blood is spilled does the bread not become unusable?
[Maaser Sheni 1:2.8] {NAME} said, they decreed on a blemished female because of her young. They decreed on a blemished male because of the blemished female. They said in the name of {NAME}, even an unblemished one is a decree. Earlier they said one may buy an animal for meat of desire and hide it from the altar. They turned to say, not even a wild animal, not even birds as it was stated: “Sabbatical [money] and Second Tithe [money] can be exchanged for a blemished female animal or other domestic and wild animals and birds whether alive or slaughtered, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, one exchanges only on slaughtered ones.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They decreed this that one should not raise them in herds. {NAME} stood next to {NAME} who said to him, {NAME} is still alive and you hang your rags on him! Did not {NAME} say even an unblemished one is a decree! Maybe this was said only for Sabbatical [money]? They found it stated for Sabbatical [money].
[Maaser Sheni 1:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody buys water, or salt, or produce still connected to the ground, or produce that cannot reach Jerusalem, the tithe [money] does not acquire. If somebody bought produce in error, the money should return to its place. If intentionally, he should bring them up and they should be eaten at the Place; if there is no Temple they should be left to rot. If somebody buys a domestic animal in error, the money should return to its place. If intentionally, he should bring it up and it should be eaten at the Place; if there is no Temple it should be buried in its hide. One does not buy slaves, real estate, and unclean animals from Second Tithe money. If he bought them, he has to eat their worth. One does not bring nests for men with gonorrhea, women with discharges, or women who have given birth from Second Tithe money. If he bought them, he has to eat their worth. This is the principle: If one bought anything except for eating, drinking, and rubbing from Second Tithe money, he has to eat its worth.
[Maaser Sheni 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: There, we have stated: “One does not buy slaves, real estate, or unclean animals from Sabbatical money. If he did buy them, he has to eat their worth.” And here, you say so? {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} disagreed. One said here as a sale, there as redemption. The other one said here if the seller is present, there if the seller went away. We did not know who said what. Since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, the buy is acquired, that means he is the one who said here as a sale, there as redemption.
[Maaser Sheni 1:3.3] Our Mishnah follows {NAME} but not {NAME}. {NAME} explained ( Deut. 14:26 ): “Spend the money on anything you want,” a general clause. “For cattle and sheep, wine and intoxicating drink”, detail. “And anything you want,” another general clause. General, detail, and general, you may judge only in the light of the detail. Just as the detail is explained as born from what is born from the earth, so only what is born from what is born from the earth. {NAME} explains: Just as the detail is explained as fruit, born from a fruit, or what prepares fruit, so only what is fruit, born from a fruit, or what prepares fruit. What is the difference between them? Fish, locusts, truffles, and mushrooms which may be bought with tithe money following {NAME}.
[Maaser Sheni 1:3.4] {NAME} said, a Mishnah said that one does not exchange coins for fruits far from the Place. He said that before {NAME} who praised him, before {NAME} who needled him: Did we not state, “coins in Jerusalem and produce in the countryside”? There is a difference because it was in one place. When {NAME} left, he found it stated: coins and produce in Jerusalem, coins and produce in the countryside. He said, if {NAME} had heard this, he would have needled me justly. He wanted to change his mind. {NAME} said to him, do not change your mind since {NAME} said, {NAME} and the rabbis [disagree] about demay ; therefore not for certain [produce]. Since {NAME} said, this is {NAME}, it follows that demay and certain are equal.
[Maaser Sheni 1:3.5] {NAME} was sitting and teaching his son: “if somebody wants to exchange [tithe] money for produce today, both these and those are consecrated, the words of the House of Shammai. The House of Hillel say, the money is as it was and the produce is as it was.” {NAME} passed by and told him, do not state it so but say “produce for money.” Therefore, everybody agrees that money for produce was not consecrated. But did we not state: “if there is no Temple they should be left to rot”? Explain it if he dedicated it when there was a Temple and the Temple was destroyed.
[Maaser Sheni 1:3.6] {NAME} stated: ( Deut . 14:25 ) “Turn it into money”, far from the Place you redeem it, near the Place you cannot redeem it. ( Deut . 14:26 ) “Spend the money”, near the Place you exchange it, far from the Place you do not exchange it.
[Maaser Sheni 1:3.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The buy is acquired. {NAME}: Expiation. {NAME} said, since we stated “he has to eat their worth”, that means it was sanctified. {NAME} said, since he took it up, the buy was acquired; from there on it is one buy. {NAME} said, he has to dedicate it again; he means that maybe it was sanctified when it was not sanctified.
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.1] MISHNAH: Second Tithe is to be used for eating, drinking, and anointing; to eat everything commonly eaten, to anoint with what commonly is used for anointing. One should not anoint with wine or vinegar, but with olive oil. One does not use Second Tithe oil as base for perfume, one does not buy perfumed oil with Second Tithe money, but one may make spice wine. If one adds it to honey and spices and it increases in value, the increase is proportional. If fish is cooked with Second Tithe leeks which increases its value, the increase is proportional. If a dough of Second Tithe when baked increased in value, the increase belongs to the Second. This is the principle: In all cases in which the increase is visible, the increase is proportional. In all cases in which the increase is not visible, the increase belongs to the Second.
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Second Tithe is to be used for eating,” etc. It is to be used for eating, since eating is written regarding it. For drinking, since drinking is included in eating. From where that drinking is included in eating? {NAME} understood if from the following ( Lev . 17:12 ): “Therefore, I said to the Children of Israel, no person among you may eat blood.” Where do we hold? If about congealed blood, did we not state: “Congealed blood is neither food nor drink”? So we must hold as is, and the Torah called it “eating.” But did we not state: “If he mashed the fat and sipped it, congealed the blood and ate it, he is guilty!” How does {NAME} explain? It is neither food, to accept the impurity of food, nor drink, to accept the impurity of drinks.
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.3] {NAME} changed his mind and understood it from the following ( Deut . 14:26 ): “Spend the money for anything you desire.” Where do we hold? If one adds the taste of wine to a dish, is that not tasting badly? {NAME} say, explain it with ’rznyyh and gmzvzynyyh . Anything auxiliary to food is considered food.
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.4] {NAME} understood it from the following: “[I swear] an oath that I shall not eat, when he ate and drank he is guilty on two counts.” The colleagues said, he is guilty only on one count. {NAME} said to them, we say after this, “an oath that I shall neither eat nor drink, when he ate and drank he is guilty on two counts.” It is as if somebody had two loaves before him when he said: [I swear] an oath that I shall not eat this one, and then he said: [I swear] an oath that I shall not eat that one, would he not be guilty on two counts?
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME} understood it from the following: “[I swear] an oath that I shall not eat, when he ate inedible food and drank undrinkable fluids he is free from punishment.” Therefore, if he drank drinkable fluids he is guilty. That is correct following “an oath that I shall not eat,” and in our Mishnah they teach “an oath that I shall not eat.” But for those rabbis who teach “an oath that I shall not eat and I shall not drink”?
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.6] {NAME} understood it from the following: “If he ate and drank in one forgetting he is guilty only once.” {NAME} understood it from here ( Deut . 26:14 ): “I did not eat from it in my mourning”, but I drank?
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.7] It is understandable for him who said, “[I swear] an oath that I shall not eat”, and he drank. But for him who said, “an oath that I shall not drink”, and he ate? Drinking is subsumed under eating, but eating is not subsumed under drinking.
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.8] Some want to understand it from this ( Deut . 12:17 ): “You may not eat in your gates the tithe of your grain, your cider, and your shining oil.” ‘Your cider’, that is the wine. ‘And your shining oil’ refers to anointing and the Torah called it ‘eating’. But this is not clear. If it were clear one should be whipped because of it outside the walls! {NAME} said, one is whipped outside the walls only for pure Second Tithe which entered Jerusalem and left. From where that it is not clear? From what was stated: “On the Sabbath, both anointing for pleasure and anointing not for pleasure are permitted. On the Day of Atonement, both anointing for pleasure and anointing not for pleasure are forbidden. On the Ninth of Ab and public fasts anointing for pleasure is forbidden but anointing not for pleasure is permitted.” Did we not state: “Anointing is equal to drinking for prohibition and replacement but not for punishment, on the Day of Atonement for prohibition but not for punishment”? Did we not state ( Lev . 22:15 ): “They should not desecrate,” to include him who anoints and him who drinks. {NAME} said, there is no ‘anoints’ here. {NAME} said, if there is no ‘anoints’ here then there is no ‘drinks’ for otherwise something that comes from two different prohibitions would be added together!
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.9] From where that it is clear as a positive commandment? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} ( Deut . 26:14 ): “Nor did I give from it to the dead.” Where do we hold? If it were to bring a casket and shrouds for him, that were also forbidden for a living person! If something is forbidden for the living, not so much more for the dead? What is something which is permitted for the living but prohibited for the dead? That is anointing!
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.10] What means “to eat everything commonly eaten”? “One does not oblige anybody to eat mouldy bread, or discarded leaves of vegetables, or spoiled food.” On the other hand, if somebody wants to eat raw beets or chew raw wheat kernels one does not listen to him. What means “to drink everything one commonly drinks”? “One does not oblige anybody to drink oily fish sauce, or sour fish sauce, or wine with yeast. He who has a toothache should not sip vinegar and spit out but he may sip and swallow. He may dip his food in as much [vinegar] as he wants without second thoughts. He who has a throat ache should not gargle with oil but he may load fish sauce with oil and sip it.” “One should not anoint with wine or vinegar, but with olive oil.” “If somebody has a headache or he has a scab, he may rub with oil but not with wine or vinegar.”
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.11] Perfumed wine of Second Tithe may not be used for anointing. Perfumed oil of Second Tithe may be used for anointing. What is the difference? For the latter it is customary, for the former it is not customary.
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.12] {NAME} asked: Second tithe oil that became rancid? {NAME} said, when it became rancid, its holiness burst from it. Why did he have to ask? Sabbatical [oil] even if rancid remains in its holiness.
[Maaser Sheni 2:1.13] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He who whispers puts oil on his head and whispers on condition that he use neither hand nor vessel. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: with hand or vessel. In what do they differ? Whether it is repulsive. For him who says with hand or vessel, it is repulsive. For him who says neither hand nor vessel, it is not repulsive. {NAME} said, they differ about Second Tithe. For him who says with hand or vessel, Second Tithe is forbidden. For him who says neither hand nor vessel, Second Tithe is permitted. {NAME} said, is all that is permitted on the Sabbath permitted with Second Tithe and all that is forbidden on the Sabbath forbidden with Second Tithe? Did we not state: A woman may douse her son with wine because of sweat, but this is forbidden with heave? Heave and Second Tithe are the same! How is that? For “the House of Hillel say, all should be redeemed and may be eaten outside except what became impure from derivative impurity inside”; what is the difference for derivative impurity between outside and inside; are not both rabbinic? When he brought it inside it was on condition it should not be “grabbed” by the enclosure.
[Maaser Sheni 3:5.5] {NAME} said, this means pure Second Tithe which he brought inside on condition that the enclosure not “grab” it, the enclosure does not “grab” it. {NAME} asked, it is pure and you say so? But it must be: If he transgressed and redeemed it, it is redeemed.
[Maaser Sheni 3:5.6] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If it became impure outside of Jerusalem and was brought inside, it should not leave lest one say, we saw Second Tithe entering Jerusalem and leaving? Leaving is publicized, redemption is not publicized.
[Maaser Sheni 3:5.7] {NAME} inquired before {NAME}: If it became impure by derivative impurity and he redeemed it, then it became impure in original impurity; do we say that if the original money is still there he redeems with it, otherwise he cannot redeem with it, and one is whipped neither for the first nor the second monies? {NAME} asked, is it the same for him who buys? {NAME} said, the enclosure “grabs” and the buyer “grabs”. What was said for the enclosure was said for the buyer.
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.1] MISHNAH: If what was bought with tithe money became impure, it should be redeemed. {NAME} says, it should be buried. They said to {NAME}, if original Second Tithe which became impure is redeemed, what was bought with tithe money and became impure certainly should be redeemed. He said to them, no! If you said about original Second Tithe, which can be redeemed when it is pure and far from the Place, can you say the same about what was bought with tithe money which cannot be redeemed when it is pure and far from the Place? If a deer bought with tithe money died, it should be buried in its hide. {NAME} says, it should be redeemed. If he bought it alive and slaughtered it, if it became impure it should be redeemed. {NAME} said, it should be buried. If he bought it slaughtered and it became impure, he treats it following the rules of produce. If somebody lends flasks for Second Tithe, even if he closed the top with clay, tithe did not acquire it. If he filled them without saying anything, before he closed the top with clay, tithe did not acquire it; after he closed the top with clay, tithe acquired it. Before he closed the top with clay, one may lift by 101, after he closed the top with clay any one sanctifies. Before he closed the top with clay, he gives heave from one for all, after he closed the top with clay he has to give heave from each single one. The House of Shammai say, he opens and pours into a vat, but the House of Hillel say, he opens and does not have to pour. Where has this been said? At a place where usually one sells sealed, but at a place where usually one sells open, the flask did not become profane. However, if he is meticulous to sell by volume, the flask did become profane. {NAME} said, also if somebody says to another person, I am selling to you this amphora except its flask, the flask became profane.
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.2] HALAKHAH: What is the reason of {NAME}? The first money, not second money. Only because they objected to him by an argument de minore ad majus , he answered in terms of an argument de minore ad majus.
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They treated deer like dedications for the upkeep of the Temple to require standing and appraisal.
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.4] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does an unclean animal need standing and appraisal? He said to him, if {NAME} had said in the name of {NAME} that a pure wild animal does not need standing and appraisal, an unclean animal would not need it. {NAME} said, we have stated thus ( Lev . 27:21 ): “If an unclean animal, he should redeem it as appraised.” Just as an unclean animal is particular in that it is the same at the time of its redemption as at the time of its dedication, so I am adding the dead animal which is the same at the time of its redemption as at the time of its dedication, and I exclude the one for which he said, this is dedicated, and then it died, which is not the same at the time of its redemption as at the time of its dedication. {NAME} said, a Mishnah said so: “One commits larceny with a donkey and its milk.” Is not milk comparable to its being dead? With all that needs redemption one can commit larceny. You cannot explain it as giving the rules of dead [animals] since we stated “a donkey”. {NAME} said before {NAME}, explain it following {NAME} since {NAME} said, dedications for the upkeep of the Temple do not need standing and appraisal. He said to him, if it is following {NAME}, why a donkey and not any animal?
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.5] {NAME} said, the Torah said, spend it in the Holy Place and assemble it in the countryside. Just as in the holy place the flask is profane, in the contryside can the flask be grasped by tithe?
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, so is the Mishnah: “If before he sealed the top with clay he gave it its name, tithe did not acquire it; if after he sealed the top with clay he gave it its name, tithe acquired it. If before he sealed the top with clay he gave it its name, one may lift by 101, if after he sealed the top with clay any one sanctifies. If before he sealed the top with clay he gave it its name, he gives heave from one for all, if after he sealed the top with clay he gave it its name, he has to give heave from each single one.”
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.7] When has this been said? For wine; but for oil, whether he closed the top with clay or did not close the top with clay, tithe did not acquire it. Whether he closed the top with clay or did not close the top with clay, he may lift by 101. Whether he closed the top with clay or did not close the top with clay, he gives heave from one for all.
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.8] {NAME} said, it is difficult about the House of Shammai! What is the difference between this and five sacks on a threshing floor? For five [separate] sacks on one threshing floor, can one not give heave and tithe from one for the other?
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.9] {NAME} said, it refers back to the first [part]. {NAME} said, to the second.
[Maaser Sheni 3:6.10] “If he said, a quartarius of profane is in this barrel, the barrel is profane.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah says so, “{NAME} said, also if somebody says to another person, I am selling to you this amphora except its flask, the flask became profane.”
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody transports Second Tithe produce from a place of high prices to one of low prices or vice versa, he redeems at the level of his place. If he brings produce from the threshing floor to town or from the wine-press to town, the excess value belongs to the Second but the expense is on him. One redeems Second Tithe following the low rate at which the grocer buys, not at which he sells; the one at which the banker gives small coins, not at which he assembles large coins. One does not redeem Second Tithe en bloc ; if the price is known it is redeemed by the information of one person, if the price is not known by the information of three, as e. g., wine getting sour, fruit rotting, or coins rusting.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody transports Second Tithe produce,” etc. {NAME} said, they said only “if somebody transports”; therefore originally it is forbidden. This is about Second Tithe produce, but for produce which is ṭevel for Second Tithe it is originally permitted, following this: Rebbi had produce here and in Batanaia; he fixed the tithes of here there and redeemed them according to the going price there.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.3] It was stated: Whether it was expensive and became cheap or cheap and became more expensive. We understand “expensive and became cheap”. “Cheap and became more expensive”? There is a difference because he could use a trick and free it from the fifth.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.4] It was stated: “{NAME} the small-town man said, when has this been said? For certain [produce], but for demay whether it was expensive and became cheap or was cheap and became expensive, he may sell it cheaply.” Why? Is it because it always may be sold cheaply or because it may not be returned to its place? What is the difference? If later it rose in price again at its place. If you say, because it may not be returned to its place, did it not increase in value? If you say, because it always may be sold cheaply also in this case it can be sold cheaply. Like this: {NAME} was in Rome and he saw them redeem there Nicolaos dates from here at the price here. He said, who taught them? Ḥilfai the small-town man taught them.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.5] It was stated: A person may earn up to a šeqel , a person may earn up to a quarter. How is this done? A denar here is worth 2000, but in Arbel 2000 and a laqan . He wants to give 50 myriads and brings it up, here by 2000 and in Arbel by 2[000] and laqan .
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.6] It was stated: One does not redeem Second Tithe as Second Tithe but as profane. {NAME} asked: Think of it, if everybody knew that it was Second? Even so. It was stated: One redeems Second Tithe only from its own kind. Otherwise, what would we say? One might redeem wheat for barley, barley for wheat; even fine wheat for coarse wheat, coarse wheat for fine wheat.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.7] {NAME} said: Rebbi took early ripe green melons for the government and fixed their Second Tithe in each peduncle. He considered them as if cut. {NAME} asked, they were whole and you say cut? {NAME} said, that is correct! If two people were partners in a green melon, one having one part and the other two, can he say, take your part and I shall take mine? But for the two together it is sold more dearly; here also together it is sold more dearly. Like this: {NAME} commanded those Southerners who were disregarding it. {NAME} lifted them and before him cut them into little pieces. He said to him, is that worth anything? So far, some things are cut into little pieces and they are no good, other things are cut into little pieces and are good.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.8] {NAME} said, one redeems Second Tithe only up to thirty six times [the coin’s] worth. And {NAME} said, one who exchanges should not exchange for half a peruṭah so he should not be like one who exchanges for a blank; it must be worth a peruṭah .
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.9] {NAME} said, Kama came before {NAME} and {NAME}. They said to him, go and pay according to those Tannaїm: “One redeems Second Tithe when it is cheap, not when it is expensive; at the rate at which the grocer buys, not at which he sells; the one at which the banker gives small coins, not at which he assembles large coins.” So far for large quantities, what about small ones? Even so, at the rate at which the grocer buys, not at which he sells; the one at which the banker gives small coins, not at which he assembles large coins.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.10] {NAME} showed a basket of palm leaves to a carpenter and redeemed following his opinion. {NAME} showed a quarter [ qab ] wheat to a wheat dealer and redeemed following his opinion. {NAME} showed produce to {NAME} who asked him, by their true value? He answered, yes. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, one does not redeem Second Tithe following the opinion of imbeciles. {NAME} showed produce to a grits-maker who asked him, by their true value? He said to him, so said {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, one does not redeem following the opinion of imbeciles. {NAME} said, how much a person wants [to pay] on a clear noontime at the summer solstice when the bath master takes up his bunches, he brings coins and redeems. {NAME} said, as much as a person wants Friday afternoon from women braiders when he passes by, he brings coins and redeems. {NAME} said, {NAME} left it lying until it got moldy and redeemed it immediately after the Sabbath.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.11] {NAME} had oil which he brought down to Acco. {NAME} said to him, if your oil there at the parapet is still there, it is your time that you should redeem it for [there] it is not worth six minas.
[Maaser Sheni 4:1.12] {NAME} said, one redeems Second Tithe by the offers of three buyers, even if one of them is a Gentile, even if one of them is an owner. {NAME} asked: Not two Gentiles, not two owners; also not one Gentile and one owner? No, it was said separately.
[Maaser Sheni 4:2.1] MISHNAH: If the owner says a tetradrachma and another says a tetradrachma, the owner is preferred since he adds a fifth. The owner says a tetradrachma and someone else says a tetradrachma and an as, the one who offers a tetradrachma and an as is preferred since he adds to the capital. He who redeems his own Second Tithe adds a fifth, whether it is his own or was given to him as a gift.
[Maaser Sheni 4:2.2] HALAKHAH: Is not the fifth of this more than the addition of that one? {NAME} said, there is a difference that he can circumvent and free it from the fifth.
[Maaser Sheni 4:2.3] “A tetradrachma and an as is preferred since he adds to the capital”. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not add a fifth for any Second Tithe which itself is not worth a peruṭa. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not add a fifth for any Second Tithe for which the fifth is not worth a peruṭa . {NAME} objected: Did we not state “there are five peruṭot ”, should one not state “six” according to {NAME}, “Second Tithe which is worth a peruṭa !” And “seven” according to {NAME}, “the fifth of Second Tithe worth a peruṭa .” In addition, from what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Real estate cannot be acquired for less than a peruṭa . In addition, from the following: If the value of Second Tithe is not known, it is enough that one say: it and its fifth shall be exchanged for this tetradrachma. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: this baraita deals with a tetradrachma of tithe money where it is impossible that it not contain some profane.
[Maaser Sheni 4:2.4] {NAME} said, if somebody redeemed dedications for more than their worth, [the Temple] grabs everything. If somebody redeemed Second Tithe for more than its worth, it does not grab everything. What is the difference between dedications and Second Tithe? {NAME} said, because a person usually adds to his dedications. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If the person was checked and he said, that was not what I intended? He said to him, when he will be checked.
[Maaser Sheni 4:2.5] {NAME} asked, that is following him who said that it is not his property. But for him who says that it is his property, what is the difference between dedications and Second Tithe? {NAME} said, the reason has already been explained, because a person usually adds to his dedications.
[Maaser Sheni 4:2.6] {NAME} said, if somebody redeemed his dedication without adding a fifth, it is redeemed. If somebody redeemed his Second Tithe without adding a fifth, it is not redeemed. What is the difference between dedications and Second Tithe? {NAME} said, dedications have claimants, Second Tithe has no claimants. {NAME} asked, that is following him who said, it is not his property. But for him, who says it is his property, what is the difference between dedications and Second Tithe? {NAME} said, the reason has already been explained, dedications have claimants, Second Tithe has no claimants.
[Maaser Sheni 4:2.7] “He who redeems his own Second Tithe adds a fifth, whether it was his own or was given to him as a gift.” Our Mishnah is {NAME} since {NAME} says, a gift is not like a sale. {NAME} said, it is the opinion of everybody, explain it with produce still ṭevel for tithes. But did we not state: “He who redeems his own fourth-year tree adds a fifth, whether it is his own or was given to him as a gift”? Can you say that this speaks about produce still ṭevel for (Second Tithe? We have stated) “fourth-year tree!” That means the fourth-year tree itself! So here, you will end up saying “tithe”.
[Maaser Sheni 4:3.1] MISHNAH: One may circumvent about Second Tithe. How is this? A person may say to his neighbor, his adult son or daughter, his Hebrew male or female slave: Take these coins and redeem this tithe for yourself. But he should not say so to his minor son or daughter or his Canaanite male or female slave because their hand is like his hand. If somebody was standing on the threshing floor and no coins were in his hand, he says to a friend, this produce is given to you as a gift; then he goes on and says to him, it is redeemed by coins in the house.
[Maaser Sheni 4:3.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} disagree. One said, why may one circumvent it? For “blessing” is written about it. The other said, why is it redeemed at a cheap rate? For “blessing” is written about it.
[Maaser Sheni 4:3.3] How do we hold? If he said to him, go and redeem for me, he is his agent; go and redeem for yourself, they are the other’s property. But we have to hold that he said to him, redeem for me of your property, or redeem for yourself of my property. We have stated thus: “Redeem for me of your property, or redeem for yourself of my property, he does not add a fifth.” {NAME} said, for any tithe, where neither it nor its redemption money is his, he does not have to add a fifth. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, the reason of {NAME} ( Lev. 27:31 ): “If a person goes to redeem of his own tithes, his own fifth he shall add to it;” both it and its redemption money must be his.
[Maaser Sheni 4:3.4] How do we hold? If she is an adult, she acquired [her freedom] by the signs [of puberty]; if she is a minor, may a minor acquire? {NAME} said before {NAME}, explain it following him who said, a minor may give heave. He said to him, even following him who said, a minor may give heave, may a minor acquire? Following the opinion of the rabbis there it is acceptable since there, they say in the name of {NAME}: One to whom one gives a nut and he throws it away, a pebble and he keeps it, what is found in his hand is as if found on a garbage heap; a nut and he keeps it, a pebble and he throws it away, what is robbed from him is robbed because of communal peace; a nut or a pebble he takes, hides them, and produces them later, what is robbed from him is total robbery. He can acquire for himself but not for others. {NAME} said, just as he can acquire for himself so he can acquire for others. Everybody agrees that his gift is not a gift since it is written ( Ex. 22:6 ): “If a man give.” The gift of a man is a gift, but the gift of a minor is no gift, the words of the Sages. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, robbing from him is not total robbery unless he grew two pubic hairs. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, that is, to recover from him by a law suit, but to have to bring a sacrifice for [a false] oath only if he grew two pubic hairs. But following the rabbis here, {NAME} asked that even for himself he should not be able to acquire since it is written ( Ex . 22:6 ): “To his neighbor”, until he be like his neighbor. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} explained it by the method of small children. As we have stated there: “For school children, their buying is buying and their selling selling, for movables.” But did we not state: “He cannot make them acquire through his minor son or daughter or his Canaanite male or female slave, because their hand is like his hand.” {NAME} say, here a minor with knowledge, there a minor without knowledge.
[Maaser Sheni 4:3.5] There, we have stated: “If somebody borrows a cow and [the lender] sent her to him through his son, his slave, or his agent.” Does this not say that a slave is able to transfer rights from his master to another person? {NAME} said, explain it about a Hebrew slave. {NAME} said, you can even explain it for a Canaanite slave, it he told him, open the gate for her and she will go by herself, as we have stated: If he led her, drew her, called her and she followed him, he is required to pay as a borrower.
[Maaser Sheni 4:3.6] {NAME} understood it from here: “But he cannot make them acquire through his minor son or daughter or his Canaanite male or female slave, because their hand is not like his hand.” Does this not imply that a slave is not able to transfer rights from his master to another person? Explain it following {NAME} since {NAME} makes the hand of the slave the hand of his master. But did we not state “his wife”? {NAME} holds that the hand of the wife is the hand of her husband! {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, explain it following the Tanna who stated: “His wife cannot redeem Second Tithe for him. {NAME} says in the name of {NAME}, his wife can redeem Second Tithe for him.” For that Tanna, {NAME} makes the hand of the slave the hand of his master but not the hand of the wife the hand of her husband!
[Maaser Sheni 4:3.7] In earlier times, they were doing so with coins. They took them and fled. They instituted that one does it with produce. Nevertheless, they took and ate it. They instituted that he should give him the right to one in ten on the ground.

[Maaser Sheni 4:4.1] MISHNAH: If [somebody] took from [another] tithe in the value of a tetradrachma and did not pay to redeem it until it became worth two, he gives him a tetradrachma, gains a tetradrachma, and the Second Tithe is his. If [somebody] took from [another] tithe in the value of two and did not pay to redeem it until it became worth one tetradrachma, he gives him a tetradrachma of profane money and a tetradrachma of his Second Tithe [money]. [Maaser Sheni 4:4.5] {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}, when do they differ? If they thought about other things but if they still were on the same subject, it is a bill of divorce.

[Maaser Sheni 4:5.1] MISHNAH: He who put aside an as and ate for half of its worth, then went to another place where it is worth a dupondius , has to eat another as for it. [Maaser Sheni 4:6.1] MISHNAH: All found coins are profane, even gold denars with silver or change. If one found with them a potsherd reading “tithe”, it is tithe. If one finds a vessel inscribed ק it means sacrifice, מ tithe, ד demay , ט ṭevel , ת heave since in times of danger one wrote ת for heave. {NAME} says, all these are people’s names. {NAME} said, even if he found an amphora full of produce and inscribed “heave”, these are profane since I say last year it was full of tithe produce but he emptied it. [Maaser Sheni 4:6.2] HALAKHAH: That you should not say, since people do not usually act like this, one has to say “profane”.
[Maaser Sheni 4:6.3] It was stated: Alef dalet ḥet ṭet mem tav heave. א “first”. ד “ demay ”. ח “its fat”. ט “its best”. ר “beginning”. ת “heave”. ב ש “Second Tithe”, פ ש “Second Tithe”. י מ “tithe”. Tithe for the City, redemption. Those on the name of Yose, on the name of Simeon, to take it up to eat in Jerusalem, are profane; I am saying contributions they arranged among themselves.
[Maaser Sheni 4:6.4] So far new ones. Old ones, I am saying yesterday it was full of heave but he empties it, like this: {NAME} and {NAME} were partners in a cellar of (wine)-barrels. [Maaser Sheni 4:6.5] Were these exchanged? We have stated there: “If he prepared black ones and found white, white and found black, two and found three, they are forbidden, three and found two they are permitted.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, this is Rebbi’s, as we have stated: “Two hundred and he found a talent, a talent was taken, the word of Rebbi, but the Sages say, it is profane.” He turned around and said, this is everybody’s opinion since pigeon chicks usually start to fly. But did not {NAME} state: The same rule applies to pigeon chicks and to eggs. Therefore, it is Rebbi’s. There, he put it there and he found, here, his father put it there, did his father find it? {NAME} said before {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} taught according to Rebbi for Second Tithe.

[Maaser Sheni 5:3.1] MISHNAH: How does one redeem a fourth-year orchard? He puts a tetradrachma before three [experts] and asks, how much does a person redeem for himself for a tetradrachma when all expense is on him? Then he puts down the money and says, all that is collected under this is exchanged for this money; so and so many baskets per tetradrachma. In a Sabbatical, he redeems its full value. If all of it was abandoned, he has only the cost of harvesting. He who redeems a fourth-year orchard adds its fifth whether it was his or was given to him as a gift. The removal was on the day before the first day of Passover in the fourth and the seventh year [of the Sabbatical cycle.] What is the removal? One gives heave and heave of the tithe to its recipients, First Tithe to its recipients, tithe of the poor to its recipients. Second Tithe and First Fruits are removed on the spot. {NAME} says, first fruits one gives to the Cohanim like heave. A cooked dish the House of Shammai say one has to remove, but the House of Hillel say it is as if removed. He who had produce in this time and the year of removal came, the House of Shammai say he has to exchange it for money; the House of Hillel say, either money or produce.
[Maaser Sheni 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: To redeem for a tetradrachma [means] he buys for himself for a tetradrachma. “He has only the cost of harvesting” including the cost of removing the pedicles. {NAME} took three wholesalers [?] and redeemed on their word.
[Maaser Sheni 5:3.3] It is written ( Deut . 14:28 ): “At the end of three years you shall take out all tithe of your produce, in that year, and deposit it in your gates.” I could think that once in a Sabbatical cycle you have to distribute the tithes including the tithe of the poor. The verse says “at the end of three years,” once in three years and not once in seven; i. e., in the third and the seventh, twice in a Sabbatical cycle. Do I understand at New Year’s Day, that on New Year’s Day you have to distribute the tithes including the tithe of the poor? The verse says “at the end of three years.” “At the end” means at its conclusion you remove, you do not remove on New Year’s Day. If it is at the end of the year, I could understand that at the beginning of the fourth you have to remove the tithes including the tithe of the poor; the verse says ( Deut . 26:12 ): “If you have finished tithing [all tithe of] 78 your produce,” when you have tithed all your fruits. If it is when you have tithed all your fruits, could I understand even on Ḥanukkah? It says here, “at the end of;” it says further ( Deut . 26:12 ): “At the end of seven years, on the fixed time of the Sabbatical year, on the festival of booths.” Since “at the end” there means at a fixed time, so here also at a fixed time. Since there “at the end” means the holiday of booths, does it here also mean the holiday of booths? The verse says “if you have finished tithing all tithe of your produce,” when you have finished tithing all of your fruits? On Passover of the fourth year.
[Maaser Sheni 5:3.4] ( Deut . 14:28 ) “In that year” your are obliged to remove it but you are not obliged to remove it in any other year. “In that year” you are obliged to remove; you are not required to remove vegetables which grew between New Year’s Day and Passover. [Challah 1:3.1] MISHNAH: The following are subject to ḥallah but exempt from tithes: Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and peah , as well as abandoned property, First tithe of which its heave had been taken, second tithe and dedicated [grain] that were redeemed, the excess of the ‘ omer , and grain not yet one-third ripe. {NAME} said, grain not yet one-third ripe is exempt from ḥallah . The following are obligated for tithes but free from ḥallah : Rice, millet, poppies, sesame, legumes, and less than five quarter [ qab ] of grain. Bismarcks, honey cakes, roasted cakes, pancakes, and dema ‘ are free from ḥallah.

[Challah 1:3.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This is one of three well-explained verses in the Torah ( Deut . 14:27 ): “The Levite shall come, for he has neither part nor inheritance with you.” You must give him from what you have but he has not. [Challah 1:3.9] “And grain not yet one-third ripe”. What is the rabbis’ reason? “Bread” is mentioned in connection with Passover and “bread” is mentioned in connection with ḥallah. “Bread” mentioned in connection with Passover includes all that may be maẓẓah or leavened, [therefore] also “bread” mentioned in connection with ḥallah includes all that may be maẓẓah or leavened. What is {NAME} reasoning? ( Num . 15:20 ) “You shall lift it like heave from the threshing floor.” Since heave from the threshing floor is only from produce at least one-third ripe, that also is only from produce at least one-third ripe. Does {NAME} not have “bread, bread”? It was found stated in the name of {NAME}: It is not subject to ḥallah and nobody can use it to fulfill his duty on Passover.

One one-third ripe and one of grasses are two both for ḥallah and tithes.

[Challah 2:2.2] HALAKHAH: How is this? [Challah 2:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody gives ḥallah from flour it is not ḥallah and will be robbery in the hand if the Cohen. The dough itself is subject to ḥallah ; the flour, if it is a full measure, is obligated for ḥallah and forbidden to laymen, the words of {NAME}. They said to him, it happened that a layman rabbi grabbed it. He said to them, he destroyed himself and put others in order. Five quarters of coarse flour are obligated for ḥallah ; including hulls and bran it is obligated by five quarters. If the bran was sifted out and later returned, it is free. The rate of ḥallah is one in 24. If somebody makes dough for himself or his son’s wedding feast, one in 24. A baker who makes to sell on the market, and also a woman who makes to sell on the market, one in 48. If the dough became impure by error or accident, one in 48. If it became impure intentionally, one in 24 so the sinner should not be rewarded. {NAME} says, it may be taken from pure for impure. How is this? With pure and impure dough, he takes the amount needed for ḥallah from dough from which ḥallah was not yet taken and gives less than the volume of an egg in the middle so he should take from the earmarked. But the Sages forbid it.
[Challah 2:3.2] HALAKHAH: “He said to them, he destroyed himself and put others in order.” He destroyed himself by eating and exposed himself to punishment; he put others in order since they eat and unload [their sin] on him. Some Tannaїm state: He put himself in order and destroyed others. He put himself in order since anyhow he ate. But he destroyed others since they tend to say it is free when it is obligated.

[Challah 2:3.5] It was stated: “{NAME} said, why did they say the private person one in 24 but the baker one in 48? Because the baker is generous with his dough but the private person is stingy with his dough. But the Sages say, not because of this category or reason, but ( Num. 18:28 ): “You shall give from it the Eternal’s heave to Aharon the priest;” they should be given to the priest in his status as priest. The baker makes a large dough with enough to make a gift to the Cohen but the private person makes a small dough that would not be enough to make a gift to the Cohen.
[Challah 2:3.6] But did we not state: “If somebody makes dough for himself or his son’s wedding feast, one in 24?” Not to make a distinction in doughs of a private person. But did we not state: “And also a woman who makes to sell on the market, one in 48?” When she makes it for herself, she is stingy with her dough; when she makes to sell on the market she is generous with her dough. Rebbi said, the Mishnah speaks about one used to give one in 48, but about one who is used to give one in 24, we should state that “the sinner should not be rewarded”.
[Challah 2:3.7] Does the house not combine them together? Things which one objects to being mixed the house will not combine together; if one would not object to their being mixed the house will combine them. The status of impure and pure dough is that one is assumed to object to their being mixed.
[Challah 2:3.8] If the dough is ḥallah . But a dough of secondary [impurity] has no [invalidating] touch for ṭevel .

If somebody pickled olives in impurity and wants to give heave in purity, he brings a funnel whose opening is less than [the width of] an egg, fills it with olives and puts it on top of the amphora; it turns out that he gives heave from what is earmarked.” Why does it have to be less than [the width of] an egg? Are these not single pieces? It is only that not many olives should become impure. “They said to him, the only food fluids called fluid are wine and olive oil.” How is that? One beam for two pits or two beams for one pit. [One understands one beam for two pits, but two beams for one pit?] Is it not that if it is partially impure it is totally impure? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it, if he had intended to process it in one batch, and he changed his mind to make it in two batches. {NAME} said, this applies if it became impure after he siphoned off [the froth] and [the seeds] formed lumps. [Challah 3:1.1] MISHNAH: One may eat a snack from the dough until it was rolled if wheat dough or compacted if barley dough. [Challah 3:1.8] {NAME} said, the statement is reasonable on Sabbath eves; since everybody is bringing, it is as if she separated from what is obligated for what is obligated. But on weekdays, while they instituted that ḥallah may be taken from pure for impure and not earmarked, but from what is exempt for what is obligated? {NAME} said, it is only reasonable on weekdays, but on Sabbath eve she would have to say “all, including the impure.” Why? Since [some dough] is taken before all is one mass, when all is made into one mass the former is sanctified as ḥallah . If one would say “except the impure contained in it”, it would turn out that impure ṭevel is mixed with ḥallah . If you say “all, including the impure,” it is impure profane; therefore, it is better to give from what is exempt for what is obligated to avoid impure ṭevel mixed with ḥallah . {NAME} said, does it not become dedicated retroactively? Since it is dedicated retroactively, it is as if one gave from what is obligated for the obligated.
[Challah 3:1.9] Why “on condition that there not be five quarters of flour?” Rebbi said, the Mishnah was formulated before they instructed the Cohanot.
[Challah 3:2.1] MISHNAH: If the dough became dema‘ before it was rolled it is exempt since dema‘ is exempt from ḥallah . If a doubt of impurity arose before it was rolled it may be processed in impurity but after it was rolled it must be processed in purity.
[Challah 3:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said: The elder {NAME} stated two contradictory things, that ṭevel is counted with profane food and that every doubt invalidates heave and disables profane food from becoming heave. This is difficult; if ṭevel is counted with profane food why should it disable profane food from becoming heave? That means, it is counted with heave! {NAME} said, we also have stated both statements! [Challah 3:3.1] MISHNAH: If she dedicated her dough and redeemed it before she rolled [the dough], it is obligated. If she dedicated before she rolled, the Temple treasurer had it rolled, and then she redeemed it, it is exempt since at the moment of obligation it was exempt. Parallel to this, if somebody dedicated his produce before the time of tithes and redeemed it, it is obligated; after the time of tithes, it is obligated. But if he dedicated it before it was fully processed, the treasurer finished it, and then the owner redeemed it, it is free since at the time of obligation it was free.

[Challah 3:4.1] MISHNAH: A dough which a Non-Jew gave to a Jew to make is exempt from ḥallah . If he gave it as a gift before it was rolled it is obligated, after it was rolled it is free. If somebody makes dough in partnership with a Non-Jew, it is exempt from ḥallah if the Jew’s part is less than the measure. If a proselyte became Jewish while he had dough, if it was made before he became Jewish it is exempt, after he became Jewish it is obligated. In case of doubt it is obligated but one does not owe a fifth because of it. {NAME} says, all goes after forming a crust in the oven.
[Challah 3:4.2] HALAKHAH: What is the difference between this and a dough of annona? Is the latter not obligated for ḥallah ? There it is in the possession of the Jew until the Gentile decides to take it. But here it depends on the latter’s opinion.

If the inventory belongs to a Gentile and Jewish workers make it, it is not subject to ḥallah.” {NAME} said, we also have stated this: “A dough which a Non-Jew gave to a Jew to make is exempt from ḥallah .”

[Challah 3:4.6] {NAME} said: Two Gentiles who made a dough of two qabim, split, and then each of them added to it, are obligated because they never were potentially obligated but exempted. Two Jews who made a dough of two qabim, split, and then each of them added to it, are exempted because they were potentially obligated but exempted. A Jew and a Gentile made a dough of two qabim, split, and then each of them added to it, it is clear that the Jew’s part is obligated. What is the status of the Gentile’s part? Would the Gentile’s part not be obligated only because of the Jew? The Jew’s part is obligated, the Gentile’s is exempt.
[Challah 3:4.7] “{NAME} says, all goes after forming a crust in the oven.” The colleagues in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} agrees with the Sages that rolling the dough of a layman makes it ṭevel. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} agrees with the Sages that rolling the dough by the Temple exempts. {NAME} said, the words of {NAME} imply that shaping the heap by the Temple does not exempt. {NAME} said, that of {NAME} disagrees with that of {NAME}. He who says rolling exempts, [says] shaping exempts. And he who says rolling does not exempt, [says] shaping does not exempt. But according to the rabbis, rolling exempts in the Gentile’s power, shaping does not exempt in the Gentile’s power. It is difficult for the rabbis, if rolling exempts in the Gentile’s power, why does shaping not exempt in the Gentile’s power? There is a difference since it is written ( Lev. 27:30 ): “All tithe from the Land from the seed of the Land.” But is here not written ( Num. 15:19 ): “From the bread of the Land?” From the bread, not all bread. {NAME} said, from the rabbis we infer that {NAME}’s statement does not disagree with {NAME}. Just as the rabbis say, rolling exempts in the Gentile’s power but shaping does not exempt in the Gentile’s power, so {NAME} says, rolling does not exempt in the Gentile’s power and shaping does not exempt in the power of the Temple.
[Challah 3:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody makes dough from wheat and rice, if it has the taste of flour it is subject to ḥallah and a person may satisfy his Passover obligation with it. If it does not have the taste of flour it is not subject to ḥallah and a person may not satisfy his Passover obligation with it. If somebody takes sourdough from a dough from which no ḥallah was taken and adds it to dough from which ḥallah was taken, if he can provide for it from another place he should take in proportion; otherwise he should take ḥallah for everything. Similarly, if harvested olives were mixed with plucked olives, or harvested grapes with gleanings, if he can provide for it from another place he should take in proportion; otherwise he should take heave and heave of the tithe for everything but the remainder of tithe and Second Tithe in proportion. If somebody takes sourdough from grain dough and adds it to a rice dough, if it imparts the taste of grain it is subject to ḥallah, otherwise it is exempt from ḥallah. Then why did they say ṭevel is forbidden in the most minute amount? In its own kind; not in its own kind if it can be tasted.

[Challah 3:5.12] “If somebody harvested a pumpkin to use to give now and in the future, any time he harvests he has to come and note, up to here is heave, up to here is heave, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} says, he harvests and computes as is usual for him.” They wanted to say, for him who says up to here is heave, up to here is heave, ṭevel disappears in a plurality but for him who says he harvests and computes as is usual for him, ṭevel does not disappear in a plurality. {NAME} said, between them is the duty to immediately give it to the tribe.
[Challah 3:5.13] “ If he had to give heave for four or five amphoras in a cistern, he lifts the first one to the mouth of the cistern and says, this is heave. [Challah 4:1.1] MISHNAH: If two women each made a qab and they touched one another, even if they are of the same kind they are exempt. But if both belong to the same woman and are of the same kind they are obligated, different kinds are exempt. What is the same kind? Wheat combines with nothing but spelt. Barley combines with everything except wheat. {NAME} said, the remaining kinds all combine with one another.
[Challah 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Two women who each made,” etc. {NAME} said, usually for women, one does not mind, two do mind. They gave to one woman who minds the status of two women, to two women who do not mind the status of one woman. If she does not mind, why does she make it at two different places? {NAME} said, because she has not enough space to knead. The word of {NAME} implies that if she had enough space to knead but she makes it in two portions, she does mind. Clean and coarse [flour], she does mind. {NAME} said, they gave two different habits the status of two women. {NAME} asked, even if they come to agree?
[Challah 4:1.3] Certain situations are connections for ḥallah but not for a ṭevul yom , [others] for a ṭevul yom but not for ḥallah . But one is not obligated for ḥallah ; as {NAME} said, if somebody makes dough in order to distribute it, the dough is exempt from ḥallah .

[Challah 4:2.1] MISHNAH: Two qabim and a qab of rice or heave between them do not combine. If a thing of which ḥallah was taken is between them, they do combine since already they are subject to ḥallah . If a qab of new grain and one of old bit one another, {NAME} says one should take from the middle but the Sages prohibit this. If somebody takes ḥallah from a single qab, {NAME} declares it to be ḥallah but the Sages say, it is not ḥallah. If ḥallah of two qabim was taken separately, when he then combinrd them together into one dough, {NAME} exempts but the Sages obligate; it turns out that the severity becomes a leniency.
[Challah 4:2.2] HALAKHAH: Should one have stated “rice” but not “heave”? If we had stated “rice” but not “heave”, we would have said that rice does not combine because it is not of that kind, but heave, which is of that kind, should combine. It is necessary to state “heave.” If we had stated “heave” but not “rice”, we would have said that heave does not combine because it is not dragged in, but rice, which is dragged in, should combine. It is necessary to state “rice” and “heave”.

Dedicated [dough] may be redeemed and made obligated, ḥallah cannot be redeemed and made obligated.
[Challah 4:2.4] “Half a qab of wheat, half a qab of barley, half a qab of spelt: He takes from spelt for what is needed. Since it is far from it, it does not look similar.

[Orlah 1:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody plants for fences or building logs he is exempt from ‘ orlah . {NAME} says, even if he says the inner part is for food, the outer part for a fence, the inner part is obligated but the outer is exempt.
[Orlah 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody plants for fences or building logs he is exempt,” etc. It is written ( Lev . 19:23 ): “If you plant any food tree.” What is for food is obligated; for fencing, logs, or wood it is exempt. Then the one for food even if he intended it as a fence should be obligated! The verse says, “a food tree.”
[Orlah 1:1.3] {NAME} understood the text from its beginning, from the meaning of what is said ( Lev . 19:23 ): “Three years it shall be like ‘foreskin’ for you, it may not be eaten.” Does this not imply that the verse speaks about a fruit tree? Why does the verse say: “If you plant any food tree”? What is for food is obligated, for fencing, logs, or wood is exempt. {NAME} understood the text from its end, from the meaning of what is said ( Lev . 19:25 ): “In the fifth year you shall eat its fruit, to increase its yield for you.” Does this not imply that the verse speaks about a fruit tree? Why does the verse say: “If you plant any food tree”? What is for food is obligated; for fencing, logs, or wood it is exempt.
[Orlah 1:1.4] It was stated: “{NAME} says, when has this been said? If he planted for fencing, logs, or wood, kinds appropriate for that use. If he planted an inappropriate kind it is obligated.” {NAME} said it correctly, what is the reason of the rabbis? {NAME} said, if he changed the way it is usually planted: For wood tightly together, for logs cutting off branches, for a fence the location of the fence proves it.
[Orlah 1:1.5] It was stated in the name of {NAME}: “All trees can be exempted by intention except olive and fig trees.” {NAME} is consistent since he says all trees are futile except olive and fig trees.
[Orlah 1:1.6] It was stated in the name of {NAME}: The only kinds admitting an intention of exemption are three: [buckthorn], sycamore, and caper bush. Are these obligated for tithes? This is a dispute between {NAME} and {NAME}. They differed: If somebody kept his fruit trees for wood, {NAME} said he is obligated, {NAME} said he is exempted. {NAME} said he is obligated, from the following: ( Deut . 14:29 ) “The Levite shall come, because he has neither part nor inheritance with you.” You are obliged to give him from what you have but he has not. This excludes abandoned property for which your and his hands are equal. Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, peah , and abandoned property are all equal.
[Orlah 1:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said he is exempt, from the following: “If coriander is sown for its seed, its greenery is free.” Coriander is different since it has a different threshing floor. But he says from the following: “If someone keeps cabbage for seeds, his opinion is inoperative; for single stalks it is not inoperative.” {NAME} said, only if he collected greens. But if he did not collect greens, do we say that wood is subject to tithes?
[Orlah 1:1.8] Are these forbidden because of robbery? Is wood not also forbidden because of robbery? What is his problem? For example, mulberry trees having no solidity.

He who says “permitted from what is permitted”, in the case of dema ‘ by pure heave.

[Orlah 2:1.20] It is obvious that his knowledge permits it. Does the knowledge of a third person permit it? How is this possible? He is not aware of it; another person is aware of it.
[Orlah 2:1.21] Does uncertain knowledge permit like certain knowledge? How is this? If there were two boxes before him, one containing 200 and one less than 200. If one seah of heave fell into one of them but it is not known into which one it fell and then [another seah ] fell into the second. It was measured and found to be 202. If you say uncertain knowledge permits like certain knowledge, it can be lifted, but if you say uncertain knowledge does not permit like certain knowledge, it cannot be lifted. If there was one chest and there is a doubt whether it contains 200 or not; if one seah of heave fell into [some box] but it is not known whether it fell into that box or not, and then a second time something [forbidden] fell into [the box in question]: If you say uncertain knowledge permits like certain knowledge, it can be lifted, but if you say uncertain knowledge does not permit like certain knowledge, it cannot be lifted.

[Orlah 2:3.1] MISHNAH: Anything which sours, or spices, or creates dema‘ from heave, or is ‘orlah , or vineyard kilaim , is forbidden. The House of Shammai say, also it transmits impurity, but the House of Hillel say nothing transmits impurity unless it has at least the volume of a chicken egg. Dositheos from Kefar Etma was a student of Shammai. He said, I asked Shammai the Elder and he said, nothing transmits impurity unless it has the volume of a chicken egg. And why did they say, anything which sours, or spices, or creates dema‘ , is restrictive if a kind is mixed with its own kind, but permissive or restrictive if a kind is mixed with another kind. How is that? Sourdough from wheat which fell into wheat dough and is enough to make the latter sour, whether it would qualify to be lifted by one in 100 or not qualify to be lifted by one in 100, is forbidden. If it does not qualify to be lifted by one in 100 it is forbidden whether it is enough to make the latter sour or not enough to make sour. Permissive or restrictive if a kind is mixed with another kind, how is that? If groats were cooked with lentils, if they can be tasted, whether they would qualify to be lifted by one in 100 or not qualify to be lifted by one in 100, are forbidden. If they cannot be tasted, whether they would qualify to be lifted by one in 100 or not qualify to be lifted by one in 100, are permitted.
