[Orlah 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Cloth dyed with ‘ orlah shells should be burned,” etc. It is written ( Lev . 19:23 ): “You shall treat its foreskin with its fruit as foreskin.” Some Tannaїm state: What is close to the fruit. Some Tannaїm state: What envelopes the fruit. He who says what envelopes the fruit, understands shells and pits. He who says what is close to the fruit understands shells but not pits. From where pits? You must finally conclude that “its fruit” means “What touches its fruit.” Some want to understand it from here: “You shall treat its foreskin with its fruit as foreskin,” anything which envelopes its fruit or its fruit envelopes it.

[Bikkurim 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Some people bring First Fruits and make the declaration, some bring and do not make the declaration, and some do not bring. The following do not bring: He who plants in his own but provines into a private or a public plot; and so he who provines from a private or a public plot into his own. If someone plants in his own and provines into his own but a private or public road is in the middle he cannot bring; {NAME} says he brings.
[Bikkurim 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Some people bring First Fruits and make the declaration,” etc. He who plants in his own but provines into a private or a public plot cannot bring even from the old tree; he who provines from a private or a public plot into his own cannot bring even from the new tree. That means that just as the new lives off the old, so the old lives off the new.
[Bikkurim 1:1.3] {NAME} said, in all cases they judged by the rules of robbers. {NAME} said, that is what the Mishnah means: “Why can he not bring? Because it was said ( Deut . 26:2 ): ‘the beginning of the First Fruits of your land.’ ”
[Bikkurim 1:1.4] It was stated: If he provined with permission, he brings and makes the declaration. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Only if the permission was permanent, not temporary. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even temporary. The force of {NAME} comes from the following: “If somebody digs a cistern, a ditch, or a cave, he may cut down as he works and the wood is his.” Is the wood not as if temporary? What does {NAME} do with this? Roots always regrow; since roots do regrow it is as if permanent. {NAME} said, the statement of {NAME} supports my father, as {NAME} said in all cases they judged by the rules of robbers. In our case, if he gave permission to provine even temporarily, the proviner is not a robber.
[Bikkurim 1:1.5] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is the Mishnah Rebbi’s since Rebbi said, all roots live off one another? He said to him, it is everybody’s opinion. Here, the Torah said ( Deut . 26:2 ): “the beginning of the First Fruits of your land,” that all growth be from your land.
[Bikkurim 1:1.6] In the opinion of {NAME}, what is the difference between him who plants on his own property and provines into a private person’s and him who plants on his own and provines into his own and a private road is in between? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, when he provined through a gourd or a pipe. If he provined through a gourd or a pipe he should bring and make the declaration! Even according to the rabbis he should bring and make the declaration! {NAME} said, {NAME} had a problem. If somebody sells a path to another person, does he sell him the place where the foot treads or does he sell him down to the abyss? If you say, he sold the place where the foot treads, he brings and makes the declaration. If you say, he sold down to the abyss, he should not bring at all. Because of the doubt he brings but does not make the declaration. For the rabbis it is obvious that he sold down to the abyss. Where do they differ? When he sells a path to another person. But if he sold him a field and reserved a path for himself, everybody agrees that he reserved for himself down to the abyss.
[Bikkurim 1:1.7] In the opinion of {NAME}, what is the difference between him who plants on his own property and provines into the public domain and him who plants on his own and provines into his own and a public road is in between? {NAME} said, {NAME} holds with {NAME}, as we have stated there: “One may not make a cavity under the public domain, cisterns, ditches, or caverns. {NAME} permits it if a truck loaded with stones can pass over it.” As {NAME} said there, under the public domain, it is his, so {NAME} said here, under the public domain, it is his. {NAME} asked, if it follows {NAME}, he should bring and make the declaration. {NAME} said, {NAME} thought that {NAME} permits to do that and it remains his permanent property, but {NAME} permits to do that but anybody quick to acquire does acquire it.
[Bikkurim 1:2.1] MISHNAH: Why can he not bring? Because it was said ( Deut . 26:2 ): “You shall bring the beginning of the First Fruits of your land,” that all the growth should be from your land. For the same reason sharecroppers, tenant farmers, sicarii , and robbers cannot bring, since it is said: “The beginning of the First Fruits of your land.”
[Bikkurim 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: So far if he robbed the real estate. If he robbed a vine and planted it, does he not owe money? But the rabbis have a problem: do commandments follow the rules of Temple sacrifices or not? If you say they are like Temple sacrifices he may not bring; if you say they are not like Temple sacrifices he may bring. Everybody agrees that from a worshipped tree which was damaged one cannot bring logs for the altar fire. {NAME} asked, may he take a lulav from it? Do commandments follow the rules of Temple sacrifices or not? If you say they are like Temple sacrifices he may not take; if you say they are not like Temple sacrifices he may take. It is obvious that he may take a lulav from it and commandments are not like Temple sacrifices. May he bring First Fruits? According to {NAME} who compares them to country sacred food he may bring; according to the rabbis who compare them to Temple sacrifices he may not bring.
[Bikkurim 1:2.3] So far about a robbery when the owners did not give up hope. Even about a robbery when the owners did give up hope? They thought to say that we can hear it from the following: “This applies to heave and tithe but not to First Fruits.” For what is this needed? Not for a robbery when the owners did not give up hope, but for a robbery when the owners did give up hope? Even for heave he did not do anything, as we stated: “A strongman, a thief, or a robber, as long as the owners pursue them, their heave is no heave, his tithes no tithes, and their dedications no dedications. If the owners do not pursue them, their heave is heave, their tithes are tithes, and their dedications dedications.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Neither of them can give heave. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even if the owners declare heave, it is no heave. {NAME} said, so far we deal with a robbery when the owners did not give up hope. Then why did we state: “This applies to heave and tithe but not to First Fruits”? It is possible for fruits to be usable without First Fruits. It is impossible for fruits to be usable without heave and tithes! But a robbery when the owners did give up hope remains a question.
[Bikkurim 1:3.1] MISHNAH: One does not bring First Fruits except from the Seven Kinds, nor from mountain dates, nor from valley fruits, nor from oil olives which are not best quality. One may not bring First Fruits before Pentecost. The people from Hyena Mountain brought their First Fruits before Pentecost but they did not accept from them because of the verse in the Torah: ( Ex. 23:16 ) “The pilgrimage holiday of harvest, the First Fruits of your work from sowing the field.”
[Bikkurim 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not bring First Fruits”, etc. If it were written ( Deut . 26:2 ): “You shall take the First Fruits of your land”, I would have said that all kinds should be obligated for First Fruits. The verse says,“ from the First Fruits”, not all firsts. If “from the first” and not all first, then you have only wheat and barley. The verse says “fruits of your land”; this is inclusive. Does it include everything? Here “your land” has been said; at another place “the Land of wheat and barley” has been said. Since “land” mentioned there deals with the Seven Kinds, so also “land” mentioned in this verse must deal with the Seven Kinds.
[Bikkurim 1:3.3] “Oil olives” that is agory . {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, that is the Avaritic. Why is it called agory ? Because it stores its oil inside. Do all other olives lose their oil? {NAME} said, all other olives will leach their oil if rains fall on them but this one stores its oil inside.
[Bikkurim 1:3.4] “And honey”. This refers to dates. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is written ( 2Chr . 31:5 ) “When the thing expanded, the Children of Israel did increase the first gifts of grain, cider, oil, and honey.” Is honey subject to tithes? But this refers to dates which are subject to tithes.

[Bikkurim 2:1.1] MISHNAH: For heave and First Fruits one incurs the penalty of death or a fine of a fifth; they are forbidden to lay persons, are Cohen’s property, may be lifted by one in 100, need washing of the hands and sundown. This applies to heave and First Fruits but not to tithe.
[Bikkurim 2:1.2] HALAKHAH: “For heave and First Fruits,” etc. It is written ( Num. 18.8 ): “Behold, I gave to you the watch over My heaves.” Two heaves, heave and First Fruits. Extirpation is already written in regard to sacrifices.
[Bikkurim 2:1.3] Should sacrifices be subject to death and extirpation? Can somebody die and die again? As we have stated: “If somebody dies at age 50, he dies of extirpation. At 52, the death of the prophet {NAME}. At 60, it is the death written in the Torah. At 70, a death of love. At 80, death of old age. After that, a life of suffering.”
[Bikkurim 2:1.4] From where do you understand that if somebody dies at age 50, he dies of extirpation? And it is written ( Num. 4:20 ): “They should not come to look, when the holies are wrapped, and die.” And it is written ( Num. 8:25 ): “At age 50, he should retire from the work force.” {NAME}, understood it from here ( Ps. 90:10 ): “The days of our lives here are 70 years.” Subtract from these 20 years during which the Heavenly Court does neither punish not extirpate, and you will find that one who dies at up to 50 years dies in extirpation.

[Bikkurim 2:2.7] So is the Mishnah: “They forbid in Jerusalem in the most minute amount; {NAME} permits. Their growth in Jerusalem is forbidden to be eaten and {NAME} permits. Also by the unauthorized or by animals does {NAME} permit.” Do not the rabbis agree with him since he asked them: Do you not agree that if they are permitted for the unauthorized, they are permitted as animal feed? Does one need walls for unauthorized eating or for feeding animals? Just as one does not need walls for unauthorized eating, one does not need walls for feeding animals! The rabbis say, they made Jerusalem something which has no possibility to become permitted. Anything which has no possibility to become permitted prohibits in the most minute amounts; similarly, Jerusalem prohibits in the most minute amounts.
[Bikkurim 2:2.8] About what do {NAME} and the rabbis disagree? About growth. But in mixtures even {NAME} agrees. What is the difference between growth and mixtures? In mixtures all exists. In growth it already has disappeared. Where {NAME} agrees with the rabbis is in mixtures of tithe, but mixtures of First Fruits are treated like growth. And so did {NAME} say: “First fruits do not forbid their mixtures or growths to be eaten in Jerusalem.” What is the difference between tithe and First Fruits? Tithe cannot be lifted, First Fruits can be lifted. {NAME} agrees that the seah lifted for another seah needs walls and needs use. But the rabbis say, all need walls and need use.
[Bikkurim 2:2.9] {NAME} went to a place and said, I am {NAME} here. There came an old man to ask him. He said, “the growth from heave is heave; the growth from their growth is profane. But the growths from ṭevel, second tithe and first tithe, aftergrowth of the Sabbatical, heave from outside the Land, dema‘ , and First Fruits are profane.” There, you say their growth is permitted, why do you say here, their growth is forbidden? He said to him, where do we say their growth is permitted? For things whose seeds disappear. Where do we say their growth is forbidden? For things whose seeds do not disappear. He said to him, but did we not state: “What is one whose seeds do not disappear? For example arum, garlic, and onions.” Are arum, garlic, and onions obligated for First Fruits? He said, the {NAME} from here went away as you say. He asked {NAME} who told him, for tithe everything was classified as things whose seeds do not disappear.

About pure second tithe which entered Jerusalem and left. Also from the following which {NAME} stated. [Bikkurim 2:3.1] MISHNAH: Some rules apply to heave and tithe but not to First Fruits since heave and tithe forbid on the threshing floor, they have a fixed measure, apply to all produce, are due whether the Temple exists or not, and apply to sharecroppers, tenant farmers, sicarii , and robbers. They apply to heave and tithe but not to First Fruits. Some rules apply to First Fruits but not to heave and tithe. For First Fruits acquire [hallowed status] when connected to the ground, a person may dedicate his entire field as First Fruits, he is responsible for them, and they need a sacrifice, song, weaving, and staying overnight. Heave of the tithe is similar to First Fruits in two ways and to heave in two ways. It may be taken from pure for impure and from produce not earmarked, like First Fruits. It forbids the threshing floor and it has a measure like heave.
[Bikkurim 2:3.2] HALAKHAH: It is true that heave makes the threshing floor forbidden? Explain it if he gave it early, from ears, as {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: First Tithe given early, from ears, is free from [the obligation of] great heave.
[Bikkurim 2:3.3] “They acquire [hallowed status] connected to the ground”, as it is written ( Num . 18:13 ): “The First Fruits of anything on their land.”
[Bikkurim 2:3.4] “A person may dedicate his entire field as First Fruits.” As it is written ( Ez . 44:30 ): “The first of all First Fruits of everything.”
[Bikkurim 2:3.5] “One is responsible for them,” for it is written ( Ex . 23:19 ): “The beginning of the First Fruits of your land.”
[Bikkurim 2:3.6] “And they need a sacrifice.” Joy is mentioned here and elsewhere. Since joy there means a well-being sacrifice, so joy mentioned here means a well-being sacrifice.
[Bikkurim 2:3.7] “And song.” Song is mentioned here and it is said there ( Ez . 33:32 ): “Behold, you are for them like an erotic song.”
[Bikkurim 2:3.8] “And weaving,” as it is written ( Deut . 26:4 ) “The Cohen shall take the basket from your hand and deposit it,” to add that First Fruits require weaving, following {NAME}.
[Bikkurim 2:3.9] “And staying overnight.” As it is written ( Deut . 16:7 ): “In the morning, you may leave and return to your tent.” That is, all your leaving should only be in the morning. {NAME} said, that is only said if there is no sacrifice accompanying them. But if there is an accompanying sacrifice, without [that Mishnah] he needs to stay overnight because of the sacrifice.

[Bikkurim 2:4.1] MISHNAH: A citron follows the rules of trees in three aspects and those of vegetables in one. [Bikkurim 2:4.2] HALAKHAH: If a tree why a vegetable, if a vegetable, why a tree? [Bikkurim 2:4.3] {NAME} said, in the remaining years of the Sabbatical cycle you treat it as a vegetable but in the Sabbatical as a tree. How is that? From the fifth to the sixth, sixth. From the sixth to the Sabbatical, sixth. [Bikkurim 2:6.1] MISHNAH: The koy in some ways follows the rules for wild animals and in some those for domestic animals, in some the rules for both domestic and wild animals, and in some those for neither domestic nor wild animals. How does it follow the rules of wild animals? Its blood must be covered like the blood of a wild animal; one does not slaughter it on a holiday but if it was slaughtered one does not cover its blood. Its fat can become impure in the impurity of a carcass like a wild animal; that impurity is one of doubt. One may not use it to redeem the first-born of a donkey. How does it follow the rules of domestic animals? Its fat is forbidden like the fat of domestic animals, but one is not punished for it by extirpation. It cannot be bought with tithe money to be eaten in Jerusalem and it is subject to the foreleg, the lower jaw, and the first stomach [to be given to a Cohen]. {NAME} frees since the claimant has to bring proof. How does it differ from both a wild and a domestic animal? It is forbidden as kilaim with wild animals and domestic animals. If somebody writes his wild or domestic animals over to his son, he did not include the koy . If somebody said, I am a nazir if that is neither a wild nor a domestic animal, he is a nazir . In all other ways it is like wild and domestic animals; it needs slaughtering by cutting its throat like both, and as carcass it is impure like both.
[Bikkurim 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: What is a koy? {NAME} said, [the offspring of] a he-goat which mated with a hind or of a stag which mated with a she-goat. But the rabbis say it is a separate kind and the Sages could not determine its nature.
[Bikkurim 2:6.3] If it was redeemd by a koy, one has to redeem again by a sheep. Therefore, if one of them died, the claimant has to bring proof.

[Bikkurim 3:5.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, one adorns First Fruits [with anything] except from the Seven Kinds. {NAME} says, one adorns First Fruits only with the Seven Kinds. {NAME} says, there are three components of First Fruits. First Fruits, additions to First Fruits, and adornments of First Fruits. Additions to First Fruits are of the same kind, adornments of First Fruits are not of the same kind. Additions to First Fruits are eaten in purity and exempt from the rules of demay , adornments of First Fruits are subject to the rules of demay .

About what do they differ? About outside the Land. For him who says, one adorns First Fruits [with anything] except from the Seven Kinds, one may adorn First Fruits with produce from outside the Land. For him who says, one adorns First Fruits only with the Seven Kinds, one may not adorn First Fruits with produce from outside the Land..

He may use them to buy slaves, real estate, and impure animals. A creditor can take them for his claim and a woman for her ketuba, like a Torah scroll. [Shabbat 1:1.1] MISHNAH: There are two [kinds] of transport on the Sabbath which are four [kinds] inside, and two [kinds] which are four [kinds] outside. How is this? The poor man stands outside and the householder inside. If the poor man stretched out his hand inside and delivered into the householder’s hand or took something from it and brought it outside, the poor man is liable but the householder is not liable. If the householder stretched out his hand outside and delivered into the poor man’s hand or took something from it and brought it inside, the householder is liable but the poor man is not liable. If the poor man stretched out his hand inside and the householder took from it or gave into it and he then took it out, neither is liable. If the householder stretched out his hand outside and the poor man took from it or gave into it and he then took it in, neither is liable.
[Shabbat 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Export on the Sabbath,” etc. What means “two which are four”? Two which are four for liability and two which are four for no liability, or four for liability and four for no liability? Let us hear from the following: “There are two kinds of oaths which are four kinds.” {NAME} said, there all are about liability, but here we come to state both liability and no liability. This implies four of liability and four of no liability. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says so, “there are two kinds of oaths which are four kinds,” not because of liability? And similarly, “there are two kinds of export on the Sabbath which are four kinds,” because there is liability. But was it not stated, “the doors of the Temple hall were two which are four?” Can you say, liability and no liability? Should we state twelve cases of no liability? We only come to state cases of no liability which correspond to cases of liability. {NAME} said, what is this “no liability” which we stated here? Permitted! {NAME} said, the poor man and the rich man are one but the Sages counted them as two. Bringing in or taking out are one but the Sages counted them as two. Taking out on the Sabbath does not include bringing in; if one exports from one domain to the other, does this not include the one who imports? Let us hear from the following, as {NAME} said in the name if {NAME}: Somebody who brings in half the size of a dried fig and takes out half the size of a dried fig is liable. And from where that taking out is called work? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} understood it from the following: Moses ordered, they made a public proclamation in the camp as follows, men or women should no longer do work to contribute to the sanctuary. The people refrained from taking objects out from their houses to give them to the collectors. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: You even understand bringing in from this. Just as the people refrained from taking objects out of their houses to give to the collectors so the collectors did not accept anything from them to bring into the office. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} understood everything from the following: do not bring out any load from your houses on the Sabbath day, and perform no work.
[Shabbat 1:1.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If one brought in half a dried fig and took out half a dried fig he is liable. What {NAME} said does not follow {NAME}, as it was stated: “If one took out half a dried fig and again took out half a dried fig during one period of oblivion, he is liable; during different periods of oblivion he is not liable. {NAME} said, during one period of oblivion and one domain he is liable, during one period of oblivion and two domains or during two periods of oblivion and one domain he is not liable.” We find this difficult. If two different transorts do not combine following {NAME}, a fortiori also not bringing in and taking out? Therefore what {NAME} said could not follow {NAME}.
[Shabbat 1:1.4] {NAME} said, not only if two doors open to two public roads but even if they open to the same public road will {NAME} agree, for {NAME} compares domains to periods of oblivion in matters of liability. Just as {NAME} compares domains to periods of oblivion in absence of liability so {NAME} compares domains to periods of oblivion in matters of liability. For if he took out the volume of a dried fig through this door and the volume of a dried fig through that door in one period of oblivion is he not liable twice?
[Shabbat 1:1.5] {NAME} said, {NAME} compares domains to eating slices. For if one ate the volume of half an olive during the time needed to eat one slice and another volume of half an olive in the time needed to eat another slice, is he not free from liability? If one ate several volumes of olives during several times needed to eat a slice in one period of forgetting, he is liable only once.
[Shabbat 1:1.6] {NAME} say, before you compare this to fat, compare it to the rules of Sabbath itself. For if one was weaving one thread on this piece of cloth and weaving one thread on that piece of cloth, is he not free from liability? If he wove several threads on several pieces of cloth in one period of oblivion he is liable only once.
[Shabbat 1:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The one who takes out is not liable until he put it down. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Unless he take up and put down. {NAME} required, unless he take it up with the intention to put it down. Not if he lifted it to eat and then changed his mind to put it down. What {NAME} said does not follow {NAME}, as it was stated: “If he took out half the volume of a dried fig and put it down, and then took out another volume of half a dried fig. If he put it down within four cubits of the first piece he is liable, otherwise he is not liable. {NAME} said, if he transported it over it, he is liable, otherwise he is not liable.” {NAME} considers the person walking as if he was putting down. Just as {NAME} considers the person walking as if he was putting down for liability so he considers the person walking as if he was putting down for non-liability. When he took it out he is considered having put it down; then he should be free from liability. Explain it if it was put down within four cubits [of the door], as it was stated, “otherwise he is not liable.” {NAME} said, explain it if the door was five cubits wide and he brought one out on this side, the other on the other side. Then the second was not taken out within four cubits of the first.
[Shabbat 1:1.8] There, we have stated: “{NAME} says, if it was a Sabbath and he carried it out. They told him, it is not the category.” Because this one is liable because of walking and that one is liable because of putting down. Who is “they said to him”? {NAME}! The argument of {NAME} is inverted. There, he does not consider the person walking equal to one who was putting down but here he is considering the person walking equal to one who was putting down! {NAME} said, explain it that he was laying on the threshold partially inside, his mouth outside, when he stretched out his hand, took it, and ate it. Then he did not walk.
[Shabbat 1:1.9] {NAME} said, one who swallowed half the volume of an olive, then threw it up, and again swallowed it, is liable. But one who brought in half the volume of a dried fig and took it out again, is not liable. What is the difference between this and the first one? There his palate enjoyed the volume of an olive, but here he never dealt with a full volume of a fig. {NAME} said, sometimes a person may be dealing with a full volume of a fig and not be liable. How is this possible? He took out half of the volume of a dried fig, put it down, again took out half of the volume of a dried fig, but did not manage to put it down before the first one was burned. He was dealing with a full volume of a fig but is not liable. Because he compared it to forbidden fat he contrived this.

[Shabbat 1:1.23] “There are four kinds of domain on the Sabbath: Private domain, public domain, karmelit, and dead-end streets. What is private domain? [Shabbat 1:1.27] A threshold in front of the door; others say whenever the door is open it is entirely inside, when it is locked it is entirely outside. What are we dealing with? [Shabbat 1:2.1] MISHNAH: A person should not sit before the barber close to the time of afternoon prayers unless he has prayed. [Shabbat 1:3.1] MISHNAH: A tailor should not leave with his needle close to sundown lest he forget and leave; nor the scribe with his pen. [Shabbat 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: Mishnah: “A tailor should not leave with his needle close to sundown lest he forget and leave,” etc. It was stated: “A tailor should not leave with a needle in his garment, nor a scribe with the pen behind his ear, nor a dyer with a sample behind his ear, nor a money-changer with a denar behind his ear. It was stated: One who checks his garments takes and throws away; only he should not rub. {NAME} says, he may rub and throw away, only he should not kill. {NAME} said, one who kills a louse is like one who kills a camel. {NAME} broke off its hands and feet and gave if to the children. {NAME} put it in a flask. {NAME} said, did we not understand this from the purple snail? Does the purple snail have sinews and bones? But was it not stated: Any which has neither sinews nor bones does not live more than six months? For {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, the Holy One, praise to Him, turns around His world once in seven years. Qamqama turns into Ḥu-Rav-Padah. Ḥar-Efer turns into Šer. The head louse turns into a scorpion and the one of garments into a lizard. A horse worm turns into a wasp, that of cattle into a bee. A male hyena turns into a female, a field rat turns into a wild boar. The spine of a fish turns into a centipede, of a human into a snake. When? If he does not bow down with his entire spine.
[Shabbat 1:3.4] {NAME} stated: But one may investigate what is in the cup or the pot without worry. [Shabbat 1:3.10] It was stated: “The House of Shammai say, a Pharisee sufferer from gonorrhea may not eat with a vulgar sufferer from gonorrhea, but the House of Hillel permit it.” What is the reason of the House of Hillel? If he gets used to him during the days of his impurity he will remain used to him in the days of his purity. [Shabbat 1:3.11] “From here did {NAME} say, promptitude brings to cleanliness, cleanliness brings to purity, purity brings to holiness, holiness to meekness, meekness to fear of sin, fear of sin to the Holy Spirit, the Holy Spirit to piety, piety to the Resurrection of the Dead, the Resurrection of the Dead through Elijah, may his remembrance be a blessing.”“Promptitude to cleanliness,” he finishes, and he atones .“Cleanliness to purity,” the Cohen shall atone for her, then she will be pure .“Purity to holiness,” he shall purify it and sanctify it .“Holiness to meekness,” for so says the High and Elevated One, Who thrones eternally, His name is Holy, in sublimity and holiness I dwell, and the suppressed and of meek spirit .“Meekness to fear of sin,” the consequence of meekness is fear of the Eternal . {NAME} said, what wisdom proclaimed as a crown to its head, meekness made a heel for its sandal, for it is written, the head of wisdom is the fear of the Eternal, but it is written, the heel of meekness is fear of the Eternal .“Fear of sin to the Holy Spirit,” as it is written, then you will understand and knowledge of God you will find .“The Holy Spirit to piety,” as it is written, then You spoke in a vision to Your pious .“Piety to the Resurrection of the Dead,” as it is written, I shall give My Spirit into you and you will live .“The Resurrection of the Dead through Elijah, may his remembrance be a blessing,” as it is written, behold I am sending to you Elijah the prophet, before the coming of the great and awesome day of the Eternal, that he turn the fathers’ hearts to the sons and the sons’ hearts to their fathers .It was stated in the name of {NAME}: Anybody permanently in the Land of Israel who eats his profane food in purity, speaks in the holy language, and recites the Shemaˋ mornings and evenings is assured to participate in the life of the World to Come.

He told him: a caravan passed by and I ate figs from them this implies that he said, a Gentile does not need preparation.
[Shabbat 1:7.5] A student of [Rebbi] Simai went to Antipatris; they brought him Morocco-plums and he ate. A student of {NAME} went there; they brought him Morocco-plums and he did not eat. He came and told it to his teacher who said to him, this one follows the argument of {NAME}, as {NAME} said, a Gentile does not need preparation. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The red grapes in a vineyard are forbidden. {NAME} in the name of Rav: The hard dates on palm leaves are permitted.
[Shabbat 1:8.1] MISHNAH: They House of Shammai say, one does not sell to a Non-Jew, nor put a load on him unless he may reach a nearby destination, but the House of Hillel permit it.
[Shabbat 1:8.2] HALAKHAH: Mishnah: “They House of Shammai say, one sells to a Non-Jew,” etc. What means “a nearby destination”? It should be as {NAME} said, for example as from Ḥuṭra to Nahardea; here it is the same. Some want to say, until he reaches his home. But some want to say, until he reaches his town. {NAME} says, that he leaves the place of the door when the day becomes holy around him. {NAME} said, these are the words of {NAME}: But {NAME} comes to determine following the words of the House of Hillel. One does not give to a Gentile on condition that he leave. If he left, you do not have to interfere. One does not give to a dog on condition that he leave. If he left, you do not have to interfere.
[Shabbat 1:8.3] It was stated: Gentile workmen who were working for an Israel, in the Israel’s house it is forbidden, in their houses it is permitted. {NAME} said, when has this been said? For contract work. But for one hired by the day it is forbidden. When has this been said, when it was cut from the ground, but as long as it is standing on the ground it is forbidden. In another town, in any case it is permitted. What means “in any case”? Whether cut from the ground or standing on the ground; whether a hireling or contract work. {NAME} said, whether separated from the ground or connected to the ground, but only for contract work. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Concerning Sabbath, mourning, and idolatry, practice follows {NAME}.
[Shabbat 1:8.4] One sends letters through a Gentile neither on Friday nor on Thursday. The House of Shammai forbid even on Wednesday but the House of Hillel permit. They said about {NAME} that his handwriting never was found in the hand of a Gentile.
[Shabbat 1:8.5] One embarks on the ocean neither on Friday nor on Thursday. The House of Shammai forbid even on Wednesday but the House of Hillel permit. If it is not dangerous, as from Tyre to Sidon, it is permitted.
[Shabbat 1:8.6] One does not lay siege to a Gentile city within three days before the Sabbath. That is in a war of choice. But in a war of obligation even on the Sabbath, for so we find that Jericho was conquered only on a Sabbath, as it is written, so you shall act for six days , and it is written, on the Seventh Day you shall circle the city seven times . And it is written, until it fell , even on the Sabbath.
[Shabbat 1:9.1] MISHNAH: The House of Shammai say, one does not give hides to the tannery worker nor clothing to the Non-Jewish washer unless the work may be done when it is still daylight. In all cases, the House of Hillel permit as long as the sun still shines. {NAME} says, my father’s house used to give their white garments to a Non-Jewish washer three days before the Sabbath. They both agree that one may load the beam of the olive press and the round stone of the wine press.
[Shabbat 1:9.2] HALAKHAH: Mishnah: “One does not give hides to the tannery worker,” etc. How long? It should come like what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, the time needed to walk four miles. And here, if he gave his clothing to the Gentile fuller and found him treating them on the Sabbath, it is forbidden. {NAME} said, he should tell him not to do it. {NAME}, {NAME} said, that is, for goodwill. But for a fee, he looks after his work.
[Shabbat 1:9.3] “{NAME} says, in my father’s house they used,” etc. They mentioned only white, therefore not colored. Following our routine we infer that white garments are more difficult to wash than colored ones.
[Shabbat 1:9.4] “They both agree,” etc. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, because every single drop was moved from its place. {NAME} said, {NAME} asked, may one touch the flow? {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} disagreed; {NAME} said it is forbidden; {NAME} said, it is permitted. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: They both agree that one may not touch the flow.

Maybe it was only said for the Passover sacrifice. There {NAME} in the name of the important {NAME}: The Passover sacrifice which was fully roasted one may return on a cooking stove which is not covered with ashes.
[Shabbat 1:10.3] “One does not put bread dough into the oven.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Women are more careful with bread than with dishes. What is the difference between bread and dish? A dish one usually eats hot, bread one usually does not eat hot. There, they say, hot bread is accompanied by fever. A wasp, cold; a scorpion, hot. He who switches is in danger.
[Shabbat 1:10.4] {NAME} agrees that the shew-bread is not called bread until it develops a crust in the oven.

[Shabbat 2:1.13] {NAME} stated before {NAME}: From where that all those to be circumcised should only be circumcised during daytime? The verse says, And on the day . {NAME} told him, is that so? All who require immersion immerse themselves normally during daytime except for the woman after her period and one who gave birth who only immerses herself during the night. A woman after her period whose time has passed immerses herself either during the day or during the night. {NAME} preached this to the people of Tyre, a woman after her period whose time has passed immerses herself either during the day or during the night. There they say, even one whose time has passed, because of her mother-in-law and her daughter-in-law. They saw a woman of our rabbis immersing herself normally during daytime. We shall say that her time had passed.

What is the reason? It should be washed a second time and will be pure . Since the first time it was intentionally, also the second time it must be intentionally. And from where that the first time it was intentionally? The Cohen has to order that they should wash . Intentionally.

Innards of fish are not smelling badly as long as they are burning; they are smelling badly when extinguished. ˋIṭran smells badly whether extinguished or burning. [Shabbat 2:5.5] There, we have stated: “All who destroy are not liable,” except the incendiary and one causing an injury. {NAME} said, even if he did not need the blood, even if he did not need the ashes. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If his bull set fire to a stack of sheaves on the Sabbath; he is liable, but if he set fire to a stack of sheaves on the Sabbath, he is not liable.” If his bull set fire to a stack of sheaves on the Sabbath; he is liable. Is that not for no purpose? So here if he set fire to a stack of sheaves on the Sabbath, he is not liable, even if it was for no purpose. {NAME} said, since it was for no purpose, did he commit a capital crime? But here even it was for no purpose he should be free from paying restitution, from the following: The slayer of an animal shall pay for it; the slayer of a human shall die. Since for the slayer of an animal you did not differentiate between unintentional and intentional to make him liable for money, so for the slayer of a human you cannot differentiate between unintentional and intentional to free him from liability for money.

[Shabbat 2:5.9] An outsider who officiated in the Temple on the Sabbath, or a deformed person who officiated in impurity, the Elder {NAME} said, two; {NAME} said, one. {NAME} objected to the Elder {NAME}: is the outsider liable for any service which is permitted to a Cohen? He said to him, there is a difference, for it is written: no outsider may eat sanctified food . Is there not the breaking of the neck; before the neck was broken it was forbidden for both; after the neck was broken it is forbidden for outsiders and permitted to Cohanim? He said to him, there is a difference, for it is written: no outsider may eat sanctified food. Is there not the ṭevel ; before it was put in order it was forbidden for both; after it was put in order it is forbidden for outsiders and permitted to Cohanim? He said to him, there is a difference, for it is written: no outsider may eat sanctified food. They said, let us go outside and learn. They went outside and heard, {NAME} said, two; {NAME} said, one. He who said one, because of outsider status. He who said two, one because of outsider status; why the other? Because of slaughter. But slaughter by an outsider is valid! But because bringing, sprinkling, and receiving. These are only because of Sabbath rest. Therefore the reason may be only because of the consumption of limbs and fat which were consumed on the altar during the entire night. In the opinion of {NAME} who said because of setting fire it is understandable. In the opinion of {NAME} who said because of cooking, what cooking is here? Since he wants their being consumed it is like cooking.

[Shabbat 3:1.12] It was stated: “A woman should not fill a pot with ˋassisiot and lupines and put them into the oven at the start of the Sabbath, at nightfall. Because the profit of the Sabbath [is forbidden] to him.” And here, since you say that after the end of the Sabbath he has to wait until the time it could have been done, he did not gain anything from the Sabbath. What is the reason of the rabbis? People are suspected about the Sabbatical but not about the Sabbath. Another explanation: One counts Sabbaticals, one does not count Sabbaths. What is this about? If somebody planted less than thirty days before the Sabbatical and now it is the Sabbatical, if it is because of suspicion, there is no suspicion; if it is for counting, it is not counted. Less than thirty days before the eighth year and now it is the eighth year, if it is because of suspicion, there is suspicion; if it is because of counting, there is counting. It follows him who says because of suspicion, but for him who says because of counting they fined the unintentional because of the intentional.

[Shabbat 4:1.1] MISHNAH: In what does one store away and in what may one not store away? One does not store away in olive cake, nor in manure, nor in salt, nor in lime, nor in sand, whether moist or dry. Not in straw, nor in fibers, nor in grape pits, nor in grasses when they are moist but one may store away in them when dry. One may store away in garments, and produce, and pigeon wings, and flax residue, and in fine sawdust. {NAME} forbids if it is fine and permits coarse.
[Shabbat 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: “In what does one store away and in what may one not store away,” etc. Because these things are hot and produce heat; if he takes away and they cool in his hand he returns them and they add heat; therefore they forbade to store away in them following {NAME}, for {NAME} said, “a box he tilts on its side and takes out.” But according to the rabbis there? For they say, if it was a vat it is permitted. And there we have stated “if there be doubt whether it is dark or not dark.” Because it was not dark; therefore if it is dark it is forbidden to store away in them. There, they are saying, because of the neglect of the house of study; {NAME} said, because of the suspicion. For if you tell him that he is permitted he will not finish it completely when it still is daylight. Because you tell him that he is forbidden he will finish it completely when it still is daylight. What is the difference between them? To hide away snow and cold water. In {NAME} opinion it is permitted, in the opinion of the rabbis there it is prohibited. They forbade hiding away because of the cooking stove; they forbade the cooking stove because of hiding away. They forbade a cooking stove which creates little heat because of a cooking stove which creates much heat. They forbade a completely cooked dish because of an incompletely cooked dish. They forbade hot water because of a completely cooked dish. They turned around and permitted hot water.
[Shabbat 4:1.3] It was stated: One does not store away in hot ashes. {NAME} said, this implies that it is permitted to store away in cold ashes. As the following: {NAME} daughter was serving her father and brought him hot dishes. He asked her, how was this made? She told him, (with a spade and) [it was hidden in] olive cake. He said to her, you should not do this, but (with a spade) [hide it] in a box and put the box on the olive cake. {NAME} said, {NAME} disagrees with this. {NAME} preached in the name of {NAME}: Olive cake at the bottom and straw on both sides is forbidden, and {NAME} agrees.

[Shabbat 4:1.5] “Not in sand.” There, we have stated: “One puts it on sand in order to wait.” This sand heats the hot and cools the cold. Straw is like the holder of a deposit; what you give it it gives to you.

[Shabbat 5:3.1] MISHNAH: With what may [an animal] not go out? The camel may not go out with its pad, nor bound on one foot, nor bound on two feet, and so all other animals. One may not tie camels one to the other and draw, but he may take the ropes into his hand and draw on condition that he not wrap up.
[Shabbat 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: Mishnah: “With what may [an animal] not go out? The camel may not go out with its pad.” Like the curved padding with which one equalizes a hump back. עָקוּד at one front leg. רָגוּל at both hind legs.
[Shabbat 5:3.3] “One may not tie camels one to the other and draw.” {NAME} said, because of the suspicion, that they should not say this man goes out to do his job on the Sabbath. {NAME} said, it was necessary for kilaim . {NAME} in the name of {NAME} (said, from his hand it is forbidden but from the neck of the animal it is permitted, for if it is not for the animal) wound around the animal’s neck it is forbidden, hanging from the animal’s neck it is permitted. {NAME} and {NAME}, both in the name of {NAME}. One said, from his hand is forbidden but from the animal’s neck it is permitted. The other one inverts. He who says from his hand is forbidden, because of a load on the Sabbath. But from the animal’s neck it is permitted, because for the animal it is not a load on the Sabbath. And he who says from his hand is permitted, because it is impossible, but from the animal’s neck it is forbidden, because he is responsible for the rest of his animal as for his own, as it is said, that your ox and your donkey rest ” “ like you ”.
[Shabbat 5:3.4] It was stated: A hand-breadth from his hand to the animal’s neck is forbidden. {NAME} said, from his hand is forbidden and from his animal’s neck is forbidden! A hand-breadth from his hand to the animal’s neck is forbidden, what is it that is permitted? {NAME} said, one who wants to do it right should lead it like a Saracen horse.
[Shabbat 5:4.1] MISHNAH: A donkey may not go out with its saddle cloth if it is not bound to it, nor with a bell even if it is plugged, nor with a ladder on its neck, nor with a strip on its foot. Chicken may no go out with threads or strips on their feet. Rams may not go out with a carriage under their tails nor female sheep with yaḥnun , nor a calf with gimun , nor a cow with hedgehog hide, nor with a strip between her horns. {NAME} cow went out with a strip between her horns against the will of the Sages.
[Shabbat 5:4.2] HALAKHAH: Mishnah: “A donkey may not go out with its saddle cloth,” etc. It was stated, “but it may walk around with it in the courtyard.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The same applies to the saddle. It was stated: “a donkey may go out with its saddle to get warm but one may not tie the load belt and not lower the strap under its tail.” {NAME} asked before {NAME}: From where these things? As we have stated: “The practices of Sabbath … are like mountains hanging on a hair,” and you are saying so? He could have objected, what is the difference between a ladder and a package of straw? A ladder is substantial, a package of straw is not substantial. {NAME} said, he could have objected, what is the difference between a package of straw and an expert amulet? As we have stated, “it is forbidden that an animal go out with an expert amulet.” {NAME} said, he could have objected, what is the difference between a package of straw and a wound dressing? There are Tannaim who state, they may not go out with a package of straw; there are Tannaim who state, they may go out. {NAME} said, this is a tannaitic difference. For him who said, they may go out with a package of straw; they may go out with a wound dressing. But for him who said, they may not go out with a package of straw; they may not go out with a wound dressing.
[Shabbat 5:4.3] “Rams may not go out with a carriage under their tails.” Because it makes a groove.
[Shabbat 5:4.4] “Nor female sheep with yaḥnun .” {NAME} says, a woolen cap. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is a root named yaḥnūnâ. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does this not imply that it is forbidden to let an animal go out with an expert amulet? He told him, yes, Babylonian, you understood it.
[Shabbat 5:4.5] “Nor a calf with gimun .” {NAME} said, a small yoke. {NAME} said, a wooden tablet. {NAME} said, a spit. Some Tannaim state gimun. Some Tannaim state gimul. He who said gimun, to bend his head like a reed . He who said gimul, she brought him up with her after she had weaned him . He who said gimun supports {NAME}. He who said gimul supports {NAME} and {NAME}.
[Shabbat 5:4.6] “Nor a cow with hedgehog hide,” because one puts hedgehog hide between her udder so she cannot nurse her young.

If to (expect) [punish] him it is forbidden, if so he should not eat his bridle it is permitted.

[Shabbat 6:1.1] MISHNAH: With what may a woman go out and with what may she not go out? A woman may go out neither with woolen or linen threads nor with ribbons on her head and she may not immerse herself wearing them unless she relaxes them. To the public domain not with a frontlet nor with a head-dress hanging down the cheeks as long as they are not sewn, nor an under-cap. Also not with a city of gold, nor with a chain, nor with nose rings, nor with a ring without a seal, nor with a pin. If she went out she is not liable for a purification offering.
[Shabbat 6:1.2] HALAKHAH: “With what may a woman go out,” etc. {NAME} said, because she loosens them because they separate for her period and she forgets and walks with them for four cubits. {NAME} said, earlier we were saying because she opens what is sewn but we were not saying anything, as {NAME} stated, a basket of palm leaves for dates one may tear and open but only one may not tie. There, we have stated: “The following separate on a human: threads of wool or of linen and the ribbons on the head of girls.” {NAME} said, there is no hair here; in the opinion of {NAME}, but only wool. Therefore hair does not separate in the opinion of everybody. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}; {NAME} in the name of the rabbis: One hair separates, two are in doubt, three do not separate.
[Shabbat 6:1.3] {NAME} asked: If one tied one hair to another, is it one? One to two are they two? To three are they three? {NAME} said, One who goes to immerse herself after her period ties her hair as a pony tail. To act on it and trust me.
[Shabbat 6:1.4] {NAME} asked Rav, may one go out with twisted chains? He told them, does one say, it is forbidden for a man to go out with his belt? {NAME} instructed the wife of the Head of the Diaspora to put golden felt on the wig. {NAME} instructed these of the House of Con to put a patch with pearls on the jacket. {NAME} said, anything connected to a garment is like the garment. And we have stated, one may go out with bells on his garment but one may not go out with bells around his neck. There are Tannaim who state that in both cases they are subject to impurity, and there are Tannaim who state that in both cases they are not subject to impurity. He who said, in both cases they are subject to impurity, if he made clappers for them, but he who said, in both cases they are not subject to impurity, if he did not make clappers for them. Even if he did make clappers for them they should be pure! Did not {NAME}, {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: Bells on a crib. Two Amoraim. One said he can move it to and fro, only he should make no sound. But the other said, if he made a sound it is forbidden, otherwise it is permitted. There, although they are not made for sound on the Sabbath they are made for sound on weekdays; but here if they are not made for sound either on the Sabbath or weekdays, why did he make clappers for them?

It was stated: {NAME} permits. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This of {NAME} comes out like Rebbi’s. Just as Rebbi said hidden things are permitted, so {NAME} said, hidden things are permitted.

[Shabbat 6:1.11] {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Everywhere they said she may not go out and when she did go out she is obligated for a purification sacrifice she is prohibited to go out with it to the courtyard. Is a man permitted because he is not vain? Let us hear from the following: {NAME} went walking in his courtyard on the Sabbath with a golden key in his hand. This implies that even when they said she may not go out but if she went out she is not obligated for a purification sacrifice, she is prohibited to go out with it to the courtyard.
[Shabbat 6:2.1] MISHNAH: A man may not go out with a nailed shoe, nor with a single one if he does not have a wound on his foot, nor with a phylactery nor with a amulet not written by an expert, nor with armor, nor with a helmet, nor with soldier’s boots. If he went out he is not liable for a purification offering.
[Shabbat 6:2.2] HALAKHAH: Why did they decree about a nailed shoe? Some say, because they saw the tips and had miscarriages. But some say, they heard its sound and had miscarriages. And some say, they were stampeding and killing one another. What is the difference between them? הדוסטא. Accordig to him who said, because they saw the tips and had miscarriages, it is permitted. But according to him who said, they heard its sound and had miscarriages or they were stampeding and killing one another, it is forbidden. But did they not decree this in an emergency? When the emergency passed it should have been permitted. There never rose a court which undid it. Then even on a weekday! People do not usually have two pairs of shoes, one for weekdays and one for the Sabbath. It was stated: If one put a patch under it it is permitted. {NAME} feet were scratched and they did this for him.
[Shabbat 6:2.3] How many nails should it have? {NAME} said five, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. {NAME} said seven, corresponding to your days are your steps . The rabbis are used to follow {NAME}. {NAME} explained following {NAME}: nine. Rebbi put thirteen on one [shoe] and eleven on the other, for the number of watches. And like planted nails , since the watches are 24, so the nails 24. {NAME} said, a crooked nail is not counted with the nails. {NAME} asked {NAME}: may one put all of them on one sandal? He told him, it is permitted. May one put all of them on one boot? He told him, it is permitted. One does not scrape old boots or sandals but one may oil them or dip them in water. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The students of the Elder {NAME} say that those of first rank said, one may scrape, those of second rank said, one may not scrape. Rebbi was asked and said, one does not scrape. {NAME} said, here goes one of the students of the Elder {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} follow him who said he scrapes but only with the back of a knife. {NAME} said, we used to sit before Rebbi and were oiling and rinsing, but not scraping. Nobody should anoint his foot in a boot or his foot in a sandal but he may oil his foot and step into his boot or oil his foot and step into his sandal. One may oil himself and roll on a new tarpaulin without worry. One should not put it on a marble slab to roll himself in it, but {NAME} permits it.
[Shabbat 6:2.4] One does not wear new boots and sandals except if he wore and walked in them during daytime. How far should he walk? [Shabbat 6:2.10] “If he does not have a wound on his foot.” Therefore if he has a wound on his foot he may wear one. On which foot does he wear it? {NAME} said, he wears it on the one which has no wound. If you would say that he wears it on the one which has the wound, how does he tie it that he could not put it on the other? {NAME} said, he wears it on the one which has the wound. {NAME} served {NAME}; he brought him his sandals as it was stated in Derekh Ereṣ : When he puts them on, he puts the right foot one on first and after this the left foot one, when he removes them he removes the left foot one and after this the right foot one. {NAME} said to him, Babylonian, you should not act in this way for the earlier generations did not do this. But when he puts them on, he puts the left foot one on first and after this the right foot one, that the right side one should not look deficient. [Shabbat 6:2.11] One may go out on Friday towards nightfall with phylacteries, but one may not go out on Friday towards nightfall with nailed shoes. What is the difference between them? These one usually takes off, those one does not usually take off.

[Shabbat 6:5.1] MISHNAH: A woman may go out with hair threads, whether her own or another woman’s or an animal’s, with a frontlet with a head-dress hanging down the cheeks if they are sewn; with an under-cap and another’s braid into the courtyard with cotton wool in her ear, or cotton wool in her shoes, or cotton wool which she prepared for her period. [Shabbat 6:9.13] Two students of {NAME} went out to chop wood. An astrologer saw them, these two if they go out will not return. He ate and prayed for them; he said to them, may your life be preserved today as you did preserve my life today. They went out in peace and returned in peace. There were people there who had heard his voice and told him, did you not say, these two if they go out will not return? He said, if it is so, this man is a liar and his astrology consists of lies. Nevertheless they went and investigated and found a viper half in this load and half in the other load. They asked, what good deed did you do today? They told him the facts. He said, what can this man do if the Jew’s God is propitiated by half a loaf!

[Shabbat 7:1.1] MISHNAH: A comprehensive principle they said about the Sabbath. Anybody who is oblivious of the principle of the Sabbath and performed many works on many Sabbaths is obligated for one purification sacrifice only. But one who knows the principle of the Sabbath and performed many works on many Sabbaths is obligated for every single Sabbath; and one who knows that it is the Sabbath and performed many works on many Sabbaths is obligated for every single work. One who performs many works similar to one work is obligated only for one purification sacrifice.
[Shabbat 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: “A comprehensive principle they said about the Sabbath,” etc. What means “comprehensive”? {NAME} said, because it is more comprehensive than the principle of the Sabbatical year, since the Sabbath falls on everything but the Sabbatical year falls on agricultural work in the Land only. What means “a comprehensive principle”? {NAME} said, because it is more comprehensive than peah. for tithes apply both to food that is stored and to food which is not stored, but peah applies only to food used as stored staple. Some want to say, what means “comprehensive”? From here that there are derivatives.

[Shabbat 7:1.6] There, we have stated: “{NAME} said, I asked {NAME}: If somebody performs many works on many Sabbaths all of the same category in one period of oblivion, what? Since for the menstruating woman, which does not entail many ramifications nor many purification sacrifices, he is liable for each single occurrence, for the Sabbath which has many ramifications and many purification sacrifices it is only logical that he be liable for each single occurrence. If you mention the underage girl who even though there is no warning now there will be one in the future, what can you say about the Sabbath where there is only one [warning] whether now or in the future. He told me, one having intercourse with an animal shall prove it. I said to him, the animal is like the Sabbath.

[Shabbat 7:2.1] MISHNAH: There are 39 categories of work. He who ploughs, who sows, who harvests, who binds into sheaves, who threshes, and who winnows, who selects, who grinds, and who sifts, who makes dough, and who bakes. He who shears wool, who bleaches it, who cards it, who dyes it, who spins it, who prepares the loom, who ties two threads as warp, who weaves two rows, who hits two threads, who ties, and who unties. Also who sews two stitches, who tears in order to sew two stitches. He who catches a deer, who slaughters it, who skins it, who salts it, who rubs it clean, who tans it, who cuts it, who writes two letters, and who erases in order to write two letters. He who builds, and who tears down, who extinguishes fire, and who lights fire, and who hits with a hammer, and who transports from one domain to another; these are the 39 categories of work.

[Shabbat 7:2.8] {NAME} stated before {NAME}: If somebody sacrificed, burned incense, and poured a libation in one forgetting, he is guilty for each action separately. {NAME} told him, Babylonian! You crossed three rivers with your hands and were broken. He is guilty only once! {Before he broke it in his hand there is “one” but not “those”; after he broke it in his hand there are “those” but not “one”.} {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Should he not be guilty for each action separately? As you say for the Sabbath: Do not perform any work , principle. Do not light fire in any of your dwelling places , a detail. Was not lighting fire subsumed under the principle, but it is mentioned separately from this principle! Since lighting fire is special in that it is the work of a single individual and one would be guilty for it alone, so everything for which one alone is guilty. Also here: Do not worship them , a principle. Do not prostrate yourself , a detail. Was not prostrating itself included in the principle and why was it mentioned separately? To infer, to tell you that prostrating oneself is special in that it is the action of a single individual and one would be guilty for it alone, so everything for which one alone is guilty. He answered: For the Sabbath, He mentioned the principle at one place and the details at another place. For idol worship, the principle is found close to the detail. He retorted: Is it not written: Do not prostrate yourself before another power ? He who sacrifices to Elohim shall be banned . He mentioned the principle at one place and the details at another place! He said, since you do [not] infer anything from it close up, you cannot infer anything from afar. The colleagues say, it makes no difference; whether He gave the principle at one place and the detail at another, or gave principle and detail at the same place, it is a matter of principle and detail. For the Sabbath, He first gave the principle and then the detail. For idolatry, He gave the detail and only later the principle. {NAME} said, it makes no difference whether He first gave the principle and then the detail or He gave the detail and only later the principle, or He gave principle, detail, and principle; it is a matter of principle and detail. For the Sabbath, He gave a general prohibition of work, followed by details; for idolatry, He gave the general principle regarding its worship but detailed the works of Heaven.
[Shabbat 7:2.9] {NAME} said, lighting fire was mentioned unnecessarily; prostrating oneself was mentioned by necessity to explain about itself since it is not work. This follows what {NAME} stated: He who sacrifices to powers shall be banned . Sacrificing was mentioned separately to teach about everything, prostrating oneself to explain about itself since it is not work. {NAME} said, lighting fire was mentioned by necessity, to teach that courts should not sit on the Sabbath. What is the reason? It says here, in all your settlements, and it says there, these . . should be rules of law for your generations , in all your settlements . Since “settlements” mentioned there refers to courts, “settlements” referred to here also refers to courts. {NAME} said, even if you say that it was mentioned separately necessarily is as if it was mentioned separately not by necessity, and any item mentioned separately unnecessarily instructs.
[Shabbat 7:2.10] This implies that one item which was mentioned separately by necessity does not divide. If it was mentioned not by necessity it divides. If two items were mentioned separately, do they divide? Let us hear from the following: From where that he transgresses a prohibition whoever brings to the altar meat of a purification offering, or meat of a reparation offering, or meat of most holy offerings, or meat from simply holy offerings, or the remainder of the ˋ Omer or the Two Breads, or the Shew Bread, or remainders of cereal offerings, or leaven, or date honey? The verse says, for any leaven or any date honey you may not turn into smoke as a fire gift to the Eternal . Therefore anything that had been given to the fire is under “do not turn into smoke”.

[Shabbat 7:2.16] If He stated a general principle as a positive commandment but the detail as a prohibition, the word of {NAME} is that this is a general principle followed by a detail. {NAME} said, one whips for ploughing in the Sabbatical year. {NAME} said, one does not whip for ploughing in the Sabbatical year. They are two different things, and two different details for one general principle do divide. In {NAME} opinion do they not divide? He holds that because they do not divide, they are for making inferences. In {NAME} opinion, are they not for making inferences? Just as one cannot make inferences for prohibitions, so one should not be able to make inferences for permissions. {NAME} said, {NAME} reason is six years you shall sow , not in the Sabbatical; and six years you shall prune your vineyard , not in the Sabbatical at all. Any prohibition inferred from a positive commandment is a positive commandment; one violates a positive commandment. {NAME} said, there is not even a positive commandment. {NAME} said, one violates a positive commandment. Why is it written that the Land shall keep a Sabbath for the Eternal ? That is for the prohibition implied by it.

They were clobbering an animal for red skins of rams. {NAME} said, this implies that he is liable who causes a wound which results in echymosis. He who colors his lips red is liable. He who causes bleeding, because of taking away life force at that place. He who makes a shape, the first one is liable because of writing and the second one because of dying. If he left out a limb and another came and finished it, he is liable because of hitting with a hammer. Wringing and washing are the same category of work. It was stated: {NAME} says, the dyers in Jerusalem made wringing a separate category of work. In the opinion of {NAME}, there are 40 categories of work. Should we state this? We come to state only items to which everybody agrees.
[Shabbat 7:2.45] One who makes ropes. The one who twines them is liable because of spinning. One who makes basket work of reeds, sieves, bast mats, is liable because of weaving. A woman when she prepares the loom, because of preparing. When she fastens the web, because of tying threads. When she erects [the loom], because of building. When she hits, because of weaving. When she cuts the threads, because of cutting. When she finishes her work, because of hitting with a hammer. One who makes boxes, when he starts, because of preparing. When he tailors, because of sewing. When he bends, because of building. When he cuts, because of cutting. When he finishes his work, because of hitting with a hammer. One who makes bed-sheets, lengthwise because of preparing, crosswise because of weaving. Grating, because of tying threads. When he cuts, because of cutting. When he finishes his work, because of hitting with a hammer. There are two warp threads per peg and two pegs for each warp thread.
[Shabbat 7:2.46] “He who weaves two rows, who hits two threads, who ties, and who unties.” What tying was in the Tabernacle? They were tying down the ropes. But was this not temporarily? {NAME} says, because they were camping and travelling by the Word, was it like temporarily? {NAME} [{NAME}] said, since the Holy One, praise to Him, has promised them that he will bring them into the Land, it is as if it were (temporary) [permanent]. {NAME} said, they learned it from the gobelin sewers. If [a thread] broke, he was tying it. If it broke again, it was impossible to make many knots but he would untie the first one. {NAME} said, an expert tailor merges the two heads. And where was this said? As {NAME} said, they learned it from the weavers of the gobelins. What is the reason? The length of one gobelin , that it should be an entity. If [a thread] broke, he was tying it. When he came to the weave, he untied it and brought it in. {NAME} in the name of (Rav) [Rebbi] Ḥuna: Even on its warp there was neither knot nor connection.
[Shabbat 7:2.47] {NAME} stated, a basket of palm leaves for dates or a plate of palm leaves one may tear and open, only one may not tie.
[Shabbat 7:2.48] Is this not untying? It is like one who breaks an amphora to eat dried figs. The handles of a double sack one may tie and untie. It is as if one opened or locked on the Sabbath.
[Shabbat 7:2.49] {NAME} said, not until it comes down an entire side. {NAME} said, say to {NAME}, get out and read! Did we not state, “if the two ends appear on the same side”? That means, only if it goes up and down and up. And did we not state, “{NAME} says, only if there are three needle stitches”? That means that [the thread] goes down, and up, and down. But so and so. A thread drawn through by means of a needle, even if it has a knot on each side, is no connection for cloth. The thread is a connection for cloth but not for the needle. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, only if it is knotted on both sides. The words of the rabbis disagree since {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of Rav: He who straightens out the sides on the Sabbath is liable because of sewing. He should have said, because of sewing and tying knots.
[Shabbat 7:2.50] Tearing applies to textiles and cutting to hides. Tearing in the middle and cutting from the sides. There are some who switch, tearing of hides and cutting of textiles. Tearing of hides, those soft ones, and cutting of textiles, felt.
[Shabbat 7:2.51] 3. One who catches a purple snail and crushes it. There are Tannaïm who state that he is liable twice. There are Tannaïm who state that he is liable only once. He who says twice, one because of catching and one because of depriving of life. But he who says once, this is because of depriving of life. Does he not have catching? It comes like what {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said: The Holy One, praise to Him, created for Moses in the desert a kind of pure animal. After the work of the Tabernacle had been finished it was hidden. {NAME} said, its name was qereš . {NAME} stated, a unicorn. It is preferable to the Eternal to a cattle ox which sprouts a horn and has split hooves . It is written, it sprouts a horn.
[Shabbat 7:2.52] “Who slaughters it.” {NAME} said, there is no slaughter here; slaughter is a derivative of wounding. And why was it (not) stated with it? Only because we stated the proceedings of a meal it was stated with it.
[Shabbat 7:2.53] “Who tans it.” What tanning was for the Tabernacle? They were drafting on them. What were they drafting on them? They were drawing lines with a ruler. It follows that what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, it is permitted to make tents from the hide of an impure animal.
[Shabbat 7:2.54] “Who rubs it clean.” What kind of erasure was in the tabernacle? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They were rubbing the hide on a pillar. One who rubbed hide clear on a pillar is liable. For what is he liable? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, because of rubbing clean. That is, if it is new. But if it be old, it is the disagreement between {NAME} and the Sages. Since they disagreed: “One who sweeps, who sprinkles, who makes cheese, who makes butter, who milks, and who takes down honeycombs, is liable for a purification sacrifice. But the Sages say, it is because of Sabbath rest.” {NAME} said, they do not disagree. He who sweeps, who sprinkles, is liable because of threshing. He who makes cheese, who makes butter, is liable because of kneading. He who milks, and who takes down honeycombs, is liable because of harvesting. He who squeezes budding olives is liable because of harvesting. Who needs this? {NAME}.
[Shabbat 7:2.55] He who files off heads of poles is liable because of cutting. He who applies salve on a wet bandage is liable because of rubbing clean.
[Shabbat 7:2.56] “If one erased a big letter where there is space to write in its stead two letters, he is liable. If he wrote one large letter even though there is space to write in its stead two letters, he is not liable. {NAME} says, this is more serious about him who erases than about him who writes that he who erases in order to correct is liable but he who writes in order to spoil is not liable.” It may happen that one writes a single dot and is liable for it because of writing and because of erasing; it may happen that one erases a single dot and is liable for it because of writing and because of erasing. How is this? If it was a ד and he makes it ר ,ר and he makes it ד; he is liable because of writing and because of erasing.
[Shabbat 7:2.57] 4. What building was at the Sanctuary? They were putting the planks on top of the bases. But was this not temporary? {NAME} says, because they were camping and travelling by the Word, it was as though permanent. {NAME} said, since the Holy One, praise to Him, has promised them that He will bring them into the Land, it is as if it were permanent. This implies, a temporary building is a building. This implies, even from the side. This implies even if was put on top of something else. Does it imply that building on implements is building? The bases are like soil.
[Shabbat 7:2.58] It was stated: “If one brings the stone and another one the mortar, he who brings the mortar is liable. {NAME} says, both are liable.” {NAME} is of the opinion that stone without mortar is building. Everybody agrees that if one put up mortar first and someone then brought stone that he is liable. “The builder who set the stone on top of the row is liable.” For whom is this needed? For the rabbis. One who put up planks and one who put up adobe walls is liable because of building.
[Shabbat 7:2.59] “And who tears down,” but only for a need. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: he who braids a palm-leaf basket is liable because of building. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: he who blows a glass vessel is liable because of building. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: There are things which are close but far away; and there are things which are far away but close. He who braids a palm-leaf basket, and he who blows a glass vessel, and he who makes a vessel in a form, all are because of building. He who selects, who filters, and who sifts, all because of removing waste. Each of them is separately liable. And why was handing over not stated with them? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because of the disagreement of {NAME} and the Sages. {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rebbi: In addition, there is handing over. And why was it not stated with them? All categories of work involve one, and this one two. All categories of work have derivatives, but this has no derivative.
[Shabbat 7:3.1] MISHNAH: They said another principle. Anything which can be preserved and one preserves its kind if he took it out on the Sabbath he is obligated for a purification sacrifice because of it, but for anything which cannot be preserved and one does not preserve its kind, if he took it out on the Sabbath only the one who preserves is obligated.
[Shabbat 7:3.2] HALAKHAH: 5. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This has been said for idol worship. {NAME} said, this has been said for things forbidden for usufruct. {NAME} said, this has been said for minimal quantities. There are Tannaim who state, he is liable for a purification sacrifice. There are Tannaim who state, a minimal amount. He who said he is liable for a purification sacrifice supports {NAME}. He who said a minimal amount supports {NAME} and {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: For example, the wad which she prepared for her menstrual period.
[Shabbat 7:4.1] MISHNAH: One who brings out straw filling the mouth of a cow, wood shavings filling the mouth of a camel, grain filling the mouth of a sheep, grasses filling the mouth of a goat. Moist garlic leaves and onion leaves the volume of a dried fig, if dry filling the mouth of a goat; they are not combined since their measures are not identical. One who brings out foodstuffs in the volume of a dried fig; they are combined since their measures are the same except for their shells, and their pits, and their stalks, and their grit, and their bran. {NAME} says except for pods of lentils which are cooked with them.
[Shabbat 7:4.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The more restrictive completes the less restrictive but the less restrictive does not complete the more restrictive. Grasses complete straw; straw does not complete grasses. There we have stated: “Cloth and sackcloth, sackcloth and leather, leather and bast matting combine with one another. {NAME} says, because they are apt to become impure as seats.” {NAME} asked, one understands that they combine for seats since as seats they equally are by a hand-width. From where in היסק 462 ? {NAME} said before {NAME}, because they are equal in היסק. He told him, we are asking about taking out and you are saying היסק? {NAME} said before {NAME}, because they are equal in היסק. He said to him, should we state, taking out a small cup? {NAME} said, meat completes bone pieces, bone pieces does not complete meat; grasses complete straw, straw does not complete grasses. {NAME} stated: If one took out straw for a cow filling the mouth of a cow, took out straw for a goat filling the mouth of a goat, he is liable. {NAME} said that {NAME} asked, if one took out food for a sick person filling the mouth of a sick person, should he be liable? {NAME} agrees that if he took out straw for a cow filling the mouth of a goat that he is not liable; for you should not think that just as he has it for restriction he also has it for leniency. {NAME} asked, think of it if the dish was not the volume of a dried fig. Does the volume of a dried fig cancel the volume of a dried fig?

[Shabbat 8:1.1] MISHNAH: One who brings out wine to mix a cup, milk for a sip, honey to put on a sore spot, oil to anoint a small limb, water to mix eye salve, and all other fluids by a quartarius , and all waste water by a quartarius . {NAME} says, all are by a quartarius; these measures were said only for those who store them.

May one drink them with interruptions? They said that he should drink, not that he should get drunk. If he drinks them with interruptions, would he not become drunk? May one fulfill his obligation with Sabbatical wine? {NAME} stated, one may fulfill his obligation with Sabbatical wine. May one fulfill his obligation with spiced wine? {NAME} stated, spiced wine is like wine, which implies that one may fulfill his obligation with spiced wine. May one fulfill his obligation with mixed wine? Since {NAME} stated: the Four Cups which they prescribed, one may fulfill his obligation either with unmixed or mixed, on condition that it have the taste and looks of wine. {NAME} said, it is meritorious to fulfill one’s obligation with red wine. What is the reason? Do not see wine when it shows its red color . It was stated, cooked for spice. May one fulfill his obligation with cooked wine? {NAME} said, one may fulfill his obligation with cooked wine. {NAME} follows his own opinion, since {NAME} drank his four cups in the Passover night and had a headache until Pentecost.
[Shabbat 8:1.6] {NAME} drank his four cups in the Passover night and had a headache until Tabernacles. A lady saw that his face was shiny. He answered her, this woman’s spirit shall be blown away, not one of these three things applies to me, but my learning is ever present with me, as it is written, a man’s wisdom illuminates his face .

[Shabbat 8:1.9] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It happened that a mule of Rebbi’s household died and they declared its blood pure regarding the carcass. {NAME} asked {NAME}, how much? He did not answer him. He asked {NAME} who told him, it is pure up to a quartarius .
