He answered him, because my mind was not clear, as {NAME} said, your life will hang far from you , that is one who buys a year’s supply of wheat, you will be fearful night and day , that is one who buys from the Saracen, and you will not believe in your survival , that is one who buys from the retail store, and I am dependent on retail stores. What about it? “{NAME} testified about blood of carcasses that it is pure.” What means pure? It is pure in that it does not prepare, but for impurity it makes impure. [Shabbat 10:6.1] MISHNAH: He who takes off his fingernails one with the other or with his teeth, and similarly his hair, or his mustache, or his beard, and similarly the woman who braids, or who puts on kohl , or puts on make-up, {NAME} declares liable for a purification sacrifice but the Sages say because of Sabbath rest. [Shabbat 10:6.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Where do they differ? If he himself took them but if another took them they are disgusting. [Shabbat 11:1.1] MISHNAH: If one throws from a private domain to the public domain or from the public domain to a private domain, he is liable. From a private domain to another private domain when a public domain is between them, {NAME} declares him liable but the Sages declare him not liable.
[Shabbat 11:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If one throws from a private domain,” etc. Throwing is a derivative of transporting.
[Shabbat 11:1.3] Is there no difference, whether according to his opinion or that of the rabbis, only if it came to rest from a public domain into a private domain? In Rebbi’s opinion, even if it did not come to rest; in the rabbis’ opinion, only if it came to rest. For {NAME} said in the name of Rav: Rebbi declared liable only for a private domain which was roofed. The word of {NAME} implies, even if it was not roofed, for {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Only if it descended to within the partitions. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does the Mishnah follow Rebbi, since Rebbi considers partitions as solidly filled up? He said to him, it is everybody’s opinion. Could one not object that Rebbi said, if it is roofed? And you say, it is not roofed? What is the difference between bills of divorce and the Sabbath? {NAME} said, about the Sabbath it is written: You shall not do any work ; it may make itself automatically. But here he shall deliver into her hand , into her domain.
[Shabbat 11:1.4] {NAME} said, they taught this only about lower than ten [hand-breadths]. Therefore higher than ten [hand-breadths] it is forbidden. The statement of {NAME} implied that even higher than ten [hand-breadths] it is permitted. For {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} learned from the carts; and were the carts not higher than ten [hand-breadths]? Some Tannaim state “how is this”; some do not state “how is this”. In {NAME} opinion there is “how is this”, in Samuels’s opinion there is no “how is this”.
[Shabbat 11:1.5] {NAME} asked: If one threw from a private domain to the public domain and remembered when it was over the public domain, in {NAME} opinion it should be considered as if it rested in the public domain and he should be liable twice. {NAME} said, {NAME} made him liable only by means of the second private domain.
[Shabbat 11:1.6] {NAME} says in the name of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If one was standing in the public domain and threw higher than ten [hand-breadths]. One sees that if it fell down it would come to rest within four cubits he will not be liable, otherwise he will be liable. But did not {NAME} state: From public domain to public domain with a private domain in the middle, one sees that if it fell it would come to rest within four cubits he will not be liable, otherwise he will be liable. There, you are saying that public domain is not joining, but here you are saying that public domain is joining? {NAME} said, there where if it falls down the ground under it is private domain but here where if it falls down the ground under it is public domain.
[Shabbat 11:1.7] It was stated in the name of {NAME}: One who threw four cubits in the public domain is liable. {NAME} considers four cubits in the public domain a separate category of work. In {NAME} opinion there are 40 categories of work: should we not state this? We come to state only things about which everybody agrees. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} learned this from those who were sewing the gobelins, for those sewing the gobelins were throwing the needles one to another. Is that not karmelit ? {NAME} said, they were throwing sideways.
[Shabbat 11:2.1] MISHNAH: How is this? Two balconies one vis-a-vis the other in the public domain: one who hands over or throws from one to the other is not liable. If they both were on the same floor, the one who hands over is liable but the one who throws is not liable, for this was the service of the Levites. Two carts, one parallel to the other in the public domain: they used to hand over from one to the other but did not throw. The enclosure of a cistern or a rock high ten [hand-breadths] and wide four [hand-breadths]: one who takes from them or puts on them is liable, less than this he is not liable.
[Shabbat 11:2.2] HALAKHAH: 2. Rav said, here there is no “not liable” but “permitted”. In Rav’s opinion, higher than ten [hand-breadths] is permitted. In {NAME}’s opinion, higher than ten [hand-breadths] is forbidden. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: on condition that the public domain surround it from all sides. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, even from one side. From these carts. Were the carts not higher than ten [hand-breadths]? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: only by two persons. Everywhere you are saying, two persons acting together are not liable, but here you are saying, two persons acting together are liable. There is a difference, because this was the office of the Levites in the Tent of Meeting. What was the office of the Levites in the Tent of Meeting? Two carts one parallel to the other in the public domain. They were handing the planks from one to the other but not throwing. {NAME} stated, not to treat the planks with contempt.
[Shabbat 11:2.3] {NAME} said, what is standing and the hollow combine together (to ten) to four, but only if what is standing is more than the hollow. {NAME} asked, only if what is standing on each side is more? {NAME} said, it is obvious for {NAME} that what is standing on one side only does not combine; it is obvious for him that (not) one side must be more. He only questions even the second standing part.
[Shabbat 11:2.4] “The enclosure of a cistern or a rock high ten [hand-breadths] and wide four [hand-breadths].” Where do we hold? If ten high (and four wide, it is a domain by itself. Ten high) but not four wide, that is what {NAME} said in the name of Issi: If a stick stuck in the public domain ten hand-breadths high, it is permitted both ways; on condition that he not exchange. But we must deal with the case that it is neither four wide nor ten high. But did not Ḥiyya, {NAME}, say, anything which hinders access in the public domain is called karmelit ? {NAME} said, what Ḥiyya, {NAME}, said refers to the middle, but on the side the public domain invalidates it.
[Shabbat 11:2.5] {NAME} said, there is here no “not liable” but “permitted.” There, we have stated: “He who opens a boil on the Sabbath, if to make an opening he is liable, if to remove fluid he is not liable.” {NAME} said, there is here no “not liable” but “permitted.” There, we have stated: “One who catches a snake on the Sabbath, if he is active that it should not bite him he is not liable, if for medicine he is liable.” {NAME} said, there is here no “not liable” but “permitted.” There, we have stated: “About rural dishes that they are pure in a tent with a corpse but impure if carried by a sufferer from gonorrhea.” {NAME} said, this is correct. If for a need, that is what we have stated, “if for medicine he is liable.” This implies that there is here no “not liable” but “permitted.”
[Shabbat 11:3.1] MISHNAH: One who throws four cubits to a wall higher than ten hand-breadths is like one who throws in the air, lower than ten hand-breadths is like one who throws on the ground and one who throws four cubits on the ground is liable. One who threw less than four cubits and it rolled further than four cubits is not liable; one who threw more than four cubits and it rolled back within four cubits is liable.
[Shabbat 11:3.2] HALAKHAH: 3. Our Mishnah applies if there is no hole there, but if there is a hole, there is the disagreement between {NAME} and the rabbis. In the opinion of {NAME}, whether it is four by four or it is not four by four one considers the wall as carved out. In the rabbis’ opinion, if it is four by four one considers the wall as carved out, otherwise one does not consider the wall as carved out but as closed. {NAME} said, if it extends slanting. But will it not finally descend? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, explain it that it was a soft fig cake and it stuck. {NAME} asked before {NAME}, does this not imply that the declivity of a terrace belongs to the level below? He said to him, there the vegetables profit from the terrace but here people rub it and it falls down. If it would say, if there is a hole [in the wall] and it profits from the hole just as vegetables profit from the terrace, you would be justified.
[Shabbat 11:3.3] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If the place was inclined, as we have stated, “one who threw more than four cubits and it rolled beyond four cubits is liable.” There came {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, only if it came to rest.
[Shabbat 11:4.1] MISHNAH: One who throws four cubits in the ocean is not liable. If there was a shallow spot in the water and a public thoroughfare passed through it, one who throws four cubits into it is liable. What is a shallow spot in the water? Less than ten hand-breadths. Shallow water and a public thoroughfare passed through it: one who throws four cubits in it is liable.
[Shabbat 11:4.2] HALAKHAH: 4. Not only four cubits in the sea, but even if he threw across the entire sea he is not liable, since any sea is called karmelit .
[Shabbat 11:4.3] And why was it stated twice? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, if there were two shallows, one which was used as a thoroughfare and one used by the public only in case of emergency. That you should not say, since the public are using it only in case of emergency it is not public domain but private domain, therefore it was necessary to say that it is public domain.
[Shabbat 11:5.1] MISHNAH: He who throws from the sea to dry land, or from dry land to the sea, of from the sea to a ship, or from a ship to the sea, or from one ship to another is not liable. If ships are tied to one another one carries from one to the other; if they are not tied to one another, even though they be surrounded, one does not carry from one to the other.
[Shabbat 11:5.2] HALAKHAH: 5. {NAME} said, it they are tied together with bast. {NAME} said, only if they made an eruv . {NAME}, {NAME}, both in the name of {NAME}. One said, if the distance between them is less than four; but the other said, even if the distance between them is four. We did not know who said what. Since {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, even if they are not ten [hand-breadths] high, it is he who said, if the distance between them is less than four [hand-breadths].
[Shabbat 11:5.3] They wanted to say, he who said, if the distance between them is less than four [hand-breadths], even if they are not ten [hand-breadths] high. He who said, if they are ten [hand-breadths] high, even if the distance between them is four. {NAME} said, only if the airspace of karmelit be within ten [hand-breadths].
[Shabbat 11:5.4] “From a ship in the sea higher than ten hand-breadths one moves neither from it to the sea nor from the sea into it. {NAME} says, if its draught was more than ten hand-breadths but it does not extend higher than ten hand-breadths above the water one moves from it to the sea but not from the sea into it.” {NAME} said that {NAME} asked, why from it to the sea? Because it is not ten high. If it is so, even from the sea into it! Why from the sea into it is forbidden? Because it is ten deep. If it is so, even from it to the sea! {NAME} said, why is it permitted from it to the sea? Because of danger.
[Shabbat 11:5.5] From a rock in the sea higher than ten hand-breadths one transports neither from it to the sea nor from the sea onto it. If it was less than this it is permitted. What is the difference between a rock and a ship? A ship rises and falls; a rock stays in its place. But is it not karmelit ? Is it permitted to move on karmelit only four cubits? {NAME} said, it refers to the beginning: “from a rock in the sea higher than ten hand-breadths one moves neither from it to the sea nor from the sea onto it.” If it was higher it becomes like a fence made for agriculture where inside one is permitted to transport only four cubits. If it was lower one transports from it to the sea and from the sea onto it, and one transports up to two bet se’ah . {NAME} asked, two adjacent karmeliot , may one transport from one to the other? {NAME} said, since the sea surrounds it from all sides it is considered as a single karmelit .
[Shabbat 11:5.6] {NAME} said, on a board outside the ship which is not four wide one may sit and provide for his needs on the Sabbath. {NAME} said, if he had said an open box it would have been correct. {NAME} said, one who wants to provide for a boat makes outside of three [hand-breadths] a plank which is not four [hand-breadths] wide and one considers it as if partitions rose. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because any three [hand-breadths] which are close to a partition are as if of the partition. {NAME} commanded {NAME}, who was a mariner, to make for himself a deficient container.
[Shabbat 11:6.1] MISHNAH: One who throws and remembers before it leaves his hand, if another person caught it, or a dog caught it, or it was burned, he is not liable. If one threw with the intention of causing an injury whether on a human or an animal and he remembered before it caused an injury, he is not liable. This is the principle: All who are liable for a purification sacrifice are liable only if beginning and end were in error. If the beginning was unintentional but the end criminal or the beginning criminal and the end unintentional they are not liable unless beginning and end be unintentional.
[Shabbat 11:6.2] HALAKHAH: 6 So is the Mishnah: “he acted intentionally.” This is difficult. If somebody shot an arrow intending to kill a person, he was warned, and changed his intention; is that anything? Finally you have to say that it was intentional.
[Shabbat 11:6.3] {NAME} said, unintentionally a prohibition, intentionally a prohibition. {NAME} said, unintentionally extirpation, intentionally extirpation. {NAME} stated, a support of {NAME}: He blasphemes the Eternal and will be extirpated . Think of it; even if he was intentional in a matter of extirpation and he was warned and is being flogged, may he bring a sacrifice? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If he was unintentional about fat but intentional about the purification sacrifice one warns him and he is flogged.
[Shabbat 11:6.4] It was stated: One experiments neither with fat nor with incest or adultery. One who experiments on the Sabbath is not liable, with fat or with incest or adultery is liable. How is this? If he said, “am going to harvest the volume half of a dried fig” and then he harvested the volume of a dried fig, he is not liable. “I am going to eat half the volume of an olive” and ate the volume of an olive; he is liable. “I am going to arouse myself by her” and then touched her; he is liable.
[Shabbat 12:1.1] MISHNAH: How much would a builder build to become liable? One who builds anything. One who chisels stone, and one who hits with a hammer or a hatchet, or who drills anything is liable. This is the principle: Anybody who performs work on the Sabbath and whose work has permanence is liable. {NAME} says, also one who hits with the back of his hammer on the anvil during work is liable because he improves the work.
[Shabbat 12:1.2] HALAKHAH: “How much would a builder build to become liable,” etc. What building was at the Sanctuary? They were putting the planks on top of the bases. But was this not temporary? {NAME} says, because they were camping and travelling by the Word, it was as though permanent. {NAME} said, since the Holy One, praise to Him, has promised them that He would bring them into the Land, it is as if it were permanent. This implies, even from the side. This implies even if it was put on top of something else. Does it imply that building on implements is building? The bases are like soil.
[Shabbat 12:1.3] It was stated: “If one brings the stone and another one the mortar, he who brings the mortar is liable. {NAME} says, both are liable.” {NAME} is of the opinion that stone without mortar is building. Everybody agrees that if one put up mortar first and someone then brought stone he is liable. “The builder who set the stone on top of the row is liable.” For whom is this needed? For the rabbis. One who put up planks or one who put up adobe walls is liable because of building.
[Shabbat 12:1.4] He who hollows out cliffs, cavities, pillars, millstones, or splits mosaic stones, splits blocks, is liable because of chiseling. One who puts together a Galilean bed is liable because of building. {NAME} said, he only is like one who takes a brick and puts it on bricks on the Sabbath. {NAME} instructed the Head of the Captivity to disassemble a composite table on the Sabbath. He said, {NAME} was with him. {NAME} heard it and said, the one who instructed him did not study or serve. {NAME} said, the one who instructed him instructed following {NAME}, as it was stated: Planking of a ship, or of a crib, and the posts of a bed, and the leg of a table, and the handle on the top of a knife one shall not return but if one returned he is not liable. But if one pushed in he is liable. {NAME} said, if they were loose he removes and returns. It was stated: “Stuck together they are a connection for impurity and sprinkling; nailed together they are a connection for impurity but not for sprinkling. Those which may be taken apart and put together again are connections neither for impurity nor for sprinkling.” And here, you are saying so? There normally they are fixed; if not fixed there is no connection. But here sticking together is the end of its manufacture.
[Shabbat 12:1.5] It was stated: “{NAME} said, one who assembles a curved horn is liable, with a straight horn he is not liable. {NAME} said, for the arms of a candelabra he is liable; for a hunter’s (whitewasher’s) rod he is not liable.” Why is he liable for the arms of a candelabra? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} and {NAME} both say, because of building. If he would come and protest, his protest would be (invalid). “If somebody tears into skin in the form of writing he is liable, if somebody sketches on skin in the form of writing it he is not liable.” “{NAME} told them, did not {NAME} only in this way bring magic formulas from Egypt? [Shabbat 12:4.4] He shall write , not engrave. And he shall write , not dropping points. He shall write , not pouring. He shall write , not engrave; some Tannaïm state, he even may engrave. Rab Ḥisda said, he who says not to engrave, if the writing stands out as on a denar. He who says even to engrave, as on a writing tablet. And he shall write , not dropping points; {NAME} and {NAME}: One said, if he did not connect the points; the other said, even if he connected the points. And he shall write , not pouring. {NAME} said, those Orientals are very sophisticated. If one of them wants to write a secret letter to another, he writes with juice of gall-nuts. The recipient pours ink without gall over it, which is absorbed at the place of writing. If one did that on the Sabbath, what? {NAME} and {NAME} both said, only if he wrote ink on ink and vermilion on vermilion. But if he wrote ink on vermilion or vermilion on ink, he is liable. {NAME} in the name of the rabbis there: He is liable twice, for erasing and for writing.
[Shabbat 12:5.1] MISHNAH: If he wrote with fluid of drinks, with fruit juice, with road dust, with scribe’s dust, or with anything which is not permanent, he is not liable. With the back of his hand, with his foot, with his mouth, with his elbow; if he wrote one letter adjacent to existing writing, wrote over existing writing, intended to write ח and wrote זז, one on the ground and one on a beam, on two walls of a house or two leaves of a wooden tablet if they cannot be read together, he is not liable. If he wrote one letter as abbreviation, {NAME} declares liable but the Sages declare not liable.

There he says, it is not writing. But here, he says, it is writing. They objected to him according to his opinion. According to your opinion, since you say that it is writing, but this is not preferable. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} did not say so, but that {NAME} argument seems inverted. There he says, it is not preferable, therefore the writing is writing; but here he says, writing on top of writing is not writing. What is writing on top of writing? One higher than the other.
[Shabbat 12:5.3] What is {NAME} reason? From one letter one may infer several letters.

[Shabbat 12:6.2] HALAKHAH: 6. It is difficult for {NAME}. [Shabbat 13:1.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, he who weaves three threads to start or one on the weave is liable. But the Sages say, whether at the beginning or at the end its measure is two threads.

To a small belt where he is liable if he wove two threads in the width of three spaces.” And with woolen warp it is as at the start, and this cloth even at the end it is weave, and this veil even at the end it is weave.
[Shabbat 13:1.4] Everybody agrees that if he writes a word only at the moment when he finishes. “One who wrote one letter to complete a word or one letter to complete a scroll is liable.” One who wrote one letter on a weekday and one letter on the Sabbath, {NAME} makes him liable for a purification sacrifice but {NAME} declares him not liable. [Shabbat 13:5.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, one who catches a bird for a cage or a deer for a house is liable, but the Sages say, a bird for a cage and a deer for a garden, or a courtyard, or a vivarium. {NAME} says, not all vivaria are equal. [Shabbat 14:4.11] {NAME} said, a baraita implies that one does not heal through spilling blood, as we have stated there: “If most of his body was outside one does not touch him, for one does not push aside one life before another life.” Not only if one would say, kill this person, but even if he told him, injure that person. It was stated, a Gentile against a Jew, is prohibited; a Jew against a Gentile is permitted. {NAME} asked, may one save the life of an adult with the life of a minor? {NAME} objected, did we not state, “If most of his body was outside one does not touch him, for one does not push aside one life before another life”? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, there it is different for it is not known who is endangering whom.

[Shabbat 15:1.1] MISHNAH: The following are the knots for which one is liable: a camel driver’s knot and a mariner’s knot. Just as one is liable for knotting them so he is liable for untying them. {NAME} says, one is never liable for a knot which one can untie with one hand.
[Shabbat 15:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The following are the knots,” etc. What tying was in the Tabernacle? They were tying down the ropes. But was this not temporary? {NAME} says, because they were travelling and camping by the Word, was it not permanent? {NAME} said, since the Holy One, praise to Him, has promised them that he will bring them into the Land, it is as if it were temporary. {NAME} said, they learned it from the gobelin needle-workers. If a thread broke, he was tying it. If it broke again, it was impossible to make many knots but he would untie the first one. {NAME} said, an expert tailor merges the two heads. And where was this said? As {NAME} said, they learned it from the weavers of the gobelins. What is the reason? The length of one gobelin , that it should be an entity. If [a thread] broke, he was tying it. When he came to the weave, he untied it and brought it in. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even on its warp there was neither knot nor connection.
[Shabbat 15:1.3] {NAME} stated, a basket of palm leaves for dates or a plate of palm leaves one may tear and open, only one may not tie.
[Shabbat 15:2.1] MISHNAH: But there are knots for which one is not liable as one is for a camel driver’s knot and a mariner’s knot. A woman may knot the openings of her garment, and the threads of the hair net, of the belt, and laces of shoe and sandal, wine and oil skins, and of a meat pot. {NAME} said, one may tie in front of an animal that it should not leave; one may tie a pail to a belt but not to a rope, but {NAME} permits it. {NAME} stated a principle: One is never liable for a knot which is not permanent.
[Shabbat 15:2.2] HALAKHAH: 2. {NAME} said, if one opens the hem which is connected to the garment. {NAME} said, if one opens a [split] garment which is made like two sheets. If shoe or sandal laces were dislocated, one removes and returns them, only one may not knot them. If its nose was dislocated, there are Tannaim who state, it is permitted to put it back, and there are Tannaim who state, it is forbidden to put it back. They wanted to say, he who says that it is permitted, if there is one hole; he who says that it is forbidden, if there are two holes. {NAME} said, in both cases it is following him who says that there are two holes. What about it? He who says that it is permitted, if they are loose; he who says that it is forbidden, if they are squeezed.
[Shabbat 15:2.3] Do they disagree with {NAME}? Since it was stated: “The Sages agree with {NAME} about seals in the ground that one pushes aside, and removes, and unties, and cuts. On the Sabbath one pushes aside but one does not remove nor untie nor cut. For implements on the Sabbath it is permitted; it is not necessary to mention on a holiday.” This implies that they do not disagree with {NAME}. {NAME} said, the Mishnah is about a rope hanging down, a rope tied hanging down.
[Shabbat 15:2.4] “To a belt but not to a rope, but {NAME} permits it.” Therefore the rabbis do not? But because the earlier statement was in the name of {NAME}, so also this is in the name of {NAME}: “{NAME} stated a principle: One is never liable for a knot which is not permanent.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: So is the Mishnah: One is never liable for a knot which is not permanent and which is temporary.
[Shabbat 15:3.1] MISHNAH: One may fold garments even four or five times and make the beds from Friday Night to the Sabbath Day, but not from Sabbath for after the Sabbath. {NAME} says, one folds garments and makes beds from the day of Atonement to the Sabbath. The fats of the Sabbath are brought on the Day of Atonement but those of the Day of Atonement are not brought on the Sabbath. {NAME} says, neither are those of the Sabbath brought on the Day of Atonement nor those of the Day of Atonement on the Sabbath.
[Shabbat 15:3.2] HALAKHAH: 3. In the House of {NAME} they said, folding by two persons is forbidden. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: On the Sabbath, two together may not fold. If one folds on a footstool it is as if two persons were folding. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Sabbaths and holidays were given only for eating and drinking. Since this mouth [is bothersome] (is smelling), they permitted him to be occupied with words of the Torah. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Sabbaths and holidays were given only for being occupied with words of the Torah. A baraita supports either one of them: What does one do? Either he sits down and eats or he sits and studies words of the Torah. One verse says, it is a Sabbath for the Eternal , and another verse says, an assembly for the Eternal , your God . How is that? Give part of it to the study of Torah and part to eat and to drink. {NAME} said, a Sabbath for the Eternal , rest like the Eternal. Since the Eternal rested from saying, you also should rest from saying.
[Shabbat 15:3.3] It happened that a pious person went to promenade in his vineyard on the Sabbath when he saw there a breach which he decided to repair after the Sabbath. He said, because I wanted to repair I shall never repair it. What did the Holy One, praise to Him, do for him? He prepared for him a tent of caper bush which grew there and mended it. From it he was fed and from there was his sustenance all his days.
[Shabbat 15:3.4] {NAME} said, with difficulty they permitted greeting on the Sabbath. {NAME} said, when {NAME} saw that his mother enjoyed talking much, he said to her, mama, today is Sabbath. It was stated: It is forbidden to pray for his needs on the Sabbath. {NAME} asked {NAME}, may one say, “shepherd us, provide for us”? He answered him, these are formulas of benediction.
[Shabbat 15:3.5] It was stated: One rinses cups, pots, and plates from Friday Night to the morning, from morning to noon, from noon to afternoon. After afternoon it is forbidden, only for cups it is permitted since drinking has no fixed times. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: An intelligent woman rinses a cup here, a pot there, a plate there; the result is that she waters down her house on the Sabbath.
[Shabbat 15:3.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, if the Day of Atonement falls to be on the Sabbath one does not blow, if after the Sabbath one does not make havdalah . Why? Following {NAME}. But following {NAME} he makes havdalah since the fats of the Sabbath are brought on the Day of Atonement. {NAME} said before {NAME}, even according to {NAME} he should not make havdalah , since one only makes havdalah to permit things which were forbidden to him. If he would burn the fats of the Sabbath on the Sabbath, would that not be permitted? {NAME} {NAME} said, he should make havdalah since by it he permits to rinse pickled and parboiled [food]. {NAME} said, he only is permitted to rinse pickled and parboiled [food] from the time of afternoon prayers or later. Could he make havdalah from the time of afternoon prayers or later? As you take it, there is no cup, there is no light, how can he make havdalah ? {NAME} said, in prayer.
[Shabbat 16:1.1] MISHNAH: One saves all holy Scriptures from a fire, whether they be used for reading or not used for reading; even though they be written in any language they have to be hidden. Why does one not read in them? Because of neglect of the House of Study.
[Shabbat 16:1.2] HALAKHAH: “All holy Scriptures,” etc. What means “whether they are used for reading or not used for reading”? Whether they contain errors or do not contain errors. Was it not stated: If a scroll contains two or three errors on every page, one corrects it and reads from it; with four one does not read from it. Since we have stated, “why does one not read in them? Because of neglect of the House of Study;” this implies that there is a difference between Torah and Prophets and Hagiographa.
[Shabbat 16:1.3] One does not save from a fire. For him who says, they render hands impure, one saves them from a fire; but for him who says, they do not render hands impure, one does not save them from a fire. They objected: Is there not a Hebrew book which was written in Aramaic; it will not render hands impure but one saves it from a fire, since we have stated: “even though they are written in any language they have to be hidden.” The Mishnah follows {NAME}, since {NAME} said, nothing forbidden only rabbinically stands in the way of Holy Scriptures. Do they disagree? There it is because of their degradation, but here everybody agrees that one saves them from a fire. For whom is it needed? For {NAME}. Even though {NAME} said, “also Hagiographa they permitted only that they could be written in Greek,” would he agree here that one saves them from a fire? “It happened that Rabban [Simeon ben] Gamliel was supervising builders on the the Temple Mount when he an Aramaic version of Job was brought to him. He told the builder to hide it under a row of stones.”
[Shabbat 16:1.4] Even though they said, one reads Hagiographa only after the afternoon prayers, nevertheless one studies and preaches about them. If he needs it, he takes and checks. An example: Rebbi, the Elder {NAME}, and {NAME} were sitting and explaining the plain sense of a scroll of Lamentations on a Ninth of Av which fell on a Sabbath (after the afternoon prayers.) They left over one alphabetic poem. They said, we shall come tomorrow and finish it. When Rebbi was on the way home, he hurt his finger and recited about himself, many are the evildoer’s hurts . [The Elder] {NAME} said to him, it is our fault that this happened to you, as it is written, our spirit , the Eternal’s anointed, was caught by their corruption . {NAME} told him, that could have been said about us if we had not occupied ourselves with it; so much more since we did occupy ourselves with it. He went home, put a dry sponge on it and tied it from the outside with bast. {NAME} said, from this we learned three things: A sponge does not heal but protects; bast is prepared, and one recites from Hagiographa only after afternoon prayers.
[Shabbat 16:1.5] Then at a place where there is a House of Study one should not read, at a place where there is no House of Study one should read? You only have what {NAME} stated, as {NAME} stated, why may one only read Hagiographa after afternoon prayers? Because of persons’ documents. Because if you were telling him that it is permitted, then he would say, there is nothing wrong if I would occupy myself with my documents. Since you are telling him that it is forbidden, then he will say, since Hagiographa are forbidden, so much more private documents. This implies that Mishnah has precedence over Bible. This supports what {NAME} stated, as {NAME} stated, he who studies the written Torah does himself good that is not so good; he who studies Mishnah is occupied in an endeavor which deserves reward; he who studies Talmud could not endeavor anything greater than this, always a person should pursue Mishnah more than Talmud. {NAME} said, this was before Rebbi incorporated most of the Mishnah in the Talmud, but since Rebbi incorporated most of the Mishnah in the Talmud, a person should pursue Talmud more than Mishnah.
[Shabbat 16:1.6] “One does not save benedictions which contain pentateuchal materials from a fire. Because of this, they said: Writers of benedictions are burners of the Torah. It happened that there was a writer of benedictions; {NAME} went to check him out. When he noticed {NAME} steps, he took a bundle of benedictions and threw them into a bowl of water. In the following formulation he spoke to him: The punishment for the later deed is worse than the one for the earlier.” {NAME} said, one who writes down sermons has no part, one who preaches them is going to be singed, one who listens to him is not rewarded.
[Shabbat 16:1.7] {NAME} said, I never looked into a book of sermon concepts, except that once I looked, and I found written there: The 175 paragraphs where in the Torah is written speech, saying, commandment, correspond to the years of our father Abraham, as it is written, you took gifts from Man , and it is written, the great Man among giants . The 147 songs written in Psalms correspond to the years of our father Jacob. This teaches that all praises by which Israel praise the Holy One, praise to Him, correspond to the years of Jacob, as it is said, You are Holy , throning over the praises of Israel . The 123 times Israel answer “halleluiah” correspond to the years of Aaron, Halleluiah , praise God by His holy one , Aaron his holy one, for Aaron , the Eternal’s holy one . Nevertheless I was frightened in the night.
[Shabbat 16:1.8] {NAME} saw a book of agadah . He said, even if what is written in there is good, the hand who wrote it should be amputated. A person told him, it was written by X’s father. He said, I was saying, the hand who wrote it should be amputated. That happened to him, as an error which is coming out from the ruler’s mouth .
[Shabbat 16:1.9] “Gospels and books of heretics, some Tannaim say, one tears out the Names and burns them; some Tannaim say, one burns them with their Names. {NAME} said, I would hit my sons; if they came into my house I would burn them together with their Names. For if a persecutor would persecute me I would seek asylum in a pagan temple but would not seek asylum in heretics’ houses, for the worshippers of idolatry do not know about Him, how could they disavow Him? But the heretics know Him and disavow Him; about them David said, Your haters , o Eternal, I shall hate , etc. This homily they preached: If in order to bring peace between a man and his wife the verse commands that the Name written in holiness be erased, it is only logical that the books of heretics which propagate ill will and quarrel between Israel and their Father in Heaven should be burned with their Names.”
[Shabbat 16:2.1] MISHNAH: One saves the case of a scroll with the scroll, and the case of phylacteries with the phylacteries even if there are coins inside. Where does one save it to? To a side street which is a dead end; {NAME} says, also one open on both ends.

[Shabbat 16:3.3] It was stated: One saves an average portion for a sick person and for a child, but for a glutton according to his wont. One prepares an eruv for a sick person or a child according to their wont but for a glutton an average portion.

[Shabbat 16:4.1] MISHNAH: One saves a bag full of loaves even if it contains food for a hundred meals, and loaves of dried figs, and wine amphoras, and one says to others, come and save for yourselves. [Shabbat 16:7.1] MISHNAH: If a Gentile comes to extinguish one tells him neither to extinguish nor not to extinguish since you are not responsible for him resting. But if a minor comes to extinguish one may not listen to him since you are responsible for him resting.

[Shabbat 17:1.1] MISHNAH: All implements may be taken on the Sabbath and their doors with them, even if they were disassembled on the Sabbath; they are not similar to doors of a house because the latter are not prepared.
[Shabbat 17:1.2] HALAKHAH: “All implements may be taken on the Sabbath,” etc. There is spelled out more for doors of a house and there is spelled out more for doors of implements. There is spelled out more for doors of implements, for even if they were unhinged on the Sabbath they may be used on the Sabbath.

[Shabbat 19:5.1] MISHNAH: A baby is circumcised on the eighth day, the ninth, the tenth, the eleventh, the twelfth, no less and no more. In the normal case, on the eighth. If he was born at dusk, on the ninth. In the twilight Friday evening, on the tenth. If there is a holiday on Sunday, on the eleventh; the two days of the New Year on the twelfth. A sick baby one does not circumcise until he gets well.
[Shabbat 19:5.2] HALAKHAH: It is possible that a child is circumcised on his first day. How is this possible? If she gave birth and then converted, he is circumcised on his first day. If she converted and then gave birth, he is circumcised on his eighth day. Jacob from Kefar-Naboraia asked {NAME}, then if he was born during twilight, should he not be circumcised at twilight? He told him, if I and you were entering the same door, could we make it simultaneous?
[Shabbat 19:5.3] {NAME} said, if he runs a fever [for one hour] one waits with him one month. May one feed him with milk-substitute from heave? May one rub him with heave oil? Since it was stated: In the night of the eighth day it enters the corral to be tithed, that means that the night of the eighth is treated like the eighth day. And it was stated so: All seven days long one is permitted to feed him with milk-substitute from heave and permitted to rub him with heave oil.

[Shabbat 20:1.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, one hangs the yeast-sieve on a holiday and one uses one hanging on the Sabbath. But the Sages say, one may not hang a yeast-sieve on a holiday and may not use a hanging one on the Sabbath but one may use a hanging one on a holiday.

[Shabbat 22:1.1] MISHNAH: If an amphora broke, one saves from it food for three meals and tells others: come and save for yourselves; only one may not absorb it in a sponge. One does not squeeze fruits to extract their juice and if it seeped out by itself it is forbidden. {NAME} says, if they are solid food, what comes from them is permitted, but if they are for drinks, what comes from them is forbidden. [Shabbat 22:2.1] MISHNAH: Everything which was in hot water on Friday one soaks in hot water on the Sabbath but anything which was not in hot water on Friday one rinses in hot water on the Sabbath except for old salted fish and anchovies in salt and Spanish mackerel, for which rinsing is the end of preparation.
[Shabbat 22:3.1] MISHNAH: A person may break open an amphora to eat dried figs from it; only he may not intend to make it into a vessel. [Shabbat 22:4.1] MISHNAH: One may put food in a cistern for preservation, and potable water into bad one to cool, and cold water into hot to warm it. One whose garments became soaked on the road walks in them without worry. If he comes to an outer courtyard he puts them out to dry in the sun but not in public.
[Shabbat 22:5.1] MISHNAH: One who bathes in the waters of a cave or in the waters of Tiberias dries himself even with ten towels but may not bring them in his hand. But ten people dry with one towel their faces, and their hands, and their feet, and bring it in their hands.
[Shabbat 22:6.1] MISHNAH: One anoints and massages the belly but one does not exercise or scratch. One does not go to a mud-bath, nor does one make an emetic on the Sabbath, nor does one stretch a baby, nor set a fracture. If somebody’s hand or foot became dislocated he cannot force it back with cold water but he may wash in his usual way and if this healed him, he was healed.
[Shabbat 23:1.1] MISHNAH: A person may ask from a neighbor wine jugs and oil jugs, only he may not say to him: lend me; and similarly a woman loaves from her neighbor. If that one does not trust him he may leave his toga with him and settle the account after the Sabbath. Similarly, on a Passover eve in Jerusalem which happens on a Sabbath he leaves his toga with him, eats his Passover sacrifice, and settles the account after the holiday.
[Shabbat 23:2.1] MISHNAH: A person counts his guests and his desserts orally but not from a written list. A person may make a lottery with his children and his family on the table on condition that he not make portions large or small, because of gambling. One casts lots on sancta on the holiday but not on portions.
[Shabbat 23:3.1] MISHNAH: A person may not hire workers on the Sabbath and not say to another to hire workers for him. One does not wait for nightfall at the Sabbath boundary to hire workers and to bring produce, but one may wait for nightfall to watch and to bring produce in his hand. {NAME} formulated a principle: For anything which I am permitted to talk about I am permitted to wait for nightfall.
[Shabbat 23:4.1] MISHNAH: One waits for nightfall at the Sabbath border to oversee preparations for a wedding or preparations for a burial, to bring a casket and shrouds. If a Gentile brought fifes on the Sabbath, a Jew should not use them for dirges unless they came from a nearby place. If they made for him a casket and dug him a grave a Jew may be buried in it; but if it was made for a Jew he never should be buried in it.
[Shabbat 23:5.1] MISHNAH: One does all that is needed for a corpse, one anoints, and rinses, on condition that none of his limbs be moved. One takes away the pillow under him and lays him on sand so he can wait. One ties the jaw, not to lift it but lest it descend. Similarly, if a beam broke one supports it by a bench or the long logs of a bed-frame, not to lift it but lest it descend. One does not close the eyelids of a corpse on the Sabbath, nor on a weekday at the moment of death. Anybody who closes the eyes at the moment of death is spilling blood.
[Shabbat 24:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody is caught on the road when it gets dark, he gives his wallet to a Non-Jew; if no Non-Jew is with him he puts it on the donkey. If he comes to an outer courtyard he removes the implements which may be moved on the Sabbath. For those which may not be moved he unties the rope and the sacks fall down by themselves.
[Shabbat 24:2.1] MISHNAH: One unties bundles of straw for animals and one separates packages but not sheaves. One does not crush green stalks or carob for animals whether small or large; {NAME} permits carob for small animals.
[Shabbat 24:3.1] MISHNAH: One does not stuff a camel, nor force-feed, but puts food in its mouth. One does not stuff calves but gives food into their mouths. One hand-feeds chickens and adds water to bran but does not give water to bees and pigeons of the dovecote, but gives to geese and chicken and for Herodes pigeons.
[Shabbat 24:4.1] MISHNAH: One cuts squash for animals and a cadaver for dogs. {NAME} says, if it was not a cadaver before the Sabbath it is forbidden since it is not prepared.
[Shabbat 24:5.1] MISHNAH: One dissolves vows on the Sabbath and one may ask about vows if it is a need for the Sabbath. One plugs the skylight and measures a rag and a miqweh . [Eruvin 1:1.1] MISHNAH: An alley which is higher than twenty cubits should be reduced; {NAME} says, this is not necessary. If it is wider than ten cubits it should be reduced; if there is a door-frame even though it is wider than ten cubits there is no need to reduce.
[Eruvin 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “An alley which is higher than twenty,” etc. {NAME} said it without attribution, {NAME} in the name of Rav: The rabbis inferred it from the door of the Sanctuary, but {NAME} inferred it from the door of the Hall. An argument from the door of the Hall is sufficient only up to forty cubits, as we have stated there: “The door of the Hall was forty cubits high and twenty cubits wide.” {NAME} stated, even forty or fifty cubits; {NAME} stated, even a hundred cubits. {NAME} said, {NAME} follows his opinion and the rabbis follow their opinion, as we have stated there, “and similarly one carries under panelled bridges on the Sabbath, the words of {NAME}, but the Sages forbid it.” As you are saying there, one considers the cross-beam as if it came down and closed, here also one considers the roof as if it came down and closed. This is the opinion of {NAME} in the case of a sukkah, this is his opinion in the case of an alley. Also the opinion of the rabbis in the case of a sukkah is their opinion in the case of an alley. But they do not compare. There are items qualified for a sukkah which are disqualified for an alley and those qualified for an alley but disqualified for a sukkah. Double pointed stakes are qualified for a sukkah but disqualified for an alley, and it was stated thus: If he brought four double pointed stakes and thatched over them it is qualified as a sukkah but disqualified for an alley. That is, if they are higher by more than three [hand-breadths] than the walls of the alley. But if they are not higher by more than three [hand-breadths] than the walls of the alley it is qualified. If they are not, but if they are four [hand-breadths] wide they are qualified even if arbitrarily high. Walls may be qualified for a sukkah but disqualified for an alley, and it was stated thus: “Two regular and the third even one hand-breadth is qualified.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Two of four hand-breadths each and the third even one hand-breadth is qualified. But for an alley only if it is closed in its four directions. Wider than ten cubits is qualified for a sukkah but disqualified for an alley. “If he drew a vine or squash.” That means, up to an area of two bet se’ah. But more than an area of two bet se’ah it is a partition made for agriculture where one may transport only four cubits. If its sunshine is more than its shadow it is disqualified as sukkah but qualified for an alley. A roofed sukkah is disqualified, a roofed alley is qualified. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Not only roofed, but if he put there a cross beam four hand-breadths wide, it makes the alley permitted.
[Eruvin 1:1.3] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice does [not] follow {NAME}. If it were not so what would we say? {NAME} versus the Sages, practice should follow {NAME}? He told him, did I not say Eruvin but partitions? {NAME} shares {NAME}’s opinion. Therefore it was necessary to say that practice does not follow {NAME}.
[Eruvin 1:1.4] They only said “higher than twenty”. Therefor at the end of twenty it is qualified. This follows Rav who said that the end of measurements is for leniency; {NAME} said that the end of measurements is for restriction. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: For an alley whose beam is higher than twenty he puts another beam within twenty and this reduces to less than twenty. {NAME} said, on condition that the entire qualification beam be within twenty. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, even this comes following Rav, as Rav said that slaughter half by half is qualified, and why did they say that it is disqualified? Because of the visual impression. For if you say that he has to put it within twenty, he would put it higher than twenty.
[Eruvin 1:1.5] “It should be reduced.” How does one reduce? He makes a platform at the entrance of the alley and permits the alley. How much must it be? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Four hand-breadths for an alley. {NAME} says, one hand-breadth corresponding to the beam. The colleagues say, anything, since here is no longer a height of twenty cubits in the widths of a hand-breadth.
[Eruvin 1:1.6] If its height was less than ten hand-breadths one has to dig out. How much does he have to dig? {NAME} said, four cubits as an alley. {NAME} said, four hand-breadths as a space. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, he makes a ditch at the entrance of the alley, ten [hand-breadths] deep and four wide; this permits the alley from inside and out, on condition that it be within three [hand-breadths] of the walls of the alley. And even he who says there four, here he agrees with three. There it is outside of the alley, but here within the alley.
[Eruvin 1:1.7] If he made a stone fence at the entrance to the alley, ten [hand-breadths] high and four wide, it permits the alley from inside and out. If there had been a stone fence, if it reduces to ten hand-breadths within three it needs a beam, otherwise it does not need a beam. There are Tannaim who state, within four [cubits]. He who says, within three [cubits], the rabbis. He who says, within four [cubits], {NAME}. If there was a slope in the middle of the alley, for those at the high end it acts as a ditch, for those at the low end as a stone fence.
[Eruvin 1:1.8] “If it is wider than ten cubits it should be reduced.” How does one reduce? He puts a cross-beam on the entrance of the alley and permits the alley. This was said for width; the rabbis also apply it to height. Is it not as if opened in its length? It is turned into a porch. Rebbi permitted a porch in Bet Shearim. How many pillars did it have? {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME}, one said, six, but the other one said, eight. {NAME} said, they do not disagree. He who said six does not count the two outer ones, he who said eight does count the two outer ones. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Six is not important, eight is not important. [Eruvin 1:5.4] “Round, one considers it as if square.” Again this is {NAME}. They inferred it from the sea. He made the sea cast , ten cubits . It is impossible to say “circular” since already it was said “square”. It is impossible to say “square” since already it was said “circular”. If you said circular, it would turn out to contain 160 times the measure of purity. If you said square, it would turn out to contain 122 times the measure of purity. Therefore you have to say that the upper two cubits were circular, the lower three cubits were square and it turns out that it contained 150 times the measure of purity. One verse says, it contained 2’000 bat 204 , but another verse says, it contained a volume of 3’000 bat . It is impossible to say 2’000 since already it says 3’000 and it is impossible to say 3’000 since already it says 2’000. Therefore you have 2’000 in fluid measure which are 3’000 in dry measure. From here the Sages learned that 40 seah in fluid measure are two kor in dry measure.

[Eruvin 1:8.1] MISHNAH: If a caravan rested in an area of difficult access which they surrounded by the implements of animals one may move things inside on condition that the fence be ten hand-breadths high and the openings not be more than the built-up part. [Eruvin 1:8.3] It turns out that concerning kilaim everything less than three [hand-breadths] is considered closed. From three to four, if what is standing is more than what is torn down it is permitted, but if what is torn down is more than what is standing, it is forbidden. From four [hand-breadths] to ten [cubits], if what is standing is more than what is torn down, it is permitted; but if what is torn down is more than what is standing it is permitted where it is standing, forbidden where it is torn down.
[Eruvin 1:8.4] Concerning the Sabbath, everything less than three [handbreadths] is considered closed. From three to four, and from four [hand-breadths] to ten [cubits], it is permitted if what is standing is more than what is torn down, but forbidden if what is torn down is more than what is standing. [Eruvin 1:9.2] HALAKHAH: “One may surround by three ropes,” etc. {NAME} said, they said this only about ten or more than ten; therefore no less than ten. But was it stated thus? If one brought a wall of seven hand-breadths and raised it less than three from the ground, is it permitted? There you are saying, everything less than three [handbreadths] is considered closed, and here you should be saying, everything less than three [handbreadths] is considered closed. If you want to object, object to the following: If one brought a wall of slightly more than (four) [seven] hand-breadths and raised it less than two hand-breadths from the ground, should it come following what {NAME} said, what is standing and empty space combine for four hand-breadths, on condition that what is standing be more than the empty space.
[Eruvin 1:9.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If one put in four poles at the four corners of a vineyard and connected them with a bast string on top, this saves as a symbolic fence. {NAME} said, the rules of separation walls for the Sabbath are the rules for kilaim . {NAME} said, it happened that {NAME} went to {NAME} at Nagnigar; he showed him a field called bet ḥaverata whose wall had parts torn down more than ten [cubits] wide. He took wood to insert, forked poles to insert, until he reduced to less than ten. He said, just like that is a dividing wall for the Sabbath. {NAME} said, {NAME} agrees that on the Sabbath, a symbolic fence does not save more than ten. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says so: “One may surround by three ropes one higher than the other.” If you say that the string saves, one rope would be sufficient.
[Eruvin 1:9.4] {NAME} said: {NAME} asked, what do you say about that symbolic fence, on top or at the sides? If you say on top, so much more on the sides. If you say on the sides, then not on the top. If you say on the top, {NAME} said it correctly. If you say from the sides, {NAME} did not say anything. What do you want to say, if on top, it must be on top. Or from the sides, it is on the sides. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it if they were strung on forked poles.
[Eruvin 1:9.5] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: In height even one hundred cubits. {NAME} said, that is, for kilaim , but as regards the Sabbath, a symbolic fence should not be better than a beam. {NAME} said (in the name of Rebbi), it is the same for kilaim and Sabbath. According to Rebbi [Yose], what is the difference between a beam and a symbolic fence? A beam saves in one direction; a symbolic fence does not save from one side unless it is used to close all four sides;. This follows what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: A symbolic fence does not save unless it seals all four sides.
[Eruvin 1:9.6] {NAME} said, it is forbidden to carry under the four-gated bowers in vineyards since they form the end of the roof and the end of a roof cannot save as a symbolic fence. {NAME} said, a case came before {NAME} of four pillars and on them four beams; he permitted to carry under them because of a symbolic fence. {NAME} and {NAME} asked before {NAME}, does a symbolic fence save in a sukkah ? He said to them, a symbolic fence saves in a sukkah . Does the end of the roofing save in a sukkah ? He said to them, the end of the roofing does not save in a sukkah . What is the difference between them? One is made for the purpose, the other one is [not] made for the purpose. {NAME} said, all these things are for discussion’s sake, but as far as teaching, it is forbidden to teach it. If this is forbidden for the minor commandment of sukkah , so much more for the strict commandment of Sabbath! {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is not the Tanna, according to whom a symbolic fence saves, {NAME}? He said to him, that is the Tanna.

To disassemble tents in a camp, as it was stated: “ Tents in a camp need an eruv , tents of a caravan do not need an eruv . “{NAME} says, also they may camp anywhere and at the place where they are killed they are buried, lest you say that they should be treated like war dead.” There are Tannaim who state that it is forbidden to remove them; there are Tannaim who state that it is permitted to remove them. He who said that it is permitted to remove them, if they are together; he who said that it is forbidden to remove them, if they are dispersed. Why did they have to return sneaking? Because of the enemies. {NAME} in the name of Rav: Just as they are exempt from four matters when they are marching out, so they are exempt from four matters when they are returning.

[Eruvin 2:1.5] “If one big stone was there one sees that if it is split and there be six [hand-breadths] in both directions it is considered a double column.” Some Tannaim state, if it is hollowed out. They wanted to say that he who says, if it is hollowed out, measures from the inside while he who says, if it is split, measures from the outside. {NAME} said, would you not let it stand if it was like garlic skin? This implies that both he who says that it is split as also he who says it is hollowed out measures from the inside. He who says, if it is hollowed out, if it is round; he who says, if it is split, if it is square. You should know that it is so since one Tanna said to the other, the only difference between my formulation and yours is that you are speaking of a round one but I about a square one.
[Eruvin 2:1.6] If there was a ditch ten [hand-breadths] deep and four wide, and it extends six in each direction, it is judged to be a double column. Not only a ditch but also a heap. Partially a ditch and partially a heap? If there were five sticks with less than three [hand-breadths] between them which together cover six [hand-breadths] in each direction, they are judged to be a double column. If there were three and he tied bast on top, would this save as symbolic fence? Does not a symbolic fence save only if it is proven from each side? Then what was tied around is as if blocked. Similar to what you are saying there, one sees that if it is split and there would be six [hand-breadths] in both directions it is considered a double column, could you say the same here? There would you not let it stand if it was like garlic skin; here what can you say? If you would say so you would abrogate the rules of symbolic fences.
[Eruvin 2:1.7] A wall, and a tree, and a copse of reeds are counted as double columns. If they grew by themselves one may carry there up to an area of two bet se’ah . If he planted them with his hands one may carry there even one or two bet kor . If there was one large well and he made [the double columns] for one half but not for the other half. For the half for which he made it it is permitted, for the half for which he did not make it it is forbidden. If there were two, could the space in-between be considered for both sides? What is his problem? If both were used to fill; but if only one was used to fill it is usable for both sides.

[Eruvin 4:9.1] MISHNAH: If somebody started to go to another town for which one makes an eruv but another person intercepted him, he is permitted to go but the remainder of the town is forbidden, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, anybody who could have made an eruv but did not make the eruv is a donkey driver-camel driver.
[Eruvin 4:9.2] HALAKHAH: Paragraph. “If somebody started to go to another town.” One may give this two interpretations. If he said, I shall make an eruv for you and your townspeople, and made the eruv for his townspeople but not for him. He is forbidden to go in that direction but permitted all other directions in his town; they are permitted to go in that direction but forbidden all other directions in their town. One may give it another interpretation. If he said, I shall make an eruv for you and your townspeople and made the eruv neither for his townspeople nor for him. He is permitted to go in that direction for his feet already acquired for him the day before; they are forbidden to go in that direction but permitted all other directions in his town.

[Eruvin 5:1.12] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav. If a city is built on the banks of a river, if between it and the river are four hand-breadths one measures from the wall, three one measures from the outer bank of the river unless the river be [wide] more than 70 and remainder. [Eruvin 5:1.14] “One makes it rectangular in the four directions of the world, so that its Western direction be in the West of the world and its Southern direction be in the South of the world. {NAME} said, if he does not know how to determine the directions let him go and learn from the solstices. From the place where the sun rises on the day of the summer solstice to the place where it rises on the day of the winter solstice is Eastern direction; from the place where the sun goes down on the day of the winter solstice to the place where it goes down on the day of the summer solstice is Western direction; the remainder are North and South. That is what is written, it goes to the South and turns to the North. It goes to the South during the day and turns to the North during the night; all around in circles goes the wind, to its circuits returns the wind , these are Eastern and Western directions.”
[Eruvin 5:1.15] One understands this for Shilo and the Temple, as {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, how much did the earlier prophets exercise themselves to make the Eastern gate so that the sun be exactly on it on the summer solstice and the winter solstice. It was called by seven names: the gate “desist”, the foundation gate, the sun gate, the entrance gate, the middle gate the new gate, the upper gate. The gate “desist” since there the impure separate; that is what is written, desist, impure one calls them . The foundation gate, for there practice was founded. The sun gate, since it was directed towards sunrise, as you are saying, Who says to the sun not to shine . The entrance gate, since it serves as entry and exit. The middle gate, since it is fixed between two gates. The new gate, for there the Sopherim renewed practice. The upper gate, since it was higher than the courtyard of Israel and the courtyard of women. The Temple had another distinction.

[Eruvin 6:8.4] It is obvious that “one makes eruv for courtyards and participates in alleys. If one makes eruv for courtyards, if they want to participate in the alley they may not participate. But if they participated in an alley, if they want to make it eruv they may do so.” And it was stated: “One makes eruv and participates simultaneously, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, one makes eruv for courtyards or participates in alleys.” If they made eruv for the courtyards, they are permitted in the courtyards and forbidden in the alley. But if they participated in the alley they are permitted here and there. He told them, also you will cause the rules of eruv to be forgotten among us, for the relationship of alley to courtyards is like the one of courtyards to houses.
[Eruvin 6:8.5] How many courtyards must be in an alley? Rav and {NAME} both say no less than two. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even a courtyard on one side and a house on the other, a house on one side and a store on the other. {NAME} asked: An alley has no less than two courtyards, does a courtyard have no less than two houses? An alley whose length and width are equal is not permitted by lath or beam but by planks like a courtyard. {NAME} asked Rav, by how much must their length exceed their width? He told him, anything. The dwellers in the Land of Israel make them square.

[Eruvin 6:10.2] HALAKHAH: Paragraph. “If one of the outer courtyard forgot,” etc. If one of the outer courtyard forgot and did not make the eruv , the outer one is forbidden since they do not have an eruv ; the inner one is forbidden because they put their eruv at a forbidden place. If one of the inner courtyard forgot and did not make the eruv , the inner one is forbidden since they do not have an eruv ; the outer one is forbidden because they put their eruv at a forbidden place, since the right of access makes it forbidden. “If one of the outer courtyard forgot and did not make the eruv ;” one understands that the outer one is forbidden because they have no eruv . Why the inner one? Because they put their eruv at a forbidden place. But if they did not put their eruv at a forbidden place? But because the right of access makes it forbidden. There is no right of access which makes it forbidden! {NAME} said, because they put it at one place they all were made one domain.

Do not two different domains use the same domain? Explain it if there were houses on one side.
[Eruvin 8:7.3] The following is obvious: If it is ten deep but not four wide one may move and fill. If it was four wide but not ten deep it is obvious that one may move. [Eruvin 8:9.1] MISHNAH: If a courtyard be less that four [by four] cubits one may not pour water in it on the Sabbath unless one make for it a sump containing two seah below the hole, whether inside or outside; only that outside one has to cover but inside one does not have to cover. {NAME} says, one may pour water on the Sabbath into a sewer which is covered for four cubits in the public domain, but the Sages are saying, even from a roof or a courtyard 100 cubits [wide] one may not pour into the sewer but one may pour onto the roof and it flows down into the sewer. [Eruvin 10:1.1] MISHNAH: He who finds tefillin brings them in pair by pair; {NAME} says, two by two. When has this been said? For used ones, but for new ones he is not liable. You have only what {NAME} said: Everything that is not clear one supports from many places.

[Eruvin 10:3.1] MISHNAH: He who reads a scroll on the threshold and the scroll rolls away from his hand, rolls it back to himself. [Eruvin 10:3.2] HALAKHAH: Paragraph. The Mishnah: On the threshold it is permitted, but outside the threshold it is forbidden. Explain it that he was sitting there reading when it still was daytime, or he forgot and took it out. Before it reaches ten hand-breadths he rolls it back to himself. [Pesachim 1:1.1] MISHNAH: At nightfall of the Fourteenth one checks leavened matter by candle light. A place into which no leavened matter is introduced does not need checking. And where did they say two rows in the cellar? A place where one introduces leavened matter. The House of Shammai are saying two rows in the front of the entire cellar, but the House of Hillel are saying the outermost two rows which are the uppermost.
[Pesachim 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “At nightfall of the fourteenth,” etc. It is written: You shall guard the mazzot, because on this same day I took out your multitudes from the Land of Egypt. On the first, on the fourteenth of the month, in the evening, you shall eat mazzot, etc. Where do we hold? If for eating mazzah, is it not already written, seven days you shall eat mazzot ? Or if to say that one starts on the Fourteenth, is it not written, until the twenty-first of the month ? But if it is not needed as a reference to the eating of mazzah, take it as a reference to the elimination of leavened matter.
[Pesachim 1:1.3] Why by candlelight? {NAME} said, because a candle permits checking everywhere. Why in the night? {NAME} said, because checking with a candle is exact only during night time. {NAME} did not say so: And guard this day for your generations as an eternal law , see to it that day and night be guarded. Then should one not start on the Thirteenth that day and night be guarded? He also agrees with the statement of {NAME}. Then should one start in the evening of the Thirteenth? If so, he could even check on the beginning of the month.
[Pesachim 1:1.4] {NAME} said that {NAME} asked: May one check by the light of torches? What is his problem? Because their light is unsteady. {NAME} is consistent since {NAME} said, because a candle permits checking everywhere. [ Even though it is not proof of the matter, it is an allusion to the matter: It shall be on that day that I shall search Jerusalem by candles . But some want to say,] one can understand it from the following: A candle of the Eternal is a person’s soul, it searches all rooms of the body .
[Pesachim 1:1.5] {NAME} said, the Mishnah implies that checking during daytime is called checking, as we have stated: “{NAME} says, one checks at nightfall of the Fourteenth, and on the Fourteenth, and at the moment of elimination.” Not only {NAME} but even the rabbis, as we have stated: “If he did not check at nightfall of the Fourteenth he shall check on the Fourteenth.”
[Pesachim 1:1.6] Is it obligatory to check by candlelight? Let us hear from the following “One checks neither by sunlight, nor by moonlight, nor by starlight, but by candlelight.” One understands “neither by moonlight, nor by starlight,” but “neither by sunlight”? Is there any sun in the night? This implies, even during daytime one has to check by candlelight; not only in a house without light, but even in a house which has light, even during daytime, it is necessary to check by candlelight.
[Pesachim 1:1.7] May one check dark passages purposely by candlelight? The words of the rabbis imply that not as it radiates at night it radiates during the day, as {NAME} said, when we were fleeing to these catacombs of the great assembly they were lighting candles for us. When they were faint, we knew that it was day; when they were bright we knew that it was night. This parallels what {NAME} said, when Noah entered the Ark he brought with him precious stones and pearls. When they were dull, he knew that it was daytime; when they were shiny he knew that it was nighttime.Why? There are animals eating at daytime and there are animals eating at nighttime. But is there not written, make a skylight to the ark ? Following him who said that the stars were not operative in the year of the flood.
[Pesachim 1:1.8] {NAME} asked: Do synagogues and houses of study need checking? What is his problem? Since one brings there for intercalations and on the days of the New Moon. It should be obvious for him, but what really is his problem? Since they are very well illuminated, may one check them purposely during daytime by candlelight?
[Pesachim 1:1.9] {NAME} asked: The courtyards in Jerusalem where one eats the bread of thanksgiving offerings and the wafers of a nazir , do they need checking? Are they not checked anyhow for leftovers? It should be parallel to what {NAME} the son-in-law of {NAME} stated: A menstruating woman washes her hair and combs. A priestly woman does not wash her hair and comb. A menstruating priestly woman washes her hair and combs, not to differentiate between one menstruating woman and another. So also here, not to differentiate between elimination and elimination. {NAME} stated before {NAME}: A menstruating woman who interrupts for seven days washes her hair and combs. A priestly woman who immerses herself every day does not wash her hair and comb. He told him, it is necessary for one who watches one day for a day.
[Pesachim 1:1.10] “Holes in the house, the upper and the lower ones, and the veranda, and the ditch, and the upper floor, and the roof of the olive press, and the roof of the tower, the storage room of straw, and the cattle stable, and the storage room of wood, and the storage room of provisions, wine storage, and oil storage, and produce storage, do not need checking.” One understands the upper ones. The lower ones? Does this mean that they did not worry about things falling down? {NAME} said, explain it if both were close to the wall, whether higher than ten or lower than ten [hand-breadths]. Did we not state “the ditch”? Does this not mean that they did not worry about things falling down? The toddler is afraid to go there. But should one not be afraid that leavened matter rolled there? Explain it by a ditch which has a rim. “And the roof of the olive press, and the roof of the tower.” That is, if they are three hand-breadths high; but if they are not three hand-breadths high they are like ground. And if they were not used for leavened matter, but if they were used for leavened matter even if it is very high it needs checking. {NAME} said, this is correct. Would we say that this papyrus scaffold which is very high should not need checking?
[Pesachim 1:1.11] It was stated: “{NAME} says, a couch which was separated in the house but wood and stones are stored under it, one checks at the outside but does not have to check on the inside.” Because wood and stones are stored under it, but if no wood and stones are stored under it, one has to check on the inside. Does this mean that they did (not) worry about things falling down? I am saying that (a child exerted himself and) [an unruly child] brought leavened matter there.
[Pesachim 1:1.12] A wine cellar needs checking, an oil cellar does not need checking. What is the difference between wine and oil? Wine has no staying power, oil has staying power. Storage, whether of wine or oil, does not need checking. What is a cellar? Anything used with bread in the courtyard. There exists a cellar which is like storage and storage which is like a cellar. A cellar in which he is ashamed to eat is like storage; storage where he is not ashamed to eat is like a cellar. There is a courtyard which is like an alley and an alley which is like a courtyard. A courtyard which is used by the public is like an alley, and an alley which is not used by the public is like a courtyard. But should one not be afraid that animal drivers introduce leavened matter into it? Animal drivers usually do not introduce leavened matter into it but sweets since they help in checking the quality of the wine.
[Pesachim 1:1.13] “If somebody leaves to travel by sea, before thirty days he does not have to check; within thirty [days] he has to check”. That is to say, if he intends to return. But if he does not intend to return, even before thirty days he has to check. If there is a doubt; but if it is certain then even from New Year’s Day. {NAME} said, but even if he intends to return he has to check, maybe he will change his mind and not return.
[Pesachim 1:1.14] Everybody is trustworthy about elimination of leavened matter, even women, even slaves. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: There is no “even” women. Women intrinsically are trustworthy; since they are slow they check everything very carefully. Samaritans any time when they prepare their mazzah with Jews are trustworthy about checking for leavened matter; if they do not prepare their mazzah with Jews they are not trustworthy about checking for leavened matter. {NAME} said, this means in the houses, but they are suspect in courtyards since they explain that it should not be found in your houses, does not apply to your courtyards.
[Pesachim 1:1.15] It was stated: {NAME} says, any commandment which the Samaritans keep they are much more exact with them than Jews. {NAME} said, that means earlier when they were concentrated in their villages. But today, when they have no commandments nor remainders of commandments they are suspect and degenerate.
[Pesachim 1:1.16] One asks about practices of Passover at Passover, practices of Pentecost at Pentecost, practices of Tabernacles at Tabernacles. In the House of Assembly one asks thirty days in advance; {NAME} says, two weeks. [Pesachim 2:1.5] But is it not written: Any fat of cattle, sheep, or goats you shall not eat ? Do you not have to understand the prohibition of usufruct from the prohibition of eating? There is a difference, for it is written: But fat of a carcass and fat of a torn animal may be used for any work, only it may not be eaten . But is it not written: Only the blood you may not eat ? Do you not have to understand the prohibition of usufruct from the prohibition of eating? There is a difference, for it is written: You shall pour it on the ground like water . Since water is permitted for use, so blood shall be permitted for use. [Pesachim 2:1.12] It was stated: {NAME} says, leavened matter may only be eliminated by burning. It is an argument de minore ad majus. Since piggul and leftover, which are not under an injunction not to be seen and not to be found, only may be disposed of by burning, for leavened matter which is under an injunction not to be seen and not to be found, it is only logical that it only may be disposed by burning. They told {NAME}, any argument de minore ad majus which you argue in the beginning as a restriction but it turns out in the end to be a leniency, is no argument de minore ad majus . It would imply that if he does not find fire he could sit and not dispose of it. The Torah said, eliminate sour dough from your houses.

[Pesachim 3:1.9] “Scribes’ glue.” In Alexandria they make tubs of dough.

If one goes from a place where he works to one where he does not work, or from a place where he does not work to one where he works, one puts on him the restrictions of the place he left and the restrictions of the place to which he comes, but a person should not change because of the controversy.
