If he is an eight months’ child, it is as if he cut flesh without need. {NAME} said, {NAME} asked, who permitted to cut flesh without need?
[Yevamot 11:7.5] It was stated: {NAME} says, any human who lives for thirty days is not a still birth, “all redeemed you shall redeem at the age of one month;” and an animal which lives for eight days is not a still birth, “from the eighth day and further it will be welcome as a sacrifice, a gift to the Eternal.” There, they say that practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} said, where do they disagree? If he was not born in his months. But if he was born in his months, even {NAME} will agree.
[Yevamot 11:7.6] “If he injured one and then injured the other, or cursed one and then cursed the other, he cannot be prosecuted.” {NAME} asked, does that not disagree with {NAME}? Since they disagree about the second day of holidays in the diaspora. {NAME} said, one accepts forwarning in a case of doubt, {NAME} said, one does not accept forwarning in a case of doubt. {NAME} said in the name of Rebbi, there is no disagreement. There, it would have been possible to make a determination, here it is impossible to make the determination.
[Yevamot 11:7.7] “If he injured both of them at the same time or cursed them at the same time, he is guilty. {NAME} frees him.” {NAME} asked: Is not the argument of {NAME} inverted? As we have stated there: “If he ate the volume of an olive of one of them and the volume of an olive of the other, he absorbs eighty [lashes]; {NAME} says, he absorbs only forty [lashes].” {NAME} said, it is not inverted. There, it was in doubt what is forbidden. But here, {NAME} is interpreting verses: “His father,” certain but not uncertain, “his mother”, certain but not uncertain.

[Yevamot 12:1.1] MISHNAH: The commandment of ḥalîṣah is to be executed before three judges; all three may be lay people. If she performed ḥalîṣah with a shoe, the ḥalîṣah is valid, with a felt slipper it is invalid. With a sandal having a heel it is valid, without a heel it is invalid. Below the knee the ḥalîṣah is valid, above the knee it is invalid.
[Yevamot 12:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The commandment of ḥalîṣah is to be executed before three judges,” etc. It is written “elders”, and you say laymen? The commandment is on the elders. From where that even laymen [are acceptable]? The verse says, “stripped of shoe”, in any case.
[Yevamot 12:1.3] There are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is valid. And there are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is invalid. He who says that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is valid follows him who says “in Israel” to include converts. He who says that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is invalid follows him who says “in Israel” to exclude converts.
[Yevamot 12:1.4] Here, you say, to exclude converts. But there, you say, to include converts. There, “the citizen” to exclude converts, “in Israel” to exclude converts; an exclusion after an exclusion to include converts. But here, “in Israel”, not converts.
[Yevamot 12:1.5] There are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah in the presence of two men is invalid; there are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah in the presence of two men is valid. Does he who says, ḥalîṣah in the presence of two men is invalid, hold that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is invalid, and he who says, ḥalîṣah in the presence of two men is valid, hold that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is valid? Even he who holds that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is valid will agree that in the presence of two men it is invalid since judgments in civil matters are valid from converts but invalid from two [judges].
[Yevamot 12:1.6] There are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah in the night is valid; there are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah in the presence of two men is invalid. Does he who says, ḥalîṣah in the night is valid, hold that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is valid, and he who says, ḥalîṣah in the night is invalid, hold that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is invalid? Even he who holds that ḥalîṣah in front of converts is valid will agree that in the night it is invalid since judgments in civil matters are valid from converts but invalid in the night.
[Yevamot 12:1.7] Some Tannaim state, only if the judges know how to instruct what to say. Some Tannaim stated, even if the judges do not know how to instruct what to say. He who said, only if the judges know how to instruct what to say, before they found a hint in Scripture, but he who said, even if the judges do not know how to instruct what to say, after they found a hint in Scripture: “You shall answer and say;” one answers only to a single person. {NAME} said, and only from the mouth of the judge, but one does not follow this.

[Yevamot 12:1.14] {NAME} said, if he took off [his shoe] and she put it on again, or she took it off but he had untied, the ḥalîṣah is invalid and if he wants to go back, he may not go back on it. If you say, because the two actions are not there together? They are there together! The reason therefore must be that they are not in the right order.

[Yevamot 12:6.1] MISHNAH: The commandment of ḥalîṣah : He and his sister-in-law come to the court of law and they give him appropriate counsel, as it is said: “The Elders of his city shall call him and speak to him”. She says: “My levir refuses to erect a name in Israel for his brother, my levir does not want;” and he says: “I do not desire to take her.” They have to speak in the holy language. “His sister-in-law comes to him before the Elders’ eyes, strips his shoe from his foot, and spits out before him,” spittle that is visible to the judges. She has to declare and say: “So should be done to a man who would not build his brother’s house.” Up to this sentence they were reading to them but when it was read for {NAME} under the oak tree in Kefar Abus he finished the paragraph; they established to finish the entire paragraph, “his house shall be called in Israel the house of the one stripped of shoe.” The obligation is on the judges, not on the students. {NAME} said, everyone present has the obligation to say,” the one stripped of shoe, the one stripped of shoe”.
[Yevamot 12:6.2] HALAKHAH: “The commandment of ḥalîṣah : He and his sister-in-law come,” etc. “They give him appropriate counsel”. What means, “they give him appropriate counsel”? If he is old, they tell her, what do you do with an old man like him? If she is old, they tell him, what do you do with that old woman? If she is a girl and he is an old man, they say to him, she is a girl and will bring you shame. If he is a boy and she an old woman, they say to her, he is a boy and will bring you shame. If he wants but she does not, one listens to her. If she wants but he does not, one listens to him. The principle: One listens to the one who wants to prevent. If both of them want, such a case came before {NAME} and he said, throw her out.
[Yevamot 12:6.3] {NAME} asked, in the case of a sister in law, who runs after whom? {NAME} answered: “His sister-in-law shall come to the gate.” When {NAME} heard this, he said, {NAME} taught us correctly.
[Yevamot 12:6.4] Does the recitation prevent [validity]? {NAME} said, for anybody able to recite, the recitation does not prevent [validity] but for anybody unable to recite, the recitation does prevent. {NAME} said, even though {NAME} said, the recitation does not prevent [validity], he agrees that if one recites, he recites in due order; in particular that it should not be said: “My levir refuses to erect, my levir does not want;” “I do not desire to take her”, but “my levir refuses to erect a name in Israel for his brother, my levir does not want;” “I do not desire to take her.”
[Yevamot 12:6.5] There, they say: “She came before us, stripped his shoe from his right foot, spat before us spittle that was visible on the ground, and said: ‘So should be done to a man who would not build his brother’s house.’ ” {NAME} said, since the spittle was visible when it left her mouth it is valid, even if the wind dissipated it. If she spat blood? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} turned to it, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} turned to it in the name of {NAME}: If it contains some liquid spittle, it is valid. How does the handless [woman] perform ḥalîṣah? With her teeth.
[Yevamot 12:6.6] The people of Simonia came to Rebbi and told him, please give us a man who preaches, judges, runs the synagogue, teaches reading, teaches Mishnah, and looks after all our needs. He gave them {NAME}. They made him a big platform and sat him on it. They came and asked him, how does the handless [woman] perform ḥalîṣah ? He did not respond. If she spat blood” He did not respond. They said, maybe he is not competent in studies, let us ask him in homiletics. They came and asked him, what is that which is written: “Truly, I shall tell you what is traced in writing, it is true.” If it is true, why is it traced, and if traced, why is it true? He did not respond. They came to Rebbi and told him, that required one we asked you for? He told them, by your lives, I gave you one who is my equal! He sent to bring him and examined him. He asked him, what if she spat blood. He said, if it contains some fluid of spittle it is valid. How does the handless [woman] perform ḥalîṣah ? He said, with her teeth. What is that which is written: “Truly, I shall tell you what is traced in writing, it is true.” If it is true, why is it traced, and if traced, why is it true? He said, until the decision of the court is sealed, it is traced. After it has been sealed, it is true. He asked him, and why did you not give any answers? He said to him, they made me a big platform and sat me on it; by that my spirit became bloated. He quoted about him: “If you became subject to contempt when you rose, if you planned, hand to mouth”; why did you become contemptible in the words of the Torah? That you used them to aggrandize yourself.
[Yevamot 12:6.7] It was stated: A mistaken ḥalîṣah is valid. What is a mistaken ḥalîṣah ? {NAME} said, a case where one told him, perform ḥalîṣah and she will be permitted to you after some time. {NAME} said, yesterday I was sitting and learning that “if he has the intention but not she, or she has the intention but not he, ḥalîṣah is always invalid unless both of them have the intention!” What is a mistaken ḥalîṣah for {NAME}? A case where one told him, perform ḥalîṣah and she will pay you a hundred talents. {NAME} said, if this was stipulated as a condition, she has to pay. A case came before {NAME} and he followed {NAME}. When he heard that {NAME} disagreed, he changed his opinion and forced a second ḥalîṣah. A case came before {NAME}. He told him, my son, this woman does not want to be married in levirate; therefore perform ḥalîṣah and remove your candidacy from her, then she will marry you in a regular marriage. After the ḥalîṣah , he said to him: Even if Moses and {NAME} came, they could not permit her. He referred to himself as “they are wise to do evil; they do not know how to do good.”
[Yevamot 12:6.8] There are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah is shameful; there are Tannaim who state that ḥalîṣah is praiseworthy. {NAME} said, he who says that ḥalîṣah is shameful follows the early Mishnah, that ḥalîṣah is praiseworthy follows the late Mishnah. {NAME} said, you might even say, in both cases one follows the early Mishnah, or in both cases one follows the late Mishnah. He who says that ḥalîṣah is shameful, since he damaged one thing in the Torah he shall come and take his damage: “his house shall be called in Israel the house of the one stripped of shoe.” He who says that ḥalîṣah is praiseworthy, it mentions here “calling” and it is said there: “My name will be called about them”. Since “calling” there is a praise, so here it is a praise.
[Yevamot 13:1.1] MISHNAH: The House of Shammai say, one makes only betrothed girls repudiate. The House of Hillel say, betrothed or married. The House of Shammai say, the husband, but the House of Hillel say, the husband or the levir. The House of Shammai say, in his presence, but the House of Hillel say, in his presence or in his absence. The House of Shammai say, in a court of law, but the House of Hillel say, in a court or outside a court. The House of Hillel said to the House of Shammai: An underage girl may repudiate even four or five times. The House of Shammai said to them: The daughters of Israel are not abandoned property! But she repudiates, waits until she is of age, or repudiates and is married.
[Yevamot 13:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The House of Shammai say, one permits repudiation,” etc. There, we have stated: “{NAME} testified to five statements: That one makes underage girls repudiate, … ” Does one disagree with testimony? One disagrees about the essence of the testimony. So was the essence of the testimony: “The House of Shammai say, one makes only betrothed girls repudiate, but the House of Hillel say, betrothed or married”. It is difficult following the House of Hillel! Her marriage permitted her, he has the right to what she finds and earns, to dissolve her vows, and she is his wife in every respect. And you say so? They gave you of your own. By right, her marriage should not be a marriage. They said that her marriage is a marriage and they said that she may repudiate him and leave.
[Yevamot 13:1.3] What is the reason of the House of Shammai? If you say so, you make all intercourse he had with her intercourse of harlotry. {NAME} said, it turns out that the House of Shammai hold with {NAME} as {NAME} said, intercourse of an unmarried man with an unmarried woman not with the intent of marriage is intercourse of harlotry. That means, for the House of Shammai her repudiation is nothing if she transgressed and repudiated after marriage. If she entered the bridal chamber but had no intercourse yet, what is her status? As betrothed or as married? If she is betrothed in Judea where he is familiar with her, what is her status? As betrothed or as married?
[Yevamot 13:1.4] If she had been in a situation that she could not repudiate, may she go and repudiate? Let us hear from the following: An underage girl who was married off by her father but then was divorced, if she went and married by herself she nevertheless can repudiate.
[Yevamot 13:1.5] What is the reason of the House of Shammai? The husband she may repudiate since she married him with her consent. The levir to whom she was given by an act of God she cannot repudiate. What is the reason of the House of Hillel? If she can repudiate the principal, so much more the levir! {NAME} said, she may repudiate the levir to invalidate the claim of the dead brother and to permit the co-wife to her father and the daughter-in-law to her father-in-law. Rav and {NAME} both say, she may not repudiate the levir to invalidate the claim of the dead brother and to permit the co-wife to her father and the daughter-in- law to her father-in-law. Do Rav and {NAME} follow {NAME}, since the House of Shammai say “the husband”? Where do we hold? If she says, I can stand neither the marriage with your brother nor with you, everybody agrees that she invalidates. If she says, I can stand marriage with you but not with your brother? Rav and {NAME} both say, she says I cannot stand marriage with you but marriage with your brother I want. The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “And all of these, if they died, or repudiated, or were divorced, or found to be she-rams, their co-wives are permitted.” Was she not divorced from him? Similarly, she repudiated him. {NAME} stated: If they repudiated or were divorced in the husband’s lifetime, their co-wives are permitted. After the husband’s death their co-wives perform ḥalîṣah but not levirate.
[Yevamot 13:1.6] {NAME}, {NAME} said: Explain it when they died and did not repudiate since there is a Mishnah: “If a woman could repudiate but did not do so and died, her co-wife performs ḥalîṣah but cannot be married in levirate.” {NAME} said, you may even say if she still lives; explain it if there is no levir besides her father.
[Yevamot 13:1.7] {NAME} said, after qiddušin . {NAME} said, even after final marriage. In the second repetition, {NAME} changed his mind. {NAME} said to him, did the rabbi not teach us “after final marriage”? He answered him, is that fixed in you with a nail?
[Yevamot 13:1.8] {NAME} said before {NAME}, did not {NAME} say correctly before he changed his mind? Once a man’s daughter is married without being a she-ram, her co-wife is forbidden. If in addition she is a she-ram, does her co-wife become permitted? He said to him, the she-ram is as if non-existent. If there are two sisters-in-law, one a she-ram and one not a she-ram, if the levir comes and performs ḥalîṣah or has intercourse with the first, did he free her companion of anything? That shows that the she- ram is as if non-existent.
[Yevamot 13:1.9] “His daughter”. How can his daughter repudiate, is she not married by Torah standards, “my daughter I gave to this man”? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it by a minor, who was married off by her father and divorced, who is like an orphan while her father is alive.
[Yevamot 13:1.10] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: This means that a minor cannot give birth; because otherwise she could wait until she grew up, repudiate her husband, and permit her co-wife to her son-in-law. The daughter-in-law of {NAME} repudiated while her son was on her shoulder.
[Yevamot 13:1.11] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah speaks about a sister-in-law who has two levirs. If one of them “bespoke” her, she may repudiate his “bespeaking” and marry on the market place. Why can she not repudiate his “bespeaking” and marry his brother? Explain it, if she says, I cannot stand you. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah speaks about a sister-in-law who has five levirs. If one of them “bespoke” her, she may repudiate his “bespeaking” and marry his brother. Why can she not repudiate his “bespeaking” and marry on the market place? Explain it if her father had married her off, this was a marriage by biblical standards.
[Yevamot 13:1.12] “ The House of Hillel said to the House of Shammai: It happened with the wife of the cameldriver Pison that the Sages repudiated for her in her absence. The House of Shammai said to them, is that a proof? Since he measured crookedly, the Sages measured crookedly for him.” This is difficult. Because a man behaves incorrectly, does one permit his incest prohibition? Rab Ḥisda said, that means that, if she transgresses and repudiated after marriage, the House of Shammai recognize her act of repudiation.
[Yevamot 13:1.13] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It happened that a girl went to wash at the river when they said to her, your betrothed is passing by. She said, let my mother go and marry him! When the case came before the Sages, they said that there is no repudiation stronger than that. {NAME} said, It happened that a girl went to buy flax from the flax dealer when they said to her, your betrothed is passing by. She said, let my mother go and marry him! When the case came before the Sages, they said that there is no repudiation stronger than that. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: “Even if she went to buy something at the store and said, I cannot endure my husband X, there is no repudiation stronger than this.
[Yevamot 13:1.14] Does a court convene for repudiation? Was it not stated: Flee from three and cling to three. Cling to ḥalîṣah , annulling vows, and making peace. But flee from repudiations, from being a guarantor, and from receiving deposits. {NAME} said, its name is not פקדון “deposit” but פק דון “go to court”. {NAME} said, “My son, if you became guanrantor for your neighbor.” Does a court convene for repudiation? Explain it that they were sitting in another matter and the case came before them.
[Yevamot 13:1.15] So is the Mishnah: Or she should repudiate him and marry. Therefore, she cannot get herself betrothed. That means, if she transgresses and repudiated after marriage, the House of Shammai recognize her act of repudiation. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A rumor spreads for a married woman but not for a betrothed one. A woman might hide herself and say, I was not betrothed, but she will not be able to hide herself and say, I did not marry.
[Yevamot 13:2.1] MISHNAH: Which underage girl needs to repudiate? Anyone whom mother or brothers married off with her knowledge. If they married her off without her knowledge she does not have to repudiate. {NAME} says, any girl who is unable to watch over her marriage gift does not have to repudiate. {NAME} says, in all legal respects, the underage girl is like one seduced: The daughter of an Israel married to a Cohen may not eat heave; the daughter of a Cohen married to an Israel may eat heave.
[Yevamot 13:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Which underage girl needs to repudiate,” etc? What means “with her knowledge”? One makes for her a canopy, dresses her in jewelry and leads the man to her.
[Yevamot 13:2.3] Do they disagree with {NAME}? From what {NAME} said, which is the underage girl that needs a bill of divorce? Anyone who is given her bill of divorce together with something else and she produces it after some time. This implies that they disagree with {NAME}.
[Yevamot 13:2.4] {NAME} says, the actions of an underage girl have no legal standing. He has no right to what she finds or earns, nor may he dissolve her vows; she is as if not his wife in any respect except that she needs repudiation from him. {NAME} said, he owns what she finds or earns, he may he dissolve her vows; she is his wife in all respects except that she needs a bill of divorce from him. {NAME} said, I looked around at all logical systems of Sages and did not find anybody who was consistent in the matter of an underage girl except {NAME}, only that he requires repudiation from him.
[Yevamot 13:2.5] {NAME} said: It happened that {NAME} mother was pushing him to marry his sister’s daughter. He said to [the girl]: go and get married, go and get married, until she said to him: Here I am your slave girl to wash the feet of my master’s servants. Even though he married her, he did not sleep with her until she had grown two pubic hairs.
[Yevamot 13:2.6] According to {NAME}, may she repudiate him and collect a fine from him? According to {NAME}, may she repudiate him and collect a fine from another man? May she repudiate this one and invalidate her bill of divorce, a desecrated or a bastard? {NAME} asked, may she repudiate and return to her father’s food? It is obvious that she does not return to her husband’s food since he writes for her: “You shall live in my house and be fed from my property,” and she is not in his house. Therefore, the only question is, may she repudiate and return to her father’s food?
[Yevamot 13:2.7] There, we have stated: {NAME} says, the heave given by a minor who has not yet grown two pubic hairs is heave. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: His heave is never heave unless he grew two pubic hairs. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of the {NAME} ( Num. 18:32 ): “You should not carry guilt because of it.” He who may carry guilt can give heave, he who cannot carry guilt cannot give heave. They objected: But a Gentile cannot incur guilt, and he may give heave! {NAME} in the name of {NAME} ( Num. 18:27 ): “Your heave will be credited to you”, ( v. 26 ) “and you shall lift”. Anybody for whom “thought” is written may give heave. But anybody for whom “thought” is not written cannot give heave. They objected: But “thought” is not written for Gentiles, and he may give heave! {NAME} stated: Gentiles have no “thought” whether for preparation or for heave.
[Yevamot 13:2.8] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Following the opinion that someone who cannot give heave cannot dedicate to the Temple. Why did he not say: following the opinion that he can give heave, can he dedicate to the Temple? Because of {NAME}, for {NAME} says he can give heave but cannot dedicate. {NAME} says, even following the opinion that he cannot give heave, he can dedicate. What can he dedicate? Holocaust and well-being offerings. He cannot bring a sin sacrifice for fat because he is not obligated to a sin sacrifice for fat. He cannot bring a sin sacrifice for blood because he is not obligated to a sin sacrifice for blood. May he bring a sacrifice relating to gonorrhea and skin disease? Since it is obligatory can’t he bring it, or since he becomes impure by these can he bring it? If it is obvious for you that he brings, can he become an agent for these? Since he may become impure by these, may he become an agent, or since he cannot become an agent for anything else, can’t he become an agent for these? {NAME} objected: His produce is ṭevel from the Torah but he can free his ṭevel by Torah law! But here, even though he may become impure by them, he cannot become an agent. May he bring First Fruits following {NAME}, for {NAME} says that First Fruits have the status of territorial consecrated things? He may not bring following the rabbis who say they have the status of things consecrated to the Temple. May he bring a sacrifice of pilgrimage? Since it is obligatory can’t he bring it, or since he may change its name to well-being offering, may he bring it? May he bring a Passover sacrifice? Since it is obligatory can’t he bring it, or since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, a person may bring a Passover sacrifice any day of the year when he changes its name to well-being offering, may he bring it? May he bring tithes of cereals? If he holds with {NAME}, since {NAME} said ( Num. 18:28 ): “From all your tithes,” that all tithes were bracketed together, then since he cannot bring tithes of grain he cannot bring tithes of animals. May he make substitutions? If {NAME} is of the opinion that all tithes were bracketed together, then since he cannot bring tithes of grain he cannot bring tithes of animals; since he cannot bring tithes of animals he cannot make substitutions. One may hold with {NAME}, since {NAME} says that tithes of animals teach you for all sacrifices about substitutions. That means, since he cannot bring tithes of grain he cannot bring tithes of animals; since he cannot bring tithes of animals he cannot make substitutions; since he cannot make substitutions for these he cannot make substitutions for any sacrifices. Is one guilty sacrificing for him outside the Temple? {NAME} said, one cannot be guilty sacrificing for him outside the Temple. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, one is guilty sacrificing for him outside the Temple. The statement of {NAME} disagrees with {NAME}, since {NAME} frees his ṭevel as biblical law. And you say so? We can say he [{NAME}] is following him who says they accepted tithes voluntarily.
[Yevamot 13:2.9] {NAME} had a difficulty with the words of {NAME}. Is her marriage valid by biblical standards? The dissolution of her vows must be by biblical standards! And you say so! {NAME} said, there is no dissolution of vows here, because of what {NAME} had against the words of {NAME}. {NAME} asked: Would it be the same for prohibitions? {NAME} said, one does not whip for prohibitions. Would that be as we stated there: “Before that time, even though they said, we know for Whom we made a vow or to Whom we dedicated, their vows are no vows and their dedications no dedications. After that time, even though they said, we do not know for Whom we made a vow or to Whom we dedicated, their vows are vows and their dedications dedications.” What is the status of that Mishnah? For {NAME} it is in dispute, for {NAME} and {NAME} it is everybody’s opinion.
[Yevamot 13:3.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} said, every impediment that comes from the man makes her as if she were his wife; every impediment that does not come from the man makes her as if she were not his wife.
[Yevamot 13:3.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} said,” etc. It was stated: “{NAME} said, every impediment that comes from the man by a bill of divorce makes her as if she were his wife; every impediment that does not come from the man by repudiation makes her as if she were not his wife.”
[Yevamot 13:4.1] MISHNAH: If [a girl] repudiates a man, he is permitted [to marry] her relatives and she is permitted [to marry] his relatives; he did not disable her for the priesthood. If he gave her a bill of divorce, he is forbidden [to marry] her relatives and she is forbidden [to marry] his relatives; he did disable her for the priesthood. If he gave her a bill of divorce and later took her back, then she repudiated him and married another man from whom she became widowed or divorced, she is permitted to return to him. If she repudiated him and he took her back, then he gave her a bill of divorce and she married another man from whom she became widowed or divorced, she is prohibited to return to him. That is the principle: By divorce after repudiation she is prohibited to return to him; by repudiation after divorce she is permitted to return to him.
[Yevamot 13:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If [a girl] repudiates a man, etc.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Her only problem would be aspersion on the priesthood, but the court will not tolerate aspersion.
[Yevamot 13:5.1] MISHNAH: If [a girl] repudiates a man and marries another who divorces her, another and she repudiates him, another who divorces her, another and she repudiates him, she is forbidden to return to anyone who had divorce her but permitted to return to those she had repudiated.
[Yevamot 13:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If [a girl] repudiates,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Her only problem would be aspersion on the priesthood, but the court will not tolerate aspersion.
[Yevamot 13:6.1] MISHNAH: If somebody divorced his wife and later took her back, she is permitted to the levir but {NAME} forbids her. Similarly, if somebody divorced an orphan girl and took her back, she is permitted to the levir but {NAME} forbids her. If an underage girl who was married off by her father was divorced, she is like an orphan during her father’s lifetime. If she was taken back, she is prohibited to the levir. The Sages agree with {NAME} in case he divorced her as a minor and took her back as a minor, since her divorce is a total divorce but her return was not complete. But if he divorced her as a minor and took her back as an adult or she became an adult while married to him, she is permitted to the levir.
[Yevamot 13:6.2] HALAKHAH: “The Sages agree,” etc. What is {NAME} reason? That she was forbidden to him for an hour. The Sages agree with {NAME} about the underage girl who was married off by her father and divorced, that she is like an orphan during her father’s lifetime. Her betrothal and divorce were by biblical standards; her remarriage was not by biblical standards.
[Yevamot 13:6.3] What is the status of her co-wife? Rav said, her co-wife is forbidden. {NAME} said, her co-wife is forbidden. {NAME} said, her co-wife is permitted. {NAME} said, I looked around at the rabbis here and at the rabbis there and did not find anybody agreeing with me except {NAME} who says, her co-wife is permitted.{NAME} was sitting before {NAME} and said, what is the status of her co-wife? He said to him, she is permitted. He asked, divorce? He answered, forbidden. He said, go around. {NAME} said, it is reasonable following him who said that her co-wife is permitted. But following him who said, her co-wife is forbidden, as you take it: The aspect he acquired in her makes the corresponding aspect forbidden in her co-wife, the aspect he did not acquire in her makes the corresponding aspect permitted in her co-wife! {NAME} said, does one admit that kind of argument in matters of incest prohibitions? What about it? For any sister-in-law who is not totally outside [the family], the acquired aspect of her belongs to an incest prohibition and an incest prohibition forbids the co-wife.
[Yevamot 13:6.4] “Two brothers are married,” etc. {NAME}: One may ask what one asked there. Should he not perform ḥalîṣah for the acquired aspect in her and free her co-wife? So here, should he not perform ḥalîṣah for the acquired aspect in the underage girl and free her (co-wife) [sister]? Before you find {NAME} difficult, you might find {NAME} difficult! You cannot find this difficult for {NAME}, since {NAME} is a Shammaite and the House of Shammai say, one lets only the betrothed [women] repudiate?
[Yevamot 13:7.1] MISHNAH: Two brothers are married to two underage orphan [sisters]. If the husband of one of them dies, the other one has to leave as wife’s sister. And so for two deaf-mute [sisters]. If one is adult and the other underage, if the husband of the underage girl died, she has to leave as wife’s sister. If the husband of the adult one died, {NAME} said, one teaches the underage one to repudiate him. {NAME} says, if she repudiated, she repudiated; otherwise she should wait until she becomes of age and the other one has to leave as wife’s sister. {NAME} says, woe to him for his wife, woe to him for his brother’s wife! He has to send away his wife by a bill of divorce and his brother’s wife by ḥalîṣah .
[Yevamot 13:7.2] HALAKHAH: Is the degree of acquisition of one equal to that of the other? Did we not state “underage and deaf-mute”? {NAME} stated ““underage and deaf-mute”: “If the husband of the underage girl died, the husband of the deaf-mute has to divorce her and the underage girl has to wait until she comes of age and perform ḥalîṣah ” Why can she not perform ḥalîṣah immediately? She cannot because of {NAME}, since {NAME} said that one does not perform levirate or ḥalîṣah with an underage girl, since she might be found to be a she-ram. “If the husband of the deaf-mute died, the husband of the underage girl has to divorce her and the deaf-mute is permanently forbidden. If he transgressed and had intercourse with the deaf-mute, he divorces her and she becomes permitted.” This follows what {NAME} said, in order to fix her status.
[Yevamot 13:7.3] So is the Mishnah: The underage girl should wait until she grows up, reaches puberty, and is being married. {NAME} said, there is no “being married” here, only “being betrothed.” {NAME} said, these are the words of {NAME}: If somebody gave qiddušin to his sister-in-law’s sister, his sister-in-law was freed from ḥalîṣah and levirate. It follows that what we had stated there, “if somebody gave qiddušin to the sister of a woman waiting for her levir” does not follow {NAME}.
[Yevamot 13:7.4] {NAME} said before {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}, if she repudiated, she repudiated. {NAME} said, one teaches the underage one to repudiate him, and you say so? {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}, if she repudiated, she repudiated. {NAME} says, woe to him for his wife, woe to him for his brother’s wife! And you say so? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} agrees with {NAME}, if she repudiated, she repudiated; otherwise she should wait until she becomes of age. If not, he has to send away his wife by a bill of divorce and his brother’s wife by ḥalîṣah.
[Yevamot 13:8.1] MISHNAH: If somebody was married to two underage orphan girls and died, intercourse or ḥalîṣah of one of them frees her co-wife. The same holds for two deaf-mutes. An underaged girl and a deaf-mute: Intercourse of neither of them frees her co-wife.
[Yevamot 13:8.2] HALAKHAH: Is the degree of acquisition of one equal to that of the other? What does he do? {NAME} in the name of Rav: He marries the deaf-mute and divorces her; the underage girl has to wait until she can perform ḥalîṣah. ” Why can she not perform ḥalîṣah immediately? She cannot because of {NAME}, since {NAME} said that one does not perform levirate or ḥalîṣah with an underage girl, since she might be found to be a she-ram. If he sleeps with the underage girl, he has to divorce her, and the deaf-mute is permanently forbidden. If he transgressed and had intercourse with the deaf-mute, he divorces her and she became permitted.” This follows what {NAME} said, in order to fix her status. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: What means, “in order to fix her status”? As you say there, he should perform ḥalîṣah for the aspect that was acquired in her and marry her co-wife; could he not perform ḥalîṣah for the aspect that was acquired in the underage girl and marry the deaf-mute? He said to him, so says {NAME}: We never find two sisters-in-law of whom one performs ḥalîṣah and one is married in levirate. Do we find two sisters-in-law of whom one performs ḥalîṣah and one is divorced? He said to him, that happens. That is what we have stated there: “If he ‘bespoke’ one and performed ḥalîṣah with the other, the first one needs a bill of divorce”.
[Yevamot 13:9.1] MISHNAH: A hearing wife and a deaf-mute: The intercourse of the hearing woman frees the deaf-mute but the intercourse of the deaf-mute does not free the hearing woman.
[Yevamot 13:9.2] HALAKHAH: “A hearing wife and a deaf-mute,” etc.: A hearing wife and a deaf-mute. The intercourse of the hearing woman frees the deaf-mute. The intercourse of the deaf-mute does not free the hearing woman but disables the hearing woman.
[Yevamot 13:10.1] MISHNAH: An adult wife and an underage wife. The intercourse of the adult woman frees the underage girl but the intercourse of the underage girl does not free the adult woman.
[Yevamot 13:10.2] HALAKHAH: “An adult wife and an underage wife,” etc. An adult wife and an underage wife. The intercourse of the adult woman frees the underage girl. The intercourse of the underage girl does not free the adult woman but disables the adult woman.
[Yevamot 13:11.1] MISHNAH: Somebody was married to two underage orphan girls and died. If the levir had intercourse with the first one and then had intercourse with the second, or his brother had intercourse with the second, the first one was not disabled. The same holds for two deaf-mutes. An underage girl and a deaf-mute. If the levir had intercourse with the underage girl and then had intercourse with the deaf-mute, or his brother had intercourse with the deaf-mute, the underage girl was not disabled. If the levir had intercourse with the deaf-mute and then had intercourse with the underage girl, or his brother had intercourse with the underage girl, the deaf-mute was disabled.
[Yevamot 13:11.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody was married.” Even if he did not have intercourse with the underage girl, the deaf-mute is disabled. If he did not have intercourse with the underage girl and she died, he would have been permitted the deaf-mute. But now that he did have intercourse with her, even if she died he had disabled the deaf-mute.
[Yevamot 13:12.1] MISHNAH: A hearing wife and a deaf-mute. If the levir had intercourse with the hearing woman and then had intercourse with the deaf-mute, or his brother had intercourse with the deaf-mute, the hearing woman was not disabled. If the levir had intercourse with the deaf-mute and then had intercourse with the hearing woman, or his brother had intercourse with the hearing woman, the deaf-mute was disabled.
[Yevamot 13:12.2] HALAKHAH: “A hearing wife and a deaf-mute. If the levir had intercourse,” etc. Even if he did not have intercourse with the hearing woman, the deaf-mute is disabled. If he did not have intercourse with the hearing woman and she died, he would have been permitted the deaf-mute. But now that he did have intercourse with her, even if she died he had disabled the deaf-mute.
[Yevamot 13:13.1] MISHNAH: An adult wife and an underage one. If the levir had intercourse with the adult and then had intercourse with the underage one, or his brother had intercourse with her, the adult was not disabled. If the levir had intercourse with the underage widow and then had intercourse with the adult one, or his brother had intercourse with her, the underage one was disabled. {NAME} says, one teaches the underage girl that she should repudiate him.
[Yevamot 13:13.2] HALAKHAH: “An adult wife and an underage one” Even if he did not have intercourse with the adult one, the underage one is disabled. If he did not have intercourse with the adult woman and she died, he would have been permitted the underage one. But now that he did have intercourse with her, even if she died he had disabled the underage one.
[Yevamot 13:13.3] “{NAME} says, one teaches the underage girl that she should repudiate him.” After the fact. Therefore, not from the start! {NAME} said it without attribution, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This is {NAME}, since {NAME} said that one does not perform levirate or ḥalîṣah with an underage girl, since she might be found to be a she-ram.
[Yevamot 13:14.1] MISHNAH: If an underage levir had intercourse with an underage sister-in-law, they should grow up together. If he had intercourse with an adult sister-in-law, she should raise him. If the sister-in-law claims within thirty days that she was not copulated with, one forces him to perform ḥalîṣah with her. After thirty days, one asks him to perform ḥalîṣah with her. But if he confesses, one forces him to perform ḥalîṣah with her even after twelve months. If a woman made a vow during her husband’s lifetime forbidding herself any usufruct from her levir, one coerces him until he performs ḥalîṣah with her. After her husband’s death, one begs him that he should perform ḥalîṣah with her. If she had [ ḥalîṣah ] in mind even during her husband’s lifetime, one begs him that he should perform ḥalîṣah with her.
[Yevamot 13:14.2] HALAKHAH: “If an underage levir,” etc. It was stated: A claim of non-virginity may be brought within thirty days, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, immediately. Where do we hold? If he copulated, immediately. If he did not copulate, even after a longer delay. But we must hold if it was not spelled out. {NAME} said, it is credible that a man may hold himself back for thirty days. But the Sages say, a man does not hold himself back even for one day. {NAME} asked: According to {NAME}, would a man be believed to assert that he held himself back for thirty days in order to make the child fatherless? Let us hear from the following: “If the sister-in-law claims within thirty days that she was not copulated with, one forces him to perform ḥalîṣah with her. After thirty days, one asks him to perform ḥalîṣah with her.” (After thirty days.) And {NAME} said, this is {NAME}. And {NAME} said, that refers only to her, but not to her co-wife. As you say there, she is not believed to damage her co-wife, so here, he is not believed to damage his son.
[Yevamot 13:14.3] “If a woman made a vow forbidding herself any usufruct,” etc. Consider the following: He said, I copulated, but she says, I was not copulated with. Even if he changed and then said, I did not copulate, he cannot be believed since from the start he had said, I copulated. But if from the start he said that he had not copulated, the two together can uproot the presumption. The colleagues asked: What are we talking about? If following the early Mishnah, we have understood that one may marry in levirate. If following the later Mishnah, we have understood that one may perform ḥalîṣah . Where did we hear that one coerces? {NAME} in the name of Rav: That is, if a bill of divorce has passed from his hand to her hand. He says, it is the bill of divorce of a wife. But she says, it is the bill of divorce of a sister-in-law. Within thirty days, the presumption is that he did not copulate; one coerces him to perform ḥalîṣah . After thirty days, one asks him to perform ḥalîṣah . {NAME} asked, after thirty days, the presumption is that he copulated and you say one coerces? But it must be the following: {NAME} in the name of Rav: That is, if a bill of divorce has passed from his hand to her hand. He says, it is the bill of divorce of a wife. But she says, it is the bill of divorce of a sister-in-law. Within thirty days, the presumption is that he did not copulate; one coerces him to perform ḥalîṣah . After thirty days, one asks him to perform ḥalîṣah . The following: If he says, I copulated, and she says, I was not copulated with, it is obvious that he has to sustain her. It is obvious that he does not inherit from her. The problem is whether he inherits his brother’s property. If she says, I was copulated with, and he says, I did not copulate, it is obvious that he does not have to sustain her. It is obvious that he inherits his brother’s property. The problem is whether he inherits from her.
[Yevamot 14:1.1] MISHNAH: A deaf-mute man who married a hearing woman or a hearing man who married a deaf-mute woman may divorce or stay married at will; just as he marries with sign language so he divorces with sign language. A hearing man who married a hearing woman who then became deaf-mute may divorce or stay married at will. If she became insane he shall not divorce. If he became deaf-mute or insane, he can never divorce.
[Yevamot 14:1.2] HALAKHAH: “A deaf-mute who married a hearing woman”, etc. How does he do it? He communicates in sign language and gives her the bill of divorce. In the same way he communicates with others, others communicate with him.
[Yevamot 14:1.3] The Mishnah applies if he became betrothed to her by money. But if he became betrothed to her by copulation, his betrothal is an action but his divorce is not an action.
[Yevamot 14:1.4] {NAME} asked {NAME}: The wife of a deaf-mute or an insane? He said to him, that does not even need a reparation sacrifice for a possible sin. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It does not even need a reparation sacrifice for a possible sin. Since you say, it does not even need a reparation sacrifice for a possible sin; if another man came and gave her qiddušin , they take hold of her. If he divorced, is she permitted to remarry the first [husband]? That is what {NAME} stated: About the wife of a deaf-mute who after being divorced by the deaf-mute went and married a deaf-mute or a hearing person, I am reading: “Her first husband who sent her away cannot come to take her back.” About the wife of a hearing person who after being divorced went and married a deaf-mute or a hearing person, I am reading: “Her first husband who sent her away cannot … ” If a deaf-mute’s husband went overseas and they came and told his wife, your husband has died, and she went and married a deaf- mute or a hearing person, and then her husband returned, she has to leave both of them. If the husband of a hearing wife went overseas and they came and told her, your husband has died, and she went and married a deaf-mute, and then her hearing [husband] returned, we would think that the deaf-mute should divorce her but the hearing person can keep her. She is still under these disabilities.
[Yevamot 14:1.5] “If she became insane he shall not divorce.” In the House of {NAME} they said, because of the fence. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, because she cannot preserve her bill of divorce. {NAME} (the son) [in the name] of {NAME} explained three cases. If he transgressed and divorced her. According to him who said because of a fence, he divorced. According to him who said because she cannot preserve her bill of divorce, it is forbidden. If she has a son, or a father, or a brother. According to him who said because of a fence, it is forbidden. According to him who said because she cannot preserve her bill of divorce, she has a father and can preserve her bill of divorce. Sometimes she is insane and sometimes of lucid mind. According to him who said because of a fence, it is forbidden. According to him who said because she cannot preserve her bill of divorce, sometimes she can preserve her bill of divorce.
[Yevamot 14:2.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} said, why can a deaf-mute woman be divorced but a deaf-mute man cannot divorce? They told him, a divorcing man is not comparable to a divorced woman since a woman can be divorced with or against her will but a man divorces only by his own will. {NAME} testified about a deaf-mute girl who was married off by her father that she could be divorced by a bill of divorce. They said to him, that is an example.
[Yevamot 14:2.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} testified,” etc. {NAME} asked before {NAME}. The matters seem reasonable for a hearing woman of sound mind, that she is divorced with or without her acquiescence. But a deaf-mute woman who has no will should not be divorced except with her acquiescence. But is it not testimony “that is an example”; does one add to a testimony? But {NAME} is of the opinion that this deals with a hearing girl who was married off by her father and became deaf-and-dumb. {NAME} is of the opinion that this deals with an underage girl who was married off by her father and became divorced.
[Yevamot 14:2.3] {NAME} said, there is nothing to be learned from the beginning, but there is something to be learned from the end. What is there at the beginning? If the deaf-mute [brother] was the husband of the deaf-mute [woman] and the hearing the husband of the hearing. But if the deaf-mute [brother] was the husband of the hearing [woman] and the hearing the husband of the deaf-mute, that should have been stated at the very end.
[Yevamot 14:3.1] MISHNAH: Two deaf-mute brothers married to two deaf-mute sisters, or two hearing sisters, or two sisters of whom one is deaf-mute, the other hearing; or two deaf-mute sisters married to two deaf-mute brothers, or two hearing brothers, or two brothers of whom one is deaf-mute, these are free from ḥalîṣah and levirate. If the women are unrelated, they must marry them, and, if they want to, they may send them away. Two brothers, one deaf-mute and one hearing, married to two hearing sisters. If the hearing [brother] married to the hearing wife died, what shall the deaf-mute married to the hearing wife do? [Yevamot 14:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Two deaf-mute brothers,” etc. What about her co-wife ? Let us hear from the following: If his hearing daughter was married to his deaf-mute brother, her co-wife is free from ḥalîṣah and levirate.
[Yevamot 14:4.1] MISHNAH: Two hearing brothers married to two sisters, one deaf-mute and one hearing. [Yevamot 14:5.1] MISHNAH: Two brothers, one deaf-mute and one hearing, married to two sisters, one deaf-mute and one hearing. [Yevamot 14:6.1] MISHNAH: Two brothers, one deaf-mute and one hearing, married to two unrelated hearing women. If the hearing [brother] married to a hearing wife died, what shall the deaf-mute [brother] married to a hearing wife do? He marries [the widow] and never can divorce her.
[Yevamot 14:6.2] HALAKHAH: “Two brothers, one deaf-mute,” etc. May she eat heave? Let us her from the following: “A hearing daughter of an Israel who married a deaf-mute Cohen does not eat heave. If he died and she came before the levir, if he is hearing, she eats, deaf-mute does not eat.”
[Yevamot 14:7.1] MISHNAH: Two hearing brothers, married to two unrelated women, one deaf-mute and one hearing. [Yevamot 14:7.2] HALAKHAH: “Two hearing brothers,” etc. “Two brothers, one of them deaf-mute,” etc. May she eat heave? Let us hear from the following: “A hearing daughter of an Israel who became engaged to a hearing Cohen, who did not manage to bring her to the bridal chamber before he became deaf-mute or before she became deaf-mute, does not eat heave. In this He increased the power of the levir over that of the husband since the deaf-mute levir enables her to eat, but the deaf-mute husband does not enable her to eat.”
[Yevamot 15:1.1] MISHNAH: A woman went overseas with her husband. If there was peace between him and her and there was peace in the world and came and said, “my husband died”, she can remarry, “my husband died”, she can marry in levirate. If there was no peace between him and her but there was peace in the world, she cannot be believed. {NAME} says, she is never believed unless she comes crying with torn clothes. They said to him, in any case she can remarry.
[Yevamot 15:1.2] HALAKHAH: “A woman went with her husband,” etc. Just as you say, “if there are witnesses that she is a married woman and she says, I was divorced, she is not trustworthy;” would I say it is the same here? There is a difference for witnesses of death since if he comes he disproves [the testimony]. Then she should be trustworthy to say: “my levir died”! That is impossible since we have stated: “A woman is not trustworthy if she says ‘my levir died’ to remarry, or ‘my sister died’ to enter her house.” {NAME} said, she is trustworthy for her husband whom she married out of her free will; she is not trustworthy about her levir on whom she was thrown against her will. {NAME} asked, think of it, then she should not be trustworthy if she was forced to marry him!
[Yevamot 15:1.3] Not only according to the current Mishnah that a single witness can permit her, but even according to the earlier Mishnah that a single witness cannot permit her, she permits herself. What is the difference between herself and a single witness? A single witness is suspected to want to cause trouble to her; she is not suspected to want to cause trouble to herself.
[Yevamot 15:1.4] Is a single witness trustworthy in wartime? Let us hear from the following: A person was living in the times of Rebbi. They asked him about X; he said, he died. They asked him about Y; he said, he died. They asked him, are they all dead? He answered, if they were alive would they not have come? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The case came before Rebbi and he said, the ones married should stay married, the ones not married should not marry. {NAME} said, it happened in wartime. That implies that a single witness is trustworthy in wartime.
[Yevamot 15:1.5] What is the difference whether peace is in the world or war is in the world? If war is in the world, she might think that he died although he is not dead. So far if war was in the North and she came from the North, in the South and she came from the South. If there was war in the North and she came from the South; she says I am coming from the North, but I am arguing that you came from the South. If she says, I am coming from the South, it is because she thinks to free herself. If she says, he died on his bed, I am arguing that he went to war; it is because she thinks to free herself.
[Yevamot 15:1.6] What is a quarrel? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. “You never gave me qiddušin , you did not divorce me, I never was your wife,” that is not a quarrel. “You gave me qiddušin , you divorced me, but you never paid me what is owed me under my ketubah ,” that is a quarrel. When {NAME} said this before {NAME}, he said to him, my son, even if she clearly requests to be divorced.
[Yevamot 15:1.7] “{NAME} says, she is never believed unless she comes crying with torn clothes.” They objected to {NAME}: Think of it, if one came crying, the other did not cry. To this one you forbid, to that one you permit. {NAME}, the colleague of the rabbis, objected: Think of it, maybe her son went overseas and died there, she remembers that and cries.
[Yevamot 15:2.1] MISHNAH: The House of Hillel say, we heard only about one who came from the grain harvest. The House of Shammai said to them, it makes no difference whether she comes from the grain harvest, or from the olive harvest, or from overseas. The Sages spoke about the grain harvest only because of what happened. The House of Hillel reversed themselves and taught following the House of Shammai.
[Yevamot 15:2.2] HALAKHAH: “The House of Hillel say, we heard only,” etc. The House of Shammai said to them: Is there not harvest the entire year? How is that? At the end of barley harvest starts wheat harvest. At the end of wheat harvest starts grape harvest. At the end of grape harvest starts olive harvest. That means, there is some harvest the year round. They accepted this argument. And why the grain harvest? {NAME} said, because there accidents are frequent, for the sun only hits a person’s head at grain harvest time. That is what is written: “The child grew and some day it went to his father, to the harvesters. He said to his father, ‘my head, my head’; who said to the servant, ‘carry him to his mother’. He carried him and brought him to his mother where he sat on her knees until noontime, when he died.” But the rabbis say, because snakes are abundant. {NAME} said, “You shielded my head at the day of kissing,” at the day summer and winter are kissing. Another explanation: “At the day of weaponry,” that is Gog’s weaponry. Another explanation, on a day when two worlds kiss one another, when this world leaves and the future world enters.
[Yevamot 15:3.1] MISHNAH: The House of Shammai say, she should remarry and collect her ketubah . The House of Hillel say, she should remarry but not collect her ketubah. The House of Shammai said to them, you permitted the stringent incest prohibition, should you not permit the lenient money matters? The House of Hillel said to them, we find that the brothers cannot access the inheritance on her testimony. The House of Shammai said, we can infer that from the text of her ketubah document in which he writes: “If you would be married to another man you shall take the amount I wrote for you.” The House of Hillel reversed themselves and taught following the House of Shammai.
[Yevamot 15:3.2] HALAKHAH: “The House of Shammai say, she should remarry,” etc. May the daughters claim upkeep based on her word?
[Yevamot 15:3.3] The House of Shammai insist on interpretation of the ketubah . As the House of Shammai explain, we can infer that from the text of her ketubah document in which he writes: “If you would be married to another man you shall take the amount I wrote for you.” The House of Hillel reversed themselves and taught following the House of Shammai. The House of Hillel insist on interpretation of the ketubah . Hillel the Elder explained it, using the vernacular. In Alexandria they were writing that a man there became betrothed to a woman. Another man abducted her from a public place. When this came before the Sages, they intended to declare [the children] as bastards. Hillel the Elder told them, bring your mothers’ ketubah . They brough their mothers’ ketubah . They found written there: “When you enter my house you shall be my wife according to the laws of Moses and the Jews.”
[Yevamot 15:3.4] {NAME} insisted on interpreting the ketubah . “{NAME} explained: ‘The sons shall inherit and the daughters shall be supported.’ Since the sons can only inherit after their father’s death, so the daughters can claim support only after their father’s death.”
[Yevamot 15:3.5] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. As {NAME} said, if somebody accepts a field as a contractor, one estimates how much it is expected to yield and give to [the owner]. Because the standard contract reads: “If I let it lie fallow and do not work on it, I shall pay as if from the best.”
[Yevamot 15:3.6] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: A person brings for his wife any sacrifice she is obligated for, even if she ate suet or desecrated the Sabbath. Also, {NAME} says, once he divorces her, he is no longer obligated for her, for she writes to him “any other obligations that come to you from earlier times.”
[Yevamot 15:3.7] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} explained: In a place where one treats the ketubah as a loan, she collects the entire amount. Where one doubles, she collects only half the amount. {NAME} [the caper grower] said, nobody is permitted to buy domesticated or wild animals or birds unless he has food prepared for them. {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text, since {NAME} said, a person lending money to another person should not take pledges from him for more than the value of the loan since he writes for him: “It will be paid by the property that came to my hand that I shall acquire corresponding to this [sum].”
[Yevamot 15:3.8] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} explained: “The sons shall inherit but the daughters must be fed.” Since the sons inherit movables, the daughters also are fed from movables. {NAME} said, the daughters are not fed from movables. A Mishnah supports {NAME}: “The female children you shall have from me shall dwell in my house and be supported from my property.” It was stated on this: From real estate but not from movables. {NAME} said: {NAME} follows Rebbi and {NAME} follows {NAME}, as it was stated: “One uses both guaranteed property and non-guaranteed property for the support of the wife and the daughters, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} says, guaranteed property may be taken by sons from sons, by daughters from daughters, by sons from daughters 59 , and by daughters from sons. But non-guaranteed property may be taken by sons from daughters but not by daughters from sons.” They said, {NAME} reversed himself. They said, that was well done, ketubah is a biblical commandment but support of the daughters is from their words. May their words uproot a biblical commandment? It must be that they differ about the money contained in their mother’s ketubah . But is the money contained in their mother’s ketubah not also real estate?
[Yevamot 15:3.9] “If somebody who works his wife’s property has the intention of divorcing her and goes and takes from the ground, he is quick and is rewarded. If somebody who works the property of prisoners heard that they prepare to return, goes and takes from the ground, he is quick and is rewarded. These are properties of prisoners: In any case where his father, brother, or any person from whom he might inherit, went overseas, he heard that they died, and he went to work the inheritance. But property of abandoning persons one takes out of their hands. These are properties of abandoning persons: In any case where his father, brother, or any person from whom he might inherit, went overseas, he did not hear that they died, but he went to work the inheritance. {NAME} said, I heard that there is no difference between prisoners and abandoning persons. But property of broken persons one takes out of their hands. These are properties of smashed persons: In any case where his father, brother, or any person from whom he might inherit, went overseas, and his whereabouts are not known.” {NAME} says, the prisoner is one who left involuntarily. If he had left voluntarily he would have given him instructions. The abandoning person is one who left voluntarily. You should know that he had the intention of keeping [the relative] off his property since he left voluntarily and did not give him instructions. {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Movables do not fall under the rules of smashed people. Rebbi{NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Standing grain ready to be harvested and grapes ready to be harvested are movables. {NAME} asked: Those date palms of Babylonia which do not need grafting, is it not reasonable that we should treat them like standing grain ready to be harvested and grapes ready to be harvested?
[Yevamot 15:4.1] MISHNAH: Everybody is accepted to be a witness for her except her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law’s daughter, her co-wife, her levir’s wife, and her husband’s daughter. What is the difference between a bill of divorce and death? The document is the proof. If one witness says that he died and she remarried, then another comes and says that he is not dead, she shall not leave. If one witness says that he died but two say that he did not die, even if she remarried she must leave. If two say that he died but one said that he did not die, even if she has not yet remarried she may remarry.
[Yevamot 15:4.2] HALAKHAH: “Everybody is accepted to be a witness for her,” etc. It was stated: “Just as they cannot be trusted for her, so she cannot be trusted about them.” Her mother-in-law’s son is like her mother-in-law’s daughter. Her husband’s son is like her husband’s daughter. Her co-wife, even if remarried. Her levir’s wife, even [if she is] her own sister. {NAME} said, a Mishnah says that they did not treat the males as they treat the females, as we have stated there: “because a woman is not trusted if she says, my levir died, that she should be free to remarry, nor that her sister died, to enter her house.” Because she has no children. But if she has children, she is trustworthy.
[Yevamot 15:4.3] Does the document prove? Do we not have to believe what she says? If she did not say ‘it was written in my presence, it was signed in my presence’, would you permit her to remarry? {NAME} said, that parallels what {NAME} said, one does not suspect him to vilify her in the eyes of Heaven; he is suspect to vilify her in the eyes of the court. Since he knows that if he were to come [and object, his objection] would not be accepted, he has [the bill of divorce] signed by witnesses in good standing. And here, since she knows that her word does not count for the other woman, she will be truthful.
[Yevamot 15:4.4] “If one witness says,” etc. “If one witness says that he died and she remarried, then another comes and says that he is not dead, she shall not leave.” Because he said that after she had remarried. Therefore if [the second witness came] before she remarried, if she remarried she has to leave. {NAME} said, these are the words of {NAME}. But the words of the Sages [are], whether he testified after she remarried or before she remarried, she should not remarry, but if she remarried she shall not leave. {NAME} said in the name of Rav, if she was married by the testimony of two witnesses, even if he returns, one says to him, “you are not he.” {NAME} asked, think of it, if he is a famous person like Immi? {NAME} said, is there nobody who would look like {NAME}? There came a case before the rabbis there. They said to him, “you are not he.” {NAME} got up and whispered in his ear saying, by your life, give her a bill of divorce because of the doubt. Rav’s students got up and beat him. Somebody said, the whip is burning and the footstool is burning. {NAME} said, I was there, no whip was burning and no footstool was burning, but my father was hit and got up. There came a case before {NAME}. He said to him, yes, it is sure that she is permitted to you but you should know that the child of this man is a bastard before Heaven. {NAME} was praising him because he made the situation clear.
[Yevamot 15:5.1] MISHNAH: One [wife] says, he died, the other one says, he did not die. The one who said that he died can remarry and collect her ketubah ; the one who said that he did not die cannot remarry nor collect her ketubah . If one said that he died, while the other one said he was killed; {NAME} says, since they contradict one another, they cannot remarry. {NAME} and {NAME} say, since both agree that he is not alive they can remarry.
[Yevamot 15:5.2] HALAKHAH: “A woman who went overseas with her husband,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} agrees in the first case. It was found stated: That is also in dispute. What is the difference between the second and the first cases? In the first case, did they not consider her word as nonexistent for her companion? {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} concede in the case of witnesses. What is the difference between witnesses and the co-wife? Did they not consider the co-wife’s words as nonexistent for her companion? {NAME} said, if {NAME} said this, he heard it from me and formulated it.
[Yevamot 15:5.3] There, we have stated: “If two groups of witnesses testified about him, one group testifying that he vowed two periods of nezirut , the other group testifying that he vowed five periods of nezirut .” Rav said, they differ in the overall testimony. But in detail, everybody agrees that five contains two, that he has to be a nazir for two periods. {NAME} said, they differ in counting. But in an overall testimony, everybody agrees that the testimonies contradict one another and there is no nezirut . What is overall and what is counting? Overall, this one says two, the other one says five. Counting, this one says one, two, the other one says three, four, five.
[Yevamot 15:5.4] Rav said, if testimony was contradicted in its essence, the testimony is not void. {NAME} said, if testimony was contradicted in itself, the testimony is void in the opinion of everybody. If testimony was contradicted in some aspects that belong after the fact, the testimony is not void. {NAME} is consistent since {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of {NAME}, if it was agreed that he counted but one [witness] said, he counted from a wallet and the other said, he counted from a bundle, that contradicts the essence of the testimony, and Rav will agree that the testimony is void. Where do they disagree? If there were two groups of witnesses, these say he counted from a wallet and the others say he counted from a bundle. That contradicts the essence of the testimony, the testimony is void but according to Rav, the testimony is not void. These say, he counted into his bosom, the others say he counted into his money-belt; everybody agrees that is contradicting testimony after the main testimony, and the testimony is not void. If one [witness] said, he killed him with a mace, the other [witness] said, he killed him with a sword, that contradicts the essence of the testimony, the testimony is void and Rav will agree that the testimony is void. Where do they disagree? If there were two groups of witnesses, these say he killed him with a mace and the others say, he killed him with a sword. That contradicts the essence of the testimony, the testimony is void but according to Rav, the testimony is not void. If these say, he ran away to the South and those say, he ran away to the North, everybody agrees that the testimony was contradictory in some aspects that belong after the fact, the testimony is not void. The strength of Rav comes from the following: “{NAME} and {NAME} say, since both agree that he is not alive they can remarry.” He did nor hear that {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} concede in the case of witnesses. What is the difference between witnesses and the co-wife? Did they not consider the co-wife’s words as nonexistent for her companion? ({NAME} said, if {NAME} said this, he heard it from me and formulated it.) A Mishnah disagrees with Rav: “Both in investigations and in cross examinations, if they contradict one another their testimony is void.” {NAME} said, Rav will explain that as referring to single witness against single witness. {NAME} said, even if you say groups and groups. There is a difference in criminal cases: “Justice, justice you shall pursue”.
[Yevamot 15:6.1] MISHNAH: One witness said that he died, another witness said that he did not die; a woman said that he died, another woman said that he did not die; she may not remarry.
[Yevamot 15:6.2] HALAKHAH: “if she says ‘my husband died’,” etc. {NAME} in the name of Rav: Anywhere they accepted the testimony of a woman parallel to that of a man, a man can contradict a woman and a woman can contradict a man. Then one should state: “A witness says that he died, and a woman says that he did not die; a woman said that he died and a witness said that he did not die.” In the House of Rebbi they stated it this way. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: One follows the majority of the testimonies. How is that? Two women against one woman they considered as if there were two witnesses against one witness. What you say refers to a woman and women. But if there were a hundred women against one [male] witness, they are like one witness.
[Yevamot 15:7.1] MISHNAH: If a woman went overseas with her husband and she returns and says “my husband died”, she can remarry and collect her ketubah , but her co-wife remains forbidden. She is suspected to cause trouble to herself in order to cause trouble to her co-wife.
