[Ketubot 1:4.1] MISHNAH: For virgins who after a final marriage become widows, divorcees, or who received ḥalîṣah , their ketubah is a mina and they are not subject to a claim of non-virginity. For a proselyte, a prisoner, and a slave who were redeemed, converted, or freed at more than three years and one day of age, their ketubah is a mina and they are not subject to a claim of non-virginity.
[Ketubot 1:4.2] HALAKHAH: “A virgin, a widow, a divorcee after final marriage,” etc. Who is a virgin after marriage? {NAME} said, any who entered the bridal chamber but her witnesses testify that she had no sexual relations. {NAME} said, this implies that if a man married a woman under the presumption that she was a virgin and she turned out not to be a virgin, that is not an erroneous acquisition to deprive her of the ketubah of a mina. If a man married a woman under the presumption that she never had illegitimate sex and she turned out that she had illegitimate sex, that is not an erroneous acquisition to deprive her of the ketubah of a mina.
[Ketubot 1:4.3] {NAME} asked, what about a male who sleeps with a manumitted slave girl? Let us hear from the following: I could think that a male who sleeps with a Gentile slave has to pay; the verse says: “He shall take her as wife by the bride price.” If he can marry her. This excludes the [gentile] slave (or any) whom he cannot marry. Only because he cannot marry her! Therefore, if he can marry her, she collects the fine, and any who collects the fine has a ketubah . {NAME} said, does that depend on a fine? Look, the adult collects no fine but her ketubah is 200, the virgin after marriage collects a fine but her ketubah is a mina! {NAME} said before {NAME}, explain it if she was converted or freed before she reached three years and one day. He said to him, any woman who was converted or manumitted before she reached three years and one day is like an Israel.
[Ketubot 1:4.4] The blind woman and the she-ram are subject to claims of missing virginity. Symmachos said in the name of {NAME} that the blind woman is not subject to claims of missing virginity. What is {NAME} reason? I say, he found [her to be a virgin] and destroyed [the evidence]. What is the rabbi’s reason? She can catch him. What does {NAME} with this argument? He can cleanse it with spittle.
[Ketubot 1:4.5] It was stated: A claim of non-virginity may be brought within thirty days, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, immediately. Where do we hold? If he copulated, immediately. If he did not copulate, even after a longer delay. But we must deal with the case that it was not spelled out. {NAME} said, it is credible that a man may hold himself back for thirty days. But the Sages say, a man does not hold himself back even for one day. {NAME} asked: According to {NAME}, would a man be believed to assert that he held himself back for thirty days in order to make the child of unknown paternity? Let us hear from the following: “If the sister-in-law claims within thirty days that she was not copulated with, one forces him to perform ḥalîṢah with her. After thirty days, one asks him to perform ḥalîṢah with her.” And {NAME} said, this is {NAME}. And {NAME} said, that refers only to her, but not to her co-wife. As you say there, she is not believed to damage her co-wife, so here, he is not believed to damage his son.
[Ketubot 1:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody eats at his father-in-law’s in Judea without chaperones cannot claim missing virginity since he is alone with her. Both for an Israel widow as a Cohanim widow the ketubah is a mina. The court of priests collected 400 zuz for a virgin, to which the Sages did not object.
[Ketubot 1:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody eats at his father-in-law’s,” etc. In earlier times they decided on a persecution in Judea because they had a tradition from their forefathers that Jehudah had killed Esaw, as it is written: “Your hand is on your enemies’ neck.” They went and enslaved them and raped their daughters; they decided that a soldier would have sex with her first. They decreed that her husband should come to her when still in her father’s house; for when she knows that her husband’s fear is on her she is drawn after him. But is she not in the end being used for sex by a soldier? She is raped, and a rape victim is permitted to her husband. What did Cohanot do? They were hiding them. Why did they not also hide the daughters of Israel? That becomes talk and the government hears it; then these and those will be taken together. What kind of a sign did they have? The talk of a cook in town: There is a wedding meal, there is a wedding meal; there is light in Beror-Ḥayil: a week for a son, a week for a son. When the persecution ended, the custom did not end. {NAME} daughter-in-law was pregnant when she married definitively.
[Ketubot 1:5.3] It was stated: “And for a widow 200.” It was stated: “This order applies both to a widow of an Israel and a widow of a Cohen”. {NAME} said, it is reasonable that the daughter of a Cohen should collect, for her tribe collects. The daughter of an Israel married to a Cohen should not collect; is it not sufficient that she rose to the priesthood that you say, she should collect? {NAME} said, it is reasonable the other way. The daughter of an Israel married to a Cohen should collect for she rose to the priesthood; the daughter of a Cohen should not collect for she stepped down from the priesthood. {NAME} said, in both cases they demanded a fine so that everybody should cling to his tribe and family.
[Ketubot 1:6.1] MISHNAH: Somebody married a woman and found that she was no virgin. She says, I was raped after you had married me preliminarily, so your field was flooded. He says not so, but it happened before I married you preliminarily; therefore, my acquisition was made in error. {NAME} and {NAME} say, she is believed. {NAME} said, we do not live off her mouth but there is a presumption that she had sexual relations before she was preliminarily married unless she provides proof of her statement.
[Ketubot 1:6.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody married a woman and found that she was no virgin”, etc. {NAME} asked: Does this mean that a claim of missing virginity is impossible following {NAME} and {NAME}, only following {NAME}? He turned around and said, a claim of missing virginity is possible following {NAME} and {NAME}, if she remains silent. And even if you say that she talks, if she said that he found her a virgin and destroyed the evidence. Why should she not be believed? One cannot tolerate it, since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, if he found the door open, he is forbidden to keep her because she might have been unfaithful. Here you say, she is believed. There, you say that she is not believed. In this case, both agree that the door was open.
[Ketubot 1:6.3] There, we have stated: “If she had bodily defects while still in her father’s house, the father has to bring proof.” {NAME} asked {NAME}: Is this Mishnah from {NAME} and {NAME}? Not from {NAME}? He said to him, those are everybody’s words. There is a difference because bodily defects have a way to appear. {NAME} said, formerly we saw rabbis who compared bodily defects to [defects of] virginity. These can be inferred from those and those can be inferred from these. Bodily defects from claims of missing virginity: For if he slept with her in her father’s house, the father has to provide proof. Claims of missing virginity from bodily defects: For if she developed bodily defects and there is a doubt whether it happened after she entered his domain or before she entered his domain, the husband has to provide proof, from claims of missing virginity. But if she lost her virginity, was it not in her father’s house? Nevertheless, you say, the husband has to provide proof; so here also, the husband has to provide proof.
[Ketubot 1:7.1] MISHNAH: She says, I was injured by wood, but he says not so, you were trampled on by a man; {NAME} and {NAME} say, she is believed. {NAME} said, we do not live off her mouth but there is a presumption that she was trampled on by a man unless she provides proof of her statement.
[Ketubot 1:7.2] HALAKHAH: “She says, I was injured by wood,” etc. {NAME} said, that follows {NAME}, since {NAME} said the ketubah of one injured by wood is 200 [ zuz ]. {NAME} said, we would think to say, when did {NAME} disagree with those rabbis? If he took her in assuming she was injured by wood. But if he took her in assuming she was a virgin and it turned out she was injured by wood, then even {NAME} agrees, since we have stated: “She says, I was injured by wood, but he says not so, you were trampled on by a man.” That means, there is a disagreement even if he took her in assuming she was injured by wood and she turned out to have been injured by wood. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} did not say so, but: She says, I was injured by wood and my ketubah is 200 [ zuz ]. He says, it is not so, but you were trampled on by a man and you have no claim on me. What are we talking about? If he married her as a virgin and she turns out to have been injured by wood, {NAME} will agree. If he married her as one injured by wood and she turns out to have been injured by wood, is there a recognizable difference in the opening of the door between wood or man? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} did not say so, but: She says, I was injured by wood and so I stipulated with you, but he says, it is not so, but you were trampled on by a man and there was no stipulation between you and me.
[Ketubot 1:8.1] MISHNAH: If she was seen speaking to a man and one asked her, what kind of man is this? He is Mr. X, a Cohen; {NAME} and {NAME} say, she is believed. {NAME} said, we do not live off her mouth but there is a presumption that she was lying with a Gibeonite and a bastard unless she provides proof of her statement.
[Ketubot 1:8.2] HALAKHAH: “If she was seen speaking to a man,” etc. What is “speaking”? She had sexual relations. Why did we state “speaking”? An expression for the knowing; Rebbi says, of purity.
[Ketubot 1:8.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME} and {NAME} since two form a majority against one. {NAME} asked: If it is practice, why two? And if two, why practice? Would that mean if {NAME} would hold with {NAME} that practice would not follow {NAME} and {NAME} but {NAME}? What about it? It is a testimony for which a woman in empowered. They wanted to say, when does {NAME} disagree with these rabbis? At a place where most are disabling, but at a place where most are qualified, even {NAME} will agree. There came {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: There is disagreement even at a place where most are qualified. Does {NAME} think that immorality runs after the disabling? {NAME} said, a baraita stated that even qualified people whore, as it was stated: Even the most pious man cannot be appointed guardian for illicit sex.
[Ketubot 1:9.1] MISHNAH: If she was pregnant and one asked her, what kind of fetus is this? He is from Mr. X, a Cohen; {NAME} and {NAME} say, she is believed. {NAME} said, we do not live off her mouth but there is a presumption that she is pregnant from a Gibeonite or a bastard unless she provides proof of her statement.
[Ketubot 1:9.2] HALAKHAH: “If she was pregnant,” etc. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that the child is of unknown paternity. It was stated thus: “Where was this said, for the testimony of the woman in her own behalf. But everybody agrees that the child is of unknown paternity.” {NAME} said to him, simply of unknown paternity! We find that a child of unknown paternity can be High Priest. How is this possible? A group of Cohanim was passing by, one of them came and had sexual relations; it turns out that the child of unknown paternity can be High Priest.
[Ketubot 1:9.3] {NAME} said to him: Is not the dough widow qualified but her daughter is disqualified? He said to him, whoever declares her to be qualified, declares her daughter to be qualified. {NAME} said, did he not say “whoever declares her to be qualified”? This implies that there is another who disqualifies! Who declares qualified? {NAME}. Who disqualifies? The rabbis. As we have stated: What is qualified dough, anyone about whom there is [no suspicion of descent from] a desecrated, a bastard, or a Gibeonite. {NAME} says, the daughter of any woman not tainted with one of these is qualified for thepriesthood. But about a family in which a disability had disappeared, {NAME} says he checks up to four mothers and marries, but the Sages say, he checks forever.
[Ketubot 1:9.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME} had a different version: {NAME} asked {NAME}, what is the rule about a dough widow? He said to him, she is qualified. What about her daughter? He said to him, the one who declares her to be qualified, declares her daughter to be qualified. They wanted to say, according to {NAME}, a child of unknown paternity is disqualified; according to {NAME}, a child of unknown paternity is qualified. {NAME} also holds that in some cases a child of unknown paternity is disqualified; he answered [{NAME}] following the latter’s reasoning: Since you reason that the child is simply of unknown paternity, we find that a child of unknown paternity can be High Priest! How is this possible? A group of Cohanim was passing by, one of them came and had sexual relations; it turns out that the child of unknown paternity can be High Priest.
[Ketubot 1:9.5] The word of {NAME} implies that a child of unknown paternity is qualified, for {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is it the same for families? He said to him, so says {NAME}: There, for families, but here for sanctified food in the country. The word of {NAME} ben [Rav] Isaac implies that a child of unknown paternity is disqualified, for {NAME} asked: Does this mean that a child of unknown paternity is does not exist following {NAME} and {NAME}, only following {NAME}? He turned around and said, a child of unknown paternity is possible following {NAME} and {NAME}, if she remains silent. And even if you say that she talks, if she said that she does not know.
[Ketubot 1:10.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} said: It happened that, when a girl was raped while she went to draw water from the spring, {NAME} said: If most people of the town can marry into the priesthood then she can marry into the priesthood.
[Ketubot 1:10.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} said: It happened,” etc. {NAME} in the name of Rav: That happened at the source of Sepphoris.
[Ketubot 1:10.3] Both {NAME}, {NAME}, say in the name of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} agrees in the case of the rape victim. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} agrees in the case of the rape victim. {NAME} said in the name of Rav: Practice follows {NAME} who said in the name of {NAME}. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: How does one act in a practical case? He said to him, following {NAME} who spoke in the name of {NAME}.
[Ketubot 1:10.4] {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: He cohabited with her inside of Sepphoris. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If he was seen coming out of Sepphoris and he cohabited, the presumption is that he disqualifies since he cohabited there. What about a thoroughfare? {NAME}, {NAME} says: By a majority. The force of {NAME} comes from the following which {NAME} had said in the name of {NAME}: If a wall fell in a dead-end street populated by Gentiles, but where one Jew lived, one digs there because of the Jew; but in a thoroughfare one follows the majority. And what is the interpretation of what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, if he was seen coming out of Sepphoris and he cohabited, the presumption is that he is disqualified since he cohabited there? In the opinion of {NAME}, if one saw him coming out of a house. In the opinion of {NAME}, even in a thoroughfare. If Sepphoris was locked. {NAME} says, until there is proof. But here, {NAME} says, by a majority! The force of {NAME} comes from the following, which {NAME} had said: Rebbi [Ḥiyya] (Yose) in the name of {NAME}: If his [box] (bread) was exchanged at the miller’s, if it was established that an am haäreẓ gave [grain] to be milled there that day, he has to worry; otherwise, he does not have to worry. Should he not worry? What is the difference between this and the Saracens? Was it not stated: “If a group of Saracens one day provisioned themselves from forbidden supplies, then that day becomes a proof for all days.” It is impossible for Saracens not to supply themselves. But here it was not established that the am haäreẓ was milling there that day. And here, I am saying that the disqualified person went to draw water only that day, and one has to worry. And here, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: He cohabited with her inside of Sepphoris. And here, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: If he was seen coming out of Sepphoris and he cohabited, the presumption is that he is disqualified since he cohabited there.
[Ketubot 1:10.5] “And everything found is judged by a majority.” In difficult cases the rabbis compare this to crawling things, as it was stated: “Nine frogs and one crawling thing in a private domain, if somebody touched one of them and it is not known which one he touched, in doubt he is impure. If he transferred to the public domain and touched, in doubt he is pure. If he returned to the private domain and touched, in doubt he is impure. And for what is found one follows the majority.” {NAME} said, no valiant person can find his hands. {NAME} said, praise to Him Who chose them and their words; do not compare this to a private domain but to the public domain! As it was stated: “Nine crawling things and one frog between them in the public domain, if somebody touched one of them and it is not known which one he touched, in doubt he is pure. If he transferred to a private domain and touched, in doubt he is impure. If he returned to the public domain and touched, in doubt he is pure. And for what is found one follows the majority.” {NAME} said, no valiant person can find his hands. {NAME} said, praise to Him Who chose them and their words; is the spring of Sepphoris not public domain? {NAME} said, since the two could be alone together it is treated as private domain.
[Ketubot 1:10.6] It happened that a baby girl was noticed who had been thrown on a garbage heap. The case came before {NAME}, who said, she should be adjoined to dough. {NAME} thought to say, to qualified dough, would {NAME} disagree with his father? {NAME} said, even if you say to disqualified dough, {NAME} would not disagree with his father. Why? While the qualified whore, only the disqualified throw away.
[Ketubot 2:1.1] MISHNAH: If a woman became widowed or divorced and she claims to have been married as a virgin, but he says not so, I married you as a widow, if there are witnesses that she went out in hinuma or with uncovered hair, her ketubah is 200 [ zuz ]. {NAME} says, the distribution of roasted kernels also is proof.
[Ketubot 2:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If a woman became widowed,” etc. We understand if she was divorced. If she became widowed, who opposes? The heirs.
[Ketubot 2:1.3] Should one follow the majority, and most women are married as virgins. Say then that she was married as a virgin! This implies that in criminal cases and in money matters one does not apply a majority argument. There, we have stated: “If an ox gored a cow and one finds her fetus beside her.” Do most cows have miscarriages? Say therefore that the goring induced the miscarriage. {NAME} said, this implies that in criminal cases and in money matters one does not apply a majority argument. {NAME} said, in one case they applied a majority argument, as {NAME} stated: If a camel was in heat among camels and one finds one of them dead, I am saying that the one in heat bit it.
[Ketubot 2:1.4] If somebody claimed a mina, the [defendant] denied it, and the [claimant] produced witnesses that the [defendant] owes him 50 [ zuz ]. The older {NAME} said, [the defendant] has to swear about the remainder. {NAME} says, he does not have to swear. The older {NAME} learned it from two who are grabbing a toga, as we have stated there: “Two are grabbing a toga, one says, I found it, and the other says, I found it.” The one who grabs half of it is as if he brought witnesses that that half belongs to him. The other says, “it belongs to me entirely”, and the fact that he grabs half of it is as if he brought witnesses that this half belongs to him. The one who says, “it belongs to me entirely”, swears that not the entire [toga] is the other’s. But he did not hear that {NAME} said in the name of {NAME} that this oath is a rabbinic institution, that a man should not see another in the market and tell him, the toga which you are wearing is mine, come and split your toga with me! {NAME} in the name of Rav: My uncle agrees in the case of a document. How is that? He claimed a mina, the [defendant] denied it, and the [claimant] produced a document that the [defendant] owed him 50 [ zuz ]. He has only fifty. And {NAME} said, we can understand it from the following: “‘The amount of … tetradrachmas’ and it was illegible, he owes no less than two. “If it is more, if the lender says five but the borrower says three, {NAME} says since he partially agreed to the claim, he has to swear, but the Sages say, what he agreed to is not of the kind which was claimed. Because it was not of the kind which was claimed! Therefore, if it were of the kind which was claimed, he would be obligated. And is it not here that the agreed sum was part of the claim? Everybody agrees that he owes her a mina. But she claimsanother mina from him, to which he does not agree. The burden of proof is on the claimant.
[Ketubot 2:1.5] “In hinuma ”. There, a veil. The rabbis here say, a phorema .
[Ketubot 2:1.6] “She went out with uncovered head.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, like those who went out on the Day of Atonement. If she went out with uncovered head, the witnesses testify that she had not been cohabitated with. Should one not worry that she was a virgin after final marriage? That means, a virgin after final marriage does not go out with uncovered head. Should one not worry that she had been injured by wood? That must follow {NAME}, since {NAME} says the ketubah of one injured by wood is 200 [ zuz ]. {NAME} said, they did not worry about infrequent occurrences.
[Ketubot 2:1.7] “{NAME} says, the distribution of roasted kernels also is proof.” Should one not worry that she was a virgin after final marriage? That means, for a virgin after final marriage one does not distribute roasted kernels. It was stated: {NAME} says, also if one brought before her an amphora of good news. Should one not worry that she was a virgin after final marriage? That means, in front of a virgin after final marriage one does not bring an amphora of good news.
[Ketubot 2:2.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} agrees that if somebody says to another: “This field did belong to your father but I bought it from him,” that he is trustworthy since the mouth which forbade is the mouth which permits. But if there are witnesses that it did belong to [the second man’s] father and [the first] said, I bought it, he is not trustworthy.
[Ketubot 2:2.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} agrees,” etc. {NAME} agrees, but he does not disagree? In the former.
[Ketubot 2:2.3] “He is not trustworthy” if he did not eat the years of legal claim from it. But if he ate the years of legal claim from it, he is trustworthy if [the second person’s] father did not die in possession. But if [the second person’s] father died in possession, he is [not] trustworthy. As the following: Reuben ate from a field claiming that it was his. Simeon brought witnesses that his father died in possession. One removes [the field] from Reuben and hands the title to Simeon. Reuben came back and brought witnesses that [Simeon’s] father did not die in possession. {NAME} said, I took it from Reuben, I am returning it to Reuben. That is what the rabbis here think. The rabbis there say, from the time it was removed, by clear testimony it was removed. So the rabbis here say, from the time she married, by clear testimony she married. {NAME} said, the rabbis there agree that if during the first proceedings two [witnesses] say that his father died in possession and two say, he did not die in possession, Reuben’s claim is upheld.
[Ketubot 2:2.4] {NAME} said, it was stated thus: “Two [witnesses] say he died, [later] two witnesses say, he did not die. She shall not remarry, but if she has remarried she should not leave. Two [witnesses] say she was divorced, [later] two witnesses say, she was not divorced. She shall not remarry; if she has remarried she must leave.” There, they say, it makes no difference; whether about death or divorce she should not leave. In the opinion of the rabbis there it is understandable, there is no difference between death and divorce. In the opinion of the rabbis here, what is the difference between death and divorce? {NAME} said it without attribution, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is reasonable to decide in the case of witnesses of death that if he returns he contradicts them. {NAME} said, the rabbis there stick to their opinion since the rabbis there say, when the [first] testimony was accepted, it was accepted as certain. So the rabbis here say, at the moment of her remarriage, she remarried based on certified testimony. {NAME} said, it is reasonable that the rabbis there did not change their argument. Do the rabbis there not agree if two [witnesses] say, his father died while in possession, [and two say his father died while not in possession,] that the field is in Reuben’s possession? Therefore, if two say, she was divorced and remarried, and two say she was not divorced, rightly she should not leave. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: “If two are saying, she was preliminarily married, and two are saying, she was not preliminarily married, she should not get married, but if she married she should not leave.” {NAME} said, {NAME} may explain it as follows: “If two are saying, she was divorced, and two are saying, she was not divorced, she should not get married, but if she married she should not leave.” What is the difference between this and the first case? There, she was considered a married woman in everybody’s opinion. Here, she is considered a married woman only for two people. If two others came and identified the man who was betrothed to her. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: “If two are saying, she was kidnapped but is pure, and two are saying, she was kidnapped and is impure, she should not get married, but if she married she should not leave.” {NAME} said, since these say, she is pure, and those say, she is impure, it is as if two said, she was kidnapped, and two said, she was not kidnapped, and we depend on what she says. If two are saying, she had been betrothed and two are saying she had not been betrothed. {NAME} compares that to fat. If two said, X ate fat, and two said, X did not eat fat, did he not have to bring a “hung” reparation sacrifice because of the doubt? Here, he should give a bill of divorce because of the doubt. {NAME} said to him, do not compare this to fat, because even if he says my conscience bothers me, he brings a “hung” reparation sacrifice. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: If two are saying she had been betrothed and two are saying she had not been betrothed, she should not get married. The end disagrees with {NAME}: If she married she must leave. {NAME} said, {NAME} did not say that she may marry, nor did {NAME} say if she married she must leave, he said only, do not compare this to fat, because even if he says my conscience bothers me, he brings a “hung” reparation sacrifice.
[Ketubot 2:3.1] MISHNAH: If witnesses said, this is our signature, but we were under duress, or underage, or disqualified, these are trustworthy. But if there are witnesses to identify their signatures, or their signatures are confirmed from another document, they are not trustworthy.
[Ketubot 2:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If witnesses said, this is our signature,” etc. It was stated: And similarly, the witnesses who testified whether to declare impure or pure, or to remove or include, or to forbid or permit, or to obligate or absolve, if they say we did invent this before their testimony was investigated by the court, they can be believed; after their testimony was investigated by the court, they are not trustworthy.” {NAME} said, they considered witnesses who signed a document as if their testimony had been investigated by the court. If they say, these are our signatures, and others say, these are their signatures, {NAME} stated: Their [testimony] does not add and does not detract. {NAME} said, our Mishnah says so, “if there are witnesses to identify their signatures, or if their signatures are confirmed from another document, they are not trustworthy.”
[Ketubot 2:3.3] They say, these are our signatures, but others say, not their signatures. {NAME} said, that becomes a document which has been put under acloud. Issi said, only if it had been put under a cloud but was confirmed by the court. {NAME} said, if it was not confirmed by a court. {NAME} said, the reason of {NAME} is, that after the witnesses were confirmed as the signatories of the document, it is as if their testimony had been investigated by the court.
[Ketubot 2:3.4] {NAME} said, one learns from a corrected scroll, like those who say, Issi’s scribe. From letters it is problematic. {NAME} said, only from three documents in the hands of three people.
[Ketubot 2:3.5] {NAME} in the name of Rav: The witnesses can be trusted if they say, that is a document given in good faith, or a document in trust. But Rav said, it is forbidden to sign a document given in good faith, or a document in trust. Does this contradict what they say in the name of Rav, the witnesses can be trusted if they say, that is a document given in good faith, or a document in trust? One word of Rav contradicts a word of Rav! {NAME} said, Rav did not say it is forbidden to sign but it is forbidden to keep. As the following, “if evil is in your hand, remove it,” that is a document given in good faith, or a document in trust, “do not let injustice dwell in your house,” that is a document of indebtedness which was paid.
[Ketubot 2:4.1] MISHNAH: If one says, this is my signature and that is my colleague’s signature, and the other says, this is my signature and that is my colleague’s signature, they are trustworthy. If each of them says, that ismy signature, each of them needs another with him, the words of Rebbi, but the Sages say, everybody is trustworthy to confirm his own signature.
[Ketubot 2:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If one says, this is my signature,” etc. Why was this necessary? For Rebbi. Even though Rebbi says, each of them needs another with him, here he agrees that they are trustworthy.
[Ketubot 2:4.3] {NAME} said: It was stated in Rav’s Ketubot : The words of Rebbi (Eleazar) that he testifies about the document, the words of the Sages that he testifies about the loan’.
[Ketubot 2:4.4] It was stated: A person may write down his testimony and testify about it even some years later. {NAME} said, only if he remembers his testimony. {NAME} said, even if he does not remember his testimony. It turns out that {NAME} follows Rebbi and {NAME}.
[Ketubot 2:4.5] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of Rav: One witness and someone from the market place cannot together certify the signature of the second witness. How is that? If one identified his own signature and that of his colleague, but that second witness’s signature was not known to anybody except his colleague, may that colleague together with somebody from the market place testify on that signature? That is what {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of Rav: One witness and someone from the market cannot together certify the signature of the second witness. Another case where there are no two persons: The signature of one is known by everybody, but that second witness’s signature is not known to anybody except his colleague. Can that colleague testify on his signature as if he were someone from the market place? If you say so, the entire testimony is confirmed by one witness. {NAME} said, that is correct. If two people come from a town that is mostly Gentile, like Hippos. One is known by everybody as a Jew, but the other is not known by anybody except his companion. Can the latter be considered one from the market place to testify about him? If you say so, the entire testimony would be confirmed by one witness! And in the prior case, the entire testimony would be confirmed by one witness.
[Ketubot 2:4.6] {NAME} said that {NAME} asked: Can one witness testifying orally and one by a document be taken together? Is a single witness on a written document worth anything? Therefore, his question was, if there are two. They managed to confirm the first signature but not the second. {NAME} asked, is one witness on a written document enough to force anybody to swear? Is a single witness on a written document worth anything? Therefore, his question was, if there are two. They managed to confirm the first signature but not the second. Parallel to it: One does not accept testimony from witnesses unless they had seen together. {NAME} says, even if they saw one after the other. {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of Rav: The Sages agree with {NAME} for witnesses about primogeniture and rights of possession.
[Ketubot 2:4.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. The same holds for testimony regarding signs. In that case, it is obvious if one says, I saw two hairs on his back and the other says, I saw two hairs on his back. If one says, I saw one hair on his back and the other says, I saw one hair on his belly, that is nothing; similarly on his back and on his back. If two say, we saw one hair on his back and two others say, we saw one hair on his belly? {NAME} and {NAME}, one said, it is invalid, but the other said, it is valid. He who saysid it is invalid considers him as one who testifies to half a sign. He who said it is valid? Maybe they were rubbed off. One says, I saw two hairs on his back and one says, I saw two hairs on his belly. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that this is valid [testimony]. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that this is invalid. {NAME} said, this is in disagreement. {NAME} said to {NAME}, does not {NAME} follow my opinion? He answered, I am disagreeing with his teacher, so much more with him. {NAME} said, {NAME} was correct. If a document was signed by four witnesses and it was disputed, if one person verified the signature of two [witnesses] and another that of the other two, is that worth anything? Does not every single signature need two witnesses? And here, every single hair needs two witnesses. {NAME} learns it from the years of possession. If one [witness] testified that he ate from the property the first, second, and third years and another [witness] testified that he ate from it the fourth, fifth, and sixth, is that worth anything? Does not every single year need two witnesses? And here, ever single hair needs two witnesses.
[Ketubot 2:5.1] MISHNAH: If a woman said, I was married but I am divorced, she is to be trusted, since the mouth which forbade is the mouth which permits. But if there are witnesses that she is married and she says, I am divorced, she is not trustworthy.
[Ketubot 2:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If a woman said, I was married,” etc. It was stated: If the witnesses came after she remarried, she should not leave. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, not only after she remarried but even after the court authorized her to remarry. As the following: A woman came to {NAME} and said to him, I was married but I am divorced, and he permitted her. After she left, they said to him, are not her witnesses at Lod? He said, so I am saying: Should she wait even if her witnesses are at קסוסנון? {NAME} said, there were two cases. In one case, they said to him, are not her witnesses at Lod? In the other case, they said to him, are not her witnesses at Caesarea? And so it was!He said to them, so I am saying: Should she wait even if her witnesses are at קסוסנון?
[Ketubot 2:5.3] {NAME} asked: “I had been married but I was divorced at place X”; if two [witnesses] come and say, no woman was divorced at place X, do they contradict her? {NAME} asked, if she said, I had been married but I was divorced at place X at a certain date,” and two came and said, a woman was divorced at that place, but two [others] came and said, no woman was divorced at that place? That is a contradiction of the essence of the testimony; we live off her mouth.
[Ketubot 2:5.4] One day, she said, I am married. The next day, she said, I am divorced. We asked her, yesterday you said this, today you say otherwise? She said to them, because of a group of amoral people who wanted to start up with me. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Since she provided an explanation for her words, she can be believed. A similar case: {NAME} wanted to sleep with his wife, but she said to him, I am impure. The next day, she said, I am pure. He said to her, yesterday, you said impure, today pure? She said to him, I did not feel well enough at that moment. He came and asked Rav, who told him, since she provided an explanation for her words, she can be believed.
[Ketubot 2:6.1] MISHNAH: 6 : If a woman said, I was kidnapped but I am pure, she is to be trusted, since the mouth which forbade is the mouth which permits. But if there are witnesses that she was kidnapped and she says, I am pure, she is not trustworthy. If the witnesses came after she was married, she should not leave.
[Ketubot 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If a woman said, I was kidnapped,” etc. {NAME} said, not only after she remarried but even after the court authorized her to remarry.
[Ketubot 2:6.3] Women were kidnapped and brought there. The case came before {NAME}, and {NAME}. They ordered and gave them over to chaperones who were to return them to the Land of Israel. He said to him: What did we do for the earlier times when they were alone with them? {NAME} said to him, would you say so if they were your daughters? {NAME}’s daughters were kidnapped, “like an error which comes from the ruler”. When they were brought here, their kidnappers came with them. They came before {NAME} and left their kidnappers outside. They said to him, we were kidnapped but we are pure. He permitted them. After they left, their kidnappers sent after them. He said, it is obvious that these are the daughters of a Sage. When they came to know who they were, they said to {NAME}, take care of your relatives. He married the first one, but she died. The second one and she died. Why? Because they lied? God forbid, they did not lie. But because of the sin of Ḥanania, {NAME} nephew, who intercalated the year outside the Land.
[Ketubot 2:7.1] MISHNAH: Two women who were kidnapped and each one of them says I am pure, are not trustworthy. But if they testify one for the other they can be trusted. Similarly, if of two men each one says that he is a Cohen, the cannot be trusted. But if they testify for one another, they can be trusted.
[Ketubot 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: “Similarly, if of two men,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah is valid for countryside sanctified food. But for family matters and the sanctified food of the altar one needs two witnesses. But was it not stated: One raises to priesthood, levitic status, or Israel, by the testimony of one witness. One understands priesthood and levitic status. But the status of an Israel? Is that not regarding family status? To give him the tithe of the poor.
[Ketubot 2:7.3] “In the Land of Israel there are two legal claims to priestly status, the priestly blessings and the distribution from the threshing floor. In Syria, priestly blessings but not distribution from the threshing floor. Up to the place where the messengers for the New Moon arrive, up to Nimerin. Babylonia is like Syria. {NAME} says, also in Alexandria in the time when regular courts are sitting there. {NAME} stated: Just as heave establishes a legal claim to priesthood, so First Tithe establishes a legal claim to priesthood. If somebody gives his heave to the court to distribute he has no legal claim to priesthood;” I am saying that the heave came to him from his mother’s father, a Cohen.
[Ketubot 2:7.4] {NAME} said, I never testified except once, when I raised a slave to priestly status. {NAME} Ḥaqula and {NAME}, one raised a brother on the testimony of his brother, the other a son on the testimony of his father; one to the priesthood, the other to levitic status. A person came before {NAME}; he said to him, this is my son and he is a Cohen. He answered him, he is your son but he is no Cohen. {NAME} the elder said to him, if you believe him that he is his son, believe him that he is a Cohen. If you do not believe him that he is his son, do not believe him that he is a Cohen. He answered, he is his son but I say that he is the son of a divorcee or one who had performed ḥalîṣah . {NAME} said, so he said to him: If you believe him that he is his son, believe him that he is a Cohen. If you do not believe him that he is a Cohen, do not believe him that he is his son. In that case, he would be unrelated and trustworthy in his testimony! He answered, he is his son but I say that he is the son of a divorcee or one who had performed ḥalîṣah . Did they not say, {NAME} Ḥaqula and {NAME}, one raised a brother on the testimony of his brother, the other a son on the testimony of his father? Let us say that Rebbi elevated a brother on the testimony of his brother. You may even say, a son on the testimony of his father, to levitic status.
[Ketubot 2:8.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, one does not elevate to the priesthood by the testimony of one witness. {NAME} said, when is this? If there are protesters; but if there are no protesters, one elevates to the priesthood by the testimony of one witness. {NAME} says in the name of {NAME}, the son of the second in command, that one elevates to the priesthood by the testimony of one witness.
[Ketubot 2:8.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} says, one does not elevate,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A complaint needs at least two [plaintiffs]. {NAME} asked, how do we hold? If they elevated him on the testimony of one person, they should demote him on the testimony of one person. If they elevated him on the testimony of two persons, even if there are many [opposed] they should not demote him! {NAME} said, it follows the rabbis there. But following the rabbis here and {NAME}, just as one elevates him on the testimony of two persons, one demotes him on the testimony of two persons.
[Ketubot 2:9.1] MISHNAH: A woman who was jailed by Gentiles, if because of money matters, she is permitted to her husband; if because of criminal matters, she is prohibited to her husband. If a city was conquered after a siege, all wives of priests in it are disqualified; but if they have witnesses, even a slave, even a slave girl, those are trustworthy; but nobody is trustworthy about himself. {NAME}, the son of the butcher, said, by the Temple! Her hand did not leave my hand from the moment the Gentiles entered Jerusalem until they left! They said to him, nobody testifies on his own behalf.
[Ketubot 2:9.2] HALAKHAH: “A woman who was jailed by Gentiles,” etc. There, we have stated: “{NAME} and {NAME} the son of the butcher testified about a girl who was given as a pledge in Ascalon and her family excluded her, but her witnesses testified that she never was in a secret place and was not impure.” Because the witnesses testified that she never was in a secret place and was not impure; therefore, not if no witnesses testified that she never was in a secret place and was not impure! {NAME} said, there is a difference about a pledge, because many treat her as permitted.
[Ketubot 2:9.3] “If because of criminal matters she is prohibited.” {NAME} Teḥumim in the name of {NAME}: Only if she was sentenced to death. {NAME} said, even if she was not sentenced to death. They said in the name of {NAME}: A robber’s wife is like a robber’.
[Ketubot 2:9.4] What are palisades? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: For examples if bells, chains, and ropes, and geese, and chickens and machinery surround the town. And {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, it happened that a blind woman was able to flee from there. If there was one breach, it saves all. If there were hiding places, it is questionable. {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME} the prince: Only if there were palisades of that government. But palisades from another government are like robbers.
[Ketubot 2:9.5] And even a minor. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even a minor, even a relative. Even an underage relative? Let us hear from the following: Ḥananiah from Cartes was kidnapped, he, his son, and his wife. They came before {NAME} who did not receive them. They came before {NAME} who received them. This implies, even an underage relative.
[Ketubot 2:9.6] {NAME} sent after his wife. He said, three students should accompany her, so that if one has to absent himself for his needs, she should still be with two of them. But did we not state: “And they give him two scholars to prevent him from sleeping with her on the trip”? {NAME} said, with her husband that makes three. Also he rented a house for her and looked after her upkeep but was never alone with her except in the presence of her children. He applied to himself the verse: “I exercised myself in my worry but found no rest”.
[Ketubot 2:10.1] MISHNAH: In the following cases, one is trustworthy to testify as an adult about what one saw in one’s minority. A man is trustworthy to say, this is my father’s handwriting, my teacher’s handwriting, my brother’s handwriting; I remember that this person went out in hinuma and uncovered hair, or that this man left school to immerse himself to eat heave, or that he took his part with us on the threshing floor, or that this place is bet happeras , or this far we went on the Sabbath. But a person is not trustworthy to say that X had a right of way at this place, or that X had a space for eulogies at this place.
[Ketubot 2:10.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: Only these which they are used to. It was stated: Only if they are supported by others.
[Ketubot 2:10.3] Should one not worry that he might be a slave? This supports what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: It is forbidden for a man to teach Torah to his slave. But did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: A slave is counted as one of the seven readers; wayedabber is counted as one of three verses! Explain it, if he learned it by himself or his master taught him like Tebi. Should one not worry that he might be a slave? This supports what {NAME} stated: Women and slaves cannot share in the distribution on the threshing floor, but one gives them the gifts of priesthood and levitic status from the house.
[Ketubot 2:10.4] May one act in money matters on their testimony? How is that? If everybody knew that the Sabbath boundary was at Reuben’s field; they came and said, this far we came on the Sabbath, and it turns out that this field is in Simeon’s hand. May one take it from Simeon and return it to Reuben?
[Ketubot 2:10.5] Would they be trustworthy to say, we went out to collect unripe figs in the sabbatical year and heard X talking about his wife Y, or woman Z talking about her children?
[Ketubot 2:10.6] {NAME}, {NAME} asked: If they were proven to be false witnesses, do they have to pay? Or it might be, following what {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of {NAME}: One does not infer one thing from another in the matter of false witnesses. And here it is so.
[Ketubot 2:10.7] It was stated: “That we ate in X or Y’s clipping.” What is clipping? If a man sold his inherited field, his relatives filled amphoras with roasted kernels and nuts and broke them before children. The children were collecting them and saying, X was clipped from his inheritance. When he bought it back, they were doing the same and saying, X returned to his inheritance. {NAME} said, also if a man married an unsuitable woman, his realtives filled amphoras with roasted kernels and nuts and broke them before children. The children were collecting them and saying, X was clipped from his family. Whe he divorced her, they were doing the same and saying, X returned to his family.
[Ketubot 2:10.8] “In the following cases, one is trustworthy to testify as an adult about what he saw in his minority,” etc. They are only trustworthy as adults about what they saw as minors; therefore, not as minors! There, we have stated: “A woman or a minor are trustworthy when they said, from there a swarm of bees left. He then can enter another’s field and take his swarm.” And here, you say so? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} said this only about a swarm of bees because taking it is not robbery by biblical standards. {NAME} stated, only if it is swarming. But not if it clings to a branch. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is that not reasonable only when it happens, but not after some time? He said to him, I agree. And we have stated: When is this said? When they testified to what they said. But if they left and came back, I am saying that they speak out of fear or were seduced.
[Ketubot 3:1.1] MISHNAH: The following adolescent girls can claim a fine: From someone who has intercourse with a bastard girl, or a Gibeonite or a Samaritan girl, and one who comes to a female proselyte, a kidnap victim, or a slave girl who was redeemed, converted, or freed, at less than three years and one day of age. Also from one who has intercourse with his sister, or his father’s sister, or his mother’s sister, or his wife’s sister, or his brother’s wife, or his paternal uncle’s wife, or a menstruating girl; he has to pay the fine since it is not a capital crime even though he is subject to extirpation.
[Ketubot 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The following adolescent girls,” etc. It is written: “She should be his wife,” one who can be his wife. Can the bastard girl be his wife? {NAME} said, “he should weigh silver appropriate for the bride-price of virgins”, that added many virgins. {NAME} said, if it had said “virgin’s brides-prices”; but it says only “appropriate for the bride-price of virgins”; the verse added them only for the bride-price. But where was this said? As {NAME} stated: “If refusing her father should refuse,” not only if her father refuses; from where even if from Heaven they refuse? The verse says “refusing should refuse”, in any case. But then a man who has intercourse with a slave girl should pay the fine! This is impossible, as it was stated: I could think that one who has intercourse with a Gentile slave-girl should be obligated, the verse says, “by bride-money he should take her as a wife to himself.” Only one whom he can marry; this excludes the Gentile slave whom he cannot marry. But he cannot marry his sister and he pays the fine! There is a difference since she can be married to others. But his daughter can be married to others and he does not pay the fine! There is a difference since it is a capital crime and nobody who commits a capital crime pays money.
[Ketubot 3:1.3] “The Gibeonite.” {NAME} said, they were worried about them only because of the detriment to the families. Could you not say, because of the disability of slaves? If that were true, one who cohabits with a Gibeonite would not be subject to a fine; but we have stated: One who cohabits with a Gibeonite is subject to a fine.
[Ketubot 3:1.4] “A Samaritan.” That follows him who said, a Samaritan is a like full Jew. But for him who says that a Samaritan is like a Gentile, it is not so. As they disagreed: A Samaritan is like a Gentile, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} said, a Samaritan is like a Jew in every respect. Even if you say, a Samaritan is like a Gentile, why are Samaritans disqualified? Not because of a Gentile and a slave? If a Gentile or a slave has intercourse with a Jewish woman, the child is a bastard. But a bastard girl can claim a fine! For restrictions or family relations you consider him a Gentile or a slave who had intercourse with a Jewish woman; the child is a bastard. But for a fine you consider this as a Jew having intercourse with a Gentile woman, in which case the child is a Gentile.
[Ketubot 3:1.5] {NAME} said, a man who rapes or seduces an orphan girl does not have to pay. {NAME} said, that is a disagreement, it follows {NAME}. But following {NAME} she can claim the fine and the fine becomes her property. {NAME} said, the Mishnah said “at less than three years and one day of age,” and is she not like an orphan? And did we not state: “Because he raped her,” that includes an orphan for a fine, the words of {NAME}? {NAME} said, explain it that he had intercourse with her when her father was alive; when her father died, he already had the obligation to give to her father.
[Ketubot 3:1.6] There, we have stated: “If somebody eats heave intentionally, he pays the principal but not the fifth.” And we have stated: “The following are flogged.” Here you say, he is flogged, and there you say, he pays. {NAME} said, the Mishnah is two-sided: If he was cautioned, he is flogged; if he was not cautioned, he pays. {NAME} is of the opinion that in a case where there is flogging or restitution, when he pays he is not flogged. Why should he not be flogged and have to pay? ( Deut . 25:2 ) “Corresponding to his guilt.” You sentence him for one offence but you may not sentence him for two offences. The verse speaks of one who may incur two punishments ( Deut . 25:2 ): “The judge shall have him laid down and flogged in his presence a number [of times] because of his guilt.”
[Ketubot 3:1.7] {NAME} said, even if he was not cautioned should he not pay since when cautioned he would be flogged? A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If somebody eats heave in error, he pays principal and fifth,” but if he was cautioned, will he not be flogged? He explains it following {NAME} since {NAME} said, he is flogged and pays. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}, as we have stated: “The following adolescent girls can claim a fine,” but if he was cautioned, will he not be flogged? He explains it following {NAME} since {NAME} said, he is flogged and pays. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} learned from the calumniator. ( Deut . 22:18 ) “They shall punish him,” flogging; ( Deut . 22:19 ) “and they shall fine him”, money. But the rabbis say, [the law of] the calumniator is separate because of its novelty; one cannot learn from a novelty! Because nowhere else will a person become guilty by speech, but here he becomes guilty by speech; therefore, nothing can be inferred. Another explanation: one cannot transfer the rules of either payment or flogging. Did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: If he [eats] fat in error but is intentional about the sacrifice, if he was cautioned he will be flogged and has to bring a sacrifice? So here, he is flogged and he pays. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, ( Deut . 25:2 ) “Because of his guilt.” If two possibilities are given to the court, one chooses one of them. This excludes matters in the power of Heaven.
[Ketubot 3:1.8] Everybody agrees that there is no money payment in capital cases, as it is written ( Lev . 24:21 ): “The slayer of an animal must pay for it but the slayer of a human shall be put to death.” Just as you did not make a difference between unintentional and intentional action of a slayer of an animal to force him to pay money, so you should not make a difference between unintentional and intentional action of a slayer of a human to free him from paying money. Where do they differ? About money in a flogging case. {NAME} said, there is no money in a capital case but there is money in a flogging case, but {NAME} said, just as there is no money in a capital case so there is no money in a flogging case.
[Ketubot 3:1.9] {NAME} in the name of the rabbis from there: The reason of {NAME} is “criminal, criminal.” “Criminal” is mentioned in capital cases, “criminal” is mentioned in cases of flogging. Just as for the criminal in capital cases there is no monetary fine, so for the criminal mentioned in flogging cases there is no monetary fine.
[Ketubot 3:1.10] {NAME} said, one speaks about an adolescent girl, the other about an adult woman. The adolescent has a fine but nobody is flogged for her; for the adult he is flogged but pays no fine, she cannot be sold; she has no claim for shame and blemish. {NAME} said, explain it that she seduced him or remitted [the fine] for him. {NAME} thinks that in a case of flogging and payment he pays but is not flogged. Why should he not be flogged and have to pay? ( Deut . 25:2 ) “Because of his guilt.” You sentence him for one offence but you may not sentence him for two offences. From perjured witnesses. Just as you say there, perjured witnesses pay but are not flogged, here also he pays and is not flogged. {NAME} said, the reason of {NAME}: ( Deut . 25:2 ): “For his evil deed.” It refers to one whose flogging frees him from his guilt, excluding one who is told: get up and pay.
[Ketubot 3:1.11] Our Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}! “If somebody eats heave intentionally he pays the principal but not the fifth.” In the opinion of {NAME} who said he pays, it is understandable. In the opinion of {NAME} who said, if he was cautioned he is flogged, but if he was not cautioned he pays, he explains it as intentional without cautioning. In the opinion of {NAME} there is no difference between intentional and unintentional, between cautioned or not cautioned. He explains following {NAME} who says, he is flogged and he pays.
[Ketubot 3:1.12] {NAME} said before {NAME}: Even if {NAME} thought the entire Mishnaiot were {NAME}, does the verse agree with {NAME}? Is it not written ( Lev . 22:14 ): “If a person ate consecrated food in error”? But {NAME} must hold that the fifth is a sacrifice. But even if he holds that the fifth is a sacrifice, can the principal be a sacrifice? {NAME} said, the Mishnah declares that the principal is a fine, as we have stated: “He does not pay in heave but in totally profane food which is turned into heave.” If he had to pay from what he ate, it would be fine. And it was stated: “If he ate impure heave, he has to pay in pure profane food, but if he paid in impure profane, he discharged his obligation.” Does he not owe him the price of wood? That shows that the principal is a fine and since the principal is a fine, the fifth also is a fine. But {NAME} follows his own opinion. Just as {NAME} said, there, everybody was under the obligation of ( Ex . 20:16 ) “Do not become a false witness against your neighbor”, but this one was treated separately, ( Deut . 19:19 ) “do to him what he intended to do to his brother”, to pay money; also here, everybody was under the obligation of ( Lev . 22:10 ) “no outsider shall eat holy [food],” but this one was treated separately, ( Lev . 22:14 ) “if somebody should eat holy [food] in error,” to pay money.
[Ketubot 3:1.13] Did we not state: The Sages admit to {NAME} that one who stole his neighbor’s heave is flogged and has to pay since whoever eats heave is flogged. Did we not state: The Sages admit to {NAME} that one who stole his neighbor’s fat is flogged and has to pay since whoever eats fat is flogged. Did we not state: The Sages admit to {NAME} that one who muzzled his neighbor’s cow is flogged and has to pay six qab per cow and four qab for a donkey since whoever muzzles his cow is flogged. {NAME} said, the same holds if death is the penalty. If he stole Temple heave and ate it, he is whipped and has to pay since in any case he caused monetary loss.
[Ketubot 3:1.14] {NAME} said before {NAME}: If it is so, he who sleeps with his minor sister should be flogged and have to pay since if he sleeps with his adult sister he is flogged. He reversed himself and said, there death and payment fall on him simultaneously. But here, when he muzzled he is subject to flogging but only later for payment. {NAME} objected before {NAME}: He who sets fire to his neighbor’s grain stack on the Sabbath is subject to capital punishment from the first ear but only later for payment! One cannot say that because for every single ear there is cautioning for the death penalty. Here also, for every moment of muzzling there is cautioning for flogging. {NAME} said, two Amoraïm. One said, if he muzzled for heave which is Temple property. The other one said, if he muzzled through an agent. Then the agent is flogged and he is free ( Lev . 17:4 ): “As a blood guilt it will be charged on this man,” not on his employers.
[Ketubot 3:1.15] In error for heave and intentional for leavened, in error for heave and intentional for nazir , in error for heave and intentional for the Day of Atonement. If one explains it with two things, it is fine. If one explains it for one, this is the disagreement of {NAME} and {NAME}.

From where if he came upon her otherwise? The verse says, “and he calumniates her”, in any way. “He said, I took this wife and came to her,” that excludes assignations; “I took”, to exclude the one waiting for her levir; “I took”, to exclude the preliminarily married one.
[Ketubot 4:4.4] “I took”, that excludes assignations. {NAME} said, even following him who says that the money from the start was given for assignation. “I took”, to exclude the one waiting for her levir; not only for the earlier teachings that the obligation of the levirate precedes that of ḥalîṣah , but even according to the later teachings that the obligation of ḥalîṣah precedes the obligation of levirate. “I took”, to exclude the preliminarily married one.
[Ketubot 4:4.5] “I came to her and did not find her a virgin.” Should we not worry that he found and made disappear? The husband brought witnesses that she committed adultery while in her father’s house. “This is proof of my daughters virginity.” Should we not worry that this is bird’s blood? The father brought witnesses to prove perjury by the husband’s witnesses. {NAME} said, in this paragraph there are witnesses, witnesses of perjury, and witnesses of perjury of the witnesses of perjury: The husband says, these are witnesses that she whored in her father’s house. The father brought witnesses to prove perjury of the husband’s witnesses. {NAME} said: The father brought witnesses to prove perjury of the husband’s witnesses. And the husband brought witnesses to prove perjury of the father’s witnesses. Some Tannaïm state: “If this was true,” that the father found witnesses to prove perjury of the husband’s witnesses.
[Ketubot 4:4.6] “And they spread out the cloth.” That is all simile. {NAME} stated: That is one of three verses in the Torah which have been written as simile. “If he gets up and walks outside on his support, the one who hit him is not prosecuted.” Could anybody think that one walks in the market and the other is executed because of him? But what is “on his support”, in his health. “If the sun shone on him, he has blood.” Does the sun shine only on him? But just as the sun is particular that it brings peace to the entire world, so also this one, if one knows that [the other] is at peace with him and he kills him, he is guilty.
[Ketubot 4:4.7] It was stated: {NAME} says, the words should be said as they are written. What means “the words should be said as they are written”? {NAME} said, he is not guilty unless he marries her definitively, has intercourse, and accuses her not to be a virgin. “They spread the cloth”. Not that “they spread the cloth” but until the things become clear like a cloth. {NAME} said, “they spread the cloth”, the witnesses are not stoned, nor is the husband flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas, until they say: you were with us at a certain place, and the husband hired them to testify falsely. If they said, you were with us at a certain place, but they did not say, the husband hired them to testify falsely? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is said here “putting”, it is said there “putting”. Since “putting” there means money, also “putting” here must mean money. But did we not state: He did not say to the witnesses, come and testify in my case, but they came on their own, he is not flogged nor does he pay 100 tetradrachmas but either she or the false witnesses would be stoned’? Because he did not say. But if he said, even if he did not hire them it is as if he hired them. If the father brought two groups of witnesses. One side say, you were with us at a certain place. The other side say, the husband hired them to testify falsely. It is obvious that those who said, you were with us at a certain place, are stoned, and those who said, the husband hired them to testify falsely, are flogged and pay 100 tetradrachmas. {NAME} said, neither by these not by those are they flogged and pay 100 tetradrachmas, but they are flogged because of “you shall not testify as a false witness against your fellow man.”
[Ketubot 4:4.8] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If the father brought witnesses to prove the perjury of the husband’s witnesses; but the father’s witnesses were proven perjurers, is he flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas by the judgment of three and the witnesses are stoned by the judgment of 23? He said to him, if the father’s witnesses are not proven perjurers, is not the husband flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas by the judgment of three and the witnesses are stoned by the judgment of 23? {NAME} is of the opinion that there are two different proceedings. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: There is only one proceeding. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: “To the town’s Elders”, that is a court of three members; “to the gate”, that is a court of 23. He explains it following {NAME}, since {NAME} says that he is flogged and pays. There, we have stated: “The seducer, the rapist, and the calumniator [are judged] by three [judges], the words of {NAME}; but the Sages say, the calumniator by 23 since it is a potential capital case.” {NAME} said, they disagree about the preliminarily married adolescent. {NAME} says, she loses her ketubah in a court of three and is stoned by a court of 23; but the Sages say, at the same place which sentences her to be stoned she loses her ketubah . But in the case of the calumniator, everybody agrees that by the court in which the witnesses are stoned, the husband is flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas. {NAME} said to him, would they differ where it was not stated? But they differ about the calumniator! {NAME} says, he is flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas by the judgment of three and the witnesses are stoned by the judgment of 23; but the rabbis say, by the court in which the witnesses are stoned, the husband is flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas. But by the case of the preliminarily married adolescent, everybody agrees that at the same place which sentences her to be stoned she loses her ketubah . [It turns out that {NAME} follows {NAME} and {NAME} [follows] {NAME}].
[Ketubot 4:4.9] The husband is never flogged, nor does he pay 100 tetradrachmas, unless the witnesses are stoned. When is he obligated for the fine? {NAME} said, at the end. {NAME} said, from the first hour. {NAME} objected to {NAME}: In your opinion, since you say at the end, can he be flogged and made to pay 100 tetradrachmas by a court of three and the witnesses stoned by a court of 23? {NAME} said, even according to {NAME} one could ask the question following him who holds that perjured witnesses need to be warned. If they did not warn them, is he flogged and made to pay 100 tetradrachmas by a court of three; are the witnesses stoned by a court of 23? {NAME} said, who is that who says so?
[Ketubot 4:4.10] {NAME}: One who rapes or seduces an orphan is free. {NAME} said, this is in dispute; following {NAME}. But following {NAME} a fine is due, and the fine belongs to herself. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says so: “She has neither a door to her father’s house nor 100 tetradrachmas;” is she not like an orphan? {NAME} and {NAME} both say, one who calumniates an underage girl is free. {NAME} said, that is correct. If she were an adult who was not warned, would there be any case? And an underage girl who was warned is like an adult who was not warned.
[Ketubot 4:4.11] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: She cannot be executed unless she is an adolescent at the time of the execution. What is the reason? “They shall execute the adolescent at her father’s door.” But did not {NAME} state: If she whored in her father’s house and [the husband] calumniated her after she became an adult, he is not flogged nor does he pay 100 tetradrachmas but either she or the witnesses are executed by stoning. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If he escaped after being sentenced and then his pubic hair grew fully.” There, you can say “they shall execute the adolescent” who whored; can you say here “they shall execute him”, the son?
[Ketubot 4:4.12] It was stated: One stones a preliminarily married adolescent girl who whored at her father’s door. If she does not have a father’s house’s door one stones her where she whored. If it was a Gentile town one stones her at the court’s door. Also, a person who practiced idolatry one stones at the place where he worshipped. If it was a Gentile town one stones him at the court’s door. But did not {NAME} state: “Take the blasphemer out from the encampment,” this teaches that the court sits inside and the place of stoning is outside. {NAME} said, there is a difference: The place where he went astray is the place where he was found, is the place where he was judged, is the place where he was stoned. “For she did a foul deed in Israel.” This one befouled all of Israel, for she came to whore in her father’s house. The bad growth they grew shall come and foul up them and their growth.
[Ketubot 4:6.1] MISHNAH: The father has the benefit to give his daughter in preliminary marriage by money, contract, or intercourse; he has the right to what she finds and to her earnings, to dissolve her vows, and to receive her bill of divorce, but cannot eat usufruct in her lifetime. If she is definitively married, the husband in addition eats usufruct in her lifetime but is required to pay for her upkeep, her ransom, and her burial. {NAME} says, even the poorest in Israel should not provide for her less than two flutes and one wailing woman.
[Ketubot 4:6.2] HALAKHAH: “The father has the benefit to give his daughter,” etc. One understands that the father has a benefit from money or contract. By intercourse? Explain it that [the groom] said to [the father]: When your daughter becomes mine by intercourse, this money shall be your property.
[Ketubot 4:6.3] “He has the right to what she finds.” {NAME} asked: How do you treat what she found on [her] field, as a find or as her usufruct? If you treat it as usufruct it is hers..
[Ketubot 4:6.4] “If she is definitively married, the husband in addition eats usufruct in her lifetime,” as a regulation they instituted that he should oversee his wife’s property and eat from it. Is it also thus for the father? Without incentives the father overseas the daughter’s property; should he eat? “He is required to pay for her upkeep and her ransom.” It was stated: If the husband said, it is impossible for me to eat and to oversee, one does not listen to him; but if the father said, I shall oversee if I can eat, one listens to him.
[Ketubot 4:6.5] “And her burial.” It was stated: If the husband refused to bury her, the father buries her and recovers his expenses in court. {NAME} said, they said only, the father. Therefore, a third party cannot recover. {NAME} says, both the father and also a third party can recover. There is a parallel disagreement, as we have stated there: “He is required to pay for her upkeep, her ransom, and her burial.” {NAME} said, they said only, a third party. Therefore, the father can recover. {NAME} says, neither the father nor a third party can recover. In the opinion of {NAME}, both for burial and for upkeep the father can recover, a third party cannot recover. In the opinion of {NAME}, for burial both the father and also a third party can recover because it is unthinkable that his wife should be thrown to the dogs. It was stated: At a place where it is customary to eulogize, one eulogizes.
[Ketubot 4:7.1] MISHNAH: She always remains in the father’s power until she enters the husband’s power for definitive marriage. If the father entrusted her to the husband’s emissaries she is in the husband’s power. If the father went with the husband’s emissaries, or the father’s emissaries went with the husband’s emissaries, she is in the father’s power. If the father’s emissaries entrusted her to the husband’s emissaries, she is in the husband’s power.
[Ketubot 4:7.2] HALAKHAH: “She always remains in the father’s power,” etc. Not only to the bridal chamber but to a house where the bridal chamber is. In which way? A banquet hall and a bedroom, the bridal chamber being the bedroom, and she entered the banquest hall. In which respect? {NAME} said, to inherit from her. {NAME} said, to dissolve her vows. {NAME} said, even though {NAME} said, to dissolve her vows, he agrees that he does not actually dissolve them until she enters the bridal chamber. {NAME} said, a baraita supports {NAME}: “To whore in her father’s house,” that excludes the case that the father’s emissaries entrusted her to the husband’s emissaries, after which she should not be stoned but strangled.
[Ketubot 4:8.1] MISHNAH: The father is not obligated to support his daughter. This inference did {NAME} explain in the vineyard of Jabneh: “The sons shall inherit and the daughters be supported.” Since the sons do not inherit before their father’s death, neither are the daughters supported before their father’s death.
[Ketubot 4:8.2] HALAKHAH: “The father is not obligated to support his daughter,” etc. It is meritorious to feed one’s daughters, unnecessary to say this of sons. {NAME} said, it is meritorious to feed one’s daughters. Some Tannaim state, the sons are most important. Some Tannaim state, the daughters are most important. He who says the sons are most important, for the study of Torah. He who says the daughters are most important, that they should not go outside for bad behavior.

[Ketubot 4:8.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They voted in Usha that one who insults an Elder or hits him has to indemnify him fully for his shame. It happened, that somebody who insulted an Elder and hit him had to indemnify him fully for his shame. They said, it happened to {NAME}.

But lest he die in the future.
[Ketubot 4:8.8] {NAME} insisted on interpreting the ketubah : {NAME} explained: ‘The sons shall inherit and the daughters shall be supported.’ Since the sons can only inherit after their father’s death, so the daughters can claim support only after their father’s death.
[Ketubot 4:8.9] The House of Hillel insist on interpretation of the ketubah. Hillel the Elder explained it, using the vernacular. In Alexandria they were writing that a man there became betrothed to a woman. Another man abducted her from a public place. When this came before the Sages, they intended to declare [the children] as bastards. Hillel the Elder told them, bring your mothers’ ketubah. They brough their mothers’ ketubah. They found written there: “When you enter my house you shall be my wife according to the laws of Moses and the Jews.”
[Ketubot 4:8.10] The House of Shammai insist on interpretation of the ketubah. As the House of Shammai explain, the text of her ketubah document teaches, for he writes: “If you would be married to another man you shall take the amount I wrote for you.” The House of Hillel reversed themselves and taught following the House of Shammai.
[Ketubot 4:8.11] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} explained, if somebody accepts a field as a contractor, at the moment [he] accepts, one estimates how much it is expected to yield and he gives to [the owner]. Because the standard contract reads: “If I let it lie fallow and do not work on it, I shall pay as if from the best.”
[Ketubot 4:8.12] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} explained: A man brings for his wife any sacrifice she is obligated for, even if she ate suet or desecrated the Sabbath. Also, {NAME} says, once he divorces her, he is no longer obligated for her, for she writes to him “any other obligations that may come to you from me from earlier times.”
[Ketubot 4:8.13] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} explained: In a place where one treats the ketubah as a loan, she collects the entire amount. Where one doubles, she collects only half the amount. {NAME} the caper grower insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} the caper grower explained: nobody is permitted to buy domesticated or wild animals or birds unless he has food prepared for them. {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} explained: a person lending money to another person should not take pledges except in court; he should not enter [the debtor’s] house to take the pledge, for he writes to him: “It will be paid by the property that came to my hand that I shall acquire corresponding to this [sum].”
[Ketubot 4:8.14] {NAME} insists on interpreting the contract text. {NAME} explained: “The sons shall inherit but the daughters must be fed.” Since the sons inherit movables, the daughters also are fed from movables. {NAME} said, the daughters are not fed from movables. It must be that they differ about the money contained in their mother’s ketubah. [Even if you say, they differ about the money contained in their mother’s ketubah. ] But is the money stipulated in their mother’s ketubah not also real estate?
[Ketubot 4:8.15] “If somebody who works his wife’s property has the intention of divorcing her and goes and takes from the ground, he is quick and is rewarded. If somebody who works the property of prisoners heard that they prepare to return, goes and takes from the ground, he is quick and is rewarded. These are properties of prisoners: In any case where his father, brother, or any person from whom he might inherit, went overseas; it was heard that they died, and he went to work the inheritance. But property of abandoning persons one takes out of their hands. These are properties of abandoning persons: In any case where his father or any person from whom he might inherit went overseas, he did not hear that they died, but he went to work the inheritance. {NAME} said, I heard that there is no difference between prisoners and abandoning persons. But property of broken persons one takes out of their hands. These are properties of broken persons: In any case where his father, brother, or any person from whom he might inherit, went overseas, and his whereabouts are not known. {NAME} says, the prisoner is one who left involuntarily. If he had left voluntarily he would have given him instructions. The abandoning person is one who left voluntarily. You should know that he had the intention of keeping [the relative] off his property since he left voluntarily and did not give him instructions. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Movables do not fall under the rules of broken people. {NAME} in the name of Rav: Those date palms of Babylonia which do not need grafting, is it not reasonable that we should treat them like standing grain ready to be harvested and grapes ready to be harvested?

[Ketubot 4:12.1] MISHNAH: “The female children you will have by me shall live in my house and be supported by my estate until they are married to men”; he is obligated, for this is a stipulation enforced by the court.
