[Ketubot 5:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Even though they said that a virgin collects 200,” etc. How does he become indebted to her? Do not {NAME} and {NAME} both say, if somebody writes a debenture for another person under the assumption that he owes him and it turns out that he does not owe, [he does not have] to give to him! He wants to give much to be called X’s son-in-law. That is, if he decided this at the time of the preliminary marriage. What if he decided this at the time of the definitive marriage? He wants to give much for sexual relations with her, which are sweet. That is if he slept with her. If he did not sleep with her? He wants to give much for the acquisition he made. If he had decided at the preliminary marriage, at the definitive marriage, he already is called X’s son-in-law, sexual relations are nothing new, there is no new acquisition; from thereon he wants to give much that she should not change her mind. But can she? Was it not stated that “a man divorces only by his own will”? {NAME} said, she makes his life miserable and he frees her.
[Ketubot 5:1.3] It was stated: Just as the husband decides, so the father decides; only that the husband transfers rights in writing but the father only by speech, restricted to those things that can be acquired by speech. What is that? Gidul in the name of Rav: How much are you giving to your son? Such and such. And how much are you giving to your daughter? Such and such. When he preliminarily married her, the daughter acquired among the daughters. {NAME} said, Gidul found something large and said something small! But it is as follows: How much are you giving to your son? Such and such. How much are you giving to your daughter? Such and such. When he preliminarily married her, the daughter acquired among the daughters and the son among the sons. {NAME} said, is that something small? Does he not acquire a wife on top of movables with one peruṭa ’s worth? But nobody can acquire two wives with one peruṭa ’s worth! But cannot a person acquire real estate and several movables with one peruṭa ’s worth? For a person can acquire two pieces of real estate with one peruṭa ’s worth, but nobody can acquire two wives with one peruṭa ’s worth.
[Ketubot 5:1.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “How much are you giving to your son? Such and such. How much are you giving to your daughter? Such and such. When he preliminarily married her, the daughter acquired among the daughters and the son among the sons,” but only if it is a first marriage. This follows what {NAME} said: If somebody definitively married off his son in a house, the latter acquired the house, but only if it is a first marriage. {NAME} said, she acquired movables but did not acquire the house. Do they disagree? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it that his father used it for storage. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is needed in case what was stored was borrowed from the market. {NAME} said, if he said it is loaned, he did not acquire it. There came a case before {NAME} and he instructed following {NAME}. {NAME} said, essentialy this has no basis but the rabbis build and add to it!
[Ketubot 5:1.5] You say that the father decides for his daughter; even if she is an adult? Let us hear from the following: The father decides for his daughter, but the mother does not decide for her daughter, nor the brother for his sister. Is there a difference about his sister whether she is an adolescent or an adult? So here, there is no difference whether she is an adolescent or an adult. {NAME} asked, even a third party? They said, even if she be an adult? A third party, let us hear from the following: The father decides for his daughter, but the mother does not decide for her daughter, nor the brother for his sister. So much more for the adult. Also in money matters it is so: Give your daughter to X and I shall give you so-and-so much. Buy this field and I shall give you so-and-so much.
[Ketubot 5:1.6] So is the Mishnah: “Because he did only add for the love of the first night, when he had intercourse with her.” If he slept with her, divorced her, and took her back, the love of the first night is still there. If he slept with her, died, and she became available to the levir, the love of the first night is still there. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME} who said, if they were divorced or widowed after a preliminary marriage she collects 200, after the definitive marriage she collects everything. {NAME} said, practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} said, they said to {NAME}, get outside to recite. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, practice follows {NAME}. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, practice does not follow {NAME}. {NAME} said, we had a rule that {NAME} and {NAME} said the same thing. As it was stated: If somebody’s son went overseas and one heard that he died, [the father] went and wrote his property to somebody else, and after that, the son returned. The gift remains valid; {NAME} says that the gift is invalid since he would not have written the deed if he had known that his son was alive. And {NAME} said, practice follows {NAME}, and the reason of {NAME} is the reason of {NAME}; and {NAME} said, they said to {NAME}, get outside to recite. And {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, practice does not follow {NAME}. An actual case was judged according to {NAME}.
[Ketubot 5:2.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, if he wants he writes for a virgin a contract of 200 [ zuz ] and she writes “I received 100 from you”, or for a widow a mina and she writes “I received 50 from you.” {NAME} says, anyone who diminishes [the ketubah ] of a virgin below 200 or that of a widow below 100 is engaging in whoring copulation.
[Ketubot 5:2.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} says, if he wants he writes,” etc. Does {NAME} think that the minimum for a virgin is a mina and for a widow 50 zuz ? Should he not write so from the start? But it must be a diminution afterwards. Why can he not write that “I received from you such and such”? It was found that {NAME} stated: “I received from you such and such”. {NAME} said: {NAME} formulated this only for the end; but at the start, even {NAME} agrees. What is the beginning and what is the end? The colleagues in the name of {NAME}: Before he had intercourse, and after he had intercourse. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Before he took her in, and after he took her in. If he did not have intercourse with her, divorced her, and took her in again; that is before and after.
[Ketubot 5:2.3] What is a wife and what is a concubine? {NAME} says, a wife has a ketubah, a concubine has no ketubah . {NAME} says, both have a ketubah. A wife has a ketubah and the ketubah stipulations; a concubine has a ketubah but no ketubah stipulations. {NAME} in the name of Rav: These are the opinions of {NAME} and {NAME}. But the words of the Sages: “A man may marry a woman and stipulate with her not to feed her and not to provide for her. Not only that, but that she should feed and provide for him and teach him Torah. It happened that {NAME}, married a woman and stipulated with her not to feed her and not to provide for her. Not only that, but that she should feed and provide for him and teach him Torah. But when years of famine came and they distributed the properties among themselves, she started complaining about him to the Sages of Israel. He said to them, for me she is trustworthy more than anybody. She told them, it is true that thus I stipulated with him. [They said to her], nothing comes after acquisition.”
[Ketubot 5:3.1] MISHNAH: One gives a virgin twelve months from when the husband requested to marry her to provide for herself. Just as one gives to the woman so one gives to the man to provide for himself. And to a widow thirty days. If the time has come and they are not definitively married, they eat from his [property] and may eat heave. {NAME} says, one gives her everything in heave. {NAME} said, half profane and half heave.
[Ketubot 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: “One gives a virgin twelve months.” It was stated: Adulthood in its time is twelve months. {NAME} said, state: One gives an adult twelve months and one gives her a preliminary wedding, and thirty days to a widow. We have stated: “One gives a virgin twelve months,” and you say so? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: After she was an adult for twelve months one gives her the preliminary marriage and afterwards thirty days. If she spent twelve months for the first and then the second one came. If he says to her, did you not wait already? She can say to him, I love you better than the young one. He is a widower, she is a virgin, and he wants to definitively marry. She can say, I love you better than a bachelor. If he is a bachelor and she a widow, and she wants to be definitively married. He can say, I love you better than a virgin. If she is underage and wants to grow up one listens to her.
[Ketubot 5:3.3] When the time came and they were not definitively married, they eat from his property and [do not] eat heave. If the husbands died, they eat from his property and eat heave. {NAME}, {NAME}, said: Only if the time was up on a Wednesday. What if the time was up on Tuesday or Thursday? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} and Levi: Both say that he is as if the Sages had jailed him. {NAME} said, if the delay is his fault, she is fed from his property.
[Ketubot 5:3.4] It was stated: “{NAME} says, one gives all heave to her, for heave is found everywhere. {NAME} says, half profane [food] and half heave, for women frequently are impure for holy things.” It was stated: “{NAME} says, any place, where heave is mentioned, one gives her twice the corresponding amount of profane [food].
[Ketubot 5:4.1] MISHNAH: The levir does not cause her to eat heave. If she spent six months for her husband and six months for the levir, or even all the time for the husband except for one day for the levir, or all the time for the levir except for one day for the husband, she cannot eat heave. That is the earlier Mishnah. The court in later times said that no woman eats heave unless she had been entering the bridal chamber.
[Ketubot 5:4.2] HALAKHAH: “The levir does not cause her to eat heave,” etc. {NAME} said, we stated there: The sister-in-law is fed from her husband’s estate all of the three months. If her levir had come before the court and fled, she is fed from his property. If he became sick it is as if he had fled. If he went overseas it is as if he had fled. If the widow said, I am bound in my widowhood to my husband’s house, one listens to her. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The one who says, I shall not give ḥalîṣah , is like the one who says, I shall not divorce. {NAME} said, {NAME} intructed that the one who says., I shall not give ḥalîṣah, is like the one who says, I shall not divorce.
[Ketubot 5:4.3] “If she spent six months for her husband and six months for the levir, she cannot eat heave. Not only six months for the levir but even all the time for the levir except for one day, she cannot eat heave.” The Mishna follows neither the earliest not the last Mishnah, but the intermediate development. As it was stated: First, they were saying that a preliminarily married woman, daughter of an Israel, could eat heave, for they were explaining: “If a Cohen acquires a person, acquistion by money;” for what would be the difference between one who acquires a wife and one who acquires a slave girl? They changed, to say: after twelve months, when he becomes responsible for her upkeep. The court of the later ones said: A woman never eats heave before she enters the bridal chamber. ”Already {NAME} sent to {NAME} at Nisibis: They say in your name that the preliminarily married daughter of an Israel eats heave. He sent back the following: I had been convinced that you are knowledgeable in the secrets of the Torah, but you do not even know the rules de minore ad majus ! Since money can acquire a Gentile slave girl to permit her to eat heave, but she cannot be acquired by sexual relations to permit her to eat heave, whereas a wife can be acquired by sexual relations to permit her to eat heave, it is only logical that money can acquire a wife to permit her to eat heave! But what can I do? They said that no woman eats heave before she enters the bridal chamber,” and they supported it by the verse: “Every pure person in your household shall eat it.” {NAME} said, that is an argument de minore ad majus that can be reversed! Because he could say to him, since a Gentile slave girl can be acquired by active possession to permit her to eat heave, what can you say about a wife who cannot be acquired by active possession? If an argument de minore ad majus can be reversed, the argument is invalid.
[Ketubot 5:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody dedicates his wife’s earnings, she can work and sustain herself. The excess, {NAME} says, is dedicated, {NAME} says, it is profane.
[Ketubot 5:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody dedicates his wife’s earnings,” etc. {NAME} says, it is sanctified as his property. {NAME} says, it is profane as his property. {NAME} said, they disagree about the excess over five tetradrachmas. He explains it in the case of one who supports his wife with food but does not give her an obolus for her needs, as we stated: “If he does not give her an obolus for her needs, what she earns is hers”. {NAME} said, they disagree about the excess left after [the husband’s] death; for he explains it if he does not support her with food. But if he supports her with food, everybody agrees that it became dedicated. {NAME} said, what one states there supports {NAME}: “When was this said? If he does not feed her. But if he feeds her, everybody agrees that it was sanctified.” But is not everything a wife has subject to the husband’s claim to its yield?
[Ketubot 5:5.3] {NAME} said, [the status] of her earnings is between them. {NAME} says, the earnings are susceptible to be dedicated from the first moment; {NAME} says, the earnings are not susceptible to be dedicated from the first moment. “What I shall inherit from my father (today) is sold to you, what I shall catch today in my trap is sold to you; his words are valid.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If he takes out a loan for his father’s burial shrouds, if his father was sick or in mortal danger. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Only if the trap was set. And {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: But as a dedication it would not be sanctified. Why? Because of the disagreement of {NAME} and {NAME}. One could say, there is a difference about the dedication, because the trap is not usually successful. {NAME} said to {NAME}: Do you remember that both you and {NAME} were saying in the name of {NAME}: Who stated about the dedication, because the trap is not usually successful? The disagreement of {NAME} and {NAME}! {NAME} has many a thought.
[Ketubot 5:5.4] {NAME} asked: If somebody dedicated his slave’s earnings and the latter was a hunter, what are the rules? Let us hear from the following: If somebody dedicates his slave, that one is dedicated but his earnings are profane. His [slave’s] earnings, he is profane and his earnings are dedicated. {NAME} said, if somebody cuts off the hands of another person’s slave, that one’s owner collects the payments for his injuries, his pain, his shame, and impairment but he shall go out and subsist on alms. Did we not state: If somebody dedicates his slave, that one takes out his provisions but the remainder is dedicated. {NAME} said, nobody thinks that he should die. [ ] more than for slaves. Did not {NAME} say, if somebody cuts off the hands of another person’s slave, that one’s owner collects the payments for his damages, his pain, his shame, and impairment but he shall go out and subsist on alms. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Jews are obligated to care for amputees, even slaves. {NAME} gave to his slave from everything he himself ate and quoted for this: “Did not his Maker make me in the belly and formed me likewise in a womb?”
[Ketubot 5:6.1] MISHNAH: These are the kinds of work a woman does for her husband: She grinds flour, bakes, launders, nurses her baby, makes his bed, and spins wool. If she brought a slave girl with her, she does not have to grind flour, bake, and launder. Two, she does not have to nurse her baby. Three, she does not have to make his bed or spin wool. Four, she sits in a chair. {NAME} says, even if she brought him a hundred slave girls, he forces her to spin wool because indolence causes immorality. {NAME} says, also a man who by a vow forbids his wife to work must divorce her and pay her ketubah since idleness induces mental illness.
[Ketubot 5:6.2] HALAKHAH: “These are the kinds of work a woman does for her husband,” etc. It was stated: Seven main labors did they enumerate; the rest the Sages did not need to specify.
[Ketubot 5:6.3] “She nurses her baby.” {NAME} said, is says only “her baby,” therefore not twins. Why does it say “ her baby ”? As it was stated: “A man cannot force his wife to nurse another man’s child, nor can a woman force her husband to let her nurse another woman’s child. If she made a vow not to nurse her baby, the House of Shammai say that one removes the breast nipple from his mouth, but the House of Hillel say, one forces her. If she was divorced, one cannot force her if [the baby] is not used to her, but if he is used to her one forces her and pays her wages to nurse her baby.” How old is the baby if he can be presumed to know her? {NAME} in the name of Rav: Three months. But {NAME} was staring at him. He asked him, why are you staring at me? Should I say to you following {NAME}, since {NAME} said, three days? {NAME} follows his opinion, since {NAME} said, I recognized the midwives who delivered me. {NAME} said, I recognized the circumciser who circumcised me. {NAME} said, I recognized the women who kept my mother company.
[Ketubot 5:6.4] It was stated: A baby suckles continuously until 24 months; after that he is as if an unclean creature would suckle, the words of {NAME}. But {NAME} says, he suckles continuously even four or five years. If he stopped, one does not return him. How long? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: From hour to hour. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Three days from hour to hour. It was stated: From hour to hour. {NAME}, Rav: When has this been said? If he stopped while being healthy. But if he stopped because of sickness, one does return him. When there was no danger. But if it was because of danger, one returns him even after a number of days.
[Ketubot 5:6.5] “If she brought”. {NAME} said, not only if she brought but even if she could have brought. As it was stated: His wife ascends with him but does not descend with him; a widow and her children descend but do not ascend; workers ascend but do not descend. The daughter neither ascends nor descends. {NAME} said, because one cares for the slave girl. {NAME} said, Because these labors are degrading, they are referred to as the slave girl’s. {NAME} said, because usually a woman does not sit aimlessly in her house. {NAME} said, even if she brought him 100 slave girls, he can force her to serve him with particular attention. What are services with particular attention? She rubs his body, washes his feet, and mixes him the cup. Why? Because she is obligated to do that, or because it is not appropriate to use a slave girl for these? If you say because it is not appropriate to use a slave girl for these, here she brought him slaves! It must be because she is obligated to do that. {NAME} in Sepphoris asked before {NAME}: Is it not reasonable because she is obligated to do that? He said to him, that is what I am always thinking.
[Ketubot 5:6.6] It was stated so: He forces her to work with wool, but not with flax since that causes bad breath and broadens the lips.
[Ketubot 5:7.1] MISHNAH: If somebody by a vow bars his wife from sexual intercourse, the House of Shammai say two weeks, the House of Hillel say one week. Students can go to study Torah for thirty days without permission; journeymen one week. The period mentioned in the Torah: People who do not have to work every day, journeymen twice a week, donkey drivers once a week, camel drivers once in thirty days, sailors once in three months, the words of {NAME}.
[Ketubot 5:7.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody by a vow bars his wife from sexual intercourse,” etc. The House of Shammai say, two weeks as after the birth of a girl. But the House of Hillel say one week, as after the birth of a boy or the days of her menstruation.
[Ketubot 5:7.3] “Students can go to study Torah for thirty days without their wives ’ permission.” Therefore, with permission even longer. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “He sent them to the Libanon, ten thousand per month.” {NAME} said, the Holy One, praise to Him, preferred being fruitful and multiplying over the Temple. What is the reason? “One month they would be in Libanon, two months each in his house.” Rav said, “the one entering and the one leaving, month for month for all months of the year.”
[Ketubot 5:7.4] Here you say, one week. But there, you say, twice a week. {NAME} stated: “Journeymen can hire themselves out without their wives’ permission for one week.”
[Ketubot 5:7.5] ”The period mentioned in the Torah.” Some Tannaïm state: שְׁאֵר that is intercourse; עוֹנָה that is food. Some Tannaïm state: עוֹנָה that is intercourse; שְׁאֵר that is food. He who said שְׁאֵר is intercourse: “No person to the שְׁאֵר of his flesh;” עוֹנָה is food: “He fed you and made you hunger”. He who said שְׁאֵר is food: “He let rain on them שְׁאֵר like dust”; עוֹנָה that is intercourse, “that you should not deprive my daughters,” that refers to intercourse. {NAME} explains the verse, “her flesh her garment”, that her garment should fit her flesh, that he should not give a young woman clothes of an old woman nor an old woman clothes of a young one. “Her garment her season”, that he should not give summer clothing for the rainy season nor that for the rainy season in summer. From where does he get food? Since he is not permitted to withhold from her things that are not necessities of life, not so much more things that are necessities of life! From where does he get the obligation of periodic intercourse? Since he may not withhold from her things which do not constitute the main reason for marriage, so certainly he may not withhold the things which constitute the main reason for marriage!
[Ketubot 5:7.6] {NAME} inferred from the gift which Jacob had sent to his brother Esaw, for he sent him according to copulations. “200 she-goats and 20 he-goats,” one for ten; “200 ewes and 20 rams,” one for ten. “Nursing camels and their sons 30.” {NAME} said, because it is decent in his sexual behavior did the verse not publicize. “40 cows and ten bulls,” one for four since they are tired; “20 she-donkeys and ten he-donkeys,” one for two since they are tired.
[Ketubot 5:7.7] {NAME} asked: Is it reasonable to consider scholars like those who do not work? {NAME} said, would it not be more reasonable to compare them to sailors since they exert themselves harder? Rav said, “she eats with him every Friday night”, in clean language.
[Ketubot 5:8.1] MISHNAH: If a woman revolts against her husband, one reduces her ketubah by seven denars a week; {NAME} says, by seven tropaïkes . For how long does one reduce? Up to the amount of her ketubah . {NAME} says, he continues to reduce, for maybe an inheritance will come to her from outside and he would be able to collect from it. Similarly, if the husband revolts against his wife, one adds to her ketubah three denars a week; {NAME} says three tropaїkes .
[Ketubot 5:8.2] HALAKHAH: “For how long does one reduce? Up to the amount of her ketubah ” , etc. Here you say seven, and there you say three? {NAME} said, since she is obligated for seven, he deducts seven; he, since he is obligated for three, has to add three. Think of it, if she brought him slaves, she is not obligated for anything! Think of it, if he stipulated [that he is not obligated for] either šĕ‘ēr , or dress, or ‘onāh , he is not obligated for anything! What is it? Following {NAME}, that the suffering of the male is greater than that of the female. That is what is written: “It was when she had nagged him day after day and pressured him.” What means “and pressured him”? {NAME} said, that she slipped away from under him. “He felt badly, to die”. He felt badly, ready to die, but she did not feel badly, to die. But some say that she fulfilled her needs with others. So much more she should have wanted, since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: This human limb, if you starved it you satisfied it, if you satisfied it you starved it.
[Ketubot 5:8.3] Following {NAME}, how far can he deduct? Let us hear from the following: {NAME} stated: One writes a bill of rebellion for the husband of a preliminarily married woman, or a sick one, a menstruating woman or one who is waiting for her levir. Where do we hold? If she rebelled against him when she was having her period, the Torah made her rebel against him! But we must hold that she rebelled against him before she had her period and now she has it. At that moment she would not be able to rebel but you say one writes, therefore one also deducts. From where does one deduct? From the additions to her ketubah . Let us hear from the following: “{NAME} says, he continues to reduce, for maybe an inheritance will come to her from outside and he would be able to collect from it.” He mentioned only inheritance, which is infrequent. That means he deducts from the additions to he ketubah. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One writes a bill of rebellion for a preliminarily married woman, but one does not write a bill of rebellion for one who is waiting for her levir. But did not {NAME} state that one writes a bill of rebellion on the ketubah of a menstruating woman or a sick one, a preliminarily married woman or one who is waiting for her levir? There, according to the first Mishnah, here according to the later Mishnah. {NAME} said, even if you say according to the later Mishnah, ”the later Court [instituted that] one warns her for four weeks, then she writes a receipt for her ketubah and leaves.”
[Ketubot 5:8.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A wife who leaves because of a bad reputation has no rags; the rebellious one has rags. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The rebellious one and the one who leaves because of a bad reputation can claim neither sustenance nor rags.

[Ketubot 5:9.1] MISHNAH: If somebody provides for his wife through a third party, he cannot give her less that two qab of wheat or four qab of barley. {NAME} said, only {NAME} assigned her barley, becaused he lived in proximity of Idumea.

[Ketubot 5:10.1] MISHNAH: One gives her half a qab of legumes and half a qab of oil, a qab of dried figs or a mina of fig cake; if there are none available one finds her fruit from other places. Also one gives her a bed and a mat; if he has no bed, a mat and a rug. One does not give her new ones in the summer or worn ones in the winter, but one gives her garments worth 50 tetradrachmas in the winter and she covers herself with the worn garments in the summer; and the rags are hers.

[Ketubot 5:11.1] MISHNAH: One gives her a silver obolus for her needs and she eats with him Friday nights. If he does not give her a silver obolus for her needs, she works for herself. And what does she work for him? In Judea, a weight of five tetradrachmas warp, which is ten tetradrachmas in Galilee, or in Judea the weight of ten tetradrachmas woof which are twenty tetradrachmas in Galilee. If she was nursing, one reduces the amount of her work and increases her food. When has this been said? For the poorest man in Israel. But for the most honored one, everything commensurable with his honor.
[Ketubot 5:11.2] HALAKHAH: “One gives her a silver obolus for her needs and she eats with him every Friday night,” etc. The matters are formulated in clean language. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Really eating. In the opinion of Rav, she eats at his expense; in the opinion of {NAME} she eats at her own expense.
[Ketubot 5:11.3] She has no claim to wine since poor Jewish women do not drink wine. Do rich women drink? How can the court assign wine? {NAME} said, because of “Whoring, wine, and cider will destroy the mind.” But did we not state: ”If she was nursing, one reduces the amount of her work and increases her food”? {NAME} said wine, for it increases the milk. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Also they assigned it for cooking. Nevertheless, she cursed them and said to them, so you should give to your daughters. {NAME} said, and we answered her, Amen. {NAME} said, I should not see consolation if I did not see her collecting barley grains between horses’ hooves at Acco. I quoted about her the verse: “The dainty one among you and the pampered, …” “If you have no experience, most beautiful of women, go following the flock …”. But did we not state: It happened that the Sages assigned to Miryam, {NAME}, a daily supply of perfume for 500 denar, when she was only waiting for her levir. Nevertheless, she cursed them and said to them, so you should give to your daughters. {NAME} said, and we answered her, Amen. {NAME} said, I should not see consolation if I did not see her bound with her hair to a horse’s tail at Acco. I quoted about her the verse: “The dainty one among you and the pampered, …”.
[Ketubot 6:1.1] MISHNAH: What a woman finds or makes with her hands belongs to her husband. Of what she inherits he eats the yield during her lifetime. [Payments she receives for] settlements for shame and diminution of value belong to her; {NAME} says, in case it is covered, she receives two thirds and he one third; in case it is visible, he receives two thirds and she one third. His part shall be given immediately; her part shall be invested in real estate and he eats its yield.
[Ketubot 6:1.2] HALAKHAH: “What a woman finds or makes with her hands belongs to her husband,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} and {NAME} disagree: One said, this is everybody’s opinion, the other said it is in dispute. We do not know who said what. It is reasonable that {NAME} should be the one who said it is in dispute since he explained that [the husband] provides her with food but does not give her a silver obolus as pocket money, and we did state: “If he does not give her a silver obolus as pocket money, what she makes with her hands is hers.” The work of her hands is parallel to what she finds. {NAME} came in the name of {NAME}: It is everybody’s opinion. That means that {NAME} varies in his opinions.
[Ketubot 6:1.3] For whom is it needed? For {NAME}! Even though for {NAME} the hand of the slave is his master’s hand and if the wife acquired title the husband should have acquired it; he agrees that his rights over it are restricted to the use of the yield. There, we have stated: “The finds of his underage son and daughter or of his Canaanite slave or slave-girl as well as his wife’s find belong to him,” for he can direct them to do other work. Why do we say: “The finds of his adult son and daughter or of his Hebrew slave or slave-girl belong to them,” because he cannot direct them to do other work. But his wife he cannot direct to do other work and you say that her find belongs to him! {NAME} said, there is another reason for his wife. What is the other reason for his wife? {NAME} says, because of quarrel. {NAME} does not say so, but that she should not smuggle away any of her husband’s property and say, I found it. Think of it, if another person gave it to her as a gift! A gift is public knowledge, a find is not public knowledge. Think of it, if she found it in the presence of witnesses! This because of that. {NAME} said, if they are not dependent on their father. But if they are dependent on their father, their finds belong to him.
[Ketubot 6:1.4] {NAME} instructed about one who had sent away his wife but not liquidated her ketubah , that he has to feed her until the time he liquidated it.
[Ketubot 6:1.5] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: Because he does not make her lose anything. In secret, why does he take? Because of the pain he suffers with her.
[Ketubot 6:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody decided on money for his son-in-law and the son-in-law died, the Sages said that he can say, I was ready to give to your brother, but it is impossible for me to give to you.
[Ketubot 6:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody decided on money for his son-in-law and the son-in-law died,” etc. Are these not the things that are acquired by speech? {NAME} stated: He promised the dowry on condition there be a marriage. And it is so: If somebody decided on money for his underage daughter, one forces him to give. But not for the adult one? {NAME} said, one forces [the groom] to give a bill of divorce.
[Ketubot 6:3.1] MISHNAH: If she decided to bring him 1’000 denars, he decides as equivalent fifteen minas. Corresponding to estimates he decides one-fifth less. If it was appraised for a mina and it is worth a mina, he has only a mina. For the estimate of a mina she gives him 31 [tetradrachmas and one] denar. For 400 she gives 500, for what the groom decides, he decides one-fifth less.
[Ketubot 6:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If she decided to bring him 1’000 denars,” etc. Why did they say for money, one and one half times, and for estimations less one fifth? {NAME} said, one estimates the will of the woman that she wants to use her vessels and depreciates them by a fifth. One estimates the will of the man to use it in trade and to make them one and one half. {NAME} said, this implies that nobody has the right to sell his wife’s vessels. Example: {NAME}, {NAME}, and {NAME} went to appraise for {NAME} daughter. They said to [the groom]: Deduct a fifth and double. He said to them, he deducts a fifth and does not double.
[Ketubot 6:3.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If she brought him gold, at full value. This was also stated. Jewellery to be turned into denars, at the rate of one and one half. Denars to be turned into jewellery, at their full value. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If she brought him an animal? He said to him, at full value. If she brought him real estate: He said to him, at full value. But does he not gain from it? But she collects the real estate, he has only the usufruct.
[Ketubot 6:4.1] MISHNAH: If she decided to bring him money, each tetradrachma is turned into six denars and the groom engages himself for ten denars for the perfume box for each mina; {NAME} says, all follows local custom.
[Ketubot 6:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If she decided to bring him money,” etc. “If she decided to bring him 500 denars by appraisal, he makes it 400. If he did not do that but made it 1’000; if she made an agreement, she collects everything; if not, he deducts five denars for each tetradrachma, but he cannot touch the addition. If she decided to bring him 500 denars in coin, he makes it 750. If he did not do that but made them 1’000; if she made an agreement, she collects everything; if not, he deducts six denars for each tetradrachma, but he cannot touch the addition. If she decided to bring him 1’000 zuz , he must turn them into fifteen minas. If he did not do that but wrote over to her a field worth 12 minas in place of the 1’000 zuz . If she made an agreement, she collects everything; if not, one does not decrease for a virgin to less than 200 and for a widow to less than a mina.” Here, you say, he deducts. But there, you say, he does not deduct. Here, if she invalidated part of it, there if she did not invalidate part of it. Here, you say, he touches the addition but there, you say, he does not touch the addition. Here, he added but did not subtract; there, he subtracted but did not add. It was stated: Both for appraisal and for coin. Why for appraisal? Corresponding to what he subtracts, corresponding to what what he adds, corresponding to what she brings.
[Ketubot 6:4.3] So is the Mishnah: “And a perfume box for every mina.” {NAME} said, they made usufruct of perfumes like usufruct of money. {NAME} said, they made usufruct of procreation like usufruct of money. As the following: The students of {NAME} went to Qaddišin; they found them childless. They said to them: Did you stipulate between you? If you stipulated, it is fine; otherwise everything follows the local custom.
[Ketubot 6:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody marries off his daughter without mentioning particulars he should not give her less than 50 zuz If he had decided to take her in naked the husband should not say, if she comes to my house I shall clothe her in my garment, but he covers her when she still is in her father’s house. Similarly, those who marry off an orphan girl should not give her less that 50 zuz , and if money is available one provides for her according to her social standing.
[Ketubot 6:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody marries off his daughter,” etc. {NAME}, {NAME} brother, asked: Did we not state: From where that even if he said, I shall go naked but clothe her, one does not tell him to be naked and to clothe her but he clothes her according to her social standing? There, it is the way of people to say, it is better for me to stand naked if only I cover my wife; but here it was a prior condition.
[Ketubot 6:5.3] So is the Mishnah: And so those who provide for the orphan girl. {NAME} said, this means that one says to the overseers to take out a loan. For he explains it, if nothing is in the wallet one takes out a loan up to fifty. But if there is money in the wallet, one may add. {NAME} said, this means that one does not say to the overseers to take out a loan. For he explains if there is money in the wallet. But if there is no money one diminishes. As the following, about a girl in the days of {NAME}. [Ketubot 6:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If an orphan girl was married off by her mother or her brothers,” etc. So is the Mishnah: If they married off the first one there should be given. [Ketubot 6:6.3] {NAME} asked {NAME} and {NAME}, who is the Tanna of “a tenth of the estate”? {NAME} said to him in the name of {NAME}: A tenth of the estate following Rebbi. They asked before Rebbi: If there were ten daughters. Then if the first one took a tenth of the estate, the second took a tenth of the estate, the third, the fourth, the fifth, and so on up to the tenth, there is nothing left for the son! He said to them: The first one takes a tenth of the estate and leaves; the second takes a tenth of the remainder, the third from what then is left, the fourth of what then is left, up to the tenth from what then is left. It turns out that the daughters take two thirds less a little, and the son takes one third plus a little.

[Ketubot 6:7.3] ”If somebody says, give my sons one šeqel per week and they need a tetradrachma, one gives them a tetradrachma. Do not give them more than one šeqel per week, one gives them a šeqel. [Ketubot 6:7.4] ”If they died, others should inherit.” Did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: A person can transfer property rights in any language except with an expression of inheritance? [Ketubot 7:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody makes a vow that his wife should not have any usufruct from him, up to thirty days he shall appoint a provider, more than that he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah. {NAME} says, if he is an Israel, for one month he should keep her, for two he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah ; in the case of the wife of a Cohen for two months he should keep her, for three he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah.
[Ketubot 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody makes a vow that his wife should not have any usufruct from him,” etc. There, we have stated: “If somebody by a vow bars his wife from sexual intercourse,” and here you say so? There, he makes a vow to separate her from his body, but here he makes a vow to separate her from his property. But can anybody make a vow not to pay his debt? {NAME} said, since in the future he will divorce her, pay her the ketubah, and stop her food supply, it is as if there was no debt. Why could she not sit there and wait; if he divorced her everything would be in order, otherwise let him provide her with food? It follows him who said that the wife’s food is not from words of the Torah, as it was stated: The court will not determine food for the wife from Sabbatical money, but she may be given Sabbatical produce to eat at her husband’s. Then should she not be considered as a worker not worth a peruṭah ? This proves that she is not considered as a worker not worth a peruṭah.
[Ketubot 7:1.3] He could appoint a provider, as the following: “X is forbidden any profit from me by a vow and I do not know what to do.” Let him appoint a provider! A woman has the right to say, it is impossible for me to be provided for by anybody other than my husband. But did we not state: “If somebody provides for his wife through a third party.” There, if she accepted it; here, if she did not accept it. If she did not accept it then he should not appoint even for one day! She continues with him for one month, perhaps he will find an opening for his vow. {NAME} says, if he vowed for thirty days. But if he vowed forever, he shall divorce immediately and pay the ketubah. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: Even if he vowed forever, she continues with him for one month, perhaps he will find an opening for his vow.
[Ketubot 7:1.4] Some Tannaïm state: thirty days. Some Tannaïm state: up to thirty days. He who says thirty days supports Rav; he who says up to thirty days supports {NAME}.
[Ketubot 7:1.5] {NAME} said, they differ about wives of Cohanim. “Beyond that he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah ,” at the end of the second [month]. “{NAME} says, if he is an Israel, for one month he should keep her, for two he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah ,” at the end of the second [month]. “In the case of the wife of a Cohen for two months he should keep her, for three he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah ,” at the beginning of the third. It was stated thus: At the end of three by everybody’s opinion.
[Ketubot 7:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody causes a vow of his wife that she should not taste any kind of fruits has to divorce her and pay the ketubah. {NAME} says, if he is an Israel, for one month he should keep her, for two he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah ; in the case of the wife of a Cohen for two [months] he should keep her, for three he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah.
[Ketubot 7:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody causes a vow of his wife,” etc. Can anybody cause somebody else’s vow during his lifetime? It must be that the wife made a vow, the husband heard it, and said to her: If you will eat from such and such, my property will be forbidden to you. If she ate from such and such, why should his property not be forbidden to her? Is that not the case from the beginning of the chapter? But if his wife made a vow, her husband was informed, and did not dissolve it, following him who says that he put his finger between her teeth, he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah. {NAME} said, even he who said that she put his finger between her teeth, and should be divorced without ketubah, will agree in case he provoked her to make the vow.
[Ketubot 7:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody causes a vow of his wife that she should not adorn herself with one of the kinds has to divorce her and pay the ketubah. {NAME} says, among the poor if he did not give a time limit, among the rich for thirty days.
[Ketubot 7:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody causes a vow of his wife that she should not adorn herself,” etc. {NAME} said, so is the Mishnah: “Among the poor if he did not give a time limit.” {NAME} said, among the poor if he did not give a time limit; but if he gave a time limit even if it were for ten years it is permitted, for no fox dies if he gets dusty from his lair. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Except holidays.
[Ketubot 7:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody causes a vow of his wife that she should not go to her father’s house, if they live in the same city she does, for one month he should keep her, for two he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah. If they live in another city, for one holiday he should keep her, for two he has to divorce her and pay the ketubah.
[Ketubot 7:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody causes a vow of his wife that she should not go to her father’s house,” etc. {NAME} said, they stated there: If he made her make a vow that she should not wash in the bathhouse, in walled cities one week, in villages two weeks. That she should not wear shoes, in villages three months, in walled cities 24 hours.

[Ketubot 7:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody causes a vow of his wife that she should not pay condolence visits or go to weddings has to divorce her and pay the ketubah. [Ketubot 7:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody causes a vow of his wife that she should not pay condolence visits,” etc. ”If he made her vow not to lend out fine and coarse sieves, he shall divorce her and pay the ketubah, since he gives her a bad reputation among her [female] neighbors. [Ketubot 7:5.3] “If he argues because of another reason, he is in his rights,” because of bad reputation.

[Ketubot 7:6.1] MISHNAH: The following leave without ketubah : Any one violating the laws of Moses or Jews. What is the law of Moses? She feeds him what is not tithed, or makes him sleep with her when she is menstruating, or does not cut ḥallah , or makes vows which she does not keep. And what is the law of Jews: She leaves home with her hair in disorder, or spins in public, or speaks with everybody. {NAME} says, also one who curses his parents in his presence. {NAME} says, also the big-voiced. What is the big-voiced? Any who speaks inside her house and her neighbors hear her voice.
[Ketubot 7:6.2] HALAKHAH: “The following leave without ketubah ,” etc. “What is the big-voiced,” etc. And all with witnesses. “X tithed, X saw the stains, X cut her ḥallah , X permitted her vow.” They checked and found it was not so.
[Ketubot 7:6.3] “She feeds him what is not tithed, or makes him sleep with her when she is menstruating, or does not cut ḥallah, or makes vows which she does not keep.” We understand all these because he is involved. “She makes vows which she does not keep,” what is his interest in this? He can say, I cannot live with a vowing wife because she buries her children. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: Children die for the sin of vows, as it is written: “For vain [vows] I smote your children.
[Ketubot 7:6.4] “With her hair in disorder.” They said that for the courtyard; so much more for the passageway. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If one goes out in her wig, she does not go out with her hair in disorder. That is, to the courtyard; if she does it in the passageway, she goes out with her hair in disorder. There exists a courtyard which is like a passageway and a passageway which is like a courtyard. A courtyard through which outsiders have broken is like a passageway and a passageway through which no outsiders are breaking is like a courtyard.
[Ketubot 7:6.5] {NAME} says, also one who curses their child in his parents’ presence. {NAME} says, also the big-voiced. What is the big-voiced? {NAME} says, any who speaks and her women neighbors hear her voice. Rav says, any one whose voice is heard by other people from bed to bed during intercourse.
[Ketubot 7:6.6] {NAME} stated in the name of {NAME}: Both for women about whom they said that they have ketubah as also those about whom they said they leave without ketubah , as the minor, the secondarily prohibited, and the she-ram, did they speak about a mina or 200 [ zuz ]?
