[Ketubot 10:6.1] MISHNAH: If somebody was married to two wives when he sold his field and the first wife wrote to the buyers “I have no claims against you”, the second takes from the buyer, the first from the second, and the buyer from the first; they go on in circles until they compromise between them. The same holds for a creditor and a woman who is a creditor.
[Ketubot 10:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody was married to two wives,” etc. {NAME} said, this means that if somebody borrowed from two persons and the second comes and says to him, get up and let us settle, and [the borrower] says, will not in the end the first hear of it and come to foreclose, he [the second lender] may say let us settle, and if he forecloses, he forecloses. If he settled, one may assume that the first will come and foreclose. If he settled with the first, {NAME} said, such a case came before {NAME} who said, he settled. {NAME} said, did he not write “what I shall acquire”? It happens only with an heir. {NAME} said, even with a creditor it can happen if he did not write “anything I shall acquire”, or if he said, “you shall not be paid except from this.” {NAME} said, this follows him who said, for ketubah but not for stipulations. But for him who said, for ketubah and for stipulations, does it not return?
[Ketubot 11:1.1] MISHNAH: If a widow is supported by the orphans’ property, she has to work for them but they are not obligated to bury her. Her heirs, the heirs of her ketubah , are obligated to bury her.
[Ketubot 11:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If a widow is supported by the orphans’ property,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: What she finds belongs to herself. If she had sustenance left over? Since her finds belong to her husband, the married woman’s leftover sustenance belongs to her husband. Since a widow’s finds belong to herself, her leftover sustenance belongs to herself. Her worn-out clothing belongs to her. Since even a married woman, whose leftover sustenance belongs to her husband, keeps her worn-out clothing to herself, the widow, whose leftover food belongs to herself, her worn-out clothing so much more! There, she needs them for the time of her period. Here also, she needs them for the time of her period.
[Ketubot 11:1.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Also she does not perform for them services of intimacy. What are services of intimacy? She rubs their bodies, washes their faces, or mixes their cup.
[Ketubot 11:1.4] One adds to her sustenance: A married woman has no wine, a widow has wine. If a married woman said, my earnings should be counted against my sustenance, one does not listen to her; if a widow said, my earnings should be counted against my sustenance, one listens to her.
[Ketubot 11:1.5] Rav said, if a dying person said, do not bury me, he is buried as a charge on public charity. {NAME} asked, how could one think that others are provided for by his property and he is buried as a charge on public charity? The Mishnah disagrees with Rav: “Her heirs, the heirs of her ketubah , are obligated to bury her.” Explain it, if they inherited real estate. As it was stated: “If he left male and female slaves, mortgages, and movables, anybody who takes them first acquires them and he shall be buried by public charity.” Because he took it first. Therefore, if he did not take it first one removes from his hand. Explain it, if he said, bury me. As {NAME} said in the name of the rabbis: If a dead person was buried who had not said “bury me”, even though others came and took [of his property] one removes from their hands. If they took real estate. In fact, what you say, one removes from their hands, if they took real estate. But if they took movables, one does not remove from their hands, if it was a loan by witnesses. But for a documented loan, whether they took real estate or movables one does not remove from their hands. For {NAME}, said: They made the words of a bedridden person equal to those of a healthy person who wrote and delivered. But only if he died from that illness, not if he recovered. And if he was explicit and said, give field X to Y. If he said, give field X to Y? Is it as if he was explicit or only if he said, the Northern half, the Southern half? {NAME} asked: If he said, burn me by pagan rites and give half of field X to Y. Since they do not burn, do they give? {NAME} asked: A sick person who said, my daughters shall be supported. Would the daughters not be supported anyway? No, it is necessary, for otherwise would they be supported from pledged real estate or would they be supported from movables? {NAME} [ ] there came a case before {NAME} about a bedridden person who had said, my documents shall be given to X. He said to him, the bedridden can only transfer property which is acquired either by a document or by taking hold. But these are acquired by a document and by taking hold. As it was stated: “A ship is acquired by taking hold in the opinion of everybody. {NAME} says a ship and documents are acquired by a document and by taking hold. If he wrote and did not take hold, or took hold without writing [a transfer document] he did not do anything unless he both writes and takes hold.”
[Ketubot 11:2.1] MISHNAH: A widow, whether after preliminary or definitive marriage, may sell without court supervision. {NAME} says, after definitive marriage she may sell without court supervision; after preliminary marriage, she may sell only under court supervision since she has no sustenance and any person who has no claim to sustenance may sell only under court supervision.
[Ketubot 11:2.2] HALAKHAH: “A widow, whether after preliminary or definitive marriage,” etc. {NAME} is of the opinion that everything depends on sustenance. If he had agreed to sustain her after preliminary marriage, she may sell without court supervision If he had agreed to sustain her after definitive marriage, she may sell only under court supervision. The words of the Sages? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A person is concerned for his widow’s dignity whether after preliminary or after definitive marriage.
[Ketubot 11:2.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The one who renounced her ketubah in favor of the orphans is sustained by them. This is difficult. If there were a woman without ketubah , does she not have claim to sustenance? A woman without ketubah has claim to sustenance. But here is it not enough that she renounced her ketubah in favor of the orphans, that you want to cheat her of her sustenance?
[Ketubot 11:2.4] {NAME} in the name of Rav: If she requested her ketubah in court, she lost her claim to sustenance. {NAME} said, but only from a clear mind; not if forced. As in the case of the widow of {NAME} to whom they said, {NAME} wants you. She requested her ketubah and lost her sustenance. After the matter became known, it was brought before {NAME} and she returned to her sustenance.
[Ketubot 11:2.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A widow who lived two or three months without asking for sustenance, loses the sustenance of these three months. That is, if she did not take a loan. But if she took out a loan, she collects. If there is no pledge in her hand. But if she has a pledge in her hand, she collects even if she did not take a loan. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: That is what they said, at the start one sells for sustenance of twelve months but one gives her sustenance for 30 days. If at the end of thirty days they say, we gave, but she says, I did not receive, it would be similar to what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: If one took a loan of 12’000 for a year in order to repay one gold denar per month. It is obvious that he gave for the first month and did not give for the last. About the days in between they said, not at the start.
[Ketubot 11:2.6] {NAME} quoted in the name of {NAME}: At the start one sells for sustenance of twelve months but one gives her sustenance for 30 days. Why should they sell for the sustenance of 12 months? Not to disadvantage the woman. Why do they give her sustenance for 30 days? If you said otherwise, you would act in detriment of the orphans, as it was stated: If a widow took possession even of 1’000 zuz for her sustenance, one does not take it away from her. What could one say to her? “Show what is in your hands!” The students of {NAME} said to her, “show what is in your hands.” {NAME} said to them, since in the end she will have to swear about anything in her hands, one says to her, let it be so.
[Ketubot 11:3.1] MISHNAH: If she sold her ketubah entirely or partially, or donated her ketubah to another, entirely or partially, she cannot sell the remainder except under court supervision. But the Sages say, she may sell even four or five times, and may sell for sustenance without court supervision but writes in the document that “I sold for sustenance.” A divorcee may sell only under court supervision.
[Ketubot 11:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If she sold her ketubah entirely or partially,” etc. It was stated: “She sells and writes ‘this I sold for ketubah ’ and ‘this I sold for sustenance,’ the words of {NAME}. {NAME} said, she sells and writes non-specifically; in this she is empowered.” If a loan before witnesses [comes due], she says, I sold for sustenance. If a loan by contract [comes due], she says, I sold for my ketubah . And even if a loan before witnesses [comes due], she sells for sustenance and turns around and forecloses it for her ketubah ; could one not say to her, show your sale? Explain it, if the object increased in value.
[Ketubot 11:3.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Just as a man is concerned about his widow’s honor so he has to be concerned about his divorcee’s honor, as {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, “do not hide yourself from your flesh”, that refers to one’s divorcee. {NAME} wife did mistreat him badly. {NAME} went to him and told him, rabbi, send her away, for she does not treat you with the honor due to you. He said to him, her ketubah is too large for me. He said to him, I shall give you the ketubah and send her away. He gave him the ketubah and he divorced her. She went and married the city treasurer. That one lost his property and became blind. She took him around the town and led him. Once they went around the entire town and nobody gave him anything. He said to her, is there not another neighborhood? She said to him, there is the neighborhood of my divorcer; it is beyond my powers to bring you there. He started hitting her. {NAME} passed by and heard them demeaning one another in public. He took them, brought them to one of his houses, and provided them with food all the days of their lives, because “do not hide yourself from your flesh”, that refers to one’s divorcee. Nevertheless they quarelled loudly in the night and her voice was heard saying, the pain she suffered outside her body was easier to bear than that inside her body.
[Ketubot 11:4.1] MISHNAH: If a widow’s ketubah was 200 and she sold either the worth of a mina for 200 or the worth of 200 for a mina, her ketubah was paid. If her ketubah was for a mina and she sold the worth of a mina and a denar for a mina, her sale is void. Even if she says, I shall return the denar to the heirs, her sale is void.
[Ketubot 11:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If a widow’s ketubah was 200,” etc. We understand worth a mina for 200 or worth 200 for a mina. In any case, she made the orphans lose a mina. [If it was worth] a mina [and she sold it] for 200, would the sale not be invalidated as erroneous buy? Explain it that the property increased in value. {NAME} said, this supports {NAME}, since {NAME} said, real estate buys are never under the laws of overcharging. {NAME} said, if the transaction was excessive, it comes under the law of overcharging. The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “The following do not fall under the laws of overcharging: Slaves, securities, real estate, and redemptions.” He explains it, unless it was excessive. If he redeemed what was worth a mina by 200, {NAME} said, it is not redeemed, but {NAME} said, it is redeemed. A baralta disagrees with {NAME}: If he said, this toga instead of this donkey, the latter becomes profane. And its end disagrees with {NAME}: It is necessary to compute the value. {NAME} said, the baraita itself implies that it is necessary to compute the value. Where do they disagree? To bring [a sacrifice to atone for] larceny. {NAME} said, he has to bring a sacrifice for larceny; {NAME} said, he does not have to bring a sacrifice for larceny.
[Ketubot 11:5.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, her sale is valid unless there would have been left a field [for sowing] nine qab , and in a garden half a qab , or following the words of {NAME}, a fourth. [Ketubot 11:5.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} says, her sale is valid,” etc. That is, if she sold them in four contracts. [Ketubot 11:6.1] MISHNAH: If the judges estimated one sixth too little or too much, their sale is invalid. {NAME} says, their sale is valid; otherwise, what is the court’s power worth? But if they offered public tender, even if they sold either the worth of a mina for 200 or the worth of 200 for a mina, their sale is valid.
[Ketubot 11:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If the judges estimated one sixth too little or too much,” etc. As you say for a private person, in real estate up to one third, in movables up to one sixth. And similarly, for Temple property, in real estate up to one sixth, in movables up to [one in] twelve. There, we have stated: “The estimation for orphans is thirty days, the estimation for Temple property sixty days, and one publicly announces mornings and evenings.” And why thirty? In order to empower the orphans. Why should they not announce longer? Up to thirty days you empower the orphans, more than that you diminish their power. Why do you not say that for Temple property? Temple property is different because each offer made is firm. Then they should announce forever! If suffices for the Temple that it should be twice that of a private person. {NAME} said, since you say that Temple property is different because each offer made is firm, this implies that if they find their estimation they do not continue but close the deal.
[Ketubot 11:6.3] “And one announces mornings and evenings,” at the time when [agricultural] workers go out or come back, and he mentions the field and its description. {NAME} said, if they do not get their estimated price, they can conclude the sale. Is that the Mishnah, “if the judges estimated one sixth too little or too much, their sale is invalid”? Becausethey sold too low or too high, but if they found their estimate they close the deal. {NAME} said before {NAME}: What can you say, we deal with the case that they did not announce in public! From what is said afterwards: “Except if they offered public tender.” What is public tender? {NAME} said, announcement.
[Ketubot 11:6.4] {NAME} said, slaves lest they flee, securities and movables lest they be stolen. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does this not imply that a slave is redeemed in front of three people? He answered him, yes. He said to him, but did we not state: “Real estate nine persons and a Cohen, and a human by the same rule”? He answered him, the human here is a free person.
[Ketubot 11:6.5] {NAME} in the name of Rav: A case came before Rebbi, who wanted to act following the rabbis. {NAME}, {NAME}, said to him: Did you not teach us in your old man’s name, “except if they offered public tender”? He accepted it; Rebbi changed his mind and acted following {NAME}.
[Ketubot 11:7.1] MISHNAH: Neither the orphan, nor the secondarily prohibited, nor the she-ram may claim ketubah , or usufruct, or sustenance, or depreciation. A widow [married] to the High Priest, a divorcee or one who had received ḥalîṣah to a common priest, a bastard or Gibeonite girl to an Israel, an Israel girl married to a bastard or Gibeonite, have claim to ketubah .
[Ketubot 11:7.2] HALAKHAH: “Neither the orphan girl, nor the secondarily prohibited, nor the she-ram,” etc. One understands the secondarily prohibited and the she-ram. The orphan? Does an orphan not have ketubah ? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rebbi J̣oḥanan: Explain it for an orphan who repudiated. {NAME}, {NAME}: Just as they fined her, so they fined him. In which respect? That if he preliminarily married her by [giving her] a pound of gold, he loses it all.
[Ketubot 11:7.3] “No usufruct.” {NAME} said, that he has from her only the usufruct. {NAME} stated before {NAME}, in disgreement with {NAME}: “He has the right to what she finds and earns, and to dissolve her vows.” What means “no usufruct”? That she cannot reclaim from him the usufruct he had [from her property].
[Ketubot 11:7.4] {NAME} said: All the time my teacher {NAME} told me, state in your baraita that he inherits from her and defiles himself for her. We have also stated so: A man defiles himself for his qualified wife but does not become defiled for his disqualified wife.
[Ketubot 11:7.5] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: May the slaves of a secondarily forbidden [wife] eat heave? He said to him, be quiet, it is better for you. She eats but her slaves do not eat.
[Ketubot 11:7.6] There, we have stated: “A forced bill of divorce is valid in Israel; it is invalid from Gentiles.” {NAME} said, it is invalid and disqualifies for the priesthood. {NAME} said, one does not force, only disqualify. {NAME} said, one does not force except for example a widow married to a High Priest, a divorcee or one freed by ḥalîṣah for a simple priest. But did we not state: “Secondarily forbidden”? Did he not say “for example”? But did we not state: “A person who by a vow forbids his wife to have any usufruct from him, up to 30 days he shall appoint a caretaker; after 30 days he shall divorce her and pay ketubah ”! We heard that he shall divorce; did we hear that one forces him?
[Ketubot 11:7.7] What is the difference between these and those? Since these are words of the Torah and the words of the Torah [do not] need support, therefore they have ketubah . Those, because they are words of the Sopherim and the words of the Sopherim need support, therefore they do not have ketubah . Some want to say since these are punished together with the child, they did not fine them, therefore they have ketubah . Those, since they are not punished together with the child, they fined them, therefore they do not have ketubah . What is the difference between them? He who remarried his divorced wife after she had remarried. For him who says since these are words of the Torah, and this case is a word of the Torah, therefore she has ketubah . For him who says since these are punished together with the child, this one, since neither she nor the child is punished, therefore, she has no ketubah .
[Ketubot 11:7.8] {NAME} said that {NAME} and {NAME} say that they differ about sustenance. {NAME} said, she may demand sustenance. {NAME} said to him, one says to him, divorce her! And you say so? They wanted to say, for him who says they differ about the conditions attached to a ketubah , {NAME} said, she has the ketubah stipulations. {NAME} said to him, everybody agrees that she cannot claim support since they even punished her heirs, so much more herself. But for him who says that they differ about sustenance, it follows that they do not differ about the stipulations of a ketubah . They fined her, but did not fine her heirs.
[Ketubot 12:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody marries a woman and contracts with her to sustain her daughter for five years, he is obligated to sustain her for five years. If [the mother] was married to another man who contracted with her to sustain her daughter for five years, he is obligated to sustain her for five years. The first one cannot say, if she will come to live with me I shall sustain her, but he has to bring her support to her place. Similarly, the two cannot say we shall support her in common, but one of them sustains her and the other gives the money equivalent to her sustenance.
[Ketubot 12:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody marries a woman and had contracted with her,” etc. How does he become indebted to her? Do not {NAME} and {NAME} both say, if somebody writes a debenture for another person under the assumption that he owes him and it turns out that he does not owe, he does not have to give to him! {NAME} said, they gave it the status of an addition to the ketubah . Then he should have to pay in the end! They gave it the status of the gift for a woman’s preliminary marriage. Then he should pay up front! They treated it as when one marries a woman preliminarily by promising to give her twelve silver denars within one year by delivering one silver denar’s worth every month.
[Ketubot 12:1.3] It was stated: He supports her the first five years, whether in inflation or in deflation. If [living expenses] were high and became low, if he was the cause, he pays the high rate, if she was the cause, he pays the low rate. If they were low and became high, whether he was the cause or she was the cause, he pays the low rate. That is, “the daughter neither ascends nor descends.”
[Ketubot 12:1.4] There, we have stated: “The female children you will have by me shall live in my house and be supported by my estate,” and it was stated about this: They will be clothed with garments supplied by me. For whom does the daughter work? Let us hear from the following: “The husband has to sustain her and they pay the cost of her sustenance.” This means, he feeds her but she works for her husband. {NAME} said, this means that if somebody had agreed to sustain his daughter-in-law, he has to sustain her, but she works for his son. If he wants her to be with him but she does not want to, the law is with her, as we have stated: “They pay the cost of her sustenance.” If she fell ill, it is as if she had married. If she died, is it as if she had married? If she died, she already is dead.
[Ketubot 12:2.1] MISHNAH: If the daughter married, the husband has to sustain her and they pay the cost of her sustenance. If they died, their daughters are supported from unincumbered property but she is supported from mortgaged property since her status is that of a creditor. The intelligent ones did write: On condition that I support your daughter for five years the entire time you are with me.
[Ketubot 12:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If the daughter married, the husband has to sustain her,” etc. What is the status of the ketubah stipulations if he wrote them in the document? {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} disagree. {NAME} said, he wrote them for emphasis; {NAME} said, he wrote them to collect from encumbered property. {NAME} switched the traditions. {NAME} said, a Mishnah supports him who said, he wrote them for emphasis, since we stated there: “One does not foreclose from mortgaged property to indemnify for produce or investment, or sustenance of widow and daughters, in order not to impede the economy.” Are [the first categories] not based on a document? Here also based on the document. {NAME} said, “since her status is that of a creditor”! Is that not based on a document? Here also based on the document.
[Ketubot 12:2.3] If she dies she is not with him. If she was divorced she is not with him. If he took her back? One says, this was stated for the ketubah but not for the stipulations; one says, both for the ketubah and the stipulations, which opinion is valid? “The intelligent ones did write: On condition that I support your daughter for five years the entire time you are with me;” on that it was stated: Only for the first marriage. This parallels what {NAME} said, if somebody marries off his son in a house, the latter acquires the house, but only for a first marriage.
[Ketubot 12:3.1] MISHNAH: If the widow said, I cannot move from my husband’s house, the heirs cannot say to her, go to your father’s house and we shall support you there, but they support her and give her a dwelling commensurate with her honor.
[Ketubot 12:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If the widow said, I cannot move from my husband’s house,” etc. It is written ( Ps . 88:6 ): “Among the dead is freedom.” When a person dies he becomes free from the Commandments.
[Ketubot 12:3.3] Rebbi commanded three things on his death-bed: My widow should not move from my house; do not eulogize me in small towns; and he who served me during my lifetime should also serve me in death. “My widow should not move from my house,” is that not a Mishnah? “The widow who said, I cannot possibly move from my husband’s house …” {NAME} said, that they should not say, this is the house of the patriarchate and must serve the patriarchate. {NAME} said, as we have stated: “She lives in the houses just as she lived while her husband was overseas, she uses silver and gold vessels just as she used to while her husband was overseas, she is fed just as she was fed while her husband was overseas.” “Do not eulogize me in small towns” because of the quarrels. “He who served me during my lifetime should also serve me in death;” {NAME} said, for example Yose Ephrati and Joseph from Haifa. {NAME} added, do not use many shrouds on me and let my coffin have holes at the bottom. These words say that Rebbi was buried in a single shroud since Rebbi said, not as a man left, he will come. But the rabbis say, just as a man left, he will come. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: The garment that went with a person to the grave will come back with him. What is the reason? ( Job 38:14 ) “The seal turns itself around like clay, they appear in dress.” Antoninus asked Rebbi, what is the meaning of what is written: “The seal turns itself around like clay?” He said to him, He Who brings the generation clothes it.

[Ketubot 13:2.6] Who is the Tanna of “the gain should be given to the sacred fund”? {NAME}! Let us hear from the following: “If he said, this loaf shall be dedicated, if he or another person ate it, they committed sacrilege; therefore, it can be redeemed. But if he said, it is for me [as if dedicated], if he ate it he committed sacrilege on goodwill but others would not commit sacrilege.” He said only, if he ate it. Therefore, to warm his hands is permitted. The students of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: That is if he said I shall not eat it nor taste it; if he forbade only eating to himself. But the question was, if somebody made a vow [to forbid] a loaf to himself, can he use it to warm his hands?
[Ketubot 13:2.7] As it was stated: “If somebody went overseas and another person provided for his wife.” {NAME} said, they said only, another. Therefore, the father can recover. {NAME} says, neither the father nor a third party can recover. There is a parallel disagreement, as we have stated there: “He has the right to what she finds and to her earnings, to dissolve her vows, and to receive her bill of divorce, but cannot eat usufruct in her lifetime… He is required to pay for her upkeep, her ransom, and her burial.” {NAME} said, they said only, the father. Therefore, a third party cannot recover. {NAME} says, both the father or a third party can recover. In the opinion of {NAME}, both for burial as for upkeep the father can recover, a third party cannot recover. In the opinion of {NAME}, for burial both the father and also a third party can recover because it is unthinkable that his wife should be thrown to the dogs. For sustenance, neither the father nor a third party can recover.
[Ketubot 13:3.1] MISHNAH: Admon promulgated seven [rules]. If somebody dies and is survived by sons and daughters. If the estate is large, the sons inherit and the daughters will be sustained. If the estate is small, the daughters shall be sustained and the sons shall go begging. Admon said, because I am a male, shall I lose? {NAME} said, I am convinced by Admon’s statement.
[Ketubot 13:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Admon promulgated seven [rules],” etc. How large is a large estate? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: That there should be twelve months of sustenance for all of them. {NAME} heard this and said, this is the opinion of {NAME}, but the Sages say, until they reach adulthood or are married. They asked before {NAME}, what did you hear from {NAME}? He said to them, let us explain the words of the Sages by their words! {NAME} asked before {NAME}, if there was sustenance for twelve months but the estate diminished in value? He answered him, since the heirs started to eat with permission, they continue to eat until the last coin is gone.
[Ketubot 13:3.3] When does one appraise for them? {NAME} said, one appraises at the end. {NAME} said to him, the words of the rabbis imply that one does not listen to you, for {NAME} asked before {NAME}, if there was sustenance for twelve months but the estate diminished in value? He answered him, since the heirs started to eat with permission, they continue to eat until the last coin is gone! Therefore, one appraises at the start. {NAME} asked: If there was sustenance for twelve months and then the property increased in value? Let us hear from the following, for {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: If the heirs sold, they sold from their own property. So here, if it increased in value, their property value increased. If the estate was not sufficient for twelve months’ sustenance, may the sons say to the daughters, take what is yours and leave! {NAME} said, is that a question? The Mishnah says that they cannot say so to them, as we have stated there: “If the orphans say, we accept the properties of our father for the value of an extra denar in order to take their mother’s ketubah ; one does not listen to them but one appraises the properties in court.”
[Ketubot 13:3.4] As you say, after deduction for her ketubah , after deduction of burial costs, after deduction of loans by witnesses or by contract. After deduction for daughters’ dowries? For him who says, one forecloses from mortgaged property for daughters’ dowries, the dowries are privileged. For him who says, one does not foreclose from mortgaged property for daughters’ dowries, the dowries are not privileged. Let us hear from the following: The widow and the sons are of equal rank. The widow and the daughters are of equal rank. The widow does not push the sons aside and the widow does not push the daughters aside. How is that? If there was enough for 12 months sustenance and a widow to sustain. That explains that sometimes the widow pushes out the sons by means of the daughters. Just as she pushes out the sons by means of the daughters, should she not push them out by means of the sons? She might claim her ketubah and lose her right to sustenance.
[Ketubot 13:3.5] “The sons shall go begging.” Some Tannaïm state, “shall support themselves.” He who says “shall support themselves”, “make yourselves comfortable under the tree.” He who says, “go begging”, “may his children wander about begging, asking out of their ruins.”
[Ketubot 13:3.6] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav; Ze‘ira in the name of {NAME}: Ḥanan made two statements, practice follows him; Admon made seven statements, practice does not follow him. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: In every case in which {NAME} said, I am convinced by Admon’s statement, practice follows him.
[Ketubot 13:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody sues another for amphoras of oil, and the defendant admits [that he owes him] vessels, Admon says, since he admitted part of the claim he is made to swear, but the Sages say, what he admitted was not of the kind that was claimed. {NAME} said, I am convinced by Admon’s statement,
[Ketubot 13:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody sues another for amphoras of oil,” etc. The Mishnah, if he sued him for wheat and he admitted barley; but if he sued him for two kinds and he admitted one of them, according to everybody he is free.
[Ketubot 13:4.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah, if he sued him for wheat and he admitted barley; but if he sued him for two kinds and he admitted one of them, according to everybody he is free. And why did we state: “{NAME} obligates him”? This comes to tell you the power of {NAME}, how far he obligates people. {NAME} [supported] that of {NAME}. {NAME} says, the Mishnah, if he sued him for wheat and he admitted barley; but if he sued him for two kinds and he admitted one of them, according to everybody he is obligated. Rav followed {NAME}: A person went with another to court before Rav. He started claiming from him barley, wheat and spelt. Rav told him, charge him with anything you have to charge, and in the end he will swear one oath about everything. {NAME} said, so argued {NAME} against {NAME}: In your opinion, since you say that if he sued him for two kinds and he admitted one of them, according to everybody he is free, did we not state “if he sued him for vessels and real estate; if he admitted the vessels and denied the real estate, the real estate and denied the vessels”? If he is obligated for vessels about vessels, not so much more vessels for real estate? What does he do with it? He explains it, to transfer an oath to him. But did we not state: If somebody sues another for amphoras of oil, and the defendant admits [that he owes him] vessels”? How do we hold? If he sued him for vessels and oil, and he admitted one of them, everybody agrees that this refers to the claim. But if he sued him for oil and he admitted vessels, everybody agrees that what he admitted does not refer to the claim, for {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of Rav: The Mishnah deals with the case that he sued for vessels full of oil; the ones are full, the others empty. One understands vessels but not oil. Oil but not vessels? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} formulates it as oil bucket. Can one not ask him in the end? If he lost his speech.
[Ketubot 13:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody obligates himself about money for his son-in-law but then goes bankrupt, she must wait until her hair grows white. Admon says: “If I had obligated myself, I would have to wait until my hair grows white. My father obligated himself, what can I do? Marry definitively or divorce!” {NAME} said, I am convinced by Admon’s statement.
[Ketubot 13:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody obligates himself about money for his son-in-law,” etc. The Mishnah [deals with the case] that he obligated himself in her presence. But if he obligated himself not in her presence, even the rabbis will agree.
[Ketubot 13:5.3] It was stated: {NAME} said, Admon and the rabbis did not disagree about one for whom the father had promised money but went bankrupt that she may sit until her hair grows white. Where did they disagree? If she promised herself. Admon says, she might say, “I was of the opinion that my father wants to give, but now my father does not want to give, what can I do? Marry definitively or divorce!” {NAME} said, I am convinced by Admon’s statement.
[Ketubot 13:6.1] MISHNAH: If somebody protests about a field when he himself had signed as a witness, Admon says: “The second one fits me, the first one was harder”; but the Sages say, he lost his right [of appeal]. If he made [the field] a marker for another, he lost his right.
[Ketubot 13:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody protests about a field,” etc. Not only if he himself made it a marker for another [field], but even if a third person made it for a fourth, when he signed as a witness, he lost his right.
[Ketubot 13:7.1] MISHNAH: If somebody went overseas and lost the way to his field, Admon says, he shall go the shortest way but the Sages say, he has to buy a right of access for a hunded minas or fly through the air.
[Ketubot 13:7.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody went overseas,” etc. {NAME} said, if he sues with reasons. This means, only if four [owners] surround him. {NAME} says, even if one surrounds him on all sides. Joshua’s stipulation! “If he was lost in vineyards or fields, he crosses and leaves until he reaches a road to his house, even a plot full of vineyards, for this is one of the conditions under which Joshua distributed the Land to Israel.” Joshua stated this to leave, maybe to enter? Joshua stipulated for a person, perhaps for his cow? {NAME} said, his cow usually returns; since a swarm of bees does not usually return, they treated it as if it were his body.
[Ketubot 13:7.3] {NAME} said, both Admon and {NAME} said the same thing, as we have stated there: “If he sold them to another person, {NAME} said, he does not have to buy access, but the Sages say, he has to buy access.” He had not heard that {NAME} said, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They disagree when nothing was mentioned. Where do we hold? If it is obvious that access was included, everybody agrees that he does not have to pay for access. If it is obvious that access was not included, everybody agrees that he has to pay for access. But we must hold that nothing was mentioned. Then {NAME} said, he does not have to buy access, but the rabbis say, he has to buy access. But in the case here, even while it is clear that he had access, everybody agrees that he has to pay for access.
[Ketubot 13:8.1] MISHNAH: If somebody produces a promissory note on another person who in his turn produces a document that [the creditor] sold him a field, Admon says, “if I really owed you, you should have collected what is yours when you sold me the field;” but the Sages say, that one was smart when he sold him real estate because he can take it as a pledge.
[Ketubot 13:8.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody produces a promissory note on another person,” etc. {NAME} says, if it is worth it; {NAME} says, even if it is not worth it. Think of it, if he had real estate! He can say to him, I want good real estate. Think of it, if he had good real estate! He can say to him, I want mine. In addition, he can say to him, to care for two parcels overtaxes my powers.
[Ketubot 13:9.1] MISHNAH: If two people mutually produced promissory notes of one on the other, Admon says: “If I owed you, how come you borrowed from me?” But the Sages say, each collects the amount of his note.
[Ketubot 13:9.2] HALAKHAH: “If two people mutually produced promissory notes of one on the other,” etc. If one borrowed a mina from the other, but the other borrowed from him 200 [ zuz ]. {NAME} said, {NAME} and Rab Sheshet disagree. One says, one counts one mina against the other mina, but the other says, each one collects the amount of his note. He who says, one counts one mina against the other mina, learns it from tame oxen who injured one another, where half of the excess damage is paid. He who says, each one collects the amount of his note, learns it from the Sages and Admon. Can the Sages and Admon not agree that one counts one mina against the other mina? Because we have stated: Admon says: “If I owed you, how come you borrowed from me?” Therefore it was necessary to say, each one collects the amount of his note. If the holder of the note of 200 forgave a mina, but the holder of the note of a mina did not forgive. For him who says, one counts one mina against the other mina, already one mina against the other mina was counted. But for him who says, each one collects the amount of his note, then what he forgave he cannot collect but what was not forgiven he can collect. If the note for 200 was written in a document but the loan for a mina was not written. For him who says, one counts one mina against the other mina, already one mina against the other mina was counted. But for him who says, each one collects the amount of his note, the holder of the written note can collect but the recipient of the oral promise cannot collect.
[Ketubot 13:10.1] MISHNAH: There are three districts for marriage, Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee. One does not move from one village to another village and from one walled city to another walled city, except that in one district one moves from one village to another village and from one walled city to another walled city, but not from a village to a walled city or from a walled city to a village. One moves from a bad neighborhood to a better one but not from a better one to a worse one. {NAME} says, not even from a bad neighborhood to a better one, because the better neighborhood tests.
[Ketubot 13:10.2] HALAKHAH: “There are three districts for marriage, Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee.,” etc. The Mishnah refers to the case that he was from Judea and married a woman in Galilee, or from Galilee and married a woman in Judea. But if he was from Judea and married in Judea, or from Galilee and married in Galilee, one forces her to move. ”‘I, x, am from Judea and married a woman in Judea,’ one forces her to move, ‘in Galilee’ one does not force her to move. ‘I, X, am from Galilee and married a woman in Galilee,’ one forces her to move, ‘in Judea’ one does not force her to move. One moves from a mostly Gentile village to a totally Jewish village but not from a totally Jewish village to a mostly Gentile village.”
[Ketubot 13:10.3] And from where that a better neighborhood tests? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} in the name of Ḥanina: “That disaster should not cling to me and I die.” He was in the plain and was directed to the mountains, and you say so? But from here that a better neighborhood tests!
[Ketubot 13:11.1] MISHNAH: Everybody moves to the Land of Israel but not everybody leaves. Everybody moves to Jerusalem but not everybody leaves. How is this? If he married a woman in the Land of Israel and divorced her in the Land of Israel, he pays her in coin of the Land of Israel. If he married a woman in the Land of Israel and divorced her in Kappadokia, he pays her in coin of the Land of Israel. If he married a woman in Kappadokia and divorced her in the Land of Israel, he pays her in coin of the Land of Israel; {NAME} says, in coin of Kappadokia. If he married a woman in Kappadokia and divorced her in Kappadokia, he pays her in coin of Kappadokia
[Ketubot 13:11.2] HALAKHAH: “Everybody moves,” etc. If he wants to move to the Land of Israel but she does not, one forces her to move. If she wants but he does not, one does not force him to move. If he wants to move to Jerusalem but she does not, one forces her to move. If she wants but he does not, one does not force him to move. If he wants to leave the Land of Israel but she does not, one does not force her to leave. If she wants to leave but he does not, one forces her not to leave.
[Ketubot 13:11.3] “He pays her in coin of the Land of Israel.” This implies that the coins of the land of Israel are the best of all countries. This supports him who says that a woman’s ketubah is from the words of the Torah, against {NAME}, as it was stated: A woman’s ketubah is from the words of the Torah. {NAME} says, a woman’s ketubah is only an institution of the Soferim .

[Sotah 1:1.1] MISHNAH: If a man declares his jealousy to his wife, {NAME} says, he declares his jealousy in front of two [witnesses] and takes her to drink by the testimony of one witness or his own testimony. {NAME} says, he declares his jealousy in front of two [witnesses] and takes her to drink by the testimony of two [witnesses].
[Sotah 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If a man declares his jealousy to his wife,” etc. It is written: “A spirit of jealousy overcame him and he declared his jealousy to his wife;” this implies that he should not declare his jealousy jokingly, or in the middle of a conversation, or lightly, or in a friendly manner but in a way that inspires fear. If he transgressed and declared his jealousy in one of the aforementioned ways: was this said as an obligation or as a necessity? If you say as an obligation, his declaration of jealousy is valid. If you say as a necessity, his declaration of jealousy is invalid. This is resolved referring to the statement: Anywhere “law” or “teaching” is mentioned, it is an absolute necessity.
[Sotah 1:1.3] The declaration of jealousy, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, is obligatory; but {NAME} said, it is optional. {NAME} said before {NAME}, it turns out that {NAME} follows the House of Shammai and {NAME}. As the House of Shammai say, a man may not divorce his wife except if he found in her a matter of nakedness. If he found her behavior ugly, he cannot divorce her since he found no proof of adultery; he cannot keep her since he found her behavior ugly. Therefore, he says, it is obligatory. But was it not stated in the name of the House of Shammai: Not only that the woman must leave because of incest; from where that she must leave if her head’s [hair] is loose, if the side seams of her dress are open, or her arms stripped bare? The verse says, “for he found in her a matter of nakedness.” {NAME} said, I confirmed this if there are witnesses, but not if there are no witnesses.
[Sotah 1:1.4] “And {NAME} [follows] the House of Hillel.” For the House of Hillel say, even if she burned his food. Therefore, he says it is optional. If he wants to declare his jealousy, he declares his jealousy; if he wants to divorce her, he divorces her.
[Sotah 1:1.5] What is {NAME} reason? “For he found in her a word of nakedness.. “Nakedness”, that is the rendez-vous. “Word”, that is the declaration of jealousy. “Word, word”; just as “word” mentioned there requires two witnesses, so “word” mentioned here requires two witnesses. “But he can take her to drink by the testimony of one witness or his own testimony,” “she was untrue to him in untruthfulness”, about the conditions spelled out to her through the mouth of others.
[Sotah 1:1.6] It was stated: “{NAME} says in the name of {NAME}, he declares his jealousy by the testimony of one witness or his own testimony; he takes her to drink on the testimony of two witnesses.” It is said here: “For he found in her a word of nakedness”; “finding” anywhere has to be validated by witnesses. How does {NAME} explain “a word”? A circumstance that brings into the habit of nakedness. May a single witness let him take her to drink? His own testimony can never obligate him to swear in money matters but it will let him take her to drink, a single witness who will obligate him to swear in money matters not so much more? May a relative bring her to drink? Who is a closer relative than her husband? May a hearsay witness bring her to drink? What is the difference between him and a relative? A relative may be disabled today but he might be enabled later, a hearsay witness is not acceptable either today or later.
[Sotah 1:1.7] What is the reason of {NAME}? ““For he found in her a word of nakedness.” “Word”, that is the declaration of jealousy. “For he found”; “finding” has to be validated by witnesses. (“But he can take her to drinkby the testimony of one witness or his own testimony,” “she was untrue to him in untruthfulness”.) How does {NAME} explain “nakedness”? [A prohibition of] nakedness that came because of a word.
[Sotah 1:1.8] They answered on the words of {NAME}: If so, there is no end to it. If he is believed, he declares his jealousy (before two) [by himself], brings witnesses that she was in a secluded place and disables her from receiving the ketubah . {NAME} said, what business did she have in a secluded place? But it refers to the statement in the Mishnah. Is he believed to declare formally his jealousy and then say that she was in a secluded place and disable her from receiving her ketubah ? {NAME} said, even for that other Tanna it is [a] valid [objection], following him who says that he may declare his jealousy in respect to her father or her son. Is he believed to declare his jealousy with respect to her father and her son, can he then bring witnesses that she was in a secluded place with them and disable her from receiving her ketubah ? If you ask, what business did she have in a secluded place? The Torah permitted her to be in a secluded place, since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, it is written: “If your brother, your mother’s son, incites you, etc.,” Your daughter, in secret; your mother, in secret; a man may be alone with his mother and dwell with her, with his daughter and dwell with her, with his sister but may not dwell with her.
[Sotah 1:1.9] Witnesses of a declaration of jealousy who were found to be false are whipped. About witnesses concerning her being in a secluded place who were found to be false, you say that they are whipped; why should they not pay? It is not through their action that she loses her ketubah . Or it might be, following what {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of {NAME}: One does not infer one thing from another in the matter of false witnesses. And here it is so.
[Sotah 1:1.10] If she was seen going to a secluded place by one witness in the morning and by one witness in the evening, it is to be treated like the following: “If she was together alone with him by the testimony of two witnesses, she needs a second bill of divorce from him; if there was a single witness she does not need a second bill of divorce from him. With one witness in the morning and one witness in the evening, such a case happened and {NAME} asked the Sages, who told him that this is not being together alone.” If he declared his jealousy before one witness in the morning and before one witness in the evening; since he is a man and she is a woman, his declaration is nothing. Or is it to be treated like the following: “One accepts the witnesses’ testimony only if they saw it together. {NAME} says, even if they saw it one after the other.” {NAME}, {NAME} bar [Rav] Isaac in the name of Rav: The Sages agree with {NAME} with regard to witnesses of firstlings and witnesses of squatters’ rights. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. The same holds for testimony regarding signs. In that case, it is obvious if one says, I saw two hairs on his back and the other says, I saw two hairs on his back. If one says, I saw one hair on her back and the other says, I saw one hair on her back, that is nothing; similarly on his back and on his back. If two say, we saw one hair on his back and two others say, we saw one hair on his belly? {NAME} and {NAME}, one said, it is invalid, but the other said, it is valid. He who says it is invalid considers him as one who testifies to half a sign. He who says it is valid? I say, maybe they were rubbed off. Two say, we saw one hair on his back and two others say, we saw one hair on his belly. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that this is invalid [testimony]. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that this is valid. {NAME} said, this is in disagreement; {NAME} said, this is in disagreement. {NAME} said, does not {NAME} follow my opinion? He answered, I am disagreeing with his teacher, so much more with him. {NAME} said, {NAME} was correct. If a document was signed by four witnesses and it was disputed, if one person verified the signature of two [witnesses] and another that of the other two, is that worth anything? Does not every single signature need two witnesses? And here, every single hair needs two witnesses. {NAME} learns it from the years of squatting rights. If one [witness] testified that he ate from the property the first, second, and third years and another [witness] testified that he ate from it the fourth, fifth, and sixth, is that worth anything? Does not every single year need two witnesses? And here, ever single hair needs two witnesses.
[Sotah 1:2.1] MISHNAH: How does he declare his jealousy? If he said to her in front of two [witnesses]: Do not speak with the man X, and she spoke with him, she still is permitted to her house and to eat heave. If she enters a hidden room together with him and remains there long enough for impurity, she is forbidden to her house and forbidden to eat heave; if he dies she needs ḥalîṣah but cannot be married in levirate.
[Sotah 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: “How does he declare his jealousy,” etc. Does this mean only, until she talks with him? That would imply, if she went to a secluded place with him without talking, that going to a secluded place would count for nothing? It comes to tell you more: Even if she talked to him but was not with him in a secluded place, she still is permitted to her house and to eat heave, since the Mishnah uses chaste language: Do not be alone with Mr. X.
[Sotah 1:2.3] May he declare his jealousy with respect to two men together? {NAME} said, that is in dispute. He who says that he may declare his jealousy with respect to her father and her son, [says] that he may declare his jealousy with respect to two men together. {NAME} asked: May he declare his jealousy with respect to a hundred men? {NAME} said to him: If he said to her, do not enter the synagogue, she enters.
[Sotah 1:2.4] “With him.” {NAME} said, it only said “with him.” Therefore, not one after the other. {NAME} said, even one after the other since anyhow it is obvious: On a road during the night, in a ruin during daytime, in dark passageways during daytime.
[Sotah 1:2.5] “They asked {NAME}: Why is a doubt in a private domain considered impure? He said to them: Where is the suspected wife? In a private domain. He said to them, we find that she is forbidden for her house.” The words of the rabbis disagree, since {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: An underage girl who whored has no will to be forbidden to her husband. But did we not state: “In any case where there is no mind to be asked, the doubtful case is pure”? Therefore, if there is a mind to be asked, the doubtful case is impure. But here, even while there is a mind to be asked, the doubtful case is pure! “Why is a doubt in a public domain considered pure? He said to them: We find that the public prepare their Passah [as in] purity when most of them are impure. If known impurity was permitted in public, so much more for a case of doubtful impurity.”
[Sotah 1:2.6] There, we have stated: “In all matters of incest, He made him who touches equal to him who completes and one is guilty for each single intercourse. He was more stringent with the slave girl since in her case He treated the intentional as unintentional.” {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: “Flow of semen,” until he ejaculates. Here is written “flow of semen”, and here is written “flow of semen.” Here, you say “flow of semen” until he ejaculates. And here, you say so? {NAME} said, there is a difference, for it is written: “She was hidden and became impure.” From the moment she was hidden, the Torah calls her “impure”. But here, “flow of semen,” until he ejaculates. For what reason is written “flow of semen”? For measures, as it is stated: “She was hidden and became impure”; what is counted as hiding? Time to become impure. What is the time for impurity? Time for intercourse. What is the time for intercourse? Time for ‘touching’.
[Sotah 1:2.7] “How long is ‘touching’? {NAME} says, [time needed] to walk around a date palm; {NAME} says, to mix a cup [of wine]; {NAME} says, to drink it; {NAME} says, [time needed] rolling an egg; {NAME} says, to sip three rolled eggs one after the other; {NAME} says, [time needed] for the weaver to bind a thread; Miniamin says, that she can stretch out her hand and lift a loaf of bread from the basket. And though there is no proof, at least there is a hint: ‘For a whoring woman up to a loaf of bread.’” {NAME} said, all these measurements [of time] are after she removes her underpants. {NAME} said, each of them judged by his own experience. But did {NAME} ever marry? Some want to say, he had an erection. But some want to say, he was married and gave it up. Some want to say, “the secret of the Eternal is for those who fear Him, to inform them about His covenant.”
[Sotah 1:2.8] It was stated: Rebbi said, three times is “impurity” said in the paragraph, one for the husband, one for the paramour, and one for heave. For heave? Do we find that a woman is forbidden to her house and permitted to eat heave? Why not? If the daughter of a Cohen was married to an Israel and raped, is she not permitted to her house but forbidden heave? We never find that a woman is forbidden to her house and permitted to eat heave! {NAME} said, it was said: One for the husband, one for the paramour, and one for the levir. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says so: “If he dies she needs ḥalîṣah but cannot be married in levirate.”
[Sotah 1:2.9] {NAME} stated before {NAME}: “‘If you deviated from under your husband.’ This excludes rape.” How do you understand this? He said to him: Just as she is “under your husband” by her consent, so also in this case by her consent.
[Sotah 1:2.10] Just as the woman accused of infidelity is forbidden to her husband, so she is forbidden to her paramour. Just as she is forbidden to her husband’s brother, so she is forbidden to her paramour’s brother. I might think that just as the co-wife of a woman accused of infidelity is forbidden to her husband’s brother, so she should be forbidden to her paramour’s brother. Let us hear from the following: “A woman’s husband went overseas; they came and told her that her husband had died, and she had a levir here; he married her in levirate and died. Then her husband returned. She is forbidden to him but her co-widow is permitted to him; she is forbidden to him but his brother’s wife is permitted to him.” Is his brother’s wife not like the co-wife of a woman accused of infidelity? That means that the co-wife of a woman accused of infidelity is permitted to her paramour’s brother. {NAME} said, this follows the rabbis there, as {NAME} said, one states there, for incestuous relationships no divorce is needed except for a married woman; {NAME} says also from his wife’s sister. But following the rabbis here? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: everybody agrees that his brother’s wife needs a bill of divorce from him because of the rule of a married wife. She is forbidden by the incest rules, and an incest-prohibited woman frees her co-wife. {NAME} said, it is accepted even according to the rabbis here. They fined her but not her heirs. {NAME}, said, according to the rabbis there, she should be permitted to him. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, the co-wife of a woman accused of infidelity is forbidden, the co-wife of a divorcee is permitted. {NAME} [{NAME}] in the name of {NAME}: All co-wives are permitted except the co-wife of a woman accused of infidelity. {NAME} said, the divorcee herself is permitted to her house. Why is the co-wife of a woman accused of infidelity forbidden? {NAME} said, they touched this case because it looks like adultery. [Sotah 1:4.3] {NAME}, the son-in-law of {NAME}, reported the following happening. {NAME} used to preach in the synagogue of Ḥamata every Friday evening. There was a woman who used to hear him. Once he extended his sermon. She went and wanted to come to her house but found the light had gone out. Her husband asked her, where have you been? She said to him, to hear the preacher’s voice. He said to her, so and so, that this woman will not enter here into her house unless she went and spat into the preacher’s face. {NAME} saw this in the holy spirit and faked pain in his eyes. He said, any woman who knows charms for the eye should come and do the charm. Her neighbors said to her, this answers your needs. Go to your house, represent yourself as a sorceress and spit in his eye. She came to him; he asked her, do you know to make a charm for the eye? In her fear of him, she said no. He said to her, if you spit into it seven times, he will feel better. After she had spat, he said to her: Go, and tell your husband, you said to me once, but she spat seven times! His students said to him, so does one denigrate the Torah? If you had ordered about him, would we not have brought him, whipped him on the footstool, and make him agree to make up with his wife? He said to them, the honor of Meïr should not be greater than that of his Maker. Since the verse says that the Holy Name, written in holiness, should be erased by the water in order to make peace between husband and wife, the honor of Meïr not so much more?

[Sotah 1:7.3] It was stated in the name of {NAME}: Just as there are opinions in eating and drinking, so opinions are [varied] among men. Or you have a man who if a fly flies over his cup, takes it, pours [the contents] out, and does not taste them. That is a bad human attitude because he thinks of divorcing her. Or you have a man who, if a fly sits on his cup, takes it and leaves [the cup] untouched. That is {NAME} who locked his wife in. They said to him, did your forefathers behave like this? Or you have a man who finds a dead fly in his cup, takes it, licks it, and drinks. That is the wicked one who sees that his wife is overbearing with her slaves and slave-girls, where he would be commanded to divorce her, as it is said: “She left his house and went and married another man.” The verse called him other because he is not of the class of the first who expelled his wife because of a sexual transgression and the other one stumbled over her.
