[Nazir 6:9.1] MISHNAH: He cooked the well-being offering or scalded it. A Cohen takes the cooked fore-leg of the ram, one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened thin bread, places it on the nazir ’s hands and waves it. Afterwards the nazir is permitted to drink wine and to defile himself with the dead. {NAME} says, when one of the bloods was sprinkled, the nazir is permitted to drink wine and to defile himself with the dead.
[Nazir 6:9.2] HALAKHAH: A Mishnah states that scalding is called cooking, as we have stated: “If he cooked the well-being offering or scalded it.” A verse [states] that “roasted” is called “cooked”: “They cooked the pesaḥ ”, etc. If you say, against the rules, {NAME} said, “as is the rule”. A Mishnah states that scalded is called cooked: “Is one who makes a vow to abstain from cooked food permitted roasted and scalded food”? {NAME} said, in matters of vows one follows common usage. {NAME} said, in matters of vows one follows biblical usage. What is the difference between them? ‘A qônām that I shall not taste wine on Tabernacles.’ In the opinion of {NAME} he is forbidden on the last day of the holiday. In the opinion of {NAME}, is he permitted? {NAME} also agrees that he is prohibited. {NAME} said it only for restrictions.
[Nazir 6:9.3] {NAME} said, {NAME} ate bake-meats and said, I did not taste food on that day. But did we not state: “He who made a vow not to eat food is permitted water and salt”? Explain it following {NAME}, who said, in matters of vows one follows biblical usage. And from where that everything is called food? {NAME} said: “And ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and food, etc.” Why does the verse say, “and food”? From here that everything is called food.
[Nazir 6:9.4] It is written: “The Cohen takes the cooked fore-leg of the ram.” If cooked, I could think separately. The verse says, “from the ram”. How is this? He cuts it off so that only a barley grain’s width remains. Does not the sanctified absorb from the profane, or the profane from the sanctified?.
[Nazir 6:9.5] Ḥilfai asked {NAME} and {NAME}, do condiments forbid with more than 200? They said to him, condiments are not in more than 200. But did we not state: “Anything which sours, flavors, or creates dema ‘?” If you say about 100 or 200, even if it does not sour, flavor, or create dema ‘! But we deal with grapes. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, if they were not raisins, but if they were raisins they are condiments in more than 200. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, if they were not cooked, but if they were cooked they are condiments in more than 200.
[Nazir 6:9.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: All sources of flavor one in a hundred. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: All sources of flavor one in sixty. {NAME} said to {NAME}: {NAME} disagrees with you and the Mishnah disagrees with both of you: “Anything which sours, flavors, or creates dema ‘? If you say about 100 or 200, even if it does not sour, flavor, or create dema ‘! Therefore, we hold even more. {NAME} said, explain it for meat in meat. {NAME} said, meat in meat is the same as all other prohibitions since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, one estimates as if they were onion or leeks.
[Nazir 6:9.7] How is this? One says, all sources of flavor by one in 100; the other says, all sources of flavor by one in 60. For him who says all sources of taste by one in 100, you take the foreleg as one in 100 of the ram. For him who says all sources of taste by one in 60, you take the foreleg as one in 60 of the ram. For him who says one in 100, you remove the bones from the foreleg. But if you remove the bones from the foreleg, remove them from the ram! This you cannot do, as it was stated: “The waste of heave does not combine with heave to forbid the profane, but the waste of profane combines with the profane to lift the heave.” {NAME} asked: Does the waste of heave combine with profane to lift the heave? Since {NAME} said, the husks of what is forbidden combine to permit; that means waste of heave combines with profane to lift the heave.
[Nazir 6:9.8] {NAME} stated: All I forbade to you at other places I permitted to you here. Since everywhere 100 is a prohibition, more than 100 is permitted, but here even 100 is permitted.
[Nazir 6:9.9] Rav said, waving stops the nazir . But did we not state: “The teachings for the nazir ,” whether or not he has wings? What Rav says, if he does, as it was stated thus: For somebody able to wave, waving stops him; for somebody unable to wave, waving does not stop him. {NAME} says, measure stops a nazir , as for the waves and thumbs of a sufferer from skin disease. But did we not state: “The teachings for the sufferer from skin disease,” whether or not he has thumbs? He explains it following {NAME} who said, he puts it on their place.
[Nazir 6:10.1] MISHNAH: If he shaved for one of the sacrifices and it turned out to be invalid, his shaving is invalid and his sacrifices are not counted for him. If he shaved for the purification offering not in its name but brought the other sacrifices in their names, his shaving is invalid and his sacrifices are not counted for him. If he shaved for the elevation or well-being offerings not in their names but then brought his sacrifices in their names, his shaving is invalid and his sacrifices are not counted for him. {NAME} says, that sacrifice is not counted for him but the others are counted for him. But if he shaved for all three and one of them is valid, his shaving is valid and he has to repeat the other sacrifices.
[Nazir 6:10.2] HALAKHAH: Is it counted for him and his shaving? If you would say that it is not counted for him and his shaving, then his sacrifices count for nothing. {NAME} asked: Following {NAME}, may he shave for his holiday well-being offerings? Is that not the Mishnah? “{NAME} says, that sacrifice is not counted for him but the others are counted for him.” When he slaughtered them are they not like voluntary well-being offerings? This means that he may shave for voluntary well-being offerings following {NAME}. {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME}. For {NAME} it is problematic, but for {NAME} it is obvious.
[Nazir 6:11.1] MISHNAH: If one of the bloods had been sprinkled for him when he became impure, {NAME} says, he has to repeat everything. But the Sages say, he shall bring his remaining sacrifices once he became pure again. They told him, it happened with Miriam the Palmyrene, that one of the bloods had been sprinkled for her when she was informed that her daughter was dying; she went and found her dead; then the Sages said, she shall bring her remaining sacrifices once she becomes pure again.
[Nazir 6:11.2] HALAKHAH: The argument of {NAME} seems inverted. There, he says: “he has to repeat only for 30,” and here, he says so? {NAME} says, he has to repeat all his sacrifices. It is obvious, if it would have been valid without him becoming impure, then why is it not valid if later he becomes impure? {NAME} said, is that not {NAME}? And {NAME} follows the Shammaites, as it was stated: Concerning a nazir who lost all his hair, the House of Shammai say, he has to move a shaving knife over his head; the House of Hillel say, he does not need to move a shaving knife over his head.
[Nazir 6:11.3] So is the Mishnah: He shall become pure again and then bring his remaining sacrifices. So is the Mishnah: She shall become pure again and then bring her remaining sacrifices.
[Nazir 7:1.1] MISHNAH: The High Priest and the nazir do not defile themselves for their relatives. If they were walking on a road and found a corpse of obligation, {NAME} says, the High Priest shall defile himself but the nazir shall not defile himself. But the Sages say, the nazir shall defile himself but the High Priest shall not defile himself. {NAME} said to them, the Priest shall defile himself, who does not bring a sacrifice for his defilement, but the nazir shall not defile himself, who has to bring a sacrifice for his defilement. They told him, the nazir shall defile himself, whose holiness is temporary, but the Priest shall not defile himself, whose holiness is permanent.
[Nazir 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The High Priest and the nazir ,” etc. It is written: “He shall not go close to a dead body.” Where do we hold? If to forbid non-relatives, is he not also under the rules of a simple priest? If it cannot refer to non-relatives, refer it to relatives. It is written: “Not to go close to a dead body,” and you say so? {NAME} said, from here repeated prohibitions in the Torah. But it is to permit the corpse of obligation. Some understand it from the following: “ The man shall not defile himself, in the midst of his people” he may not defile himself. But he defiles himself for a corpse of obligation. Some understand it from the following: “ To profane himself.” He may not defile himself to profane himself; he defiles himself for a corpse of obligation.
[Nazir 7:1.3] Some want to derive it from the following: “For a hanged person is blasphemy.” Anybody warned about blasphemy is warned about a corpse of obligation. Anybody not warned about blasphemy is not warned about a corpse of obligation. They objected, are there not Gentiles? Those executed by hanging, this exludes those executed by the sword. “Bury!” A positive commandment. From where do you add the sword he was killed with, the gallows on which he was hanged, the towel with which he was strangled? Why does the verse say, “you shall bury him”? I could think he alone is buried; the verse says “bury, you shall bury him”, a burial for him, and his gallows, and his stone. How does one do it? One digs down three [handbreadths], so the plough shall not unearth him. “You shall bury him”, whole and not partially. “You shall bury him”, from here that if he left anything [unburied], he did not do anything, for it is said “bury, you shall bury him”. From here that it is not a corpse of obligation unless it consists of his head with most of the body.
[Nazir 7:1.4] {NAME} stated before {NAME}: Just as one defiles himself for a corpse of obligation, so one defiles himself for a limb of a corpse of obligation. {NAME} answered him: Is that so? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it if he returns. It was stated: {NAME} said, nobody has to defile himself for a limb from his living father, but one has to defile himself for bone the size of a barley corn from his father. {NAME} says, just as one has to defile himself for bone the size of a barley corn from his father, so one has to defile himself for a limb from his living father. “It happened that {NAME} developed a growth on his foot. When the surgeon came to remove it, he told him to inform him when only a hair’s breadth was left. He cut until only a hair’s breadth was left, and informed him. He addressed his son Onias and told him, Onias my son, up to now you had to care for me, but leave now since nobody has to defile himself for a limb from his living father. When this came before the Sages, they said, about him it was said: “It happens that a just man is lost in his merit;” the just is lost and his merit accompanies him.
[Nazir 7:1.5] What is a corpse of obligation? Anyone for whom he shouts and nobody comes. If the villagers come, he refrains. How many? For the carriers of the bier, their replacements, and the replacements of their replacements. If he is not needed; but if he is needed, it is different. If [the deceased] is not recognized. But if he is recognized, it is different. If it is not according to his honor; but if it is according to his honor, it is different. For the Patriarch it is his honor.
[Nazir 7:1.6] May a Cohen defile himself for the Patriarch? When {NAME} died, {NAME} proclaimed and said: “There is no priesthood today.” When {NAME}, {NAME}, died, {NAME} did push {NAME} in the Gufna synagogue of Sepphoris and defiled him. When Yehudinai, the sister of {NAME}, died, {NAME} sent for {NAME} but the latter did not come. He said to him, if one does not defile himself for them during their lifetime, so much less in their death. {NAME} said, in their death they treated them like a corpse of obligation.
[Nazir 7:1.7] May a Cohen defile himself for the honor of his teacher? The father-in-law of {NAME} died. He was both his father-in-law and his teacher. He asked {NAME} who forbade it. {NAME} (?) heard it and said: His students should defile themselves for him. The students [of {NAME}] defiled themselves for him but ate meat and drank wine. {NAME} told them: One of two things you cannot escape. If you are mourners, why did you eat meat and drink wine; if you are not mourners, why did you defile yourselves?
[Nazir 7:1.8] May a Cohen defile himself for the study of Torah? {NAME} was sitting and teaching when a dead body was brought in. He did not say anything either to those who remained sitting or to those who left.
[Nazir 7:1.9] {NAME} said: My father did not walk under the arch of Caesarea. {NAME} walked. {NAME}, {NAME} and {NAME} went walking in the streets of Caesarea. They came to the arch and {NAME} left. They reached a place of purity and he returned to them. He asked them: “What were you discussing?” {NAME} said to {NAME}: “Do not tell him anything!” We do not know whether it was because he was angry that he left since one defiles oneself for words of Torah or whether it was because he was haughty.
[Nazir 7:1.10] It is stated: A Cohen may defile himself by leaving the Land for civil and criminal suits, for the consecration of the New Moon and intercalation of a year, to redeem a field from a Gentile, to study Torah, and to marry a wife. {NAME} says, if he has a place to study, he should not defile himself. {NAME} says, even if he has a place to study, he may defile himself, since a man may not have the luck to learn from every teacher. They said about Joseph the Cohen that he followed his teacher and defiled himself following his teacher to Sidon. In truth, they said a priest should not go abroad unless one promised him a wife.
[Nazir 7:1.11] May a (High) Priest defile himself for the lifting of hands? On second thoughts he said, maybe he heard from me what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Every Cohen who stays in the synagogue and does not lift his hands transgresses a positive commandment, and he wanted to say that a positive commandment supersedes a negative commandment. I never told him anything. Bring him in and I will flog him!
[Nazir 7:1.12] {NAME} was sitting teaching in the fortified synagogue in Caesarea; there was a coffin there. There came the time for lifting the hands and they did not ask him. There came the time for eating and they asked him. He said to them: For the lifting of hands you did not ask me, for eating you are asking me? When they heard this, each one was taking himself away and fled.
[Nazir 7:1.13] {NAME} said: A Cohen defiles himself in order to see the King. When {NAME} visited here, {NAME} was seen stepping over graves at Tyre in order to see him. {NAME} and {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: There is an obligation to see great persons of government, so that when the kingdom of the dynasty of David will return one will know how to distinguish one government from the other.
[Nazir 7:1.14] May [a Cohen] defile himself in honor of his father and mother? {NAME} heard that his mother had come to Bostra. He went and asked {NAME}, may I leave? He said to him, if it is because of danger on the road, leave. If it is in order to honor your mother, I do not know. {NAME} said, {NAME} still needs to answer. [Nazir 7:1.15] May a (person) [Cohen] defile himself in honor of the public? It is stated: When there are two acceptable roads, one long and pure, the other one short and impure: If the public was walking on the long one, he goes on the long one; otherwise, he goes on the short one in honor of the public. That refers to impurity by their words; also for impurity that is from the words of the Torah? From what {NAME} said, so great is the honor of the public that it temporarily pushes aside a prohibition, that means even impurity that is from the words of the Torah.
[Nazir 7:1.16] {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: One does not ask rulings on practice before the bier of a deceased. [Nazir 7:1.17] It is stated: The carriers may not wear sandals lest a shoelace of one of them break so he would be prevented from performing a good deed.
[Nazir 7:1.18] {NAME} bent down during a eulogy. They wanted to straighten him up and found that he tarried. They said to him, what is this? He said to them, because we will go there, following ( Eccl . 7:2 ): “Let the one who is alive take it to heart.”
[Nazir 7:1.19] If somebody finds a corpse of obligation, he has to take care of it and bury it at its place. When is that? If he finds it outside the town limits. But if he found it inside the town limits, he brings it to the cemetary to bury it.
[Nazir 7:1.20] {NAME} said, the start of my practice before the Sages was the following. Once I was on the road when I found a corpse of obligation; I carried it about four mil to a cemetery and buried it. When I came to {NAME} and {NAME} and told them, they said to me that every step that you walked is counted against you as if you were shedding blood. I said, if I became guilty when I intended to acquire merit, how much worse is it if I do not intend to acquire merit. From that time on I did not interrupt practicing before Sages. He used to say, anybody who did not practice before Sages deserves the death penalty.
[Nazir 7:1.21] The corpse of obligation acquired its place, four cubits even in a field of saffron, for on this condition did Joshua distribute the Land to Israel. When is this? If he found it in the field. But if he found it on the road, he buries it either to the right or to the left of the road. A fallow and a ploughed field, he buries it in the fallow field. A ploughed and a sown field, he buries it in the ploughed field. A vineyard and a sown field, he buries it in the sown field. A vineyard and an orchard, some Tannaïm state, he buries it in the vineyard; some Tannaïm state, he buries it in the orchard. He who says, he buries it in the vineyard but not in the orchard, because of a tent over the corpse. He who says, he buries it in the orchard but not in the vineyard because of the preparation of the grape harvest. If he switched, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: He transgressed “do not defile your land.” If both were fallow, or ploughed, or sown, he buries in the one he chooses.
[Nazir 7:1.22] A Cohen and a Levite, the Levite shall defile himself. A Levite and an Israel, the Israel shall defile himself. No, is not the Levite like the Israel? {NAME} said, it was taught in the time of the platform. The Sages agree with {NAME} that between a High Priest and a nazir , the nazir shall defile himself but not the High Priest. {NAME} agrees with the Sages that between a High Priest and a nazir , the nazir shall defile himself but not the High Priest. Think of it, if his father sanctified him from birth. The one is from the Torah, the other is not from the Torah. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} parallels the House of Shammai. As the House of Shammai say, between holy and frequent the holy has precedence, so {NAME} says, between holy and frequent the holy has precedence. A nazir for 30 days and a nazir for 100, the nazir for 30 days shall defile himself. A nazir for 100 days and a nazir forever, the nazir for 100 days shall defile himself. A nazir forever, and a nazir of neziriot , some Tannaïm state, the nazir forever shall defile himself; but some Tannaïm state, the nazir of neziriot shall defile himself. He who says, the nazir forever shall defile himself but not the nazir of neziriot , since he shaves more frequently. He who says, the nazir of neziriot shall defile himself but not the nazir forever, since he brings more sacrifices. If he switched, it should be as {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: He transgressed “do not defile your land.” Here it is the same.
[Nazir 7:2.1] MISHNAH: The nazir shaves for the following impurities: For a corpse, for flesh in the volume of an olive of a corpse, and for the volume of an olive of decayed matter from a corpse, and for a spoonful of decay, for the spine and for the skull, for a limb from a corpse or a limb from the living on which there is sufficient flesh, for half a qab of bones, and for half a log of blood, if they are touched, or carried, or under a tent. Also for a bone in the volume of a barley grain if it is touched, or carried, (or under a tent.) For these, the nazir shaves, he sprinkles on the third and seventh [days], he disregards the preceding days and starts to count only after he purifies himself and brings all his sacrifices.
[Nazir 7:2.2] HALAKHAH: “The nazir shaves for the following impurities,” etc. An old man asked {NAME}: If the volume of an olive from a corpse makes impure, then certainly all of it also? He said to him, to include the stillbirth which did not reach the volume of an olive. He continued to ask: If a limb of a corpse makes impure, then certainly all of it also? He said to him, to include the stillbirth whose limbs did not yet jell. {NAME} said, was that old man wise? His questions were not wise since after he asked the first question, it was not necessary to ask the second. If he wanted to ask both, he should have asked the second and after that the first. The students of {NAME} asked the second but did not ask the first because it was obvious for them that if he did not reach the volume of an olive it is certain that his limbs did not yet jell. {NAME} said, do you remember when {NAME} was here, were not both questions by that old man [asked] about Ahilut that the nazir shaves for them? In addition, from what {NAME} said, I thought that the stillbirths were not Torah. But since he makes his mother sit days of purity, it is implied that [the rules of] stillbirths are Torah.
[Nazir 7:2.3] It was stated: {NAME} says, why did they say that a crawling animal the size of a lentil makes impure? Because the start of the creation of a crawling animal is the size of a lentil. {NAME} asked: Should not a corpse bring impurity even if it is less than the volume of an olive, for did not {NAME} say, “to include the stillbirth which did not reach the volume of an olive”? And a carcass the size of a pea should cause impurity, for {NAME} said, I saw a calf the size of a pea in a placenta! How is that? I say, [these are] sermons. Preach and receive reward.
[Nazir 7:2.4] What is decayed matter? Flesh of the corpse which was separated and fluid that coagulated. Therefore not when it is still mashed? Did not {NAME} say in the name of Rebbi: Fat from a corpse which was melted remains impure; if he cut it and then melted it, it is pure. {NAME} and {NAME}, one says to exclude the fluid in the flesh; the other says that if it will fill the volume of an olive when congealed, it will be impure when still mashed.
[Nazir 7:2.5] We have stated: “{NAME} said, dried flesh from a corpse which even if soaked will not return to its former status is pure. What is {NAME} reason? Did he not infer this from a carcass? From a carcass, since a dried carcass is pure, so also a dried corpse should be pure. {NAME} asked: Since a foul-smelling carcass is pure, would a foul-smelling corpse also be pure? Then there can be no decayed matter for {NAME}! It was found stated in {NAME} name that there was decayed matter. The colleagues asked before {NAME}: Since a carcass has no decay, so a corpse should have no decay! He told them that he inferred from an animal only for the flesh, not for the bones. There is no decay from flesh, there is decay from bones, as {NAME} stated, “decay of bones is jealousy.” {NAME} said, “or a grave”, even if one touched the first Adam’s grave. The colleagues say, he transposes the verse: “or a grave qbr ” means “or decay rqb ”. {NAME} stated, “or a grave qbr ”, “or decay rqb ”.
[Nazir 7:2.6] {NAME} said, the Holy One, praise to Him, took a spoonful from the place of the altar and created Adam from it. He said, he shall have been created from the place of the altar so that he should be able to stand up. That is what is written: “The Eternal Omnipotent formed Adam the first of dust from the earth”, and it is written: “You shall build for me an altar of earth.” Since “earth” there means an altar, here also [it means] an altar. “His days should be a hundred and twenty years.” Adam the first lived close to a thousand years and you say, “his days should be a hundred and twenty years”! But after 120 years he returns to be a spoonful of decay. That is difficult. For Og, the king of Bashan, 120 years, and for a newborn baby 120 years? Og [becomes] a spoonful of decay, and a newborn baby becomes a spoonful of decay. “ The spoonful of decay which they mentioned is from his finger joints and upwards, the words of {NAME}, but the Sages say, from a fully developed hand.” {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rebbi was illustrating that of {NAME} one way, that of the rabbis in another way.
[Nazir 7:2.7] “Which corpse has decay? One who was buried naked in a marble coffin, or on a stone floor, or on a marble table. But if he was buried in a wooden casket or on a woooden plank; that is not decay but graves’ dust and needs somewhat more than a spoonful.” {NAME} said, if even the smallest attachment was buried with him, there is no decay. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Of two corpses which were buried together, each one becomes an attachment for the other. This is automatic; could one alone be an attachment to another? {NAME} objected: Think of it, that somebody brought half a spoonful from one and half a spoonful from the other! He was considering it when he was seen laughing; he was offended by him and he died. {NAME} said, there this man is gone and we did hear nothing about it. What about it? There, neither of them will produce a spoonful of decayed matter, but here, each of them can generate a spoonful of decay.
[Nazir 7:2.8] If his foot was cut off, from above the joint there is no “decay”, from below the joint there is “decay”. If it was buried together with him, from below the joint it becomes an attachment to him, from above the joint it does not become an attachment to him. The colleagues asked before {NAME}: If he bound from below the joint as attachment? He said to them, if it were so, even if it was not cut I should consider it as if cut and it should be an attachment! Since it is connected to him, it forms one body. If there is something missing, can it have “decay”? Let us hear from the following: If it is imcomplete, there is no “decay”, it does not require the surrounding earth, and it is not part of a row of graves. {NAME} asked, how much must be missing that it have no “decay”? Might it follow what we have stated there: “That he will die if it was removed.” Is it the same here? Think of it, if the esophagus was perforated, nothing was missing but he could not survive. You have only the following: If his foot was cut off, from below the joint there is “decay”, from above the joint there is no “decay”. If it was buried together with him, from below the joint it becomes an attachment to him, from above the joint it does not become an attachment to him.
[Nazir 7:2.9] Do stillbirths generate “decay”? For him who says that their blood induces impurity by a quartarius they generate “decay”; for him who says that their blood does not induce impurity by a quartarius , do they generate “decay”? Let us hear from the following: “Why is the dust from small heaps impure? Because women bury there their stillbirths.” {NAME}, {NAME}, said: Would it not be reasonable otherwise, that lepers bury their limbs there? You must say that it is because of “decay”, not because a bone the size of a lentil, since it was stated: “If he took some dust from it and replaced it, [the small heap] is pure.” Explain it following Tannaïm, as it was stated: If one removed it, it remains impure; {NAME} declares it pure.
[Nazir 7:2.10] {NAME} said, it was formulated following {NAME}, as it was stated: The spine and the skull are impure even if crushed, even disconnected, because the grave unites them as “a human in a tent”.
[Nazir 7:2.11] The Mishnah follows {NAME}, as it was stated: “{NAME} said, earlier the courts were divided; some said, a quartarius of blood, a quarter bones; some said, half a log of blood, a half a log of bones, for nezirut and the impurity of the Sanctuary and its sacred offerings.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They said this as explanation from the mouths of Ḥaggai, Zachariah, and Malachi.
[Nazir 7:3.1] MISHNAH: But for overhanging branches, or protuberances, or broken fields, or Gentile territory, or the cave door, or its frame, or a quartarius of blood, or a tent, or a quarter ( qab ) of bones, or objects that touched the corpse, or the days of his counting or his being absolute, the nazir does not shave but sprinkles on the third and seventh days, does not disregard the preceding, starts counting immediately, and has no sacrifice. In truth, the days of a male or female sufferer from flux and the days of quarantine of the sufferer from skin disease are counted for him.
[Nazir 7:3.2] HALAKHAH: “But for overhanging branches, or protuberances,” etc. What is the status of the undistributed middle? {NAME} said, the undistributed middle is judged leniently. {NAME} said, the undistributed middle is judged restrictively. What is the undistributed middle? That is a limb from a corpse or a limb from a living body which is not sufficiently covered by flesh. {NAME} asked: From where [do we infer that] a bone [induces impurity in the size of] a barley grain? Not from that verse, “or a person’s bone”? Here you require a barley grain, there you do not require a barley grain! {NAME} stated: “A slain one”, anything from a slain person, that is a limb from a corpse or a limb from a living body which is not sufficiently covered by flesh.
[Nazir 7:3.3] {NAME} said, overhanging branches and protuberances are biblical for heave even though the nazir does not shave. {NAME} asked, if to burn it, one burns even for a rabbinic doubt; maybe to whip? Rebbi [Yose] from Sidon stated before {NAME} and disgagrees with {NAME}: “For any impurity deriving from a corpse for which a nazir shaves one is guilty if entering the Sanctuary, but any impurity deriving from a corpse for which a nazir does not shave one is not guilty if entering the Sanctuary.”
[Nazir 7:3.4] {NAME} said, layers of a tree which cover four-by-four [handbreadths]: the nazir shaves. {NAME}, {NAME} said, if one of his hands is on the other side and one hand is in the layer, the nazir does not shave. {NAME} asked: If it separates from impurity it also should separate from purity; if it does not separate from impurity, it should not separate from purity. {NAME} said, if the corpse is in the bedroom and the nazir under the bed, the nazir shaves. Certainly if the corpse is under the bed and the nazir in the bedroom, does the nazir not shave? {NAME} said, if the corpse and the nazir are under the bed frame, under the belly of a camel, under the width of a gate, under the gutters, the nazir does not shave, nor for anything which is there for protection. {NAME} heard it and said, they purified the dead! {NAME} said, if the corpse is in the anteroom and the nazir in the dining hall, the nazir shaves; certainly if the corpse is in the dining hall and the nazir in the anteroom, the nazir shaves. {NAME} asked, if it is a tent to separate it should be a tent to draw along; if it is not a tent to draw along, the impurity should disappear! {NAME} said, if the impurity is under the outer half of the wall, the nazir shaves. {NAME} said, if impurity is hidden in the ground of the house, the nazir shaves. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The nazir does not shave for most of the skeleton or most of the bones.
[Nazir 7:3.5] “In truth;” {NAME} said that every place where they stated “in truth,” refers to practice going back to Moses on Mount Sinai.
[Nazir 7:3.6] “They shall fall away, for his vow of nazir is impure.” From here that the days of impurity fall away. Then should he invalidate? He invalidates only the days of [impurity of] the dead. Why should they not be counted? If you say that days in which he causes [impurity to] couch and seat are counted, days in which he does not cause [impurity to] couch and seat are certainly counted! What did you see to say that they are not counted? Rebbi [] said in the name of {NAME}: “For a wild growth of his head’s hair”. Days of hair growth are counted, days preparing for shaving are not counted. So far in his days of counting; in the days of his definite status? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “Please do not let her be like a corpse.” Since the days of a corpse are not counted, the days of quarantine are not counted. A student quoted this saying cf {NAME} before {NAME}, who did not accept it. He said to him: Here, you call it quarantine, but there, you want to call it absolute; you cannot do that. For {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: “Please do not let her be like a corpse; let her be quarantined.” Just as the days of the dead are seven, so the days of quarantine are seven.
[Nazir 7:4.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: For any impurity caused by a corpse for which the nazir shaves, one is guilty if entering the Sanctuary, but for any impurity caused by a corpse for which the nazir does not shave, one is not guilty if entering the Sanctuary. {NAME} said, this should not be less than the impurity of a dead reptile! {NAME} said, I argued before {NAME}: If for a barley-grain sized bone, which does not cause impurity to a human in a tent, a nazir shaves if he touches or carries it, should it not be logical that for a quartarius of blood, which causes impurity to a human in a tent, a nazir should have to shave if he touches or carries it? He said to me, what is that, Aqiba? This is not a place for an argument de minore ad majus ! When I came and expounded that before {NAME}, he said to me, you have a good argument, but that is what they said was practice.
[Nazir 7:4.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} said in the name of {NAME},” etc. There, we have stated: “Two are impure from the dead, one is impure for seven days and one is impure by the impurity of evening. Three are impure from the dead, two are impure for seven days and one is impure until nightfall. Four are impure from the dead, three are impure for seven days and one is impure until nightfall. How is it for two? Any person who touches a corpse is impure for seven days; a person who touches him is impure until nightfall,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: All are biblically [impure] for heave, but for entering the Sanctuary only the second impure who touched the first impure. What is the reason? “A person who would be impure and did not purify himself;” anybody needing purification is guilty for entering the Sanctuary; anybody not needing purification is not guilty for entering the Sanctuary. They objected: But a person who touches objects which touched a corpse needs purification, but is he the second? {NAME} said, for impurity of a person from a person, not for impurity of a person from objects. The statement of {NAME} [implies that] only the first is guilty. Since [for impurity of] a person from a person only the first is guilty, so here the first is guilty. {NAME} said, only if he immersed himself. That is a statement of Rebbi, since Rebbi said, all impure persons remain impure until the are immersed in water.
[Nazir 7:4.3] {NAME} said: He himself, who touched the corpse, is guilty. He said it and gave its reason: “who became impure,” that refers to the impurity of a human. But is there not a third? As {NAME} said, for impurity of a person from a person a man is guilty for impurity in the Sanctuary. They objected: If objects touch the corpse, a human the objects, and objects the human. For impurity of a person from a person, not for impurity of a person from objects. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Tanna there disagrees with {NAME}: “For an object made half of cement־earth and half of dung one is not guilty for coming to the Sanctuary” Because it is half of earth and half of dung; but if it were totally of earth, one would be guilty. Who is guilty? Not the one who touches it? Is he not the second who touches the first? {NAME} said before {NAME}: Explain it if he threw it. He answered him, about him who threw it we stated: For washing his body he is subject to extirpation, for washing his garments to the forty. {NAME} said before {NAME}, do we not have the Mishnah in support of that first Tanna, as is stated: “{NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: For any impurity caused by a corpse for which the nazir shaves, one is guilty if entering the Sanctuary, but for any impurity caused by a corpse for which the nazir does not shave, one is not guilty if entering the Sanctuary.” For the first, for which the nazir shaves, one is guilty if entering the Sanctuary; for the second, for which the nazir does not shave, one is not guilty if entering the Sanctuary. {NAME} said, it is needed from what comes from the corpse: For a quartarius of blood or a quarter qab of bones, for which the nazir does not shave, one is not guilty if entering the Sanctuary; for half a log of blood and half a qab of bones, for which the nazir shaves, one is guilty if entering the Sanctuary. {NAME} said, we were of the opinion that they disagree about a sacrifice, but one whips even the third, even the fourth. {NAME} stated before {NAME} in opposition to {NAME}: “For any impurity caused by a corpse for which the nazir shaves, one is guilty if entering the Sanctuary, but for any impurity caused by a corpse for which the nazir does not shave, one is not guilty if entering the Sanctuary.” {NAME} said, {NAME}, {NAME}: It is needed from what comes from the corpse: For a quartarius of blood or a quarter qab of bones, for which the nazir does not shave, one is not guilty; for half a log of blood and half a qab of bones, for which the nazir shaves, one is guilty.
[Nazir 8:1.1] MISHNAH: If a person said to two nezirim : I saw one of you becoming impure but I do not know which one of you it was, they bring one sacrifice of impurity and one of purity. One of them says, if I am impure, the sacrifice of impurity is mine and that of purity is yours; otherwise the sacrifice of purity is mine and that of impurity is yours. Then they count another thirty days and bring one sacrifice of purity; ( Mishnah 2 ) one of them says, if I was impure, the sacrifice of impurity was mine and that of purity was yours, hence this is my sacrifice of purity; otherwise the sacrifice of purity was mine and that of impurity was yours, hence this is your sacrifice of purity. If one of them died, {NAME} said, he should seek out a person from the general public who would make a vow of nazir corresponding to his needs and say: If I was impure, you are a nazir immediately, but if I was pure, you are a nazir after 30 days. They count 30 days and bring one sacrifice of impurity and one of purity (Mishnah 3) and he says: If I am impure, the sacrifice of impurity is mine and that of purity is yours; otherwise the sacrifice of purity is mine and that of impurity is questionable. Then they count another thirty days, bring one sacrifice of purity ( Mishnah 4 ) and he says: If I was impure, the sacrifice of impurity was mine and that of purity was yours, hence this is my sacrifice of purity; otherwise the sacrifice of purity was mine and that of impurity was questionable; hence this is your sacrifice of purity. {NAME} said to him, who would accommodate him to make a vow of nazir corresponding to his needs? But he brings a bird as purification offering and an animal as elevation offering and says: If I was impure, the purification offering is for my obligation and the elevation offering is voluntary. But if I was pure, the elevation offering is for my obligation and the purification offering is questionable. Then he counts 30 days and brings one sacrifice (of impurity and one) of purity (Mishnah 5) and says: If I was impure, the first elevation offering was voluntary and the one now is for my obligation. But if I was pure, the first elevation offering was for my obligation and now I am bringing the remainder of my sacrifices. {NAME} said, then it turns out that he brings his sacrifices piecemeal! But the Sages accepted the words of {NAME}.
[Nazir 8:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If a person said to two nezirim ,” etc. Not only if he said to one of them, “I saw one of you becoming impure but I do not know which one of you it was,” but even if he said, “I saw one of you vowing to be a nazir but I do not know which one of you it was,” both of them have to follow the rules of nazir because of his testimony. If they do not contradict him. But if they contradict him, this does not apply. If both of them contradict, it parallels the following: “If one witness says, he became impure, but he says, I did not become impure, he is pure. If two witnesses say, he became impure, but he says, I did not become impure, the two are believed more than he is, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, everybody is believed about himself.” {NAME} in the name of Rav: So is the Mishnah: {NAME} declares impure, {NAME} and the Sages declare pure. {NAME} said, so is the Mishnah: {NAME} declares impure, {NAME} declares pure. The rabbis’ words support {NAME}, since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} said this only about an old impurity, for he can say to them, I had been impure but I purified myself, and we have stated: The same holds for eating suet; the same holds for entering the Sanctuary. Should they not accept his position for impurity? Because of the impurity of a nazir , could they not say, where is the sacrifice which you brought? Then should they not accept his position for heave? So far the questions of {NAME}.
[Nazir 8:1.3] {NAME} understood it from the following: “They told him, if he wishes, he says that he did it intentionally.” What can he say for an assigned slave girl? In error, he is obligated; intentionally, he is obligated! He can tell him, I touched her but did not finish, or as {NAME} said, I was forced to it by the spell she put on me. For a nazir what can you say? In error, he is obligated; intentionally, he is obligated; forced, he is obligated! “Suddenly”, to include in error, “suddenly”, to include intentionally. “There was a condition in my mind that if I should become impure, my nezirut should burst away from me and a new nezirut would fall on me”; in any case he was not obligated to be a nazir until now. (“There was a condition in my mind that if I should become impure, my nezirut should burst away from me and a new nezirut would fall on me”; in any case he was not obligated to be a nazir until now.) What do you have in case of an oath? In error, he is obligated; intentionally, he is obligated! A condition may apply to words; there is no condition for oaths! It follows what {NAME} said, {NAME}: For error, its sacrifice, for intention, its sacrifice. But if he said, I thought that this was no oath, he is free. Therefore, all these subjects cannot be stated, but the following can be stated.
[Nazir 8:1.4] From what {NAME} said, “X ate suet, and they warned him,” he is not whipped. If one person said to him, you are a nazir , and based on this testimony he behaved like a nazir , when then he drank wine or became impure in the impurity of the dead, if two warned him, he is whipped. Is not the main testimony given by a single witness? From what {NAME} said, “X is the wife of a Cohen and whored; her husband, a Cohen, then had relations with her but I had warned him;” he is [not] whipped. If she went to a secluded place in the presence of two, and one said, I saw her that she became impure; when her husband, the Cohen, had relations with her but two had warned him, he is whipped. Is not the main testimony given by a single witness?
[Nazir 8:1.5] “They bring one sacrifice of impurity and one of purity.” That is, if they are at the end of thirty days. But if one is in the middle of thirty days, one has to wait till the end of thirty days. If both of them were nezirim for thirty days. But if one was a nazir for thirty and the other a nazir for 100, one has to wait for 100. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If one of them became impure during these days, what is the rule? He said to him, like one who has to seek out a person from the general public.
[Nazir 8:1.6] If he drank wine within the first 30 days, he is (not) whipped; within the last 30 days, he is [] whipped. The one coming from the general population cannot be whipped, either for the (second) or the last period. So far, if he was warned separately for each period. If they warned him for both together this is the disagreement between {NAME} and {NAME} who disagreed about the two days of holiday in the diaspora. {NAME} said, one accepts warning in case of a doubt; {NAME} said, one does not accept warning in case of a doubt.
[Nazir 8:1.7] “I made a vow of nazir but I forgot whether it was for now or for a later date.” They told him, this [warning] is for now, and that for the later date. If he drank wine within the first 30 days, he is [] whipped; within the last 30 days, he is (not) whipped. Should one not say that the first days may be within the period of his vow, the later ones are after the period of his vow? “All days of his status as nazir ,” to make the days after he finished his term like the days before he finished his term with respect to wine, impurity, and shaving.
[Nazir 8:1.8] Why can he not bring his sacrifices one by one? Not to preclude answers in the house of study.
[Nazir 8:1.9] (The community) [A person] who became impure by a doubt relating to a private domain on Passover. {NAME} said, he should be pushed to the Second Passover. {NAME} said, one sends him on a far journey. (A nazir ) [The community] who became impure by a doubt relating to a private domain on Passover. {NAME} said, it should be presented in their doubt; {NAME} said, it should be made in impurity. [Nazir 8:1.10] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One sprinkles on an uncircumcised Jew, for we find that our forefathers in the desert received sprinkling when uncircumcised. {NAME} said, following him who said that they circumcised on the eleventh. But for him who said that they circumcised on the tenth, they did not count sprinkling when uncircumcised. {NAME} said, did they not have to count for sprinkling when uncircumcised in any case 68 ? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It happened that an uncircumcised Cohen was sprinkled and the sprinklings were declared valid. [Nazir 8:2.1] MISHNAH: A nazir who was doubtfully impure and doubtfully definitely [suffering from skin disease] may eat sacrificial meat after 60 days and drink wine and become impure by the dead after 120 days, since the shaving for skin disease supersedes the shaving of the nazir when it is certain, but when it is in doubt it does not supersede.
[Nazir 8:2.2] HALAKHAH: Who is doubtfully definitely [suffering]? Two who came to him. He declared one of them definitively affected but before he could declare the second one definitively affected, they were changed for him. That is a doubtfully definitely [suffering person]. This is the one about whom {NAME} stated: A nazir , in doubt whether impure or pure, but certainly he was a nazir . A sufferer from skin disease, in doubt whether impure or pure, but certainly he was a sufferer from skin disease. He eats from sacrificial meat after 60 days, drinks wine and defiles himself for the dead after 120 days. How is that? One said to him, you are an impure nazir , go count seven [days]. He sprinkled, repeated, shaved, and brought. He then counted seven [days] and wanted to shave. One said to him, impure nazir , go count seven [days] and continue for 30. He counted 30 [days] and wanted to shave. One said to him, you are a pure nazir , does not a pure nazir shave on kinds of blood? He brings an elevation offering and shaves on it, a bird purification offering and stipulates, saying: “If I was impure, the purification offering is my obligation and the elevation offering is voluntary. If I was pure, the elevation offering is my obligation and the purification offering is in doubt.” He shaves his head, his beard, and his eyebrows in the way the sufferer from skin disease shaves.
[Nazir 8:2.3] How does one deal with him in a restrictive way? He brings two swallows and slaughters one of them over a clay vessel filled from running water; one digs und buries it, for it is forbidden for usufruct. He shaves his head, beard, and eyebrows in the way the sufferers from skin disease do. He counts 30 days and brings another animal as elevation offering, saying: “If I was impure, the first elevation offering was voluntary and this one is obligatory, and the purification offering is my obligation. If I was pure, the first elevation offering was my obligation, this one is voluntary, and the purification offering is in doubt.” He shaves his head, his beard, and his eyebrows in the way the sufferer from skin disease shaves.
[Nazir 8:2.4] {NAME} said: On the next day, he brings his reparation sacrifice and a log of oil with it and says: If I was impure, this is my obligatory offering, otherwise it is my doubtful offering. He stipulates and says: If I was impure, that is my obligation. Otherwise, this is in doubt.

[Nazir 9:1.1] MISHNAH: Gentiles cannot take a vow as nazir . Women and slaves can take a vow as nazir . A man’s power is restricted for his wives more than for his slaves since he can force his slave but he cannot force his wife. His power is restricted for his slaves more than for his wives since he can dissolve his wife’s vows but not his slave’s vows. If he dissolved his wife’s, they are eternally dissolved. If he dissolved his slave’s, once the slave gains his freedom he has to fulfill his nezirut . If [the slave] is not in the presence of his master, {NAME} says, he cannot drink, but {NAME} says, he may drink.
[Nazir 9:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Gentiles cannot vow as nazir ,” etc. Israelites can vow as nazir , Gentiles cannot vow as nazir . Since you say, “a man”, why does the verse mention “a man”? To include Gentiles, who make vows and offer voluntary gifts like Israelites! Why should one not say the same here? There is a difference, for it is written “He shall atone for him.” This refers to one to whom atonement applies. It excludes Gentiles, to whom atonement does not apply.
[Nazir 9:1.3] There, we have stated: “The Non-Jew, {NAME} says, is evaluated but does not evaluate; {NAME} says, he evaluates but is not evaluated. Both agree that they make vows and are objects of vows.” {NAME} asked: For him who says there that he evaluates, here can he declare a nazir ? For him who says there that he is evaluated, here can he be declared a nazir ? How would it be possible for him to [be declared a nazir ]? A Israelite can declare a Gentile to be a nazir . Would he listen to him? But the Israelite said, “I am a nazir ,” the Gentile heard it and said, “I am responsible for what this one said.” It is only as if he paid a debt. How would it be possible for him to [declare a nazir ]? A Gentile can declare an Israelite to be nazir . Since an Israelite cannot declare [another] Israelite to be a nazir , a Gentile cannot declare an Israelite to be a nazir . But it must be that the Gentile said, “I am a nazir ”, the Israelite heard it and said, “I am taking upon me what this one said.” What did you exclude from him? An Israelite is subject to “not to desecrate”, a Gentile is not subject to “not to desecrate”. {NAME} said, Israelites can be relieved by a Sage, Gentiles cannot be relieved by a Sage. {NAME} said, Israelites need a Sage to be relieved, Gentiles do not need a Sage to be relieved. It follows that Rebbi (Jonah) [Yose] follows {NAME}. A Gentile woman came before {NAME}, who said to {NAME}: Go and find her an opening by unforeseen circumstances. And {NAME} follows {NAME}, who said that Laban was Kushan-Riš‘ataim . Why was he called “Kushan the doubly bad”? Because he committed two evils. One that he desecrated his oath, the other that he subjugated Israel for eight years.
[Nazir 9:1.4] Why can he not force his wife? Did not {NAME} say, [if she vowed] any benefit from me [shall be forbidden] to you, he forces her and sleeps with her. Any benefit from you [shall be forbidden] to me, he hasto dissolve. There is a difference because it is a benefit for him and her. He should not be able to force his slave! There is a difference, “because his God’s crown is on his head,” a person who has no other master. This excludes the slave who has another master. If he comes to protest his master’s word, one says to him: this is practice, obey your master’s orders! If his master pushed him and he became impure, does he have to bring a sacrifice of impurity? Is he a nazir , did not you decide for him that he should become impure? You say, he brings a sacrifice of impurity; could he bring here a sacrifice of impurity? Does he annul? Is he a nazir , did not you decide for him that he should become impure? You say, he annuls; could he here annul?
[Nazir 9:1.5] The following is obvious: If he became impure and then was manumitted, he brings a sacrifice of impurity. When is that, if his master forced him or if his master did not force him? If you say that he forced him, how can be bring a sacrifice of impurity? If you say he did not force him, should he not count for his master as long as he still is in the latter’s power? {NAME} said, we are dealing with the case that his master forced him. You should not say that because he was manumitted, the nezirut in impurity was lifted from him. Therefore, it was necessary to say that he counts nezirut in impurity.
[Nazir 9:1.6] “{NAME} said, if a slave said, ‘I shall be a nazir when manumitted,’ his master forces him in matters of nezirut . [The master] can force a slave in matters of nezirut ; he does not have to force him in matters either of vows or of oaths.” {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If his master forced him and he became impure, is he to be whipped? Or is that only practice? Where do we hold? If his nezirut has biblical status and by practice one may force, he is whipped. If both are rabbinical, he is not whipped. {NAME} said, does one whip for practice? But it must be the following: If his nezirut is practice and by practice one may force, he is whipped. If both are rabbinical, he is not whipped.
[Nazir 9:1.7] If his master forced him in one respect, did he force him in all respects? We came to the disagreement between {NAME} and {NAME}: “If [the slave] is not in the presence of his master, {NAME} says, he cannot drink, but {NAME} says, he may drink.” Where do we hold? If he told him, drink whether in my presence or not in my presence, even {NAME} will agree. If he told him, drink in my presence, do not drink in my absence, even {NAME} will agree. But we hold in the case that he tells him: “drink!” {NAME} says, [it means] drink in my presence, do not drink in my absence. {NAME} says, [it is] as if he said, drink whether in my presence or not in my presence.
[Nazir 9:2.1] MISHNAH: If a nazir was informed that he was impure after he had shaved and it was a known impurity he cancels, but if it was impurity of the abyss he does not cancel. If it was before he shaved, he cancels in any case. How is that? If he went to immerse himself in a cave where a corpse was floating at the entrance, he is impure. If it was found buried in the ground and he went there to refresh himself, he is pure, but to purify himself from the impurity of the dead he is impure since the presumptive state of the impure is impure and the presumptive state of the pure is pure, for it is not unsubstantiated.
[Nazir 9:2.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, who is the Tanna of “when he had shaved, before he shaved”? {NAME}! But for the rabbis it would be before the blood was sprinkled for him. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: What is {NAME} reason? “The nazir shall shave the hair of his crowned head.” The Torah made his nezirut dependent on his hair.
[Nazir 9:2.3] If he completed his nezirut but did not manage to shave before he was informed about a possible case of a grave in the abyss, he cancels. If he designated his sacrifices but did not manage to shave before he was informed about a grave in the abyss? {NAME} said before {NAME}: Is that not the Mishnah? Whether he shaved or did not shave following {NAME}, or whether it happened before or after blood was sprinkled according to the rabbis!
[Nazir 9:2.4] From where about a doubtful case of a grave in the abyss? {NAME} in the name of the rabbis: “Or on a far trip for you.” What is open for you, including everything in the open. This excludes the case of a grave in the abyss which is not open.
[Nazir 9:2.5] So far for the people celebrating Passover. From where the nazir ? {NAME} in the name of Rebbi [Yannai]: “If a person dies suddenly on him”. Since on him it is in the open, so everything in the open. This eliminates the grave in the abyss which is not in the open.
[Nazir 9:2.6] If the public became publicly impure in a doubtful case of a grave in the abyss, does the diadem make it acceptable? It is a conclusion de minore ad maius. Since in the case of a single person, whose position you clarified to his disadvantage in the case of known impurity, you clarified to his advantage in the case of a grave in the abyss 64 , it should be only logical that for the public, whose position you clarified to its advantage in the case of known impurity, you should clarify it to its advantage in the case of a grave in the abyss. A leniency which you apply to a single person you treat as a restriction for the public. A leniency which you apply to a single person, so that if it became known to him after sprinkling he should be treated as if he became impure before sprinkling, that he should eat the meat. The leniency which you apply to the pure nazir is a restriction for the impure nazir . The leniency which you apply to the pure nazir , so that if it became known to him after sprinkling he is treated as impure after sprinkling, that he should bring a sacrifice of impurity. You treat it as a restriction for the impure nazir , that if it became known to him after sprinkling he is treated as somebody repeatedly becoming impure so that he has to bring a sacrifice of impurity for each single case. As it was stated: If he repeatedly became impure, he has to bring a sacrifice for each single case. If somebody is officiating for the Passover sacrifice, does the diadem make it acceptable? It is a conclusion de minore ad maius. Since for the owners [of the Passover sacrifice] whose position you clarified to their disadvantage in the case of the infirm and the aged, you clarified to their advantage in the case of a grave in the abyss, it should be only logical that for the officiating, whose position you clarified to his advantage in the case of the infirm and the aged, you should clarify it to his advantage in the case of a grave in the abyss. No. For the owners [of sacrifices] you clarify to their disadvantage in the case of impurity during the rest of the year; you also say for the officiating that you clarify their position to their disadvantage in the case of impurity during the rest of the year. Since you clarify their position to their disadvantage in the case of impurity during the rest of the year, you also clarify their position to their disadvantage in the case of the impurity of the dead on Passover. How is it really? “For you”, whether for him or for the one officiating for him. So far for the people celebrating Passover. From where the nazir ? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: We thought, “on him”, not on the one officiating for him. Since we stated that the same rules apply to the nazir and to those celebrating Passover, it means that what holds for the one holds for the other.
[Nazir 9:2.7] “What is a grave of the abyss? A corpse buried in stubble, straw, dust, or pebbles. But if it was buried in water, a dark spot, or rock crevasses, it does not create a grave of the abyss.” The principle: Any place from where it can be removed creates a grave of the abyss; any place from where it cannot be removed does not create a grave of the abyss. Can stubbles and straw not be removed? Does the Mishnah not follow {NAME}, since {NAME} said, straw said to be disregarded is disregarded. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is everybody’s opinion. What {NAME} said, if he mixed it with dust. “There is straw which is treated like dust and dust which is treated like straw. Straw not to be removed is like dust; dust to be removed is like straw.” In the House of {NAME} they said: If he covered it with mats it is disregarded. Come and see: If he [filled] it with mats it is not disregarded, if he covered it with mats it is disregarded. If he filled it with branches of date palms it is problematic. {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: Even thin sheets.
[Nazir 9:2.8] “What is a grave of the abyss? Any which nobody remembers.” Should we not be cautious and say, maybe one at the end of the world? And is the permanence of the living not like living? Explain that he was found compressed.
[Nazir 9:2.9] It was stated: “Only a corpse creates a grave of the abyss.” Therefore, not a carcass. Would it not be a conclusion de minore ad majus ? Since a corpse, which does not cause impurity of couch and seat, creates a grave of the abyss, should a carcasss which causes impurity of couch and seat not create a grave of the abyss? Why was it said that only a corpse creates a grave of the abyss? To exclude couch and seat.
[Nazir 9:2.10] {NAME} said that {NAME} asked Rebbi: So far in a cave that had a ceiling. Even in a cave without ceiling? {NAME} think that if there is a doubt regarding floating impurity, it is pure? Rebbi told him, {NAME} remains in his stupidity: No case of doubt regarding floating impurity is declared pure except a reptile; but a corpse is like something fixed in place. As it was stated: “Anything thrown is pure in case of a doubt except an olive-sized piece from a corpse, [and] also those covers which induce impurity on bottom and top.”
[Nazir 9:2.11] Does this not disagree with {NAME}, since {NAME} said, if impurity is hidden in the ground below the house, the nazir shaves. {NAME} said, here on the side, there on place. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Even if you say in both cases on the side, in both cases on place. What means “impure”? Impure and he does not shave?
[Nazir 9:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody finds a corpse in original position, lying as usual, he takes him and his surroundings. If he finds two, he takes them and their surroundings. If he finds three and between one and the next is a distance of between four and eight cubits, enough for the bier and the people who bury, that is a cemetery. He has to check on both sides for another 20 cubits. If he finds a grave at the end of 20 cubits, he has to check another 20 cubits since it is obvious that if this were a new burial ground, one would have taken him and his surroundings there.
[Nazir 9:3.2] HALAKHAH: What means “lying as usual”? His legs straight and his hands over his heart. But if he found him compressed, I am saying that a heap fell on him and killed him. But did we not state: “If he found two with their heads beside their legs, he takes them and their surroundings?” They wanted to say, what means “compressed”? Their heads beside their legs. {NAME} said, like fried fish, the head of one near the tail of the other and vice versa.
[Nazir 9:3.3] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: In a statement you say, “he collects every single bone and everything is pure;” and here, you say so? He answered him, say what comes afterwards: “If he prepared it from the start as a grave, it has surroundings.”
[Nazir 9:3.4] How much is the surrounding of a grave? One shaves off three finger-breadths, the place where fluid penetrates.
[Nazir 9:3.5] {NAME} said, [the Mishnah] implies that it is permitted to remove a corpse of obligation. {NAME} said, explain it if the burial was unauthorized or subject to question. Should one not be afraid that it might be a corpse of obligation? {NAME} thinks that corpses of obligation are infrequent. “It turns out that there are three kinds of burials. A grave which is found one removes; after removal the place is impure and forbidden for use. A known grave may not be removed; but if it was removed the place is pure and permitted for use. A grave which endangers the public is removed; after removal the place is impure and forbidden for use.” {NAME} instructed in Kefar Aqabia that its place is permitted for use. Does he disagree? There if it preceded the village, here if the village preceded it. It was stated: “A grave surrounded by a village on three sides can be removed,” on two sides, some Tannaïm state that one removes it, some state that one may not remove it. {NAME} said, he who says that one removes it, if it is within slightly more than 70 cubits. He who says that one does not remove it, if it is outside slightly more than 70 cubits. He who says that one removes it, if [the village] is built in the form of a Γ. He who says that one does not remove it, if [the village] is built in the form of a ה. “All kinds of graves may be removed except the graves of a king or a prophet. They said to him, were not the graves of David’s sons removed but the graves of the sons of Ḥulda were in Jerusalem and nobody ever touched them to remove them. {NAME} told them, is that a proof? A duct was there and the impurity exited from there horizontally into the Qidron valley.”
[Nazir 9:3.6] There, we have stated: “He makes a courtyard in front of the cave six cubits square as a place for the bier.” And here, he says so? There for a bier standing, here for the width of a turning bier. How far? For the carriers of the bier, their replacements, and the replacements of their replacements.
[Nazir 9:3.7] There, we have stated: “If a vineyard is planted with less that four cubits of space, {NAME} says that it is no vineyard. But the Sages say that it is a vineyard and one disregards the plants in the middle as if nonexistent.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Just as they disagree here, they disagree about a graveyard. {NAME} said, one cannot compare these. There, they form a graveyard; here, they do not form a graveyard. {NAME} said, one cannot compare these. There, if they were spaced apart and one moved them closer together, that is the disagreement. If they were close and one moved them apart, everybody would agree. But here, what is their disagreement? When one found them close together. {NAME} said, a landslide fell on them and compressed them. But the Sages say, were they spaced apart and somebody brought them close together?”
[Nazir 9:3.8] How far does one importune him? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Up to 40 cubits. If he checked twenty and found, he checks another ten. If he checked twenty and found, he checks another ten. Some Tannaïm state: If he checked ten and found, he checks another ten. If he checked ten and found, he checks another ten.
[Nazir 9:4.1] MISHNAH: Any person with initially doubtful skin disease is pure as long as he was not declared impure. After he was declared impure, in doubt he is impure. In seven ways does one check the sufferer from a genital discharge before he becomes impure: About eating and drinking, carrying a load or jumping, sickness, looking, and thought. After he becomes impure one does not check him; his accident, doubtful case, and semen are impure since the matter is not unsubstantiated.
[Nazir 9:4.2] HALAKHAH: “He shall declare him impure.” The certain case he declares impure, he does not declare the doubtful case impure. Forever he is in his impurity until he is known to be pure. “He shall purify him.” The certain case he declares pure, he does not declare the doubtful case impure. Forever he is in his purity until he is known to be impure.
[Nazir 9:4.3] It is written: “The unwell woman in her separation and the sufferer from flux in his flux.” Since the menstruating woman may become impure also by accident, so the sufferer from flux may become impure also by accident. Then even at his first episode? {NAME} said, from the moment he becomes like a menstruating woman.
[Nazir 9:4.4] “His accident,” {NAME} said, his real accident. “His doubtful case,” a doubt whether it is flux or ejaculation. Are flux and semen not impure anyhow? But one does not consider it for the 24 hour period.
[Nazir 9:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody injured another person who was judged dying and then this person’s state improved but later he died, he is guilty. {NAME} says, he cannot be prosecuted since it is not unsubstantiated.
[Nazir 9:5.2] HALAKHAH: So is the Mishnah: {NAME} declares him not prosecutable but the Sages declare him guilty since it is not unsubstantiated. The Sages say, two estimations have precedence over one estimation; {NAME} says, the intermediate estimation has precedence over the two. What is {NAME} reason? “ ‘If he gets up and walks outside on his cane, the attacker is exonerated.’ Could you think that this one walks in the market and the other is executed because of him? But even if he died according to the first estimation he cannot be prosecuted.” What is the rabbi’s reason? “If he does not die but is bedridden.” Would we not know that even if he does not die that he will be bedridden? But if they estimated that he would die. If they estimated that he would die, that is what is written: “If he gets up and walks outside on his cane.” Therefore, if he does not get up, [the attacker] is guilty. But if they did not estimate that he would die? If they did not estimate that he would die, that is what is written: “But he has to pay for his disability.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It is an extraordinary decree of Scripture that he has to pay. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It was an erroneous estimation. What is the difference between them? If his state improved. For him who says, it is an extraordinary decree of Scripture that he has to pay; if he paid, he paid. If he did not pay, the verse makes him pay. A baraita supports one and a baraita supports the other. A baraita supports {NAME}: If they estimated that he would die, when does he have to pay him? From the moment he improves. For him who says, it was an erroneous estimation; if he did not pay one does not order him to pay. If he paid, can he take it back? This supports {NAME}: If they estimated that he would live but he died. From when does one have to pay him? From the moment he turns worse. {NAME} said, it does not say here, “from the moment he turns worse” but “from the moment he turns better.”
[Nazir 9:5.3] If he hit him on his hand and it withered. The physicians said, if it is amputated he will live. Does he have to pay for the [hand]? Let us hear from the following: “If people quarrel,” “if people brawl.” Is not quarrel brawl and brawl quarrel? Why does the verse say, “if people quarrel, if people brawl”? To apply the rules of the unintended to the intended and of the intended to the unintended. It must be the following: If he hit him on his hand and it withered. The physicians said, if it is amputated he will live. Does he have to pay for the [hand]? Since you say there, it is an extraordinary decree of Scripture that he pay for the hand, so here it is an extraordinary decree of Scripture that he pay for the hand.
[Nazir 9:6.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} was a nazir following the words of {NAME}, as it is said: “A shaving knife shall not come on his head.” It is said about Samson “a shaving knife”, and it is said about {NAME} “a shaving knife”. [Gittin 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Somebody who brings a bill of divorce from overseas must be able to say: “It was written and signed before me.” {NAME} says, even somebody who brings from Reqam and Ḥeger; {NAME} says, even from Kefar Ludim to Lydda; but the Sages say that the only one who has to be able to say that it was written and signed before him is one who brings from overseas or to overseas. One who brings from one province to another overseas has to say that it was written and signed before him; {NAME} says, even from one district to the next.
[Gittin 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody who brings a bill of divorce from overseas,” etc. This is difficult. If somebody brings a gift document from overseas,would you require him to say, it was written and signed before me? {NAME} said, there is a difference because they are not conversant with the fine points of bills of divorce. {NAME} said, that is a leniency lest she sit abandoned. Is that a leniency? It is only a restriction, for if he does not say to her, it was written and signed before me, you do not permit her to remarry. {NAME} said, the difficulty which you impose upon her at the beginning, that he is required to say, it was written and signed before me, makes it easy for her at the end. For if [the husband] would come and protest, his protest would be void. {NAME} wanted to say, a protest other than the text of the bill. But is a protest about the text of the bill a protest which has no validity? Even for a protest which has validity, said {NAME}, since you say that the reason for the difficulty which you impose upon her at the beginning, that he is required to say, it was signed before me, is to make it easy for her at the end, that if [the husband] would come and protest, his protest would be void; this means that there is no difference whether it is a protest not about the text of the bill or about the body of the bill, a protest which has no validity, or a protest which does have validity! But should you worry that maybe be gave the bill to disqualified witnesses to sign? {NAME} said, he is not suspect to damage her before Heaven. Before the court he is suspect to damage her. But since he knows that if he comes and protests his protest is void, he will choose qualified witnesses to sign.
[Gittin 1:1.3] If [the bill of divorce] contained documentation of a gift and [the messenger] said, it was written and signed before me, is [the husband’s] protest about the gift void since it is void about the divorce? Or, since his protest is void [only] about the divorce, is it valid about the gift? We have stated later: “Bills of divorce for wives and documents of manumission are equal in the rules of carrying and bringing.” If [the document of manumission] contained documentation of a gift and [the messenger] said, it was written and signed before me, is [the master’s] protest about the gift void since it is void about the manumission? Or since his protest is void [only] about the manumission, is it valid about the gift? If somebody signed all his property over to his slave, you say that the gift is the document of manumission. How do you treat this? Is it a document of manumission and his protest is void or is it a gift and his protest is valid? This can be compared to the following: If somebody signed all his property over to two persons in one document and the testimony of the witnesses was valid for one but invalid for the other. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} and {NAME} disagreed; one said, since it is invalid for one it is invalid for the other, but the other said, it is valid for one and invalid for the other. {NAME} did not specify; {NAME} specified: {NAME} said, since it is invalid for one it is invalid for the other; but {NAME} said, it is valid for one and invalid for the other. {NAME} said, a Mishnah supports {NAME}: “Since testimony of two [witnesses] is invalid if one of them turns out to be related or disqualified, so also of three [witnesses] it is invalid if one of them turns out to be related or disqualified”. {NAME} said, {NAME} the colleague of the rabbis and the rabbis disagree. One says, the argument of {NAME} is correct, but the other says, {NAME} is not correct. For him who says, the argument of {NAME} is correct, it is a testimony about one person; as testimony it is totally invalid if it is partially invalid. For him who says, the argument of {NAME} is not correct, it is as if two groups of witnesses came, valid for one and disqualified for the other.
[Gittin 1:1.4] Only if he says, it was written before me during the day and signed during the day; only if he says, it was written before me especially for her and signed expressly for her. It was asked before {NAME}: Does he have to know the names of the witnesses at the moment of their signing? He said to them, did the Gentiles Luciani sign it? And you say so? A baraita supports {NAME}: “All bills of divorce coming from overseas are valid even if their names sound Gentile since Jews outside the Land of Israel bear Gentile names.” He said only, outside the Land; therefore not in the Land of Israel. If there is no synagogue, he assembles there ten people. {NAME} said, it would be better to certify the signatures than to assemble there ten people. What about this? Even in a Jewish store.
[Gittin 1:1.5] If he did not say: “it was written and signed before me”? Should not an Amora have asked this question? He said to him, that is what {NAME} said: If he brought a bill of divorce, gave it to her, but did not tell her: “It was written and signed before me”? The reason of {NAME} is to make her known as divorcee in front of two [witnesses].
[Gittin 1:1.6] A case came before {NAME}. He said to him, it is unnecessary. The opinion of {NAME} seems inverted. [Gittin 1:1.7] {NAME} in the name of Rav, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Two who brought a bill of divorce do not have to declare: It was written before us and signed before us. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They have to. [Gittin 1:1.8] {NAME} asked: If he wrote it in the Land of Israel, signed it outside the Land, went to deliver it to her outside the Land but did not find her outside the Land, returned and found her in the Land of Israel. [Gittin 1:1.9] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If a man and his wife held on to a bill of divorce; she says, I acquired it, but he says, you did not acquire. Does this refer to the disagreement between Rebbi and {NAME}? Since they disagreed: If creditor and borrower both hold on to the bond; the creditor says it is mine; I had lost it. The borrower says, it is mine because I paid it off. [Gittin 1:2.6] It was stated: A student who gave instructions about practice in front of his teacher has committed a deadly sin. [Gittin 1:3.1] MISHNAH: Somebody who brings a bill of divorce from the Land of Israel does not have to say: “It was written and signed before me.” If the document is contested, it should be confirmed by its signers. A protest not concerning the text of the bill is void, a protest concerning the text of the bill is valid.

[Gittin 1:5.1] MISHNAH: If one says, “give this bill of divorce to my wife or this document of manumission to my slave,” if he wants to change his mind in either case he can retract, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, only for women’s bills of divorce but not for slaves’ documents of manumission because one may bestow benefit on a person in his absence but put a detriment on him only in his presence; for if one chooses not to sustain his slave, he has the right not to do so, but not to sustain his wife he has no right. He said to them, but he disqualifies his slave for heave the same way he disqualifies his wife! They answered him, because he is his property. [Gittin 1:5.2] HALAKHAH: If one says, “give this bill of divorce to my wife,” etc. Elsewhere you say that “give” means “bring”, but here you say that “give” means “acquire”!
