[Kiddushin 2:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody performed preliminary marriage with a woman on condition that she had no obligation of vows on her and it turns out that she had vows to fulfill, she is not preliminarily married. If he married her definitively without inquiry and she had vows to fulfill, she should leave without ketubah . For all defects which disqualify a priest disqualify a woman.
[Kiddushin 2:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody performed preliminary marriage with a woman etc. We have stated defects. Which vows? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If she vowed not to eat meat, or not to drink wine, or not to wear dyed garments. {NAME} said, the fine linen garments which come from Bet She‘an have the status of dyed garments. {NAME} said, the Mishnah deals with the case that he said to her, “on condition that you have no obligation of vows on you.” But if he said to her, “on condition that you have no vow on you,” then even if she made a vow not to eat carob fruit it is a vow.
[Kiddushin 2:4.3] “If she went to an Elder and he dissolved her vow, she is preliminarily married. To a doctor and he healed her, she is not preliminarily married.” What is the difference between the Elder and the doctor? The Elder uproots the vow from its start; the doctor heals only for the future. Some Tannaïm state: Even if she went to an Elder and he dissolved her vow, she is not preliminarily married. The baraita follows {NAME}, as we have stated there: “{NAME} said, it would have been logical about a vow which has to be investigated by a Sage, because the Elder uproots the vow from its start. Why did they forbid a vow which has to be investigated by a Sage? Because of a vow which does not have to be investigated by a Sage. Some Tannaïm state: She is allowed to marry without a bill of divorce. Some Tannaïm state: She is forbidden to marry without a bill of divorce. They wanted to say that he who says, she is allowed to marry without a bill of divorce is {NAME}, and he who says, she is forbidden to marry without a bill of divorce are the rabbis. Everything follows the rabbis. He who says, she is forbidden to marry without a bill of divorce, the rabbis. He who says, she is allowed to marry without a bill of divorce: Since she knows that if she went to an Elder, he would dissolve her vow, since she does not go therefore she can be married without a bill of divorce. What is the reason of him who says, she is forbidden to marry without a bill of divorce, that she should not go to an Elder who would dissolve her vow, then the preliminary marriage would become retroactively valid for her and it would turn out that her children became bastards. Therefore she is forbidden to marry without a bill of divorce.
[Kiddushin 2:4.4] “If he married her definitively without inquiry”. {NAME} said, the Mishnah deals with the case that he married her preliminarily conditionally but definitively silently. But if he married her preliminarily silently and definitively silently, she can claim her ketubah . {NAME} said, even if he married her preliminarily silently and definitively silently, she has no ketubah . {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: But she needs a bill of divorce from him even if he married her preliminarily conditionally but definitively silently. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: In case he married her preliminarily silently and divorced her after the preliminary marriage, what does {NAME} say? Let us hear from the following: “If she had bodily defects, as long as she is in her father’s house, the father has to prove.” This implies that if he proved his case, she can claim her ketubah . What do you see to say, if he married her preliminarily silently and divorced her after the preliminary marriage! Where do we hold? Since afterwards [it is stated]: “When was this said? For hidden defects, but he has no claim about visible defects.” If he. made it conditional, could he not also claim for visible ones? But did not the colleagues say before {NAME}: Should we say that the following statement disagrees with {NAME}? “Once she entered her husband’s domain, the husband has to prove.” This implies that if the husband proved his case, she has no claim to ketubah . But by the statement of {NAME}, she has a claim to ketubah . {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah deals with the case that he definitively married her but did not sleep with her; {NAME} speaks about the case that he definitively married her and slept with her; I am saying that she was acceptable to him since he took her to bed.
[Kiddushin 2:4.5] “And all defects which disqualify a priest disqualify a woman. They added to them for women mouth odor, sweat odor, and a hairless mole.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They taught this about the skin of the face. But did we not state: “When was this said? For hidden defects, but he has no claim about visible defects.” Is this not of the visible defects? Explain it if she hid it under her headgear. It was stated: “A mole with hairs is a defect, whether it be large or small, whether it be on the body or on the face. Without a hair it is a defect on the face but not on the body. When has this been said? If it is small. But if it is large, it is a defect whether it be on the body or on the face. How big is large? {NAME} says, up to an Italic as .” {NAME} said, for example such a Gordianic denar: its measure is half a ubiquitous gold piece. {NAME}, {NAME}: {NAME} asked: A bald woman with a row of hair going from one ear to the other? They wanted to understand it from the following: “They added to them for women mouth odor, sweat odor, and a hairless mole.” They did not mention baldness. They wanted to conclude that it is not a defect. There came {NAME}: {NAME} said, it is a defect. It is listed only if it is ugly for both sexes. But something which is beautiful in one sex but ugly in the other, like a bald pate, even though it is a defect it was not listed. You should know that this is so because a beard is beautiful for a man and a defect for a woman, and we did not state: In addition, for a woman a beard. There are breasts which are beautiful for a woman and a defect for men, and we did not state: In addition, for a man women’s breasts.
[Kiddushin 2:5.1] MISHNAH: Somebody who preliminarily marries two women with the value of a peruṭah , or one woman with the value of half a peruṭah , is not preliminarily married even if afterwards he sent presents, since he sent them based on the earlier preliminary marriage. The same holds for an underage boy who contracted a preliminary marriage.
[Kiddushin 2:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody preliminarily marries two women with the value of a peruṭah ,” etc. It was stated: “In all these cases, if they had intercourse they acquired. {NAME} [ben] Jehudah says in the name of {NAME}: In all these cases, if they had intercourse they did acquire since his intercourse was predicated on the preceding preliminary marriage.” What did they acquire? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They acquired for restrictions. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: With any condition which refers to a preceding action, she is preliminarily married for restrictions. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Who is the Tanna who stated: “Any condition which refers to a preceding action is invalid”? This does not follow {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: She is preliminarily married for restrictions. How is that: “I am marrying you preliminarily by intercourse on condition that rains should fall.” If rain fell, she is preliminarily married, otherwise she is not preliminarily married. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: In matters of a preliminary marriage by a loan for restrictions, for real estate it was not acquired, for movables one does not deliver him to “Him Who exacted retribution.” If [the buyer] insists on the deal? Let us hear from the following: “You have wine to get from me, when he had no wine.” Therefore, if he had wine he would be obligated to deliver. {NAME} stated, if he has wine he is obligated to deliver. {NAME} did (not) say there: You should know that {NAME} instructed following {NAME} that a preliminary marriage by a loan is for restrictions. {NAME} resented it. Why? Because they were restrictive in practice and he taught them leniency? {NAME} said, they were lenient in practice and he taught them to be restrictive, that if another man came and married her preliminarily, his marriage would hold. {NAME} said, if there is a doubt between adultery and no adultery, decide on no adultery.
[Kiddushin 2:6.1] MISHNAH: If somebody preliminarily marries a woman and her daughter or two sisters simultaneously, they are not preliminarily married. It happened to five women, among them two sisters, that a man collected a bag of figs from their own property in the Sabbatical year and said: All of you are preliminarily married to me by this bag, and one of them accepted for all of them. Then the Sages said, the sisters are not preliminarily married.
[Kiddushin 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody preliminarily marries a woman and her daughter,” etc. {NAME} said, one understands from this five rules: One understands that five women can be preliminarily married simultaneously. That a woman may receive her own wedding gift and that of her companion. And one may use the spoils of robbery for a preliminary marriage. And one may preliminarily marry using produce acquired by a prohibited act. And preliminary marriage is impossible in incest situations.
[Kiddushin 2:6.3] {NAME} said, sisters are not preliminarily married but in the case of purification sacrifices it atoned. How is that? If one slaughtered two purification offerings for one transgression, the altar selects that which is appropriate; both are forbidden to be eaten. If one slaughtered two reparation offerings for one damage, the altar selects that which is appropriate; both are forbidden to be eaten. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If the first one was slaughtered not for its purpose but the second for its purpose, it did atone since the first, which was not for its purpose, becomes acceptable only through the purpose stated later. But if the first was slaughtered for its purpose but the second not for its purpose: if the first atoned for what may the second atone? For impurity which occured between the first and the second. But for Passover sacrifices it did not atone since the Passover sacrifice is only for the meat to be eaten. This does not follow {NAME} since {NAME} said, one fulfills one’s duty by sprinkling [the blood] without eating.
[Kiddushin 2:7.1] MISHNAH: If somebody uses his portion either from most holy or simply holy sacrifices for preliminary marriage, she is not preliminarily married. From Second Tithe there is no preliminary marriage whether unintentionally or intentionally, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, intentionally he performed preliminary marriage, unintentionally he did not perform preliminary marriage. From Temple property, intentionally he performed preliminary marriage, unintentionally he did not perform preliminary marriage, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, unintentionally he performed preliminary marriage, intentionally he did not perform preliminary marriage.
[Kiddushin 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, it is everybody’s opinion. {NAME} said, it is in dispute. There, we have stated: “One may sell a firstling unblemished alive, blemished alive or slaughtered, and one may use it for preliminarily marrying a woman.”
[Kiddushin 2:7.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Alive, but not slaughtered. And {NAME} said, {NAME} learns all sacrifices from animal tithe. Just as one may not become betrothed to a woman with animal tithe, so no sacrifices may be used to become betrothed to a woman. {NAME} learns all dedicated things from the firstling. Just as one may become betrothed to a woman with a firstling, so all sacrifices may be used to become betrothed to a woman. The opinion of {NAME} is inverted. There, he says, alive or slaughtered. But here, he says alive, but not slaughtered. There in his own name, here in the name of {NAME}. Even if you say there and here in his own name; if he becomes betrothed while it is still alive and with what is scheduled to fall to him. After slaughter, what is the reason of {NAME}? ( Num . 18:18 ): “Their meat shall be for you, like the breast of weaving.” And what is the reason of {NAME}? “ Shall be for you ”, even after slaughtering. How does {NAME} uphold “ shall be for you ”? He added another being that it should be eaten during two days and one night.
[Kiddushin 2:7.4] There, we have stated: “ Ḥallah of the am haäreẓ , food containing heave, food bought with money of the Second Tithe, and the remainders of flour sacrifices are free from demay .”
[Kiddushin 2:7.5] It was stated: “Concerning all of these, if he gave a name to their heave of the tithe or Second Tithe, what he did is done.” {NAME} said, with the exception of the remainders of flour sacrifices. {NAME} said, the rest is in dispute. {NAME} asked, what dispute? Where are we standing, if according to {NAME}, both for Second Tithe and for the remainders of flour sacrifices, he did not do anything. If according to {NAME}, what he did is done. {NAME} said, I went to Caesarea and heard {NAME} who was sitting there, stating: “If [a priest] preliminarily marries by means of his share in the holiest sacrifices or simple holy sacrifices, she is not married.” {NAME} said, that is everybody’s opinion. {NAME} said, it is in dispute. I said to him, from whom did you hear this, and he said, from {NAME}. I said, this explains the matter! {NAME}, who heard that {NAME} said, it is everybody’s opinion, he says it is in dispute. {NAME}, who did not hear that, asked which dispute? If according to {NAME}, both for tithe and for the remainders of flour sacrifices, he did not do anything; if according to {NAME}, what he did is done.
[Kiddushin 2:7.6] When {NAME} expired, {NAME} decided and said, {NAME} students shall not enter here. Symmachos squeezed by and entered. He said, “Most holy sacrifices for preliminary marriage,” how could a woman enter the Temple courtyard? He said to him, if he contracts preliminary marriage through an agent. By what does he contract preliminary marriage? {NAME} said, by its body. {NAME} said, by the goodwill created. Or we might say that they do not disagree. When {NAME} said, by its body, [he meant] by the expected goodwill from it. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One may contract preliminary marriage with a peruṭah from Second Tithe.
[Kiddushin 2:7.7] “With Second Tithe.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He did not intend to transgress the words of the Torah. {NAME} said, in one case he did not intend, in one case she did not intend. {NAME} said, the sanctified he did not intend, Second Tithe she did not intend. {NAME} said, the sanctified neither he nor she did intend; Second tithe he did intend but she did not.
[Kiddushin 2:7.8] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Intentionally desecrated Temple property becomes profane without redemption. But did we not state: “In error,” that excludes intention? That you say for the additional fifth and the sacrifice, but profaned it is. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The excluded well-being offerings become profane without redemption. But did we not state: “From the sancta,” not all sancta? That you say for the additional fifth and the sacrifice, but profaned it is.
[Kiddushin 2:7.9] There, we have stated: “An animal that is found as from Jerusalem to Migdal-Eder in every direction.” The elder {NAME} said, this was taught for their monetary value. {NAME} said to him, does one say to a person, go and commit larceny with sacrifices? But in every case they followed the majority of cases: If most are male, they are elevation offerings, if most are female, well-being offerings. But do not well-being offerings come from males and females? What does he do? He redeems them as profane and then turns them into elevation offerings. This is difficult. Can a purification offering become an elevation offering? {NAME} said, it is a stipulation by the court that all redundant animals should be brought as elevation offerings. {NAME} said to {NAME}, is that not intentional [misuse]? He said to him, since it is a stipulation by the court, it is not intentional [misuse]. {NAME} said, as you say there, it is a stipulation by the court that lost animals should be brought as elevation offerings.
[Kiddushin 2:8.1] MISHNAH: If a man performs preliminary marriage using ‘ orlah , or kilaim of a vineyard, or an ox sentenced to be stoned, or a calf whose neck was broken, or the birds of a sufferer from skin disease, the hair of a nazir , or the first-born of a she-ass, or meat cooked in milk, or profane meat slaughtered in the Temple precinct, [the woman] is not preliminarily married. If he sells any of these items and uses their proceeds for preliminary marriage, she is preliminarily married.
[Kiddushin 2:8.2] HALAKHAH: “If a man performs preliminary marriage using ‘orlah , or kilaim of a vineyard,” etc. The first-born of a she-ass, {NAME} said, may be used to preliminarily marry a woman; {NAME} said, it may not be used to preliminarily marry a woman. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The first-born of a she-ass may be used to preliminarily marry a woman by an argument de minore ad majus . Since you say that a firstling, whose prohibition cannot be lifted during its lifetime, can be used to preliminarily marry a woman, this one, whose prohibition can be lifted during its lifetime, not so much more? What is the difference between them? If somebody transgressed and redeemed it without the knowledge of its owner. {NAME} said, it is not redeemed. {NAME} said, it is redeemed. A baraita supports {NAME} and disagrees with him. A baraita supports {NAME}: If somebody steals the first-born of another person’s she-ass, he has to pay double restitution. The end disagrees with him: For even though he has no interest in it now he will later. The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: One may not use the first-born of a she-ass to preliminarily marry a woman. {NAME} explained that, after breaking of [the foal’s] neck. For {NAME} said, everybody agrees that after its neck was broken it cannot be redeemed.
[Kiddushin 2:8.3] “One may not use the first-born of a she-ass to preliminarily marry a woman, but {NAME} permits it.” That disagrees with {NAME} in two respects. If during its lifetime, it disagrees following the rabbis; if after breaking the neck, it disagrees following {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Explain it that it died. If he broke its neck, it is forbidden for usufruct, but {NAME} permits it. “Breaking the neck, breaking the neck.” Since “breaking the neck” mentioned there implies that one has to break its neck, bury it, and it is forbidden for usufruct, so “breaking of the neck” mentioned here implies that one has to break its neck, [bury it,] and it is forbidden for usufruct. Following {NAME} it is understandable. He permits during its lifetime; he needs an argument to forbid it after the breaking of the neck. Following {NAME} it is difficult. If it is forbidden during its lifetime, not so much more after breaking of its neck? There came {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of the rabbis: It is needed following the rabbis, lest you say that since the Torah combined the breaking of its neck with its redemption, and its redemption makes it profane, so also the breaking of its neck should make it profane. Do we find anything whose lifting makes profane and which is forbidden for usufruct? They objected: There is ṭevel containing the tithe of the poor which becomes totally profane by its lifting; but {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of Rebbi: A person eating produce which is ṭevel for the tithe of the poor is guilty of a deadly sin. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: So the rabbis answer {NAME}: Do we find anything that needs redemption and is permitted for usufruct? He replied to them: There is the first-born human who needs redemption and is permitted for usufruct.
[Kiddushin 2:8.4] “If he sells any of these items and uses their proceeds for preliminary marriage, he is married.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because it is not its proceeds. {NAME} said, this means that one cannot marry preliminary with [the proceeds of] robbery.
[Kiddushin 2:9.1] MISHNAH: If a man perform preliminary marriage using heaves, or tithes, or gifts to priests, or money for purification, or the ashes of purification, she is married even if he is an Israel.
[Kiddushin 2:9.2] HALAKHAH: {NAME} said, a person gives his tithes for the benefit of goodwill. What is the reason of {NAME}? ( Num . 5:10 ) “Everybody shall be the owner of his holy things.” How does {NAME} explain this? He may give them to whomever he likes.
[Kiddushin 2:9.3] A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “A vow that no Cohanim or Levites should have any advantage from me: they should take against his will.” He explains it about a person who says, I cannot possibly give them any gifts. You should know that this is so, since we have stated: “ These Cohanim and Levites should [not] have any advantage from me; let others take.” A baraita disagrees with {NAME}: “One may say, here you have a tetradrachma and give this firstling to my daughter’s son, a Cohen.” He explains, if he already wanted to give it to two Cohanim and that daughter’s son was one of them; then one said, here you have a tetradrachma and give it whole to my daughter’s son, a Cohen.
[Kiddushin 2:9.4] They asked before {NAME}: a Cohen to an Israel, Rebbi forbids. What does {NAME} say? He did not respond. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, so he said to them: In the opinion of {NAME}, why is a Cohen to an Israel forbidden, not because it looks badly? Also {NAME} holds that from an Israel to an Israel it is forbidden because it looks badly. In addition, because of the following, as it was stated: “Cohanim and Levites who help at the threshing floor have no right either to heave or to tithe, and if the farmer gave, it is desecrated, as it is said ( Lev . 22:15 ): ‘They should not desecrate the sanctified things of the Children of Israel,’ but they do desecrate them! In addition, they said that their heave is no heave, their tithes are no tithes, their dedications are no dedications, and about them the verse says ( Micha 3:11 ): ‘Their heads judge for bribes, their priests instruct for hire, etc.’ The Omnipresent brings over them three catastrophes; that is what is written ( Micha 3:12 ): ‘Therefore, because of you Zion will be ploughed over as a field, Jerusalem will be desolate, and the Temple Mount a wooded hill.’
[Kiddushin 2:9.5] A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If a man performs preliminary marriage using heaves, or tithes, or gifts to priests, or water for purification, or the ashes of purification, she is married even if he is an Israel.” He explains it with heave he inherited from his maternal grandfather, a Cohen.
[Kiddushin 3:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody said to another: go and marry me preliminarily to woman X, and [the agent] went and married her preliminarily himself, she is preliminarily married. Also, if somebody said to a woman, you are preliminarily married to me after thirty days and another man married her preliminarily within these thirty days, she is preliminarily married to the second man; as a daughter of an Israel married to a Cohen she may eat heave. From today and after thirty days, and another man married her preliminarily within these thirty days, she is and is not preliminarily married. As a daughter of an Israel married to a Cohen or daughter of a Cohen married to an Israel she may not eat heave.
[Kiddushin 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody says to another: go and marry me preliminarily to woman X,” etc. He looks out for himself and is rewarded since his acquisition is valid, but he behaved treacherously. The same holds for monetary transactions. If somebody says to another: go and buy for me goods X, and [the agent] went and bought [the merchandise] for himself, he looks out for himself and is rewarded since his acquisition is valid, but he behaved treacherously. {NAME} cursed those who saw another person trying to buy certain goods and outbid him. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Also about one who organizes a group against another, the rabbis quote: “A person who prevents a good thing coming to his neighbor abandons the fear of the Almighty.”
[Kiddushin 3:1.3] If the agent was not identified as such by the witnesses and he says, I married her preliminarily for myself, but she says, to the first, the second is like one who says to a woman: I married you preliminarily but she says, you did not marry me preliminarily. Also it is as if she said to the first, you married me preliminarily but he says, I did not marry you preliminarily. If she says, I do not know, the presumption is in favor of the second. If the agent was identified as such by the witnesses and he says, I married her preliminarily for myself, but she says, to the first, the presumption is in favor of the first. If she said, I do not know, both of them give a bill of divorce or, if they so desire, one gives a bill of divorce and the other marries definitively.
[Kiddushin 3:1.4] Therefore, if the second died within thirty days or divorced her, the preliminary marriage of the first is activated after thirty days. If he died after thirty [days] without having divorced her, the preliminary marriage of the first is not activated. That is what {NAME} stated: With any condition which was fulfilled, even if later it becomes moot, she is preliminarily married. But with any condition which was not satisfied at the moment of preliminary marriage, even if later it became moot, she is not preliminarily married.
[Kiddushin 3:1.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “This animal shall be an elevation sacrifice after thirty days.” If he sold it within the thirty days, it is sold; its dedication sanctifies. If he bought it back within the thirty days, the dedication as elevation sacrifice applies to it. After thirty days, the dedication as elevation sacrifice no longer applies. But an elevation sacrifice cannot be compared to a woman! Could an elevation sacrifice be compared to a woman? {NAME} said, explain it that the second man died but he had a brother. Since she is a candidate for levirate, the preliminary marriage of the first cannot be valid. Could an elevation sacrifice be compared to a woman? {NAME} said, explain it that he dedicated an animal with a permanent defect. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: There you say, my promise to Heaven is like my delivery to a private person, and here, you say so? He answered him: there, immediately, but here if he says, after thirty days.
[Kiddushin 3:1.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “This shall be an elevation sacrifice for thirty days,” it is an elevation sacrifice for thirty days; after thirty days it automatically becomes profane. What is its status regarding larceny? {NAME} said, the larceny is clear. {NAME}, {NAME} both say, the larceny is in doubt. “You are preliminarily married to me for thirty days,” she is preliminarily married. What is the difference between dedication and woman? We find that a dedication can be eliminated without redemption but we do not find that a woman could leave without a divorce document. Where do we find that a dedication can be eliminated without redemption? Following {NAME}, since {NAME} says, “they enter without paying.” {NAME} said, explain it according to everybody regarding a bought field. “This is your bill of divorce for thirty days”: it is no bill of divorce. {NAME} ben {NAME} said, when do you say that she is preliminarily married? If he effectuated the preliminary marriage by money. But if he effectuated the preliminary marriage by a document, since marriage documents were inferred from divorce documents and in the case of a divorce she is not divorced, so in the case of a preliminary marriage she is not preliminarily married.
[Kiddushin 3:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “This animal shall be an elevation sacrifice after thirty days;” if he sold it during the thirty days, it is not sold; its dedication does not sanctify. For which purpose did he say: “after thirty”? To reserve for himself shearing and work. “Pick from this field that it should be acquired by you after thirty days;” if he sold it within thirty days it is not sold, if he dedicated it it is not sanctified. Why did he say, after thirty days? To reserve usufruct for himself. “Here you have this tetradrachma that your field should be mine after thirty days,” if he sold it within thirty days it is not sold, if he dedicated it it is not sanctified. What is the difference between this and a woman? But if he sold it, it is sold.
[Kiddushin 3:1.8] “Here you have money that your slave shall become acquired by me after thirty days.” Some Tannaïm stated: The first [owner] is subject to “a day or two”. But some Tannaïm stated: The second [owner] is subject to “a day or two”. Some Tannaïm stated: Neither the first nor the second [owners] are subject to “a day or two”. But some Tannaïm stated: Both first and second [owners] are subject to “a day or two”. He who says, the first [owner] is subject to “a day or two”, “if he dies in his possession.” He who says, the second [owner] is subject to “a day or two”, “for he is his money.” He who says, both first and second [owners] are subject to “a day or two”, the first because of “if he dies in his possession,” the second because of “for he is his money.” He who says, neither the first nor the second [owners] are subject to “a day or two”, for he is not the first’s money and does not die in the possession of the second.
[Kiddushin 3:1.9] “As daughter of an Israel married to a Cohen she may eat heave.” Some Tannaïm state: She may not eat heave. {NAME} said, the one who says that she may eat heave refers to the case that the second man is a Cohen, but the one who says that she may not eat heave refers to the case that the second man is not a Cohen.
[Kiddushin 3:1.10] “From today and after 30 days.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even preliminary marriages of a hundred men apply to her. {NAME} said, it was necessary [to state], even if the second preliminarily married her absolutely. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: As you take it; what the first acquired, he acquired; the remainder the second finished. He answered, is this kind of argument applicable to incest prohibitions? How is that? To any woman who is not acquired by one man only, even preliminary marriages of a hundred men apply.
[Kiddushin 3:1.11] A student asked before {NAME}: If he gave it to her in the morning on condition that he divorce her in the afternoon? A certain David was of the opinion that anything acquires; {NAME} said that after thirty days he acquires absolutely. But if the second one added absolute acquisition, I am reading for her: “Her first husband who had sent her away cannot return to take her back.”
[Kiddushin 3:1.12] If both were Cohanim or brothers, both are forbidden. If there were three brothers; two of them contracted a preliminary marriage with her and then died. That is what {NAME} stated: The wife of one deceased contracts levirate marriage but not the wife of two deceased men. If they were brothers, both contracted a preliminary marriage with her and then one of them died. Is she permitted to the second? As you take it, what he had acquired, he had acquired; the rest he inherits from his brother. {NAME} said, she is forbidden to him. {NAME} said, the reason of {NAME} is that the aspect acquired in any sister-in-law who is not totally inside [the family] is considered to be under the incest prohibition and an incest prohibition frees the co-wife. {NAME} said, {NAME} said it correctly. Does she not become his because of his brother? To his brother she was forbidden; to him she should be permitted?
[Kiddushin 3:1.13] “A daughter of a Cohen married to an Israel may not eat heave.” This is a necessary statement, even in case the second man is a Cohen.
[Kiddushin 3:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody says to a woman: You are preliminarily married to me on condition that I give you 200 zuz , she is preliminarily married and he is obligated to give. On condition that I give you within the next 30 days; if he gave her within 30 days she is preliminarily married; otherwise she is not preliminarily married. On condition that I owe 200 zuz , she is preliminarily married if he has it. On condition that I show you 200 zuz , she is preliminarily married once he shows it to her; but if he showed it on his bank she is not preliminarily married.
[Kiddushin 3:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody says to a woman: You are preliminarily married to me,” etc. There, we have stated: “This is your bill of divorce on condition that you give me 200 zuz , she is divorced and has to pay. If she did not manage to pay before he died, it was stated: {NAME} says, she pays his father or his brother and is free from ḥalîṣah and levirate marriage. The same holds for preliminary marriage: “You are preliminarily married to me on condition that I give you 200 zuz ;” if he did not manage to pay before he died, {NAME} says, his father or his brothers pay and she is subject to ḥalîṣah or levirate marriage.
[Kiddushin 3:2.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The following is the contract text: “I, X son of Y, contract a preliminary marriage with you, Z, daughter of U, on condition that I give you property A and definitively marry you by day B. If that day should pass without me having taken you in, I shall have no claim on you.” If anything intervened beyond his control? {NAME} said, matters beyond his control are as if he were inactive. {NAME} said, matters outside his control are as if he had acted. In the opinion of {NAME}, what would be necessary? “If that day should pass without you having taken me in, I shall have no claim on you.” When {NAME} was dying, he told his daughters to act following {NAME}. He said, sometime in the future there might be a court which follows him; then his descendants might be in danger of bastardy.
[Kiddushin 3:2.4] If the appointed time has arrived and he says, I gave, but she says, I did not receive: {NAME} said, since he tries to wrest the contract from the woman’s hand, the burden of proof is on him. Think of it, maybe there was no contract? {NAME} said, since he tries to forbid her to anybody, he has to prove that they entered into the contract. A case came before {NAME}; he said to him, go and deliver. He answered, Rabbi, I did not acquire a wife and you say to me, go and deliver! {NAME} said, it never happened to me that one got the better of me except this one. He rephrased and said: If he changed his mind, he shall deliver. If she changed her mind, she shall deliver. Is that not his former judgment? He rephrased to give it the status of a court document.
[Kiddushin 3:2.5] The following is the way of contracting: One witness for the groom and one witness for the bride; these two together select a third in order to have two witnesses for each side. That is, if not both of them agree. But if both of them agree, both may invalidate the preliminary marriage. As, e. g., “if he said, I copulated, but she says, I was not copulated with. Even if he changed his story and then said, I did not copulate, he cannot be believed since from the start he had said, I copulated. But if from the start he said that he had not copulated, the two together can uproot the presumption.” If there was one witness for the groom, one witness for the bride, and the groom signed personally: {NAME} said, it is a symphōn , {NAME} said, it is preliminary marriage, for I am saying that he did not really intend a symphōn but thought that it would permit her sister to him.
[Kiddushin 3:2.6] Only if it be with his and her agreement. If it was symphōn in his opinion and preliminary marriage in her opinion, {NAME} said, it is symphōn , {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, it is preliminary marriage. {NAME} was taking up arms against {NAME}, when {NAME} said to him, accept Ḥaggai, for Ḥaggai is a thinking man; this is what {NAME} said. In the first Adar, {NAME} died. In the second Adar, a case came before {NAME}, the colleague of the rabbis, and he wanted to rule following {NAME}. {NAME} told him, {NAME} was wrong when he told you, accept Ḥaggai, for Ḥaggai is a thinking man. {NAME} said, a Mishnah supports him: “ ‘You married me preliminarily’, and he says, ‘I did not marry you preliminarily.’ He is permitted her relatives but she is forbidden his relatives.” {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is it the same with symphōn ? He answered, a symphōn is not doubtful but the rules are identical for symphōn and preliminary marriage.
[Kiddushin 3:2.7] If he performed a preliminary marriage during the validity of the symphōn , this is unconditional preliminary marriage. If he divorced, the students of {NAME} said, divorce touched her; {NAME} said, divorce did not touch her. When {NAME} died, his students acted following him. They said, since after 30 [days] she would leave without a bill of divorce, how can you say that divorce touched her? But divorce did not touch her. If he died during the time stipulated in the symphōn , {NAME} said, she is permitted to marry; {NAME} said, she is not permitted to marry. {NAME} asked the family of {NAME} father: How did your master usually act? He said to him, when it was a long time, he said that she should go and marry immediately. If the time was short, he said, what is the hurt if she waits? If he sent things during the validity of the symphōn , {NAME} said, [it follows the rules of] symphōn ; {NAME} said, [it follows the rules of] preliminary marriage. The rabbis take note of {NAME} opinion.
[Kiddushin 3:3.1] MISHNAH: “On condition that I possess a bet kor of arable land,” she is preliminarily married if he owns it. “On condition that I possess it at place X”, she is preliminarily married if he owns it at place X, otherwise she is not preliminarily married. “On condition that I shall show you a bet kor of arable land,” she is preliminarily married and he has to show her, but if he showed it in the valley she is not preliminarily married. {NAME} says, any condition which is not formulated in the manner of the condition imposed on the tribes of Gad and Reuben is invalid, as it is said: “Moses said to them, if the tribes of Gad and Reuben cross over … but if they will not in arms cross over with you, etc.” {NAME} said, that formulation was necessary for otherwise one would have understood that even in the Land of Canaan they should not inherit.
[Kiddushin 3:3.2] HALAKHAH: “On condition that I possess a bet kor of arable land,” etc. {NAME} asked: If somebody said, my son A should perform action X and receive property Y, and the rest of my sons shall inherit my properties; if he performs, he takes, but if he does not perform, he does not take. Or maybe it is a difference since it is written: “To give to Nine and a half tribes.” It is as if he said, my son A should perform action X and receive property Y, and the rest of my sons shall inherit my properties; if he performs, he takes, but if he does not perform, he does not take from here or from there.
[Kiddushin 3:3.3] There, we have stated: “A person can impose a condition of his ‘eruv.” So is the Mishnah: “A person can impose a condition of his ‘eruvin .” {NAME} said, who is the Tanna of “if they came”, “if they did not come”? {NAME}! Which {NAME}? The colleagues say, {NAME} . As it was stated: If somebody say to a woman: You are preliminarily married to me on condition that there will be rain. If rain fell, she is preliminarily married, otherwise she is not preliminarily married. {NAME} says, she is preliminarily married whether or not rain fell unless he doubled his condition. Everybody agrees that if he said, after rainfall, if it rained she is preliminarily married, otherwise she is not preliminarily married. {NAME} said, it follows {NAME} in Eruvin , as we have stated there: “If it be in doubt, {NAME} and {NAME} say, he is a camel-donkey driver.” {NAME} said, {NAME} said this only as a restriction. {NAME} said, that is correct. He cannot acquire his ‘ eruv since he is not able to enjoy it. [Why not] like the people of his place? If he had decided to leave his place. And here, she is not preliminarily married to the first, since no rain came. She is not preliminarily married to the second, since [the first] did not double his condition. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is this “if” not a reaction? He answered, there is a difference since the land was in their hand and he wanted to take it away from them.
[Kiddushin 3:3.4] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. They formulated the symphōn according to {NAME}. {NAME}, the colleague of the rabbis, asked: Why does it have to follow {NAME} but not also the rabbis? Did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: The following is the contract text: “I, X son of Y, contract a preliminary marriage with you, Z, daughter of U, on condition that I shall give you property A and definitively marry you by day B. If that day should pass without me having taken you in, I shall have no claim on you.” Why can he not say “on condition” but not double his stipulation? If he did not double his stipulation, could this eliminate the preliminary marriage? {NAME} said, everywhere {NAME} holds that from “no” you infer “yes”, except here? {NAME} said, one is more restrictive in matters of incest and adultery.
[Kiddushin 3:4.1] MISHNAH: If a person contracts a preliminary marriage with a woman and then says, I was of the opinion that she was a Cohenet but she is a Levite, a Levite but she is a Cohenet, poor but she is rich, rich but she is poor, she is preliminarily married since she did not trick him.
[Kiddushin 3:4.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} says, any condition,” etc. {NAME} said, she is preliminarily married as if by witnesses. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: She is preliminarily married as a restriction.
[Kiddushin 3:4.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Reuben owes to Simeon; he transferred [the debt] to Levi. Levi became poor; then Reuben owes nothing to Simeon. That is, if it was not done in bad faith, but if it was done in bad faith, he is obligated.
[Kiddushin 3:4.4] Similarly, the pedlars directed the village wax chandlers to a merchant. The merchant absconded. The case came before {NAME}, who said, if it is a matter of pennies, they were negligent. If it is a matter of denars, it is the way of merchants to move around.
[Kiddushin 3:4.5] A person met another in the market place. He said to him, give me the linen which you hold for me. The other responded, give me the denar which you hold for me. The first said, give me the linen and deduct the denar. The case came before {NAME}, who said to him, you admitted that you owe him a denar; he did not admit anything about the linen. Go and give him the denar! {NAME} said, {NAME} will agree that this is not the law but that he obligated him lest the other deny his liability for the linen.
[Kiddushin 3:4.6] A person owed another one 100 denars on a document. He sent 50 with an agent and instructed him: If he does not surrender the document, do not give him anything. The case came before {NAME}. He said, go and give it, for we know. Think of it, {NAME} [might die]! One writes for him a proclamation of the court. If one accepts for another person, the rabbis here say, what he accepted, he accepted for the claimant.
[Kiddushin 3:4.7] Explanation: {NAME} and {NAME} descended to collect there for the colleagues when they were slandered. They asked but were not given anything. Then they came and wanted to take it back from them. They answered, we already acquired it. They said, we wish for you to accept it in good faith; they answered, we are unpaid trustees. They approached {NAME} who told them, there it is, all of it. They took {NAME}, whipped him with ropes, and took it from him. When they returned here, he went to his father and told him, look what your son did to me! He asked him, what did he do to you? He answered, if he had taken my position, they could not have taken anything from us. He asked him, why did you act in such a way? He said, I saw that they were a unanimous court, their hats were a cubit wide, they were directing blows, my brother Yose was bound and the whip ascended and descended. I said, does my father have another Dositheos? {NAME} said, you say that for somebody who cannot give a warranty in good faith. But if somebody gives a warranty in good faith, one takes from this one and gives to the other. If somebody forgave a bond to another person: {NAME} and {NAME}: one said it is forgiven; the other said it is not forgiven unless he handed over the bond.
[Kiddushin 3:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody say to a woman: You are preliminarily married to me after I convert, or after you are converted, after I am freed, or after you are freed, after your husband has died, or after your sister has died, or after your levir has given you ḥalîṣah , she is not preliminarily married. Similarly, if somebody say to another, if your wife have a daughter, she shall be preliminarily married to me, he did not say anything.
[Kiddushin 3:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody say to a woman,” etc. They asked before {NAME}: What is the difference between this and one who says, “this shall be heave for this standing produce after it has been cut”? He said to them, there, it is in his power to cut; but here, it is not in his power to be freed. {NAME} asked, think of it, if she was his slave girl? {NAME} said, “after you are freed”, she is made dependent on another person’s will.
[Kiddushin 3:5.3] The elder {NAME} and {NAME} Neśia were sitting together. They said, let us say something on the subject of preliminary marriage. If somebody say to his wife, here you have a peruṭaḣ that you should be preliminarily married to me after I have divorced you, what is the rule? They laughed and got up. {NAME} said, why did they laugh? Did not {NAME} say, “after you are freed”, she is made dependent on another person’s will; and here “after you are divorced,” she is made dependent on another’s will. If you want to find a difficulty. ask the following: A person went to preliminarily marry a woman. Another person overtook him and said to her, you should know that the man who is coming to preliminarily marry you has a bad mind. In the future he will abandon you. But here you have this peruṭah that you should be preliminarily married to me after he will have divorced you. What is the rule?
[Kiddushin 3:5.4] There, it was stated: “These orchard trees shall be qorbān if they are not cut, this garment shall be qorbān if it is not burned.” And it was burned. Were they sanctified retroactively? He committed larceny. If you say that it refers to the future, he did not commit larceny.
[Kiddushin 3:5.5] {NAME} said, if he redeemed them they revert to their sanctity. {NAME} said, if he redeemed them they are redeemed. The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “These have no redemption.” He explains thus: After they were cut they do not need redemption. {NAME} said, what {NAME} said refers to the case that he himself redeemed them. But if another person redeemed them, the sanctity is removed from them. The argument of {NAME} is switched: There, he says that if [another] redeemed them, the sanctity is removed from them, but here, he says that if she was married to another man the qiddušin [of the first] were not removed! All that is questionable for him is if he gave her two peruṭot , one for the moment and one for after he divorced her; what is the situation?
[Kiddushin 3:5.6] {NAME} said: More than 30 Elders voted: from where that qiddushin have no legal effect on a sister-in-law? The verse says, “the wife of the deceased may not belong to any outside unrelated man”, that she cannot have any existence with an outsider. {NAME} said to him, is that not a Mishnah? “Or after your levir will have performed ḥalîṣah with you, she is not preliminarily married.” And {NAME} praised him “those who pour out gold from the wallet,” “my son, they should not be removed from your eyes,” “get wise, my son, and make me happy, that I can answer those who insult me”, “give to the wise that he shall become wiser,” “let the wise listen that he increase in knowledge.” {NAME} said, after all these praises I can explain it following {NAME} since {NAME} said that there exists a bastard from a sister-in-law!
[Kiddushin 3:5.7] {NAME} said, in our poverty, she needs a bill of divorce from him. {NAME} said, the Mishnah [said], “after your levir has given you ḥalîṣah ”; but if he said, “after your levir has died,” she is preliminarily married. {NAME} stated: A one-day-old girl can be preliminarily married by money; a girl of three years and one day can be preliminarily married by intercourse.” {NAME} said, the Mishnah implies this: “Similarly, if somebody say to another, if your wife have a daughter, she shall be preliminarily married to me, he did not say anything,” because she does not exist. Therefore, if she does exist, she is preliminarily married.
[Kiddushin 3:6.1] MISHNAH: If somebody says to a woman, be preliminarily married to me on condition that I speak for you to the government, or work for you as a worker, she is preliminarily married if he did speak for her to the government or did work for her as a worker; otherwise she is not preliminarily married. On condition that my father agree; if the father agreed, she is preliminarily married, otherwise she is not preliminarily married. If the father died, she is preliminarily married; if the son died, one instructs the father to say that he does not agree.
[Kiddushin 3:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody says to a woman, be preliminarily married to me,” etc. Rav said, we deal with the case that he gave her a peruṭah ’s worth. {NAME} asked (before Rebbi): Do we not always deal with the case that he gave her a peruṭah ’s worth? But so it is: “By what I shall speak for you to the government; if he did speak for her to the government for a peruṭah ’s worth she is preliminarily married, otherwise she is not preliminarily married.” “By what I shall work for you as a worker; if he did work for her as a worker for a peruṭah ’s worth, she is preliminarily married, otherwise she is not preliminarily married.” {NAME} in the name of Rav: Only if she set aside a tetradrachma in her chest for him. With what did he effectuate the preliminary marriage? As we have stated there: “If anything is bartered instead of money, if one party entered in possession, the other is obligated for its trade-in.”
[Kiddushin 3:6.3] “On condition that my father agree; if the father agreed, she is preliminarily married; if the father does not agree, she is not preliminarily married;” silently he does not agree. “If the father died, she is preliminarily married;” silently he agreed. “If the son died, one instructs the father to say that he does not agree;” silently he agreed. {NAME} asked {NAME}, can the Mishnah say so? He answered him, do you ask wretched Yannai to explain Qiddušin ? {NAME} returned and explained the Mishnah: “On condition that my father agree; if the father agreed, she is preliminarily married; otherwise she is not preliminarily married,” he said on condition that [the father] express his opinion but he did not. “If the father died, she is preliminarily married;” as if he had given his opinion. “If the son died, one instructs the father to say that he does not agree;” as if he had given his opinion. {NAME} said [before {NAME}]: Can {NAME} explain the Mishnah as he wishes? He answered him, so says {NAME}, Rebbi does not refrain from stating generality and detail simultaneously. {NAME} said, the Mishnah states thus: “On condition that I have a bet kor of arable land”, a generality; “at place X”, a detail.
[Kiddushin 3:7.1] MISHNAH: “I preliminarily married off my daughter but I do not know to whom I married her preliminarily,” and somebody comes and says, I married her preliminarily, he is believed. This one says, “I married her preliminarily,” and that one says, “I married her preliminarily,” both give a bill of divorce or, if they so wish, one gives a bill of divorce and the other marries her definitively.
[Kiddushin 3:7.2] HALAKHAH: “If one says, I preliminarily married off my daughter”, etc. About what is he trustworthy? {NAME} says, he is trusted to give a bill of divorce. {NAME} said, he is trusted to marry. {NAME} said in the name of Rav: He is trusted to marry. {NAME} said, he is trusted to marry but one does not infer anything for another case from this ruling. What means, one does not infer anything for another case from this ruling? I sold one of my fields but I do not remember to whom I sold it. If someone comes and says, I bought it, he is not trusted in any way. In preliminary marriage, the same holds true. “I betrothed one of my daughters but I do not remember to whom I betrothed her. If someone comes and says, I married her preliminarily,” he is not trusted in any way. The Mishnah disagrees with Rav: “If somebody brings a bill of divorce from overseas and says, it was written and signed in my presence, he shall not marry that woman.” There, she is considered by everybody to be a married woman. Here, she is considered to be a married woman only by two persons. One waits until these two come and say, this is the man who gave her qiddushin . The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “This one says, I married her preliminarily, and that one says, I married her preliminarily. Both of them give a bill of divorce, but if they agree, one gives a bill of divorce and the other one marries.” He explains this, if [the father] says, I did betrothe her to one of these two but I do not remember which one it was. {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of {NAME}: If one of them jumped the gun and married her, one does remove her from him. That is, if this one says, I married her preliminarily, and that one says, I married her preliminarily, and one of them jumped the gun and married her definitively. But if he said, I married her preliminarily and then married her definitively, and another one comes and says, I married her preliminarily, he is not trusted in any way. It was stated thus: If after the marriage another man comes and says, I married her preliminarily, he is not trusted in any way.
[Kiddushin 3:8.1] MISHNAH: “I preliminarily married off my daughter, married her preliminarily and received her bill of divorce while she was underage,” and [now] she still is underage, he is believed. “I preliminarily married off my daughter, married her preliminarily and received her bill of divorce while she was underage,” and [now] she is an adult, he is not believed. “She had been kidnapped and I ransomed her,” he is not believed whether she is underage or adult. If somebody said when dying, I have children, he is believed; I have brothers, he is not believed. If somebody preliminarily marries off his daughter without mentioning her name, the adult ones are not included.
[Kiddushin 3:8.2] HALAKHAH: “I preliminarily married off my younger daughter,” etc. “I preliminarily married off my daughter.” The underaged are included, the adults are excluded. “My daughter was preliminarily married,” even the underaged are not included. “I accepted my daughter’s bill of divorce,” the underaged are included, the adults are excluded. “My daughter was divorced,” even the underaged are not included. “I preliminarily married off my daughter to one of those disqualified for her,” he is believed. “I made her sleep with one of those disqualified for her,” he is not believed. “She had been kidnapped and I ransomed her,” whether she is underage or adult or had intercourse with one of those disqualified for her, he is not believed.
[Kiddushin 3:8.3] So is the Mishnah: “If somebody said when dying, I have children, he is believed; I have brothers, he is not believed;” Rav said, since it is in his hand to divorce, he is to be believed. The word of {NAME} agrees with this. A Persian when dying said to them: Give this man’s wife a bill of divorce. They asked him, why? Because of your wretched brother? After he died, the case came before {NAME} who said, since it was in his hand to divorce, he is to be believed. {NAME} said, he is not to be believed. {NAME} descended there and said this in the name of {NAME}; they ganged up on him. Think of it, if he was a Cohen?
[Kiddushin 3:8.4] {NAME} objected: Does not the Mishnah disagree? “You married me preliminarily but he says, I did not marry you preliminarily; he is permitted her relatives but she is forbidden his relatives.” They said, so did it happen: {NAME} brought a bill of divorce and delivered it in front of one witness. The case came before {NAME}, who said, a single witness in marital matters is nothing. Did not {NAME} in the name of {NAME} say: a single witness in marital matters is nothing? Rav said, one who performs a preliminary marriage in front of a single witness did not do anything. {NAME} said, he who performs a preliminary marriage without prior negotiation is whipped, but the preliminary marriage holds. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said three things: He who performs a preliminary marriage without prior negotiation is whipped; one who sleeps with his betrothed in his father-in-law’s house is whipped; one who insults the court bailiff is whipped.
[Kiddushin 3:9.1] MISHNAH: If somebody has two groups of daughters from two wives and he says, I preliminarily married off my older daughter, but he does not know whether the oldest of the older ones, or the oldest of the younger ones, or the youngest of the older ones who is older than the oldest of the younger ones, all are forbidden except the youngest of the younger ones, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, all are permitted except the oldest of the older ones. I preliminarily married off my younger daughter, but he does not know whether the youngest of the younger ones, or the youngest of the older ones, or the oldest of the younger ones who is younger than the youngest of the older ones, all are forbidden except the oldest of the older ones, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, all are permitted except the youngest of the younger ones.
[Kiddushin 3:9.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody has two groups of daughters,” etc. {NAME} said, two of two. {NAME} said, for example I, who have two of two. The Mishnah [speaks of] him who has two groups of daughters from two wives, but if he has only one group and he said, the older, he married off only the oldest; if he said, the younger, he married off only the youngest.
[Kiddushin 3:9.3] There, we have stated: “ ‘Until before Passover’, {NAME} says, until it comes, {NAME} says, until it passed.” {NAME} asked before {NAME}: The opinion of {NAME} seems inverted; the opinion of {NAME} seems to be inverted. The opinion of {NAME} seems inverted: There, he says “until all the elder possibilities are exhausted, until all the younger possibilities are exhausted,” and here, he says so? He said to him: {NAME} and {NAME} died, the perseverers disappeared; no perseverer was there until Jeremiah appeared. {NAME}, said, why does he needle him? Did not great mountains find this difficult, did not {NAME} already ask before {NAME}, does not the opinion of {NAME} seem to be inverted? He said to him, it is not inverted, the Mishnah is inverted, for in the House of Rebbi they stated: “ ‘Until before Passover’, {NAME} says, until it passed, {NAME} says, until it comes.” He said: We ask “until before”, and you say so? He said to him, this is a Nabatean expression, “much before Passover”. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that he is permitted on Passover. Where do they disagree? The day before Passover. One of them says, until it passed, the other until it comes.
[Kiddushin 3:10.1] MISHNAH: If somebody says to a woman, I married you preliminarily, but she says, you did not marry me preliminarily, he is forbidden her relatives but she is permitted his relatives. I she says, you married me preliminarily but he says, I did not marry you preliminarily, she is forbidden his relatives but he is permitted her relatives. “I am preliminarily married to you,” but she says, you are only preliminarily married to my daughter; he is forbidden the relatives of the old woman, and the old woman is permitted his relatives; he is permitted the relatives of the young woman, and the young woman is permitted his relatives.
[Kiddushin 3:10.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody says to a woman,” etc. {NAME} said, it is reasonable that {NAME} not disagree in this case. {NAME} said, the entire series implies that he disagrees. Since there, where they are all older and younger, you say that {NAME} disagrees, so here, where all are old compared to young or young compared to old, he certainly disagrees.
[Kiddushin 3:11.1] MISHNAH: “I am preliminarily married to your daughter,” but she says, you are only preliminarily married to me; he is forbidden the relatives of the young woman, and the young woman is permitted his relatives; he is permitted the relatives of the old woman, and the old woman is forbidden his relatives.
[Kiddushin 3:11.2] HALAKHAH: “I am preliminarily married to your daughter,” etc. {NAME} said, one induces him to give a bill of divorce, and one forces him to pay a fine. Think of it, if he was a Fellow and knew that he would be obligated for a bill of divorce and a fine; if he went and married her sister, would one force the divorce of the certain because of the doubtful?
[Kiddushin 3:12.1] MISHNAH: In any case of a not sinful preliminary marriage, the child follows the father. Who is this? A priestly, or Levitic, or Israel woman married to a Cohen, a Levite, or an Israel. And in any case of a sinful preliminary marriage, the child follows the blemished part. Who is this? A widow [married to] a High priest, a divorcee or one who has received ḥalîṣah to a common priest, a bastard or a Gibeonite to an Israel, the daughter of an Israel to a Gibeonite or a bastard. In any case where a preliminary marriage with him is impossible but with others is possible, the child is a bastard. Who is this? This is one having sexual relations with any woman forbidden in the Torah because of incest or adultery. And in any case where a preliminary marriage is impossible with anybody, the child follows the mother. Who is this? The child of a slave girl or a Gentile woman.
[Kiddushin 3:12.2] HALAKHAH: “In any case of a not sinful preliminary marriage,” etc. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If a proselyte married a bastard girl, there is no sinful preliminary marriage, but the child follows the blemished part? He answered, everywhere Rebbi taught, he explained: “Who is this? A priestly, or Levitic, or Israel woman married to a Cohen, a Levite, or an Israel.” {NAME} understood this from the second part: (In any case of a not sinful preliminary marriage, the child follows the father.) [In any case of a sinful preliminary marriage, the child follows the blemished part.] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If a proselyte married a bastard girl, there is no sinful preliminary marriage, but the child follows the blemished part? He answered, everywhere Rebbi taught, he explained: “Who is this? A widow [married to] a High priest, a divorcee or one who has received ḥalîṣah to a common priest, a bastard or a Gibeonite to an Israel, the daughter of an Israel to a bastard or a Gibeonite.” Could he not have objected to him: In the case of a disqualified priest married to the daughter of an Israel there is no sinful marriage but the child follows the blemished part? In the case of a man taking back his divorcee after she had been remarried, there is (no) sinful marriage but the child is unblemished since {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: The daughter of a man taking back his divorcee after she had been remarried is enabled for the priesthood. What is the reason? [For she is an abomination,] she is an abomination but her children are not an abomination.
[Kiddushin 3:12.3] {NAME} in the name of Rav: A proselyte, a freedman, and a disqualified priest are permitted priestly wives. What is the reason? Qualified men are warned against disqualified women and disqualified women against qualified men but not qualified women against disqualified men nor disqualified men against qualified women. Did we not state: “they should not take, should not take”, which teaches that the woman is warned through the man? They wanted to say, qualified women against disqualified men but it is only disqualified women against qualified men.
[Kiddushin 3:12.4] A proselyte came to {NAME} and asked him, is it permitted to marry a bastard girl? He answered him, it is permitted. He continued and came to {NAME}, who answered him, it is permitted but you should know that the children of such a man would be bastards before Heaven. He returned to {NAME} and told him, since you knew that, why did you permit it to me at the start? He replied, I answered you what you asked me. {NAME} said, the proselyte can be compared to cotton. If one wants to use it with wool it is permitted, with linen it is permitted.
[Kiddushin 3:12.5] One understands “the daughter of an Israel to a bastard or a Gibeonite,” for it is written: “A bastard shall not come into the Eternal’s congregation.” Why does the verse say: “ of his shall not come”? To disqualify. {NAME} said, what means ממזר? “A strange defect.” This disagrees with what {NAME} said, “God installs singles as heads of families,” even if there is a male bastard at one end of the world and a female bastard at the other, the Holy One, praise to Him, brings them and copulates them with one another. {NAME} said, a bastard does not live more than thirty days. In the days of {NAME}, a Babylonian immigrated here; he was informed that this was a bastard. He said to him, support me. He told him, tomorrow you will stand up in the community and I shall look for an allowance for you. He came and sat during the sermon. When he finished the sermon, he said, our brothers, support this man for he is a bastard. After the congegration had left, he said to him, rabbi, I requested material support from you but you destroyed this man’s life. He answered, by your life, life I gave you for {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of Rav: A bastard lives only thirty days. When? If he is not publicly known. But when he is publicly known, he survives.
[Kiddushin 3:12.6] When {NAME} immigrated here, he heard voices call “he-bastard, she-bastard”. He said, what is this? There goes that of {NAME}, since {NAME} said, no bastard lives more than thirty days. {NAME} said to him, I was with you when {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of Rav: No bastard lives more than thirty days, when? If he is not publicly known. Therefore, if he is publicly known, he lives.

[Kiddushin 4:1.3] “Desecrated priest.” Following “from the sons of Cohanim, the family Ḥavaya, the family Haqqoṣ . . . they tried to find their genealogical documents; but they were not found and they were freed from priesthood. One understands there, as it is written: “Put up signposts for yourself.” What can one say here? Following him who said, they accepted tithes voluntarily. “Until a priest will be appointed for urim and tummim .” But were there any urim and tummim then, in the Second Temple? But [he is] like a person who says until the dead will be resurrected, until David’s son will come.

[Kiddushin 4:1.5] Any person who converts because of love, i. e., a man because of a woman or a woman because of a man, or proselytes of the king’s table, or lion proselytes, or the proselytes of Mordechai and Esther, one does not accept. [Kiddushin 4:1.6] “Proselytes,” meaning “everyone who separated himself from the impurities of the peoples of the earth to join them.” Freedmen, as in “and all the Gibeonites, etc.” Bastards. {NAME} said, it is written: “And the following came up from Salt Hill, Ploughing Hill”. Ploughing Hill.
[Kiddushin 4:1.7] [“The dedicated ones”]. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, because of: “At that moment Joshua dedicated them as hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation.” One understands “for the congregation.” But “for the Eternal’s altar”? But Joshua kept them in limbo. He said, I shall not include nor exclude them. But he who sometime in the future will build the Temple, if he wants to include them he may include, exclude them he may exclude. David came and excluded them as it is said: “But the Gibeonites are not part of the Children of Israel.” Why did he exclude them? Because “ there was a famine in David’s time, three years year after year.” David said, for four sins the rains are locked away. For the sins of foreign worship, incest and adultery, murder, and the sins of those who publicly promise money for welfare but do not pay. From where for the sin of foreign worship? “ Beware, lest you be seduced” etc. What is written afterwards? “The Eternal’s rage will be inflamed against you and he locks the sky, etc.” From where for the sins of the incestuous and adulterers? “ You distorted the Land by your immorality and your evil deeds.” What is the punishment? “Rainshowers were withheld, there was no late rain,” etc. From where because of the murderers? “ Because blood will distort the Land.” From where for the sins of those who publicly promise money for welfare but do not pay? “ Clouds and wind but no rain means the man who prides himself by lying gifts.” David checked his entire generation and did not find one of these. He turned to ask the urim and tummim . That is what is written: “ David asked before the Eternal” by urim and tummim . {NAME} said, “Ask the Eternal, all the meek of the Land, who execute His Law.” What means “Whose Law is Work”? He enforces His Law and this is His Action. “ The Eternal said, because of Saul and the House of blood guilt.” “Because of Saul,” whom you did not grant the last favor, “and because of the House of blood guilt, for he had killed the Gibeonites.” David sent and called them, what is between you and {NAME}? They told him, because he killed seven of our men, two hewers of wood, two drawers of water, a religious leader, a scribe, and a beadle. He asked them, what do you want now? They said to him: “ May there be given to us seven men of his sons and we shall hang them before the Eternal on the hill of Saul, the elected of the Eternal.” He said to them, what use is it for you that they be killed? Take silver and gold for yourselves! But they answered, “there is no money for us from Saul and his house.” He said, maybe they are afraid; he separated them and spoke to each one separately, trying to mollify him by himself, and asked him: What use is it for you that they be killed? Take gold and silver! But he said, “there is no money for us from Saul and his house.” It is written “for me”. At this moment, David said that the Holy One gave three good gifts to Israel: They are merciful, decent, and charitable. From where that they are merciful? “He gave you mercy.” From where that they are decent? “That His fear should be on your faces.” This is a sign, for a decent person does not sin. About anybody indecent it is clear that his ancestors did not stand on Mount Sinai. From where that they are charitable? “The Eternal, your God, kept for you covenant and charity.” But these, nothing of this in found in them. Immediately he went to exclude them as it is said: “But the Gibeonites are not of the Children of Israel.” And Ezra also excluded them, as it is said: “And the dedicated ones dwelt in the Ophel.” Also in the future the Holy One, praise to Him, will exclude them as it is written: “One crossing the city they cause to be lost.”
[Kiddushin 4:1.8] It is written: “The King said, I shall give.” “The King took the two sons of Riṣpah bat Ayah whom she had born to Saul, Admoni and Mephiboshet,” etc. “Michal, Saul’s daughter, did not have a child until the day of her death,” and you say so? Say now that they were sons of Merab but Michal raised them, so they were named after her. “He gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites who hanged them on the mountain before the Eternal; all seven fell together.” Defective without י. The passers-by were saying: How did these people sin that the rules of justice were changed for them? They were answered: Because these had attacked attached proselytes. They would say that even for those who did not convert for the sake of Heaven, the Eternal avenged their blood; if one would convert for the sake of Heaven not so much more? There is no Power like your God and no people like your people. Many converts were converted at that time; that is what is written: “Solomon counted all proselytes and appointed from them 70’000 carriers and 80’000 hewers of stone in the mountains.”

[Kiddushin 4:4.1] MISHNAH: One who comes to marry a woman from a priestly family has to check four mothers who are eight: Her mother, and her maternal grandmother, her mother’s paternal grandmother and great-grandmother. But for a levitic or Israel woman one adds another generation.
[Kiddushin 4:4.2] HALAKHAH: “One who comes to marry a woman from a priestly family,” etc. {NAME} said, this is {NAME}, as we have stated: “What is qualified dough? Anyone about whom there is [no suspicion of descent from] a desecrated one, a bastard, or a Gibeonite. {NAME} says, the daughter of any woman not tainted with any of these is qualified for the priesthood. But about a family in which a disability had disappeared, {NAME} says he checks up to four mothers and marries, but the Sages say, he checks forever.” Rav said, these are the words of {NAME}, but the Sages say, he checks from which family one marries into the priesthood and marries. Through whom does he check? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He checks through his female relatives. To {NAME} came an old man; he asked him: Does one marry into the priesthood from this family? He answered: yes, and he was making a match based on this information. Rav said to his son Ḥiyya: Descend a degree to marry a wife. {NAME} said, the following is a frequent saying of the rabbis: “If the woman was not impure but she is pure.” If she was not impure, she is pure. Not like {NAME} who locks the door before his wife. One said to him, did your forefathers act like this? A Cohen came to {NAME} and said to him: I acted on the Mishnah when I married a woman from a priestly family and checked after her four mothers which are eight. He said to him, if the origin was defective, who would inform you?
[Kiddushin 4:4.3] “But for Levites or Israel one adds another generation.” Does it not turn out that one is more stringent for an Israel than for a Cohen? {NAME} said, in both cases the Sages demanded a fine so that everybody should cling to his tribe and family.
[Kiddushin 4:5.1] MISHNAH: One does not investigate from the altar and before, or from the podium and before. [Kiddushin 4:5.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not investigate from the altar and before,” etc. It is written: “You certainly shall put a king over you.” This refers not only to a king; from where to add public officials, administrators of welfare, clerks of the court, and those who whip with a lash; from where? The verse says, “from amidst your brothers you shall appoint a king over you,” anybody whom you appoint over you shall only be from the select among your brethren. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “Their distinguished lineage in the army in war.” The merit of their lineage supports them in war. So far from tradition; from the words of the Torah? “No bastard shall come into the Eternal’s congregation.” “No person injured in his testicles shall come, etc.” What is written afterwards? “When you encamp against your enemies, etc.”
[Kiddushin 4:6.1] MISHNAH: The daughter of a male desecrated priest is always disqualified for the priesthood. The daughter of an Israel who married a desecrated woman is qualified for the priesthood. [Kiddushin 4:6.2] HALAKHAH: “The daughter of a desecrated priest,” etc. {NAME} in the name of Rav: Daughter, daughter’s daughter, forever. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “In his clans.” Since by “in his clans” said there males are forbidden and females permitted, so by “in his clans” said here males are forbidden and females permitted. What is the difference between them? A Cohen who came to a divorcee and fathered a son; the son went and fathered a son and a daughter. The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “{NAME} says, the daughter of a male proselyte is like the daughter of a desecrated priest.” He explains that {NAME} only comes to add. If he had said that the daughter of a desecrated priest is like the daughter of a male proselyte, you would have had a point.

[Kiddushin 4:6.5] “{NAME} says,” etc. There, we have stated: “{NAME} says, the daughter of proselytes should not marry into the priesthood unless her mother be from Israel” They all interpret the same verse ( Ez . 44:22 ): “Only virgins from the seed of the House of Israel.” {NAME} says, unless his father be from Israel. {NAME} says, either her father or her mother. {NAME} says, unless they are born in the holiness of Israel. {NAME} says, unless they grow the hymen in the holiness of Israel. You shall let live as slaves and slave girls for yourselves.
[Kiddushin 4:6.6] {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}; {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of Rav: Practice follows {NAME}, but Cohanim are used to follow {NAME}. [Kiddushin 4:6.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: It happened that a family in the South had a bad reputation. Rebbi sent Romanus to investigate them. Analogously, ( Lev . 21:14 ) “only a virgin from amidst his people he shall take as wife,” not a proselyte. Is any prohibition deduced from a positive commandment a positive commandment? {NAME} objected: But the second generation of an Egyptian is a prohibition deduced from a positive commandment! {NAME} turned around and said, a positive commandment for Israel cannot be compared to a positive commandment for Cohanim. A positive commandment for Israel implies a prohibition for everybody. A positive commandment for Cohanim implies a prohibition for Cohanim but a permission for Levites and Israel.
[Kiddushin 4:7.1] MISHNAH: If somebody says, this my son is a bastard, he cannot be believed. Even if both of them say about the fetus in her belly that he is a bastard, they cannot be believed. {NAME} says, they are believed.

That he was not his son but at the moment of his death he said that he was his son, he is believed. [Kiddushin 4:8.1] MISHNAH: If somebody empowered his agent to contract preliminary marriage for his daughter and then went himself and contracted for her, ifhe was first, his preliminary marriage is valid, but if his agent was first, that preliminary marriage is valid. Similarly, if a woman empowered her agent to contract preliminary marriage for her and then went and contracted for herself, if she was first, her preliminary marriage is valid, but if her agent’s was first, that preliminary marriage is valid. If precedence cannot be established, both give a bill of divorce or, if they agree, one gives a bill of divorce and one marries definitively.

[Kiddushin 4:9.1] MISHNAH: If somebody left for overseas together with his wife; he returns with his wife and her children and says, “the wife with whom I left for overseas is this one and those are her children,” he does not have to bring proof either about the wife or the children. “She died and those are her children,” he has to bring proof about the children but not about the wife.

[Kiddushin 4:10.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody empowered his agent,” etc. It was stated: “If a man and a woman come from overseas; he says, she is my wife, and she says, he is my husband.
