He answered, it is my fault, they said the following: “We testify against X that he killed ox Y” and the other says, I do not know, he is liable. [He said, that was stated.]
[Bava Kamma 8:7.1] MISHNAH: Even though he did pay, he will not be forgiven unless he asks for forgiveness, as it is said: “Now return the man’s wife since he is a prophet.” From where that the person asked to forgive shall not be cruel? It is said: “Abraham prayed to the Omnipotent, etc.”
[Bava Kamma 8:7.2] HALAKHAH: “Even though he did pay,” etc. [And so you find with Job’s friends. “Now yourselves take seven bulls and seven rams, etc.” “Eliphas the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Ṣophar the Naamite went and did, etc.” What does it say at the end? “The Eternal changed Job’s fortunes.” When? “When he was praying for his neighbor, etc.” “The Eternal doubled everything that Job had had.”]
[Bava Kamma 8:7.3] It was stated: {NAME} says in the name of {NAME}. Since it says that “He will give you mercy etc.”, let the following be a sign in your hand: Whenever that you show mercy, the Omnipresent will have mercy on you. If you do not show mercy, the Omnipresent will not have mercy on you. Rav said: If a person misbehaved towards another and asked for pardon but the other did not respond, let him assemble a row of people and ask for pardon, as it is written: “Form a row of men, etc.” If he does so, what is written there? “He redeemed his soul from the pit, not to go to destruction etc.” {NAME} said, that is if he did not defame, but the defamer is never pardoned.
[Bava Kamma 8:8.1] MISHNAH: If one says: Blind my eye, cut off my hand, break my leg, he is liable. On condition not to be liable, he is liable. Tear my garment, break my pitcher, he is liable. On condition not to be liable, he is not liable. Do that to another person, on condition not to be liable, he is liable whether about his person or his money.
[Bava Kamma 8:8.2] HALAKHAH: “If one say: Blind my eye, cut off my hand,” etc. “If he says, blind my eye because it damages me, cut off my hand because it damages me, he is liable. On condition not to be liable, he is liable.” {NAME} said, the Mishnah deals with a “yes” which really means “no”. But for a “yes” which does mean “yes” he is not liable. The statement of {NAME} is about the family’s loss of standing. {NAME} said, the Mishnah deals with a “yes” which means “yes”. But for a “yes” which means “no”, he is liable. The statement of {NAME} imples that one estimates the relatives’ loss of standing. It was stated: “If Gentiles forced a Jew and took from him another person’s money in his presence, he is not liable. If he handed it over, he is liable.” {NAME} said, that means if they simply demanded “money”. But “X’s money”, he is not liable even if he handed it over.
[Bava Kamma 9:1.1] MISHNAH: One who robbed wood and turned it into utensils, wool and turned it into garments, pays their value at the time of the robbery. If he robbed a pregnant cow and it calved, a sheep in its wool and he shore it, he pays the price of a pregnant cow ready to calve, or a sheep in its wool ready to be shorn. If he robbed a cow which became pregnant in his possession and it calved, or a sheep which grew wool with him and he shore it, he pays their value at the time of the robbery. This is the principle: All robbers pay for value at the time of the robbery.
[Bava Kamma 9:1.2] HALAKHAH: “One who robbed wood and turned it into utensils,” etc. Here, you say that bleaching is a change, and there you say that bleaching is not a change. If you say that bleaching is a change, if he made it into wool flakes. If you say that bleaching is not a change, if he left it unchanged. We find bleaching without flakes. Are there flakes without bleaching? {NAME} said, it is a leniency instituted for the robber that he pay their value at the time of the robbery. If somebody robbed raw hide and cleaned it, can you say that he turned it into flakes? Again it is a leniency instituted for the robber that he pay the value at the time of the robbery.
[Bava Kamma 9:1.3] “One who robbed a beam and built it into a large building. The House of Shammai say, he has to tear down the entire building and return it. But the House of Hillel say, he has to pay its worth to support the penitents. If he went into another person’s ruined building and rebuilt it without permission, one estimates for him and his hand is disadvantaged. If he rebuilt it with permission, one estimates for him and his hand is advantaged. If he wanted to take his wood and stones, one does not listen to him.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because of the settlement in the Land of Israel. {NAME} asked: If somebody temporarily entered another person’s ruin to put down his bundle, when he wanted to take it up again does one not listen to him? When he heard what {NAME} had said, because of the settlement in the Land of Israel, he said: That is a statement. But if he built at a place unfit for building, or planted trees at a place unfit for planting, Rav said one estimates for him but one tricks him to permit entry both in summer and in winter. One said to him: Was that not already stated: “One estimates for him and his hand is disadvantaged?”
[Bava Kamma 9:1.4] {NAME} said, this implies that if he robbed a fattened animal and it became thin, he has to replace the fat. {NAME} said, this implies that if he robbed a thin animal and fattened it, he has to return it as is.
[Bava Kamma 9:1.5] Because it became pregnant at his place and calved he pays its value at the time of the robbery. Who stated this? {NAME}, as it was stated: “This is the principle about which {NAME} said: About any robbed object which exists as before and was not changed from the state in which it was created, he tells him: Here is your property before you. And the thief always pays the value at the time of theft.”
[Bava Kamma 9:2.1] MISHNAH: If he robbed an animal and it aged, slaves and they aged, he has to pay their value at the time of the robbery. {NAME} says, he may say about slaves: Here is your property before you.
[Bava Kamma 9:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If he robbed an animal and it aged,” etc. {NAME} said, if he robbed a calf and it became a bull; but if he robbed a bull and it aged, he tells him: Here is your property before you. {NAME} said, even if he robbed a calf and it became a bull, he tells him: Here is your property before you. {NAME} stated: Even if he robbed a calf and it became a bull before he slaughtered or sold it, he pays quadruple or quintuple the value of a calf. {NAME} {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}.
[Bava Kamma 9:3.1] MISHNAH: If he robbed a coin and it was split, fruits and they rotted, wine and it spoiled, he pays their value at the time of the robbery. A coin and it was declared invalid, heave and it became impure, leavened matter and Passover passed, an animal which was used for sin, or which became disqualified from the altar, or which was taken out to be stoned, he tells him: Here is your property before you.
[Bava Kamma 9:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If he robbed a coin and it was split,” etc. {NAME} said, if the government invalidated it. {NAME} said, if really it was split. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Only if they rotted because of maggots but if they rotted because of worms they are like healthy ones. {NAME} said, if the government invalidated it, but if the country invalidated it, he may say to him: Here is your property before you. {NAME} said, even if the government invalidated it, he may say to him: Here is your property before you.
[Bava Kamma 9:3.3] {NAME} did not go to the house of assembly. He met {NAME} and asked him, what was new for you in the house of study today? He told him, such and such a subject. He replied, is that not a Mishnah, “heave and it became impure”? He replied, explain it if it became impure by itself and you cannot infer anything.
[Bava Kamma 9:3.4] Ḥilfai said, if he swore to him before Passover, then after Passover he pays him for fully useable leavened matter. {NAME} said, I went to Caesarea and asked {NAME}, who quoted this in the name of {NAME}, is there anybody who disagrees with Ḥilfai so that he would not have to pay for fully useable leavened matter? Everybody agrees about leavened matter that he has to pay for fully useable leavened matter.
[Bava Kamma 9:4.1] MISHNAH: If one gave something to artisans to repair and they broke it, they are liable. If one gave a chest, a box, or a cupboard to a woodworker to repair and he broke it, he is liable. And the builder who contracted to take down a wall is liable to pay if he ruined the stones or caused damage. If he was taking it down on one side when if collapsed on the other side he is not liable, but when it happened because of the pounding he is liable.
[Bava Kamma 9:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If one gave something to artisans to repair and they broke it,” etc. {NAME} said, only if he put in the last nail to acquire the rights to his utensils.
[Bava Kamma 9:5.1] MISHNAH: If one gave wool to the dyer and the vat burned it, he gives him the value of his wool. If he dyed it poorly, if the increased value is more than the expenses, he gives him his expenses; if the expenses are more than the increased value he gives him the increased value. To dye it red and he dyed it black, black and he dyed it red, {NAME} says, he gives him the value of his wool. {NAME} says, if the increased value is more than the expenses, he gives him his expenses; if the expenses are more than the increased value he gives him the increased value.
[Bava Kamma 9:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If one gave wool to the dyer,” etc. {NAME} said, if chemicals burned it, but if the vat burned it, he may say to him: Here is your property before you. {NAME} said, even if chemicals burned it, he may say to him: Here is your property before you.
[Bava Kamma 9:5.3] What means “if the increased value is more than the expenses, he gives him his expenses”? A person gave to another five lots of wool, five portions of dye, and ten minas for his wages. He told him, dye it red, but the other dyed it black. He told him, if you had dyed it red, it would have been worth 25 minas, now that you dyed it black it is worth only 20 minas. You lost yours, I did not lose mine. {NAME} said, you can understand from here that if a person gave to another eight denars to buy for him wheat in Tiberias but he bought for him in Sepphoris, he may say to him, if you had bought for me in Tiberias there would have been 25 modii ; now that you bought in Sepphoris there are only 20 modii. You lost yours, I did not lose mine.
[Bava Kamma 9:5.4] It was stated: One gives money to another to buy wheat for him, but the man bought barley. If it went down in price, it went down in price for him; if it rose in price, it rose for him. We stated otherwise: “If it went down in price, it went down in price for him; if it rose in price, it rose for both of them.” [He who said if it went down in price, it went down in price for him; if it rose in price, it rose for him, is {NAME}. What is {NAME} reason? Because the seller intended to transfer ownership only to the buyer. But he who said, if it went down in price, it went down in price for him; if it rose in price, it rose for both of them, is {NAME}.] What is {NAME} reason? Because the seller intended to transfer ownership only to the owner of the money. Why does he (not) split with him? Because it is forbidden to take advantage of another person. Then even if one gave him money to buy wheat and he bought wheat? [{NAME} said, if he had given money to buy wheat and he bought wheat,] the seller intended to transfer ownership only to the owner of the money. If he had given money to buy wheat and he bought barley, the seller intended to transfer ownership only to the buyer, who is stuck with what he has on his hands. {NAME} said, if he was true to his agency, did the seller not intend to transfer ownership to the owner of the money? If he was not true to his agency, he intended to transfer ownership to the buyer. Then why does he split with him? He said, because he realizes a profit by means of the other man’s money, he splits with him.
[Bava Kamma 9:5.5] {NAME} objected before {NAME}. Did we not state: “Both the person who dedicates and the one who vows his own valuation exclude their wives’ and children’s clothing.” He answered, nobody thought to include their wives’ and children’s clothing. But did we not state: “My valuation on myself”; at the moment when he said, my valuation on myself, he only obligated himself for fifty tetradrachmas. If he says, my valuation on myself on condition not to pledge what is worn by my wife and children? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One who says, my valuation on myself on condition not to pledge a particular thing, one cannot use that particular thing as a pledge. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This implies that one does not foreclose valuations from movables by biblical decree but only from the rabbis.
[Bava Kamma 9:6.1] MISHNAH: He who robbed at least a peruṭa ’s worth from a fellow man and swore to him should deliver it to him even in Media. He should deliver neither to [the victim’s] son nor to his agent, but he may deliver to an agent of the court, and if [the victim] had died, he has to make restitution to his heirs. If he had returned the capital but not the fifth, or [the victim] had forgiven him the capital but not the fifth or had forgiven him both except for less than a peruṭa ’s worth of the capital, he need not follow him. If he had returned the fifth but not the capital, or [the victim] had forgiven him the fifth but not the capital or had forgiven him both except for a peruṭa ’s worth of the capital, he has to follow him. If he paid the capital but swore on the fifth, he pays a fifth for the fifth until the capital becomes less than a peruṭa ’s worth. And so “for a deposit, or a partnership, or robbery, or if he oppressed his neighbor, or found lost property and denied it, and swore falsely,” has to pay the capital, and a fifth, and a reparation sacrifice.
[Bava Kamma 9:6.2] HALAKHAH: “He who robbed at least a peruṭa ’s worth from a fellow man,” etc. So is the Mishnah: Until the last fifth becomes less than a peruṭa ’s worth. {NAME} said: By handing over the fifth, the fifth becomes capital. This only applies with witnesses and at the time of sacrifices.
[Bava Kamma 9:7.1] MISHNAH: Where is my deposit? He told him ‘it was lost’. ‘I will make you swear’ and he said ‘amen’. If witnesses testify against him that he ate it, he pays the capital. If he confessed on his own, he has to pay the capital, and a fifth, and a reparation sacrifice. Where is my deposit? He told him ‘it was stolen’. ‘I will make you swear’ and he said ‘amen’. If witnesses testify against him that he stole it, he pays double restitution. If he confessed on his own, he has to pay the capital, and a fifth, and a reparation sacrifice. He who robbed from his father and swore to him when he died has to pay capital and fifth to his sons or brothers. But if he refuses, or does not have the money, he takes a loan and the creditors come and make themselves paid.
[Bava Kamma 9:7.2] HALAKHAH: “Where is my deposit? He told him ‘it was lost’,” etc. It was stated: “One does not accept deposits from women, or slaves, or underage children. If one accepted from a woman, he should return it to her; if she died, he should return it to her husband. If one accepted from a slave, he should return it to him; if he died, he should return it to his master. From an underage child, he should return it to him, if he died he should return it to his father, and make it a safe investment. If any of these said at the moment of their death, it should be given to X because it is his property, one should follow his interpretation.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Only before witnesses. As the following: When {NAME} wife was dying, she said, these rings belong to my daughter. But he said no, they are mine. The case came before Rav who said, people are not given to lying at the time of their death.
[Bava Kamma 9:8.1] MISHNAH: If somebody says to his son: A qônām that you cannot enjoy anything from me, when he dies he can inherit from him. During my lifetime and after my death, when he dies he cannot inherit from him but should give it to his sons or his brothers, and if he has nothing he may take a loan; the creditors come and make themselves paid.
[Bava Kamma 9:8.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody says to his son: A qônām that you cannot enjoy anything from me,” etc. {NAME} said, look what we did state here: “If somebody says to his son, ‘a qônām that you can not enjoy anything from me,’ if he dies, the son inherits; ‘during my lifetime and after my death,’ if he dies, he cannot inherit.” Did we not state, ‘during my lifetime’, he inherits; ‘after my death’, he inherits, ‘during my lifetime and after my death’, he cannot inherit? What is the difference between the one who says it one by one and the one who says it by twos? {NAME} and {NAME} both say, ‘a qônām that I shall not enter this house during my lifetime and after my death’, since he said “this house”, he forbade it on himself during lifetime and after death. {NAME} said, we have stated in Neziqin what we did not state in Nedarim : ‘A qônām that I cannot enjoy these my properties during my lifetime and after my death,’ from the moment he said “these” he forbade them to himself during his lifetime and after his death.
[Bava Kamma 9:9.1] MISHNAH: One who robbed from a proselyte, swore to him, and [the proselyte] died, has to pay the capital and the fifth to the priests and the reparation offering to the altar as it is said: “If the man has no heirs to give the reparation to, the reparation etc.” If he was bringing the money and the reparation offering when he died, the money should be given to his sons and the reparation offering shall graze until it becomes disqualified, then be sold, and the amount be given for voluntary offerings. If he had given the money to the men of the watch when he died, the heirs cannot ask it back from them since it is said: “What a man give to a Cohen shall be the latter’s.”
[Bava Kamma 9:9.2] HALAKHAH: “One who robbed from a proselyte,” etc. Ḥilfai and {NAME} said, this is {NAME}, as {NAME} explained: Of what does the verse speak? About one who robbed from a proselyte, swore to him, who then died, that he would pay the capital and the fifth to the priests and the reparation offering to the altar. “If the man have no relative,” he who needs atonement is obligated; this excludes the one who does not need atonement. {NAME} explained when he came from Zephyrium: About one who robbed from a proselyte, swore to him, who then died, that he would pay the capital and the fifth to the priests and the reparation offering to the altar, as it is said: “If the man have no relative,” etc. The only person in Israel who has no relative is the proselyte. Rav and {NAME} said, it is {NAME} who said that the wrongly acquired property has to be returned in any case.
[Bava Kamma 9:10.1] MISHNAH: If he gave the money to Yehoiarib and the reparation offering to Yedaiah, he has fulfilled his obligation. The reparation offering to Yehoiarib and the money to Yedaiah, if the offering still is alive it should be brought by Yedaiah; otherwise he was to come back and bring another reparation offering; for he who brings the robbed item before he brings the reparation offering has fulfilled his obligation, but he who brings the reparation offering before he brings the robbed item has not fulfilled his obligation. If he paid the capital but not the fifth, the fifth is no obstacle.
[Bava Kamma 9:10.2] HALAKHAH: “If he gave the money to Yehoiarib,” etc. {NAME} said, they disagree about two weeks, {NAME} said about one week. He who said about two weeks, “if he gave the money to Yehoiarib on Yedaiah’s watch and the reparation offering to Yedaiah on Yehoiarib’s watch, he has fulfilled his obligation. Rebbi said, following {NAME} words if the men from Yehoiarib offered the reparation offering there was no atonement; but the money should be transferred from the men of Yedaiah to the men of Yehoiarib; the men from Yehoiarib then shall offer the reparation offering for atonement.” This implies that one removes the money given to men of a watch not during their week. He who said that they disagree about one week, if he gave the money to Yehoiarib on Yedaiah’s watch and the reparation offering to Yedaiah on Yehoiarib’s watch, means that he did not fulfill his obligation, etc. This implies that one does not remove a sacrifice which men of a watch received during their week. But if the watch of the men of Yehoiarib dragged their feet, then the baraita implies that they dragged their feet after the men of Yehoiarib received the reparation offering after days, and there is no atonement. But one has to transfer the money from the men of Yedaiah to the men of Yehoiarib, the men of Yedaiah shall offer the reparation offering, and there will be atonement. This implies that if men of a watch received a sacrifice during their week but were lazy and did not offer it, one removes it from their hand.
[Bava Kamma 10:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody robbed to feed his children and they inherited from him, they are not liable to pay; if it was mortgageable property they have to pay. One changes money neither from the chest of the publican nor the wallet of the tax collector and one does not accept charity from these, but one accepts from their house or from the market place.
[Bava Kamma 10:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody robbed to feed his children,” etc. It was stated: “A Jew who is engaged in lending with interest and repented, has to return it. If he died and left it to his children, about him the verse says ‘he prepares but the just will wear it.’ If he left them a cow or a stole, they have to return it.” He went and stated that for robberies.
[Bava Kamma 10:1.3] “If it was mortgageable property they have to return it.” What is mortgageable property? {NAME} says, if they inherited real estate. {NAME} said, if they inherited robbed items. Rav said, an heir is like the holder of encumbered property. Just as a loan executed before witnesses cannot be collected from encumbered property, so it cannot be collected from heirs. {NAME} said, what was received cannot be foreclosed on mortgaged property, but on free property it can be foreclosed. But does [the Mishnah] not disagree with Rav? Since Rav said, an heir is like a holder of encumbered property; just as a loan executed before witnesses cannot be collected from encumbered property, so it cannot be foreclosed from heirs. Explain it if he left them real estate. But might it not disagree with {NAME}? Did not {NAME} say, what was received cannot be foreclosed on mortgaged property? Explain it if they inherited robbed items.
[Bava Kamma 10:1.4] If he robbed a stole and gave it to another person. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, one takes away from the first one but not from the second. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, one takes away even from the second. {NAME} said, even {NAME} will agree with this since {NAME} said, one takes away even from the second.
[Bava Kamma 10:1.5] If his vessels were switched at the artisan’s he may use them while he goes out and searches for his own. At a mourner’s house or at a wedding, he may not use them while he goes out and searches for his own. {NAME} said, my uncle {NAME} explained this only as in the case of one {NAME} where everybody who takes from him takes by permission and everybody who puts something up there does so with permission.
[Bava Kamma 10:1.6] “If thieves who stole by stealth repented, they have to make restitution. If one of a gang repented, he has to make restitution for himself. But if he traded for them, he has to make restitution for all of them.”
[Bava Kamma 10:1.7] It was stated: “If somebody robbed to feed his children, whether adult or underage, they are not liable to pay. If they inherited from him, both adult and underage are liable to pay. Symmachos says, the adults are liable, the underaged are not liable. If they said, we do not know whether our father accounted for it at the end, they are not liable.” {NAME} objected: Think of it, if they inherited real estate, they are not able to say, we do not know whether our father accounted for it at the end. {NAME} objected: Think of it, if it was a notorious robbery; they are not able to say, we do not know whether our father accounted for it at the end. {NAME} objected: For the underaged the court will argue. What can you say? {NAME} said, explain it if they argue, we do not know, etc., we know that our father was in dispute with you on this account, but we do not know how it was resolved.
[Bava Kamma 10:2.1] MISHNAH: If the publicans took his donkey and gave him another donkey, or armed robbers took his garment and gave him another garment, they are his since the owners had given up hope of recovery. Things saved from a flood or from armed robbers are his if the owners had given up hope of recovery. Similarly, a swarm of bees is his if the owners had given up hope of recovery. {NAME} said, a woman or a child are trusted if they say: “This swarm of bees came from here.” [The beekeeper] may enter another’s field to take his swarm; if he caused damage he has to pay what he damaged, but he cannot cut off a branch intending to pay for it. {NAME}, {NAME} son, said: he may even cut a branch and pay for it.
[Bava Kamma 10:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If the publicans took,” etc. It was stated: “Things saved from an army, or a fire, from a whirlpool in the sea, a whirlpool of a river, are his.”
[Bava Kamma 10:2.3] “Similarly, a swarm of bees is his if the owners had given up hope of recovery.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah is about a swarm taken in flight and from a schoolboy, and only immediately. But if one left and returned, I am saying that he said it because of fear, or being seduced. It was stated: {NAME} says, it is a stipulation by the court that this one may cut a branch and pay for it since on this condition did Joshua distribute the Land to Israel.
[Bava Kamma 10:3.1] MISHNAH: If one recognizes his own vessels or books in the hand of another, if the theft was a known fact in town, [the other] shall swear to him how much he paid and take this amount. Otherwise he cannot be believed, for I am saying that he had sold the items to a third party and the other had bought them from there.
[Bava Kamma 10:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If one recognizes his own vessels or books,” etc. {NAME} said, it would have been correct that they should not have to swear. Why did they say they have to swear? That homeowners should not be fences. {NAME} said, only if it was a known fact that his books had been stolen. Rav said, he has to bring proof that he stayed there the night in question. {NAME} said, if he claims: “I bought them from X,” he is to be believed. A case came before {NAME} and he did not accept it. Does he disagree? They said, he was a known troublemaker; therefore he did not accept the case.
[Bava Kamma 10:4.1] MISHNAH: One comes with his amphora of wine, the other comes with his jug of honey. If the amphora of honey sprang a leak, if the other one poured out his wine and saved the honey into it, he only has his wages. But if he said, I shall save yours if you pay me the value of mine, he is liable to pay him.
[Bava Kamma 10:4.2] HALAKHAH: “One comes with his amphora of wine,” etc. It was stated: “Two people are in the desert; in the hand of one is an amphora of water, in the other’s hand an amphora of honey. If the water amphora springs a leak it is a stipulation of the court that the other pour out his honey in order to save the water since water sustains life in the desert but not honey.” It was stated: “If a worker and a poor man climbed on a tree and broke a branch; if workers are supposed to climb the tree they are not liable, otherwise they are liable.”
[Bava Kamma 10:5.1] MISHNAH: If a river washed away his donkey and another’s donkey; his was worth a mina, the other’s 200. If he abandoned his own and saved the other’s, he only has his wages. But if he said, I shall save yours if you pay me the value of mine, he is liable to pay him.
[Bava Kamma 10:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If a river washed away his donkey,” etc. It was stated: If he abandoned his to save the other’s, but the other’s climbed out by himself, he does not owe him anything. But if he abandoned his to save the other’s, and his own climbed out by himself, may he say, “I did not abandon hope of recovery”? Let us hear from the following: If a river washed away his donkey and he was crying: “I did not abandon hope of recovery!” {NAME} said, as long as he is crying he did not abandon hope of recovery. {NAME} said, there is a presumption that he had abandoned hope.
[Bava Kamma 10:6.1] MISHNAH: Somebody had robbed a field which subsequently was taken by discharged veterans. If it is a provincial plague, he may tell him: Here is your property before you. But if it was because of the robber, he has to give him a field. If a river had washed it away, he may say to him: Here is your property before you. He who robbed from another, or took a loan from him, or accepted a deposit in a built-up area cannot give it back to him in the desert. [If it was given] with the intent to depart for the desert, he can give it back to him in the desert.
[Bava Kamma 10:6.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody had robbed a field from another person,” etc. {NAME} said, but did they not say that “real estate cannot be robbed”? Why did they say, “he has to give him a field”? It is a fine by which they fined him. If the discharged veterans took it from the robber because of the robbed, could he tell him, in any case give me what is mine and let any claimant come and deal with me? {NAME} said, nobody is held responsible for his neighbor and the latter has to repay him except annona and head-tax. Rav said, he can tell him, you redeemed your pledge with my money.
[Bava Kamma 10:7.1] MISHNAH: He who says to another: I robbed you, or I took a loan from you, you deposited with me, but I do not known whether I returned it to you or did not return it, is liable to pay. But if he said to him: I do not know whether I robbed you, or I took a loan from you, or you deposited with me or did not deposit, he is not liable to pay.
[Bava Kamma 10:7.2] HALAKHAH: “He who says to another: I robbed you,” etc. {NAME} said, if he wants to clear himself before Heaven. I robbed you, or I took a loan from you, you deposited with me; did I return it to you? The other party says, I do not know. {NAME} wanted to say, he is required to make good as a matter of law. {NAME} wanted to say, still it is to become clear before Heaven. I took from the wallet and gave to you, and the other party says, I do not know. {NAME} said, one tells him: You do not know but the other party knows.
[Bava Kamma 10:8.1] MISHNAH: If one stole a lamb from the flock and returned it, if it died or was stolen he is liable. If the owners were unaware both of the theft and the return, he is no longer liable after they counted the flock and found it complete.
[Bava Kamma 10:8.2] HALAKHAH: “If one stole a lamb from the flock,” etc. {NAME} said, if the owners knew of the theft, they have to be notified of the return. If they did not know of the theft, they do not have to be notified of the return. {NAME} said, even if they did not know of the theft, they have to be notified of the return. {NAME} said, if it was similar to the case of a ram, they do not have to be notified of the return. What means “similar to the case of a ram”? Some say, the shepherd’s staff. Some say, a pandura . Some say, the bell-wether.
[Bava Kamma 10:9.1] MISHNAH: One does not buy wool, or milk, or lambs from shepherds, nor wood or fruits from orchard watchmen; but one may buy linen garments from women in Galilee, and calves in the Sharon. In all cases it is forbidden if they told to hide. One buys eggs and chickens everywhere.
[Bava Kamma 10:9.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not buy from shepherds,” etc. It was stated: “One does not accept deposits from women, or slaves, or underage children. If one accepted from a woman, he should return it to her; if she died, he should return it to her husband.”
[Bava Kamma 10:10.1] MISHNAH: Fibers which remain at the washer’s are his, but what the carder produces are the consignor’s. The washer takes three threads and they are his, more than that belong to the consignor. If it was black on a white background he takes all of them and they are his.
[Bava Kamma 10:10.2] HALAKHAH: “Fibers which remain at the washer’s,” etc. {NAME} was a washer. He made himself a tunic of a single kind of wool lest people say: He wears our property.
[Bava Kamma 10:11.1] MISHNAH: The tailor who had enough thread left to sew with it, and cloth three by three finger breadths, has to return if to its owners. What the woodworker takes off with a small plane is his, with a large one belongs to the consignor; if he works at the latter’s place even the chips are the consignor’s.
[Bava Kamma 10:11.2] HALAKHAH: “The tailor who had enough thread left,” etc. {NAME} stated: A needle full. The House of {NAME} explained: Twice a needle full. {NAME} stated: The stitching with a needle. The House of {NAME} explained: twice the stitching of a needle. Do they disagree? What {NAME} stated, a needle full, the House of {NAME} explained: Twice a needle full. {NAME} stated: the stitching with a needle, the House of {NAME} explained: twice the stitching of a needle.

TRACTATE: Bava Metzia

[Bava Metzia 1:1.1] MISHNAH: If two persons hold on to one toga and each of them says “I found it” [or] “it wholly belongs to me”, each of them has to swear that he owns no less than half of it and they shall divide it evenly. If one says “it wholly belongs to me” and one says “half of it belongs to me”, the one who says “it wholly belongs to me” shall swear that he owns no less than three parts and the one who says “half of it belongs to me” shall swear that he owns no less than a quarter. The first one takes three parts, the second takes a fourth.
[Bava Metzia 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If two people hold on to one stole,” etc. It was stated: One person said to another, give me the mina which you owe me. He answered, it never happened. He went and brought witnesses that the other owed him 50 zuz. The elder {NAME} said, the confession of the witnesses is the same as his own confession; he has to swear about the remainder. {NAME} said, the confession of the witnesses is not the same as his own confession that he should have to swear. {NAME} said, {NAME} the elder’s statement is implied by “if two people hold on to one stole”. Since he holds on to half of it, is it not as if he brought witnesses that one half belongs to him? Could one not say that he swears and collects? Is this a similar case?
[Bava Metzia 1:1.3] This topic came up between {NAME} and {NAME}. One said, one does not entrust an oath to a suspect person. The other said, one does not even formulate an oath for such a one. {NAME} said: “An oath that I have property rights to it to the amount of no less than (the value of a peruṭah ) [half of its value]. {NAME} said, if it is about this, it is an institutional oath.
[Bava Metzia 1:1.4] It was stated: “If two persons were holding a document and one said, it is mine but I had lost it; the other said, it is mine since I paid you. The document should be validated by its signatories, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} said, they should split.” {NAME} said, it all depends on who is holding the signatures. {NAME} said, if this is true information, it follows {NAME}.
[Bava Metzia 1:1.5] One says, half is mine; the other says, a third is mine. The one who says that half is his shall swear that no less than a quarter be his; the one who says that a third is his shall swear that no less than a sixth be his. The principle involved: One only swears on half of what he agreed to.
[Bava Metzia 1:2.1] MISHNAH: If two persons were riding on an animal or one was riding and one was walking, each of them says “it wholly belongs to me”, each of them has to swear that he owns no less than half of it and they shall divide it evenly. If they agree or if they have witnesses, they divide without an oath.
[Bava Metzia 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If two persons were riding on an animal,” etc. {NAME} said: It was stated there: “A woman comes riding on an animal and two men lead her. She says: these are my slaves; the donkey and the load are mine. Each of them says: this is my wife, the other is my slave, and the donkey and the load are mine. She needs a bill of divorce from both of them and has to manumit both of them. They have to manumit one another. In the donkey and the load they are equal co-owners.
[Bava Metzia 1:3.1] MISHNAH: Somebody was riding on an animal when he saw a find and said to another person: “give it to me”. If [that one] took it and said: “I acquired it”, he acquired it. If after he had handed it over, he said: “I acquired it first,” he did not say anything.
[Bava Metzia 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody was riding on an animal,” etc. {NAME} says, from this rule one cannot infer anything, not from its beginning nor from its end. “Somebody was riding on an animal when he saw a find and said to another person: ‘give it to me’. If [that one] took it and said: ‘I acquired it’, he acquired it”. If he had said, “acquire it for me”, he would have acquired it. That means, from this rule one cannot infer anything, not from its beginning nor from its end.
[Bava Metzia 1:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody saw a find and fell upon it when another person grabbed it, the one who grabbed it acquired it. If one saw people running after a find, after an injured deer, after young pigeons unable to fly, and he said: “my field shall acquire it for me”, it acquired it for him. If the deer was running normally, or the pigeons were flying, and he said: “my field shall acquire it for me”, he did not say anything.
[Bava Metzia 1:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody saw a find” etc. {NAME} said [in the name of] {NAME}: A person acquires a find within four cubits from himself. {NAME} said, only if it fell into his hand. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If he took some of the peah and threw it on the rest, he has nothing of it.” He answered: Explain it if the did not say that his four cubits should acquire it for him. But does it not say afterwards: “If he fell on it or spread his talith on it, one removes him from it?” That is the same, if he did not say that his four cubits should acquire it for him. But did not {NAME} state: “If two were pushing one another because of a sheaf and another poor person came and grabbed it from before them, he is entitled to it.” It is the same; he did not say that his four cubits should acquire it for him. But did we not state: “If somebody saw a find and fell upon it when another person grabbed it, the one who grabbed it acquired it.” It is the same, he did not say that his four cubits should acquire it for him. But did we not state: “If it landed close to her it is a bill of divorce, close to him it is no bill of divorce, half and half she is divorced and not divorced.” {NAME} said, the Mishnah speaks of the scribe’s fee. They objected: Is it not written: “I in my poverty did prepare”? How is that? If it was in his possession, he was rich. If it was not in his possession, how can a person dedicate what is not his? It must be that it was within four cubits from him. {NAME} said, what means “in my poverty?” That there is no wealth before Him Who commanded and the world came into existence! Another explanation: he fasted and donated the price of his meal to Heaven.
[Bava Metzia 1:4.3] It was stated: “One who says, my house shall acquire for me any find that fell into it, did not say anything. If the find was known, his words stand.” As in the case of {NAME} sharecropper who climbed a date palm, found pigeon chicks there, and took them. He went to ask the master, who said nothing to him. He went and returned them. {NAME} said, his returning is more difficult for us than his finding.
[Bava Metzia 1:5.1] MISHNAH: The find of his small son or daughter, or of his Canaanite male or female slave, his wife’s find, these are his. The find of his adult son or daughter, or of his Hebrew male or female slave, his wife’s find after he divorced her even though he did not yet pay her ketubah , these are their own.
[Bava Metzia 1:5.2] HALAKHAH: “The find of his small son or daughter,” etc. {NAME} said, only if they are not dependent on their father. But if they are dependent on their father, their finds belong to the latter. {NAME} says, a person cannot acquire a find for another. Rebbi [Hila] said: Not that {NAME} had formulated thus, but he had a problem with what {NAME} stated: If a person hires a worker for any work, the latter’s finds belong to the employer. {NAME} said, should the finds of a person who can resign at any moment belong to his employer?
[Bava Metzia 1:5.3] What is the difference between his Hebrew male and female slaves and his Canaanite male and female slaves? {NAME} said, since he is not empowered to change the employment of his male or female Hebrew slave, that one’s find belongs to himself. Since he is empowered to change the employment of his male or female Canaanite slave, their find belongs to their master. They objected: He is not empowered to change the employment of his wife, but her find belongs to him. As we have stated there: “He forces her to work with wool,” he cannot force her to work any other material. {NAME} and {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: there is another reason in the case of the wife. What is another reason in the case of the wife? {NAME} said, because of quarrel. {NAME} said, lest she smuggle away her husband’s property and say: it is a find. They objected: before witnesses? They forbade one because of the other.
[Bava Metzia 1:5.4] “His wife’s find after he divorced her.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A man who divorced his wife without paying her ketubah is liable for her upkeep until he gave her the last penny. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says this, “his wife’s find after he divorced her.” {NAME} said, the Mishnah is needed lest you say that because he is liable for her upkeep until he gave her the last penny, her find should be his.
[Bava Metzia 1:6.1] MISHNAH: One who found documents of indebtedness containing an alienation clause should not return them since the court will foreclose on their basis. If they do not contain an alienation clause, he should return them since the court will not foreclose on their basis, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, in no case should he return them since the court will foreclose on their basis.
[Bava Metzia 1:6.2] HALAKHAH: “One who found documents of indebtedness,” etc. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: Both based on a document containing an alienation clause or a document containing no alienation clause, he collects from unincumbered property. Following this opinion of {NAME}, to what purpose does he return it? To cover the mouth of his pitcher. Rav said, an heir is like the holder of encumbered property. Just as a loan executed before witnesses cannot be collected from encumbered property, so it cannot be collected from heirs. {NAME} said, what was received cannot be foreclosed on mortgaged property, but on free property it can be foreclosed. Here you say, it can be collected, but there you say, it cannot be collected. There is no comparison between one who agreed to a small lien and one who never agreed to a lien.
[Bava Metzia 1:6.3] {NAME} said, for I am saying that he wanted to take a loan but did not. {NAME} said, if the debtor agreed, he should return it. {NAME} said, if the document was generally known to be in the creditor’s hand, he should return it. But all three are broken, “the Sages say, in no case should he return them.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because of conspiracy. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If its date was that very day, he should return it.
[Bava Metzia 1:6.4] But could he not return it if the date was not of the same day? Do they disagree? But {NAME} said* in the name of {NAME}: Because of conspiracy. {NAME} said*: If its date was that very day, he should return it.
[Bava Metzia 1:7.1] MISHNAH: One who found women’s bills of divorce or slaves’ bills of manumission, dispositions of gift or receipts should not return them since I say that they were written but he changed his mind not to deliver them.
[Bava Metzia 1:7.2] HALAKHAH: “One who found women’s bills of divorce,” etc. It was stated: One whou found women’s bills of divorce with ketubot should return them.” Is the ketubah not prime facie evidence?
[Bava Metzia 1:7.3] If a person took a documented loan and paid it back, he cannot use the document to take a second loan because it diminishes the power of the buyers. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Even on the same day. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Here you say, even on the same day. But there, you say, if its date was that very day, he should return it! He answered, a person is apt to take a loan and repay it the same day, but a person is not apt to repay a loan and take it the same day. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: It is the same day, the same witnesses, and the same amount. What is the meaning of “it diminishes the power of the buyers”? He answered, if the property had not been mortgaged. But some say, if the witnesses did not sign for this loan.
[Bava Metzia 1:8.1] MISHNAH: One who found letters of appraisal, letters of sustenance, or documents of ḥalîṣah or repudiation, or documents of arbitration, or any other court document, should return them. If he found in a basket or in a box a bundle or joined documents he should return them. How many are joined documents? Three documents connected one to the other. {NAME} says, if one persons borrows from three, he should return it to the borrower; if three persons borrow from one, he should return it to the lender. If he found a document among his documents whose nature was unknown to him, it should lie there until Elijah comes. If it has an agreement attached to it, he should follow the agreement.
[Bava Metzia 1:8.2] HALAKHAH: “One who found letters of appraisal,” etc. {NAME} in the name of Rav: If it contained a certification by the court, it should be returned. {NAME} {NAME} said, the tamarisks among the judges of the diaspora are like chicks among the judges of the Land of Israel.
[Bava Metzia 1:8.3] {NAME} said, if the sale contract was written on the first of Nisan but payment was only on the tenth of Nisan, they have to write: Even though we wrote the document on the first of Nisan it was agreed that payment be made on the tenth of Nisan.
[Bava Metzia 1:8.4] {NAME} in the name of Rav: A stipulation produced by the creditor in the creditor’s handwrtiting is invalid, for I am saying that he has trained in writing documents. This implies that in the hand of another it would be valid. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A stipulation is only valid if it is in the possession of the creditor but written by the debtor. But did we not state: “That our father did not charge us, that our father did not tell us, that we did not find a document among our father’s documents that this note was paid.” Therefore, it might be found paid. What about this? {NAME} said, explain it that it was a testamentary gift., since people are not likely to impair their testamentary gifts.
[Bava Metzia 2:1.1] MISHNAH: Which finds are his and which ones does he have to make public? The following finds are his: If he found scattered produce, scattered coins, bundles of grain in the public domain, or fig cakes, baker’s loaves, strings of fish, cuts of meat, local fleece-wool, bundles of flax, or strips of purple wool; these are his.
[Bava Metzia 2:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Which finds are his,” etc. From where may an owner’s hopelessness be deduced from the Torah? {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: “So you shall proceed with his donkey,” etc. What is lost by him but may be found by anybody you have to make public. But what is not lost by him but may be found by anybody you do not have to make public. This excludes the owner’s hopelessness about that which was lost by him or anybody.
[Bava Metzia 2:1.3] It was stated: “One who found bundles of grain in the public domain does not have to make it public; in a private domain he has to make it public. Sheaves he has to make public, whether in the public or the private domain.”
[Bava Metzia 2:1.4] “Fig cakes.” That is, large cakes. But small cakes which come from Bostra he has to make public since they are typical for that place. Cuts of meat and among them a loaf or a kidney he has to make public. Strings of fish strung together with a vegetable or a whitefish he has to make public.
[Bava Metzia 2:2.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, anything out of the ordinary one has to make public. How is this? If he found a fig cake containing a potsherd, or a loaf containing coins. {NAME} said, merchandise of any kind one does not have to make public.
[Bava Metzia 2:2.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} says, anything out of the ordinary,” etc. It was stated: If it is embedded in it. Here you say, if it is embedded in it. But there you say, if it lies on top of it. When you say, if it is embedded in it, in the public domain. When you say, if it lies on top of it, in a private domain. Maybe even in the public domain? If it lies on top of it, I am saying that if fell there.
[Bava Metzia 2:2.3] “{NAME} said, merchandise of any kind one does not have to make public.” {NAME} made this public and stated about it: “The following are these. For example needle strips, fire tongs, and strips of axes. The Amora of {NAME} found a web rolled in a scarf. He came before {NAME} who instructed him following {NAME}. The Amora of {NAME} found a web rolled in a scarf. He came before {NAME} who asked him, where did you find it? In an alley, in a public square? For he wanted to free him following {NAME}.
[Bava Metzia 2:3.1] MISHNAH: But the following must be made public: If one found produce in a container or simply a container, coins in a wallet or simply a wallet, heaps of produce, heaps of coins, three coins one on top of the other, bundles of grain in a private domain, home-baked loaves, fleece wool taken from an artisan’s house. Pitchers of wine and pitchers of oil he has to make public.
[Bava Metzia 2:3.2] HALAKHAH: “But the following must be made public,” etc. {NAME} says three coins of three kings. {NAME} said, or even three from one king if they form a tower? Of three kings and they are in three towers? Or even three of one king as a tower.
[Bava Metzia 2:3.3] “Pitchers of wine and pitchers of oil he has to make public.” {NAME} said, if it was like a tripod one does not have to make it public. What means, like a tripod? For example, a corral belonging to three people. Since one does not know to whom to return it, he does not have to make it public. {NAME} said, one understands from here that if a person went behind {NAME} and a denar fell down from them, since one does not know to whom to return it, he does not have to make it public. {NAME} was walking behind {NAME}; a denar fell down from him. {NAME} presented it to him. He answered, I already had given up hope about this. They said, {NAME} only intended it for {NAME} because he was poor.
[Bava Metzia 2:4.1] MISHNAH: If one found pigeon chicks bound together behind a temporary or permanent fence or on paths between fields, he should not touch them. If one found a vessel on garbage heaps, if it was covered he should not touch it, if in the open he should take it and make it public. What one found in a heap or an old wall belongs to him. At a new wall, from the middle to the outside belongs to him, from the middle to the inside belongs to its owner. If he was renting out to others, even what is inside the house belongs to him.
[Bava Metzia 2:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If one found behind a temporary fence”, etc. {NAME} said: Only pigeon chicks tied together at their wings. {NAME} found a ring covered in a box and took it. He came and asked Rav, who told him, you did not act correctly. He said, shall I return it? He answered, no, for we might say that his owner came, looked for it, did not find it and gave up hope for it.
[Bava Metzia 2:4.3] It was stated: What one found on a garbage heap he has to make public, for garbage is moved. What one found in a heap or an old wall belongs to him, for I am saying that it belonged to the Emorites. It was stated: If one found between planks, from the door and inside is like inside, from the door and outside is like outside. If it was opening to the inside, even from from the middle to the outside belongs to the owner of the property; if it was opening to the outside, even from the middle to the inside belongs to the finders.
[Bava Metzia 2:4.4] “If he was renting out to others, even what is inside the house belongs to him.” {NAME} says, they disagree about a hostelry, but in a courtyard everybody agrees that he is required to make it public. {NAME} said, they disagree about a courtyard, but in a hostelry everybody agrees that it belongs to its finder.
[Bava Metzia 2:5.1] MISHNAH: What one found in a store is his. Between the counter and the storekeeper it is the storekeeper’s. Before the moneychanger it is his. Between the chair and the moneychanger it is the moneychanger’s. If one bought produce from another person or another person sent him produce and he found coins in it, they are his. But if they were bundled, he takes them and makes it public. The garment was subsumed under “anything”; why was it mentioned separately? To bracket with it and tell you, just as a garment is special in that it has distinguishing marks and claimants, so about everything which has distinguishing marks and claimants you have to give public notice.
[Bava Metzia 2:5.2] HALAKHAH: “What one found in a store is his,” etc. {NAME} said, so is the Mishnah: On his chair, on his counter.
[Bava Metzia 2:5.3] {NAME} was working with linen. His students said to him, Rabbi, in order to make it easier for you we want to buy a donkey, then you will not have to work so hard. They went and bought a donkey from a Saracen; a pearl was hanging on its neck. They came to him saying, because of this you will not have to work anymore. He said to them, why? They told him, we bought for you a donkey from a Saracen and a pearl is hanging on its neck. He asked them, does its owner know about this? They answered, no. He told them, go and return it. But did not {NAME}, {NAME}, in the name of Rav say, they objected before Rebbi: Even according to him who says that an object robbed from a Gentile is forbidden, everybody agrees that what he lost is permitted. Do you think that {NAME} was a barbarian? {NAME} wanted to hear: Praised be the God of the Jews, more than any gain in this world.
[Bava Metzia 2:5.4] The following implies the same. {NAME} reports the following case: The elder rabbis bought a heap of wheat from the household of the general and found in it a bundle of denars. They returned it to them. They said, praised be the God of the Jews.
[Bava Metzia 2:5.5] {NAME} [was a washer. The queen came to bathe in a water pond. She lost her בינדילנין; he found it. When she left, he handed it to her.] She said, this is for you; it is not important for me and I have more of this. He told her, the Torah decided that we have to return it. She said, praised be the God of the Jews.
[Bava Metzia 2:5.6] {NAME} went to Rome. The queen had lost her דילניה but he found it. A herold went through the city: One who will return it within 30 days will receive such and such; after 30 days his head will be lifted from him. He did not return it within 30 days. After 30 days he returned it. She asked him, had you not been in the city? He answered, yes. She asked him, had you not heard the voice of the herold? He answered, yes. She asked him, what did he say? He answered, one who will return it within 30 days will receive such and such; after 30 days his head will be lifted from him. She asked him, why did you not return it within 30 days? He answered, one should not say that I acted out of fear of you, but out of fear of the Merciful. She said to him, praised be the God of the Jews.
[Bava Metzia 2:5.7] Alexander the Macedonian went to the king of Cassia. He saw that he had much gold, much silver. He told him, I do not need your gold nor your silver; I came only so see your practice, how you are dealing, how you are judging. While he was still discussing with him, there came a man having a dispute with another, for he bought (a plot, entered it) [a garbage heap, dug in it] and found a treasure trove of denars. The buyer said, I bought a garbage heap, I did not buy a treasure. The seller said, I sold a garbage heap and all it contains. While they still were arguing with one another, the king asked one of them, do you have a male son? He answered, yes. He asked the other one, do you have a female daughter? He answered, yes. He told them, marry them to each other and the treasure should belong to both. He started to laugh. He asked him, why are you laughing? Did I not judge correctly? He asked him, if the case came before you, how would you have judged? He told him, one kills both of them and the treasure falls to the king. He told him, do you love gold so much? He made him a meal and brought before him golden meat, golden chicken. He asked him, can I eat gold? He told him, the spirit of this person should be wiped out. You cannot eat gold, why do you love gold so much? He asked him, does the sun shine upon you? He answered, yes. Does rain fall on you? He answered, yes. He asked him, do you have small animals? He answered, yes. The spirit of this person should be wiped out; you live only by the merit of the small animals, as it is written: “Man and animal You are saving, o Eternal!”
[Bava Metzia 2:6.1] MISHNAH: How long does one have to make it public. Until his neighbors know, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, three holidays, and after the last holiday seven days so that one goes home during three days, comes back during three days, and makes it public for one day.
[Bava Metzia 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: “How long does one have to make it public,” etc. It was stated: In earlier times one made it public during three holidays, and after the last holiday seven days so that one goes home during three days, comes back during three days, and makes it public during one day. After the destruction of the Temple they instituted that one has to make it public during three days. Starting from the danger they instituted that one has to inform his relatives and neighbors; this is sufficient.
[Bava Metzia 2:7.1] MISHNAH: If one described the lost object but not its identifying marks, he should not deliver. To the swindler one should not deliver even if he describes its identifying marks, since it is said: “Until investigating your brother about it,” until you investigate your brother whether he be a swindler or no swindler.
[Bava Metzia 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: “If one described the lost object,” etc. What is a swindler? He shows himself as one who returns finds and uses this for a big coup. How does he make a big coup? He shows himself to people as one who returns finds so they will give him valuables in trust. He takes all of them and disappears. But some say, he goes to one synagogue and hears about distinguishing marks; then he goes to another synagogue, describes the indentifying marks and takes [the finds] away.
[Bava Metzia 2:8.1] MISHNAH: Anything which works and eats shall work and eat. What does not work but eats should be sold because it is said, “and return it to him,” plan to return it to him. What happens with the money? {NAME} says, he may use it; therefore if it is lost he is liable for its alienation. {NAME} says, he may not use it; therefore if it is lost he is not liable for its alienation.

[Bava Metzia 2:9.1] MISHNAH: One who found book-scrolls reads in them once every thirty days; if he is illiterate, he rolls them up. But he should not study a new subject in them, nor should a second person read with him. One who found a garment shakes it out every thirty days; he spreads it out for its conservation, but not to show off. Silver and brass vessels he uses for their preservation, but not to rub off. Gold and glass vessels he should not touch until the prophet Elijah comes. If one found a sack or a chest or anything which he does not take up, he need not take it.
[Bava Metzia 2:9.2] HALAKHAH: “One who found book-scrolls,” etc. It was stated: “One who found book-scrolls reads in them once every thirty days; if he is illiterate he rolls them up. He should not read a paragraph and repeat it, nor should he read a paragraph and translate it, nor should he open more than three pages, nor should three persons read from the same tome. When has this been said? For new ones. But for old ones twelve months. Silver vessels he may use cold but not hot because it blackens them. Brass vessels he may use hot but not on the fire because it diminishes them. Rakes and axes he may use on soft material but not on hard. With a rake he may receive mortar, wash it, and put it back in its place. With an ax he may split wood, but not stone-palm or olive wood. What has been said about a find is valid equally for deposits. If one deposits a garment with another person, he has to shake it out once every thirty days. If it is much work, he can collect his expenses from it.
[Bava Metzia 2:10.1] MISHNAH: What is a lost animal? If he found a donkey or a cow grazing on the road, this is no lost animal. A donkey whose gear is upside-down or a cow running in a vineyard are lost animals. If he returned it but it ran away, returned it but it ran away even four or five times, he is obligated to return it since it is said: “Return it returning.” If he was losing time worth a tetradrachma, he cannot say, give me a tetradrachma but [the owner] may pay him at the rate of an unemployed worker. If there is a court, he can stipulate with him before the court. If there is no court, before whom could he stipulate? His own comes first. If one found it in the cow-shed, he has no obligation; in the public domain he is obligated. But if it was between graves, he may not defile himself. If his father told him to defile himself, or told him not to return it, he should not listen to him. If he unloaded and loaded, unloaded and loaded even four or five times, he is obligated since it is said: “restoring restore”. If he sat down and said, since it is your religious obligation, if you want to unload, unload, he is free since it is said: “with him”. It is a religious obligation to unload, but not to load; {NAME} says, also to load. {NAME} said, if the load was more than the ordinary, he need not do anything since it is said: “under its load,” a load which it can carry.
[Bava Metzia 2:10.2] HALAKHAH: “What is a lost animal,” etc. “If one found it in the cowshed, he has no obligation; in the public domain he is obligated. Between graves, he may not defile himself. If his father told him to defile himself, or told him not to return it, he should not listen to him.” Everywhere you say that a positive commandment has precedence over a prohibition, but here, you say that a positive commandment does not have precedence over a prohibition? There is a difference since both he and his father are required to honor the Omnipresent.
[Bava Metzia 2:10.3] It was stated: “Lying down” but not one which habitually lies down. But then it was stated: “He unloads with him even a hundred times in a day.” When you said, “lying down” rather than one which habitually lies down, about one which lies down by himself. When you said, “he unloads with him even a hundred times,” in an accident.
[Bava Metzia 2:10.4] “if you hit upon.” I could think, really if you hit upon him; the verse says, “if you see.” Concerning “if you see,” I could think even at a distance of a hundred mil ? The verse says, “if you hit upon.” How is this? The Sages estimated one in 7 1/2 of a mil, i. e., a stadion . Putting in order you shall put in order,” this is unloading. “Uplifting you shall uplift,” this is loading. {NAME} says, just as his unloading is [an obligation] from the Torah, so his loading is from the Torah. If the donkey was a Jew’s but the load a Gentile’s, everybody says that he unloads and loads. If the donkey was a Gentile’s but the load a Jew’s, according to the Sages one neither unloads nor loads. According to {NAME} one unloads but does not load.
[Bava Metzia 2:11.1] MISHNAH: Between his lost property and his father’s lost property, his own has precedence. Between his lost property and his teacher’s lost property, his own has precedence. Between his father’s lost property and his teacher’s lost property, his teacher’s lost property has precedence, for his father brought him to the life of this world, but his teacher who taught him wisdom brought him to the life of the future world. But if his father was his teacher’s equal, his father’s lost property has precedence. If his father and his teacher were carrying loads, he unloads his teacher’s and after that his father’s. If his father and his teacher were jailed, he redeems his teacher and after that redeems his father; but if his father was learned he redeems his father and after that redeems his teacher.

The one who taught him first, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, the one from whom he received most of his instruction. {NAME} said, anyone who explained a Mishnah to him.” Rav followed {NAME}, {NAME} {NAME}, and {NAME} {NAME}.

[Bava Metzia 3:1.1] MISHNAH: If one deposited an animal or vessels with another and they were stolen or lost: If the other paid and did not want to swear although they said that the unpaid trustee swears and is absolved, in case the thief was found, he pays double restitution; if he slaughtered or sold it, he pays quadruple or quintuple restitution. To whom does he pay? To the person with whom it was deposited. If the other had sworn and did not pay, in case the thief was found, he pays double restitution; if he slaughtered or sold it, he pays quadruple or quintuple restitution. To whom does he pay? To the owner of the deposit.
[Bava Metzia 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If one deposited an animal or vessels with another,” etc. From where does he bring this? “If the stolen object be found in his hand.” Do we not know that if the thief is found that he has to pay double? To whom does he pay? To the owner of the deposit.” Should he not pay to the person with whom it was deposited? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: “Alive, double he shall pay.” To the place where the capital goes, there the double fine goes. {NAME} and {NAME}; {NAME} adds in the name of {NAME}: Not only when he paid, but even when he stated his willingness to pay it is as if he had paid.
[Bava Metzia 3:1.3] If he said, I am paying, one may suspect that possibly he took it for himself. If he said, I am swearing, but then he saw that other oaths were added and he said, I am paying, one is suspicious. {NAME} said, the Torah did not impose an oath on him to restrict him but to ease for him; for if he wants to pay, he shall pay, and if he wants to swear, he shall swear. If he had witnesses that it was forcibly stolen, to that case refers what {NAME} said: If somebody sells his claims of fines to someone else, he did not do anything. If he had witnesses that it was stolen because of negligence, he comes under the category of “he shall pay”. If afterwards the stolen object was found, to whom does [the thief] pay? To the first, or to the second, or to both of them?

[Bava Metzia 3:3.1] MISHNAH: If one says to two people, I robbed a mina from one of you but I do not know who it was or, the father of one of you deposited a mina with me but I do not know who it is, has to pay a mina to each of them since he himself confessed. [Bava Metzia 3:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody deposits produce with another person, the latter returns it deducting losses, for wheat and rice 9/2 qab per kor , for barley and millet nine qab per kor , for spelt and linseed three se‘ah per kor ; everything proportional to quantity and time elapsed. {NAME} said, do the rats care, do they not eat from much as from little? [Bava Metzia 3:6.1] MISHNAH: If somebody deposits an amphora with another person without insisting on a separate place, when it was moved and broke in his hand, if [the moving] was for his needs, he is liable; for its needs he is not liable. If it broke after it was put down, whether it was for his or its needs, he is not liable. If its owner insisted on a separate place but it was moved and broke, whether in his hand or after it was put down, for his needs he is liable, for its needs he is not liable.
[Bava Metzia 3:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody deposits an amphora with another person,” etc. Did not {NAME} say, to what can the situation be compared? He said, there is a difference because [the trustee] has authority over it. {NAME} said, some say because the trustee has authority over it. What means “for its needs”? If the owner insisted on a specified place, at another place, whether it is for his needs or its needs, he is (not) liable. There are those who say that the trustee is not authorized; there is no difference whether at this place or at another place; for his needs he is liable, for its needs he is not liable.
[Bava Metzia 3:7.1] MISHNAH: If somebody deposits coins with another person who binds them together and carries them on his back or gives them to his underage son or daughter, or locks them insufficiently, he is liable because he did not take care the way people take care. But if he took care the way people take care, he is not liable.
[Bava Metzia 3:7.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody deposits coins with another person,” etc. {NAME} said: One understands from this that in case a man gave plyṭvryn to another in the market place and that one handed it over to his underage son or daughter, if they were stolen or lost he is not liable since I say that nobody is in the market place because of plyṭvryn .
[Bava Metzia 3:7.3] When did they say that the unpaid trustee swears and is absolved? If he took care of it the way caretakers do: He locked as he should, tied as he should, put it into his money-belt, tied it into his poncho and kept it in front of him, put it into a cupboard, a chest, or a safety box; if they were stolen or lost he is required to swear but not liable to pay. If there are witnesses that he did so, he even is freed from the oath. He locked carelessly, tied carelessly, put it on his back, left it on his roof; if it was stolen he is liable for payment. If he put it at a place where he usually keeps his own things, if it was kept safe as it should have been he is not liable, otherwise he is liable.

[Bava Metzia 4:1.1] MISHNAH: Silver acquires gold but gold does not acquire silver. Brass acquires silver but silver does not acquire brass. [Bava Metzia 4:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Cheating is four obols,” etc. Rav said, this is the rate; {NAME} said, it is not the rate. Rav said, if somebody trades on condition that the rules of cheating not apply to him, the rules of cheating do apply to him. {NAME} stated: Cheating applies to a peruṭah, cheating can be by a peruṭah . But what is the status of cheating? It was stated: The item was acquired, he returns the overcharge, the words of {NAME}; {NAME} said, the sale is annulled.
[Bava Metzia 4:3.3] {NAME} asked before Rav: If the seller is being cheated, he is cheated up to a fifth; if the buyer is being cheated, he is cheated up to a sixth! He answered him, it and the amount of cheating add up to a sixth. If he sold him what was worth five for six, can [the seller] not say, you were taken in for a denar, take your denar! {NAME} said, the other can say to him, it is not to my honor that people say, this one was made a laughing stock. Some say, he can say to him, it is not to my honor to wear a garment of five denars. {NAME}, {NAME} and {NAME} say, what is that Tanna’s reason? “I know that my merchandise was worth only five denars, but because he needed it, I gave it to him for six. Take yours and return mine.”
[Bava Metzia 4:3.4] If he sold him what was worth five for six; [the buyer] did not have time to ask around until it appreciated to be worth seven. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Since the sale is annulled for one, it also is annulled for the other. There, we have stated: “Four situations in sales. If he sold him high quality wheat and it turned out to be low quality, the buyer can annul the transaction. Low quality and it turned out to be high quality, the seller can annul the transaction.” [Therefore, the buyer cannot annul the transaction.] {NAME} said, it follows this Tanna: “Nobody dealing in words only may one deliver to “Him Who exacted retribution”.
[Bava Metzia 4:4.1] MISHNAH: By how much could a tertradrachma be deficient without it being cheating? {NAME} says four assarii, one assarius per denar. {NAME} says four dupondii, a dupondius per denar. {NAME} says eight dupondii, two dupondii per denar.
[Bava Metzia 4:4.2] HALAKHAH: “By how much could a tertradrachma be deficient,” etc. It was stated: “More than that he spends it for its worth, a tetradrachma up to a šeqel , a denar up to a quarter [ šeqel ]. If it is less than this even by an assarius, he may not spend it. If it was circulating as a blank for a tetradrachma or as a šeqel coin, as a blank for a šeqel or as a tetradrachma coin, he only has the shape of the coin. He should give it neither to a person who condemns property nor to a tax assessor since they defraud people, but he drills a hole into it and hangs it on his son’s neck. When has this been said? About tetradrachmas and denars. But gold denars and silver coins one may spend according to their value. Just as one spends it for profane things one may spend it for Second Tithe provided one does not plan it.”
[Bava Metzia 4:5.1] MISHNAH: How much time does one have to return it? In walled cities until one can show it to a banker, in villages until Sabbath eve. If he recognizes it, he should take it back even after twelve months, but he has only a complaint against him. He may use it for Second Tithe without hesitation since it is only miserly’. Cheating is by four oboli, claim is about two oboli, confession is about one peruṭah . There are five peruṭot : Confession is about one peruṭah ; a woman is preliminarily married by one peruṭah ’s worth; one who used one peruṭah ’s worth of Temple property committed larceny; one who finds one peruṭah’ s worth has to make it public; one who robbed another of one peruṭah ’s worth and swore about it, has to return it to him even in Media. There are five fifths: He who eats heave, or heave of the tithe, or heave of the tithe of demay , or ḥallah , or first fruits, adds a fifth. He who redeems his vineyard in the fourth year or his Second Tithe, adds a fifth. He who redeems his own gifts to the Temple, adds a fifth. He who used one peruṭah ’s worth of Temple property, adds a fifth. He who robbed another of one peruṭah ’s worth and swore about it, adds a fifth.
[Bava Metzia 4:5.2] HALAKHAH: “How much time does one have to return it,” etc. {NAME} said, to add it for Jerusalem, he adds it as good coin. If he uses it to redeem in the countryside, he redeems with the underweight coin. But did we not state: “He chooses the better one of the two and exchanges it for them”? Why can he not take the worse [coin] and treat it [as a good one]. He said, there is a difference here because it already was shown to be Second Tithe.
[Bava Metzia 4:5.3] “He may use it for Second Tithe without hesitation since it is only miserly.” {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not add a fifth for any Second Tithe which in itself is not worth a peruṭah. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: One does not add a fifth for any Second Tithe for which the fifth is not worth a peruṭah . A baraita supports the one, a baraita supports the other. As it was stated: “From its tithe,” except what is worth less than a peruṭah . This means, not unless itself is worth a peruṭah. Another Tanna states: “From its tithe, its fifths” except if it is worth less than a peruṭah. This means, not unless the fifth is worth a peruṭah. {NAME} said, our Mishnah follows neither one since we have stated “there are five peruṭot ”, but we did not state “not unless itself is worth a peruṭah ”; we have stated “there are five fifths”, but we did not state “not unless the fifth is worth a peruṭah ”.
[Bava Metzia 4:6.1] MISHNAH: The following are not under the rules of cheating: Slaves, securities, real estate, and Temple property; they are not under the rules of double or quadruple or quintuple restitution. An unpaid trustee does not have to swear, a paid trustee does not pay. {NAME} says, sacrifices which he is obligated to warrant are under the rules of cheating; those for which he is not obligated to warrant are not under the rules of cheating. {NAME} says, also he who sells a Torah scroll, an animal, or a pearl is not under the rules of cheating. They told him, they said only these.
[Bava Metzia 4:6.2] HALAKHAH: “The following are not under the rules of cheating,” etc. It was stated: “{NAME} says, also a Torah scroll, an animal, and a pearl are not under the rules of cheating. A Torah scroll, for its value is infinite. An animal and a pearl need to be paired. They said to him, does not a person want to pair everything?” It was stated: “{NAME} says, a sword, a horse, and a shield are not under the rules of cheating at wartime.”
[Bava Metzia 4:7.1] MISHNAH: Just as there is cheating in trade so there is cheating by words. One should not say to another: how much for this object, if he is not interested in buying. If somebody was a repentant sinner, one should not say to him: remember your earlier deeds. If somebody was the son of a proselyte, one may not say to him: remember the deeds of your forefathers, for it is written: “A sojourner you may neither cheat nor oppress, for you were sojourners in the Land of Egypt.” One does not mix produce, not even new with new; no need to say new with old. In truth they permitted to mix strong wine with weak since it improves it. One does not mix wine lees with wine but one delivers the lees with the wine. If water became mixed with somebody’s wine, he should not sell it in the store unless he declares it, and not to a trader for that one would only use it to trick people; at a place where they usually put water into the wine they may do so. The trader may buy from five threshing floors and put into one chest, wine from five wine presses and put into one barrel, on condition that he not intend to mix. {NAME} says, a store owner should not distribute roasted kernels and nuts to children because he induces them to come to him, but the Sages permit. He should not reduce the price, but the Sages say, may he be remembered as a benefactor. He should not clean the groats following {NAME}, but the Sages permit it. However, they agree that he may not clean the upper layer of the chest since that gives a dishonest impression. One may not put makeup on humans, animals, or vessels.
[Bava Metzia 4:7.2] HALAKHAH: “Just as there is cheating in trade,” etc. “One may not put on make-up.” {NAME} the salt dealer was mollifying his spread. {NAME} said to him, did we not state: “one may not put on make up”? His word implies that there is make-up on food. {NAME} was working with flax. He went to {NAME} and asked him, may I make my work look good? He told him, go and apply all you know. {NAME} was working on those shawls. He came to ask {NAME}, how am I with those shawls?
