He told him, go and apply all you know. {NAME} painted a bathtub. {NAME} stated: What means: “one may not put on make up”? One may not say to him, paint yourself.
[Bava Metzia 5:1.1] MISHNAH: What is biting and what is increase? What is biting, lending a tetradrachma for five denars, two se’ah of wheat for three; because this bites. What is increase? Paying more for produce. How is this? One bought from another wheat for a gold denar the kor at the going rate. Wheat appreciated to thirty denars. He told him, deliver my wheat, for I want to sell it and buy wine with the proceeds. The other said, let your wheat be given to me for thirty denars and you have wine with me, but he has no wine. A creditor may not dwell on the debtor’s premises for free or rent it below the going rate, for this would be interest.
[Bava Metzia 5:1.2] HALAKHAH: “What is biting,” etc. {NAME} said, this is interest which is taken away by the judges. They asked before {NAME}, can interest be taken away by the judges? He said, if it were so, nothing would be left for the great people of the Land of Israel. {NAME} agrees that no document obligates another. {NAME} agrees that if the document exists one subtracts [the interest].
[Bava Metzia 5:1.3] “What is increase?” It was stated: A Jew who lent to another Jew with interest can collect neither principal nor interest, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, he may collect the capital but not the interest. It is written: “Your money you shall not give him by biting.” Not only money by biting and food by increase. From where increase in money and biting in food? The verse says, “do not take from him biting and increase,” it brackets biting with increase and increase with biting. Since biting refers to money, increase also refers to money; since increase refers to food, biting also refers to food.
[Bava Metzia 5:1.4] “One bought wheat from another.” {NAME} said, the rate which is valid for everybody. Less than that, woe to the seller; more than that, woe to the buyer!
[Bava Metzia 5:1.5] “He told him, deliver my wheat, for I want to sell it.” How did he acquire? {NAME} was of the opinion that he had to deliver (to the other person) [by law. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: His money acquired for him by biblical law.]
[Bava Metzia 5:1.6] “A creditor.” A person lent money to another, who let him live in his house, then said, give me the rent for my house. The first one said, give me my money. The case came before {NAME}, who told him to give what was a reasonable rent.
[Bava Metzia 5:1.7] It was stated: “There are things which are interest but are permitted. How is that? A person may buy another’s promissory notes at a discount, or bills of debt at a discount, and need have no compunctions because of interest. Other things are not interest but are forbidden because of circumventing interest. How is that? One received from another a field for ten kor of wheat.… A person said to another, lend me a tetradrachma. He answered, I only have a kor of wheat, take it. If he then turned around and bought it back for 24 it is not interest but forbidden because of circumventing interest.” He might have said to him, you do not have to do this and take your denar but then you have to pay for vessels and porters of the containers.
[Bava Metzia 5:1.8] {NAME} said, he pays him the wages of his foot; {NAME} said, he rents him the dwelling at an inflated price.
[Bava Metzia 5:2.1] MISHNAH: One may increase rental fees but not sale price. How is this? He leased a courtyard saying to him, if [you pay] now it is yours for ten tetradrachmas a year but if paid monthly it is a tetradrachma per month; this is permitted. He sold his field and said to him, if [you pay] now it is yours for 1’000 zuz, but if after the threshing floor it is twelve mina ; this is forbidden. If one sold his field, [the buyer] made a partial payment and [the seller] said, anytime you wish bring the remainder and take yours; this is forbidden. If one lent money on a field and said, if you do not repay me in three years from now, it will be mine, it is his; {NAME} acted thus following the Sages.
[Bava Metzia 5:2.2] HALAKHAH: “One may increase rental fees,” etc. It was stated: “If somebody sells a field to another and stipulates, on condition that I shall work it as a sharecropper, on condition that I shall be part owner, on condition that the tithes shall be mine, on condition that if you sell it, you will sell it only to me, that anytime I want I may pay you back and take it; this is permitted.” “If he owed him money and wrote his field over to him as a sale, any time the seller eats the yield it is permitted; any time the buyer eats the yield, it is forbidden. {NAME} says, in any case it is permitted. {NAME} said, that is what {NAME} did following the Sages. They said to him, is that a proof? The seller was eating the yield.” {NAME}, {NAME}, and {NAME} said, {NAME} learned from the houses of walled cities. As it was stated: The year mentioned in the Torah regarding walled cities is like interest but it is not interest. Another Tanna stated: This is interest but the Torah permitted it. He who said, it is like interest but it is not interest, {NAME}. He who said, this is interest but the Torah permitted it, {NAME}. {NAME} said, when I came from the Diaspora, I found that a case was before {NAME} of “it is like interest but it is not interest.” {NAME} said, they only said that “this is interest but the Torah permitted it.” There, the Torah permitted it, therefore not in any other case. Nevertheless, {NAME} did not consider it, for he said: a house dwells with its inhabitants.
[Bava Metzia 5:3.1] MISHNAH: One does not hire a shop clerk for half the gain; one does not give him money to buy produce for half the gain unless one pays him wages as an unemployed worker. One does not give chickens to breed for half, nor does one hand over calves and foals for care for half the risk unless one pays for his work and food. But one takes in calves and foals for half and grows them until they are one-third grown, and a donkey until it becomes a beast of burden.
[Bava Metzia 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not hire a shop clerk,” etc. A person lent another one denars. He said to him, take two denars as your wages and what they will bring shall be mine and yours.
[Bava Metzia 5:3.3] It was stated: “If somebody gives money to another to buy produce with it for half [the gain]; if that one says, I did not buy, he only has a complaint on him. But if it was known that he bought, the other forcibly extracts from him.”
[Bava Metzia 5:3.4] “If somebody gives money to another to buy produce with it for half the gain and one of them wants to age it, the other may hinder him. But if it was the eve of a Sabbatical year, the other may not hinder him because it was understood that it was bought for that purpose.”
[Bava Metzia 5:3.5] “If somebody gives money to another to buy produce with it for half the gain and one says, here you have a mina for I cannot be bothered with the details, that is forbidden. But if he saw that grain was going up in price, it is permitted.
[Bava Metzia 5:3.6] If somebody gives money to another to buy produce with it for half the gain, the trader is permitted to buy of the same kind. When he sells, he may not sell everything together but sells this first and that later.
[Bava Metzia 5:3.7] “If somebody gives money to another to buy produce with for half the gain, the trader is permitted to buy any kind he wants, but he should not buy a garment or wood.” {NAME} said, this implies that if one who leaves another’s capital unemployed, he only has a complaint on him. If he leaves another’s field unused, he is obligated to serve him. If he leaves another’s ship or store unused, what [is the rule]?
[Bava Metzia 5:3.8] “A person was transporting from a lowprice place to a highprice one. Another said to him, give it to me, I shall pay you what you would charge at place X. If the responsibility is the giver’s, it is forbidden, but the buyer’s is permitted. A person was transporting a package from place to place. Another said to him, give it to me, I shall pay you what you would charge at place X. If the responsibility is the giver’s, it is forbidden, but the buyer’s is permitted. But donkey drivers who receive from householders obtain produce for a highprice place at lowprice rates.” {NAME}: At a place where usually they can go and return the same day. {NAME} said, he becomes his agent. But did one not object to [Rav] Huna: If an agent fell victim to an accident, is he liable? If he was the victim of an accident, he is not liable. Does it not happen that an unpaid trustee accepts to be like a borrower? But did not {NAME} state: Just as he is liable for the entirety, so he is liable for a part! Why does one quote this? There, he would pay a high price, but here he pays at the low rate.
[Bava Metzia 5:4.1] MISHNAH: One hands a cow or a donkey over for care as well as anything which works and eats. At a place where one usually divides the young immediately, one divides; at a place where one usually raises them, they should be raised. {NAME} says, one hands over a calf with its mother, a foal with its mother, and one invests in improving a field and does not worry about interest.
[Bava Metzia 5:4.2] HALAKHAH: “One hands a cow or a donkey over for care,” etc. It was stated: “A person may receive from another an animal on condition to deliver to him one lamb and one shearing per year, a chicken for ten eggs a month. The woman receiving a chicken has to care for the chicks as long as those depend on their mother. One cares for small animals 30 days and for large animals 50 days. {NAME} says, for (large) [small] animals three months because they need special care. After that, he gives the owner his part equally, everything according to local practice.” What means “he gives the owner his part equally”? A person gave to another 100 denars; they produced 20 denars. Each takes half of it; the half of the owner remains with him as capital. Do people do that? But they trade, and at the end they divide it up. “A person receiving an animal for care is responsible for it, for an unclean animal twelve months, for a human 24 months. At a place where work is compensated separately, one pays; for offspring of animals, one pays, everything following local custom.”
[Bava Metzia 5:4.3] “{NAME} says, one hands over, etc., even at a place where one pays additional money for exertion, and one is not worried because of interest.”
[Bava Metzia 5:4.4] “If one accepts an animal for care from another person, how long does he have to care for it? Symmachos says, small asses twelve months, adult donkeys 24 months. If he terminates the care in the middle of the term, one estimates for him; after the term one does not estimate for him, but care for one year is not comparable to two years.”
[Bava Metzia 5:4.5] “If it dies because of gross negligence, he gives everything; not because of gross negligence, he gives half. How is this? It was estimated as one mina and improved and now is worth 200. If it dies because of gross negligence, he gives six gold denars; if not because of gross negligence, he gives 50 zuz .”
[Bava Metzia 5:4.6] “If one accepts an animal for care from another person, it is for no less than twelve months. If he occupied himself with it all through the summer and he says to sell it, one forces him to feed it all through the winter. If he fed it all through the winter and he wants to sell it in the summer, one forces him to occupy himself with it all through the summer.”
[Bava Metzia 5:4.7] It was stated: “{NAME} said, one invests in improving a field and does not worry about interest. How is this? One leased a field for ten kor of wheat and said to him, give me a tetradrachma and I shall give you twelve kor at threshing time, it is permitted.” {NAME} said, because the field may bring an extraordinary yield. {NAME} said, it is as if he increased the rent for the field. What is the difference between them? A store or a ship. According to him who said, because the field may bring an extraordinary yield, one invests in a store or a ship. According to him who said, it is as if he increased the rent for the field, one may not invest in a store or a ship. {NAME} said, they disagree explicitly: {NAME} said, one invests in a store or a ship. {NAME} said, one may not invest in a store or a ship, nor in anything which is not invested in the object itself.
[Bava Metzia 5:5.1] MISHNAH: One may not receive mortmain property from a Jew because that is interest. But one may receive mortmain property from Gentiles, one may borrow from them and lend them on interest, and similarly from a sojourner. A Jew can lend a Gentile’s money on interest by the Gentile’s instruction but not by a Jew’s.
[Bava Metzia 5:5.2] HALAKHAH: “One may not receive mortmain property form a Jew,” etc. “What is mortmain property? He had 100 sheep and told another: They are valued for you at 100 gold [denars]; their young, their milk, and their shearings are yours, but if they die you are liable for them and you pay me a tetradrachma for every one of them at the end of the year. This is forbidden.”
[Bava Metzia 5:5.3] {NAME} asked: There you say that a paid trustee who would be responsible for accidents is forbidden. But here you say that a paid trustee who is responsible for accidents is permitted. Does it not happen that an unpaid trustee agrees to be like a borrower? {NAME} asked: There you say that mortmain belongs to the first, but here you say to the second. {NAME} said, there since the essence belongs to the first, the offspring are counted for the first. But here the essence belongs to the second since the offspring belong to the second.
[Bava Metzia 5:5.4] “One may borrow from them and lend them on interest, and similarly from a sojourner.” Rebbi said, I do not know the definition of “sojourner” quoted in reference to the Hebrew slave. I do not know the definition of “proselyte” quoted in reference to interest.
[Bava Metzia 5:5.5] “A Jew can lend a Gentile’s money on interest by the Gentile’s instruction but not by a Jew’s.” “A Jew had loaned money from a Gentile and wanted to return it when another Jew said to him, give it to me and I shall pay him the same rate as you are paying; this is forbidden. But if he introduced him to the Gentile, it is permitted.” [{NAME} said, only if he let him stand with the Gentile.]
[Bava Metzia 5:5.6] “A Gentile had borrowed money from a Jew and wanted to return it when another Jew said to him, give it to me and I shall pay him the same rate as you are paying; this is permitted. But if he introduced him to the Gentile, it is forbidden.” {NAME} said, only if he let him stand with the Gentile.
[Bava Metzia 5:5.7] “A Jew had borrowed money from a Gentile or a Gentile from a Jew when he converted. Whether the loan was finalized before or after his conversion, he can collect the principal but not the interest. But if a Gentile had borrowed money from a Jew and converted, if the loan was finalized before he converted, he can collect principal and interest; after he converted, he can collect principal but not interest. {NAME} said, he can collect both principal and interest.” {NAME} said, {NAME} reason is that if you exempt him from interest he is turned into an insincere proselyte.
[Bava Metzia 5:5.8] “A person may borrow from his sons or daughters on interest, but he educates them for interest.” Rav said, e. g., I from {NAME} bar {NAME} or {NAME} bar {NAME} from me. “A person may not borrow for a šeqel and lend out for a tetradrachma; but a Gentile may borrow for a šeqel and lend out for a tetradrachma.”
[Bava Metzia 5:5.9] A Jew may borrow from a Gentile, and a Gentile from a Jew, and a Jew can become his guarantor without any worries about interest. If a Jew appointed a Gentile as guardian or steward, it is permitted to borrow from him on interest. But if a Gentile appointed a Jew as guardian or steward, it is prohibited to borrow from him on interest. It is forbidden to borrow on interest a Gentile’s money deposited with a Jew; it is permitted to borrow on interest a Jew’s money deposited with a Gentile. This is the principle: Anything which the Jew has to warrant is forbidden, what the Gentile has to warrant is permitted.
[Bava Metzia 5:6.1] MISHNAH: One does not contract for produce until a rate was established. If he was the first to harvest, he may contract for the stack of sheaves, or the vat of grapes, or the barrel of olives, or for potter’s clay and lime when it was loaded in his oven. One may contract for manure the entire year; {NAME} says, one may not contract for manure unless he has manure on his dungheap, but the Sages permit it. One contracts for wholesale price; {NAME} says, even if one did not contract for wholesale price he may say to him, give me some like that or return my money. A person may lend to his sharecroppers wheat for wheat as seed grain but not as food; but Rebban Gamliel lent his sharecroppers wheat grain; if at high price and the rate went down or at low price and the rate went up, he took from them at the low rate, not because this is practice but because he wanted to be strict with himself.
[Bava Metzia 5:6.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not contract for produce,” etc. May one contract based on Saracens’ rates? {NAME} says, one may contract; {NAME} said, one may not contract. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Would it not be reasonable that {NAME} agree with {NAME} about rates of Saracens of Sepphoris, since that is uninterrupted? {NAME} said, I am wondering about what the rabbis disagree? Whether contracting for produce, or contracting for money, or a loan on produce? {NAME} said, they disagree about a loan, but about (a hostelry) [a contract] everybody agrees that it is forbidden. {NAME} said, they disagree about a contract, but about a loan everybody agrees that it is permitted. In the House of {NAME} they said, one contracts for cattle feed. {NAME} said, also on honeycombs. {NAME} said, in all villages near Tiberias one contracts once the rate was established at Tiberias.
[Bava Metzia 5:6.3] “If he was the first to harvest, he may contract for the stack of sheaves,” etc. Rav said, if one processing stage was missing, one may contract; if several processing stages were missing, one may not contract. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, even if several processing stages were missing, one may contract. But the Mishnah disagrees with Rav: “If he was the first to harvest,” etc.
[Bava Metzia 5:6.4] {NAME} gave a denar to the food merchant and took from him at the cheapest rate of the entire year. Rav did not agree. {NAME} had flax. The donkey drivers wanted to buy from him. He told them, it is not my intention to sell this before Purim. They said to him, sell it to us now at the price which you would sell it for at Purim. He went to ask Rebbi, who told him, it is forbidden. He went out, formulated this in a baraita, and stated the following: “If one was owing money and the other wanted to take from him on the threshing floor, when he told him, credit it to my account by the market rate and I shall provide you all twelve months; this is forbidden for it is not as if the assarion came to his hand.” Rav said, my uncle {NAME} will agree that if they paid him and he immediately acquired, then it is permitted. If he paid beforehand and acquired afterwards, it is permitted; if he acquired earlier and paid afterwards, it is forbidden.
[Bava Metzia 5:6.5] {NAME} invested a denar with a person and told him, what it earns between now and Ḥanukkah is mine [and yours], afterwards I do not have any part with you, whether they earn or lose it is yours. He wanted to give to him after Ḥanukkah but he did not accept. {NAME} had misgivings because of “close to gain and far from loss,” as it was stated: “Close to gain and far from loss is the way of the wicked. Close to loss and far from gain is the way of the just. Close and far equally to both is the way of everybody.” {NAME} invested denars with a person. He wanted to stipulate as did {NAME} but the other did not accept. {NAME} invested 40 denars with a person to buy flax for him. Flax went up in price. He went to ask Rav, who told him to go and collect 40 large kor .
[Bava Metzia 5:6.6] Rebbi wanted to permit the ocean’s absorption but {NAME} did not admit it; some say that {NAME} wanted to permit but Rebbi did not admit it. What is the ocean’s absorption? A person gave 100 denars to another. [He tells him, my yield is 20 denars. If it is less, it is on your account, if it is more, it is for your account. If it is lost, it is of both. {NAME} said,] for instance those who give merchandise to those who depart overseas to the stadia for two or three xestes . That is not interest but property.
[Bava Metzia 5:6.7] {NAME} and {NAME} said the same thing, as we have stated there: “If he had little, he may continuously add to it, but {NAME} says only if he raises or lowers it by three [hand-breadths] or puts it on a rock.”
[Bava Metzia 5:7.1] MISHNAH: A person may not say to another, lend me a kor of wheat and I shall return it to you from the threshing-floor, but he may tell him, lend me until my son comes or until I find the key, but Hillel forbids. Similarly, Hillel said that a woman may not lend a loaf to another unless she fixed its price, for possibly wheat may rise in price and they would be entangled in problems of interest.
[Bava Metzia 5:7.2] HALAKHAH: “A person may not say to another,” etc. It was stated: “A person may not say to another, lend me a kor of wheat and I shall return it to you from the threshing-floor,” therefore for two or three weeks it is permitted; “but Hillel forbids.” {NAME} said, practice follows Hillel.
[Bava Metzia 5:8.1] MISHNAH: A man may say to another, weed with me and I shall be weeding with you, hoe with me and I shall be hoeing with you, but he shall not tell him, weed with me and I shall be hoeing with you, hoe with me and I shall be weeding with you. All the dry season is one, all the wet season is not; one may not say to him, plough with me in the dry season and I shall be ploughing with you in the wet season. {NAME} says, there exists predated and postdated interest. How is this? If one indended to borrow from him and sent him [a gift] saying, so you should lend me; that is predated interest. If one had borrowed and returned the money when he sent him [a gift] saying, that is for your money which was not earning for you while it was with me; that is postdated interest. {NAME} says, there exists verbal interest. One should not say to him, you should know that X came from place Y. The following transgress prohibitions: The creditor, and the debtor, and the guarantor, and the witnesses; the Sages say, also the scribe. They transgress “do not give,” and “do not take from him,” and “do not be a creditor,” and “do not burden him with interest,” and “before a blind man do not put an obstacle; and fear your God, I am the Eternal.”
[Bava Metzia 5:8.2] HALAKHAH: “The following transgress prohibitions,” etc. “{NAME} said, come and see how blind are the eyes of people who lend on interest. If a person calls another one idolator, or adulterer, or murderer, the other will want to destroy him. But this one pays witnesses and a scribe and tells them, come and testify that I negated the roots [of Judaism]. {NAME} said, they negate much more than the roots, for they declare the Torah false and Moses an idiot and say, if Moses had known how much we are earning, he would not have written it. {NAME} says, interest is difficult since even a favor can be interest. If one told him to buy vegetables on the market for him, even though he gave him the money, this is interest. {NAME} said, interest is difficult since even greeting can be interest. If he never greeted him but because he took a loan from him he is quick to greet him, this is interest. In this sense, {NAME} used to say, about a person who has money and does not lend it on interest the verse says: ‘his money he did not lend on interest,’ etc. {NAME} said, we would not know what this tottering was if Salomon had not come and explained: ‘to save those taken to death.’”
[Bava Metzia 6:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody hired tradesmen and they tricked one another, they only have mutual complaints on one another. If somebody hired a donkey driver, or a teamster, carriage carriers, or flute players for a bride or a burial, workers to bring his flax from the soaking pond, or anything in danger of being lost, if they reneged at a place where nobody is available, he hires at their expense or tricks them.
[Bava Metzia 6:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody hired tradesmen,” etc. What means, they tricked one another? Come, work for me for five large [coins]. It turned out it was work for ten large [coins]. You work for me a job which needs ten days. It turned out it was work for five days. What means, [they] tricked the householder? Come, work for me with your colleagues {for ten large [coins]. It turned out it was work for five large [coins]. You work for me a job which needs five days.} It turned out it was work for ten days. “When was this said; if the donkey drivers did not start yet. But if they went and did not find grain, or workers to weed and found the field flooded, he has to pay them for going and coming. But one cannot compare coming loaded with coming empty, or working with being idle, sitting in the shadow with sitting in the sun.” {NAME} hired donkey drivers to bring his flax. They went and found it wet. (Rav) said to him, go and pay them their full fee. He said to them, not that I would be obligated to pay you your fee but I, Ḥiyya, am handing it over to you.
[Bava Metzia 6:1.3] “When was this said? Before they started. But if he accepted to harvest a field for two tetradrachmas, harvested half and left half uncut, a garment to weave for two tetradrachmas, wove half and left half unwoven, one estimates for him. How does one estimate what he did? If what he did was worth six denar, he gives him a sela‘ or he has to finish his work. If it was worth a tetradrachma he gives him a tetradrachma; {NAME} says, one estimates what remains to be done. If what remains to be done was worth three denar, he gives him a šeqel or he has to finish his work. If it was a šeqel, he gives him a šeqel .” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: practice follows {NAME}.
[Bava Metzia 6:1.4] “When was this said? If nothing is in danger to be lost. But if it is in danger to be lost, he hires others on his account or tricks him and tells him, I contracted with you for one tetradrachma, I shall give you two. He takes from one and gives to the other.” {NAME} said, only up to his wages. So far, only up to his wages for that day, or only up to his wages for that hour? “When was this said? At a place where no workers are ready to be hired. But if one saw that donkey drivers approached, or that he was unloading his ship in a port, he may tell him, go and hire yourself one of these; he only has a complaint on him.”
[Bava Metzia 6:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody hired tradesmen and they backed out they are disadvantaged; if the householder backs out, he is disadvantaged. Anyone changing the terms of a contract is disadvantaged; anyone backing out of a contract is disadvantaged.
[Bava Metzia 6:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody hired tradesmen,” etc. Rav said, “because the Children of Israel are My servants,” Jews cannot buy one another. {NAME} said, this was stated about a Hebrew slave. In Rav’s opinion, both a worker and an employer can back out; in {NAME} opinion the worker can back out but not the employer.
[Bava Metzia 6:3.1] MISHNAH: Somebody who rented a donkey to lead it on the mountain but led it in the valley, in the valley but led it on the mountain, even if both ways were ten mil, if it died he has to pay. If he rented a donkey and it developed eye trouble or it was taken to government service, he tells him, here is your property before you. If it died or broke a limb, he has to provide him with another donkey. Somebody rented a donkey to lead it on the mountain but led it in the valley; if it slipped, he is not liable; if it suffered a heat stroke, he is liable. In the valley, but he led it on the mountain; if it slipped, he is liable; if it suffered a heat stroke, he is not liable but if it happened because of the ascent, he is liable. Somebody rented a cow to plough on the mountain but ploughed in the valley, if the plough’s peg broke, he is not liable. In the valley but he ploughed on the mountain, if the plough’s peg broke, he is liable. To thresh legumes but he threshed grain, he is not liable; to thresh grain but he threshed legumes, he is liable, for legumes make [the floor] slippery.
[Bava Metzia 6:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody who rented a donkey,” etc. One understands on the mountain, but he led it in the valley. In the valley, but he led it on the mountain? {NAME} said, if it died because of the air. {NAME} said, if it was bitten by a snake. {NAME} said, it is {NAME} who said, anybody who deviates from the owner’s instructions is called a robber.
[Bava Metzia 6:3.3] “If he rented a donkey and it developed eye trouble,” it was stumbling. “Or it was taken to government service.” There are Tannaїm who state, government service is like death; but there are Tannaїm who state, he tells him, here is your property before you. He who stated, government service is like death, if he can find an accomodation; he who says, he tells him, here is your property before you, if he cannot find an accomodation.
[Bava Metzia 6:3.4] “It was stated, {NAME} says, if it happened on the road, he does not have to provide him with another donkey; if it did not happen on the road, he has to provide him with another donkey.” {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: At a short-cut he does not have to provide him with another donkey; on the king’s highway he has to provide him with another donkey. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If he hired it from here to Lydda and it was taken into government service from here to Lydda, he does not have to provide him with another donkey; from here to Lydda and it was taken into government service from here to Tyre, he has to provide him with another donkey.
[Bava Metzia 6:3.5] “If it died or broke a limb, he has to provide him with a donkey.” {NAME} said, if [the lessee] requested “a donkey” without specifications. But if he requested “this donkey”, [the lessor] may tell him, you wanted this one, bring it before us. {NAME} said, he has to deal with it on place. {NAME} said, if he can get enough from his effort to lease a small donkey, he does not need to provide him with another donkey. Otherwise, he has to provide him with another donkey. {NAME} said, if the cadaver is worth enough to buy a small donkey, he does not need to provide him with another donkey. Otherwise, he has to provide him with another donkey.
[Bava Metzia 6:4.1] MISHNAH: Somebody who rented a donkey to use it to transport wheat but transported barley, grain but transported straw, is liable. How much did one add to the load that he became liable? Symmachos said in the name of {NAME}: one se’ah for a camel, three qab for a donkey.
[Bava Metzia 6:4.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody who rented a donkey,” etc. “How much did one add to the load that he became liable? Symmachos said in the name of {NAME}: one se’ah for a camel, three qab for a donkey, one qab for a porter, and three se‘ah for a cart. But a ship according to its size”.
[Bava Metzia 6:4.3] “If a caravan was attacked by soldiers one computes according to value but not according to persons. If they sent a scout ahead of them, one computes according to persons. One does not deviate from the usage of caravans.”
[Bava Metzia 6:4.4] “If a ship encounters a calamity and one lightens its load, one computes according to weight and value but not according to persons. But one who rents a carriage or a ship from another person computes according to load and persons but not according to value.”
[Bava Metzia 6:4.5] “If a caravan was attacked by soldiers and one of its members managed to save something from their hand, he saved equally [for all]; but if they gave him permission, he saved for himself. If donkey-drivers were attacked by robbers and one of theirs managed to save something from their hand, he saved equally [for all]; but if he stipulated with them in court, he saved for himself. If toll collectors forgave to partners, they forgave equally [for all]; but if they indicated, we forgave to Mr. X, what they forgave, they forgave him.”
[Bava Metzia 6:4.6] “The repentance of publicans and toll collectors is difficult. They should return to those whom they know; [moneys taken] from people they do not know they should use for the public good.”
[Bava Metzia 6:5.1] MISHNAH: All artisans are paid trustees, but in any case where he said, take what is yours and bring money, he becomes an unpaid trustee. Watch over what is mine and I shall watch over what is yours, paid trustee. Watch over what is mine, and he said, put it down before you, an unpaid trustee. He who gives a loan on a pledge is a paid trustee; {NAME} said, if he lent money, he is an unpaid trustee, if produce, a paid trustee. {NAME} said, a person is authorized to rent out a poor person’s pledge to continuously slice off [from the loan] because he is like a person who returns lost property.
[Bava Metzia 6:5.2] HALAKHAH: “All artisans are paid trustees,” etc. This ἀντίχρησις is interest.
[Bava Metzia 6:5.3] {NAME} said, if he said, put it down before me. But if he said, put it down before yourself, he is neither an unapaid nor a paid trustee.
[Bava Metzia 6:5.4] {NAME} said, a person is ready to give something so that he can sell his produce based on a pledge. {NAME} in the name of {NAME} said, a person is ready to give something so that he can sell his produce to somebody who will appease him by a pledge.
[Bava Metzia 6:6.1] MISHNAH: One who transports an amphora from place to place and it breaks shall swear, whether unpaid or paid trustee. {NAME} said, both shall swear, but I am wondering whether any of them be able to swear.
[Bava Metzia 6:6.2] HALAKHAH: “One who transports an amphora from place to place,” etc. It was stated: {NAME} the potter gave his pots to a person who broke them. He confiscated his coat. He went to {NAME}, who told him, go and tell him: “That you should go in the ways of good people.” He went and told him who then returned his coat. He asked him, did he pay your wages? He said, no. He told him, go and tell him: “And to the paths of the just you shall keep.” He went and told him who then paid his wages.
[Bava Metzia 7:1.1] MISHNAH: One who hires workers and tells them to start early and work late, at a place where it is not customary to start early or work late cannot force them to do so. At a place where it is customary to feed them, he has to feed them; to supply a snack, he has to supply it, always following local custom. It happened that {NAME} said to his son, go and hire workers for us. He awarded them food, but when he returned to his father, the latter told him, even if you serve them Solomon’s meal in his time you did not fulfill your pledge since they are descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. But before they start work go and tell them: On condition that your only claim be for bread and legumes. {NAME} said, that was unnecessary; one always follows local custom.
[Bava Metzia 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: “One who hires workers,” etc. {NAME} said, this means that usage supersedes practice. {NAME} said, everywhere the burden of proof is on the claimant except here.
[Bava Metzia 7:1.3] In Tiberias one does not work early or late. In Bet Ma‘on one works early and late. People from Tiberias who climb up to be hired in Bet Ma‘on are hired on the terms of Bet Maon. People from Bet Ma‘on who descend to Tiberias are hired on the terms of Tiberias. But an employer from Tiberias who climbs up to hire workers in Bet Maon can tell them, you should not think that I could not find workers to hire in Tiberias but came up because I heard that you start early and work late. At a place where there is no common usage, {NAME}, {NAME}, {NAME}: It is a stipulation of the court that the early part of morning belong to the workers and the late part of evening to the employer. What is the reason? “You make darkness, there is night; the young lions roar for prey; You give to them, they are collecting; the sun shines, they return; man leaves for his work.” (In the evening) [Fridays] both early rising and late going is at the employer’s expense. How much? That he may fill an amphora of water, fry himself a fish, and light the candle.
[Bava Metzia 7:1.4] In the opinion of {NAME}, a man who goes to another place to preliminarily marry a woman has to stipulate with her and tell her, on condition that you work so and so much and eat for such and such costs.
[Bava Metzia 7:2.1] MISHNAH: The following eat by Torah law: He who works on produce connected to the ground at the completion of work, or separated from the ground before the completion of work, only things grown from the earth. But the following may not eat: He who works on produce connected to the ground before the completion of work, or separated from the ground after the completion of work, or things not grown from the earth. If he was working with his hand but not with his feet, with his feet but not with his hands, even with his shoulder, he may eat. {NAME} says, only if he works with hands and feet.
[Bava Metzia 7:2.2] HALAKHAH: “The following eat by Torah law,” etc. {NAME} said, “if you come into your neighbor’s vineyard.” Could anybody think that he would eat wood or stones? Why does the verse say “grapes”? That he may not skin figs or suck grapes.
[Bava Metzia 7:2.3] “If he was working with his hand but not with his feet.” {NAME} said, it is written: “If you come into your neighbor’s standing grain,” etc. With his hands, binding. With his feet, he compresses. Even with his shoulder, he carries.
[Bava Metzia 7:2.4] “{NAME} says, only if he works with hands and feet; this excludes him who works with his hands but not with his feet, with his feet but not with his hands.”
[Bava Metzia 7:2.5] “{NAME} says, threshing. Since threshing is special in that it refers to something grown from the earth, this excludes the one who milks, makes cheese with rennet or with mold, which is not something grown from the earth. Since threshing is special in that it refers to something not completely processed; this excludes wine after it was fermented, [olive oil] after it descended into the vat, one who isolates dates or separates dried figs, done after complete processing. Since threshing comes before the obligation of tithes, this excludes him who kneads dough, separates into cakes, or bakes, which comes after it became obligated for tithes.”
[Bava Metzia 7:3.1] MISHNAH: If one was working on figs he may not eat grapes, on grapes he may not eat figs; but he may restrain himself until he reaches the place of the good ones and eat there. In all cases they only referred to the time of finishing work, but because of returning lost property to its owner they said that workers may eat when they go from row to row, and when they return from the wine press, and a donkey while offloading.
[Bava Metzia 7:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If one was working on figs,” etc. {NAME} said, it is written: “If you come into your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat grapes to satisfy yourself.” What else is there in the vineyard to eat but grapes? To teach you that if he was working on grapes he may not eat figs.
[Bava Metzia 7:4.1] MISHNAH: A worker may eat zucchini even for a denar’s worth, or dates even for a denar’s worth. {NAME} Ḥasma said, a worker may not eat more than his wages and the Sages permit it, but one instructs a man not to be voracious lest he close the door before him. A person may contract for himself, for his adult son or daughter, for his adult male and female slaves, for his wife, because they have understanding. But he may not contract for his underage son or daughter, nor for his underage male and female slaves, nor for his animal, because they have no understanding.
[Bava Metzia 7:4.2] HALAKHAH: “A worker may eat zucchini even for a denar’s worth,” etc. {NAME} says in the name of {NAME}, this means that a worker may eat more than his [daily] wages. But some say, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This means that a worker may eat the first or the last bunch of grapes.
[Bava Metzia 7:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody hires workers to work with him in his fourth-year plantation, they may not eat. If he did not inform them, he has to redeem it and feed them. If his fig cakes were dislodged or his amphoras opened, they may not eat. If he did not inform them, he has to tithe and feed them.
[Bava Metzia 7:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody hires workers to work,” etc. Anything which is of a kind apt to be under the rules of tithing but another prohibition caused it [to be forbidden to eat], if one hired [a worker] without mentioning it, he has to redeem and feed, tithe and feed. If [the worker] contracted for it, he eats. But if it is of a kind exempt from the rules of tithing but another prohibition caused it [to be forbidden to eat], if one hired [a worker] without mentioning it, that one cannot eat; if he contracted for it, he eats.
[Bava Metzia 7:6.1] MISHNAH: Watchmen of produce eat because of local practice but not from the Torah. There are four kinds of keepers: The unpaid trustee and the borrower, the paid keeper and the renter. The unpaid trustee swears about everything, the borrower pays for everything. The paid keeper and the renter swear about the broken, the kidnapped, and the dead but pay for the lost and the stolen.
[Bava Metzia 7:6.2] HALAKHAH: “Watchmen of produce eat because of local practice,” etc. {NAME} said, the Mishnah refers to watchmen of produce. But watchmen of vegetable gardens and orchards eat by Torah law. {NAME} said, the Mishnah refers to watchmen of vegetable gardens and orchards. But watchmen of produce eat neither by Torah law nor by local practice. {NAME} stated in support of {NAME}: “The Cohen shall be impure until evening,” to include watchmen, that they make their garments impure.
[Bava Metzia 7:7.1] MISHNAH: One wolf is not an unavoidable accident, two wolves are. {NAME} says, in times when wolves appear in packs, even a single wolf is an unavoidable accident. Two dogs are not an unavoidable accident. Yaddua the Babylonian says in the name of {NAME}: From the same direction it is not an unavoidable accident; from two different directions it is an unavoidable accident Robbers are an unavoidable accident. A lion, and a bear, and a leopard, and a panther, and a snake are unavoidable accidents. When? If they came by themselves. But if he led [the flock] to a place of troops of wild animals or robbers, these are not unavoidable accidents. If [an animal] dies a natural death it is an unavoidable accident. If he tortured it and it died, it is not an unavoidable accident. If it climbed to the top of a cliff and fell, it is an unavoidable accident. If he led it onto the top of a cliff and it fell, it is not an unavoidable accident. The unpaid keeper may stipulate that he be free from swearing, the borrower that he not be liable to pay, the paid keeper and the renter that they not be liable to swear or to pay. The stipulation of anybody who stipulates against what is written in the Torah is invalid. Any stipulation which follows a prior action is invalid. But any stipulation which it is possible to fulfill at the end and he stipulated it at the start is valid.
[Bava Metzia 7:7.2] HALAKHAH: “One wolf is not an unavoidable accident,” etc. “The stipulation of anybody who stipulates against what is written in the Torah,” etc. It was stated: “The stipulation of anybody who stipulates against what is written in the Torah, monetary stipulations are valid, nonmonetary stipulations are invalid.” How is this? If one said to a woman: be preliminarily married to me on condition that you have no claim on me for sustenance, clothing, and marital relations, she is preliminarily married [and his stipulation is valid. “On condition] that it I die you shall not be obligated for levirate marriage, she is preliminarily married but his stipulation is invalid.”
[Bava Metzia 7:7.3] “This is the principle enunciated by {NAME}: Anything which is impossible to keep but he stipulated for her only to put her off. Whether we put it in writing or said it orally, everything valid orally is valid when written”. “And Kefar Othnay belongs to Galilee, Antipatris to Judea; the places in between are interpreted stringently.”
[Bava Metzia 8:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody borrowed a cow and asked its owner [to work with him], or borrowed a cow and paid its owner [to work with him], or asked or paid its owner [to work with him] and then borrowed the cow: if it died he is not liable since it was said: “if its owner was with it he does not pay.” But if he borrowed the cow and afterwards asked or paid its owner [to work with him] and it died he is liable since it was said: “if its owner was not with it, certainly he shall pay.”
[Bava Metzia 8:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody borrowed a cow,” etc. {NAME} said, from the meaning of what is said, “certainly he shall pay”; would we not have known that if its owner was with it he does not pay? Why does the verse say, “if its owner was not with it, certainly he shall pay”? But since he borrowed the cow and did not ask its owner at the same time, even if the latter was ploughing with it when it died, he is liable.
[Bava Metzia 8:1.3] “But if he borrowed the cow and afterwards asked or paid its owner [to work with him] and it died he is liable.” {NAME} said, from the meaning of what is said, “if its owner was not with it, certainly he shall pay,” would I not have known that if its owner was not with it, certainly he shall pay? Why does the verse say, “if its owner was with it he does not pay”? But since he borrowed the cow and did ask its owner at the same time, even if the latter was ploughing at another place when it died, he is not liable.
[Bava Metzia 8:2.1] MISHNAH: Somebody borrowed a cow; he borrowed it for half a day and leased it for half a day, or borrowed it for one day and leased it for the next, or borrowed for one and leased for one. The lessee says, the borrowed one died, or it died on the day it was borrowed, or it died during the time it was borrowed, and the other one says “I do not know”, he is liable. The lessor says, the leased one died, or it died on the day it was leased, or it died during the time it was leased, and the other one says “I do not know”, he is not liable. One says the borrowed and the other one says the leased; let the lessee swear that the leased one died. If both say “I do not know” they shall split.
[Bava Metzia 8:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody borrowed a cow,” etc. What is the status of the night in between? Some say, usually cows rest at their owners’, and this one, because it is leased to him, stays overnight and is as if loaned to him; he is liable. But some say, usually cows do not rest at their owners’, and this one is as if being leased to him; he is not liable.
[Bava Metzia 8:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody borrowed a cow and [the lender] sent it through his son, or his slave, or his agent, or through the borrower’s son, or slave, or agent, and it died, he is not liable. If the borrower said, send it to me through my son, or slave, or agent, or through your son, or slave, or agent, or if the lender said, I am going to send it to you through my son, or slave, or agent, or through your son, or slave, or agent, and the borrower said: send! If it died, he is liable. The same holds when he returns it.
[Bava Metzia 8:3.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: ‘Lend me your cow for ten days and you shall be lent to me the first five days.’ If it died, was it subject to the first days’ servitude? It died subject to the later days’ servitude. ‘Lend me your cow for ten days and you shall be lent to me the first of these.’ If it died during the later days, was it subject to the first days’ servitude? it died subject to the later days’ servitude. ‘Lend me your cow after ten days.’ The other one said, ‘take it now.’ If it died, was it subject to the first days’ servitude? It died subject to the later days’ servitude.
[Bava Metzia 8:3.3] Lend me your cow and I shall respond to your request; lend me your cow and come work with me; lend me your axe and come weed with me; lend me your plate and come eat with me. If he borrowed it from the superintendent of cisterns, the steward, or the administrator and it died, it is as if the owners were with it.
[Bava Metzia 8:4.1] MISHNAH: Somebody exchanged a cow for a donkey and it gave birth, or he sold his slave girl and she gave birth. If one said, [it happened] before I sold, the other said, after I bought, they shall split. If he had two slaves, one adult and one young, or two fields, one large and one small. The buyer says, I bought the large one, and the seller says, I do not know: he acquired the large one. The seller says, I sold the small and the other party says, I do not know: he has only the small one. If one says the large one and the other says the small, let the seller swear that he sold the small one. If both say, I do not know, they shall split.
[Bava Metzia 8:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If he said to him, lend me,” etc. “Somebody exchanged a cow,” etc. {NAME} said, this contradicts Symmachos who says that in all cases of doubt one splits evenly. {NAME} said, explain it if both of them say, I am certain. {NAME} explained, if both of them say, I am certain, that is what {NAME} refered to when he said, this contradicts Symmachos’s words.
[Bava Metzia 8:5.1] MISHNAH: Somebody sold his olive trees for their wood. If they produced less than a quartarius [of oil] per se‘ah , it belongs to the owner of the olive trees. A quartarius [of oil] per se‘ah, one says, my olive trees grew [the olives], the other says, my land grew them: they shall split evenly. If a river flooded his olive trees and carried them to another’s field; one says, my olive trees grew them, the other says, my land grew them: they shall split evenly.
[Bava Metzia 8:5.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody sold his olive trees for their wood,” etc. {NAME} asked, what is their status if they become moist?
[Bava Metzia 8:5.3] {NAME} said, if it swept them away in their earth. {NAME} said, the years of ‘orlah are their dispute.
[Bava Metzia 8:6.1] MISHNAH: He who rents a dwelling to another person cannot remove him from there during the rainy season, from Tabernacles to Passover, but in the dry season on thirty days’ notice. But in walled cities, whether in the dry or the rainy season, on twelve months’ notice. For a store, whether in a walled city or in a village, twelve months. {NAME} said, a baker’s or dyer’s store, three years.
[Bava Metzia 8:6.2] HALAKHAH: “He who leases a dwelling to another person,” etc. It was stated: “Anywhere they mention 30 days or twelve months it does not mean that one has to dwell there 30 days or twelve months but notice must be given before 30 days or twelve months. An oil press, the entire period it is in use. A wine press, the entire period it is in use. A potter’s atelier no less than twelve months. {NAME} said, when has this been said? For those who work with black earth. But one who works with white earth collects his stock and leaves.”
[Bava Metzia 8:7.1] MISHNAH: He who leases a dwelling to another person: the lessee must provide the door, the key-bolt and the door handle and everything that requires expert installation. But anything that does not require experts, the lessor does it. Manure belongs to the lessee; the lessor only has what comes from the oven and the cooking stove.
[Bava Metzia 8:7.2] HALAKHAH: “He who leases a dwelling to another person,” etc. {NAME} instructed that a mezuzah requires expert installation.
[Bava Metzia 8:8.1] MISHNAH: He who leases a dwelling to another person by the year, if the year was intercalated, it was intercalated for the lessor. If he leased by the month, if the year was intercalated it was intercalated for the lessee. It happened in Sepphoris that a person leased a bathhouse from another for twelve gold denars per year, one gold denar per month. The case came before {NAME} and {NAME} who said, they should split the intercalated month.
[Bava Metzia 8:8.2] HALAKHAH: “He who leases a dwelling to another person,” etc. Why? If he came to claim at the end of the month, can he collect everything? And if he came to him at the beginning of the month, he can tell him, get out. {NAME} says, the Mishnah is so: If he came to claim in the middle of the month. Rav said, a rule to collect. {NAME} said, this clearly does not follow the rule of {NAME} who said, the later language supersedes the earlier one.
[Bava Metzia 8:9.1] MISHNAH: He who leases a dwelling to another person and it collapsed has to provide him with a dwelling. If it was small he may not make it large, large he may not make it small. One room he shall not make into two, two he may not make into one. He may not reduce the number of windows nor add to them except with the agreement of both parties.
[Bava Metzia 8:9.2] HALAKHAH: “He who leases a dwelling to another person,” etc. {NAME} said, if he puts him into it. {NAME} said, if he told him, a dwelling like this I shall lease to you. But if a person leasing a house wants to sell it? {NAME} said, nobody thinks that this one should die of hunger. {NAME} and {NAME} both say, while certainly it is acquired by him, he has to tell him, let him dwell there until the time of his recall. There came a case before {NAME} and he did not accept this. Does he disagree? They said, his daughter was given as a pledge to a Roman [and he did not have the wherewhithal to redeem her and {NAME} instructed to sell;] therefore he instructed following {NAME}.
[Bava Metzia 9:1.1] MISHNAH: One who contracts with another for a field, at a place where one usually cuts, he has to cut, to uproot, he has to uproot, to plough after harvest, he has to plough, everything according to local usage. Just as they divide the grain, so they divide straw and chaff. Just as they divide the wine, so they divide the vine tendrils and the props; they both provide the props together.
[Bava Metzia 9:1.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field” etc. If he uprooted at a place where one usually cuts, he may tell him: “you make it sterile.” Where one uproots and he cuts, one tells him, go out and make it clean.
[Bava Metzia 9:1.3] It was stated: “One who contracts with another for a field has to harvest, bind into sheaves, thresh, winnow, and grade. The digger, the measurer, the steward, the town watchmen, and the administrator take their wages from the community. The builder of furnaces, the maker of seals, and the scribe, if hired by the tenant they take from the tenant; if hired by the landlord they take from the landlord. One does not change local usage.”
[Bava Metzia 9:2.1] MISHNAH: One who contracts with another for a field, if it is an irrigated field or an orchard and the source dried up or the orchard was cut down, he may not deduct from his leasing fee. If he said, this irrigated field or this orchard shall be leased to me and the source dried up or the orchard was cut down, he may deduct from his leasing fee.
[Bava Metzia 9:2.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. {NAME} said, if the well dried up completely. But if it was two storeys deep and now it is three storeys deep, one may tell him: exert yourself and it will be sufficient.
[Bava Metzia 9:2.3] “The orchard was cut down.” {NAME} said, if the entire orchard was cut down. But if there remained ten trees standing per bet se’ah he may tell him: At the beginning they were sickly and were not bearing much. But now they are sparse and will be productive.
[Bava Metzia 9:3.1] MISHNAH: One contracts with another for a field; if after he received it he lets it lie fallow one estimates how much it could yield and gives to him, for so he writes to him: If I let it lie fallow or do not work it, I shall pay as if well-worked.
[Bava Metzia 9:3.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. {NAME} said, this implies that if one lets another’s money lie idle, the other only has a complaint against him. If one lets another’s field lie idly, he has to compensate him adequately. If one lets another’s ship or store lie idly, what is the rule?
[Bava Metzia 9:4.1] MISHNAH: One who contracts with another for a field, did not want to weed, and told him, what do you care since I am paying you rent? One does not listen to him since he may tell him, tomorrow you leave it and I’ll have it overgrown with grasses. One who contracts with another for a field and it did not produce. If it is enough to make a pile, he has to work on it. {NAME} said, what is the definition of a pile? But if it is enough for spreading.
[Bava Metzia 9:4.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. How much is “enough to make a pile”? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: that the winnowing shovel can stand upright in it. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: only that its handle be on top. {NAME} said: in addition to his expenses. {NAME} said: in addition to the expenses of both of them. {NAME} said: “for spreading”, to recover the seed grain which was spread on it.
[Bava Metzia 9:5.1] MISHNAH: One who contracts with another for a field, but it was eaten by locusts or scorched. If it was a countrywide calamity, he reduces his leasing fee; if it was not a countrywide calamity, he does not reduce his leasing fee. {NAME} says, if he contracted for a sum of money in no case does he deduct from the leasing fee.
[Bava Metzia 9:5.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. {NAME} said, if the entire area in that direction was scorched. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. But only if it was sown. [But if he did not sow], the other can tell him, if you had sown it would have produced a lot. Think of it, if there were other fields [which were not hit]? He may tell him, the Holy One, praise to Him, is forbearing with the evildoers. If there were other fields which were damaged? He may tell him, so far I was liable in the case; from now on I am no longer liable.
[Bava Metzia 9:6.1] MISHNAH: One who contracts with another for a field, for ten kor of wheat per year. If it was damaged, he delivers from it. If the wheat turned out to be of high quality, he may not tell him: I am buying wheat in the market, but he delivers from the yield.
[Bava Metzia 9:6.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. It was stated: “One who contracts with another for a field tithes and delivers to him, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, both for the same kind and for the same field he lifts heave and delivers to him. But from another field or another kind he tithes and delivers to him. {NAME} says, only for the same kind and for the same field he lifts heave and delivers to him. But from another field or another kind he does (not) tithe and deliver to him.”
[Bava Metzia 9:7.1] MISHNAH: One who contracts with another for a field to sow barley shall not sow wheat; for wheat he may sow barley. {NAME} prohibits. For legumes he may not sow grain; for grain he may sow legumes. {NAME} prohibits.
[Bava Metzia 9:7.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. One understands that for barley he may not sow wheat; for wheat, may he not sow barley? It follows {NAME} or is the opinion of everybody at a place where the yield of barley is not twice that of wheat. But at a place where barley produces twice as much as wheat he may sow barley.
[Bava Metzia 9:8.1] MISHNAH: One who contracts with another for a field for a few years may not sow flax and does not have sycamore logs. If he contracted for seven years, he may sow flax and does have sycamore logs.
[Bava Metzia 9:8.2] HALAKHAH: “One who contracts with another for a field,” etc. One understands that for wheat he may not sow flax. For flax may he not sow wheat? Flax damages the soil for three years and you say so? {NAME}, {NAME}, explained before {NAME}: It is better to sow flax after flax but not barley after barley.
[Bava Metzia 9:9.1] MISHNAH: If one who contracts with another for a field for a Sabbatical cycle at 700 denars, the Sabbatical year is included. If he contracted for seven years at 700 denars, the Sabbatical is not included.
[Bava Metzia 9:9.2] HALAKHAH: “If one contracts with another for a field,” etc. It was stated: “One contracts with another for a field; he sowed it a first year and it did not grow; one forces him to sow a second year. If the second time it did not grow, one cannot force him to sow a third year.” {NAME} said, that is, a field which had not been checked out. But if it had been checked out, one can force him to sow a third year.
[Bava Metzia 9:10.1] MISHNAH: A person hired for the day collects the entire night; a person hired for the night collects the entire day. A person hired for hours collects the entire day and the entire night. A person hired for a week, a month, a year, or a Sabbatical period, if he finishes during daytime, he collects the entire day; if he finishes at nighttime, he collects the entire night and the following day.
[Bava Metzia 9:10.2] HALAKHAH: “A person hired for the day collects the entire night,” etc. {NAME} said, the next morning he is in violation on his behalf because of “ “you must pay his wages on his day”. {NAME} said, is there one day when you can say that he transgresses on all these counts? If it is to refer to the verses, explain it about a person hired by the hour during day and night who can collect the entire day and the entire night. And it was stated thus: “A person hired by the hour during the day collects the entire day; in the night he collects the entire night. A person hired by the hour during day and night collects the entire night and the entire day.”
[Bava Metzia 9:11.1] MISHNAH: Wages of a human, as well as wages for an animal, as well as wages for implements are subsumed under “you must pay his wages on his day” and “one may not withhold a hireling’s wages until the morning”. When? If he claimed it. If he did not claim it, one does not transgress. If one gave him a draft on a storekeeper or a banker, he does not transgress. In his time the hireling swears and takes; after his time he does not swear and take. But if there are witnesses that he did claim, he swears and takes. The resident proselyte is protected by “you must pay his wages on his day” but not by “one may not withhold a hireling’s wages until the morning”.
[Bava Metzia 9:11.2] HALAKHAH: “Wages of a human,” etc. It is written: “Do not oppress the poor and needy of your brothers,” this refers to Israel. “Your proselytes,” this refers to the just proselytes. “In your land,” to add animals and slaves. “In your gates,” to add movables.
[Bava Metzia 9:11.3] It was stated: I could think that if one gave him a draft on a storekeeper or a banker, he would transgress about him. He does not transgress about him but they transgress about him. When? If he claimed it. If he did not claim it, one does not transgress.
[Bava Metzia 9:11.4] “In his time the hireling swears and takes.” {NAME} said, if he said: I paid. But if he said, I shall pay tomorrow: if then he said, I paid, he cannot be believed. {NAME} said, even the next day, if he said, I paid, he is believed.
[Bava Metzia 9:11.5] “The resident proselyte is protected by ‘you must pay his wages on his day’ ”, etc. It is written: “Do not oppress your neighbor,” excluding the resident proselyte.
[Bava Metzia 9:12.1] MISHNAH: A person who lends to another may take a pledge from him only in court. He may not enter his house to take his pledge, as it is said: “You have to stand outside.” If he had two vessels, he takes one and returns one. He returns the pillow for the night and the plough for the day. If he dies, he does not return it to his heirs. {NAME} says, even to himself he returns it only up to 30 days; after thirty days he sells it in court
[Bava Metzia 9:12.2] HALAKHAH: It is written about torts that the collection be from the best quality, as it is said: “his best field, etc.” And it is written about a loan that the collection be from average quality, as it is said: “and the man to whom you are creditor, etc.” They inferred real estate from pledges. Similarly, should not pledges be inferred from real estate? {NAME} explained: It is a word of the Torah that the court’s bailiff enter and collect from average quality. For if the creditor enter, he would bring out the best. And if the debtor enter, he would bring out the worst. But the court’s bailiff enters and collects from average quality. {NAME} stated: It is a word of the Torah that the debtor enter, as it is said: “and the man to whom you are creditor etc.” {NAME} said, it was stated there: “to seize as pledge”, by the court. Outside the court, from where? The verse says, “if to seize as pledge you seize as pledge.” If he took the pledge without authorization, he transgresses all these verses. {NAME} said, he caused himself to transgress all these verses.
[Bava Metzia 9:12.3] If he took a pledge and then returned it, by law he can collect from the property mortgaged to him. “But if he returns it, why does he take a pledge? Rebbi explained, for maybe there will be a Sabbatical year and annul [the debt]. Or maybe that one will die and leave the movables in the heir’s hand.”
[Bava Metzia 9:12.4] It was stated: He takes a day garment as pledge during the night and a night garment during the day. He returns a day garment during the day and a night garment during the night. Pillow and bed sheet which are used as cover during the night he may take as pledge during the day and return for the night. An axe and a plough which usually are used for work during the day he may take as pledge during the night and return for the day. {NAME} said: Sometimes one explains the verse “the sun shall not come onto it,” as “the sun shall not rise upon it”, but sometimes one explains as “the sun shall not set upon it” since it is written “returning you shall return the pledge to him when the sun comes,” at sunrise, “until the going of the sun return it to him,” until sundown.
[Bava Metzia 9:13.1] MISHNAH: One may not take a pledge from a widow, whether poor or rich, since it was said: “And do not take a widow’s garment for a pledge.” One who takes a flour mill as pledge transgresses a prohibition and is guilty for two vessels, as it was said: “Do not take upper and lower millstones as pledge.” They said, not only upper and lower millstones but everything used to make food, as it was said: “For he takes a living person for a pledge.”
[Bava Metzia 9:13.2] HALAKHAH: “One may not take a pledge from a widow, whether poor or rich,” etc. It was stated: “One may not take a pledge from a widow, whether poor or rich, since it was said: ‘And do not take a widow’s garment for a pledge’, whether poor or rich, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, from a poor one he cannot take any pledge at all, from a rich one he may take a pledge but does not return it since if he came to her he would ruin her reputation.”
[Bava Metzia 9:13.3] One who takes a pair of barber’s scissors transgresses for the two blades separately. If he took only one component, he transgresses for this one [only]. One who takes a yoke of cows transgresses for each one separately. If he took only one, he transgresses for this one only.
[Bava Metzia 10:1.1] MISHNAH: If the ground floor and the upper floor belonging to two different persons collapse, they divide wood, stones, and dust between themselves. One takes into consideration which stones were at risk to break. If one of them recognized his stones, he takes them, and they are debited to his account.
[Bava Metzia 10:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If the ground floor and the upper floor belonging to two different persons collapse,” etc. It was stated: If they were blackened like an oven, the upper ones were apt to break. If they fell to the outside, the lower ones were apt to break.
[Bava Metzia 10:1.3] “If one of them recognized his stones, he takes them, and they are debited to his account.” {NAME} said, this means that the hand rules on one side. There, we have stated: “A hundred ṭevel in a hundred profane, he removes 101. A hundred ṭevel in a hundred tithe, he removes 101.” {NAME} said, if you say that he takes 100, I would say that only profane came to his hand and the other remains ṭevel . So he takes 101 in order to separate heave and heave of the tithe from the ṭevel.
[Bava Metzia 10:1.4] Those bearing columns. {NAME}: He tells the bottom dweller, you are obliged to support me. {NAME}: He tells the dweller in the upper floor, the builders say that both have to build the foundations. The following supports the builders: “If his ruined building was close to the wall of his neighbor’s courtyard, he should not tell him: I am contributing to the foundations of your wall where it comes up, but he has to contribute to the foundations from the bottom and up. If it was built on top of ditches or caves, he is not obligated for anything.” {NAME} said, explain it, for example those inhabitants of Bet Shean where the bottom dweller cannot build unless the builder of the upper floor builds.
[Bava Metzia 10:2.1] MISHNAH: The ground floor and the upper floor belong to two different persons; if the upper floor sprang a leak and the owner of the ground floor does not want to fix it, the owner of the upper floor descends and dwells below until he fixes the upper floor for him. {NAME} says, the lower one gives the roofing and the upper one the roof covering.
[Bava Metzia 10:2.2] HALAKHAH: “The ground floor and the upper floor belong to two different persons,” etc. It was stated: “If it sprang a leak above the oven, he descends. If it sprang a leak above the fireplace, he descends.” But he may tell him, make yourself a ladder so you do not have to ascend and descend through my dwelling.
[Bava Metzia 10:2.3] “{NAME} says, the lower one contributes the roofing and the upper one the roof covering,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}:: The bottom dweller contributes the logs and the planks; the dweller on the upper floor contributes the roof covering. Which kind of roof covering? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: heavy roof covering. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: medium roof covering, since they only spoke about rinsing cups. But if he wanted to wash clothing, also {NAME} in the name of {NAME} will agree that the roof covering has to be heavy. {NAME} instructed those of Sepphoris that both of them should contribute the logs and the plates since they expect to bring up there their wine and their produce.
[Bava Metzia 10:3.1] MISHNAH: If the ground floor and the upper floor belonging to two different persons collapse, and the owner of the upper floor suggests to the owner of the ground floor to rebuild but himself refuses to build, then the owner of the upper floor rebuilds the ground floor and dwells in it until he pays his expenses. {NAME} says, but he who dwells in another person’s [place] would have to pay him rent; so the owner of the (ground) floor builds ground and upper floors and makes the roof over the upper floor but dwells on the ground floor until he pays his expenses.
[Bava Metzia 10:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If the ground floor and the upper floor,” etc. But if the owner of the ground floor wants to build and the owner of the upper floor does not, may he tell him: seal it? Let us hear from the following: “If his collapsed building was next to another’s collapsed building, and he rebuilt without permission, he computes his actual expenses and he has to pay him all his expenses.” This implies that he cannot tell him, seal it on the side. Just as he cannot tell him, seal it on the side, so he cannot tell him, seal it on top.
[Bava Metzia 10:4.1] MISHNAH: And so an olive press built into a rock with a vegetable garden on its top: If it caved in, the garden’s owner may sow on the bottom until he build cupolas on his olive press. If a wall or a tree fell into the public domain and caused damage, he is not liable to pay. If he was given an order to tear down the wall or cut down the tree; within the term he is not liable, after the term he is liable.
[Bava Metzia 10:4.2] HALAKHAH: “And so an olive press,” until “if a wall or a tree,” etc. {NAME} said: It happened that a vine was growing on another person’s peach tree, and the peach tree withered. The case came before {NAME} who told him, go and provide him with a peach tree. {NAME} told him: Is this not a Mishnah? “And so an olive press built into a rock and another’s vegetable garden is on its top”? Do we not understand that one does not force? But {NAME} stated that one forces! We may say that they did not disagree. He who says that one forces, if he is there. But he who says that one does not force, if he is absent.
[Bava Metzia 10:4.3] “If he was given an order to cut down.” What is the time limit? {NAME} said, 30 days.
[Bava Metzia 10:5.1] MISHNAH: Somebody’s wall bordering on another’s vegetable garden collapsed. That one told him, remove your stones; if he said, they are yours, one does not listen to him. If after the other had accepted, he told him: here are your expenses and I shall take what is mine, one does not listen to him. Somebody hired a worker to work on straw and chaff. When he said to him, pay me my wages, he answered, take what you worked on as your wages, one does not listen to him. If after the other had accepted, he told him: here are your wages and I shall take what is mine, one does not listen to him. If somebody brought his manure into the public domain, he who brings, brings, and he who uses it to manure, manures. One does not soak loam in the public domain nor does one form bricks; one kneads loam in the public domain but not bricks. If somebody builds in the public domain and somebody brings stones; he who brings, brings, and he who builds, builds; but if he caused damage, he pays for what he damaged. {NAME} says, also he has to prepare his work 30 days in advance.
[Bava Metzia 10:5.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody who brought his manure,” etc. It was stated: ”A person may unload his manure at his courtyard door in the public domain in order immediately to remove it. But it is forbidden to leave it there. If another person was injured by it, he is liable. {NAME} says, at the time of carrying out manure a person may unload his manure at his courtyard door in the public domain for it to be broken down by the feet of people and animals for 30 days, for on this condition did Joshua distribute the Land to Israel.” “A person may unload his dust at his courtyard door in the public domain in order immediately to mix it with water and to bring it to the row of stones; it is forbidden to leave it there. If another person was injured by it, he is liable. He should not knead on one side [and build on the other] but on the side where he is building.” “A person may unload his stones at his courtyard door in the public domain in order immediately to remove them; it is forbidden to leave them there. If another person was injured by them, he is liable. If the quarryman delivered to the camel driver, the camel driver is liable. The camel driver to the stone-mason, the stone-mason is liable. The stone-mason to the porter, the porter is liable. It it was brought up to scaffolding, it was wobbly there and fell, the master-mason is liable. If the (stone-mason) [quarryman] handed it to the (porter) [stone mason] and somebody was injured either by splinters or the stone, the stone-mason is liable. The stone-mason to the porter and he was injured by a splinter, the stone-mason is liable. By the stone, the porter is liable. If it was delivered, settled in the row, and fell, he is not liable.”
[Bava Metzia 10:6.1] MISHNAH: Two vegetable gardens, one on top of the other and vegetables growing between them. {NAME} says, it is the upper’s. {NAME} says, it is the lower’s. Said {NAME}: If the upper’s owner wanted to remove his earth, there would be no vegetables. Said {NAME}: If the lower’s wanted to fill up his vegetable garden with earth, there would be no vegetables. Said {NAME}: Since both of them may object to one another one looks from where these vegetables grow. {NAME} says, any which the upper’s may take by stretching out his hand are his; the remainder is the lower’s.
[Bava Metzia 10:6.2] HALAKHAH: “Two vegetable gardens,” etc. What shall one do? Ephraim in the name of {NAME} said, they shall split. In the House of {NAME} they say, up to ten handbreadths. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Only he shall not force himself.
[Bava Metzia 10:6.3] A wall between two partitions which was breached. Rav and {NAME}, one said, half belongs to one party, the other half to the other party. The other said, both own it entirely. What is the difference between them? If one found a find. For him who said that half belongs to one party, the other half to the other party, if it was on one side it belongs to this party, one the other side it belongs to the other party. For him who said that both own it entirely, the finder acquired it.
