[Bava Batra 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Condominium owners who want to make a separation in the courtyard build the wall in the middle. At a place where commonly one builds with unhewn stones, or hewn stones, or half-bricks, or bricks, everything follows local custom. For unhewn stones, each partner gives three handbreadths. For hewn stones, each gives two and one half handbreadths. For half-bricks, each gives two handbreadths. For bricks, each gives one and a half handbreadths. Therefore, if the wall collapsed the place and the stones belong to both of them.
[Bava Batra 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Condominium owners who want to make a separation,” etc. As we have stated there: “One does not subdivide a courtyard unless each party has four cubits.” They said, there if the two parties do not agree. But here if both parties agree. And you may even say, here if the two parties do not agree. If this one wishes, one forces the other; if the other one wishes, one forces this one. {NAME} said, one forces for courtyards; one does not force for roofs. {NAME} wanted to say, in case of a courtyard which is higher than the roof. But in case of a roof which is higher than the courtyard, one forces. {NAME} wanted to say, in case of a courtyard which is higher than the roof one forces. But in case of a roof which is higher than the courtyard, one does not force.
[Bava Batra 1:2.1] MISHNAH: Similarly for a vegetable garden; a place which customarily is fenced in, he must fence in. But in an agricultural area, a place which customarily is not fenced in, one does not obligate him. But if he wishes, he builds inside his land and makes a façade to the outside; therefore if the wall collapses both land and stones are his. But if they did it with mutual agreement they build the wall in the middle and make façades on both sides; therefore if the wall collapses both land and stones belong to both of them.
[Bava Batra 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Similarly for a vegetable garden,” etc. It was stated: For a vegetable garden, whether it be a place where it is customary to build a fence, or a place where it is not customary to build a fence, one forces. But in an agricultural area, at a place where it is customary to build a fence one forces; where it is not customary to build a fence one does not force.
[Bava Batra 1:3.1] MISHNAH: Somebody’s [property] surrounded another’s on three sides. If he fenced in the first, and the second, and the third sides, one does not hold [the other] liable. {NAME} said, if the latter then fenced in the fourth side, one rolls everything over to him. If the wall of a courtyard collapsed, one obligates him to rebuild up to four cubits. There is a presumption that he gave, unless he brings proof that he did not give. Higher than four cubits one does not obligate him, but if he built an adjacent wall, even though he did not put on roofing, one rolls everything over to him. There is a presumption that he did not give, unless he brings proof that he gave.
[Bava Batra 1:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody’s [property] surrounded another’s,” etc. Halakhah 5: “If the wall of a courtyard collapsed,” etc. {NAME} said, only at the rate he is building now. For if he built it arched, he had to build arched. But here if it was built arched and he built it with bricks, he can collect the cost of arches, and if it should collapse, he has to rebuild it.
[Bava Batra 1:3.3] “{NAME} said, if the latter then fenced in the fourth side, one rolls everything over to him.” {NAME} said, one rolls over the length of the wall to him.
[Bava Batra 1:3.4] So far lengthwise. What about its width? {NAME} said, the wall of the courtyard is only made to save for him. They intended to say that if he wanted to make a roof, he cannot make a roof. {NAME} said, explain it by his beams.
[Bava Batra 1:4.1] MISHNAH: One forces him to build a porter’s lodge and a door for the courtyard. {NAME} says, not all courtyards are appropriate for a porter’s lodge. One forces him to build a wall for the town with double doors and bolt. {NAME} says, not all towns are appropriate for a wall. How long does he have to stay in a town to be like an inhabitant of the town? Twelve months; if he bought an apartment he immediately is an inhabitant of the town.
[Bava Batra 1:4.2] HALAKHAH: “One forces him to build,” etc. {NAME} said: So it is; the way of a provident person is to build himself a wall, as it is said: “The wealth of the rich is the fortification of his might, etc.” It was stated: “If he stayed there for thirty days he is like the townspeople for the charity chest, for clothing six months, for assessments and penalties twelve months.” After all these, was twelve months said only for assessments and penalties? {NAME} said for Passover wheat, both to take and to give.
[Bava Batra 1:5.1] MISHNAH: One does not divide the courtyard unless there be four cubits for each one, nor the field unless there be nine qab for each one; {NAME} says, nine half qabbim for each one. Not the vegetable garden unless there be half a qab for each one; {NAME} says, the area of a quarter [ qab ]. Not the dining hall, nor the storage room, nor the dovecote, nor the stole, nor the bathhouse, nor the olive press unless there is one for each of them. This is the principle: Anything which is divided and retains its name one divides, otherwise one does not divide. When is that? If the two of them do not agree. However, if both of them want it, they may divide even if it is less. But Holy Scripture they should not divide even if both of them want it.
[Bava Batra 1:5.2] HALAKHAH: “One does not divide the courtyard,” etc. {NAME} said, the four cubits which they mentioned are outside the four cubits of the doors. {NAME} stated thus: One does not subdivide a courtyard unless there be eight cubits for each party. {NAME} said, the four cubits which they mentioned are not acquired by him but they are for him to park his animal temporarily and unload his package. {NAME} asked: did they only say for him to park his animal temporarily and unload his package temporarily? It was found stated: also the circular enclosure of a cistern has four cubits. They said in the House of {NAME}: the chicken coop also has four cubits.
[Bava Batra 1:5.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. Everything the co-owners can prevent one another from doing in the courtyard except laundering because of the honor of the daughters of Israel. {NAME} said, this is at a place where women do the laundering, but not at a place where men do the laundering. And what was said, except laundering because of the honor of the daughters of Israel, only that in his own four cubits he may prevent it. And what was said, everything the co-owners can prevent one another from doing in the courtyard, in the entire courtyard except in the other person’s own four cubits where he cannot prevent him. But if the place was at an incline, even in the other person’s own four cubits he can prevent him, since he may tell him: you are pouring out in your domain but it flows down into mine.
[Bava Batra 1:5.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. If anybody does not want to participate in an ‘eruv one enters his house and makes the ‘eruv against his will. But was it not stated: if he does not want to make an ‘eruv, if he does not refuse one enters his house and makes the ‘eruv against his will? Because he does not refuse. But not if he does refuse. But was it not stated: “The dwellers at a dead end alley may force one another to make a lath or a beam for the dead end alley.” {NAME} said, not that he refused but out of ill-will he does not want to participate in an ‘eruv .
[Bava Batra 1:5.5] {NAME} said, a courtyard is divided by the number of doors. {NAME} said, the baraita refers to manure. It was stated as follows: “For the cooking stove one handbreadth, for manure according to doors, for the covered walkway according to people.” “Five courtyards which were using a water conduit and it broke. All of them repair together with the uppermost. The uppermost repairs at its place; the others with the second one. The second one repairs at its place; the lowest one repairs with all of them and at its place.” “Five apartments are built above a house which broke. All of them repair with the lowest. The lowest repairs at its place; the others with the second one. The second one repairs at its place; the uppermost repairs with all of them and at its place. If it was a storm sewer they can prevent it being used for laundry. For laundry they cannot prevent it being used as storm sewer.”
[Bava Batra 1:5.6] “But Holy Scripture they should not divide even if both of them want it.” {NAME} said, for example, Psalms and Chronicles. But Psalms and Psalms one may divide. {NAME} said, even Psalms and Psalms one may not divide. Since one may not divide, each of them comes and reads in the other’s [book].
[Bava Batra 2:1.1] MISHNAH: A person may not dig a cistern close to his neighbor’s cistern, nor a ditch, nor a cave, nor a water canal, nor a washer’s pond except if he distanced himself from his neighbor’s wall three handbreadths and lined with lime. One removes olive peat, and manure, and salt, and lime, and rocks from his neighbor’s wall three handbreadths or lines with lime. One distances seeds, and ploughs, and urine three handbreadths from the wall. One distances a grindstone three from the base, which means four from the moving stone, and the oven three from the base, which means four from its rim.
[Bava Batra 2:1.2] HALAKHAH: “A person may not dig a cistern,” etc. So is the Mishnah: “[A person may not dig a cistern close to the wall of his neighbor’s cistern. Nor a ditch, nor a cave, nor a water canal, nor a washer’s pond except if he distanced himself from his neighbor’s wall three handbreadths] and lined with lime. If he lined with lime, any distance. If he did not line with lime, three handbreadths. From the following: “One removes olive peat, and manure, and salt, and lime, and rocks from his neighbor’s wall three handbreadths or lines with lime.” Here you say, because rocks generate heat. But there you say that they do not generate heat. {NAME} said, in no case do rocks generate heat. But because they loosen the earth and damage the ground around the wall.
[Bava Batra 2:1.3] It was stated: “If it was solid rock, it is permitted.” As we say, {NAME} left the synagogue and let water behind the door. But we do not know whether it was because it was solid rock or because he suffered pain and could no bear it.
[Bava Batra 2:1.4] This means, about grindstones there, but for our grindstones three from the pine cone which is four from the enclosure. “And the oven three from the base which are four from its rim.” {NAME} said, from the outer rim inwards; but the rabbis say, from the inner rim outwards. If if was built like a dovecote, what [are the rules]? Let us hear from the following: “{NAME} said, unless there be under it insulating material three handbreadths and for a stove one handbreadth.” Is a stove not build like a dovecote, and you say both above and below a handbreadth? Also here, both above and below a handbreadth.
[Bava Batra 2:2.1] MISHNAH: A person should not put an oven in the house unless there be above it a space of four cubits; or if he puts it on the upper floor unless there be under it insulating material three handbreadths and for a stove one handbreadth But if he caused damage, he must pay what he damaged. {NAME} said, the reason they indicated these measures is that he not be liable to pay if he caused any damage,.
[Bava Batra 2:2.2] HALAKHAH: “A person should not put,” etc. It was stated: Nor a smithy. {NAME} stated: If he was like a metal worker, or it was built originally as a smithy, it is permitted. How is it in front of his dwelling? {NAME} said, certainly not in front of his dwelling. {NAME} said, a person causing damage has no claim of undisturbed posession. {NAME} said, the rabbis object to permanent smoke. As the following: A woman was burning sand below [the apartment of] {NAME}. He wanted to object to her. The case came before {NAME} who said, they said it only about continuous smoke.
[Bava Batra 2:3.1] MISHNAH: A person may not open a bakery or a dye shop under the storage room of another person, nor an animal barn. In truth they permitted for wine, but not an animal barn. About a store in the courtyard one may object and tell him, I cannot sleep because of the noise of those coming and the noise of those leaving. One who manufactures vessels has to leave and sells them in the market; nobody may object and tell him, I cannot sleep because of the noise of the hammer, nor because of the noise of a grindstone, nor because of the noise of children.
[Bava Batra 2:3.2] HALAKHAH: “A person may not open,” etc. {NAME} moved a preparer of fried food from one stall to another stall. One preparer of fried food was dwelling below [the apartment of] {NAME} {NAME}. {NAME} passed by and did not object. He said, the rabbis are passing by and do not object. {NAME} got angry with him. {NAME} {NAME} became seriously ill. {NAME} came to visit him. He said, I shall go and ask him. He went and said, if a court had mercy on somebody would the court prepare shrouds for him?
[Bava Batra 2:3.3] A person sold his entire house; he reserved for himself one stone bench where he went and sat. The case came before {NAME} and {NAME}. They said, it is not in your power to go and sit there and observe who comes and goes in his house. A person sold half his house; he reserved a bake shop for himself. The case came before {NAME} and {NAME}. They said, you are coming to him; he is not coming to you, as it is stated: “If the barn or the store preceded the storage room, he cannot object.”
[Bava Batra 2:3.4] It was stated: In truth, they permitted for wine even though it diminishes it because it improves it. {NAME} when he heard this statement put his wine in the attic of the bath house. His wine became foul-smelling. He said, the Mishnah led me astray. But the Mishnah did not lead him astray; the smell of the bath house made his wine foulsmelling.
[Bava Batra 2:3.5] It was stated: About his neighbor he may change his mind. Once he accepted it he can no longer change his mind. {NAME} says, even after he accepted it, he can change his mind, for he can tell him, they come and go here, they are looking for you and do not find you, and they increase traffic here. {NAME} and {NAME}, one said, what is “his neighbor”? He let him live in his house. Once he accepted it he can no longer change his mind. {NAME} said, one said, what is “his neighbor”? He opened a store for him. Once he accepted it he can no longer change his mind. {NAME} parallels {NAME}, as we have stated there: “For all of these says {NAME} that, even if he contracted with her, she can say ‘I thought that I could stand it, now I cannot.’ ”
[Bava Batra 2:3.6] “Nobody may object and tell him, I cannot sleep because of the noise of the hammer, or because of the noise of a grindstone, or because of the noise of children.” Those who teach boys and those who feed one another, their fellows may object to what they are doing, for he can tell him, they come and go here, they are looking for you and do not find you, and they increase traffic here. Those Sepphoreans can object to one another for nailing down their looms. {NAME} instructed to put one loom between two walls. {NAME} distanced a saw-horse four cubits from the wall. {NAME} said, those pillars which are weakened are weakened because of the force of shouts. The wall of Ḥoms fell before the noise of the Persians’ arrows.
[Bava Batra 2:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody’s wall was close to another’s wall he may not build his wall close by unless he moves it four cubits away. If there are windows, on top, from below, and on equal height, four cubits.
[Bava Batra 2:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody’s wall was,” etc. In the House of {NAME} they said, the Mishnah speaks of those coming first to settle in a new town. {NAME} said, The Mishnah speaks of a sealed wall. {NAME} said, the Mishnah speaks of a barricade wall. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says so: “If there are windows, on top, from below, and on equal height, four cubits.” On top four cubits, lest he could stand and see; from below four cubits, lest he could stand and see; at equal hight lest he obscure the sides. This was stated: “One distances the wall from a window by the size of a window.”
[Bava Batra 2:5.1] MISHNAH: One distances the ladder from a dovecote by four cubits lest a marten jump, and the wall four cubits from the leader so it can support the ladder. One distances the dovecote from town by fifty cubits. A person may not build a dovecote on his property unless he have fifty cubits in each direction. {NAME} says, the area of four bet kor , the distance one sends a pigeon. But if he bought it even with the area of a quarter [ qab ], it is in his power.
[Bava Batra 2:5.2] HALAKHAH: “One distances the ladder,” etc., until “in his power.” {NAME} said, that is, to the right hand side. But to the left he may put it up immediately.
[Bava Batra 2:5.3] Here, you say 50 cubits. But there, you say 30 stadia. {NAME} said, they feed within fifty cubits; they fly even four mil .
[Bava Batra 2:6.1] MISHNAH: A pigeon chick which is found within 50 cubits belongs to the owner of the dovecote; farther away than 50 cubits it belongs to its finder. If it was found between two dovecotes, if it is closer to one of them, it belongs to it; in the middle, both [owners] shall split evenly.
[Bava Batra 2:6.2] HALAKHAH: “A pigeon chick which is found within 50 cubits,” etc. That is, if no public road interrupts between them. But not if a public road interrupts between them. This is learned from that, and that is learned from this. This is learned from that: if there were two, he has to make it public. That is learned from this: if there were three, it would belong to its finder.
[Bava Batra 2:7.1] MISHNAH: One distances a tree from a town by 25 cubits; but carob tree or sycamore by 50 cubits; {NAME} says, every non-fruit tree by 50 cubits. If the town existed before the tree, one cuts it down and does not pay for it; if the tree existed before the town, one cuts it down and pays for it. If there is a doubt which one existed before the other, one cuts it down but does not pay. One distances a threshing floor 50 cubits from the town. A person shall not make a threshing floor on his property unless he owns 50 cubits in each direction. He distances it from another’s orchards or ploughed field so that he will not cause damage.
[Bava Batra 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: “One distances a tree from a town,” etc.. אֲפִילוּ בְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ אָסוּר Because it creates shadow where it stands or because its falling leaves are dangerous? What is the difference between them? If it stands on one’s own property. If you say, because it creates shadow where it stands, on his property it is permitted. But it you say, because its motion is dangerous, even on his property it is forbidden.
[Bava Batra 2:8.1] MISHNAH: One distances carcasses, and graves, and tanneries 50 cubits from the town, and one builds a tannery only to the East of a town. {NAME} says, one may build in any direction except to the West, and distances himself by 50 cubits.
[Bava Batra 2:8.2] HALAKHAH: “One distances carcasses,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: To the place where one prepares the skins. In the House of {NAME} they said, up to the place where one might smell what he makes. It was stated so: “{NAME} says, he may build it in any direction and distances himself, except to the West because that [wind] is frequent.” {NAME} went to accompany a person afflicted with a skin disease. His father told him, do not walk to the East of him but rather to the West of him.
[Bava Batra 2:9.1] MISHNAH: One distances a soaking pond from vegetables, and leeks from onions, and mustard from bees. {NAME} permits mustard.
[Bava Batra 2:9.2] HALAKHAH: “One distances a soaking pond,” etc. It was stated: One distances an onion bed from leeks, but {NAME} permits it. {NAME} said, from these teachings [it follows] that mutually they have to distance themselves one from the other. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Because the bees’ mouth becomes sharp and they destroy the honey.
[Bava Batra 2:10.1] MISHNAH: One distances a tree 25 cubits from a cistern, but carob tree and sycamore 50 cubits, whether on top or level. If the cistern existed before, he shall cut it down and pay for it; if the tree existed before, one shall not cut it down. {NAME} said, even if the cistern existed before, one shall not cut it down since the one digs on his property and the other plants on his property. A person should not plant a tree next to another’s field unless he distanced himself from it by four cubits, whether vines or any other tree. If there was a wall between them, each one goes close to the wall. If its roots extended to another’s field, he lowers the roots three handbreadths in order not to hinder the plough. If one was digging a cistern, or a ditch, or a cavern, he cuts and excavates and the wood is his.
[Bava Batra 2:10.2] HALAKHAH: “One distances a tree,” etc. Halakhah 12: “A person should not plant,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The rabbis’ reason is that civilization is based on cisterns. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} answers the rabbis thus: just as you hold that civilization is based on cisterns, so I am holding that civilization is based on trees.
[Bava Batra 2:10.3] [{NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Roots are irrelevant for First Fruits.] {NAME} said, he said it correctly. For if he did say that roots are important, nobody could ever bring First Fruits since the roots of one enter the other’s ground and vice-versa. Therefore, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Roots are irrelevant for First Fruits.
[Bava Batra 2:11.1] MISHNAH: If a tree overhangs another’s field, he may cut it in the height of the plough’s ox-goad; carob tree and sycamore along the plumb line. Over an irrigated field along the plumb line. {NAME} says, every non-fruit-bearing tree along the plumb line. If a tree overhangs the public domain, one has to cut it so that a camel with a rider on it may pass; {NAME} says, loaded with flax or bundles of vine cuttings. {NAME} says, any tree [must be cut] along the plumb line because of impurity.
[Bava Batra 2:11.2] HALAKHAH: “If a tree overhangs another’s field,” etc. “If a tree overhangs the public domain,,” etc. {NAME} was careful in judging; there was a Roman there who was his neighbor both in the field and the house. {NAME} had a tree overhanging the Roman’s property. A similar case came before him. He told them, go and return next morning. This Roman said, because of me he did not decide the case. Tomorrow I will abandon my work and see how the judgment goes. If he judges all people and does not judge himself, he is not human. At nightfall, {NAME} sent for his carpenter and told him, go and cut everything that overhangs the Roman’s. In the morning, the parties appeared before him. He told him, go and cut what overhangs into his property. The Roman said to him, what is with yours? He told him, go and see; what was done with mine do with yours. He went out and looked. He said, praised be the Jews’ God.
[Bava Batra 2:11.3] A woman honored {NAME} with figs. He told her, please if you brought them covered, take them away covered; but if you brought them in the open, take them away in the open, so that people should not say that she brought him denars and he honored her with figs.
[Bava Batra 2:11.4] {NAME} brought {NAME} to his garden and served him figs. When he left, he saw one tree of white benot ševa‘ . He asked him, why did you not let me eat from these? He told him, they are my son’s. {NAME} was afraid of robbing his son.
[Bava Batra 2:11.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Everybody agrees that practice follows {NAME}.
[Bava Batra 3:1.1] MISHNAH: Confirmation of claim of undisturbed possession of houses, cisterns, ditches, and caverns, and bath houses, and dove-cotes, oil presses, irrigated land, and slaves, and everything which yields continuously is three years from day to day. The claim of undisturbed possession of an unirrigated field is three years, but not from day to day.
[Bava Batra 3:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The claim of undisturbed possession of houses, cisterns, ditches, and caverns,” etc. From where confirmation of claims of undisturbed possession? {NAME} said, we heard from those who went to Usha that they learned it from the notorious bull. {NAME} said, who holds that a bull becomes notorious after three days? Not {NAME}? As we stated there: “{NAME} said, they said three years only for the case that if he is in Spain, he should be in possession for one year; they went and told him during one year, and he returns within one year.”
[Bava Batra 3:1.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If someboldy is selling a house to another, when he delivered the key [the buyer] took possession. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody is selling a house to another, when [the buyer] stored produce there, he took possession. {NAME} said, only produce usually stored. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody is selling a cistern to another, when he handed over its pails [the buyer] took possession. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody sold a flock to another person, when [the seller] delivered the maškokît, [the buyer] took possession. What is maškokît ? Some say, the shepherd’s staff. But some say, a pandura . And some say, the bell-wether. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody is selling a burial chamber to another, when that one buried there one dead it is confirmation of claim for the entire chamber. When he buried three dead in three chambers, it is confirmation of claim for the entire burial cavern.
[Bava Batra 3:1.4] “And slaves.” {NAME} {NAME} in the name of Rav: As long as a baby lies in the public domain, his father or his mother can testify about him. Once he has been collected from the public domain, one needs two witnesses and its father and mother are like two witnesses. {NAME} said, can a person be suspected to say about one who is not his son that he is his son? Maybe it was said about the property of a convert? He told him, but all our teachers in the Diaspora testify that in this form we heard it from {NAME}. {NAME} said: That is, if the baby is not moving. But [the case of] a baby which is moving refers to what {NAME} said: property rights on jumping calves and lambs which move from place to place cannot be proven by possession.
[Bava Batra 3:1.5] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If two fields of a proselyte were involved, with a boundary strip in between. If he cut off from one of them with the intent of taking possession also of the other but not the boundary strip in between, the one was acquired by him but not the other. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If he intended to acquire starting [from] the boundary strip and below? {NAME} said, property of a proselyte which he took possession of in the North by cutting off with the intent of also acquiring the one to the South, but did not have the intent of acquiring the strip in the middle, he acquired the one to the North but not the one to the South. There, we have stated: “If it was connected to the ground and he cut off anything, he acquired.” {NAME} said, he acquired only what he cut off. {NAME} said, this was said concerning the property of a proselyte. {NAME} said, {NAME}: It was reported that this was said concerning the property of a proselyte, so it should present no difficulty for {NAME}.
[Bava Batra 3:1.6] {NAME} said, “draw this animal close to you in order to take possession,” he took possession. “To take possession of its offspring,” he did [not] take possession. “To take possession of it together with its offspring,” he did (not) take possession. {NAME} said, that is, if it was not pregnant. But if it was pregnant, they treated [the fetus] as one of its limbs, as we did state: He who sells the fetus of his animal to another person did not do anything; the future children of his slave girl to another person, he did not do anything; the tithes of his field to another person, he did not do anything; the airspace of his dry land to another person, he did not do anything. But he may sell him an animal and reserve her fetus for himself, sell him a slave girl and reserve her children for himself, sell him a field and reserve the tithes for himself, sell him dry land and reserve the airspace for himself.
[Bava Batra 3:1.7] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Three are trustworthy immediately: a midwife, a caravan, and the one who purifies her colleagues. A midwife as long as [the woman] sits on the birthing chair, from the verse: “The midwife took and wound, etc.” A caravan, as {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of Rav: As long as [a baby] lies in the public domain, either its father or its mother can testify about him. Once he has been collected from the public domain, one needs two witnesses; its father and mother may become its two witnesses. The one who purifies her colleagues, as we have stated there: “Three women sleep on one bed. If blood was found under one of them, all three are impure. If one of them checked herself out and found herself impure, she is impure and the other two are pure.” {NAME} said, only within 24 hours.
[Bava Batra 3:2.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} says, three months in the first and three months in the last with twelve months in the middle, for a total of eighteen months. {NAME} says, one month in the first and one month in the last with twelve months in the middle, for a total of fourteen months. {NAME} said, when has this been said? A field of grain. But for an orchard, if he harvested his yield, lifted his olives, and collected his cut figs it counts for three years.
[Bava Batra 3:2.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} says, the first three months,” etc. {NAME} said, these are the words of {NAME} and {NAME}. But the Sages say, three years grain cutting, three years grape harvesting, three years olive harvesting. Rav said, these are the words of {NAME} and {NAME}. But the Sages say, three years from day to day. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Just as they disagree here, so they disgree about Elijah’s years.
[Bava Batra 3:3.1] MISHNAH: There are three regions for claims of undisturbed possession: Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee. If he was in Judea and somebody claimed undisturbed possession in Galilee, or in Galilee and somebody claimed undisturbed possession in Judea, it is not undisturbed possession unless he be in the same province. {NAME} said, they said three years only for the case that if he is in Spain, he should be in possession for one year; they went and told him during one year, and he returns within one year.
[Bava Batra 3:3.2] HALAKHAH: “There are three regions for claims of undisturbed possession,” etc. Rav said, this was taught in emergency situations.
[Bava Batra 3:3.3] {NAME} said, the years of ‘orlah are in dispute between them.
[Bava Batra 3:3.4] Rav said, there can be no claim of undisturbed possession from a fugitive, nor one made from one country to another. {NAME} said, there can be a claim of undisturbed possession from a fugitive, and a claim of undisturbed possession made from one country to another. {NAME} said, a verse supports what {NAME} said: “The king gave her an adjutant,” etc.
[Bava Batra 3:3.5] {NAME} said: Even two אבטיניות, e. g., שלומי and נבירו separated by the Jordan and a person may see another taking possession of the field, his property, there is no creation of a claim of undisturbed possession unless he was in the same locality, in the same province.
[Bava Batra 3:3.6] Rav said, the main confirmation of a claim of possession is storing the produce. Does Rav not agree about weeding and turning the soil? Rav agrees about weeding and turning the soil. What does it mean that Rav said, the main indication of a claim of possession is storing the produce? That if they saw him ploughing, and harvesting, and binding into sheaves, and threshing, and grading, but did not see him storing the produce, there is no claim of possession without storing the produce.
[Bava Batra 3:3.7] Rav said, the essence of ḥalîṣah is the untying of the shoelace. Did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} turns to it in the name of Rav: The words of the Sages: If she slips off but did not spit, or spat but did not take off, the ḥaliṣah is invalid unless she slips off and spits. Rav agrees “unless she slips off and spits”; it is implied by what Rav said, the essence of slipping off is untying the shoelaces.
[Bava Batra 3:3.8] {NAME} asked {NAME}: Must a protest be filed before a court? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: a protest does not have to be filed before a court. But some say, {NAME} asked {NAME} student: Must a protest be filed before a court? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: a protest must be filed before a court. {NAME} said, even if he protested against him in front of workers, it is a protest, but he has to protest in each one of the three years. {NAME} had a case; his judges were {NAME}, {NAME}, and {NAME}. {NAME} told them, so said my father: Once he protested the first three years, he is not required to protest further. It was stated thus: “If he ate it as his own for six years, he protested against him the first three years; then he said, you sold it to me, you gave it to me as a gift, there is no claim of undisturbed possession. Because of an initial claim it would have been a claim of undisturbed possession since any claim of undisturbed possession not accompanied by a claim of legal ownership is not a claim of undisturbed possession.” {NAME} said, if it is so, nothing would be left for the great people of the Land of Israel.
[Bava Batra 3:4.1] MISHNAH: Any claim of undisturbed possession not accompanied by a claim of legal ownership is not a claim of undisturbed possession. How is this? He said to him, what are you doing on my property? Nobody ever said anything to me is not a claim of undisturbed possession. You sold it to me, you gave it to me as a gift, is a claim of undisturbed possession. A person entering because of inheritance does not need a claim.
[Bava Batra 3:4.2] HALAKHAH: “Any claim of undisturbed possession not accompanied by a claim of legal ownership,” etc. But it needs proof of undisturbed possession. There, we have stated: “{NAME} agrees that if somebody says to anothet, ‘this field’, etc.” As the following. Reuben ate from a field claiming that it was his. Simeon brought witnesses that his father died in possession. One removes [the field] from Reuben and hands it over to Simeon. Reuben went and brought witnesses that [Simeon’s] father did not die in possession. {NAME} said, I took it from Reuben, I am returning it to him. Rav said, when you gave it to him, you gave it on the basis of a court decree. From there on the burden of proof is on the claimant.
[Bava Batra 3:4.3] Who informs? {NAME} said, the witnesses to the death inform. Think of it, if the witnesses did not know! {NAME} said, the field always is in the possession of its owner. From there on the burden of proof is on the claimant.
[Bava Batra 3:5.1] MISHNAH: Partners and sharecroppers have no claim of undisturbed possession. A husband has no claim of undisturbed possession in his wife’s property, nor a wife in her husband’s property, nor a father in his son’s property, nor the son in his father’s property. When has this been said? For one who claims undisturbed possession. But if one is given a gift, or brothers distributed the estate, one takes possession of a convert’s property, when he locked, fenced in, or made any breach that is a legal form of taking in possession.
[Bava Batra 3:5.2] HALAKHAH: “Partners and sharecroppers,” etc. “A partner.” {NAME} said, “partner” is not mentioned here. Does the partner not have a claim to undisturbed possession? Did not {NAME} say that the partner who went and planted, planted with permission? When you say, the partner who went and planted, planted with permission, if he was there. When you say, the partner has no claim of undisturbed possession, if he was not there. What does he include in his stead? Artisans and robbers have no claim of undisturbed possession. “If somebody saw his slave at an artisan’s, or his garments at the washer’s, and told him, give me my slave, give me my garments, but he answered him, you gave him to me as a gift; you sold him to me; this is no claim of undisturbed possession. You told me to sell him; you instructed to give him to me as a gift, this is a claim of undisturbed possession.”
[Bava Batra 3:5.3] “Sharecroppers.” {NAME} said, a permanent sharecropper, but a temporary sharecropper has a claim of undisturbed possession. {NAME} and {NAME} both teach that even a temporary sharecropper has no claim of undisturbed possession, for we may say that he is satisfied with him and let him have it. There, they say that a sharecropper has no claim of undisturbed possession but a sharecropper’s son has a claim of undisturbed possession; {NAME} and {NAME} say, neither a sharecropper nor a sharecropper’s son have a claim of undisturbed possession, for we may say that he was satisfied with his father and let the son have it. As {NAME} said, a sharecropper who engaged another sharecropper has no claim of undisturbed possession since it is common for sharecroppers to engage sub-sharecroppers.
[Bava Batra 3:5.4] In truth, should a man supervising his wife’s properties have a claim of undisturbed possession, since usually husbands supervise their wife’s properties? “A husband has no claim of undisturbed possession in his wife’s property” during her lifetime. But after her death he has a claim of undisturbed possession. “Nor a wife in her husband’s property” during his lifetime. But after his death she has a claim of undisturbed possession. “Nor a son in the father’s property” during his lifetime. But after the father’s death he has a claim of undisturbed possession. “Nor the father in his son’s property” during his lifetime. But after the son’s death he has a claim of undisturbed possession.
[Bava Batra 3:5.5] Rav said, if he lowered it below ten [handbreadths] or increased above ten. {NAME} said, even if he made a breach at a place where a breach was irrelevant or a fence where a fence was irrelevant, it is legally taking possession.
[Bava Batra 3:5.6] As we have stated: If somebody sells a field to another but the buyer was lazy and did not enter into possession when the seller went and legally took possession, the taking possession invalidates the sale or the gift.
[Bava Batra 3:6.1] MISHNAH: Two testify for him that he ate its yield for three years; if they are found perjured they pay everything to him. Two for the first [year], two for the second, two for the third, pay together. Three brothers and another joins them; these are three testimonies which count as one testimony.
[Bava Batra 3:6.2] HALAKHAH: “Two testify for him,” etc. One said to another “what are you doing in my field?” “For I have the years of undisturbed possession of it.” He went and brought witnesses that he had the years of undisturbed possession of it. The first one went and proved the witnesses of the second perjured. He has to give him the field and the yield of three years.
[Bava Batra 3:6.3] {NAME} said, this implies that the perjurer is not disqualified by the court.
[Bava Batra 3:7.1] MISHNAH: The following count for a claim of undisturbed possession and the following do not count for a claim of undisturbed possession. If one put his animals into a courtyard, an oven, a cooking stove, or a grindstone, or raises chickens, or puts his manure in a courtyard, it does not count for a claim of undisturbed possession. But if he made for his animals an enclosure ten [handbreadths] high, or did it for an oven, a cooking stove, or a grindstone, brought chickens into the house, or made a place for his manure three [handbreadths] low or three high: this counts for a claim of undisturbed possession.
[Bava Batra 3:7.2] HALAKHAH: “The following count for a claim of undisturbed possession,” etc. {NAME} said, co-owners usually permit chickens to one another. {NAME} said, a Mishnah says otherwise: “Both of them are forbidden to put up there a grindstone or an oven, or to raise chickens there.” {NAME} said, if somebody raised chickens in a courtyard which is not his, it is taking in possession. {NAME} said, this is correct. As you take it, if he has permission to raise chickens there, he raises them. If he does not have permission to raise, it would be legally taking in possession.
[Bava Batra 3:8.1] MISHNAH: The drain pipe does not represent a right of possession; its location represents a right of possession. The leader represents a right of possession. An Egyptian ladder does not represent a right of possession; a Tyrian one represents a right of possession. An Egyptian window does not represent a right of possession; a Tyrian one represents a right of possession. What is an Egyptian window? Any where a man’s head cannot enter. {NAME} says, if it has a wooden frame it represents a right of possession even if a man’s head cannot enter.
[Bava Batra 3:8.2] HALAKHAH: “The drain pipe does not represent a right of possession.” {NAME} said, to lengthen and to widen it. {NAME} said, in all of that direction, as we have stated: the leader has a domain of four cubits. You have to say, in all this direction. Similarly, the drain tube does not represent a right of possession in all of this direction. It was stated thus: “The location of the drain tube does represent a right of possession, the location of its spout does not represent a right of possession.”

[Bava Batra 3:10.1] MISHNAH: A person may not open windows into the common courtyard. If he bought a house in another courtyard he may not open it into the common courtyard. If he built a second floor on top of his house he may not open it into the common courtyard but he may build a room inside his house or a second floor on top of his house on condition that the access to it be from within his house. In a common courtyard a person may not open a door opposite a door, a window opposite a window. If it was small, he may not enlarge it. If it was one, he may not make it double. But he may open into the public domain a door opposite a door and a window opposite a window. If it was small, he may enlarge it. If it was one, he may make it double.
[Bava Batra 3:10.2] HALAKHAH: “A person may not open windows,” etc. Here you say, a door opposite a door is permitted, and there you say, a door opposite a door is forbidden. Where you say it is permitted, in an alley. And where you say it is forbidden, in a condominium courtyard. But did we not state: “Just as the inhabitants of a courtyard may object to one another, so the inhabitants of an alley may object to one another”? {NAME} said, here when permission was given, there when permission was not given. {NAME} said, there is a difference because gardens are usually dug into. {NAME} said, are ruins not to be rebuilt?
[Bava Batra 3:10.3] {NAME} said that there, one states: If somebody opens a window in the wall of somebody else’s courtyard in the presence of the other (four cubits), [Rebbi says] he takes down with his left hand and closes with his right. Think of it, was he not standing there? He may tell him, I wanted to enjoy myself. If he handed him stones? He may tell him, I was making fun of this man.
[Bava Batra 3:10.4] If there were five openings one inside another, the measure of all of them is a drill hole. This supports what the builders say, viz., that a window open above a stone bench is made only to let light in. Since it cannot represent a right of possession, it cannot bring impurity.
[Bava Batra 3:11.1] MISHNAH: One makes no hollow under the public domain, cisterns, ditches, and caves. {NAME} permits if a cart filled with stones can pass over it. If somebody bought a courtyard and there are protrusions and balconies, that remains a right of possession.
[Bava Batra 3:11.2] HALAKHAH: “One makes no hollow,” etc. If they collapsed and he wants to rebuild. {NAME} said, he gave up his rights. {NAME} said, he did not give up his rights. A Mishnah supports one, a baraita supports the other. A Mishnah supports {NAME}: “If a public road went through somebody’s field and he took it and gave them on the side. What he gave, he gave, but his own did not come to him.” A baraita supports {NAME}: “If somebody bought a courtyard and there are protrusions and balconies, if they collapsed he rebuilds them based on his right of possession.”

From four cubits to eight or from eight to sixteen? He told him, from eight to sixteen so that one truck may leave and the other come.
[Bava Batra 5:2.1] MISHNAH: He who buys two trees on another’s property did not acquire the land; {NAME} says, he acquired the land. If they grew, he need not cut them. What grows from the stem is his, from the roots is the owner’s of the ground. If they died, he has no land. If he bought three, he bought the land. If they grew, he has to cut them. What grows from the roots is his. If they died, he has the land.
[Bava Batra 5:2.2] HALAKHAH: “He who buys two trees on another’s property,” etc. (The words) [In the House of] {NAME} they said, what sees the shadow is root, what sees the sun is stem. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: What grows from its roots and its stem is root, from its stem but not its roots is tree. {NAME} said, he who buys three trees buys the land in between them, under them, and outside of them the width of the harvester and his bag. {NAME} said, while he has no access, he has the width of the harvester and his bag outside of them.
[Bava Batra 5:3.1] MISHNAH: He who sells the head of a large animal did not sell the feet; if he sold the feet he did not sell the head. If he sold the windpipe he did not sell the liver; if he sold the liver he did not sell the windpipe. But for a small animal, if he sold the head he sold the feet; if he sold the feet he did not sell the head. If he sold the windpipe he sold the liver; if he sold the liver he did not sell the windpipe.
[Bava Batra 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: “He who sells the head of a large animal,” etc. {NAME} asked: If he sold half of the head, did he sell half of the legs? If he sold half of the windpipe, did he sell half of the liver? [If he sold half of the liver,] did he sell half of the windpipe? Let us hear from the following: “If he sold him the entire foot, the entire head, the entire intestines, he gives to the Cohen and does not deduct from the price. If he bought by weight, he gives to the Cohen and deducts from the price.”
[Bava Batra 5:4.1] MISHNAH: Four situations for sellers. If one contracted to sell high quality wheat and it turned out to be low quality, the buyer may annul the contract. Low quality and it turned out to be high quality, the seller may annul the contract. Low quality and it turned out to be low quality, high quality and it turned out to be high quality, neither of them may annul the contract. Brown grain and it turned out to be white grain, white grain and it turned out to be brown grain, olive wood and it turned out to be sycamore wood, sycamore wood and it turned out to be olive wood, wine and it turned out to be vinegar, vinegar and it turned out to be wine, either of them may annul the contract. If somebody sold produce to another and this one moved it without measuring, he took possession. If he was measuring without moving, he did not take possession. If he is intelligent, he rents its place. If somebody buys flax from another he he did not take possession until he moved it from place to place; but if it still was standing on the ground and he plucked anything, he took possession. If somebody sold wine or oil to another and it rose or fell in price, if it was before the measure was filled it is for the seller, after the measure was filled for the buyer. If a broker was involved and the amphora broke, it broke for the broker. He is obligated to let it drip three drops. If he tilted and emptied it, [the remainder] is for the seller. The grocer does not have to let it drip three drops. {NAME} says, Friday evenings close to sundown he is not liable.
[Bava Batra 5:4.2] HALAKHAH: “Four situations for sellers.,” etc. How is this? If the measuring vessel belonged to the seller, he has the property rights, if to the buyer, he has the property rights. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of the Great {NAME}, so is the Mishnah: If the measuring vessel belonged to a third person. It was stated: {NAME} says, Friday evenings close to sundown he is not liable since he has permission, but the Sages say, in any case he is liable. What is the reason for what {NAME} said? “If he is hired, it is paid for by his wages.”
[Bava Batra 5:5.1] MISHNAH: Somebody sent his son to a grocer who measured him oil for an assarius and he gave him the assarius ; if he broke the flask and lost the assarius , the grocer is liable. {NAME} holds him not liable since for that he sent him. The Sages agree with {NAME} that if the flask was in the child’s hand and the grocer measured into the flask, the grocer is not liable. The wolesaler cleans his measuring vessels once every thirty days, the householder every twelve months. {NAME} says, it is the other way around. The retail grocer cleans his measuring vessels twice a week, wipes his weights clean once a week, and cleans his scales after each weighing. {NAME} said, when has this been said? For fluids, but for dry matter it is not necessary; he has to let [the scales] bend down a handbreadth. If he weighed strictly by eyesight he has to give him surplus, one tenth for fluids and one twentieth for dry products. At a place where one is used to small measures he should not use large ones, to large measures he should not use small ones, to level one must not heap, to heap one must not level.
[Bava Batra 5:5.2] HALAKHAH: “Somebody sent his son to a grocer,” etc. {NAME} said, for the tenths he has to let bend down a handbreadth. It is written: “Fair scales, fair weights.” From here the Sages said that any commandment whose reward is noted, the court is not warned about. “You shall have,” appoint market overseers over this. {NAME} said, so is the baraita : Any commandment whose reward is noted the court is not punished about. Rav was appointed market overseer by the Head of the Diaspora; he intervened about measuring vessels but not prices. The Head of the Diaspora jailed him. {NAME} went to see him and said, the market overseer about whom they spoke was for measures but not prices. He answered, but you had stated: the market overseer is for both measures and prices. He said to him, go out and tell them, the market overseer is for measures but not prices. He went out and said to them, a person who teaches hidden things they send to jail!
[Bava Batra 5:5.3] At a place where one is used to small measures he should not use large ones, to large measures he should not use small ones, to level one must not heap, to heap one must not level.
[Bava Batra 6:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody sells grain to another and it did not sprout, or even flax seed, he is not responsible for it. {NAME} said, for garden seeds which are not edible he is responsible. If somebody sells produce to another he has to accept a quarter [ qab ] of chaff per se’ah ; for figs he has to accept ten worm-bitten ones per hundred; with a wine cellar he has to accept ten sour ones per hundred; with vessels in the Sharon he has to accept ten pitassaot per hundred. If somebody sells wine to another and it turned into vinegar, he is not responsible for it. But if it was known that his wine turns into vinegar, it is a buy in error. If he told him, I am selling you spice wine, it has to keep until Pentecost. “Old” is from the year before, “aged” from three years.
[Bava Batra 6:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody sells grain to another,” etc. It was stated: “If somebody sells grain to another and it did not sprout, even flax seed, he is not responsible for it. But if he made it conditional from the start as seeds, he is liable. What does he pay him? The value of the seeds. Some say, he gives him his expenses.”
[Bava Batra 6:1.3] Here, he has to accept it, but there it should be diminished. Here only chaff, but there another kind. Here only the way he touched it, but there only the way he carried it. Here {NAME} agrees, but there, {NAME} says they are two kinds and do not count together.

These 100 amphoras I am selling to you, even if they were vinegar they are delivered.” {NAME}: If the vessels belonged to the buyer, he may tell him: I sold to you for [immediate] consumption.

[Bava Batra 6:2.1] MISHNAH: If somebody sells a plot to another to build a house, or he contracts to build him a wedding building for his son, a widow’s seat for his daughter, builds four by six cubits, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, this is a cowshed. [Bava Batra 6:3.1] MISHNAH: If somebody has a cistern inside another’s house, he may enter at times when people usually enter and must leave when people usually leave. He cannot bring his animal and let it drink from his cistern but draws water and lets it drink outside. Each of them makes a lock for himself. If somebody has a vegetable garden inside another’s vegetable garden, he may enter at times when people usually enter and must leave when people usually leave. He cannot bring traders inside and cannot use it to go to another field; the outside owner may sow on the path. If he was allowed a path on the side by common accord, he may enter any time he wishes and leave any time he wishes; he can bring traders inside but cannot use it to go to another field; neither owner may sow on it.
[Bava Batra 6:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody has a cistern,” etc. It was stated: The outer one cannot sow on the path for the other can tell him, I would walk on slippery ground. The inner one cannot sow on the path for the other can tell him, you would take care of yours and step on mine.
[Bava Batra 6:4.1] MISHNAH: If a public way was passing through somebody’s field, he took it away and gave them [a road] to the side of his property, what he gave, he gave, but what he wanted for himself he did not get. A private way is four cubits wide, a public way sixteen cubits; a king’s highway has no limit; the way to the cemetary has no limit. The place for funeral orations, the judges of Sepphoris say an area of four qab . If somebody sells a plot to another to build a grave, or he contracts to build him a grave makes the cavity of the cavern four cubits by six and opens into it eight sepulchral chambers, three on each side and two at the back wall. The chambers are four cubits long, seven [handbreadths] high and six [handbreadths] wide. {NAME} says, he makes the cavity of the cavern six by eight [cubits] and opens into it thirteen sepulcral chambers, four on each side, three at the back wall, one to the right of the entrance and one to its left. In front of the cavern he excavates a courtyard of six by six [cubits] for the bier and its carriers. He opens into it two caverns, one at each side. {NAME} says four, each to each direction of the compass. {NAME} says, all depends on the rock.
[Bava Batra 6:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If a public way was passing through somebody’s,” etc., to the end of the Mishnah. {NAME} said, he makes them like keyholes. {NAME} told him, but dogs are not buried in that way! What does he do? He builds inside as if outside. Do the crossings not interfere with one another? They do not cross; he builds one higher and one lower.
[Bava Batra 7:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody says to another: I am selling you a bet kor of dust, if there were depressions ten handbreadths deep or rocks ten handbreadths high, they are not measured with it; less than that they are measured with it. But if he said, about a bet kor of dust, if there were depressions deeper than ten handbreadths or rocks higher than ten handbreadths, they are measured with it.
[Bava Batra 7:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody says to another: I am selling you a bet kor of dust,” etc. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Only if it is the smaller part of his field and enclosed in it. And a rock with a total surface area of a bet rova‘ is not measured with it. If it is in the middle, it is measured, at the side it is not measured. What is a side and what is in the middle? In the House of {NAME} they said, any place surrounded by a ploughed area is in the middle; any place not surrounded by a ploughed area is to the side. {NAME} came in the name of {NAME}: If it was a majority on one side, but if you spread it, it becomes a smaller part, and it is measured with it. How wide? {NAME} said, up to four cubits. {NAME} said, up to ten handbreadths. If there was a depression ten handbreadths deep but less than four wide, what is the rule? Let us hear from the following, what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: “Only if it is the smaller part of his field and enclosed in it. And a rock with a total surface area of a bet rova‘ is not measured with it. If it was split, it is measured with it.” This means that if the greater part of it was on one side, but if you spread it, it becomes the smaller part and is not measured with it. If there was a long depression which added up to a bet rova‘ ? {NAME} asked: If it was shaped like sticks, is it measured with it or not? {NAME} asked: If it was like marble plates, is it measured with it or not? {NAME} asked: If it was formed like chairs, does he measure from the place of its wall or does he measure from its declivity? {NAME} in the name of Rav, [Rebbi] Ḥiyya in the name of {NAME}: Only if the total agricultural area was four bet kor .
[Bava Batra 7:2.1] MISHNAH: “I am selling you a bet kor of dust measured by the surveyor’s measuring tape,” if a little bit be missing, he deducts, if it be a little more, he has to refund. If he said “more or less,” even if it was deficient by a quarter [ qab ] per se’ah or redundant by a quarter [ qab ] per se’ah, he received it. For more than that one makes a computation. What does he return? Money. But if he agreed, he returns land to him. Then why did they say, he returns money to him? To empower the seller, for if this one retained for himself a space for nine qab , or in a vegetable garden the space for half a qab (or following {NAME} a bet rova‘ ) he returns land to him. Not only the quarter [ qab ] he has to return but all the excess.
[Bava Batra 7:2.2] HALAKHAH: “I am selling you a bet kor of dust,” etc. Here, you say that “he has received it.” But there, you say that “not only the quarter [ qab ] he has to return but all the excess”? They said, since you exclude him from the rule of “less than measured by the surveyor’s measuring tape” you return him to the rules of “by the surveyor’s measuring tape.”
[Bava Batra 7:3.1] MISHNAH: “Measured by the surveyor’s measuring tape, more or less;” “more or less” invalidated “measured by the surveyor’s measuring tape”. “More or less, measured by the surveyor’s measuring tape;” “measured by the surveyor’s measuring tape” invalidated “more or less”, the words of {NAME}. “By its description and its boundary strips,” less than one sixth he received it, up to a sixth he shall deduct.
[Bava Batra 7:3.2] HALAKHAH: “What does he return? Money,” etc. {NAME} stated: If somebody sell a slave to another and he turns out to be a thief or a gambler, he received him. But if he was a robber or proscribed by the Government, he did not receive him.
[Bava Batra 7:3.3] “If somebody say to another: I am selling you half a field,” etc. {NAME} said, the sixth itself he shall deduct.
[Bava Batra 7:4.1] MISHNAH: If somebody say to another: I am selling you half a field, they estimate in common and he takes half of his field. Its Southern part I am selling to you, they estimate in common and he takes the Southern half. He has to accept the place of the wall, the trench or the small trench. How much is a trench? Six handbreadths. And the small trench, three.
[Bava Batra 7:4.2] HALAKHAH: It was stated: If somebody says to another: I am selling you half a field, and X and Y and half of Z surround you. {NAME}, and {NAME}, and {NAME}.
