[Bava Batra 8:1.1] MISHNAH: Some inherit and bequeath; inherit but do not bequeath, bequeath but do not inherit, neither inherit nor bequeath. The following inherit and bequeath: The father from the sons, and the sons from the father, and the paternal brothers inherit and bequeath. A man from his mother, a man from his wife, and the sons of sisters inherit but do not bequeath. A woman to her son, a woman to her husband, and the mother’s brothers bequeath but do not inherit. But the maternal brothers neither inherit nor bequeath. The order of inheritances is the following: “If a man die without a son, you shall transfer his estate to his daughter.” The son precedes the daughter and all the son’s descendants come before the daughter. The daughter precedes the brothers and all the daughter’s descendants precede the brothers. The brothers precede the father’s brothers and all their descendants precede the father’s brothers. This is the principle: For every one preceding in inheritance, his descendants precede. But the father precedes all his descendants.
[Bava Batra 8:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Some inherit and bequeath,” etc. It is written: “If a man die without a son, you shall transfer his estate to his daughter.” {NAME} stated: The verse distinguished this inheritance from all other inheritances mentioned in the Torah, since for all of them it is written “you shall give,” but here is written: “you shall transfer.” It is an extension of the law that the daughter shall inherit. The Gentile Sages say, son and daughter are equal, for they explain “if he have no son;” therefore, if he has one both are equal. One objected, is it not written “if he have no daughter;” therefore, if he has one are both equal? And you agree, if there is no child, here also, if there is no son. The Sadducees say, the son’s daughter and the daughter are equal, for they explain: Since my son’s daughter who comes by force of her father does inherit from me, would it not be logical that my daughter who comes by force of myself should inherit from me? One told them, no. If you mention the son’s daughter who only inherits by the power of the brothers, what could you say about the daughter who only inherits by the power of the old man? The verse says, “any daughter who is an heiress of the tribes.” How is it possible for a daughter to inherit from two tribes? But explain it if her father was from one tribe and her mother from another.
[Bava Batra 8:1.3] So far the son [inherits from] the father. The father from the son? Since the son only inherits by the father’s power, is it not logical that the father on whom the son depends inherit from him? The verse says, “close”; the closer relative has precedence.
[Bava Batra 8:1.4] So far a daughter. A son? Since the daughter, whose power is diminished regarding the father’s property, has her power increased regarding the mother’s property, should the son’s power not be increased regarding the mother’s property, since his power is increased regarding the father’s property? It turns out that for the daughter one infers from the verse and for the son from an argument de minore ad majus. Does the son precede the daughter? {NAME} said in the name of {NAME} the butcher’s son: So did {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}: Both son and daughter are equal for the mother’s tribe {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} had a case; the judges were {NAME}, {NAME}, and {NAME}. {NAME} told them: Our brothers outside the Land are unqualified and err in practice; in particular they rely on {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, but it is not so. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice does not follow {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice does not follow {NAME}. {NAME} {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice does not follow {NAME}. {NAME} and {NAME} were sitting when {NAME} came and asked concerning: “Any daughter who is an heiress of the tribes,” what is the rule? He said to him, it binds the father’s tribe together with the mother’s tribe. Since from the father’s tribe there is nothing for the daughter when there is a son, so also from the mother’s tribe there is nothing for the daughter when there is a son. Or is it the other way around? Since from the mother’s tribe there is something for the daughter when there is a son, so also from the father’s tribe is there something for the daughter when there is a son? {NAME} said to him, let us leave; that man does not want to listen to words of instruction.
[Bava Batra 8:1.5] “A man from his mother, a man from his wife.” Is “a man from his mother” not the same as “a man from his wife”? {NAME}: he wanted to enumerate all cases and did not find them, so he formulated the rule twofold.
[Bava Batra 8:1.6] “Son.” Not only a son, from where a daughter’s son? The verse says, “a son”, from anywhere. “Daughter.” Not only a daughter, from where a daughter’s son, a son’s daughter, daughter’s daughter, a son’s son? The verse says, “a daughter”, from anywhere. “Brothers.” Not only brothers, from where brothers’ sons, brothers’ daughters, brothers’ sons’ daughters? The verse says, “his flesh’s relatives”, from anywhere.
[Bava Batra 8:2.1] MISHNAH: Zelophehad’s daughters took three parts in inheritance: Their father’s who was of those who left Egypt, his part among his brothers in the estate of Hepher, and because he was firstborn he was taking two parts.
[Bava Batra 8:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Zelophehad’s daughters,” etc. Zelophehad’s daughters said before our teacher Moses: If we are Zelophehad’s daughters, we should inherit from our father. If we are not Zelophehad’s daughters, let our mother enter levirate marriage. Immediately, “ he brought their suit before the Eternal.” The Holy One, praise to Him, told him, “ Zelophehad’s daughters speak correctly. Give them possession of inheritance,” give them real estate, give them movables, give them their father’s part among their father’s brothers.
[Bava Batra 8:2.3] {NAME} said, the Land was distributed to those who left Egypt, as it is written: “By the names of the fathers’ tribes they shall inherit.” Then why does the verse say: “To those”? Only because of women and because of children. {NAME} said, the Land was distributed to those who entered the Land, as it was said, “to those it shall be distributed.” Then why does the verse say: “By the names of the fathers’ tribes”? This inheritance was different from all other inheritances in the world. For in all other inheritances in the world the living inherit from the dead but here the dead from the living. It was stated: {NAME} said, the Land was distributed to those who left Egypt and to those who stood in the plains of Moab. How is that? If one was both of those who left Egypt and those who stood in the plains of Moab, he took two parts. Of those who left Egypt but not of those who stood in the plains of Moab, or of those who stood in the plains of Moab but not of those who left Egypt, he took one part. The daughters of Zelophehad took five parts: their part with those who left Egypt and their part with those who stood in the plains of Moab. And because he was a firstborn they took two parts. And their father’s part among his brothers. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says otherwise. But “giving you shall give them inheritance among their father’s brothers.” That is what is written: “Ten measures fell to Manasseh”.
[Bava Batra 8:2.4] Joshua and Caleb took three parts: Their part with those who left Egypt and their part with those who stood in the plains of Moab; in addition they took the parts of the spies. This is what is written: “Joshua bin Nun and {NAME} lived off the men, etc.” But the part of the complainers and Korah’s gang became common property; their sons [inherited] from their paternal and maternal grandfathers. That is what is written: “Korah’s sons did not die.”
[Bava Batra 8:2.5] Rebbi explained it by a parable; to what can this be compared? To two brothers, co-owners who left Egypt. One had nine sons, the other a single son. They inherited ten bet kor. Each of them takes a letekh . They return it to their fathers and then split. It turns out that the single son takes half and the sons of the other take half.
[Bava Batra 8:2.6] {NAME} explained it by a parable; to what can this be compared? To two brothers, Cohanim and co-owners who stood by a threshing floor; one had nine sons and the other had one. They took (the area of) ten qab. They returned it to their father and split. It turns out that the son of one takes half and the sons of the other take half.
[Bava Batra 8:2.7] {NAME} objected: “I shall bring you to your forefathers’ land, etc.” If it was a gift, why an inheritance? And if an inheritance, why a gift? But after he gave it to them as a gift, he turned around and gave it as inheritance. {NAME} said, anywhere one mentions מוֹרָשָה it means weariness. They objected, is it not written, “an inheritance (מוֹרָשָׁה) of the congregation of Jacob”? He said, there is no weariness greater than this. He who studies forgets everything.
[Bava Batra 8:3.1] MISHNAH: Both son and daughter are equal for the rules of inheritance, except that the son take a double portion of the father’s property but no double portion of the mother’s property. And the daughters can claim sustenance from the father’s property but not from the mother’s property.
[Bava Batra 8:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Both son and daughter are equal for the rules of inheritance,” etc. It is written: “Of anything which will be found with him,” etc. How could he inherit the expectancy like existing property? How? If his father died during his father’s father’s lifetime, he takes a double portion of his father’s estate but not a double portion of his grandfather’s estate. But if his father was a firstborn, just as he takes from his father’s estate so he takes from his grandfather’s estate. {NAME} in the name of Abba [Cohen] {NAME}: It was said “a rule of law” in the matter of a double portion just as it was said “a rule of law” in the matter of a single portion. Since for a single portion one considers the son as if he were alive to take his father’s single portion so for a double portion one considers the son as if he were alive to take his father’s double portion.
[Bava Batra 8:4.1] MISHNAH: One who says, “my firstborn X shall not take a double portion,” [or] “my son Y shall not inherit together with his brothers,” did not say anything since he stipulated against what is written in the Torah. One who distributes his property orally, if he increased for one, or diminished for another, or made the firstborn equal to the others, his words are upheld; except if, however, he formulated it in terms of inheritance, he did not say anything. But if he wrote in terms of gift, whether at the start, or in the middle, or at the end, his words are upheld.
[Bava Batra 8:4.2] HALAKHAH: “One who says, “my firstborn X shall not take a double portion,’ ” etc. {NAME} made the right of the firstborn equal to that of the brothers. {NAME} said to them: Is that not a verse, “he shall not be able to declare as firstborn.” {NAME} said, by the Temple Service! He is able, but he is not permitted. Except that he is able designating it as a gift.
[Bava Batra 8:4.3] “But if he wrote in terms of gift, whether at the start, or the middle, or the end, his words are upheld.” {NAME} said: “There shall be given to Mr. X the inheritance I want him to inherit.” “X should inherit the gift I want him to inherit.” “X shall inherit the inheritance which I gave to him .” “Write and give field X to person Y.” {NAME} and {NAME} brought a case before {NAME} He told them, if it is documentation, then write and deliver. If it is to transfer property, everybody agrees that nobody can transfer property after his death.
[Bava Batra 8:4.4] {NAME} asked {NAME}: if one wrote a gift in the language of a sale? He answered, he made it ride on two racing horses; {NAME} said, they only said that one brings two white horses and makes it ride on both. One goes in one direction and the other in another; it turns out that he caught nothing.
[Bava Batra 8:5.1] MISHNAH: One who says, Mr. X shall inherit from me while he has a daughter, or, my daughter shall inherit from me while he has a son, did not say anything since he stipulated against what is written in the Torah. {NAME} said, if he said that about anybody who can be his heir, his words stand; about anybody who cannot be his heir, his words do not stand.
[Bava Batra 8:5.2] HALAKHAH: “One who says, Mr. X shall inherit from me,” etc. {NAME} said, {NAME} said only this about a son among sons or a daughter among daughters, but not a daughter among brothers or a brother among daughters. {NAME} said, practice follows {NAME}. Rebbi asked {NAME}; {NAME} said, so was the question: What is {NAME} reason? {NAME} said, so was the question: What did they see to say that practice follows {NAME}? He told him, did you not teach us so: “they shall inherit”? So is the Mishnah: “they shall take.” [Rebbi] La said, even following him who said “inherit”, is not the power of the court strengthened? As you say, nobody can transfer property using the language of gift; here he may do it. Similarly, nobody can transfer property using the language of inheritance; here he may do it.
[Bava Batra 8:5.3] There, we have stated: “{NAME} said, if she dies, he should inherit from her since he made a condition contradicting what is written in the Torah.” {NAME} in the name of Rav: “Since he made a condition contradicting what is written in the Torah and anybody’s condition contradicting what is written in the Torah is invalid”? Conditions other than for money matters. But here we are dealing with a money matter! What is Rav’s reason? Because in the end he acquired it. {NAME} said, practice follows {NAME}, for {NAME} said, if she sold or gave away, the rule should be that it is valid. Then why did they say that her sale is invalid? Lest she smuggle away her properties from her husband and say, they are mine. {NAME} had a case before the rabbis and they obligated him. He came before {NAME} who told him, enter your properties. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Did not Rav say, because in the end he acquired it. Did not {NAME} say, practice follows {NAME}? Did not {NAME} say, go and enter your properties? Who are these rabbis? The rabbis of {NAME}.
[Bava Batra 8:5.4] “And he shall inherit from her.” I could think that just as he inherits from her, she should inherit from him. The verse says, “from her.” He inherits from her, she does not inherit from him. {NAME} said, the words of the Sages are that her father inherits from her, her brothers inherit from her. {NAME} objected: If you say that the inheritance status of a woman is not from the Torah, should he not inherit from his preliminarily wedded wife? As you say there, “the one close to him,” not the preliminarily wedded one, so also here, “the one close to him,” not the preliminarily wedded one. {NAME} objected: If you say that a woman does not inherit by the word of the Torah, should not the husband inherit the expectancy like existing property? {NAME} said, so did Rebbi teach: The husband does not take the expectancy like that which is at hand. {NAME} said, there is the first-born whose inheritance is from the Torah but he does not take the expectancy like that which is at hand.
[Bava Batra 8:5.5] {NAME} said: About those who write, if she should die without children, all that was hers shall revert to her father. This is a stipulation about money; the stipulation is valid.
[Bava Batra 8:5.6] “Segub fathered Jair,” etc. From where did Jair have cities on Mount Gilead? But he married a woman from the daughters of Manasse who died and he inherited from her. If you would say that the inheritance from a wife was not a word of the Torah it should not say that “Jair had” but that “Segub had.” Similarly, “{NAME} died.” From where did Phineas have property on the Mountain of Ephraim? But he married a woman from the daughters of Ephraim and inherited from her. If you would say that the inheritance from a wife was not a word of the Torah it should say that “Eleazar had” not that “Phineas had.”
[Bava Batra 8:6.1] MISHNAH: If one writes his properties over to others while neglecting his children, what he did is done but the Sages do not approve of him. {NAME} says, if his children did not behave properly, let him be well remembered.
[Bava Batra 8:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If one writes his properties over to others,” etc. {NAME} said, about one who writes his properties over to others while neglecting his children, the verse says: “their sins were on their bones.” As the following: A person deposited his properties with {NAME} and told him, if my sons will be useful give them half and keep half. His sons came and took half. Later they came to appeal against him. He told them, your father said only: If my sons will be useful give them half and keep half. Now you are badly educated, return to me what I gave to you.
[Bava Batra 8:7.1] MISHNAH: He who says, this is my son, is to be believed. This is my brother, he is not to be believed but he shall split his part with him; if he dies the properties shall return to their origin. If he received property from another source, his brother shall inherit with him. If somebody died and a will was found tied to his hip, this is nothing. If in it he transferred property to another, whether of the heirs or not of the heirs, his words are confirmed.
[Bava Batra 8:7.2] HALAKHAH: “He who says, this is my son, is to be believed,” etc. If it was the general belief that he was his son, but at the moment of his death he said, he is not my son, or about one not his son he said, he is my son, he is believed. If he stood near the toll collector and said, he is my son and then changed and said, he is my slave, he is believed. He is my slave, and then said, he is my son, he cannot be believed. Some Tannaïm state, he is to be believed. {NAME} said, for example those Nabateans who particularly use their sons as slaves.
[Bava Batra 8:7.3] “If somebody said that all his property should be given to X, a Cohen, and [the estate] contained slaves, even if [the Cohen] said ‘I cannot have them’ they eat heave. {NAME} said, since he said ‘I cannot have them’, the heirs acquired them.” {NAME} said, they disagree if he did not specify. How do we hold? If it is clear that he wants them, everybody agrees that his slaves may eat heave. If it is clear that he does not want them, everybody agrees that the heirs acquired them. But we deal with the case that he did not specify, where the rabbis think that at the start he wanted them and then he changed his mind. {NAME} said, since he said ‘it is impossible for me’, the heirs acquired them.
[Bava Batra 8:7.4] It was stated: “{NAME} says: A will invalidates a will, a gift does not invalidate a gift.” {NAME}: {NAME} and {NAME} both are saying that in any case where he can invalidate his will if he recuperates, he also can repeal his gift. As the following: {NAME} sister wrote her property over to {NAME}. She needed money and sold it to her husband. After she died, he came to protest against him. He asked him, why did you not claim it during her lifetime? He answered, I did not want to cause her pain. Nevertheless, {NAME} removed it.
[Bava Batra 8:8.1] MISHNAH: One who writes his properties over to his sons must write: “from today and after my death,” the words of {NAME}. {NAME} said, it is unnecessary. If one writes his properties over to his son for the time after his death, the father cannot sell them because they are written over to the son; the son cannot sell because they are in the father’s possession. If the father sold, they are sold until he dies. If the son sold, the buyer has no claim until the father dies. The father harvests and feeds anybody he pleases; what becomes part of his estate belongs to the heirs.
[Bava Batra 8:8.2] HALAKHAH: “One who writes his properties over to his sons,” etc. {NAME} brought a case before {NAME}. “From today after his death,” his gift is a gift. “From today and after death” it is no bill of divorce. The colleagues say, so he told him: this is no condition. {NAME} said, so he told him: It applies neither to bills of divorce nor to gifts. {NAME} said, for a gift; since he said “from today”, the gift is clear. Why did he write “after death”? To reserve the yield to himself. But in bills of divorce, since he wrote “from today” in the bill, it would be a separation. Why did he write “after death”? To reserve her body to himself. {NAME} said before {NAME}, not to reserve her earnings for himself? He answered, we do not find a woman married to one man and her earnings belonging to another. {NAME} confirmed him and called him “son of the Torah.”
[Bava Batra 8:8.3] “If somebody says, I freed my slave Ṭabi, I freed him, I shall free him, he is free, this one is free; then he acquired.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: But only by a document. “He should be freed, Rebbi says, he acquired, but the Sages say, he did not acquire.”
[Bava Batra 8:8.4] If someone said, field X I gave to Y, it is given to him, it should be his, Y should inherit my property, Y should take possession of my property, he did not say anything. It should be given to him as a gift, Rebbi says, he acquired, but the Sages say, he did not acquire; but one forces the heirs to fulfill the deceased’s words. It was stated: {NAME} says, also if one writes διέθεμεν in Greek it is a gift. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: I turned to all linguists to know what is διέθεμεν and nobody told me anything.
[Bava Batra 8:8.5] One who said, my property should be given to X, if X died to Y, if Y died to Z. The one who was mentioned earlier receives the property earlier. If the second died during the first’s lifetime, the first one has the usufruct; when he dies the property reverts to heirs of the bequeather. If the third died during the second’s lifetime, the first one has the usufruct; when he dies the property reverts to heirs of the bequeather. If both the second and the third die during the first’s lifetime, the first has the usufruct and acquired the real estate, the words of Rebbi. {NAME} said, he only has the usufruct. {NAME} said, practice follows Rebbi. {NAME} said, Rebbi agrees that he cannot dispose of it by a death-bed will. {NAME} said, not even as a gift from a healthy person. As in the following: A woman wrote her properties over to a certain man. She needed money and sold it to her husband. {NAME} brought the case before {NAME}. Did not {NAME} say, Rebbi agrees that he cannot dispose of it by a death-bed will? {NAME} said to him, is that not the gift of a healthy person? Since the husband of this woman is obligated to provide for her food, is that not like a death-bed will? So far, he is obligated to provide for her bread and legumes. Maybe eggs? Maybe chicken? Since it was stated that the first has the usufruct and acquired the real estate, that means that she may sell the property even in order to eat delicacies. {NAME} said, it was stated there that her burial is part of her upkeep. If she did not have a burial site, since it was stated that the first has the usufruct and acquired the real estate, it means that he may sell the real estate and acquire a burial site.
[Bava Batra 8:8.6] {NAME} said: About those who write, “if she hates, if she is hated”. This is a stipulation about money; the rabbis upheld it.
[Bava Batra 8:9.1] MISHNAH: If he left adult and underage sons, the adult ones cannot be provided for at the expense of the underaged, nor the underaged fed at the expense of the adults, but they split evenly. If the adult ones wed, the underaged may wed. But if the underaged said, we want to have weddings just as you had, one does not listen to them, because what their father gave them, he gave. If he left adult and underage daughters, the adult ones cannot be provided for at the expense of the underaged, nor the underaged fed at the expense of the adults, but they split evenly. If the adult ones wed, the underaged may wed. But if the underaged said, we want to have weddings just as you had, one does not listen to them. It is a restriction about daughters which does not exist for sons, that daughters will be fed at the expense of sons but not at the expense of daughters.
[Bava Batra 8:9.2] HALAKHAH: “If he left adult and underage sons” etc. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Could the older ones take 100 barrels, each worth twenty denars, and the younger ones take 100 barrels, each worth ten denars? He told him, what these take, those should be taking.
[Bava Batra 9:1.1] MISHNAH: If somebody die and is survived by sons and daughters. If the estate is large, the sons inherit and the daughters will be sustained. If the estate is small, the daughters shall be sustained and the sons shall go begging. Admon said, because I am a male, shall I lose? {NAME} said, I am convinced by Admon’s statement.
[Bava Batra 9:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody die and is survived by sons and daughters,” etc. So is the Mishnah: “the daughters shall be sustained and the sons shall go (begging) [peddling].
[Bava Batra 9:1.3] {NAME} in the name of Rav: That there should be twelve months of sustenance for all of them. {NAME} said, this is the opinion of {NAME}, but the words of the Sages are, until they reach adulthood or are married. That is both a leniency and a restriction. Sometimes they are close to adulthood, sometimes far from adulthood. They asked before {NAME}, what did you hear from {NAME}? He said to them, I did not hear anything from him concerning this matter except what {NAME} asked before {NAME}: what if there was sustenance for twelve months but the estate diminished in value? He answered him, since they started with permission, they started.
[Bava Batra 9:1.4] {NAME} and {NAME}. One said, only if at the end there be sustenance for twelve months. But the other said, even from the start. If there was not sustenance for all of them for twelve months but they increased it so that how there is sustenance for all of them for twelve months? {NAME} said, let us hear from the following: If the heirs sold, they sold from their own property. So much more, if they increased it, they should be able to divide it. If there was sustenance for all of them for twelve months and a widow to support, may the sons say to the daughters: you have sustenance only for twelve months? {NAME} said, let us hear from the following: “If the orphans said, we accept the properties of our father for the value of an extra denar, one does not listen to them.” {NAME} asked: if there was sustenance for all of them for twelve months and a widow to support, may the sons say to the daughters: you have sustenance only for twelve months? But this means, only if there was sustenance for all of them for twelve months, except for ketubah of the wife, except for the sustenance of the widow, except for the dowries of the daughters, except for loans by document, except for loans by witnesses, except for her burial. The widow and the daughters are of equal rank. The widow and the sons are of equal rank. The widow does not push the daughters aside and the daughters do not push the widow aside. Sometimes the widow pushes the daughters out by means of the sons. Just as the widow pushes out the daughters by means of the sons, should the widow not push out the sons? She might claim her ketubah and lose her right to sustenance.
[Bava Batra 9:1.5] As the following: {NAME} widow was wasting the estate. His sons came before {NAME}. He said to them, what can one do for you; they are stupid. When they left, they said, let us ask the scribe what to do. He told them: Behave as if you would sell of the real estate and she will demand her ketubah and will no longer have support. After some time she came before {NAME}. He said, It should come over me if I had told them anything. What can one do, this one was hit by predatory people.
[Bava Batra 9:1.6] {NAME} in the name of [Rav]; {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Practice follows Ḥanan in his two statements; practice does not follow Admon in his seven statements. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: In every case in which {NAME} said, I am convinced by Admon’s statement, practice follows Admon.
[Bava Batra 9:1.7] {NAME} said, one can transfer benefits to the fetus; {NAME} said, one cannot transfer benefits to the fetus. A baraita disagrees with {NAME}. “If a proselyte died and Jews plundered his estate, then it became known that he had a son or that his wife was pregnant, everybody is required to return [what he took]. If they returned everything and then the son died or his wife had a miscarriage, the last one in possession acquires it.” Did the first group acquire or not? Explain it, because of hopelessness and it does not even disagree with {NAME}. Or should the last one not have acquired it? Still it is because of hopelessness.
[Bava Batra 9:2.1] MISHNAH: If he is survived by sons, daughters, and a sexless child, if the estate is large the males push him to the females; if the estate is small the females push him to the males. If somebody says, in case my wife gives birth to a male, he shall take a mina; if she gave birth to a male he takes a mina. But if a female 200, if she gave birth to a female she takes 200. If a male a mina, if a female 200, if she gave birth to a male and a female, the male takes a mina and the female 200. If she gave birth to a sexless child, he does not take anything. If he said, any that my wife shall give birth to shall take, and if there is no heir but him, he inherits everything.
[Bava Batra 9:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If he is survived by sons, daughters,,” etc. It was stated: “If somebody says, he who brings me the news that my wife gave birth to a male shall take 200”: if his wife gave birth to a male he takes 200. If she gave birth to a female he shall take a mina”: if his wife gave birth to a female he takes a mina. If it was a male and a female, he only takes a mina.” {NAME} said, the pain about the daughter invalidates the joy about the son.
[Bava Batra 9:3.1] MISHNAH: If he is survived by adult and underage children and the adult ones improved the property, the improvement goes to the estate. But if they said, make an inventory of what our father left and we are going to work and profit from it, they improved it for themselves. Similarly, a woman who improved the property improved for the estate. But if she said: see what my husband left for me, I shall work it and eat from it; then she improved it for herself.
[Bava Batra 9:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If he is survived by adult and underage children,” etc. {NAME} said, “if they said” in court. In the House of {NAME} they said, even a jug. Rav said, even a basket, even an axe. {NAME} stated: Even a needle, even a thread to tie down.
[Bava Batra 9:3.3] {NAME} said, if somebody definitively married off his son in a house, the latter acquired it. {NAME} stated, the house but not the movables. {NAME} divided the dining hall between himself and his son. {NAME} asked {NAME}: If the ceremony was in the bedroom but the wedding party was in the dining room, what is the rule? He told him, one does not see him leaving.
[Bava Batra 9:3.4] {NAME} said: One divides for the underaged because of the adults. But if the underaged found something additional and protested? {NAME} said, they have to swear for them. {NAME} said, everywhere the burden of proof is on the claimant except in this case. The Great {NAME} says, without contract brothers are co-owners up to three generations. Rebbi [Yose] {NAME} said, also {NAME} did instruct in this sense.
[Bava Batra 9:3.5] {NAME} said, if a son was seen separated during his father’s lifetime, what he accumulated, he accumulated for himself. As the following: A person learned to be a barber. His brother wanted to share with him. The case came before {NAME} who said, do we say that if a person found something, his brothers share with him? A person became an agent. His brother wanted to share with him. The case came before {NAME} who said, do we say that if a person went into robbery, his brothers share with him? A {NAME}, {NAME}, wanted to share with him. He told him, brother Alexander, do you not know that our father left us thousands?
[Bava Batra 9:3.6] “Similarly, a woman,” etc. {NAME} said, “if she said” in court.
[Bava Batra 9:4.1] MISHNAH: If one of co-owning brothers was requisitioned, he was requisitioned from the estate. If he fell sick and was healed, the medical costs are his own. If some of the brothers together sent a wedding gift during their father’s lifetime, if a corresponding gift was returned, it returned to them in common since wedding gifts can be sued for in court. But if somebody’s friend sent him pitchers of wine or oil they cannot be sued for since they represent deeds of charity.
[Bava Batra 9:4.2] HALAKHAH: “If one of co-owning brothers,” etc. It was stated: If one of co-owning brothers was requisitioned for government service. If this was because of the sharecroppper, he takes because of the sharecropper. If because of the head of household, he takes as head of household. As the following: {NAME} was appointed to the city council. The case came before {NAME}. He said, if Naḥman who was caught has enough property, it should be given from his property; otherwise it should be given to him from the common estate.
[Bava Batra 9:4.3] If she fell sick and was healed, the medical costs are on the estate. It was stated: “{NAME} says, for any hurt which has a fixed medical fee, she is healed from her ketubah ; if it does not have a fixed medical fee, she is healed from the estate.” As the following: The eye of a female relative of {NAME} hurt. She came to {NAME}. He asked her: Did your doctor mention a fixed fee? If [the fee] is fixed, from your ketubah , if it is not fixed, your husband will give it to you. But did we not state: “Do not turn yourself into a pleader”, and did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}, it is forbidden to disclose a judgment to a party? They said, {NAME} knew her to be an honest woman; therefore, he disclosed it to her. If her husband wants a treatment at a fixed rate, but she wants one without fixed rate, does one not listen to her husband? {NAME} said, only if the case not be before him. But if the case be before him, he has to tell it as it is.
[Bava Batra 9:5.1] MISHNAH: If somebody sent bridal gifts to his father-in-law’s house, if he sent there for 100 minas and ate there a marriage meal for at least a denar’s worth, they cannot be collected. If he did not eat there a marriage meal, they can be collected. If he sent large bridal gifts which she is expected to bring with her to her husband’s house, they can be collected. Small bridal gifts which she is supposed to use in her father’s house cannot be collected.
[Bava Batra 9:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If somebody sent bridal gifts to his father-in-law’s house,” etc. A person sent to his preliminarily wedded wife large bridal gifts. His relatives told him not to taste anything there. He went, did not listen to them, and ate. The house collapsed; they kept everything.
[Bava Batra 9:5.3] A person sent to his preliminarily wedded wife 24 gourds filled with various kinds of agricultural produce between Passover and Pentecost. It was only a problem for the rabbis: from where did he bring flax and olive seeds?
[Bava Batra 9:5.4] {NAME} brought before {NAME} two radishes between New Year’s Day and the Fast. It was the year after a Sabbatical, and they were a camel’s load. He said to him, rabbi, are they not forbidden? Are they no aftergrowth? He said to him, they were sown after the end of the Sabbatical year. At that moment did Rebbi permit to buy vegetables immediately after the end of the Sabbatical year.
[Bava Batra 9:6.1] MISHNAH: If a bedridden person distributed all his properties to others but reserved any real estate his gift is permanent; if he did not reserve any real estate his gift is not permanent. If [in the document] it was not written “bedridden”; he says, I was bedridden, but they are saying, he was healthy, he must prove that he was bedridden, the words of {NAME}. But the Sages say, the burden of proof is on the claimants.
[Bava Batra 9:6.2] HALAKHAH: “If a bedridden person distributed all his properties to others,” etc. {NAME} in the name of Rav: If he reserved any movables, he did not do anything. But if he reserved money and bought real estate it is as if he reserved real estate. And what you say that if he did not reserve any real estate his gift is not a gift, if he did (not) recuperate. But if he did [not] recuperate, that is the case about which {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, they treated words of a bedridden person like those of a healthy person who wrote and delivered; but only if he died from that sickness. If a critically ill person distributed his property, whether on a weekday or on the Sabbath, what he did is valid. But if he was healthy [it is valid] only if he wrote “by money, or contract, or possession.”
[Bava Batra 9:6.3] {NAME} said: Somebody became possibly impure in an agricultural area whether in summer or in winter; this refersn to the dispute between {NAME} and the Sages. If he comes to ask in summer, one answers him according to the rules of summer; in the winter, one answers him according to the rules of winter. {NAME} said, only days close to the rainy season.
[Bava Batra 9:6.4] {NAME} in the name of Rebbi: The holder of documents is disadvantaged. {NAME} said to him, is that not the Mishnah: “If [in the document] it was not written ‘bedridden’ but he says, I was bedridden,” etc. {NAME} praised him “those who pour out gold from the wallet,” “my son, they should not be removed from your eyes,” etc. A young man was selling his properties. The case came before {NAME} and {NAME}. {NAME} said, the presumption is that they signed for a mentally capable person. {NAME} said, since he undertook to uproot the properties from the family, he has to bring proof. {NAME} said, the holder of documents is advantaged. {NAME} asked before {NAME}, how about Rebbi, since Rebbi said, the holder of documents is disadvantaged? He told him, everybody agrees that the holder of documents is advantaged. But how could you say that a case came before {NAME} who said, the presumption is that they signed for a mentally capable person. And you said, since he undertook to uproot the properties from the family to another family, he has to bring proof! He told him, I never said this. {NAME} said before {NAME}, even if {NAME} wants to deny it, did not {NAME} say in the name of Rebbi: The holder of documents is disadvantaged. {NAME} said to him, is that not the Mishnah? This is the opinion of the Sages who follow Rebbi.
[Bava Batra 9:6.5] {NAME} in the name of Rav: Practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} said, the Mishnah is inverted. In what is the Mishnah inverted? The senior colleagues said, “witnesses.” The junior colleagues said, no “witnesses”: did they only disagree about witnesses? {NAME} said, since I told you to write “bedridden” and you did not write it, you are liers.
[Bava Batra 9:7.1] MISHNAH: If somebody distributes his property orally, {NAME} says that whether he is healthy or critical, guaranteed properties can be acquired by money, or contract, or possession. Not guaranteed properties can only be acquired by drawing close. They said to him, it happened that the mother of the Bene Rokhel was sick and said, give my bonnet to my daughter, it is worth twelve minas. She died and the Sages confirmed her words. He answered them, the Bene Rokhel should have been buried by their mother.
[Bava Batra 9:7.2] HALAKHAH: So far if real estate and movables were at the same place. If real estate was at one place and movables elsewhere? {NAME} said, let us hear from the following: {NAME} said to them, it happened that a man from Meron was dwelling in Jerusalem who was rich in movables. He wanted to distribute them, to give them as gifts. They said to him, you cannot do that except if you acquire real estate. What did he do? He went and bought a rock near Jerusalem and said: The Northern part I give to X with a hundred sheep and a hundred amphoras of wine, the Southern part I give to Y with a hundred amphoras of oil. The matter came before the Sages, who upheld his words. {NAME} said before {NAME}: But was he not bedridden? For in general a person might give property rights only in writing, and here even orally. In general, a person might give only if real estate and movables are at the same place; here, however, the real estate was at one place and the movables elsewhere. [Sanhedrin 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Money matters are judged by three [judges]; robberies and injuries by three [judges], damages, half damages, double restitution quadruple and quintuple restitution. The rapist, the seducer, and the calumniator are judged by three [judges], the words of {NAME}; but the Sages say that the calumniator is judged by 23 because it might be a capital case.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Money matters are judged by three [judges],” etc. From where comes this? These shall be the laws of procedure to you , I would say that both civil cases and criminal cases are subject to the rules of verification and examination.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.3] From where that civil cases are heard by three [judges]? The owner shall go to the judge , he added here one judge. Before the judge , these are two. Whom the judges will find guilty, these are three, the words of {NAME}. {NAME} said, the first mention introduces the subject; one does not infer anything from introductions. But before the judge, there is one. Whom the judges will find guilty, there are two. No court may be even-numbered, so one adds another one; this makes three.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.4] Rebbi said, the verse speaks about two. You say about two, or maybe it is only about one? What He said, it is not written “whom the judge will find guilty” but whom the judges will find guilty . No court may be even-numbered, so one adds another one; this makes three.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.5] {NAME} asked. According to Rebbi, should not civil suits be heard by five; should sentence not be passed by 23? It was found stated by (Rebbi) {NAME}: Since the Torah said, kill by a vote of the majority, kill by the testimony of witnesses. Since witnesses must be two, a majority also must be two. No court can be even-numbered; one adds another one. This makes five.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.6] Do not robberies and injuries fall under the same rules? It was found that {NAME} stated: These are the procedures which you shall put before them. It serves to explain to you the plain sense of the verse. This follows {NAME}.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.7] {NAME}, when two people came before him for judgment and told him, “on condition that you judge us by the law of the Torah,” told them, “the law of the Torah I do not know, but He Who knows thoughts should collect from those people. You have to accept what I shall tell you.”
[Sanhedrin 1:1.8] When a person came to {NAME} to have a suit decided before him, he told him: “You should know before Whom you are standing, before Him Who commanded and the world came into existence, as it is said: The two people who are quarrelling shall stand before the Eternal, not before {NAME}.”
[Sanhedrin 1:1.9] It was stated: Forty years before the Temple was destroyed, criminal jurisdiction was removed from Israel, and in the days of Simeon ben (Šetaḥ) civil jurisdiction was removed. {NAME} said, praised be the Merciful, for I am not intelligent enough to judge.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.10] {NAME} said, if two men acted as judges, their judgment stands, but they are called an insolent court. {NAME} and {NAME} both are instructing: Even if two men acted as judges, their judgment is no judgment. There, we have stated: “If he rendered judgment, acquitted the guilty and condemned the innocent, declared the pure impure or the impure pure, what he did is done but he has to pay from his own pocket.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: if they told him, we accept you as if you were two. What are we dealing with? If his error was that he judged them on his discretion, then what he did is done. If his error was that he judged them by Torah law, why should he pay from his own pocket? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: if they told him, we accept you as if you were three on condition that you judge us by Torah law. He erred and judged them on his discretion. What he did is done, but since he erred and judged them on his discretion, he has to pay from his own pocket because he was presumptuous to judge alone by Torah law, as we have stated: “Do not judge sitting alone, for only One judges sitting alone.”
[Sanhedrin 1:1.11] {NAME} said, even the Holy One, praise to Him, does not judge alone, as it is said: all the hosts of Heaven were standing by Him, to His right side and to His left. These vote to acquit, those to convict. Even though He does not judge alone, He signs alone, as it is said: really I shall tell you what is noted in true writing. {NAME} said, the Holy One, praise to Him, never does anything in His world unless He took counsel with the Heavenly Court. What is the reason? True is the statement and a large host. When is the seal of the Holy One, praise to Him, true? When He took counsel with the Heavenly Court. {NAME} said, any place where it is said “the Eternal, Almighty,” it is He and His Heavenly Court. The paradigm of all is: and the Eternal spoke evil about him.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.12] What is the seal of the Holy One, praise to Him? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, “true.” What means “true”? {NAME} said, that He is a Living Power and the King of this World. {NAME} said, א is the start of the alphabet, מ the middle, and ת the end. To say, I, the Eternal, am First, I did not receive anything from another. Besides Me there is no supreme power , for I have no co-owner. And with the last, I shall be , I shall not in the future turn it over to anybody else.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.13] {NAME} and {NAME} had a lawsuit before {NAME}; the judgment was for {NAME}. {NAME} wanted to complain; {NAME} came and taught: If an expert forced his opinion as a judgment, his judgment stands.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.14] {NAME} was sitting as sole judge in the inclining synagogue of Caesarea. His students said to him, did the rabbi not teach: “Do not judge sitting alone”? [Sanhedrin 1:1.15] {NAME} went with a lawsuit before the Elder {NAME}. He took a student to sit with him. But did we not state: “A father and his son, a teacher and his student, the two are counted as one.” Let us say that he was both student and colleague, like {NAME} to {NAME}.

[Sanhedrin 1:1.18] A person brought a suit before {NAME}, He told him, bring me a person who climbs the date palm instead of me.

[Sanhedrin 1:1.20] A person made a Cohen impure. The case came before {NAME} who made him eat profane food. They wanted to say that one deducts the price of heave from the amount.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.21] It was stated: {NAME} says, the person who arranges a compromise is sinning, and the one who praises a compromiser is like a blasphemer before the Omnipresent, as it is said: he who blesses a compromiser slanders the Eternal! [Sanhedrin 1:1.23] {NAME} says, why does the verse say, he who blesses unlawful gain slanders the Eternal ? These are Joseph’s brothers, as it is is said: What is the gain if we slay our brother, etc.”
[Sanhedrin 1:1.24] “{NAME} says, it is a good deed to mediate a compromise, as it is said: Truth and judgment of peace . If there is truth, there is no judgment of peace. If there is peace, there is no judgment of truth. What is truth containing a judgment of peace? I am saying, this is compromise.”
[Sanhedrin 1:1.25] “If somebody judged correctly, absolved the innocent and condemned the guilty, the verse counts it as if he practiced kindness both towards the innocent and towards the guilty. Kindness towards the innocent, because he returned his money to him. And towards the guilty, for he removed the proceeds of robbery from his hands.” {NAME} said, judgment and judgment is written in the verse: “Truth and judgment of peace judge in your gates.”
[Sanhedrin 1:1.26] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does one act following that Tanna, as it was stated: “{NAME} says, sometimes you are empowered to propose a compromise, sometimes you are not empowered to propose a compromise. How is this? Two come before a judge; before he heard their arguments, or after he heard their arguments but does not know how to correctly apply the law, he may tell them, go and work out a compromise. After you heard their arguments and know how to correctly apply the law, you may not propose a compromise, as it is said: One may remove the beginning of a quarrel like water; before it becomes manifest, the quarrel may be abandoned. Before the quarrel became manifest, you are permitted to abandon it; after the quarrel became manifest, you are not permitted to abandon it.” {NAME} said, even compromise needs intelligent decision.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.27] “{NAME} said: If two people appeared before a judge, one decent and one agressive. Before he started to hear their arguments, he may tell them, I will not hear your case, lest the agressive one lose his case and become his enemy. After he started hearing their arguments, he may not tell them, I will not hear your case, for it is said, do not be afraid of anybody.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.28] “{NAME} says, if somebody was sitting next to a judge and saw a benefit for the poor and a detriment for the rich, from where that he should not keep silent? For it is said, do not be afraid of anybody.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.29] The judges have to know with Whom they judge, and the witnesses have to know before Whom they are testifying: before Him Who commanded and the world came into existence, as it is said, the two people who are quarrelling shall stand before the Eternal, and it is said, the Almighty stands in the assembly of the judges. So Josaphat told the judges, look what you are doing, for you do not judge for man, but for the Eternal . How is it possible for flesh and blood to judge his Creator? But the Holy One, praise to Him, said: I said that Reuben should have 100 denars and Simeon nothing. You take from one and give it to the other. I have to repay it to him, and will Myself be paid by this man.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.30] It was stated: “{NAME} says, judgment is passed by three [judges], a compromise is made by two. The compromise is stronger than the judgment in that two [judges] who judged can repeal their judgment but two who negotiated a compromise cannot repeal.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.31] “The rapist and the seducer,” etc. {NAME} said, they disagree about the preliminarily married adolescent female. {NAME} says, she loses her ketubah in a court of three and is stoned in a court of 23; but the Sages say, at the same place which sentences her to be stoned she loses her ketubah. But in the case of the calumniator, everybody agrees that by the court in which the witnesses are stoned, the husband is flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas. {NAME} said to him, would they differ where it was not stated? But they differ about the calumniator! {NAME} says, he is flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas by the judgment of three and the witnesses are stoned by the judgment of 23; but the rabbis say, by the court in which the witnesses are stoned, the husband is flogged and pays 100 tetradrachmas. But in the case of the preliminarily married adolescent female, everybody agrees that at the same place which sentences her to be stoned she loses her ketubah. It turns out that {NAME} follows {NAME} and {NAME} follows {NAME}.
[Sanhedrin 1:1.32] {NAME} asked: Following {NAME}, should an ox which is stoned have to pay damages by a court of three and be stoned by 23? {NAME} told him, the rules of an ox which is stoned are all about money; it is a decision of the verse that it should be stoned.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.1] MISHNAH: Whipping by three [judges]; in the name of {NAME} they said, by 23. The lengthening of a month by three [judges], the intercalation of a year by three [judges], the words of {NAME}. {NAME} says, one starts with three, one discusses with five, and one votes with seven. But if they voted with three, it is intercalated. The leaning of Elders and the breaking of the calf’s neck by three [judges], the words of {NAME}, but {NAME} says, by five. Ḥalîṣah and repudiations by three [judges], [redemption of] the growth of the fourth year and Second Tithe whose value is not known by three [appraisers], also of Temple dedications by three. Estimations of movables by three [appraisers], {NAME} says that one of them must be a Cohen; of real estate nine and a Cohen. The same holds for humans. Capital crimes [are judged] by 23. The participants in active or passive bestiality [is judged] by 23, as it is said, you shall slay the woman and the animal , and it says, and you shall slay the animal . The bull to be stoned [is judged] by 23, as it is said, the bull shall be stoned, also its owner shall die ; like the owner’s death sentence so is the ox’s death sentence. The wolf and the lion, the bear, and the tiger, and the panther, and the snake are sentenced to death by 23. {NAME} says, anyone quick to kill them is meritorious; {NAME} says, they are sentenced by 23.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Whipping by three [judges],” etc. {NAME} asked: Should not a sentence of whipping be passed by 23 [judges], since sometimes he might die from the whippings, so that it is a case of potential death sentence.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.3] {NAME} understood everything from here: May the Eternal bless you and preserve you, from here that one starts with three. May the Eternal illuminate His Presence for you and be gracious to you, from here that one continues with five. May the Eternal turn His Presence to you and give you peace, from here that one finishes with seven.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.4] {NAME} understood everything from the following: The chief executioner took … the three guards of the threshhold , from here that one starts with three. And five men from the king’s entourage , from here that one continues with five. And seven men from the King’s entourage , from here that one finishes with seven.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.5] {NAME} said, from there the great Synhedrion of all of Israel. The minister of the executioners took Seraiah the Chief Priest and Zephania the priest , these are two. And seven men from the king’s entourage , this makes nine. And sixty men from the People of the Land , this makes seventy minus one. And from the city one eunuch , this makes seventy. There are Tannaïm who state seventy-one: The chief executioner took … the three guards of the threshhold, and seven men from the king’s entourage, and sixty men from the People of the Land, and from the city he took one eunuch, this makes seventy-one. And why is he called a eunuch? Because he transposes practice.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.6] One verse says five, the other verse says seven. The latter includes the two clerks of court.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.7] There is no lengthening of the month, but sanctification of the month. {NAME} says, sanctification of the month needs no less than ten [participants] 120 . Should Fellows be able to enter for the sanctification of the month? {NAME} said, I was a Fellow and {NAME} took me to the sanctification of the month, but I do not know whether I was counted or not. It is obvious that he was not counted, but why? Was it because he was his son-in-law, or because Fellows are nor able to enter for the sanctification of the month? {NAME} said, I was a Fellow when {NAME} took me to the sanctification of the month and I was counted. This implies that Fellows enter for the sanctification of the month.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.8] Are Fellows able to enter for the intercalation of the year? Let us hear from the following: It happened that {NAME} said, call seven Elders to a meeting on the upper floor, but eight entered. He asked, who is the one who entered without permission? {NAME} minor stood up and said, I came up here without permission since I have a practical problem and I have to ask advice on it. {NAME} told him, you compare to Eldad and Medad; if I had said “two”, you would have been one of them. Nevertheless, they did not intercalate on that day but talked about themes in the Torah and intercalated the next day.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.9] lt was stated: If the Synhedrion saw the killer. Some Tannaïm state: two of them become witnesses and testify before the rest of them. There are Tannaïm who state that they all are witnesses and have to go and testify before other [judges]. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: As they differ here, so they differ about testimony for the New Moon.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.10] Why cannot always one stand up and one sit down? There is a difference because a witness cannot be a judge. {NAME} knew testimony for somebody. He came and wanted to have the suit judged before {NAME}, and denied all. {NAME} told him, because you know that (Rebbi) [Rav] Huna is an important person you deny everything. What if {NAME} went and testified against you in another court? {NAME} asked him, does one do that? He answered, yes. {NAME} recused himself from that suit, went, and testified before another court.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.11] {NAME} stated: You shall sanctify the Fiftieth Year . You shall sanctify years but not months. But did we not state: “The president of the court says: sanctified”? What means sanctified? Confirmed. It was stated: For sanctifying months one starts with the most senior person. {NAME} said, the Mishnah says this: “The president of the court says: sanctified.” It was stated, for intercalation of the (month) [year] one starts from the side. {NAME} said, but this lower house do not proceed in this way, for they did not hear what {NAME} and {NAME}, {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: For lengthening the month one starts with the most senior person, for intercalating the year one starts from the side. When {NAME} was participating as the most junior person, they told him, say: “this year is sanctified in its intercalation.” He said, “this year is sanctified in intercalation.” {NAME} said, look at the language which the smith’s son taught us. If he had said, “in its intercalation,” I would have said that this refers to the eleven days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar one, but [he said] “in intercalation”, that the Sages added thirty days to it. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: For intercalation one follows the date of ordination. In the Academy one follows usage; each one gives his opinion at his place and sums up. For example, {NAME} started, {NAME} and {NAME} summed up. {NAME} started, {NAME} and {NAME} summed up. {NAME} started, {NAME} and {NAME} summed up. {NAME} was ordained before {NAME}, but {NAME} participated in intercalation before {NAME} was invited. He said, the person who formulated the tradition does not respect it for himself.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.12] {NAME} was standing praying. {NAME} came and stood behind him in prayer. When {NAME} had finished, he sat down in order not to walk by him. {NAME} spent a long time praying. After he finished, he told him, is that your way to make your teacher suffer? He told him, I am a descendant of the House of Eli, of whom it is written: if the sin of the House of Eli would be atoned for by sacrifice and offering. By sacrifice and offering it cannot be atoned for, but it can be atoned for by prayer. He prayed for him, he reached old age while his fingernails remained red like those of a small child.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.13] They preferred an old man to {NAME} for intercalation but had to remove him by the other door. He said, this is their reward. Did he not hear what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: It happened that the year was intercalated by three cow hands. One said, in Adar, early and late grain sprout together. One said, in Adar the ox will die naked and try to strip off his hide under the fig tree. One said, if in Adar the East wind blows, open your jaws and go towards it. And we see that this year nothing of these applies. They intercalated the year on their word. {NAME} said, because the Court agreed with them. {NAME} said, but they all have to agree to the same reason. But since they all agree with one another it was that they all agreed as to the reason.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.14] Why was {NAME} offended by this? He was worried about what {NAME} said, since {NAME} said: My hand will be against the prophets who see … vain things, in my people’s council they shall not be; that is [the secret of] intercalation; in the documents of the House of Israel they will not be inscribed; that is ordination; and to the earth of Israel they shall not come; that is the Land of Israel. When {NAME} came here, he said, I have one. When they ordained him, he said, I have two.When he was asked to participate in the intercalation, he said, I have all three [with me].
[Sanhedrin 1:2.15] {NAME} in the name of Rav: The reason of {NAME}: When the Heavenly Court sees that the earthly Court sanctifies it, they also sanctify it.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.16] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. It happened that 24 people appointed by the House of Rebbi entered to intercalate the year at Lydda when an evil eye entered with them and they all died at the same time. From that time on they removed it from Judea and established it in Galilee. They also wanted to remove the signal. {NAME} told them, do we not even want to leave a remembrance in Judea? But we find that they intercalated the year at Baˋalat. This Baˋalat is sometimes [mentioned as being] in Judea, sometimes in Dan. Elteqe, and Gibbeton, and Ba ˋ alat are from Judea. Ba ˋ alah, and Iyyim, and Asem are from Dan, and we find that they intercalated the year at Baˋalat. Let us say that the houses were in Judea and the fields in Dan. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Is Lydda not in Judea? He answered, yes. Then why does one not intercalate there? He told him, because they are coarse of spirit and have little learning. He turned his face and saw {NAME} and {NAME}. He said to him, presently you made me insult rabbis.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.17] “For three indications one intercalates a year: because of fresh grain, the equinox, and tree fruits. One intercalates because of two of them, because of a single one does not intercalate; but if they intercalated, it is intercalated. If fresh grain was one of the reasons, everybody was happy. {NAME} said, also because of the equinox.”
[Sanhedrin 1:2.18] “For three regions one intercalates a year, because of Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee. One intercalates because of two of them, while because of one of them one does not intercalate; if they did intercalate it is not intercalated. If Judea was one of the reasons, everybody was happy since the ˋ Omer was brought from there.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.19] “One intercalates neither because of the cold, nor because of the rains; if they did intercalate it is not intercalated. One intercalates neither because of kid goats nor because of pigeon chicks, nor because of milk [lambs]; but all of them are ancillary reasons for the year. {NAME} said that {NAME} used to say: The sheep are thin and the pigeon chicks small; it appears good in my eyes and in those of my colleagues to add thirty days to the year.”
[Sanhedrin 1:2.20] “{NAME} said: it happened that {NAME} and the Elders were sitting on stairs on the Temple Mount; their scribe Joḥanan was sitting before them when {NAME} said to him, write: To our brothers in the Upper Southland and the Lower Southland, may you have much peace. We inform you that the time of liquidation has come, to deliver tithes from the sheaves of grain. To our brothers in the Upper Galilee and the Lower Galilee, may you have much peace. We inform you that the time of liquidation has come, to deliver tithes from the olive presses. To our brothers in the diaspora of Babylonia, the diaspora of Media, the diaspora of Greece, and all other diasporas of Israel, may you have much peace. We inform you that the sheep are thin, the pigeon chicks small, and springtime has not arrived; it appears good in my eyes and those of my colleagues to add thirty days to this year.”
[Sanhedrin 1:2.21] “One does not intercalate a year unless it be missing most of a month. How much is most of a month? 16 days. {NAME} says two thirds of a month, 21 days.” {NAME} said, only that the ˋ Omer should be brought at the end of Nisan of equinoxes. {NAME} said, before Passover. {NAME} said, only that lulav be taken at the end of Tishre of equinoxes.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.22] “One intercalates a year neither less than a month, nor more than a month; if it was intercalated, it is not intercalated.”
[Sanhedrin 1:2.23] “One intercalates neither in a Sabbatical year nor the year following a Sabbatical; but if it was intercalated it is intercalated. When does one usually intercalate? The year preceding a Sabbatical.” {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, that is before Rebbi permitted to import produce from outside the Land into the Land. But since Rebbi permitted to import produce from outside the Land into the Land, there is no difference between a Sabbatical and the remaining years of the Sabbatical cycle.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.24] {NAME} used to say: it is said, a man came from Baal Shalisha and brought to the Man of God first fruit bread, twenty loaves, etc. Since the year should have been intercalated, why did Elisha not intercalate? This teaches that it was a year of famine and people were eager for threshing floors.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.25] Some Tannaïm state: “One does not intercalate because of impurity.” {NAME} says, one intercalates, since we find that Hezekiah intercalated because of the impurity, as it is said: For most of the people from Ephraim, Manasse, Issachar, and Zevulun had not been purified, for they ate the Passover contrary to what is written, for Hezekiah had prayed, saying, the Eternal, the Benevolent, will pardon this. {NAME} says, even though he intercalated Nisan, it was Adar which was intercalated. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: Hezekiah forced the community to celebrate the Second Passover.”
[Sanhedrin 1:2.26] Some Tannaïm state: One intercalates because of impurity. Some Tannaïm state: One does not intercalate. He who says, one does not intercalate, from the following: for they ate the Passover contrary to what is written. How does the one who says one does not intercalate, explain contrary to what is written ? They intercalated in Nisan but one intercalates only in Adar. This follows what {NAME} said: they found the skull of Ornan the Yebusite under the altar.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.27] It is written: With all his heart he prepared himself to seek God, to act, and to teach law and justice in Israel. {NAME} and {NAME}. One said, with all he did for the purity of the Temple, he did not fully establish the purity of the Temple. One said, with all the good works he did, he did not fully do his duty for the purity of the Temple. It is written: They started on the first of the first month, and on the eighth day they entered the Eternal’s Hall and sanctified the Eternal’s House for three days; on the sixteenth of the month they finished. Could they not have eliminated all idolatry from there in one day? {NAME} said, because of Chaldean idols which were engraved in vermilion.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.28] Six things did Hezekiah do; with three they agreed, with three they did not agree. He dragged his father’s bones on a bier of ropes, he smashed the bronze snake, and he hid the table of medicines; they agreed. He closed the upper Giḥon spring, and he cut down the Temple doors, and he intercalated Nisan in Nisan; they disagreed.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.29] One does not intercalate before New Year’s Day; if they did intercalate it would be invalid. But for an urgent need one may intercalate immediately after New Year’s Day. Nevertheless, only Adar is intercalated. Rebbi says, Nisan was never lengthened. But did we not state: “If the New Moon appeared in time”? If it would appear; it did not appear. Rav said, Tishre was never lengthened. But did we not state: “If the month was long”? If it would be, it never was.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.30] “When they sanctified the year at Usha, on the first day {NAME}, led and recited following the opinion of {NAME}. {NAME} said, we did not follow this at Jabneh. On the second day, {NAME}, led and recited following {NAME}. {NAME} said, this we did follow at Jabneh.” But does this not mean that they sanctified it on the first and the second day? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: That year was disorganized. What is “on the first, on the second”? {NAME} in the name of Rav: The first year, the second year! But was it not stated: the first day, the second day?
[Sanhedrin 1:2.31] If they sanctified it before its time or after its lengthening, should I assume it was lengthened? The verse says, them, them; not these are My holidays ? Before its time, the 29 day; after its lengthening, the 32 day. From where that one intercalates for the year because of the diaspora who set out but did not yet arrive? The verse says, the Children of Israel. Make the holidays so they can be observed by all of Israel. {NAME} said, only if they had reached the river Euphrates.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.32] “One intercalates a year only in Judea, but if it was intercalated in Galilee it is validly intercalated. Ḥanina from Ono testified that, if it cannot be intercalated in Judea, one intercalates in Galilee.” One does not intercalate a year outside the Land; if it was intercalated, it is not validly intercalated. Look at it, one does not intercalate in Galilee; could one intercalate outside the Land? One does not intercalate in Galilee; but if it was intercalated it is validly intercalated. One does not intercalate outside the Land; if it was intercalated it is not intercalated if it was possible to intercalate in the Land of Israel; but if one cannot intercalate in the Land of Israel, one intercalates it outside the Land.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.33] Jeremiah intercalated outside the Land. Ezechiel intercalated outside the Land. {NAME} intercalated outside the Land. Ḥanania the nephew of {NAME} intercalated outside the Land. Rebbi sent him three letters through {NAME} and {NAME}. In one he wrote, to His holiness Ḥanania. And in one he wrote, the kid goats you left behind became rams. And in one he wrote, if you do not accept, go to the thistle desert, do the slaughtering and let Onias sprinkle. After the first [letter], he honored them. After the second, he honored them. After the third, he wanted to disgrace them. They said to him, you cannot do that since you already did honor us. {NAME} rose and read in the Torah: These are the holidays of Ḥanania the nephew of {NAME}. They said to him, the holidays of the Eternal. He told them, that is with us. {NAME} rose and concluded: For from Babylonia will Torah go forth and the Eternal’s word from Nahar-Peqod. They said to him, for from Zion will Torah go forth and the Eternal’s word from Jerusalem. He told them, that is with us. He went to complain about them to {NAME} at Nisibis. He said to him, follow them, follow them. He said to him, I do not know whom I left there. Who would tell me that they are knowledgeable in computations as I am? If they did not know the computations, they should listen to him. Since they are knowledgeable in computations as he is, he has to listen to them. He got up and rode on a horse. Where he reached, he reached. Where he did not reach, they continued to follow the corrupt [calendar].
[Sanhedrin 1:2.34] It is written: to the outstanding Elders in the diaspora. The Holy One, praise to Him, said: The Elders of the diaspora are very dear to me. But more beloved by Me is a small group in the Land of Israel than a great Synhedrion outside the Land. It is written: The craftsmen and the smiths one thousand, and you say so? {NAME} in the name of {NAME} and the rabbis. {NAME} said, one thousand craftsmen and one thousand smiths. But the rabbis say, together one thousand. {NAME} in the name of Rebbi [Ḥelbo said], these are the Fellows; but the rabbis say, these are the councilmen.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.35] {NAME}, when he received witnesses at Kallirhoë, used to say to them: you should know the importance of the testimony that comes from your mouths; how much rent money depends on your mouths. {NAME} said, if it is so, it is even a matter of criminal law. If somebody sleeps with a girl three years and one day old, he is stoned. The court decides to lengthen, if he sleeps with her he is not stoned. {NAME} said, I am calling to Almighty God, to the God Who decides with me. If a girl is three years and one day old, if the court decides to lengthen her hymen does (not) repair itself, otherwise it does [not] repair itself.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.36] “The leaning of Elders and the breaking of the calf’s neck by three [judges], the words of {NAME}, but {NAME} says, by five.” What is the reason of {NAME}? “[The Elders] shall lean,” two. No court has an even number of members; one adds another one; that makes three. What is the reason of {NAME}? “They shall lean,” two. “The Elders,” two. No court has an even number of members; one adds one; that makes five. And for the calf whose neck is broken, what is the reason of {NAME}? “Your Elders,” two, “and your judges,” two. No court has an even number of members; one adds one; that makes five. What is the reason of {NAME}? “Your elders, your judges,” two. No court has an even number of members; one adds another one; that makes three. Rebbi said, the words of {NAME} are reasonable for the breaking of the neck, for he does not refer to “they shall go out.” The words of {NAME} are reasonable for the leaning of the hands, for he does not refer to “they shall lean.” If you would say that the words of {NAME} are reasonable for the calf whose neck is broken, if he refers to “they shall lean”, he also should refer to “they shall go out.” It turns out that you have to say “they shall go out” two, “your Elders” two, “and your judges” two. No court has an even number of members; one adds one more; that makes seven. How does {NAME} explain “your Elders and your judges”? Your Elders who are your judges. It was stated: {NAME} says “your Elders,” that is the High Court; “and your judges,” these are king and High Priest.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.37] It was stated: Leanings by three [judges]. Is not leaning the same as leanings? There, they call ordination “leaning”.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.38] {NAME} said, in earlier times, every one was ordinating his students; for example {NAME} ordained {NAME} and {NAME}, {NAME} {NAME}, and {NAME} {NAME} and {NAME}. He said, {NAME} shall preside; the face of {NAME} became yellow. {NAME} told him, it is enough that I and your Creator recognize your power. They changed and honored this dynasty, saying: If a court ordained without the consent of the Patriarch, their ordination is no ordination, but if the Patriarch ordained without consent of the court, his ordination is ordination. They changed again and instituted that neither shall the Court ordain without consent of the Patriarch, nor the Patriarch without consent of the Court.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.39] It was stated: From earlier times, one was writing documents of ḥalîṣah : Before X and V did Z daughter of U perform ḥalîṣah for V son of W, by coming before us, removing his shoe from his right foot, spitting before us visible spittle on the ground, and saying: So shall be done to the man unwilling to build his brother’s house .
[Sanhedrin 1:2.40] It was stated: From earlier times one was writing documents of repudiation: Before X and Y did Z daughter of U repudiate V son of W, by coming before us: I do not like him, I do not want to stay with him, I do not agree to be married to him.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.41] {NAME} said, if somebody redeemed Temple dedications for more than their worth, it is redeemed. But if somebody redeemed Second Tithe for more than its worth, it is not redeemed. What is the difference between dedications and Second Tithe? {NAME} said, dedications have claimants, Second Tithe has no claimant. {NAME} asked, that is following him who says that it is not his property. But for him who says it is his property, what is the difference between dedications and Second Tithe? {NAME} said, the reason has already been explained: dedications have claimants, Second Tithe has no claimant.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.42] {NAME} asked before {NAME}: If the person was checked and he said, that was not what I intended? He answered him, when he will be checked.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.43] {NAME} said, if somebody redeemed Temple dedications without adding its fifth it is redeemed. But if somebody redeemed Second Tithe dedications without adding its fifth, it is not redeemed. What is the difference between dedications and Second Tithe? {NAME} said, because a person usually adds to his dedications. {NAME} asked, that is following him who says that it is not his property. But for him who says it is his property, what is the difference between Second Tithe and dedications? {NAME} said, did you not already give the reason? Because a person usually adds to his dedications.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.44] It was stated: “Temple dedications by three [appraisers].” That is, if one dedicated the body of a field. But if he said, I am vowing a mina for the Temple, let us hear from the following: “Appraisal of movables by three [appraisers].” Do there exist appraisals not of movables? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If somebody says, I am vowing my appraisal, and comes to settle his debt by real estate, one appraises it by ten [people], by movables by three. Is one who says, I am vowing my appraisal not like one who says, I am vowing my field’s value? But if he said, I am vowing a mina for the Temple, one appraises him by three [people]. Should he become rich, he will be judged by what he can afford.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.45] It was stated: One does not make public tender for slaves, securities, and movables. [What is public tender?] {NAME} said, announcement. {NAME} said, slaves lest they flee, securities and movables lest they be stolen. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Does this not imply that a slave be redeemed in front of three people? He answered him, yes. But did we not state: “Real estate nine and a Cohen. The same holds for humans”? He answered him, but the human here is a free person. {NAME} in the name of Rav: A case came before Rebbi who wanted to act following the rabbis. {NAME}, {NAME}, said to him: Rebbi, did you not teach us in your grandfather’s name, “except if he offered public tender”? He answered, yes, changed his mind, and acted following {NAME}.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.46] “Capital crimes [are judged] by 23.” {NAME} asked: Following {NAME}, should an ox which is stoned have to pay damages by a court of three and be stoned by 23? {NAME} told him, the rules of an ox which is stoned are all about money; it is a decision of the verse that it should be stoned.
[Sanhedrin 1:2.47] General אגנטוס asked {NAME}: the bull shall be stoned, also its owner shall die ? He answered, the robber’s partner is like the robber. When he had left, his students asked him, rabbi, this one you pushed away with a cane; what are you telling us? He said to them, it is written, the bull shall be stoned, also its owner shall die, like the owner’s death sentence so is the ox’s death sentence. Since the owner’s death sentence would be by a court of 23, investigation and cross-examination, so the ox’s death sentence is by a court of 23, investigation and cross-examination.
