[Sanhedrin 1:4.1] MISHNAH: The High Synhedrion had 71 members and a lower one 23 members. From where that the High Court has 71 members? For it is said: Assemble for me 70 men of the Elders of Israel, and Moses was presiding, that makes 71. {NAME} says, 70. From where that a lower court has 23 members? For it is said, the congregation shall judge, the congregation shall save . One congregation judges, one congregation saves, this makes twenty. And from where that a congregation consists of ten persons? As it is said, how long this evil congregation , without Joshua and Caleb. From where that one adds another three? From the interpretation of what is said, do not follow the majority to be unfavorable, I understand that He said, follow them to be favorable. Then why was it said, to bend after the majority ? Your bending to be favorable is not equal to your bending to be unfavorable. Your bending to be favorable shall be by one [vote] (witness), your bending to be unfavorable shall be by two. Since no court may be even-numbered, one adds another one to obtain 23. How many people shall live in a town that it may have a criminal court? 120. {NAME} said 230, that they might be commanders over tens.

[Sanhedrin 1:4.3] “From where that one adds another three, etc. It was stated: {NAME} said, in earlier times the ketubah of qualified women was signed only by priests, Levites, or Israel whose daughters were qualified to marry into the priesthood. {NAME} said, in earlier times there was no disagreement in Israel but the Synhedrion of 71 members were sitting in the free-stone hall; two courts of three members each were sitting, one in the glacis and one on the Temple Mount; and a court of 23 was sitting in every town of the Land of Israel. If somebody had a question of religious practice, he went and asked it from the court in his town. If they had heard [the answer], they told him; otherwise he and their distinguished member went and asked a court in their neighborhood. If these had heard [the answer], they told him; otherwise he and their distinguished member went and asked from the court on the Temple Mount. If these had heard [the answer], they told him; otherwise he and their distinguished member went and asked from the court on the glacis. If these had heard [the answer], they told him; otherwise they together entered the High Court in the free-stone hall since from there instruction came accepted in all of Israel, as it is said: From this place which the Eternal will choose . Even though the Synhedrion in the free-stone hall had 71 members, those present never numbered less than 23. If one of them had to leave, he was looking around; if 23 others were present, he would leave, otherwise he would not leave. They were in session from the daily morning sacrifice to the daily evening sacrifice. On Sabbaths and holidays, they were sitting in the study hall on the Temple Mount. If a question of practice came up, if they had heard the answer, they told them; otherwise they prepared to vote. If a majority was for acquitting, they acquitted. If a majority was for a guilty verdict, they rendered a verdict of guilty. If a majority was for declaring pure, they declared pure. If a majority was for declaring impure, they declared impure. From the time that there were many students of Shammai and Hillel who did not study enough under their teachers, many disagreements arose and two doctrines developed. From there, they were sending to all towns in the Land of Israel; any time they found a person who was wise, meek, even-tempered, benevolent, pleasing, humble, good-hearted, with good intentions, and well endowed, they were placing him on the court of the Temple Mount, from there to the court on the glacis, and from there to the High Court in the free-stone hall.

[Sanhedrin 2:5.3] He was with David at Efes Dammim . {NAME} said, at the red field. But {NAME} said, from there the money stopped. The Philistines assembled , etc. {NAME} Ḥanan said, they were lentils but a kernel was as good as a barley grain. {NAME} said, this describes the Philistines who came straight as barley and went away low as lentils, as one verse says, there was a field full of barley , and one said, full of lentils . {NAME} said, it was one year but concerning two fields, one of barley and one of lentils. It was obvious to him that he might destroy it and pay for the damage. Perhaps it was obvious to him that he might destroy it and not pay for the damage? Which one might he destroy and for which one would he have to pay? For the one of lentils or the one of barley? For the one of lentils grows human food, the one of barley animal feed. The one of lentils will not be obligated for ḥallah , barley will be obligated for ḥallah. The ˋomer comes from barley; ˋomer cannot be brought from lentils. But the rabbis said, it was one field and two years. Does one infer from last year, or does one not infer from one year to the next? They stood up in the property and saved it . One verse says, they saved it, and one says, he saved it . This shows that he returned it to its owner and it was dear to him as if it had been a field of saffron.

[Sanhedrin 3:6.7] “His brother-in-law”. Some Tannaïm state: Including sons and sons-in-law; but some Tannaïm state: Excluding sons and sons-in-law. He who said, including sons and sons-in law, from her. But he who said, excluding sons and sons-in law, from another family.
[Sanhedrin 3:6.8] Rav went to sell hides for the elder {NAME}. He passed by a place where he found {NAME} sitting and asking: We have stated, “his stepson alone.” What is the situation of his stepson’s wife, his stepdaughter’s husband? A woman is like her husband and the husband is like his wife. Therefore, the situation of his stepson’s wife is that of his stepson, and the husband is like his wife.
[Sanhedrin 3:6.9] {NAME} asked: If the third generation permitted the first generation’s wife? Is Phineas’s wife permitted to Moses? {NAME} said, one accepts the second and third generations with difficulty. {NAME} said, even with ease.
[Sanhedrin 3:6.10] As the following: A brother-in-law of {NAME} had a case with some person. He said, I am accepting anything which {NAME} will decide. {NAME} heard it and said, this is it. I know that just as they said for the preceding generations, so it is for the following. {NAME} in the name of Rav: Practice follows {NAME}.
[Sanhedrin 3:7.1] MISHNAH: The lover and the hater. The lover, that is the best man. The hater, anyone who did not talk to him for three days because of ill-will. They told him, Israel are not suspected of this.
[Sanhedrin 3:7.2] HALAKHAH: “The lover and the hater,” etc. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: They stated this for the seven days of wedding festivities.
[Sanhedrin 3:8.1] MISHNAH: How does one check out the witnesses? One brings them to court and instills fear into them, then removes them but retains the greatest among them. One says to him, tell why you know that this person owes to the other one. If he said, he himself confessed to me that he owes the money, or another person told me that he owes it, he did not say anything until he says, before us he confessed to him that he owed him 200 denar.
[Sanhedrin 3:8.2] HALAKHAH: “How does one check out the witnesses,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If he had intended to appoint them as witnesses, their testimony is valid.
[Sanhedrin 3:8.3] How does one judge? The judges are sitting, the parties are standing, and the claimant starts first with his words, as it is written: He who has something to say shall present before you .
[Sanhedrin 3:8.4] From where that the burden of proof is on the claimant? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Shall present before you , shall present his proofs.
[Sanhedrin 3:8.5] {NAME} asked, in the case of a sister-in-law, who runs after whom? {NAME} answered: His sister-in-law shall come to the gate . {NAME} said, {NAME} taught me correctly.
[Sanhedrin 3:8.6] {NAME} and {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The claimant claims, the respondent responds, and the judge decides. {NAME} said, the judge has to repeat their arguments, as it is said: The king said, this one says, my son is the living and yours is the dead one, etc.
[Sanhedrin 3:8.7] When {NAME} saw that witnesses said exactly the same, he was investigating. When he saw them essentially identical, he determined the common element. {NAME} made light of a judge who said, “accept a single witness,” but they should say it themselves. When {NAME} realized an argument in favor of a person who himself did not know it, he guided him, following open your mouth for the dumb .
[Sanhedrin 3:8.8] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He who hides his witnesses behind a wall did not do anything. As in this case: A man happened to prepare food for a meal. He said to another, give me what you owe me. That one answered, yes. When he rose, he told him, I do not owe you anything. He answered, I have witnesses. The other said, I said that only in order not to spoil your food. The case came before {NAME}, who said, this is what {NAME} said, he who hides his witnesses behind a wall did not do anything.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.1] MISHNAH: One calls in the second [witness] and examines him. If their testimonies are found consistent, one argues the case. Two say not guilty and one says guilty, he is not guilty. Two say guilty and one says not guilty, he is guilty. One says not guilty, one says guilty, and one says “I do not know”, they shall add judges. Even if two say not guilty or guilty but one says “I do not know”, they shall add judges
[Sanhedrin 3:9.2] HALAKHAH: “One calls in the second [witness],” etc. Rams , the minimum of rams are two. Why does the verse say two ? That both be equal.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.3] Sheep , the minimum of sheep are two. Why does the verse say two ? That both be equal.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.4] The minimum of birds are two. Why does the verse say two ? that both be equal. The minimum of trumpets are two. Why does the verse say two ? that both be equal.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.5] {NAME} objected to {NAME}. Is there not written: The two men shall stand ? Now, is not two the minimum of “men”? Why does the verse say two ? That both be equal? But it is written: Do not bend the lawsuit of the proselyte, the orphan , … That means that a proselyte can have a lawsuit against one who is not a proselyte, an orphan may have a lawsuit against one who is not an orphan. Then why is there written two ? It is free to be combined and to infer from it an equal cut . It is said here two and it is said there two men were left . Since there one speaks of men but not women, also here men but not women nor underaged. From this we learn that a woman may not be a judge and may not be a witness.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.6] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. It is said here two and it is said there two . Since there it must be by the testimony of two witnesses, also here by the testimony of two witnesses. Then why does the verse say two ? Lest one of them be standing while the other be sitting; one says everything he has to say, but to the other one says, make your statement short.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.7] {NAME} said, I heard that if the judge wants to let both of them sit, he may tell them to sit down. {NAME} says, one says to him, either you dress as he is dressed or pay him to be dressed as you are.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.8] {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}: The witnesses have to stand while testifying, for it is said: the two men shall stand . {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Also the parties have to stand at the moment the verdict is given, as it is said: who have the quarrel before the Eternal .
[Sanhedrin 3:9.9] It is written: Fathers shall not be killed because of sons . Is it not already written, each one should be killed for his own crime ? Why does the verse say, fathers shall not be killed because of sons ? Fathers shall not be killed on the testimony of sons, and sons shall not be killed on testimony of fathers. From here that witnesses shall not be relatives of the accused.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.10] From where that witnesses may not be relatives of one another? Think of it, if they be found perjured, would they not be killed by their testimony? From where that witnesses may not be relatives of the judges? Think of it, if one of them be found perjured, he could not be killed unless the other also was found perjured. If you say so, would he not be killed by his sentence?
[Sanhedrin 3:9.11] From where that judges may not be relatives of one another? The Torah said, kill on the testimony of witnesses, kill on the sentence of judges. Since witnesses may not be relatives of one another, neither may judges be relatives of one another.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.12] So far only fathers and sons; from where the other relatives? {NAME} sais, and sons includes the remaining relatives.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.13] So far according to {NAME}.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.14] From where following {NAME}? {NAME} stated: The congregation shall judge ; the congregation shall save . The congregation be neither relatives of the murderer nor relatives of the murdered. {NAME} said, otherwise you would say that the court is engaged in vendetta. This implies that the judges may not be related to the accused. And from where that the witnesses may not be related to the accused? The Torah said, kill on the testimony of witnesses, kill on the sentence of judges. Since judges may not be related to the accused, neither may witnesses be related to the accused. From where that witnesses may not be relatives of one another? Think of it, if they be found perjured, would they not be killed by their testimony?
[Sanhedrin 3:9.15] “Qualified one but not disqualified one.” For it is said, if he does not tell, he has to bear his punishment . If he told, the other would have to pay money. This excludes one where the other would not have to pay money even if he told.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.16] “Before the court.” To exclude a single witness. If they told him that they would accept his word as if there were two [witnesses], would he be guilty? The verse says, if he had seen or known . One who is qualified to testify according to biblical standards; this excludes a single witness who is not qualified to testify according to biblical standards.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.17] “Outside of court.” If he does not tell, he has to bear his punishment. If he told, one would have to pay money. This excludes outside of court where the other would not have to pay money even if he told.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.18] From where two witnesses? He and another make two. Or following {NAME}, as {NAME} said, any place where the Torah mentions a witness without further determination it implies two witnesses unless the verse informs you that a single witness is meant. It was found stated in the name of {NAME}: Can a single witness be found guilty of a blurted oath? Since it is possible to say that another person could team up with him, then he would be subject to the oath of testimony, how could you find him guilty of a blurted oath?
[Sanhedrin 3:9.19] Should a relative be found guilty of a blurted oath? Does it follow what {NAME} said (ben) [in the name of] {NAME}: “An oath that X gave a mina to Y,” and it turns out that X had not given; since there is nothing in the future there is nothing in the past. Or the following: “One said to another, ˋwhere is my ox?’ He responded, ˋI do not know what you are referring to.’ It so happened that it had died, or was wounded, or captured, or lost. ˋI require you to swear;’ the other said ˋAmen’. He is not liable.” Rav said, he is not liable for a keeper’s oath but is liable because of a blurted oath. {NAME} said, since it is a religious duty to appease him, he is not liable because of a blurted oath. In Rav’s opinion, is there no religious duty to appease him? One appeases with truthful statements, not with lies.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.20] {NAME} stated: He has to bear his punishment , a sacrifice. From where that one needs a court? One learns “telling, telling”. Since telling mentioned there is before a court, also telling here is before a court.
[Sanhedrin 3:9.21] Or like the following. “One accepts the witnesses’ testimony only if they saw it together. {NAME} says, even if they saw it one after the other.” {NAME} in the name of Rav: The Sages agree with {NAME} with regard to witnesses of firstlings and witnesses of squatters’ rights. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: the same holds for testimony regarding signs. In that case, it is obvious if one says, I saw two hairs on his back and the other says, I saw two hairs on his side. If one says, I saw one hair on his back and the other says, I saw one hair on his belly, that is nothing; so much more his back and his side. Two are saying, we saw one hair on his back; and two are saying, we saw one hair on his belly. {NAME} and {NAME}, one said, it is invalid, but the other said, it is valid. He who says it is invalid considers him as one who testifies to half a sign. He who says it is valid? I say, maybe they were rubbed off. One says, two hairs on his back; and one says, two on his belly. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that this is valid. {NAME} said, everybody agrees that this is invalid [testimony]. {NAME} said, this is in disagreement. Rebbi [Yose] said to {NAME}, does not {NAME} follow my opinion? He answered, I am disagreeing with his teacher, so much more with him. {NAME} said, {NAME} was correct. If a document was signed by four seals, if one person verified the signature of two [witnesses], and another those of the other two, and the document was attacked, is that worth anything? Does not every single signature need two witnesses? And here, every single hair needs two witnesses. {NAME} learns it (because of) [from the years of] squatting rights. If one [witness] testified that he ate from the property the first, second, and third years and another testified that he ate it the fourth, fifth, and sixth years, is that worth anything? Does not every single year need two witnesses? And here, every single hair needs two witnesses.

If a person was summoned by the court three times and did not appear, {NAME} said that one may receive witnesses not in the presence of the parties and issue a decision. He told him, this is seen to be the rabbis’ opinion.
[Sanhedrin 3:10.1] MISHNAH: When they have come to a decision, they bring the parties in. The chief judge says, Mr. X, you are not guilty, Mr. X, you are guilty. From where that afterwards, one may not say, I had found for you but my colleagues found you guilty, but what can I do since they were a majority against me? On such a one it was said: The gossip uncovers secrets .
[Sanhedrin 3:10.2] HALAKHAH: “When they have come to a decision,” etc. {NAME} said, one forces the one who finds guilty to write “not guilty.” {NAME} says, the one who finds guilty, writes “guilty”; the one who finds not guilty, writes “not guilty”. The Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “From where that afterwards, one may not say, I had found for you but my colleagues found you guilty.” What does {NAME} do with this? That nobody could say, I really wanted to justify X in his suit but they did not let me do it. What is {NAME} reason? That no other person should come, reason as he did, and say, also that one was there and he erred.
[Sanhedrin 3:11.1] MISHNAH: Any time one produces a proof he may demand a new trial. If they told him, produce all your proofs within thirty days, if he produced within thirty days, he gets a new trial, after thirty days he does not get a new trial. {NAME} said, what can one do if he did not find within thirty [days] but found after thirty [days]?
[Sanhedrin 3:11.2] HALAKHAH: “Any time one produces a proof,” etc. {NAME} said, there, where it is possible to add, they continue to argue. But here it is impossible to add. {NAME} and {NAME} both teach that even here it is possible to add.
[Sanhedrin 3:12.1] MISHNAH: If they told him, produce witnesses; he said, I have no witness; produce proofs; he said, I have no proofs. If later he found a proof, or he found witnesses, this is irrelevant. {NAME} said, what should he do who did not know that he had witnesses but found witnesses; he did not know that he had proof, but he found proof? If they told him, produce witnesses; he said, I have no witness; produce proofs; he said, I have no proofs; when he saw that the decision would go against him he said, X and Y shall come and testify for me, or he produced proof from his money belt, this is irrelevant.
[Sanhedrin 3:12.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} said,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Three Amoraïm. One said, any time he brings proof he can demand a new trial. The other said, if he brought within 30 days, he can demand a new trial, after 30 days he cannot demand a new trial. The other said, he never can demand a new trial unless he prove that he absolutely had no knowledge of it. But did we not state: “{NAME} said, what should he do who did not know that he had witnesses but found witnesses; that he had no proof, but found proof?” {NAME} and {NAME}: One said, unless he voided his proofs; the other said, until he disclaimed his proofs.

After a decision was reached he presented witnesses. He asked {NAME}, who said to him, is that still a problem for you? Any time one brings proof he can demand a new trial. Why did it need two cases? In {NAME} case, no formal verdict had been rendered, in {NAME} case, a formal verdict had been rendered.
[Sanhedrin 3:12.4] Does a judicial confirmation need a court? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. One said, it should be confirmed either by the handwriting of the witnesses or the handwriting of the judges; the other said, even with one handwriting and one judge.
[Sanhedrin 4:1.1] MISHNAH: Both civil suits and criminal suits require cross-examination and investigation, as it is said: One set of rules shall be for you . What is the difference between civil suits and criminal suits? Civil suits are tried before three judges, criminal suits before 23. In civil suits one starts with arguments either for acquittal or conviction; in criminal courts one starts with arguments for acquittal but not for conviction.
[Sanhedrin 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Both civil suits,” etc. {NAME} said, to protect Israel’s money they said, “tell why you know that this person owes the other.” {NAME} asked before {NAME}: What does one do in practice? He answered, following {NAME}, as {NAME} said, to protect Israel’s money they said, “tell why you know that this person owes the other.” {NAME} in the name of {NAME} and {NAME}, one said: You shall cross-examine, investigate, and inquire well . The other said, equity, equity you shall pursue . How is that? If you see that the verdict will be the truth, investigate it; otherwise, act in equity.
[Sanhedrin 4:1.3] When {NAME} saw that witnesses said exactly the same, he was investigating. When he saw them essentially identical, he determined the common element.
[Sanhedrin 4:1.4] How does one start for acquittal? One says, is it possible that this one be a murderer? {NAME} said, if this is so, if one of the witnesses said, I have something to say in his defense, and his colleague comes to support him, is that support? If you say so, would you not put guilt on the judges, to lead witnesses to lie?
[Sanhedrin 4:1.5] {NAME} said, anybody who cannot argue for the crawling animal to make it pure a hundred times cannot start arguing for acquittal. How does one argue about a crawling animal? {NAME} said, since a snake which kills is pure, a rat which does not kill logically should be pure. Since a rat which does not kill is impure, a snake which kills logically should be impure. {NAME} objected: Is there not the scorpion which kills and is pure? It was found that a Tanna said, snake and scorpion both follow the same rules.
[Sanhedrin 4:1.6] Rebbi said, Rebbi [ ] had a self-confident student who was arguing for purity or impurity of the crawling animal a hundred times. They said, this student never could instruct. {NAME} said, this student was cut-off from Mount Sinai.
[Sanhedrin 4:2.1] MISHNAH: Civil suits are decided by one witness whether for credit or debit; criminal suits are decided by one witness for acquittal and two for conviction.
[Sanhedrin 4:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Civil suits are decided,” etc. {NAME} said, if the Torah had been given decided, no foot could stand. What is the reason? The Eternal spoke to Moses . He said before Him: Master of the Universe, inform me what is the practice. He told him, to bend after the majority . If there was a majority for acquitting, they acquitted; if there was a majority for convicting, they convicted; so that the Torah could be explained in 49 ways impure and 49 ways pure, the numerical value of ודגלו. And so it says: the commands of the Eternal are pure sayings; molten silver in an earthenware crucible, refined sevenfold. And it says, the straightforward love You .
[Sanhedrin 4:3.1] MISHNAH: Civil suits can be retried both for credit and for debit. Criminal suits can be retried for acquittal but not for conviction.
[Sanhedrin 4:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Civil suits can be retried both for credit and for debit,” etc. If he left the court being acquitted, and they found reasons for conviction, could I understand that one returned him? The verse says, do not slay the acquitted . If he left the court being convicted, and they found reasons for acquittal, could I understand that one should not return him? The verse says, but do not slay the innocent . I could think that if he is acquitted in your court, he is acquitted in My court; the verse says, I shall not acquit the wicked . {NAME} said, {NAME} told me: There is no difference; if the acquittal was in error, one retries him.
[Sanhedrin 4:3.3] “In civil suits, anybody may argue for credit or debit,” etc. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Even an adulterer and an adulteress? He told him, your patch came off.
[Sanhedrin 4:4.1] MISHNAH: In civil suits, anybody may argue for credit or debit. In criminal suits, anybody may argue for acquittal but not everybody may argue for conviction. In civil suits, one who argued for credit may argue for debit and one who argued for debit may argue for credit; but in criminal suits one who argued for conviction may argue for acquittal but one who argued for acquittal is barred from arguing for conviction.
[Sanhedrin 4:4.2] HALAKHAH: “In civil suits, one who argued for credit,” etc. Rebbi said, if they only miss saying, Mr. X, you are acquitted, or you are convicted; it does not apply to the discussion. {NAME} said, it also applies to the discussion.
[Sanhedrin 4:5.1] MISHNAH: Civil suits are tried during the day and may be decided in the night but criminal suits are tried during the day and decided during daytime.
[Sanhedrin 4:5.2] HALAKHAH: “Civil suits are tried during the day,” etc. From where this? They judged the people at all times . But this is a verse about what happened! {NAME} said: so is the baraita : If they erred and judged in the night, their judgment stands, as the verse said: they shall judge the people at all times . He said, that is a statement.
[Sanhedrin 4:6.1] MISHNAH: Civil suits are decided on the same day, whether for credit or debit. But criminal suits are decided the same day for acquittal, the next day for conviction. Therefore one does not judge on Sabbath eve or holiday eve.
[Sanhedrin 4:6.2] HALAKHAH: “Civil suits are decided on the same day,” etc. It was stated: A witness may not argue either for acquittal or conviction. From where this? A witness shall not argue about anybody on trial for his life . And from where that he himself may not argue either for acquittal or conviction? The verse says, one shall not argue about anybody on trial for his life . {NAME} said, sometimes a person sees himself set up by perjured witnesses and he speaks much lest he be put to death.
[Sanhedrin 4:6.3] From where that one needs two consecutive days?
[Sanhedrin 4:6.4] {NAME}, {NAME}, said in the name of {NAME}: It is forbidden to judge money matters on Friday. Does not a Mishnah object: “Therefore one does not judge [criminal matters] on Sabbath eve or holiday eve”? Hence, one judges money matters! Also, {NAME} stated thus: One judges money matters on Friday but not criminal matters. One is for practice, the other for action.
[Sanhedrin 4:6.5] Could one not judge him on Fridays, pass sentence on the Sabbath, and execute him after the Sabbath? If you say so, it turns out that his judgment is delayed. {NAME} asked, could he not be judged on the Sabbath, have his sentence passed on the Sabbath, and be executed on the Sabbath? Temple service, which supersedes Sabbath prohibitions, is pushed aside by obligatory executions, since it is said, from My altar take him to be executed . Therefore the Sabbath, which is pushed aside by Temple service, logically should be pushed aside by obligatory executions. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This implies that courts may not sit on the Sabbath; what is the reason? It is said here, in all your dwellings , and it is said there, these shall be for you legal procedures for your generations in all your dwellings . Since there the verse refers to courts, so also here the verse refers to courts.
[Sanhedrin 4:7.1] MISHNAH: In cases of money matters, purity, and impurity, one starts with the greatest. In criminal cases, one starts from the side. Everybody is qualified to judge money matters but not everybody is qualified to judge criminal matters, but only Cohanim, Levites and Israel whose daughters may marry into the priesthood.
[Sanhedrin 4:7.2] HALAKHAH: “In cases of money matters, purity, and impurity,” etc. Rebbi says, do not argue about a quarrel . It is written against the greatest , that one does not argue after the greatest, only prior to the greatest. {NAME} said, do not argue about a quarrel . It is written before the greatest , that one does not argue prior to the greatest, only after the greatest. Rav said, do not argue , even after a hundred, the words of {NAME}.
[Sanhedrin 4:7.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: {NAME} and {NAME} disagreed. One said, our procedures are like their procedures, and one said, our procedures are not like their procedures. He who said, our procedures are like their procedures, is understandable. He wo said, our procedures are not like their procedures, how does he understand Jehudah said , Memukhan said ? They agreed with what Jehudah said, they agreed with what Memukhan said.
[Sanhedrin 4:7.4] From where that in criminal trials the voting starts from the side? {NAME} the Elder stated before {NAME}: David told his men, each gird his sword , and after this, they were sitting in judgment about Nabal. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Also when disqualifying families one starts from the side.
[Sanhedrin 4:7.5] “Anybody is qualified to judge money matters.” {NAME} says, even bastards. {NAME} says, one does not investigate about libation wine.
[Sanhedrin 4:7.6] “The Synhedrion was like a semicircular threshing floor,” etc. It is written: Do not bend your destitute’s proceeding in his trial . In his trial you do not bend; you may bend in the ox’s trial. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: But only in those rules which are different for civil and criminal suits. How many are these? We have stated nine; {NAME} stated eleven. Which rules are the last two? The castrate and one who never had children is qualified to judge civil suits but not criminal suits. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Also one who is less than twenty years of age or who does not have two pubic hairs is qualified to judge civil suits but not criminal suits. {NAME} said thirteen. Which rules are the last two? One judges two civil suits on one day but one does not try two criminal suits on one day. {NAME} said, even adulterer and adulteress.
[Sanhedrin 4:8.1] MISHNAH: The Synhedrion was like a semicircular threshing floor, so that they could see one another. Two court reporters were standing before them, one to the right and one to the left, and they wrote down the arguments of those who argued for acquittal and those who argued for conviction. {NAME} says, there were three. One wrote the arguments for conviction, one wrote the arguments for acquittal, and one wrote the arguments for acquittal and for conviction. Three rows of students of the Sages were sitting before them; each one of them knew his place. If they needed to ordain, they ordained one from the first row. One of the second row came to sit in the first, and one of the third came to sit in the second. They chose a person from the general public and placed him in the third row; he did not sit in the place of the one promoted but in the place befitting him.
[Sanhedrin 4:8.2] HALAKHAH: “Three rows of students of the Sages,” etc. {NAME} (bar) [Rebbi] Yasa in the name of {NAME}: It says here congregation , and it says there congregation . Rav brought it from a Mishnah; the Mishnah says “be a tail of lions and not a head of jackals.” The parable says, be a head of jackals but not a tail of lions. But we have stated: “If they needed to ordain, they ordained one from the first row.”
[Sanhedrin 4:9.1] MISHNAH: How does one instill fear in witnesses in criminal cases? One brings them in and instills fear in them. Maybe you would testify by a guess, or by a rumor, or from the mouth of a witness, or you heard it from a trustworthy source, or maybe you do not know that we shall examine you by cross-examination and interrogation. You should know that criminal trials are not like civil trials. In civil trials a person pays money and is forgiven. In criminal trials, his blood and the blood of all his descendants hang in the balance, to the end of all generations. So we find when Cain slew his brother, it is said: The sounds of your brother’s bloods cry to me from the earth . It does not say your brother’s blood but your brother’s bloods , his blood and that of his descendants. Another explanation: Your brother’s bloods , the blood was splashed on trees and stones. Therefore man was created single in the world to teach that for anybody who destroys a single life it is counted as if he destroyed an entire world, and for anybody who preserves a single life it is counted as if he preserved an entire world. And because of peace among men, that nobody could say to another, my father was greater than your father. And that sectarians could not say, there are a plurality of powers in Heaven. And to proclaim the greatness of the King over kings of kings, the Holy One, praise to Him. For a man coins many coins with one die; they are one like the other. But the King over kings of kings, the Holy One, praise to Him, stamps every man with the stamp of the first man, but no one is like any other. Therefore, everybody is required to say, the world was created for me. Maybe you will say, why should we go to all this trouble? There already is written: If he is a witness, or saw, or knew , etc. Maybe you will say, why should we be guilty of this man’s blood? There already is written: In destruction of evildoers is clamor .
[Sanhedrin 4:9.2] HALAKHAH: “How does one instill fear,” etc. What is meant by a guess? “Do not say, we saw him with a sword in his hand running after another person. He entered a ruined building after him; we entered after him and found him slain. We saw him coming out and his sword was dripping blood. {NAME} said: May I not see consolation if I did not see one running after another person into a ruined building. I entered after him and found him slain while the other left with his sword dripping blood. I said to him, may I not see consolation if you did not kill him. But what can I do since your blood is not delivered into my hands. But He Who knows thoughts may collect from that person. He did not manage to leave before a snake bit him and he died.
[Sanhedrin 4:9.3] “Therefore man was created,” etc. “Man was created single in the world because of the families, lest they should attack one another. Is that not argument de minore ad majus ? Since now that they are all descendants of one father they attack one another, if they had been descendants of two not so much more? Another explanation: The just ones should not say, we are the descendants of a just man, but you are the sons of evildoers.”
[Sanhedrin 4:9.4] “And to proclaim the greatness of the King over kings of kings, the Holy One, praise to Him,” etc. To proclaim the greatness of the King over kings of kings Who from one die coins all seals and no one is like the other, as it is said: The seal turns around like clay . Why did He change their looks? That no man should jump and go to another’s wife or another’s field. It was stated in the name of {NAME}: Three things did the Holy One, praise to Him, diversify in humans: looks of the face, understanding, and voice. Looks and understanding because of the robbers, voice because of forbidden women. {NAME} said, even a fig tree or a wheat plant is not identical to any other. Man was created Sabbath Eve so from the start he should enter with a commandment. Another explanation: Why was he created last? A parable of a king who made a banquet. After he had ordered the meal, he invited the guests. So wisdom built her house , that is the Holy One, praise to Him, Who created the world in wisdom, as it is said, the Eternal in wisdom based the earth , etc. She quarried its seven pillars , these are the seven days of creation. She slaughtered her slaughtering, mixed her wine , these are seas and rivers and all the needs of the world. Any silly one shall come here , that is Adam and Eve.
[Sanhedrin 4:9.5] “Maybe you will say, why should we go to all this trouble,” etc. It is written: The clamor erupted in the camp . What is “the clamor”? Quiet. And so it says, when they went in front of the armed forces , to teach that even the downfall of the evildoers is no joy before the Omnipresent.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.1] MISHNAH: They were investigating him in seven ways: In which Sabbatical period, in which year, in which month, which day of the month, which day, which hour, at which place? {NAME} said, which day, which hour, which place, do you recognize him, and did you warn him? If one worshipped idols, what did he worship and how did he worship?
[Sanhedrin 5:1.2] HALAKHAH: “They were investigating him in seven ways,” etc. But we did not state, in which Jubilee period? For that is not current. It was found stated: {NAME} says, also in which Jubilee period? We confirmed that in a year which started or concluded [a Jubilee period].
[Sanhedrin 5:1.3] From where the seven investigations? {NAME} the Elder stated before {NAME}: You shall inquire, investigate, ask in depth, and behold, the matter is well founded . He told him, this verse does not work; but: you shall inquire, investigate, ask in depth; it will be told to you, you shall listen, ask in depth . In depth, in depth for an equal cut, to require in each case listening, asking, inquiry, and investigation. {NAME} asked about this: If they caught an armed robber in Tiberias and said, this is the murderer, this is the murdered; why does this need seven investigations? Issi said, any time that the witnesses could not be proven perjured, the murderer cannot be executed on that testimony.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.4] “Do you recognize him?” Who was he, a Gentile or an Israel? Let us hear from what {NAME} said: If he was slain between Tiberias and Sepphoris, it is prima facie evidence that he was an Israel.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.5] “Did you warn him?” From where warning? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A man who would take his sister …, it is ḥesed. {NAME} said, Cain married his sister, Abel married his sister. It is charitable , I was charitable with the first generations so the world could be inhabited; I said, the world was to be built on ḥesed.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.6] It was stated: {NAME} said, by the mouth of two witnesses shall the dead die . Does he die when dead? But to tell him by which kind of death he will be executed. It was stated: {NAME} said, and if a man intentionally kill his neighbor knowingly ; they shall inform him by which kind of death he will be executed.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.7] If his death should have been a severe one but they warned him about an easy one. He could say that had he known that his death was to be severe, he would not have committed that crime. If his death should have been an easy one but they warned him about a severe one; in the opinion of {NAME} they have to inform him by which kind of death he will be executed.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.8] “If they warned him and he remained silent, they warned him and he nodded his head, even if he said, I know, he cannot be prosecuted unless he say: for that purpose I am doing it.” “If they saw him spilling blood; they told him, know that he is a son of the Covenant and the Torah said, he who spills a man’s blood, by man his blood shall be spilled , even if he said, I know, he cannot be prosecuted unless he say: for that purpose I am doing it.” “If they saw him desecrating the Sabbath; they told him, know that today is Sabbath and the Torah said, its desecrators shall be put to death , even if he said, I know, he cannot be prosecuted unless he say: for that purpose I am doing it.”
[Sanhedrin 5:1.9] {NAME} asked: What was the gatherer’s guilt? Because of tearing off or because of reaping? Let us hear from the following: The Children of Israel were in the desert when they found … This teaches that he was tearing wood off the ground.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.10] {NAME} asked: How was the gatherer put to death? By stoning. Let us hear from the following: “They knew that the gatherer should be executed but they did not know how he should be put to death.” It was found that {NAME} stated: Take the blasphemer outside the camp . How was he put to death? By stoning.
[Sanhedrin 5:1.11] “What did he worship?” Peor or Mercury? “And how did he worship?” In its proper worship or the worship of Heaven? Let us hear from the following: It happened that two [witnesses] came and said, we saw that this one was worshipping idols, but we do not know whether it was Peor or Mercury. One judges him for both and for the one in which he was found innocent one lets him go.
[Sanhedrin 5:2.1] MISHNAH: Anybody who adds inquiries is praiseworthy. It happened that {NAME} cross-examined about fig stalks. What is the difference between investigations and cross-examinations? In investigations, if one said “I do not know”, their testimony is worthless. In cross-examinations, if one said “I do not know”, or even two say “we do not know,” their testimony remains valid. Both in investigations and cross-examinations, if they contradict one another their testimony is worthless.
[Sanhedrin 5:2.2] HALAKHAH: “Anybody who adds inquiries,” etc. How did he pluck them? He plucked them with their stalks. How did he eat them? With their pits.
[Sanhedrin 5:2.3] There, we have stated: “If two groups of witnesses were testifying against a person, one group say that he vowed nazir twice, the others say that he vowed nazir five times. The House of Shammai say, the testimony is split and there is no nezirut there. But the House of Hillel say, five contains two; he should be a nazir twice.” Rav said, they differ in the overall testimony. But in detail, everybody agrees that the testimony is split. {NAME} said, they differ in counting. But in an overall testimony, everybody agrees that five contains two. What is overall and what is counting? Overall, this one says two, the other one says five. Counting, this one says one, two, the other one says three, four.
[Sanhedrin 5:2.4] Rav said, if testimony was contradictory in its essence, the testimony is not void. {NAME} said, if testimony is contradictory in itself, the testimony is void. In the opinion of everybody, if testimony was contradictory in aspects that belong after the fact, the testimony is not void. The strength of {NAME} is consistent with what {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, if it was agreed that he counted but one [witness] said, he counted from a wallet, and the other said, he counted from a bundle, that contradicts the essence of the testimony, and Rav will agree that the testimony be void. Where do they disagree? If there were two groups of witnesses, one says he counted from a wallet and the other says he counted from a bundle. That contradicts the essence of the testimony: the testimony is void, but according to Rav, the testimony is not void. One said, he counted into his bosom, but the other said, he counted into his money-belt: everybody agrees that this contradicts the essence of the testimony but the testimony is not void. If one [witness] said, he killed him with a sword, the other [witness] said, he killed him with a mace, that contradicts the essence of the testimony; Rav will agree that the testimony be void. Where do they disagree? If there were two groups of witnesses, one says he killed him with a sword and the other says, he killed him with a mace. That contradicts the essence of the testimony, the testimony is void, but according to Rav, the testimony is not void. One says, he turned to the North and one says, he ran away to the South, everybody agrees that the testimony was contradictory in aspects that belong after the fact, and the testimony is not void. The strength of Rav comes from what we have stated there: “{NAME} and {NAME} say, since both agree that he is not alive they can be remarried.” He did not hear that {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} concede in the case of witnesses. What is the difference between witnesses and the co-wife? They do not consider the co-wife’s words compared to those of her companion. {NAME} said, if {NAME} said this, he said it because he had heard it from me. The Mishnah disagrees with Rav: “Both in investigations and cross-examinations, if they contradict one another their testimony is worthless.” What does Rav do with this? {NAME} said, Rav will explain it as referring to single witness against single witness. {NAME} said, even if you say groups and groups. There is a difference in criminal cases, as it is written: Justice, justice you shall pursue .
[Sanhedrin 5:3.1] MISHNAH: One says, on the second of the month, but the other says, on the third of the month, their testimony may be valid, since one knew about the addition to the month but the other did not know. One says on the third, the other says on the fifth, their testimony is invalid. One says, at two hours but the other said at three hours, their testimony is valid. One says at three but the other says at five, their testimony is invalid; {NAME} says it is valid. One says at five but the other says at seven, their testimony is invalid since at five hours the sun is in the East but at seven in the West.
[Sanhedrin 5:3.2] HALAKHAH: “One says, on the second of the month,” etc. Until when? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Up to the greater part of the month. {NAME} said, e. g., those village dwellers. But the Sages say, it is nothing, and {NAME} said, for example I, who never in my life prayed musaf , since I do not know when the month starts.
[Sanhedrin 5:3.3] {NAME} says, from noontime on it is from their words; {NAME} says, from noontime on it is biblical. What is {NAME} reason? Only on the first day , that is the fifteenth. I could think at nightfall; the verse says only , to separate. How is this? Give it one hour before sundown. What is {NAME} reason? Only on the first day , that is the fourteenth. I could think the entire day; the verse says only , to separate. Half for leavened matter, half for mazzah . {NAME} argument seems inverted. There, he said only to add; here he said only to diminish. {NAME} said, he diminished, lest it be for leavened matter. {NAME} said, do not eat leavened matter with it , while it is eaten. {NAME} said, do not eat leavened matter with it , while it is prepared.
[Sanhedrin 5:3.4] {NAME} has both a positive and a negative commandment concerning its eating, a positive and a negative commandment concerning its removal. A positive commandment concerning its eating, seven days you shall eat unleavened bread for it , not leavened. Any prohibition which is implied by a positive commandment has the status of positive commandment. A negative commandment concerning its eating, do not eat leavened . A positive commandment concerning its removal, seven days … you shall remove sour dough from your houses . A negative commandment concerning its removal, for seven days sour dough shall not be found in your houses .
[Sanhedrin 5:3.5] Now {NAME} says, after noontime it is forbidden because of their words. The (sixth) [seventh] hour it is forbidden because of a fence. Why the (fifth) [sixth]? Because of a fence. Is there a fence around a fence? But the (fifth) [sixth] may be confounded with the seventh. {NAME} argument seems inverted. There, he says that the fifth cannot be confounded with the seventh. But here, he says that the fifth can be confounded with the seventh. {NAME} said, there the matter is given over to women who are lazy, here the matter is given over to the court who is careful. {NAME} said, there it is a matter between the beginning of the fifth and the end of the seventh hour. Here it is between the end of the fifth and the start of the seventh. It also was stated thus: At the start of the fifth hour, the sun is in the East, and the end of the seventh the sun is in the West. The sun never starts setting before the end of the seventh hour.
[Sanhedrin 5:4.1] MISHNAH: They brought in the second [witness] and examined him. If their testimonies were coherent, one starts with arguing for acquittal. If one of the witnesses said, I have an argument for his acquittal, or one of the students said, I have an argument for his conviction, one forces them to be silent. If one of the students said, I have an argument for his acquittal, one brings him up and lets him sit among them. He was not demoted from there the entire day; if his argument has substance, one listens to him. Even if he said, I have to argue for my acquittal, one listens to him if there is substance to his words.
[Sanhedrin 5:4.2] HALAKHAH: They brought in the second,” etc. It was stated: “If they found him innocent, they freed him; otherwise they hold his case over, split into groups of two, eat little and refrain from wine, and discuss during the entire night. The next morning they start early, the beadles of the synagogues come for them. They ask, Mr. X [{NAME}. Y. He says, present.] I was for conviction and I still am for conviction; or I was for acquittal and I still am for acquittal; I was for conviction and now I am for acquittal; one accepts his vote. I was for acquittal and now I am for conviction; argue as before.” It was stated: If one of the judges erred, the clerks of court remind him. If he was for conviction, they tell him, argue as before.
[Sanhedrin 5:4.3] {NAME} said, why does one record the argument of him who argues for acquittal? Because of him who argues for conviction, maybe his memory will fail him. If he switches his argument, they could say to him, this you said, this you did not say. [Does this mean] that it needs two [groups of] witnesses? It would mean that the trial would be extended. {NAME} said, because of him who argues for acquittal.
[Sanhedrin 5:5.1] MISHNAH: If they found him innocent, they free him. Otherwise they hold his case over to the next day, split into groups of two, eat little and refrain from wine the entire day, and discuss during the entire night. The next morning they start early. One who voted for acquittal says, I am for acquittal and I remain for acquittal. One who voted for conviction says, I am for conviction and I remain for conviction. He who voted for conviction may vote for acquittal; but he who voted for acquittal may not change and vote for conviction. If they erred in the matter, the two clerks of court will remind them. If they found him innocent, they free him; otherwise they tally the vote. If twelve are for acquittal and eleven for conviction, he is found innocent. If twelve are for conviction and eleven for acquittal, or even twenty-two are for acquittal or conviction and one says, I do not know, they shall add judges. Up to what number does one add? [One adds] two and two up to 71. If 36 vote for acquittal and 35 for conviction, he is found innocent. If 36 vote for conviction and 35 for acquittal, they have to continue to argue with one another until one of the voters for conviction is convinced by the arguments of those in favor of acquittal.
[Sanhedrin 5:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If they found him innocent, they free him,” etc. It was stated: If one of the witnesses said, I have an argument for his acquittal, and another came to support him, (and another came to support him,) whom do you co-opt? Let us hear from the following of {NAME}: If somebody was acquitted following his own pleading, one does not place him with the judges. Therefore, if he was acquitted following (his own) pleading, then one person would be simultaneously witness and judge. We do not find that anybody can be both witness and judge.
[Sanhedrin 5:5.3] In civil suits one declares the judgment as definitive [but in criminal suits one does not declare the judgment as definitive.] The greatest among the judges declares the judgment as definitive .
[Sanhedrin 5:5.4] “Up to what number does one add,” etc. It was stated: Why does one add judges? For if there were two of the original judges voting affirmatively, together with one of the later ones judgment will be rendered by three. {NAME} said, since the judgment can be rendered by four, one does not render it by three.
[Sanhedrin 5:5.5] {NAME} said, one understands from here: If three sat in judgment and one of them died, two sign and note: Even though we are two who sign, we were three in judging. {NAME} said, a Mishnah implies this: “The judges sign at the bottom or the witnesses.” Does one learn court documents from prozbol ? It was found stated: This about court documents he inferred from the rules of prozbol .
[Sanhedrin 5:5.6] If nobody changes his opinion? {NAME} said, he is acquitted. {NAME} said, he is convicted. {NAME} said to him, is he not acquitted? Why do they have to continue to argue with one another? So the judgment should not be in question.
[Sanhedrin 6:1.1] MISHNAH: If sentence was passed, one brings him out to be stoned. The place for stoning was outside the court as it is said: Bring the blasphemer outside the camp . One person was standing outside the court building with towels in his hand; a horse was standing ready at a distance but so he could see him. If one said, I have an argument in his favor, that one waves his towels, the horse gallops and stops him. Even if he himself says, I have an exculpatory argument for myself, one returns him even four or five times, on condition that his argument be substantial.
[Sanhedrin 6:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If sentence was passed,” etc. The Mishnah either follows Rebbi or the rabbis in a Gentile city. As we have stated: Rebbi said, at your gates , at the gate they were found. You are saying so, or maybe at the gate they were judged? It is said here, at your gates , and it says there, if there be found in your midst, at one of your gates . Since gates mentioned there refers to the gate where he was found, gates mentioned here also refers to the gate where he was found. But the rabbis say, at your gates , at the gate where he was judged. You are saying so, or maybe at the gate were he was found? It is said here, at your gates , and it says there, take this man or this woman … to your gates . Since gates mentioned there refers to the gate where he was judged, gates mentioned here also refers to the gate where he was judged.
[Sanhedrin 6:1.3] {NAME} said, the first time one listens to him whether or not his arguments are substantial. After that, if his arguments are substantial one listens to him, otherwise one does not listen to him. They said, only if his later arguments are substantial. {NAME} asked: If he was led out to be executed when he became paralyzed, do we say that had he not become paralyzed, he would have argued for his acquittal? {NAME} heard this and said, this is a donkey’s question. But it must be: If he was led out to be executed and said, I have to argue for my acquittal: when he became paralyzed, do we say that had he not become paralyzed, he would have argued for his acquittal? He said, that is a statement.
[Sanhedrin 6:2.1] MISHNAH: If they found him innocent, they free him, otherwise he is led to be stoned. The herald goes before him: “X ben Y is led to be stoned because he committed crime Z; U and V testified against him. Anybody who knows of his innocence shall come and argue.”
[Sanhedrin 6:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If they found him innocent,” etc. It was stated: If a bull was led out to be stoned when its witnesses were found to be perjured, {NAME} said, the first to come acquires it; {NAME} said, it was a false declaration of ownerlessness. Similarly, if a slave was led out to be stoned when his owner dedicated him to the Temple, {NAME} said, he acquired himself; {NAME} said, it was false despair.
[Sanhedrin 6:3.1] MISHNAH: Ten cubits’ distance from the place of stoning one tells him: confess! So is the way of any dying person to confess, since anyone who confesses has part in the World to Come. For so we find about Achan towhom Joshua said, my son , honor the Eternal , the God of Israel, confess to Him, and tell me what you did, do not hide it from me . Achan answered Joshua and said, in fact I sinned against the Eternal, the God of Israel, and such and such I did . From where that his confession atoned for him? For it is said, Joshua said to him , how did you devastate us ; may the Eternal devastate you on this day . This day you are devastated; you are not devastated in the Future World. If he does not know how to confess, one tells him, say: “My death shall be atonement for all my sins.” {NAME} said, if he knows that he was the victim of perjurers, he says: “My death shall be atonement for all my sins except this one.” They told him, if so, everybody would say so to declare themselves innocent.
[Sanhedrin 6:3.2] HALAKHAH: “Ten cubits’ distance from the place of stoning,” etc. You find that when Achan stole from the ban, Joshua started supplicating before the Holy One, praise to Him, and said: Master of the Universe, inform me who is the man. The Holy One, praise to Him, answered: I never publicize any creature. In addition, would I not be guilty of slander? But go and let Israel stand up by its tribes and throw lots, then immediately I shall draw him out. That is what is written: Joshua got up early in the morning and summoned Israel by its tribes. {NAME} ben Zeraḥ from the tribe of Jehudah was caught . Achan told him, how? Do you catch me by lots? There is nobody more pious in the present generation than you or Phineas. Let lots be thrown between you, certainly one of you will be caught. Not only this, but your teacher Moses died only 30 or 40 days ago. Did not our teacher Moses instruct us: By the testimony of two witnesses ? You started erring. At that moment did Joshua have a vision by the holy spirit how he distributes the Land to Israel by lots. That is what is written: Joshua threw lots for them . This means, we are giving lots a bad name. Not only this, but if lots are confirmed now, all of Israel will say, since the lots were true in criminal matters, so much more in money matters. But if they are repudiated now, all of Israel will say, since the lots were repudiated in criminal matters, so much more in money matters. At that moment, Joshua started supplicating Achan, entreated him in the name of Israel’s God, and said to him: my son , honor the Eternal , the God of Israel , … Achan answered Joshua and said, in fact . What means אָמְנָה? Truth. I sinned against the Eternal, God of Israel . He told him, I asked you for one and you are answering me two? he answered, I stole from the ban of Midian and the ban of Jericho. {NAME} said, he stole from four bans: The ban of the Phoenician, king of Arad, the ban of Siḥon and Og, the ban of Midian, the ban of Jericho. From where that his confession atoned for him? It is said, the sons of Zeraḥ : Zimri and Ethan , etc. {NAME} said, Zimri is Achan who behaved like Zimri. {NAME} said, Heman that is Achan, omna I sinned. Altogether five . Did I not know that they were five? But it teaches that Achan also has part in the World to Come.
[Sanhedrin 6:3.3] “If he does not know how to confess,” etc. “It happened that one was led out to be executed. They told him, say: ˋMy death shall be atonement for all my sins.’ He said, ˋmy death shall be atonement for all my sins except for this sin; if I committed it, He should never forgive me, but the court of Israel is innocent.’ When the case came before the Sages, their tears flowed. They said, it is impossible to reopen the case, since it would never end. But this person’s blood hangs on the witnesses’ necks.”
[Sanhedrin 6:3.4] “At a distance of four cubits from the place of stoning,” etc. “{NAME} said, may I never see consolation if I did not execute a perjured witness, for they were saying, until he was executed, as it is said, a life for a life . {NAME} told him, may I never see consolation if it is not held against you that you spilled innocent blood. At that time, he took it upon himself not to teach except what he heard from {NAME}.”
[Sanhedrin 6:3.5] {NAME} hands were hot. There came a group of scoffers who said, let us take counsel, testify against his son, and kill him. They testified against him. He was sentenced to be executed. When he was taken to be killed, they told him, our Master, we are liars. From the dog , the pious man’s dog.
