If he used it to bake bread, it is forbidden for usufruct. If it was mixed with other loaves, all are forbidden for usufruct. {NAME} says, he should bring his profit to the Dead Sea. They said to him, idols cannot be redeemed.
[Avodah Zarah 3:12.2] HALAKHAH: “If he took wood from it,” etc. {NAME} said, they are disagreeing in the indeterminate case. Where do we hold? If to heat, everybody agrees that it is permitted. If to fumigate, everybody agrees that it is forbidden. Where do we hold? In the indeterminate case.
[Avodah Zarah 3:13.1] MISHNAH: If he took from it [wood to make] a weaver’s shuttle, it is forbidden for usufruct. If he used it to weave cloth the cloth is forbidden for usufruct. If it was mixed up with others, all are forbidden for usufruct. {NAME} says, he should bring his profit to the Dead Sea. They said to him, idols cannot be redeemed.
[Avodah Zarah 3:13.2] HALAKHAH: “If he took from it [wood to make] a weaver’s shuttle,” etc. {NAME} said, when I descended from a ship I found {NAME} sitting and asked him. “If he took from it [wood to make] a weaver’s shuttle, it is forbidden for usufruct. If he used it to weave cloth the cloth is forbidden for usufruct.” But did we not state, “it should all be sold to a Gentile except for the value of the libation wine in it”? {NAME} said, Ḥaggai raised the question, Ḥaggai resolved it. What is it? There people do not buy from the Gentile; but here people buy cloth from the Gentile.
[Avodah Zarah 3:14.1] MISHNAH: How does one make it insignificant? If he pruned dry branches, green branches, took from it a rod, or a twig, even a leaf, it became in significant. If he planed it for its benefit it is forbidden, not for its benefit it is permitted.
[Avodah Zarah 3:14.2] HALAKHAH: “How does one make it insignificant,” etc Rav said, for his benefit, both it and its shavings are permitted; for its benefit it is forbidden but its shavings are permitted. {NAME} said, for its benefit both it and its shavings are forbidden, for his benefit it is forbidden but its shavings are permitted. {NAME} said, for its benefit it is forbidden but its shavings are permitted.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.1] MISHNAH: {NAME} said, three stones next to one another and next to a Mercury are forbidden, but two are permitted. But the Sages say, what is seen with it is forbidden, what is not seen with it is permitted.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: “{NAME} said,” etc. {NAME} said, the reason of {NAME} is because of a small Mercurius next to a large Mercurius. But the rabbis say, because of the feet of Mercurius. How large are the feet of Mercurius? 50 cubits.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.3] The practice of Mercurius is the following: Two stones one touching the other and the third on top of them. If one put down the second one and they warned him because of “it and its young”, he is whipped. Because of idolatry he is stoned. If he put down the third; there is a disagreement between {NAME} and {NAME}. For they disagreed: If somebody slaughters an animal and its young for idolatrous purposes. {NAME} says, if he was cautioned about an animal and its young he is flogged, about idolatry he is stoned. {NAME} said, even if he is cautioned about an animal and its young he is not flogged since he would be stoned to death had he be cautioned about idolatry.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.4] What is a Mercurius? Any which borders the ocean or roads. The practice of Mercurius is by throwing. What if he bowed down before it? {NAME} said, essentially is is called Mercurius only for bowing down, a maskit stone you shall not put up in your land to bow down on it . I could think that one may not put two stones next to one another and put his box down on them, the verse says to bow down on it , you do not bow down on it but you put your box down on it; you do not bow down on it but you bow down on the stones of the Temple.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.5] Rav commanded to the family of {NAME}, {NAME} commanded to his own family, if you go out on the fast day you should not incline normally. {NAME} inclined on his side; {NAME} inclined on his side. {NAME} said, I saw {NAME} inclining normally. {NAME} said, I pointed out a difficulty before {NAME}, is it not written, a maskit stone you shall not put up in your land to bow down on it . Explain it if he fixed a place for it. But is it not written, it was when David arrived at the mountain top where one bows down before God ? Except bowing down which is not on the ground. Does there exist bowing down which is not on the ground? They fell down with their faces to the ground and bowed down . {NAME} added up to give thanks to the Eternal for He is good; {NAME} added up to for eternal is His kindness to Israel . {NAME} said to {NAME}: Babylonian, two things came from you, the stretching out on the Fast Day, and the willow of the Seventh Day. {NAME} say, also this blood letting. It follows what {NAME} said, the Babylonians in the name of the rabbis there: They permitted prostrating only on a public fast, and only on the side. The younger {NAME} in the name of his fathers: Anybody who is not qualified like Joshua that if he falls on his face the Holy One, praise to Him, would tell him, get up , should not fall down, in the case of an individual [praying] for the community.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.6] “But the Sages say, what is seen with it is forbidden, what is not seen with it is permitted.” (What is seen with it, its body, is forbidden; what is not seen with it is permitted.) What is seen with it is its body, what is not seen with it is not its body. Does this not disagree with {NAME} since {NAME} said, an idol which was broken is permitted? And so we are thinking to say if in the future he can restore it whole it is permitted according to everybody. Does this not disagree with {NAME}, as {NAME} said, an idol which was broken is forbidden? And so we are thinking to say if in the future he cannot restore it whole it is permitted according to everybody.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.7] But {NAME} {NAME} said, if they were lying on their spot it is as if he would return it to its wholeness. And these are at their place.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.8] {NAME} in the name of Rav: Sometimes you are saying, broken pieces of idols cannot be nullified. And sometimes you are saying, serving pieces of idols cannot be nullified He who says serving pieces, certainly idols. But he who says idols, therefore not serving pieces. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: Mercurius stones which were scattered never can be nullified, because of worship of idols. {NAME} heard it and said, our teacher taught us well, since if one bows down before an idol of (mourners) they never can be nullified.
[Avodah Zarah 4:1.9] How does one nullify it? {NAME} said, by spit. But did not {NAME} state: Scattered stones of Mercurius have no nullification? {NAME} said, here those which where thrown at it; there those which were not thrown at it. As this: {NAME} had a Mercurius on his field. He came to his burgonar and told him, since I heard that the magistrate wants to pass by here tomorrow, by your life lift these stones. After he had lifted them, he wanted to take them away. He told him, they are mine. {NAME} heard this and said, did not the Elder {NAME} state this? But since he had heard it from him, he reinforced and fixed it.
[Avodah Zarah 4:2.1] MISHNAH: If one found on top of it coins, garments, or vessels, they are permitted. Branches of vine, wreaths of ears of grain, wines, oils, and fine flours, and anything similar to what is offered on the altar is forbidden.
[Avodah Zarah 4:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If one found coins on top of it,” etc. {NAME} said, not only wreaths of ears of grain but even wreaths of roses. {NAME} said, not only a Mercurius and on top of it coins but even any pagan place which has no lattice work and he found in it garments or vessels, they are permitted.
[Avodah Zarah 4:3.1] MISHNAH: If an idol had a garden or a bath house, one may benefit from them not with a favor but one may not benefit with a favor. If it belongs to it and a third party one benefits whether with or without a favor.
[Avodah Zarah 4:3.2] HALAKHAH: “If an idol had a garden,” etc. So is the Mishnah: A favor to the priests or without a favor to the priests. “It is forbidden to sell fifes of idols, but if one pays the rental fee to the state if it is used to supply the needs of idol worship it is permitted to sell them. It is forbidden to rent a store from a pagan temple, but if one pays rent to the state even if it is used to supply the needs of idol worship it is permitted to rent it. It is forbidden to give to collectors for idol worship. If he pays a fee to the state even though he collects for idol worship it is permitted to give to him.” And the Mishnah said so, “if it belongs to it and a third party one benefits whether with or without a favor.”
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.1] MISHNAH: A Gentile’s idol is immediately forbidden but a Jew’s only when it is worshipped. A Gentile is able to annul his idol and that of a Jew; but a Jew cannot annul the idol of a Gentile. If one annulled an idol he annulled its appurtenances; if he annulled its appurtenances the appurtenances are annulled but it is forbidden.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.2] HALAKHAH: “A Gentile’s idol is immediately forbidden,” etc. {NAME} said, the Mishnah speaks about an artist who works to sell it on the market. When he finishes it, it is a sure thing that he bows down before it. {NAME} asked, if it is a sure thing that he bows down before it, why did we state “a Gentile’s idol is immediately forbidden but a Jew’s only when it is worshipped”?
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.3] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If one cuts an idol in stone, even though you say that nothing connected to the ground is forbidden, one warns him on every single chiseling and when it will be separated from the rock he will be flogged. {NAME} said, from this you understand that if somebody makes a statue for idol worship, even though you say that nothing breathing can be forbidden, one warns him about each single mallet and he will be flogged when it is finished.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.4] “A Gentile’s idol is immediately forbidden,” therefore it can be annulled. “But a Jew’s only when it is worshipped,” therefore it cannot be annulled. {NAME} said, there is no “therefore”, only “it cannot be annulled or it can be annulled”. “A Gentile’s idol is immediately forbidden,” as it is written: you certainly shall destroy. “But a Jew’s only when it is worshipped,” as it is written, cursed be the man who makes a hewn or molten image , etc., when he puts it up. But some are switching this. “A Jew’s idol is immediately forbidden,” for it is written, cursed be the man . “But a Gentile’s only when it was worshipped,” as it is written, you certainly shall destroy all the places where these peoples worshipped . {NAME} in the name of {NAME} understood it from the following: If you inherited it when it was a god you shall burn it in fire, otherwise of which you will inherit their gods . {NAME} in the name of {NAME} understood it from the following: You should not covet silver or gold for them . You cannot covet and take, but others can covet and you are taking.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.5] {NAME} said to {NAME}, go down and break all those statues in the public baths. He went down and broke them all except one. Why this? {NAME} said, because another Jew was suspected of burning incense for it.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.6] {NAME} in the name of Rav: Rebbi was sitting and teaching his son {NAME}. The Gentile annuls his own idol and that of his neighbor. He said to him, when you still were in full mental powers you quoted Tannaim stating that a Gentile annuls his own idol and that of a Jew. He answered him, no, my son. An idol which a Jew had worshipped can never be annulled. And it was stated so: “{NAME} says, an idol which a Jew had worshipped can never be annulled.” Rav stated in the name of the reason of this Tanna: Cursed be the man who makes a hewn or molten image , forever.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.7] {NAME} found a ring with an idol. An Aramean youth was running after him. He was hitting him, cursing him, and told him, spit on it! He did not accept. Urinate on it! He did not accept. This implies that a Non-Jew annuls his own and another person’s idols under duress, on condition that he knows the nature of this idol. An idol which had been worshipped by a Jew can never be annulled. Could it not be like an idol which was abandoned by its worshippers and by that being annulled? {NAME} said, anything which becomes annulled by itself, a Jew can annul. But anything which does not become annulled by itself, a Jew cannot annul.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.8] Rav said, a pedestal is not annulled. Therefore if one annulled it it is annulled. The opinions of Rav seem inconsistent. There he says, if one casts a cup for idolatry it is immediately forbidden, and here he says so? Here if he burned incense, there if he did not burn incense. And even if you are saying, in both cases if he burned incense, Rav follows his opinion since Rav said, if one casts a cup for idolatry it is immediately forbidden.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.9] Rav said, a pedestal is not annulled. Therefore its appurtenances are annulled. The opinions of Rav seem inconsistent. There {NAME} said in the name of Rav, if the procession was using another way, and here he says so? There if he burned incense, here if he did not burn incense. And even if you are saying, in both cases if he burned incense, Rav follows his opinion since Rav said, if one casts a cup for idolatry it is immediately forbidden.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.10] {NAME} said, a stele is a monolith, an altar has many stones. {NAME} said, a stele is annulled once it is damaged; of an altar one has to damage each single stone. A baraita of {NAME} disagrees with him: If you tore down the altar, leave it alone; if you broke the stele, leave it alone . {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}; {NAME} (Rebbi) Abba, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: When He turns all stones of the altar like smashed pieces of chalk , persecute them until you eliminated its egg from the world. But here, if you broke a stele, leave it alone; if you tore down an altar, leave it alone.
[Avodah Zarah 4:4.11] It is written, do not make idols for yourselves, statue and stele you shall not erect for yourselves. Is not making the same as erecting? {NAME} said, making is from new; erecting, if it falls down one shall not re-erect it. It is written, you shall tear down their altars and break their steles. From where to apply one to the other? {NAME} said, it was said to refer to both sides; either breaking, or cutting down, or tearing down for each of them.
[Avodah Zarah 4:5.1] MISHNAH: How does one annul it? If he cut off the top of its earlobe, the tip of its nose, the tip of its finger. If he disfigured it even though nothing is missing, he annulled it. If he spat in its face, urinated before it, dragged it, threw excrement on it, this is not annulled. If he sold or mortgaged it, Rebbi says it is annulled, but the Sages say it is not annulled.
[Avodah Zarah 4:5.2] HALAKHAH: “How does one annul it,” etc? {NAME} said, this is if he sold it in peace. But if he sold it in ill-will, everybody agrees that it is annulled; it happens that he is hungry, falls into a rage, and curses his king etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: They disagreed in case he sold it to a goldsmith. But if he sold it to its worshipper, everybody agrees that it is not annulled. {NAME} in the name of Rav: they disagreed if he sold it to its worshippers. But if he sold it to a goldsmith everybody agrees that it is annulled. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: the opinion of everybody. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: in dispute. It turns out that {NAME} held with {NAME} and {NAME} with {NAME}. What about it? They disagreed in case he sold it to a goldsmith. But if he sold it to one of its worshippers, everybody agrees that it is not annulled.
[Avodah Zarah 4:6.1] MISHNAH: An idol which was abandoned by its worshippers in times of peace is permitted, in times of war is forbidden. Pedestals of kings are permitted since they put them up when the kings pass by.
[Avodah Zarah 4:6.2] HALAKHAH: “An idol which was abandoned by its worshippers,” etc. It was stated: The war of Joshua is forbidden, similar to the war of Joshua is permitted. The war of David is permitted, like the war of David is forbidden. The war of Joshua is forbidden, as it is written, for certainly you should ban them . Similar to the war of Joshua is permitted, for it is a short time. The war of David is permitted, what Itai from Gat annulled. Like the war of David is forbidden, for it is permanent.
[Avodah Zarah 4:7.1] MISHNAH: The Elders were asked in Rome, if He does not approve of idol worship, why does He not eliminate it? They answered, if they would worship something which the world does not need, He would eliminate it. But they worship sun and moon, stars and planets, mountains and hills. Should He destroy His world because of the stupid? They told them, if it is so, He should eliminate things which are not needed in the world, and keep things necessary for the world. They answered, then we would strengthen the worshippers of the latter who would say, you should know that these are divinities since those were eliminated and these were not eliminated.
[Avodah Zarah 4:7.2] HALAKHAH: “The Elders were asked in Rome,” etc. If somebody stole seeds and sowed, would it not grow in the end? If somebody sleeps with a married woman, would he not in the end cause a bastard to be born? But let the world continue its usual way. The stupid who misbehave will in the future have to account for their deeds.
[Avodah Zarah 4:7.3] {NAME} said, if it were written, “like them should be their worshippers”, that would be difficult; the sun’s worshippers like the sun, the moon’s worshippers like the moon? But, like them should be their makers . {NAME} said, if it were written, “like them should be their worshippers”, it would not be difficult, as it is written, the moon will be ashamed and the sun abashed . {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: In the future, an idol will come, spit in the face of its worshippers, make them ashamed, and disappear from the world. What is the reason? All worshippers of statues will be ashamed . {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: In the future, an idol will come, bow down before the Holy One, praise to Him, and disappear from the world. What is the reason? Bow down before Him, all gods .
[Avodah Zarah 4:8.1] MISHNAH: One may buy a used wine-press from a Non-Jew. Even if he takes it in his hands and puts it on the pile. It does not become libation wine until it flows down into the cistern. If it flowed into the cistern, what is in the cistern is forbidden and the remainder in permitted.
[Avodah Zarah 4:8.2] HALAKHAH: “One may buy a used wine-press,” etc. {NAME} stated: Only if the Jew did not turn his eyes away from him. But if he turned his eyes away from him, not then. So far if he was taking juice and grapes together to put on the heap. If he gave these and those separately, (even from what was left in the fissures, what is under the bunches is forbidden, on the sides is permitted.) {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Itself it becomes libation wine.
[Avodah Zarah 4:8.3] A wine press on which a Gentile stopped a leak from the inside is forbidden, from the outside permitted, for it is impossible that there not be wet bast where he touches and turns the entire cistern into libation wine.
[Avodah Zarah 4:8.4] {NAME} in the name of Rav: The jet is like the cistern. {NAME} asked: Everywhere you do not say that flow is connection, but here you are treating flow as connection? {NAME} is of the opinion that if the cistern became libation wine, the flow became libation wine; if the flow became libation wine the cistern did not become libation wine. {NAME} did not say so, but if the cistern became libation wine, the flow did not become libation wine; if the flow became libation wine the cistern became libation wine. What {NAME} said in the name of Rav, the jet is like the cistern, for {NAME} is of the opinion, just as the cistern becomes libation wine so the jet becomes libation wine. There, they say in the name of Rav, the touch of a Gentile makes libation wine. {NAME} said, only when it is flowing.
[Avodah Zarah 4:8.5] An Aramean fell into a cavity. The case came before {NAME} who said, immobilize him until you have emptied the cavity. {NAME} said, he is moving his hand. He said, bring willow baskets and approach from under his hand.
[Avodah Zarah 4:8.6] {NAME} was instructing {NAME}. Starting when does a Gentile make libation wine? He told him, from when he knows the nature of idol worship. ({NAME} left) [Rav put out his head] from the curtain and told him, you may say this if one buys grapes from the Gentile. But the Gentile proper makes libation wine when he is one day old.
[Avodah Zarah 4:8.7] May a Gentile make libation wine with his mouth? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A Gentile cannot make libation wine with his mouth. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A Gentile can make libation wine with his mouth. And we have stated thus: “If a market supervisor tasted from a cup or from a suction pipe and returned to the amphora it is forbidden.” In the opinion of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, only if the Gentile returned it. In the opinion of {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, even if a Jew returned.
[Avodah Zarah 4:9.1] MISHNAH: One may stamp with a Non-Jew in the wine press but one may not harvest with him. With a Jew who works in impurity one neither stamps nor harvests with him but one transports with him amphoras to the wine press and brings with him from the wine press.
[Avodah Zarah 4:9.2] HALAKHAH: “One may stamp with a Non-Jew in the wine press,” etc. {NAME} said, that is, you say only if they walked over it crosswise. But if they did not walk over it crosswise, it does not apply. {NAME} asked, if they walked over it crosswise, even following the earlier teaching? As it was stated: “Originally they were saying that one harvests grapes with the Non-Jew and stamps with a Jew who works in impurity. They changed and said, one does not harvest grapes with the Non-Jew nor stamp with a Jew who works in impurity, but one stamps with a Gentile and helps him as long as it did not disappear from sight. Once it disappeared from sight it became libation wine”.
[Avodah Zarah 4:9.3] What is {NAME} reason? Because it already became impure when it was prepared by the grape harvest. What is the reason of {NAME}? They were pure by biblical standards. You are the one who decided that they be impure. The strength of {NAME} is the following, as {NAME} said in the name of {NAME} It should be logical that one may (free) his ṭevel as it is written, you should give from it the Eternal’s heave to Aaron the priest . You have to give it to Aaron in his quality of priest. But here, since you cannot give it to Aaron the priest in his quality of priest, you may make it impure.
[Avodah Zarah 4:10.1] MISHNAH: If a baker works in impurity one does not knead with him nor form the bread with him, but one may bring bread to the seller with him.
[Avodah Zarah 4:10.2] HALAKHAH: “If a baker works in impurity,” etc. One states about this: One does not moisten, nor grind, nor mix with him. {NAME} said, here for profane [bread], there for heave. Can you say heave at a baker’s? The colleagues: one if he moistens, the other if he does not moisten. But did we not state: “But she may not touch hers once water has been put in because one does not support transgressors.”
[Avodah Zarah 4:10.3] {NAME} and {NAME}. One said, “plough it well; then I will rent it from you after the Sabbatical.” The other one said, “may you succeed.” For him who said, plough it well; then I will rent it from you after the Sabbatical, what means “one greets them”? “May you succeed.” But he who said that one says to a Gentile, may you succeed, what means that one greets Jews? “Peace be on you.”
[Avodah Zarah 4:10.4] Explanation. {NAME} and {NAME} passed by one of the ploughmen in the Sabbatical. {NAME} said to him, may you succeed. {NAME} said to him, did not Rebbi teach, the passers-by did not say , etc., that it is forbidden to say “may you succeed” to one who ploughs in the Sabbatical? He told him, you know how to read but you do not know how to make a homily. The passers-by did not say , these are the nations who pass out of the world because they did not say to Israel, the blessing of the Eternal is on you. What does Israel say to them? We bless you in the name of the Eternal . Israel says to them, all the good things and happy circumstances that come into the world because of us are not enough for you; you do not say, come and take from these blessings for yourselves, but you roll over us pro-rated contributions and fines, head taxes and annonae .
[Avodah Zarah 4:10.5] {NAME} instructed: It is forbidden to take the bread out of the oven with him. Similarly, it is forbidden to sprinkle with him.
[Avodah Zarah 4:11.1] MISHNAH: A Non-Jew who was found standing next to a wine cistern, if he has a loan secured by it, [the wine] is forbidden, if he has no loan secured by it, it is permitted. If he fell into the cistern and climbed out, or measured it with a measuring rod; if he tried to hit a wasp with a stick, or was drumming on the mouth of a fermenting amphora; all these cases happened and they said, it should be sold, but {NAME} permits. If he took the amphora and threw it into the cistern; this happened and they declared it kosher..
[Avodah Zarah 4:11.2] HALAKHAH: “A Non-Jew who was found standing,” etc. Rab Sheshet in the name of Rav: Only if he has a lien on this particular cistern. But if he has no lien on this particular cistern, it is the way of creditors to stand near wine presses and threshing floors. They wanted to say, he who says, only if he has a lien on this particular cistern, within his outstretched arms, but he who says, even if he has no lien on this particular cistern, even outside his outstretched arms. But did not {NAME} say in the name of {NAME}, just as they gave outstretched arms for purity so they gave it for libation wine? But it must be so: He who says, only if he has a lien on this particular cistern, within his outstretched arms, but he who says, even if he has no lien on this particular cistern, only outside his outstretched arms.
[Avodah Zarah 4:11.3] “One who makes a Non-Jew’s wine in purity,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, practice follows {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. I am atoning for {NAME}, either permit to drink or forbid for usufruct. {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}. There was a case and they permitted for drinking following {NAME}. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: A Gentile does not make libation wine by throwing. Does a Gentile make libation wine in his rage? Let us hear from the following: An Aramean had boxes in a wine press. There came a Jew and sprinkled wine on them. The Aramean came [with] a pitcher and poured it out into the cistern. The case came before the rabbis who said, a Gentile does not make libation wine in his rage.
[Avodah Zarah 4:11.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}. One who mixes wine, with hot water it is forbidden, with cold water it is permitted. It should come over me, if I ever did this. {NAME} went to Tyre. He saw them drinking wine with hot water and an Aramean was mixing. He told them, what did allow you?
[Avodah Zarah 4:12.1] MISHNAH: One who makes a Non-Jew’s wine in purity and leaves it in his domain, in a house open to the public domain in a city where there are Gentiles and Jews it is permitted, in a city where all are Gentiles it is forbidden unless he install there a watchman. But the watchman does not have to sit there and watch; even if he leaves and reenters it is permitted. {NAME} says, all Gentiles’ domains are the same. One who makes a Non-Jew’s wine in purity and leaves it in his domain, if this one writes to him that I received the money, it is permitted. But if the Jew wants to remove it and he does not let him do it before he paid him his money, this was a case in Bet Shean and the Sages forbade.
[Avodah Zarah 4:12.2] HALAKHAH: “One who makes a Non-Jew’s wine in purity,” etc. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Not only a door but even a window wide four by four and high ten, on condition that it be roofed and glued closed. If it was growing, we would say if he is seen climbing up and coming down it is forbidden, otherwise it is permitted. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The Mishnah speaks of a town “with double doors and bolts.” Was it stated in that case “a watchman even if he comes only at intervals”?
[Avodah Zarah 4:12.3] It was stated “A Jew and a Gentile who brought their wine into the surroundings of the city, even if the watchmen are Gentile, even if the amphoras are open, they are permitted since one does not make a libation in this way.”
[Avodah Zarah 4:12.4] {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The buyer has the same status as the seller. It was stated thus: Whether the seller or the buyer [stores] on the Gentile’s property. If the wine is the Jew’s and a Jew lives there it is permitted on condition that in his hand are key and seal. If the wine is the Gentile’s and a Jew lives there it is permitted on condition that in his hand are key and seal; but if no Jew lives there it is forbidden even if key and seal are in his hand.

[Horayot 1:1.1] MISHNAH: If the Court ruled to violate one of the commandments spelled out in the Torah and a single person went and acted inadvertently following their pronouncement, whether they acted and he acted simultaneously with them, or they acted and he followed their example, or they did not act but he did, he is not liable since he depended on the Court. If the Court ruled but one of them knew that they erred, or a student worthy of ordination went and acted following their pronouncement, whether they acted and he acted simultaneously with them, or they acted and he followed their example, or they did not act but he did, he is liable since he did not depend on the Court. This is the principle: The person depending on himself is liable, but one depending on the Court is not liable.
[Horayot 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “If the Court ruled.” etc. A person who would transgress; one would transgress; acting he would transgress; these are restrictions: the person depending on himself is liable, but one dependent on the Court is not liable. Everywhere it is said that a restriction after a restriction is an addition, but here it is said, a restriction after a restriction is to reduce? {NAME} said, it is different here since there is written a restriction after a restriction after a restriction.

[Horayot 2:5.3] But one never is liable for any positive commandment in the Torah! {NAME} said, we only came to state matters similar to the matter. How is that? If he entered the Temple impure, he is liable. If he entered pure but became impure, if he leaves on a long path he is liable, on a short one not liable. Similarly, if he was having sex with an impure woman, he is liable. If he was having sex with a pure one and she said to him, I became impure, if he leaves on a long path he is liable, on a short one not liable. What is his shortcut? He shall cool down.
[Horayot 2:5.4] “What is the positive commandment about the menstruating woman?” {NAME} said, Keep the Children of Israel away from their impurities . {NAME} sent to ask {NAME}, from where a warning for one having sex with an impure woman? He answered him, that is not my problem. My only problem is rather “if he was having sex with an impure woman, he is liable. If he was having sex with a pure one and she said to him, I became impure,” if he separates immediately, is he liable? He told him, I and you have the same problem. Let us go out and learn. They went out and heard the voice of a Tanna who stated following Ḥiskiah: If lying a man will lie with her . Not only that if he was having sex with an impure woman, he is liable. If he was having sex with a pure one and she said to him, I became impure, if he separates immediately, is he liable? The verse says, her secretion shall be , even if her secretion starts with him. What should he do? {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, he shall cool down. If he did not cool down? {NAME} said, for him I am reading do not come near as “do not separate”. Closeness is separation. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: Those who say, be close to yourself, do not touch me for I sanctified you . {NAME} said, he should imagine that a sword is cutting into his flesh. Is everybody {NAME}? {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: He shall press his fingertips on the wall, then he will cool down.

[Horayot 2:7.1] MISHNAH: For all commandments of the Torah where one is liable to extirpation for willful infraction and a purification sacrifice for unintentional infraction, the individual brings a sheep or a she-goat, the Prince a he-goat, and the Anointed or the Court bring a bull. For idolatry the individual, the Prince, and the Anointed bring a she-goat, the Court bring a bull as elevation offering and a goat as purification sacrifice. For a suspended reparation sacrifice the individual and the Prince are liable but the Anointed and the Court are not liable. For a certain reparation sacrifice the individual, and the Prince, and the Anointed are liable but the Court is not liable. For hearing a sound, or expression of the lips, or the impurity of the Temple and its sancta, the Court is not liable, the individual, and the Prince, and the Anointed are liable but the Anointed is not liable for the impurity of the Temple and its sancta, the words of {NAME}. What do they bring? A variable sacrifice. {NAME} says, the Prince brings a goat.
[Horayot 2:7.2] HALAKHAH: “For all commandments of the Torah,” etc. Halakhah 8: “For a suspended sacrifice the individual and the Prince are liable,” etc. A person, to include the Prince. Should it include the Anointed? “ And sinned inadvertently. ” Any depending on acting inadvertently. This excludes the Anointed who is not depending on acting inadvertently. But following Rebbi who said, the Anointed is depending on acting inadvertently? One dependent on acting inadvertently in any situation. This excludes the Anointed who is not dependent on acting inadvertently in any situation. A person, to include the Prince and the Anointed. Here you say, to include the prince, and there you say, to include the Anointed? Like the purification sacrifices is the reparation sacrifice . Just as the purification sacrifice atones and wipes clean, also the reparation sacrifice atones and wipes clean. This excludes the suspended reparation sacrifice which atones but leaves a residue.

It is equal on the day of Atonement. But his brothers the priests are not equal on the day of Atonement! [Horayot 3:2.1] MISHNAH: If they sinned before being appointed; when afterwards they were appointed, they remain commoners. {NAME} says, if it became known to them before they were appointed, they are obligated; if after they were appointed they are not liable. Who is the Prince? This is the king, as it is said, if he transgressed one of the commandments of the Eternal, his God; a Prince who has none above him but the Eternal, his God. And who is the Anointed? This is one anointed with the anointing oil, not one clothed in multiple garb. The only difference between the priest anointed with the anointing oil and the one clothed in multiple garb is the bull brought for all commandments. And the only difference between an officiating High Priest and a deposed one is the bull of the Day of Atonement and the tenth of an ephah . Both are equal in the office of the day of Atonement, commanded about the virgin, and prohibited for a widow, and do not defile themselves for close relatives, and may not let their hair grow or rend their garments, and let the homicide return.
[Horayot 3:2.2] HALAKHAH: “If they sinned before being appointed,” etc. The colleagues say that the reason of {NAME} is because greatness atones. {NAME} said, because his sin and his knowledge are not equal. What is the difference between them? Referring to the beginning of the Chapter: “An Anointed Priest who sinned and then was removed from his anointed status, or a Prince who sinned and then was removed from his exalted status. The Anointed Priest brings a bull and the Prince brings a goat;” if there is any doubt whether they sinned. He who said, because greatness atones; just as it atones for the certain [sin] so it atones for the doubt. He who said. because his sin and his knowledge are not equal; his sin and his knowledge are not equal. If they sinned before they were appointed and after they were appointed they breached, for him who said, because greatness atones, greatness atoned for the first, but he is liable for the second and the third. For him who said, because his sin and his knowledge are not equal. If they sinned regarding hearing a sound, or expression of the lips, or the impurity of the Temple and its sancta, for him who said, because his sin and his knowledge are not equal, here his sin and his knowledge are equal. For him who said, because greatness atones, even in this case greatness atones.
[Horayot 3:2.3] {NAME} said: Greatness cannot atone (until his greatness becomes known to him) [unless his error became known to him.] If he ate half the volume of an olive before he was appointed and half the volume of an olive after he was appointed, even in one oblivion he is not liable. A doubt of half the volume of an olive before he was appointed and a doubt of half the volume of an olive after he was appointed: he brings a suspended reparation offering. Do we find anything where for the actual offense he is not liable but for a doubt he is liable? We do not find this! If he ate the volume of two olives, the true nature of one of them became known to him, the other remained for him in doubt. {NAME} asked before {NAME}: As you take it, if he ate forbidden fat, it atoned. [If he ate permitted fat, it atoned.] {NAME} said, anything which convinced him to bring a suspended reparation offering, the knowledge of the doubt establishes his transgression. So we find a case where for the actual offense he is not liable but for a doubt he is liable.
[Horayot 3:2.4] One ate the volume of an olive before he was appointed and the volume of an olive after he was appointed. If it was in one oblivion, he is liable only for one [sacrifice]. If the volume of an olive was in doubt before he was appointed, and the volume of an olive was in doubt after he was appointed, in one oblivion he is liable only for one, in two forgettings he is liable for two [sacrifices.]

[Horayot 3:2.8] The argument of {NAME} seems to be inverted. There, he said, if part of the sin was atoned, all of the sin was atoned. And here he says so? {NAME} said this only for the last realization which does not require any sacrifice.

[Horayot 3:2.11] If one ate half the volume of an olive before he was appointed, half the volume of an olive after he was appointed, half the volume of an olive after he was removed from office. [He ate] the third while oblivious of the second. If he brought for the middle ones, he is liable for the first separately and for the fourth separately.

[Horayot 3:2.23] It was stated: {NAME} says: The anointing oil made by Moses on the Mountain was from beginning to end a series of miracles since there were only twelve log to start with, as it was said: and olive oil one hin . From it the Tabernacle and all its vessels were anointed, the altar and all its vessels, the candelabra and all its vessels, the wash basin and its base. From it Aaron the High Priest and his sons were anointed all of the seven days of induction; from it all high priests and kings were anointed. A king who is first needs anointing; a king who is a king’s son does not need anointing, for it is said: Do anoint him , for this one is it , this one needs anointing, but his son does not need anointing. [Niddah 1:1.1] MISHNAH: Shammai says, every woman’s timing is exact; Hillel says, from checking to checking, even if that is a long time. But the Sages say following neither of them but for checking to checking to be reduced by 24 hours, and from 24 hours to be reduced by checking. Every woman with a regular period follows her exact timing; and if one has intercourse with cloths, this counts as checking and is reduced by 24 hours and by checking.
[Niddah 1:1.2] HALAKHAH: “Shammai says, every woman’s timing is exact,” etc. What means, “their timing is exact”? They do not retroactively impart impurity to food prepared in purity. “But the Sages say following neither of them,” not following Shammai who imposed no restriction, and not like Hillel who went overboard. “But for checking to checking it is reduced by 24 hours, and from 24 hours is reduced by checking.” How is checking to checking reduced by 24 hours? If she checked herself on Tuesday and saw blood on Thursday, [her food] is impure only from the same time on Wednesday. How is 24 hours reduced by checking? If she checked herself out in the morning and saw in the afternoon, it is impure only starting from the morning.
[Niddah 1:1.3] There, we have stated: “A [dead] crawling animal found in a dead-end alley causes impurity retroactively. {NAME} asked, does this Mishnah not disagree with Shammai? {NAME} said, this is true, it does not follow Shammai, but even Hillel it does not follow. Does Hillel not agree that a dead-end alley which was swept or inundated by a rainstorm is pure? Shammai says, since this woman regularly urinates, she is like a dead-end alley which was swept or inundated by a rainstorm and is pure.
[Niddah 1:1.4] So far if she checked and found herself dry. If she checked and found herself pure? {NAME} in the name of Rav, {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: If she checked and found herself pure she is forbidden to her husband until her [blood’s] source dries up. One {NAME} said in the name of {NAME}, she is forbidden to her house for 24 hours. {NAME} said, when I immigrated here, I heard from all rabbis that she is immediately permitted to her husband. They wanted to say that for him who says, she is permitted to her husband, this is a check which diminishes from 24 hours, but for him who says, she is forbidden to her husband, it is not counted as a check which diminishes from 24 hours. But even for him who says, she is forbidden to her husband, it is counted as a check which diminishes from 24 hours. Why is she forbidden to her husband? Because she is used to pure blood, she might get used to impure blood.
[Niddah 1:1.5] If she checked herself and found it a doubtful case. It is obvious that it is not counted as a check to diminish from 24 hours. Itself, would it be impure because of doubt? Let us hear from the following: “A sexless or a hermaphrodite who had a discharge follow their exact timing.” What do you infer from this? {NAME} said, a sexless or a hermaphrodite represent a doubt, 24 hours represent a doubt, and a doubt is not superimposed on a doubt. So here, whether she had a discharge represents a doubt, 24 hours represent a doubt, and a doubt is not superimposed on a doubt.
[Niddah 1:1.6] {NAME} said, the 24 hours which were quoted refer to sacrifices but not to pure food. {NAME} objected, was it not stated: “It happened with a girl in Aitlo that she missed for three periods and then had a period. When the case came before the Sages, they said that her timing is exact.” Are there sacrifices in Aitlo? But it must be food prepared in the purity of sacrifices! Is that not really profane food? Explain it if it was prepared in the purity of purifying water, since purifying water has more restrictive rules than sacrifices.
[Niddah 1:1.7] It was stated: For the 24 hours which were stated, one suspends but one does not burn. {NAME} enjoyed this [because] he found stated: “A woman who detects a stain makes impure retroactively. What does she make impure? Food, and drinks, and seats, and beds; her count is in disorder, and she makes her sex partner impure retroactively. A woman who detects blood makes impure retroactively. What does she make impure? Food, and drinks, and seats, and beds; her count is not in disorder, and she does not make her sex partner impure retroactively. {NAME} says, she makes her sex partner impure retroactively. In both cases, one suspends but one does not burn.” There, they say: For the 24 hours which were stated, her bed is like her touch. How? Like one who sleeps with a menstruating woman who does not make impure by moving and does not make clay vessels impure. It was found stated: He makes clay vessels impure by moving. For the 24 hours which were stated, what is the status of what she touches in the public domain? Let us hear from the following: Pregnant and nursing women are pure for their husbands, as is a woman with a regular period. And all other women are pure for sexual relations but impure in their touch. That means, what she certainly touched in the public domain is impure.
[Niddah 1:1.8] {NAME} asked: She checked her garment in the morning and found it pure, in the afternoon and found a stain on it. It is obvious that her garment is retroactively impure only after the time of her checking. Is her body impure for retroactive 24 hours? Does one not declare her body to be impure only because of her garment? Her garment is retroactively impure only after the time of her checking; her body should retroactively be impure for 24 hours?
[Niddah 1:1.9] “And if one has intercourse with cloths, this counts as checking.” How is that? If she checked herself in the morning, had intercourse with a cloth at noontime, and saw [blood] in the afternoon, she is impure only from after the time of intercourse. Levi said, the Mishnah speaks of a cloth used after intercourse, but for a cloth used before intercourse she would be impatient for her mate and not check thorougly. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}, the Mishnah speaks of a cloth used before intercourse, but a cloth used after intercourse is faded because of semen.

About oil, as we have stated: “Rebbi and his court permitted oil.” About bills of divorce, as we have stated there: “This is your bill of divorce if I die, this is your bill of divorce if [I die from this] sickness, this is your bill of divorce after my death; he did not say anything.” But our teachers said, this is a bill of divorce. Who are “our teachers”? {NAME} and his court. They should have called him “permissive court” since any court which permits three [previously forbidden] things is called “permissive court.” {NAME} said, his court disagreed with him about the bills of divorce. {NAME} shouted, you purified the women giving birth! {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: This is part of the testimony of {NAME}; as from {NAME}: If this is part of the testimony of {NAME} then it was {NAME} who shouted, you purified the women giving birth!
[Niddah 3:4.4] “What is the placenta they mentioned? Anything looking like a thread of woof and its head is blown up like a lupine. {NAME} says, anything looking like chicken intestines and its head is blown up like a crop and it is hollow like a trumpet. No placenta is shorter than a hand-breadth.”
[Niddah 3:4.5] {NAME} sent and asked {NAME}: If a placenta came out partially today and partially tomorrow? He told him, for pure blood she counts from the first day, for impure blood she counts from the second day. {NAME} said, this refers to the case that there was no child born with it. But if a child was born with it, then both for pure and for impure blood she counts only from the moment the child was born.
[Niddah 3:4.6] {NAME} asked before Rebbi: Can one refer a placenta to something which is not a child? He said to him, one does not refer a placenta to anything which is not a child. If it came out attached to it, what then? He said to him, one does not discuss anything impossible. {NAME} stated from {NAME}: One does not refer a placenta to something which is not a child, if [nevertheless] it came out attached to something else, one refers to it. {NAME} asked the students of Rav: Can one refer a placenta to stillbirths? They said to him, one refers a placenta to a child and one [does not] refer(s) a placenta to stillbirths. {NAME} praised them because they follow the argument [of their teacher]. {NAME} stated from {NAME}: One refers a placenta to a child but one does not refer a placenta to stillbirths since it does not separate until it [was completed]. {NAME} in the name of the rabbis: What you say, that one refers a placenta to a child, is because a pregnant woman does not become pregnant. Why does one not refer it to stillbirth, can a woman not have a stillbirth followed by a stillbirth? I say that she was pregnant with twins when the placenta of one amnion was crushed by the amnion of the other placenta. {NAME}, {NAME} in the name of Rav: One refers a placenta to a child for up to three days, and no child remains after another child for three days. {NAME} said, he who said this also said the other, but they disagree with one another! {NAME} said, {NAME} explained it following Rav: You say that one refers a placenta to a child for up to three days if the child was born first, and you say that no child remains after another child for three days if the sole appeared first. {NAME} said, is that correct? The active ones come out first. {NAME} said, if [the womb] opened for the large, it opened for the small; if it opened for the small it did not open for the large.
[Niddah 3:4.7] {NAME} said, this follows {NAME}, since {NAME} said, the child was dissolved before it came out. {NAME} said, {NAME} agrees that he causes his mother the days of birth. Then the house should be impure? {NAME} said, explain it if it came out partially dissolved. {NAME} said to the Sages: Do you not agree with me that if the basin is carried from the inner to an outer room it is pure? They said to him, because it becomes scrambled. He said to them, this one is already scrambled. What is the rule about vessels which were there at the time of delivery? Let us hear from the following which we stated there: “{NAME} says, if a cow brought forth a cake of blood, that should be buried and she is freed from the rule of firstlings.” It was stated on this: It does not bring impurity by being carried. {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} said the same thing. This implies that vessels which were there at the time of delivery are pure.
[Niddah 3:5.1] MISHNAH: If a woman miscarries a sexless, or a hermaphrodite, and a male, she shall observe for a male and a female. If it was a sexless and a male, or a hermaphrodite and a male, she shall observe for a male and a female. A sexless and a female, or a hermaphrodite and a female, she shall observe for a female exclusively. If it came out in pieces or defective, it is born as soon as most of its body came out. If it was a regular birth, when most of its head came out. When is it most of its head? If the forehead came out. If a woman miscarries and it is not known what it was, she shall observe for a male and a female. If it is not known whether there was a fetus, she shall observe for a male, a female, and menstruation. If she miscarries on the 40 day, she gives no thought to a child. On the 41 day, she shall observe for a male, a female, and menstruation. {NAME} says, on the 41 st day, she shall observe for a male and menstruation, on the 81 st day, she shall observe for a male, a female, and menstruation for the male is fully formed by the 41 st day and the female by the 81 st . But the Sages say, the creation of males and females is identical, both on the 41 st .
[Niddah 3:5.2] HALAKHAH: “If a woman miscarries a sexless, or a hermaphrodite,” etc. In all cases in which we have stated “she shall observe for a male and a female,” it means 14 [days] impure and 26 pure; one puts on her the restrictions of both male and female. That means, for her house. But for pure food she observes the rules of a female [birth]. “If it was a sexless and a male, or a hermaphrodite and a male, she shall observe for a male and a female,” one takes into account the possibility of a male. “A sexless and a female, or a hermaphrodite and a female, she shall observe for a female exclusively,” does one not take into account the possibility of a male? This implies that if she gave birth to a male and a female, or a female and a male, she observes the rules for a female.
[Niddah 3:5.3] If it was in pieces and the head came out, what is the rule? {NAME} said, {NAME} and {NAME} disagree. {NAME} said, its head counts for most of it. {NAME} said, its head is like any other of its limbs. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If it came out in pieces or defective, it is born as soon as most of its body came out.” Explain it if its head came out. A Mishnah disagrees with {NAME}: “If it was a regular birth, when most of its head came out.” Did not the first part say, the head is nothing? Explain it about the incomplete body. {NAME} and {NAME}; {NAME} agrees with {NAME}, {NAME} with {NAME}. {NAME} showed the colleagues his forehead with the skull. One of {NAME} asked before {NAME}: Since you say, it is a child, does this not imply that one who comes after him is firstborn neither for inheritance nor for the Cohen. He said to him, explain it if both were stillborn.
[Niddah 3:5.4] {NAME} in the name or {NAME}: The head of a bird by most of it. {NAME} in the name of {NAME}: The throat of a bird by most of it. There came a case before {NAME} about [a bird whose throat] was punctured by a needle’s width. Do we not know what “most” means?
[Niddah 4:1.1] MISHNAH: The daughters of Samaritans are menstruating from their cribs, and Samaritan men make impure bottoms like uppers because they sleep with menstruating woman since they sit for every blood. But one is not guilty about them for entering the Temple and one does not burn heave because of them since their impurity is one of doubt.
[Niddah 4:1.2] HALAKHAH: “The daughters of Samaritans are menstruating from their cribs,” etc. Menstrual blood is dirty, virginal blood is not dirty. Menstrual blood is red, virginal blood is not red. Menstrual blood is from the womb, virginal blood is not from the womb but from the side.
